==Difference from the novel==
{{main|Shehr-e-Zaat (novella)}}
Prior to adaptation ''Shehr-e-Zaat'' was a story of comprises no more than 70 to 88 pages and was published in Ahmad's book ''Meri Zaat Zara-e-Benishan'' along with two more stories in first edition. Moreover, it was also published in Umeras another book ''Main Ne Khwabon Ka Shajar Dekha Hai'' with five other stories, but as for 2010s editions of Umera's work, all adapted work is printed separately. To give the strength to story, Umera added two new characters ''Hamza'' (portrayed by [[Mohib Mirza]]) and Nani (portrayed by [[Samina Peerzada]]). Changes into story were positively accepted, although the script for Drama serial settled with different opening and ended with not a same but similar ending. Umera mentions the story plot set in Lahore and Karachi, but more than 85% of shoot was completed only in Karachi.

==Reception==

===Critical reception===
Shehr-e-Zaat received a rating of 7.9 trp,<ref>{{cite web|title=Shehr-e-Zaat Review|url=http://vidpk.com/c/726/Shehr-E-Zaat/#!c:726%7ccp:1|publisher=Video PK|accessdate=21 February 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Shehr-e-Zaat Ratings|url=http://en.cyclopaedia.net/wiki/List-of-Pakistani-television-serials|publisher=EncyclopediaNet|date=1 November 2013|accessdate=21 February 2014}}</ref> owing to its popularity, a special transmission was held in Karachi and broadcast on [[Hum TV]] at the conclusion of the drama.<ref name="Drama Archive"/><ref name="Shehr-e-ZaatAboutTimelineAbout"/> Shehr-e-Zaat was ranked No. 4. Due to story Sufism and Islamization touch it draws orthodox reviews commented that ''Shehr-e-Zaat and its misplaced knowledge of Islam''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Shehr-e-Zaat and its misplaced knowledge of Islam|url=http://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/14645/shehr-e-zaat-and-its-misplaced-knowledge-of-islam/|publisher=[[Express Tribune]]|work=Anam Zeb|date=7 November 2012|accessdate=21 February 2014}}</ref> It is the [[Pakistani drama|third highest-rated Pakistani television series]]. In a blog on The Tribune, a writer wrote about  "misplaced knowledge of Islam" due to the way the story presented [[Sufi]]sm and Islamization.<ref>{{cite web|title=Shehr-e-Zaat and its misplaced knowledge of Islam|url=http://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/14645/shehr-e-zaat-and-its-misplaced-knowledge-of-islam/|work=[[The Express Tribune]]|author=Anam Zeb|date=7 November 2012|accessdate=21 February 2014}}</ref> [[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] declared the series as one of the highlights of 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/775238/pakistani-dramas-highlights-of-2012|title=Pakistani dramas: highlights of 2012|date=31 December 2012|first=Eefa|last=Khalid|work=Dawn}}</ref> It received universal acclaim all around the world. Indian TV channel [[Star Plus]] wanted to telecast it in India but Hum TV refused it. Mahira Khan was praised for her acting many called her the heart of show, also saying that she outclassed her co-actors with her acting. Shehr-e-zaat was named the best drama serial by [[CNN]]. Shehr e Zaat won best drama serial at [[Hum Awards]] 2013. The show rose [[Mahira Khan]] to a limelight once again after ''[[Humsafar]]'' and [[Yash Chopra]] also said in an interview that after seeing the serial he decided to launch Mahira Khan. She also won Best Actress award. Many called her the new face of Pakistani Cinema.

===Controversies===
Shehr-e-Zaat was the most talked about show when it went on air, people talked about everything from the inspirational message it contained to whether Falak should or should not be wearing a dupatta. Shehr-e-Zaat is still the most talked about drama, not because people are still impressed by it but because of the rift it caused between the writer Umera Ahmed, the channel on which it was being aired and the director Sarmad Khoosat. Umera wrote the script of serial for only 16 episodes but it went on to 19 episodes due to positively received reception. [[Hum TV]] apologizes for doing that because the last three episodes were unnecessarily stretched. The final episodes lost the charm of the serial. In the final episode of serial, the director wrote an ending monologue; "cheezain behaya nahi hoti, jo kuch un se mansoob kya jata hay woh behaya hota hai..." which was actually neither the part of Novel nor the script and was written against the will of writer.

'''''Shehrnaz''''' is a Pakistani television drama serial, which aired on [[Urdu 1]] from 12 November 2016 to 22 March 2017. It starred [[Ayeza Khan]], [[Alyy Khan]], [[Imran Ashraf]] and [[Farhan Ahmed Malhi]]. It was produced by [[Danish Taimoor]].<ref name="Shehrnaaz">{{Cite web|url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1150375|title=HIP Exclusive: Ayeza Khan to play aspiring actress in serial, Shehrnaz|last=Sarym|first=Ahmed|date=5 August 2016|access-date=12 September 2016}}</ref><ref name="Ayeza Khan">{{Cite web|url=http://fashionable.pk/upcoming-drama-serial-hum-tv-shehrnaz/|title=Upcoming Drama Serial on Hum Tv Entertainment "Shehrnaz" -|date=3 September 2016|accessdate=12 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.viralsaeen.com/shehrnaz-ayeza-khan-upcoming-drama/|title=Shehrnaz Ayeza Khan Upcoming Drama|date=7 August 2016|language=en|access-date=12 September 2016}}</ref>

==Synopsis==
The story revolves around a beautiful girl Shehrnaaz. She lives with her father who is a poor tailor in Karachi's poor area. Despite their poverty, her father has made sure that his daughter goes to a top university. Shehrnaaz knows that she is beautiful and stands out amongst her peers. She wants to be a top class actress. Unfortunately, her background is a big hurdle in pursuing her career. Eventually she succeeds in realising her dream. But her success comes at a huge price.

'''Sila''' ({{langx|ur|{{Nastaliq|صلہ}}}}; [[Literal meaning|lit]]: ''Result''), is a Pakistani television [[soap opera|drama serial]], that aired on 28 October 2016, preceded by ''[[Dharkan (2016 TV series)|Dharkan]]''. It stars [[Shakeel]], [[Farhan Saeed]], [[Ainy Jaffri]], and [[Ismat Zaidi]] in key roles.

It aired every Fridays at 9:10pm [[Pakistan Standard Time|PST]]. Ainy Jaffri makes her return to [[Hum TV]] after she was last seen in the channel's serial, ''[[Aseerzadi]]''. Farhan Saeed was last seen in the serial ''[[Udaari]]''. [[Eshita Syed|Eshita]] was last seen in the channel's ''[[Zindagi Tujh Ko Jiya]]''.

== Cast ==
* [[Farhan Saeed]] as Taimoor
* [[Ainy Jaffri]] as Mariam
* [[Eshita Syed|Eshita]] as Mishal 
* [[Shakeel]] as Aleem  
* [[Ismat Zaidi]] as Razia 
* [[Javed Sheikh]] as Ehsaan 
* [[Farah Shah]] as Nargis 
* Madiha Zaidi as Mehwish 
* [[Hina Javed]] as Mehwish
* Haya Sehgal as Farkhanda 
* Arjumand Azhar as Jahangir
* Tehmina Siddiqui as Sana 
* [[Shamim Hilaly]] as Sajjad's mother
[[File:Farhan Saeed.jpeg|thumb|right|140px|Farhan Saeed]]

== Plot ==
Mariam belongs to a middle-class family. Her father is a retired banker and her mother teaches in a school. Mariam gets a scholarship to medical college where she falls in love with Taimoor, the son of a surgeon. Taimoor’s mother wants him to marry her niece, but the duo gets married against her wishes and starts a new life in a middle-class neighbourhood. What does life have in store for them? Maryam meets her professor and starts a job with him. Taimoor dislikes this as he thinks that it is his job to earn bread and butter. Here Taimoor's father and Niece Mishal trick him to think that Maryam is having an affair with her boss and saw them coming out of a five-star hotel kissing when Maryam said her father had a heart attack. Taimoor goes into depression and smokes. He slaps Maryam and then apologises but this causes a breakage in the love of the duo. Maryam goes to her father's house and finds that she is five months pregnant. She stays the night and Taimoor thinks that she is lying and gets angry. He shifts back to his dad's house and agrees to marry Mishal. Maryam goes to his office and tells him she is pregnant, but he says that he will be divorcing her soon and this child is Sajjad's. Maryam slaps him and leaves. Taimoor gets a call for a concert and opens his email where he realises Maryam was right. He refuses to marry Mishal and tells Maryam to come to this concert where she forgives him after putting her hand on her womb after Taimoor asks forgiveness for the sake of his child.

== Production ==
=== Filming ===
It was heard that this drama was shot in 2013 but it would air in 2016 starring [[Farhan Saeed]] and [[Ainy Jaffri]]. The whole shooting is done in [[United Medical and Dental College]] UMDC, a medical college in Karachi.

===Casting===
Initially [[Fahad Mustafa]] was selected to play the titular character but then he rejected due to movies. So the drama was reshot with [[Farhan Saeed]] as main lead.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sila Drama that was Shot 3 Years Ago Will onair in 2016|url=http://www.habibifeed.com/pakistani/dramas/sila-upcoming-drama-hum-tv-2016/|website=Habibi Feed|accessdate=16 October 2016}}</ref>

[[Momina Duraid|MD Productions]] chose cast [[Ainy Jaffri]] as Mariam, [[Farhan Saeed]] as Taimoor, [[Javed Sheikh]] as Ahsan, [[Farah Shah]] as Nargis, Haya Sehgal as elder sister of Marium, Farkhanda and Tehmina Siddiqui as her younger sister, Sana. [[Shakeel]] and [[Ismat Zaidi]] play role of Mariam and her siblings' parents. While, [[Eshita Syed]] was chosen to play character of Mishal, who is chosen by Taimoor's parents for his marriage. Arjumand Azhar (Hussain) was chosen for the role of Jahangir (Mishal's father) and "Uncredited" to portray role of Nargis' sister and Mishal's mother role. Meanwhile, [[Shakeel]] and [[Ismat Zaidi]] are playing role of Mariyam and her siblings' parents.
The [[drama]] has already been a hit. Both the leads had immediate successes following the drama as [[Farhan Saeed]] gained a lot of fans and released new awesome songs and [[Ainy Jaffri]] made her awesome movie debut in the movie [[Balu Mahi]].

'''Tanveer Fatima (B.A)''' ({{langx|ur|{{nq|تنویر فاطمہ (بی اے)}}}}) is a 2009 Pakistani television drama serial that aired on [[Jang Media Group|Geo TV]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Serial's information, casts and all episodes|url=http://vidpk.com/c/238/Tanveer-Fatima-BA/|publisher=vidpk.com|accessdate=19 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130320232330/http://vidpk.com/c/238/Tanveer-Fatima-BA/|archive-date=20 March 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> The serial was produced by Hassan Zia and written by [[Syed Nabeel]]. The first 72 episodes were directed by Naved Jaffrey and the latter 244 episodes were directed by Syed Nabeel, totalling 316 episodes. Among the cast were [[Samina Ahmad]], [[Nayyar Ejaz]], [[Shabbir Jan]], [[Humaima Malik]], [[Shehnaz Pervaiz]], [[Danish Nawaz]] and [[Yasir Nawaz]].

WIKIPEDIA REVISION DOCUMENT: Turkish television drama

{{Short description|Overview of television serials in Turkey}}
{{Multiple issues|
{{cleanup|reason= contains incomprehensible sections and unencyclopedic expressions|date=September 2020}}
{{Tone|date=February 2021}}
}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=May 2023}}
{{Use American English|date=October 2026}}
'''Turkish dramas''' ({{langx|tr|Türk dizileri}}) are a genre of [[television series]] made in [[Turkey]]. These dramas reflect [[Culture of Turkey|Turkish culture]] and are considered by some to be one of the country's most important economic and cultural exports.<ref name="Jenna Krajeski">{{cite web |author=Jenna Krajeski |url=http://pulitzercenter.org/reporting/turkey-diyarbakir-kurdish-roles-soap-opera-politics-ayrilik-olmasaydi |title=Turkey: Soap Operas and Politics |work=Pulitzer Center |date=30 March 2012 |access-date=2013-01-15 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130117025311/http://pulitzercenter.org/reporting/turkey-diyarbakir-kurdish-roles-soap-opera-politics-ayrilik-olmasaydi |archive-date=2013-01-17 }}</ref><ref name="The International">{{cite web|last=Moore|first=Robbie|title=Soap Opera Diplomacy: Turkish TV in Greece|url=http://www.theinternational.org/articles/339-soap-opera-diplomacy-turkish-tv-in-greec|work=The International|access-date=13 February 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130215073839/http://www.theinternational.org/articles/339-soap-opera-diplomacy-turkish-tv-in-greec|archive-date=15 February 2013}}</ref> They have seen significant growth since the 2000s, and Turkey surpassed [[Mexico]] and [[Brazil]] as the second-largest exporter of television series after the [[United States]] by the mid-2010s.<ref name="Jenna Krajeski" /><ref name="The International" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/world/mena/turkey-has-a-star-role-in-more-than-just-tv-drama-1.379054|title=Turkey has a star role in more than just TV drama|date=2012-02-08|publisher=The National|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150927181852/http://www.thenational.ae/news/world/middle-east/turkey-has-a-star-role-in-more-than-just-tv-drama|archive-date=2015-09-27|url-status=live}}</ref> The television industry has played a crucial role in increasing Turkey's popularity in [[Asia]], [[Europe]], [[Latin America]], and [[North Africa]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Television series enhances Turkey's popularity in Arab world|url=http://news.xinhuanet.com/english2010/indepth/2011-04/09/c_13820858.htm|publisher=Xinhua|date=2011-04-09|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110412093434/http://news.xinhuanet.com/english2010/indepth/2011-04/09/c_13820858.htm|archive-date=2011-04-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dailysabah.com/feature/2016/02/03/the-success-story-of-turkish-tv-series-in-latin-america|title=The success story of Turkish TV series in Latin America|website=dailysabah.com|date=3 February 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160505021557/http://www.dailysabah.com/feature/2016/02/03/the-success-story-of-turkish-tv-series-in-latin-america|archive-date=2016-05-05}}</ref>

Turkish series are chiefly produced in [[Istanbul]], following the liberalization of private television in [[Turkey]] in the 1990s.<ref>{{cite web|last=Paris|first=Julien|title=A Geographical Approach Of Creative Industries: The Case Of Tv Production In Istanbul|url=http://f.hypotheses.org/wp-content/blogs.dir/394/files/2011/12/Julien-Paris-Abstract-for-ISTANBUL.-CITY-PORTRAIT.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131113023520/http://f.hypotheses.org/wp-content/blogs.dir/394/files/2011/12/Julien-Paris-Abstract-for-ISTANBUL.-CITY-PORTRAIT.pdf|archive-date=2013-11-13}}</ref> Turkish television channels producing dramas include [[Turkish Radio and Television Corporation|TRT]], [[Kanal D]], [[Show TV]], [[Star TV (Turkish TV channel)|Star TV]], [[ATV (Turkish TV channel)|ATV]], [[Now (Turkish TV channel)|Now]], [[TV8 (Turkish TV channel)|TV8]], and [[Kanal 7]].<ref name="htssc">{{cite web|title=Turkish 'TV series spring' continues|url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkish-tv-series-spring-continues.aspx?pageID=238&nid=32562|publisher=Hürriyet Daily News|date=2012-10-17|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924135007/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkish-tv-series-spring-continues.aspx?pageID=238&nid=32562|archive-date=2015-09-24}}</ref> The Turkish TV series market is characterized by intense local competition; out of the around 70 series produced annually in the country, only around 10% of them go on to a second season. Many are taken off air after running a few episodes without even completing their first season.<ref name="TRT World">{{cite web |last1=Selvi |first1=Murat |title=There is Still Hope for Turkish Drama |url=https://researchcentre.trtworld.com/publications/analysis/there-is-still-hope-for-turkish-drama/ |website=TRT World}}</ref><ref name="ttvmn">{{cite web|title=The Heyday of Turkish Content|url=http://www.ttvmedianews.com/scripts/templates/estilo_nota.asp?nota=eng%2FDistribuci%F3n%2FMercados%2F2012%2F10_Octubre%2F15_turquia_mipcom|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130216224655/http://www.ttvmedianews.com/scripts/templates/estilo_nota.asp?nota=eng/Distribuci%F3n/Mercados/2012/10_Octubre/15_turquia_mipcom|url-status=usurped|archive-date=2013-02-16|publisher=ttvMediaNews|date=2012-10-10}}</ref> Each episode of a Turkish drama is typically between 120 and 150 minutes in length, excluding advertisements. However, this does not apply to internet series.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://t24.com.tr/haber/sektor-calisanlarinin-gozunden-turk-dizileri-neden-bu-kadar-uzun,953151 | title=Sektör çalışanlarının gözünden: Türk dizileri neden bu kadar uzun? }}</ref>

Rapid content production has led to a perceived decline in quality. Some also complain that recent shows are produced for the international market and do not cater sufficiently to Turkish tastes. Furthermore, those working on such series, including actors, set designers, screenwriters, and costume designers, often have to work ceaselessly.

Turkish dramas tend to be inoffensive with widespread cultural appeal. They are exported to many countries, particularly in South America and Asia. ''[[Çalıkuşu (TV series)|Çalıkuşu]]'' was the first Turkish TV series to be exported internationally in 1986 to the [[Soviet Union]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://trend.mynet.com/2000li-yillara-damga-vurmus-20-efsane-yerli-dizi-1056319|title=2000li Yıllara Damga Vurmuş 20 Efsane Yerli Dizi|first=Erol|last=Egemen|website=mynet.com|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160601161251/http://trend.mynet.com/2000li-yillara-damga-vurmus-20-efsane-yerli-dizi-1056319|archive-date=2016-06-01}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kanald.ro/erkan-petekkaya-tuba-buyukustun-kenan-imirzalioglu-cansu-dere-creatorii-propriului-miracol-iata-cum-au-stralucit-indragitii-actori-turci-pe-covorul-rosu-al-galei-altin-kelebek-17460741|title=Erkan Petekkaya, Tuba Buyukustun, Kenan Imirzalioglu, Cansu Dere, creatorii propriului miracol! Iata cum au stralucit indragitii actori turci, pe covorul rosu al Galei "Altin Kelebek"!|website=kanald.ro|date=12 December 2017 |url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171212112225/http://www.kanald.ro/erkan-petekkaya-tuba-buyukustun-kenan-imirzalioglu-cansu-dere-creatorii-propriului-miracol-iata-cum-au-stralucit-indragitii-actori-turci-pe-covorul-rosu-al-galei-altin-kelebek-17460741|archive-date=2017-12-12}}</ref> Turkish television shows are almost always dubbed or subtitled in multiple languages to accommodate the target country. The success of Turkish TV has also boosted tourism, as visitors are eager to visit the locations used in their favorite shows.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/programmes/fast_track/9776435.stm |title=Fast Track - Desperate soap star for a day |work=BBC News |date=2012-12-21 |access-date=2013-01-15 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130117194441/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/programmes/fast_track/9776435.stm |archive-date=2013-01-17 }}</ref> The sudden and massive international popularity of Turkish TV dramas since the 2000s has been widely analyzed as a [[social phenomenon]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Alzafeeri|first=Ahmad|title=Turkish Soap Opera and Kuwaiti audiences|url=http://www.aber.ac.uk/en/tfts/current-student/phd-mphil/phd-research/ahmad-alzafeeri/|publisher=Aberystwyth University|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120918081919/http://www.aber.ac.uk/en/tfts/current-student/phd-mphil/phd-research/ahmad-alzafeeri/|archive-date=2012-09-18}}</ref>

== Production ==
Production of Turkish television dramas is generally quite expensive, with a typical episode costing around 600,000 TL in 2016 (4,540,000 as of 2024) or around $200,000 at the time. Most of the budget is spent on production design, costumes, technical equipment and cast. Most series produce around 40 episodes during their run.<ref name="middleeasteye.net"/>

In the late 2000s, an episode of a Turkish television drama would typically last an average of 60 minutes. By 2010, this had risen to 90 minutes, and by 2016 to 130 minutes, leading to longer working hours, with crews having to work for 18 hours per day. This translates into around 5,200 hours of domestic TV content broadcast yearly. Meriç Demiray, a [[screenwriter]] who has written hundreds of pages for episodes since the early 2000s, commented in 2016 that "it was wonderful until about 10 years ago. Then I had to write a 60-minute episode per week, as opposed to today's 130-plus minutes. It has become a very mechanical and uninteresting process, just a question of keeping the melodrama going." He adds this has driven away the industry's most experienced professionals and that wages have not gone up much. Actor Kanbolat Görkem Arslan also said in 2016 that "compared to cinema or theatre there's no depth expected from a performance; the emotional curve of a character is not consistent from beginning to end. A character can change any minute according to audience reception."<ref name="middleeasteye.net"/>

Çağrı Vila Lostuvalı, 10 years in the business and four as a director, adds: "To deliver one episode per week, our crews work up to 18 hours a day. This job eats up our entire lives."<ref name="middleeasteye.net" /> According to Şükrü Avşar, one of the leading Turkish TV show producers and director of Avşar Film, some episodes need between 15 and 20 days of work to get satisfying results.<ref>Dizi Ekonomisi, from Sokagin Ekonomisi, broadcast on Turkish television channel NTV in 2016.</ref>

The average season length of a Turkish drama is around 35-40 episodes.<ref name=":2">{{cite web |url=https://www2.deloitte.com/content/dam/Deloitte/tr/Documents/technology-media-telecommunications/tr-web-tv-series-sector-in-turkey.pdf |title=World's most colorful screen - TV series sector in Turkey |date=August 2014 |access-date=2016-09-02 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160321172631/https://www2.deloitte.com/content/dam/Deloitte/tr/Documents/technology-media-telecommunications/tr-web-tv-series-sector-in-turkey.pdf |archive-date=2016-03-21 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Konuşlu |first1=Fırat |title=Production and labor process of the contemporary Turkish private television series |journal=Middle East Technical University |date=September 2012 |page=4 |url=https://etd.lib.metu.edu.tr/upload/12614688/index.pdf}}</ref>{{needs update|date=April 2026}} New episodes are filmed 6 days a week to keep up with the demanding production schedule, and crews can work up to 18 hours a day.<ref name="middleeasteye.net">{{cite web|url=http://www.middleeasteye.net/in-depth/features/turkish-tv-series-surge-popularity-worldwide-127494716#.dpuf|title=Turkish dramas conquer the world|website=middleeasteye.net|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417125614/http://www.middleeasteye.net/in-depth/features/turkish-tv-series-surge-popularity-worldwide-127494716#.dpuf|archive-date=2016-04-17}}</ref>{{update inline|date=March 2026}}

Episodes are generally much longer than those of Western series, with 60% of series running between 120 and 180 minutes per episode including advertisements.<ref name=":2" />{{rp|10}} When Turkish series are run in other markets such as the Balkans and southeastern Europe, episodes are usually split into shorter segments, usually not exceeding 60 minutes.{{citation needed|date=March 2026}}

== History ==
{{Update section|date=November 2020}}
Turkey's first TV series was ''Aşk-ı Memnu'', which was produced in 1974. It was adapted from [[Aşk-ı Memnu (novel)|the eponymous 1899 novel]] by [[Halid Ziya Uşaklıgil]]. The series was released on TRT, the public broadcaster of Turkey. The era of TV dramas on TRT alone continued until 1986 and is referred to in Turkey as the "single channel period" ({{Langx|tr|tek kanal dönemi}}), and the shows themselves are called the "old TRT series" ({{Langx|tr|eski TRT dizileri}}). TRT was known for its adaptations of Turkish classic novels into historical TV miniseries.<ref>{{cite web|title=Türkiyenin İlk Yerli Dizisini Çeken Halit Refiğ Yaşamını Yitirdi - Televizyon Dizisi|url=http://www.televizyondizisi.com/turkiyenin-ilk-yerli-dizisini-ceken-halit-refig-yasamini-yitirdi/5484/20/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160617195424/http://www.televizyondizisi.com/turkiyenin-ilk-yerli-dizisini-ceken-halit-refig-yasamini-yitirdi/5484/20/|archive-date=2016-06-17|website=www.televizyondizisi.com}}</ref>

Turkish [[Yeşilçam]] films (named after the eponymous Yeşilçam Street where many film studios were headquartered, similar to ''[[Cinema of the United States|Hollywood]]'') were more popular at the time. Yeşilçam stars did not play in TV series.{{citation needed|date=March 2026}}

Other Turkish TV channels appeared in the 1990s, and TV production increased as a result.<ref>{{cite web|title=90'larda soluksuz izlediğimiz 30 efsane dizi|url=http://www.sabah.com.tr/galeri/magazin/90larda-soluksuz-izledigimiz-30-efsane-dizi|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160522114618/http://www.sabah.com.tr/galeri/magazin/90larda-soluksuz-izledigimiz-30-efsane-dizi|archive-date=2016-05-22|access-date=2016-05-12}}</ref>

Turkish TV series produced between 2000 and 2005 were between 60 and 80 minutes in length. Screenwriters could not finish scripts on time. Because of this, soundtrack music was added to scenes. It was widely successful, and Turkish TV series changed into one long music video.{{clarify|date=February 2026}}

Turkish TV series between 2005–2010 were, on average, 90 minutes in length. TV series became more popular than Turkish cinema, which mostly consisted of festival movies and comedy movies.

Adaptations of Turkish classic novels began to be produced. Authors whose works were commonly adapted included [[Reşat Nuri Güntekin]], [[Orhan Kemal]], [[Halid Ziya Uşaklıgil]], [[Peyami Safa]], [[Ayşe Kulin]], [[Ahmet Ümit]], [[Nermin Bezmen]], [[Hande Altaylı]], and [[Elif Şafak]]. However, these adaptations usually transformed the stories from their late 18th- to 20th-century settings to contemporary times.<ref>{{cite web|last=Şentürk
|first=Semiha|title=Ekranın 'DİZİ DİZİ' romanları|url=http://www.milliyet.com.tr/ekranin-dizi-dizi-romanlari-kitap-1212854/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310170745/http://www.milliyet.com.tr/ekranin-dizi-dizi-romanlari-kitap-1212854/|archive-date=2016-03-10|website=milliyet.com.tr|date=18 June 2012 }}</ref>{{Citation needed|date=November 2023}}

In the 2010s, series ranged from 120 to 150 minutes in length on average, meaning an episode of a Turkish TV series is like a feature-length movie. The series range from period drama, modern-absurd comedy, crime, to romantic comedy. The most watched comedy series were ''[[Avrupa Yakası]]'' (2004–2009), ''[[Leyla and Mecnun|Leyla ile Mecnun]]'' (2011–2013), ''[[Kardeş Payı]]'' (2014–2015), ''[[İşler Güçler]]'' (2012–2013), [[1 erkek 1 Kadın|''1 Erkek 1 Kadın'']] (2008–2015), ''[[Yalan Dünya]]'' (2012–2014),<ref>{{cite web|title=免费任你躁国语自产在线播放_一女两男3p黑人视频_国产毛片农村妇女系列福利片_最新的黄色网址|url=http://www.bugazete.com/m/magazin/dizilerin-110-120-dakika-olmasi-manyaklik-h47009.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160513174445/http://www.bugazete.com/m/magazin/dizilerin-110-120-dakika-olmasi-manyaklik-h47009.html|archive-date=2016-05-13|access-date=2016-05-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=sitesi|first=milliyet.com.tr Türkiye'nin lider haber|title=60 DAKİKALIK DİZİ GELİYOR - Sina Koloğlu - Milliyet.com.tr|url=http://www.milliyet.com.tr/60-dakikalik-dizi-geliyor/magazin/ydetay/2203156/default.htm|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160515150939/http://www.milliyet.com.tr/60-dakikalik-dizi-geliyor/magazin/ydetay/2203156/default.htm|archive-date=2016-05-15|website=milliyet.com.tr|date=2 March 2016 }}</ref> ''[[Tatlı Hayat]]'' (2001–2004) and ''[[Belalı Baldız]]'' (2005–2006).{{citation needed|date=March 2026}}

==Storytelling of Turkish TV series==

===Censorship, bans and self-censorship in Turkish TV series===
In Turkey, the [[Radio and Television Supreme Council]] (RTÜK) regulates television channels. If the council deems a channel's content to be obscene, illegal, disruptive, or divisive, it may fine, suspend, or close the channel by revoking its license. Therefore, TV channels must pay close attention to their content. Punishments are often given for content that goes against the general moral code. Forbidden content is generally not shown on television; however, if it is shown, it is censored. However, the boundaries of what is considered immoral are often unclear and subjective. Therefore, what deserves punishment and what does not is controversial. For this reason, screenwriters have adopted self-censorship. According to one anonymous screenwriter, scenes involving alcohol or sexuality receive more attention than scenes involving abuse or violence.<ref>{{cite news |date=5 August 2018 |title=TV dizilerinin perde arkası: Sansür ve otosansür |language=tr |trans-title=Behind the scenes of TV series: Censorship and self-censorship |work=[[Deutsche Welle]] |url=https://www.dw.com/tr/tv-dizilerinin-perde-arkası-sansür-ve-otosansür/a-44947125}}</ref>

*Cursing is censored in TV shows. Cursing is either suppressed by a beep or the sound is muted. If the curse is long, the scene may be cut completely.
*Making love and kissing scenes are sensitive subjects. It is not forbidden to show, but the boundaries are not sharp either.
*TV series are also shown by censoring alcohol, drugs and cigarettes, and encouraging the use of these substances is prohibited.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://halkweb.com.tr/cukura-alkollu-icki-cezasi/|title=Çukura Alkollü Içki Cezası|date=10 December 2017|accessdate=29 December 2023}}</ref>
*Homosexual intercourse is a sensitive subject.
*Blood is also censored in TV series; scenes such as blood, body dismemberment and extreme violence are prohibited.<ref>{{cite web |date=12 January 2015 |title=RTÜK'ten Diriliş Ertuğrul'a ceza |url=https://m.aksam.com.tr/televizyon/rtukten-dirilis-ertugrula-ceza/haber-371781 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170601071759/https://m.aksam.com.tr/televizyon/rtukten-dirilis-ertugrula-ceza/haber-371781 |archive-date=2017-06-01}}</ref>
*Insulting and humiliating religion, nation, national values and state administrators is prohibited in TV series.<ref>{{cite web |date=17 February 2020 |title=RTÜK'ten vatandaşların şikayet ettiği dizilere ceza |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/kelebek/televizyon/rtukten-vatandaslarin-sikayet-ettigi-dizilere-ceza-41449328 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200421015533/https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/kelebek/televizyon/rtukten-vatandaslarin-sikayet-ettigi-dizilere-ceza-41449328 |archive-date=2020-04-21}}</ref>

===Values shown in Turkish series===
Turkish shows have become popular in the Balkan region because they depict Islam, democracy, modernity, and traditionalism. Free of violence and obscene language, these shows appeal to viewers with their realistic characters and straightforward plots.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ely |first1=Nicole |title=Much-loved Soaps Polish Turkey’s Image in Balkans |url=https://balkaninsight.com/2019/06/18/much-loved-soaps-polish-turkeys-image-in-balkans/bi/ |website=Balkan Insight |access-date=18 March 2026 |date=18 June 2019}}</ref> They evoke nostalgia for family values that people in the region have lost.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 2013 |title=Turks Bewitch the Balkans with Their Addictive Soaps |url=https://balkaninsight.com/2013/05/01/turks-bewitch-the-balkans-with-their-addictive-soaps/}}</ref>

According to Izzet Pinto, the head of Istanbul-based powerhouse distributor Global Agency, it is the "combination of family-based stories with big talents and directors, and great music" that attracts audiences so widely, and Turkish culture as a whole, which he calls both "modern, but at the same time, also very traditional".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.trtworld.com/magazine/what-s-behind-the-meteoric-rise-of-turkish-dramas-in-the-middle-east-54726|title=What's behind the meteoric rise of Turkish dramas in the Middle East|first=Priyanka|last=Navani|website=What's behind the meteoric rise of Turkish dramas in the Middle East|accessdate=29 December 2023}}</ref>

Contrary to showing elements that are not accepted in the region in Western shows, similar social problems are told within acceptable limits in Turkish TV series.<ref>{{cite news |date=27 June 2013 |title=The rise of Turkish soap power |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/magazine-22282563}}</ref>

For Latin America, the reasons were the cultural similarities, emphasis on family values, popularity of family viewing, attractive people, and picturesque locations.<ref>{{cite news |date=7 September 2016 |title=An unlikely story: Why do South Americans love Turkish TV? |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/business-37284938}}</ref>

''[[Fatmagül'ün Suçu Ne?]]'' tells the story of a courageous woman who overcame challenges faced by women around the world and achieved success in many countries.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 2012 |title=Challenge of the Turkish soap operas |url=https://gulfnews.com/business/challenge-of-the-turkish-soap-operas-1.1002249}}</ref>

===Criticism===
Some religious authorities in the Middle East have condemned Turkish TV series as "immoral" due to taboo-breaking scenes, including those involving [[premarital sex]], [[love triangle]]s, and nudity. In some cases, the series have been banned altogether.<ref>{{cite web |date=29 June 2012 |title=Turkish TV - a device for social change in the Arab world? |url=https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2012/06/29/turkish-tv-a-device-for-social-change-in-the-arab-world}}</ref>

== Social and political discourse ==
Owing to their popularity, the government of Turkey has used Turkish television series as a propaganda outlet. Every year, the Turkish public broadcaster [[TRT]] commissions several series that depict the history and values of the Turkish nation from a conservative Islamic perspective. {{lang|tr|[[Diriliş: Ertuğrul]]}} (''Resurrection: Ertuğrul''), a historical drama inspired by the life of [[Ertuğrul Bey]], son of [[Osman I]], founder of the [[Ottoman Empire]], is a prominent example of this.

State productions are also used to disparage or vilify critics. For instance, the TRT production {{lang|tr|Metamorfoz}} depicts [[Osman Kavala]], a businessman and political activist who has been imprisoned since 2017, as an enemy of the state.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Topcu |first1=Elmas |last2=Ünker |first2=Pelin |title=Popular Turkish TV series a mix of commentary, propaganda |url=https://www.dw.com/en/popular-turkish-tv-series-a-mix-of-commentary-propaganda/a-71374906 |website=[[Deutsche Welle]] |access-date=23 March 2026}}</ref>

Journalist [[Nevşin Mengü]] said of the series ''Kızılcık Şerbeti'', which depicts a cultural conflict between conservatives and [[secularism in Turkey|secularists]]: "In this series, all the women fall head over heels for the Islamist men. The secular men are clueless and unable to provide for them. They wander around aimlessly. In contrast, the Islamist men provide for their families and earn money. Though it appears secular, it is actually propaganda for political Islam."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://esitlikadaletkadin.org/nevsin-mengu-ve-orhan-sener-deliormanli-kizilcik-serbetini-tartisiyor-siyasal-islam-propagandasi/|title=Nevşin Mengü ve Orhan Şener Deliormanlı 'Kızılcık Şerbeti'ni Tartışıyor: 'Siyasal İslam Propagandası' - SES Eşitlik, Adalet, Kadın Platformu|date=19 March 2024|website=esitlikadaletkadin.org}}</ref>

According to the Turkish University Women's Association, eight out of eleven TV series depict oppression and violence against women. These series normalize polygamy, learned helplessness among female characters, dirty competition and intrigue between men and women, gender inequality, cultural bigotry, neighborhood pressures, patriarchal mentalities, male-dominated cultures, acceptance of violence as part of men's nature, and social violence. These issues are normalized by presenting them in tense, intriguing scenarios that heighten their impact and by concluding episodes with exciting events that draw in the audience. Some series even legitimize these issues. These series act as role models, instilling a violent communication style in vulnerable audience members who cannot correctly interpret the content.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://kisadalga.net/haber/detay/turkiyede-dizi-raporu-cok-eslilik-normallestiriliyor-kadina-siddet-ve-baski-ilk-sirada_96509|title=Türkiye'de dizi raporu: Çok eşlilik normalleştiriliyor, kadına şiddet ve baskı ilk sırada|date=28 March 2024|website=Kısa Dalga}}</ref>

Asked why he was less visible in recent media, veteran actor [[Şevket Altuğ]] said: "The values of Turkish society have changed. The types of available work have also changed. Therefore, I can't participate in any series with the current content. They may interpret this as criticism or blame it on my age. All of this media shows guns, rifles, and people killing each other. All the men have beards. In our time, men only grew beards if their roles required it. I can't be part of this environment. In our work, we tried to teach society about love, tolerance, living together, and solidarity. If I were offered a role in such a production, I could play it despite my age. However, I don't think I will encounter such an opportunity."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.diken.com.tr/oyuncu-sevket-altugun-uzaklasma-nedeni-toplumun-degerleri-degisti-bu-ortamda-olamam/|title=Oyuncu Şevket Altuğ'un 'uzaklaşma' nedeni: Toplumun değerleri değişti, bu ortamda olamam — Diken|website=www.diken.com.tr |date=13 April 2018 }}</ref>

== Business and finance ==
Turkish shows began expanding internationally in 1999, but only started to gain popularity in the early 21st century. In order to be able to produce high-quality content and to be competitive with the non-Turkish shows that were gaining traction in [[Turkey]], more money was needed, and the financial deficit was made up for through expansion to non-domestic markets.<ref name=":022" /> The [[Government of Turkey|Turkish government]] also played a role in motivating international expansion, creating incentives by granting awards and support to the companies that are most effective in exporting worldwide.<ref name=":022" />

In 2017, Turkish TV exports earned $350 million, officially marking the country as the second largest drama exporter in the world behind the United States.<ref name=":022" /><ref name=":122" /> According to the Secretary General of the TEA, Bader Arslan, Turkey's yearly income from TV exports will exceed 1 billion U.S. dollars by 2023.<ref name=":122" />
Turkish series are exported to approximately 140 countries around the world.

Today, there are about 45 production companies and 150 active film directors in Turkey. The production cost of a series may vary between 78,000 and 520,000 U.S. dollars (for the most famous ones).<ref>Dizi Ekonomisi(Sokağın Ekonomisi, NTV, 2016);</ref>

==Streaming ==
Turkish streaming began in the late 2010s. Foreign streaming platforms include [[Netflix]], [[Disney+]], [[Prime Video]], [[HBO Max]], and [[MUBI]], and notable native platforms include tabii, [[Exxen]], and GAİN.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ntv.com.tr/n-life/dizi-haber/trtden-uluslararasi-dijital-platform-geliyor-tabii,fv1AmqBsuk-4y-A_F5Pf_w|title=TRT'den uluslararası dijital platform geliyor: Tabii|website=www.ntv.com.tr|accessdate=29 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Sharpe |first1=Kenan Behzat |title=The new generation streams with GAİN and Exxen in Turkey |url=https://www.duvarenglish.com/the-new-generation-streams-with-gain-and-exxen-in-turkey-article-55885 |access-date=8 April 2026 |work=[[Gazete Duvar|Duvar English]] |date=16 January 2021}}</ref><ref name="bianet">{{cite news |title=RTÜK fines streaming platforms, orders removal of films over 'anti-family' content |url=https://bianet.org/haber/rtuk-fines-streaming-platforms-orders-removal-of-films-over-anti-family-content-311665 |access-date=8 April 2026 |work=[[Bianet]] |date=18 September 2025}}</ref>

=== Netflix ===
Since the late 2010s, American streaming service [[Netflix]] has produced original Turkish dramas and films for its platform.{{citation needed|date=April 2026}} Its first original Turkish series, ''[[The Protector (Turkish TV series)|The Protector]]'' ({{lang|tr|Hakan: Muhafız}}), was released on 14 December 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=Netflix airs first original Turkish series |url=https://www.dailysabah.com/arts-culture/2018/12/14/netflix-airs-first-original-turkish-series |access-date=8 April 2026 |work=[[Daily Sabah]] |date=14 December 2018}}</ref> According to Danielle Turchiano of ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'', Netflix is the only streaming platform to buy substantial amounts of Turkish television series.<ref name=":22">{{Cite news |last=Turchiano |first=Danielle |date=2018-04-09 |title=Turkey Experiences Its Own Wave of Peak TV |language=en-US |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|url=https://variety.com/2018/tv/features/turkey-experiences-its-own-wave-of-peak-tv-1202746009/ |access-date=2018-11-26}}</ref>{{needs update|date=March 2026}} ''[[Fatma (TV series)|Fatma]]'', ''[[Love 101 (TV series)|Love 101]]'', ''[[50M2|50m2]]'', ''[[Ethos (TV series)|Bir Başkadır]]'', ''[[Rise of Empires: Ottoman]]'', and ''[[The Gift (Turkish TV series)|The Gift]]'' are among the Netflix series that gathered success in Turkey as well as many other countries.{{citation needed|date=April 2026}}

Several Turkish television series have ranked among the most-watched Netflix series worldwide at various times. For instance, ''[[The Club (Turkish TV series)|The Club]]'' ({{lang|tr|Kulüp}}) was watched for a total of 7,860,000 hours during the week of 8–14 November, ranking 8th on Netflix's non-English language series list, thus making it one of the top 10 most-watched series.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cumhuriyet.com.tr/yasam/kulup-ilk-haftasinda-netflixin-en-cok-izlenen-dizileri-arasina-girdi-1885535|title = Kulüp, ilk haftasında Netflix'in en çok izlenen dizileri arasına girdi| date=17 November 2021 }}</ref>

=== Disney+ ===
The first Turkish original drama for [[Disney+]], ''Kaçış'', aired on 14 June 2022.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://whatsondisneyplus.com/first-look-at-turkish-disney-original-series-kacis/ | title=First Look at Turkish Disney+ Original Series 'Kaçış' | date=24 April 2022 }}</ref>

=== Censorship ===
Turkish streaming has come under the scrutiny of Turkish state media regulator [[RTÜK]]. For example, as part of the 2025 "Year of the Family" initiative, it fined Disney+, Prime Video, Netflix, HBO Max, and MUBI for series that "promote homosexuality," "disregard family values," and "conflict with the shared values of society."<ref name="bianet"/>

==International popularity==
{{Update|part=section|date=October 2021|reason=especially for Afghanistan following the takeover by the Taliban}}

Due to a long history of state oversight, Turkish television series have largely removed any content that the government might find objectionable. As a result, they lack political narratives or references. This has led producers to innovate by focusing on universal human dramas with simple plotlines. The stories mostly fall into non-Turkey-specific archetypes, such as love triangles, family feuds, and revenge sagas. As no prior knowledge of Turkey is required to understand these stories, the series have gained widespread popularity around the world.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pessey |first1=Arnaud |title=How Turkish TV Became the World’s Second-Biggest Export |url=https://www.gqmiddleeast.com/article/how-turkish-tv-became-the-worlds-second-biggest-export |website=GQ Middle East}}</ref>

=== Turkic countries ===
There are varying levels of [[mutual intelligibility]] among the various [[Turkic languages]], especially among [[Turkish language|Turkish]] and [[Azerbaijani language|Azerbaijani]], which are both [[Oghuz languages]]. Thus, in [[Azerbaijan]], the shows are not subtitled because the general public can understand them. Turkish shows are also aired in the ''[[de facto]]'' independent Turkish-speaking state of [[Northern Cyprus]].{{citation needed|date=April 2026}}

Turkic languages more distant from Turkish, such as [[Turkmen language|Turkmen]], [[Kazakh language|Kazakh]], [[Kyrgyz language|Kyrgyz]] and [[Uzbek language|Uzbek]], require subtitles as they have a lesser degree of mutual intelligibility. Turkish TV series are popular in the Turkic countries of [[Central Asia]].<ref>{{cite web |date=18 August 2013 |title=Fatih Altaylı - Türk dizileri niye başarılı? - HABERTÜRK |url=http://www.haberturk.com/yazarlar/fatih-altayli-1001/869873-turk-dizileri-niye-basarili |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160808065336/http://www.haberturk.com/yazarlar/fatih-altayli-1001/869873-turk-dizileri-niye-basarili |archive-date=2016-08-08 |website=haberturk.com}}</ref>
An Uzbek remake of the Turkish drama ''Kırgın Çiçekler'' aired as Бир ками тўлмаган дунё in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sod.uz/bir-kami-tolmagan-dunyo-ozbek-serial-%D0%B1%D0%B8%D1%80-%D0%BA%D0%B0%D0%BC%D0%B8-%D1%82%D1%9E%D0%BB%D0%BC%D0%B0%D0%B3%D0%B0%D0%BD-%D0%B4%D1%83%D0%BD%D1%91-%D1%83%D0%B7%D0%B1%D0%B5%D0%BA-%D1%81-127_5d30d6752.html|title=Bir kami to'lmagan dunyo (O'zbek serial) &#124; Бир ками тўлмаган дунё (узбек сериал) 128-qism|accessdate=29 December 2023}}{{dead link|date=April 2026}}</ref>

=== Arab world ===
Turkish TV series began to rise in popularity across the Arab world in 2008, when [[MBC Group]] began to acquire the rights for the series. MBC is a popular Saudi Arabian broadcasting network. Instead of dubbing the shows in [[classical Arabic]], they were rendered in [[Syrian Arabic]], a dialectal variant readily understood by ordinary viewers across the Middle East.<ref name=":1">{{cite journal |last1=Buccianti |first1=Alexandra |title=Turkish soap operas in the Arab world: social liberation or cultural alienation? |journal=[[Arab Media & Society]] |date=20 March 2010 |issue=10 |doi=10.70090/AB10TSOA}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=13 September 2019 |title=How Turkish TV is taking over the world |url=https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2019/sep/13/turkish-tv-magnificent-century-dizi-taking-over-world |website=The Guardian}}</ref>

Led by ''[[Gümüş (TV series)|''Gümüş'']]'' (known as ''Noor'' in the Arab market), a wave of Turkish melodramas made their way onto Arab televisions, wielding a kind of soft power. The show violated the local conservative cultural norms, showing some Muslim characters drinking wine with dinner and engaging in premarital sex. The Arabic-dubbed finale of the Turkish TV series ''[[Gümüş (TV series)|Gümüş]]'' (''Silver''), aired on 30 August 2008, was watched by 85 million viewers. In 2008, the [[Grand Mufti of Saudi Arabia|grand mufti of Saudi Arabia]] [[Sheikh Abdulaziz al-Sheikh|Abdulaziz al-Sheikh]] issued a [[fatwa]] against channels that broadcast ''Gümüş'', saying anyone who broadcast it was "an enemy of God and his Prophet".<ref name=":1" /> Other Turkish dramas aired in the Arab world include ''[[Asi (TV series)|Asi]]'', ''[[Kurtlar Vadisi]]'', ''[[Menekşe ile Halil]]'', and ''[[Yabancı Damat]]''.<ref>{{cite web |date=19 November 2009 |title=Ortadoğu'da hangi Türk dizileri izlenme rekoru kırıyor? |url=https://www.medyafaresi.com/haber/ortadoguda-hangi-turk-dizileri-izlenme-rekoru-kiriyor/33494 |accessdate=2021-11-25 |publisher=MedyaFaresi.com}}</ref>

In March 2018, MBC pulled all Turkish dramas off the air. Danielle Turchiano of [[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] considers this a result of the political tensions between [[Saudi Arabia]] and Turkey. The head of the Turkish Sales Company Global Agency, İzzet Pinto, said that he believed this was a political decision against the Turkish government.<ref name=":22" />

In 2019, Mashaer became the first Arabic TV series to be produced with a Turkish scriptwriting and directing team. This was done to capitalize on the popularity of Turkish TV series in Arab countries.<ref>{{cite web |date= |title="مشاعر"... مسلسل تونسي جزائري بتقنيات تركية |url=https://www.alaraby.co.uk/%22%D9%85%D8%B4%D8%A7%D8%B9%D8%B1%22-%D9%85%D8%B3%D9%84%D8%B3%D9%84-%D8%AA%D9%88%D9%86%D8%B3%D9%8A-%D8%AC%D8%B2%D8%A7%D8%A6%D8%B1%D9%8A-%D8%A8%D8%AA%D9%82%D9%86%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%AA-%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%83%D9%8A%D8%A9 |accessdate=2021-11-25 |publisher=Alaraby.co.uk |language=ar}}</ref>

''[[İstanbullu Gelin]]'' (''Bride from Istanbul'') was adapted into an Arab series titled ''Bride from Beirut'', which aired on MBC in 2019. An Arabic remake, ''[[Ala Al Hilwa Wa Al Morra]]'' of ''[[İyi Günde Kötü Günde]]'', was made in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |date=30 August 2021 |title=İyi Günde Kötü Günde'nin Arapça versiyonu çekildi! |url=https://televizyongazetesi.com/iyi-gunde-kotu-gundenin-arapca-versiyonu-cekildi/1292746}}</ref> The MBC-linked Arab digital platform Shahid is still showing Turkish dramas despite the tension.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://shahid.mbc.net/|title=MBC Shahid|website=Shahid|accessdate=29 December 2023}}</ref>{{original research inline|date=March 2026}} During Ramadan in 2020 and 2021, channels broadcast many Turkish series in Lebanon.<ref>{{cite web |date=5 May 2020 |title=Lebanese escape from economic crisis, pandemic stress with Turkish TV series {{!}} Daily Sabah |url=https://www.dailysabah.com/arts/cinema/lebanese-escape-from-economic-crisis-pandemic-stress-with-turkish-tv-series |website=[[Daily Sabah]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=2021-04-20 |title=Türk dizileri bu ramazanda da Lübnan'da en çok izlenenlerin başında geliyor |url=https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/dunya/turk-dizileri-bu-ramazanda-da-lubnanda-en-cok-izlenenlerin-basinda-geliyor/2214287 |accessdate=2021-11-25 |publisher=Aa.com.tr}}</ref>

''Hab Mlouk'', an Algerian-Tunisian remake of ''Afili Aşk'', aired in April 2022.<ref>{{cite tweet |number=1510999242927714307 |user=TvDunyasii |title=Başrollerinde Burcu Özberk ve Çağlar Ertuğrul'un olduğu #AfiliAşk'ın Cezayir-Tunus ortak yapımı uyarlaması yapıldı.… |date=4 April 2022}}</ref>

MBC Group signed a five-year output and co-development deal with Medyapım and fellow Turkish company Ay Yapım, in October 2022. It also includes a pact to exchange know-how and co-develop original Arabic-language content for the MENA region, to be filmed in Saudi Arabia.<ref>{{cite news |title=MBC Group to adapt Doctor Foster, signs Turkish drama volume deal |newspaper=C21Media |url=https://www.c21media.net/news/mbc-group-to-adapt-doctor-foster-signs-volume-turkish-drama-deal/}}</ref>

Many Turkish actors and actresses received awards from award ceremonies in the Arab world.<ref>{{cite web |date=10 February 2019 |title=Engin Altan Düzyatan'a uluslararası ödül! |url=https://www.milliyet.com.tr/cadde/engin-altan-duzyatana-uluslararasi-odul-2825393}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ranini.tv/haber/15545/1/beren-saat-ve-murat-yildirima-murex-dor-2016dan-odul-geldi|title=Beren Saat ve Murat Yıldırım'a Murex D'or 2016'dan ödül geldi!|website=ranini.tv|accessdate=29 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ntv.com.tr/n-life/magazin/sevval-sama-lubnanda-en-iyi-kadin-oyuncu-odulu,XOMALlQCRUaw7bcx02JXXw|title=Şevval Sam'a Lübnan'da En İyi Kadın Oyuncu ödülü|website=www.ntv.com.tr|accessdate=29 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fox.com.tr/Yasak-Elma/haber/3495/Yasak-Elma-nin-sevilen-oyuncusu-Eda-Ece-cok-ozel-bir-odule-layik-goruldu|title=Yasak Elma - Yasak Elma'nın sevilen oyuncusu Eda Ece çok özel bir ödüle layık görüldü! &#124; FOX|accessdate=29 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=8 November 2022 |title=Turkish actress Birce Akalay dedicates award to slain Iranian women |url=https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2196021/lifestyle}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=29 November 2021 |title=Neslihan Atagül is recognized as Best Actress at the DIAFA Awards |url=https://www.hola.com/us/entertainment/20211129306928/neslihan-atagul-best-actress-diafa-awards/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ntv.com.tr/galeri/yasam/pelin-karahana-buyuk-odul,Ia4sc7i4MUyCPbmCFiCVRw|title=Pelin Karahan'a büyük ödül|website=www.ntv.com.tr|accessdate=29 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ntv.com.tr/galeri/yasam/beyrutta-can-yaman-ve-demet-ozdemir-ruzgari,trfFZzz9x0-f3dBnm-gpZA|title=Beyrut'ta Can Yaman ve Demet Özdemir rüzgarı|website=www.ntv.com.tr|accessdate=29 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Com |first1=Ucankus |url=https://www.ucankus.com/detay/125197/erkan-petekkaya-ortadogu-yu-fethetti-murex-d-or-odul-torenine-katilan-oyuncu-en-begenilen-erkek-oyuncu-ve|title=Erkan Petekkaya Ortadoğuyu fethetti|website=ucankus.com|access-date=29 December 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=22 March 2022 |title=Kanunsuz Topraklar'ın Davut'u Uğur Güneş'e Dubai'de ödül... Büyük başarı |url=https://www.aksam.com.tr/magazin/kanunsuz-topraklarin-davutu-ugur-gunese-dubaide-odul-buyuk-basari/haber-1254087}}</ref>{{excessive citations inline|date=March 2026}}

=== Asia ===

====Afghanistan====

Turkish TV series dubbed in [[Dari|Dari Persian]] have become very popular in Afghanistan, with ratings going higher than the traditional Indian TV series that Afghans watched.{{citation needed|date=April 2026}} {{As of|2012}}, ''Fatmagül'ün Suçu Ne?'' is shown on [[TOLO TV]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Beren Saat Afgan Kadınlarını Uyarıyor|url=http://www.dizifilm.com/haberdetay.asp?newsid=214724|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150926023209/http://www.dizifilm.com/haberdetay.asp?newsid=214724|archive-date=26 September 2015|access-date=15 September 2015|work=Dizisifilm}}</ref> Other series such as ''[[Öyle Bir Geçer Zaman ki|Öyle Bir Geçer Zaman Ki]]'' (''As Time Goes By''), ''[[Beni Affet]]'' (''Forgive Me''), ''[[İffet]]'', ''[[Aşk-ı Memnu (2008 TV series)|Aşk-ı Memnu]]'' (''Forbidden Love''), and ''[[Adını Feriha Koydum]]'' are popular too.<ref>{{cite web|title=TOLO TV|url=http://www.tolo.tv/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150918114056/http://www.tolo.tv/|archive-date=2015-09-18|website=TOLO TV}}</ref>{{non primary source needed|date=April 2026}}

==== Armenia ====
The first Turkish drama to be remade in Armenia was ''[[Ezel (TV series)|Ezel]]'', under the name ''Ancanoty''{{citation needed|date=April 2026}}, by [[Shant TV]], one of the biggest channels in Armenia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/tension-with-armenia-affects-airing-of-tv-show-26085 |title=Tension with Armenia affects airing of TV show |publisher=Hurriyetdailynews.com |date=2012-07-23 |accessdate=2021-11-25}}</ref> The Armenian adaptation of the Turkish series ''[[Endless Love (2015 TV series)|Kara Sevda]]'' was broadcast under the name ''Kayaran'' ({{lang|hy|Կայարանt|}}, 'Station').<ref>{{cite web|last=Center|first=Armenian Information|title=Ժող էտ "Կայարան" սերիալը մի նայեք, լրիիիիվ թուրքական քոփիյա... (Տեսանյութ)|url=http://yn.am/?index&p=73567&l=am|website=yn.am}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title="Կայարան" հեռուստասերիալը թուրքական սերիալի խայտառակ կրկնօրինակում է. քաղաքացիները դժգոհում են (լուսանկար, տեսանյութ)|url=https://past.am/?p=103160&l=am|website=past.am| date=27 June 2023 }}</ref> Turkish series are also watched in the Armenian diaspora in Russia and elsewhere.<ref>{{cite web|author=Varduhi Balyan|url=http://www.agos.com.tr/tr/yazi/17117/turkiye-dizileri-ermenistanda-zirvede |title=Türkiye dizileri Ermenistan'da zirvede |publisher=Agos |date=2016-11-25 |accessdate=2021-11-25}}</ref>

====Bangladesh====

Turkish series began to gain popularity in [[Bangladesh]] with the arrival of ''[[Muhteşem Yüzyıl]]''. Renamed ''[[Sultan Süleyman]]'' after the [[Ottoman sultan]] it depicts, the show aired on [[Deepto TV]], which launched in November 2015. The channel's inaugural program was the first two episodes of the series. It was the first Turkish drama series to air on Bangladeshi television. By the first week of January, the program had earned the second-highest TRP. By the second week, it had reached the top spot among all Bangladeshi TV channels.<ref>{{cite web|date=21 January 2016|title=Deepto TV on top|url=http://www.dhakatribune.com/showtime/2016/jan/21/deepto-tv-top|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160122092704/http://www.dhakatribune.com/showtime/2016/jan/21/deepto-tv-top|archive-date=22 January 2016|access-date=23 January 2016|publisher=Dhaka Tribune}}</ref>

====India====

In September 2015, the first Turkish drama on Indian television, ''[[Adını Feriha Koydum]]'', aired on [[Zindagi (TV channel)|Zindagi]] and became a huge success. The third and final season of the show was broadcast in India in 2016 as "Feriha-New Season" by Zindagi due to overwhelming audience request. ''Fatmagul'ün Suçu Ne?'' is also extremely well received and appreciated by Indian audiences. The show{{which|date=March 2026}} also helped Zindagi to become the number one premium entertainment channel, garnering impressive ratings. The viewership of the channel increased due to this show.{{citation needed|date=March 2026}} ''[[Kuzey Güney]]'', ''Adını Feriha Koydum'', ''[[Aşk Laftan Anlamaz]]'', ''[[Little Lord|Küçük Ağa]]'' are some of the most popular and highest-rated shows in India.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2016-10-03|title=After Pak Show ban, Zindagi Channel to bank on Indian, Turkish content|newspaper=The Indian Express|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/television/after-pak-show-ban-zindagi-channel-to-view-indian-television-content-3063351/|url-status=live|access-date=2016-10-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161020025733/http://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/television/after-pak-show-ban-zindagi-channel-to-view-indian-television-content-3063351/|archive-date=2016-10-20}}</ref> From 25 June 2018, [[StarPlus]] started broadcasting ''Kış Güneşi'' as its first Turkish show dubbed in the Hindi language.<ref>{{Cite news|date=2018-06-13|title=Star Plus UK to air first Turkish fiction 'Winter Sun' this month|language=en-GB|work=BizAsia {{!}} Media, Entertainment, Showbiz, Events and Music|url=https://www.bizasialive.com/star-plus-uk-air-first-turkish-fiction-winter-sun-month/|access-date=2018-08-01}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Turkish Drama Winter Sun set to air on Star India - in the UK|url=http://ecchorights.com/press-releases/127|access-date=2018-08-01|website=ecchorights.com}}</ref>

In the aftermath of the [[2016 Uri attack]], which strained India–Pakistan relations, Pakistani series on Zindagi were replaced by Turkish ones.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Iqbal |first1=Sarmad |title=Turkish Soap Operas And Their Rise In Pakistan To Leave A Legacy – OpEd |url=https://www.eurasiareview.com/23112017-turkish-soap-operas-and-their-rise-in-pakistan-to-leave-a-legacy-oped/ |website=Eurasia Review}}</ref>

''[[Kya Qusoor Hai Amala Ka?]]'' and ''[[Dil Sambhal Jaa Zara]]'', Indian adaptations of ''Fatmagül'ün Suçu Ne?'' and ''Aşk-ı Memnu'', were aired in 2017.<ref name="Mirror adaptation">{{cite news|last1=Coutinho|first1=Natasha|date=22 March 2017|title=From Turkey, with a desi twist|language=en|work=Mumbai Mirror|url=https://mumbaimirror.indiatimes.com/entertainment/tv/from-turkey-with-a-desi-twist/articleshow/57762820.cms|access-date=31 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Laghate|first1=Gaurav|date=27 February 2017|title=Star Plus to reboot afternoon slot with 4 new shows - The Economic Times|work=[[The Economic Times]]|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/media/entertainment/star-plus-to-reboot-afternoon-slot-with-4-new-shows/articleshow/57378471.cms|accessdate=27 February 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=|first=|date=24 October 2017|title=India is progressing and we need to show it on TV: Sanjay|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/india-is-progressing-and-we-need-to-show-it-on-tv-sanjay-117102400740_1.html|access-date=|website=[[Business Standard]]|agency=Press Trust of India}}</ref> ''[[Binbir Gece]]'' was remade as ''[[Katha Ankahee]]'' and aired on [[Sony Entertainment Television]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Katha Ankahee: Is Kathaa's perception of Viaan changing? |url=https://www.indiaforums.com/article/katha-ankahee-is-kathaas-perception-of-viaan-changing_194416#google_vignette |website=India Forums}}</ref>

====Iran====

[[Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting|IRIB]] was one of the first networks to invest in Turkish series. [[IRIB TV3]] used to air ''[[Sırlar Dünyası]]'' (Persian: {{lang|fa|کلید اسرار|italic=yes}}, Kelid-e Asrâr). After the show got extremely popular in Iran during the early 2010s, they were dubbed into [[Persian language|Persian]] by various satellite channels. Among the most popular series were ''[[Aşk-ı Memnu (2008 TV series)|Aşk-ı Memnu]]'' ({{lang|fa|عشق ممنوع|italic=yes}}, 'Eshgh-e Mamnoo'), ''[[Sırlar Dünyası]]'', and ''[[Fatmagül'ün Suçu Ne?]]'' ({{lang|fa|گناه فاطما گل چه بود؟|italic=yes}}, Gonâh-e Fâtmâ Gol Cheh Bood?). Turkish shows lost popularity after the early 2010s when the Iranian government tried to boost their popularity by lifting production restrictions and creating more entertainment content. Turkish shows are often too long to fit into Iranians' daily lives, and they have been accused of promoting disloyalty, anger, and backstabbing.<ref>{{cite web|title=Iranian officials failing to stop of Turkish TV series| date=13 October 2011 |url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/iranian-officials-failing-to-stop-of-turkish-tv-series.aspx?pageID=238&nID=6171&NewsCatID=385|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222161235/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/iranian-officials-failing-to-stop-of-turkish-tv-series.aspx?pageID=238&nID=6171&NewsCatID=385|archive-date=22 December 2015|access-date=16 September 2015|publisher=Hurriyetdailynews}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=March 2026}}

====Israel====
''[[Menekşe ile Halil]]'' was the first Turkish TV series to air in Israel, doing so in 2011.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.haberturk.com/medya/haber/669642-menekse-ile-halil-israilde-patladi | title='Menekşe ile Halil' İsrail'de patladı! | date=15 September 2011 }}</ref> It was dubbed into [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]] and aired five days a week during primetime on Viva.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ntv.com.tr/yasam/israilde-menekse-ile-halil-cilginligi-basladi,9K7-jkW3y0SGA-kv6d0diw | title=İsrail'de 'Menekşe ile Halil' çılgınlığı başladı }}</ref> ''[[İstanbullu Gelin]]'' also received high ratings in Israel, especially among women. The star of the series, [[Özcan Deniz]], performed concerts in Israel, and [[Berkay Hardal]] appeared in Israeli commercials.<ref>{{Cite news|title=The Turks Are Back, and They've Got All of Israel Addicted|url=https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/2019-02-06/ty-article-magazine/.premium/the-bride-of-istanbul-turkey-back-in-israel-and-theyve-got-everyone-addicted/0000017f-db92-db5a-a57f-dbfa8c4d0000|newspaper=Haaretz}}</ref>

====Indonesia====
''Paramparça'' aired on [[ANTV]].<ref>{{cite web |date=6 August 2016 |title=Türk dizisinin büyük başarısı! "Paramparça"ya Endonezya'da büyük ilgi |url=https://www.temizmagazin.com/gundem/turk-dizisinin-buyuk-basarisi-paramparcaya-endonezyada-buyuk-ilgi}}</ref> The Turkish series ''Kırgın Çiçekler'' was broadcast on Indonesia's ANTV channel and became the 'Most Watched' production by female viewers aged 20–29.<ref>{{cite news |title=Endonezya'da en çok izlenen dizi 'Kırgın Çiçekler' |website=Sabah |url=https://www.sabah.com.tr/magazin/2016/10/20/endonezyada-en-cok-izlenen-dizi-kirgin-cicekler}}</ref> Turkish drama ''Elif'' aired in Indonesia, and a local remake was made as ''Elif Indonesia'' on SCTV.<ref>{{cite web |date=2015-11-29 |title=SCTV Siapkan Serial Elif Versi Indonesia - ShowBiz |url=https://www.liputan6.com/showbiz/read/2377566/sctv-siapkan-serial-elif-versi-indonesia |accessdate=2021-11-25 |publisher=Liputan6.com}}</ref>

====Japan====
''[[Magnificent Century]]'' aired on Channel Ginga as {{lang|ja|オスマン帝国外伝～愛と欲望のハレム〜}} in Japan.<ref>{{cite web |title=「オスマン帝国外伝～愛と欲望のハレム～」シーズン4｜チャンネル銀河 |url=https://www.ch-ginga.jp/feature/ottoman/ |website=www.ch-ginga.jp}}</ref> The Japanese broadcaster [[Nippon TV]] has acquired the rights to the Turkish drama series ''Anne'', a remake of the Japanese drama ''[[Mother (Japanese TV series)|Mother]]''. ''Anne'' will air on BS Nippon TV and [[Hulu Japan|Hulu]] in Japan.<ref>{{cite web |date=26 August 2020 |title=Nippon TV Acquires Turkish Remake of Mother |url=https://todotvnews.com/en/nippon-tv-acquires-turkish-remake-of-mother/}}</ref> ''Kadın'', a remake of Japanese drama ''Woman'', won the Special Award (Foreign dramas) at the Tokyo Drama Awards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=International Drama Festival:Foreign Dramas |url=https://j-ba.or.jp/drafes/english/archive/index24.html |accessdate=29 May 2023 |website=j-ba.or.jp}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=8 November 2018 |title='Kadın' dizisine Tokyo'dan ödül! |url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/kelebek/televizyon/kadin-dizisine-tokyodan-odul-41011724 |accessdate=22 November 2023 |website=hurriyet}}</ref>

====Malaysia====
The first Turkish series broadcast on Malaysian National Channel RTM was ''[[Bu Şehir Arkandan Gelecek]]'' (''Heart of the City'').<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ranini.tv/ozel/26746/1/malezya-ulusal-kanali-rtmde-yayinlanacak-olan-ilk-turk-dizisi-belli-o|title=Malezya Ulusal Kanalı RTM'de yayınlanacak olan ilk Türk dizisi belli oldu: ''Bu Şehir Arkandan Gelecek''|website=ranini.tv|accessdate=29 December 2023}}</ref> A Malaysian remake of ''Rüzgarın Kalbi'' aired as ''Degup Cinta'' in 2020.<ref name="gempak.com">{{cite web |title=Degup cinta cipta sejerah bakal |url=https://gempak.com/berita-terkini/degup-cinta-cipta-sejarah-bakal-dipertontonkan-di-turki-dan-timur-tengah-10526 |access-date=29 May 2023 |website=gempak.com |date=13 July 2018 |language=ms}}</ref>

====Pakistan====
Turkish series are also popular in [[Pakistan]]. ''[[Aşk-ı Memnu (2008 TV series)|Aşk-ı Memnu]]'' aired on the television channel [[Urdu 1|Urdu1]] in Pakistan and topped ratings, being the most successful Turkish series there.<ref>{{cite web|date=16 March 2013|title=Pakistan Hit by Fever of Turkey's Popular Cultural Export|url=https://hafsakhawaja.wordpress.com/2013/03/16/pakistan-hit-by-fever-of-turkeys-popular-cultural-export/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304211759/https://hafsakhawaja.wordpress.com/2013/03/16/pakistan-hit-by-fever-of-turkeys-popular-cultural-export/|archive-date=4 March 2016|website=wordpress.com}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=March 2026}} Other popular series include ''[[Fatmagül'ün Suçu Ne?]]'', which aired on the same channel, and ''[[Muhteşem Yüzyıl]]'' (''Magnificent Century''). According to Pakistani rating network Media Logic, ''Aşk-ı Memnu'' was watched by more than 90 million people on its last episode, whereas it averaged 45–55 million viewers from the rural and urban market. Moreover, ''Fatmagül'ün Suçu Ne?'' and ''[[Adını Feriha Koydum]]'' averaged 30 million and 28 million viewership respectively from rural and urban market.<ref>{{cite web|title=Television Viewership Overview 2013|url=http://medialogic.com.pk/tam/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Medialogic_Annual_Review_2013.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161227233316/http://medialogic.com.pk/tam/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Medialogic_Annual_Review_2013.pdf|archive-date=2016-12-27|access-date=2017-01-15}}</ref>

The popularity of Turkish series has led to some difficulties. Pakistan's entertainment industry has complained that airing Turkish and other foreign TV series diverts funding from local productions.<ref>{{cite web|last=AP|date=26 November 2013|title=Some in Pakistan threatened by Turkish TV invasion|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1058704|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924044546/http://www.dawn.com/news/1058704|archive-date=24 September 2015|website=dawn.com}}</ref> Furthermore, a [[Senate of Pakistan|senate]] committee that oversees information and broadcasting has condemned such shows for their allegedly vulgar content, which contradicts Pakistani Muslim traditions.<ref>{{cite web|last=Yusuf|first=Huma|date=2013-01-10|title=Trashy Turkish TV Shows Can't Distract Pakistanis From Reality|url=http://latitude.blogs.nytimes.com/2013/01/10/the-geopolitics-of-soap-operas/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130114200333/http://latitude.blogs.nytimes.com/2013/01/10/the-geopolitics-of-soap-operas/|archive-date=2013-01-14|access-date=2013-01-15|work=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>
