'''Ahad Raza Mir''' (born 29 September 1993) is a Pakistani and Canadian actor and singer who primarily works in [[Urdu]] television series and films.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ahad Raza Mir {{!}} Actor, Producer, Soundtrack |url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm8898391/ |access-date=2023-09-03 |website=IMDb |language=en-US}}</ref> The son of actor and producer [[Asif Raza Mir]], Mir is the recipient of several accolades, including four [[Hum Awards]] and a [[Lux Style Award]].

After graduating with a degree in bachelor of fine arts from [[University of Calgary]], Mir worked as an actor in several theatre productions in [[Canada]] before made his acting debut with a supporting role in the Pakistani social-based TV drama ''[[Sammi (2017 TV series)|Sammi]]'' (2017). He rose to prominence with the romantic drama ''[[Yaqeen Ka Safar]]'', which proved to be his breakout role, earning him a [[Lux Style Awards|Lux Style Award for Best Actor]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://tns.thenews.com.pk/introducing-rising-star/|title=Introducing the rising star|work=[[The News International]]|date=April 9, 2017|first=Buraq|last=Shabbir|access-date=November 10, 2017|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191101102113/http://tns.thenews.com.pk/introducing-rising-star/|archive-date=November 1, 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> The following year he starred in the commercially successful combat-war film ''[[Parwaaz Hai Junoon]]''. His performances in the [[Inter-Services Public Relations|ISPR]]-based ensemble drama ''[[Ehd-e-Wafa]]'', the thriller ''[[Yeh Dil Mera]]'' (both 2019) and the comedy ''[[Hum Tum (2022 TV series)|Hum Tum]]'' (2022), earned him [[Lux Style Awards|Lux Style Award for Best Actor]] nomination.

Mir has since starred in several international projects, such as the [[Indo-Pakistani wars and conflicts|Indo-Pak conflict]] based web-series ''[[Dhoop Ki Deewar]]'' (2021), the American series ''[[Resident Evil (TV series)|Resident Evil]]'' (2022) and the British series ''[[World on Fire (TV series)|World on Fire]]'' (2023).

== Early life and family ==
His grandfather [[Raza Mir]] was a director and his father Asif Raza Mir is an actor. Mir's mother Samra Raza Mir is a musician who was part of Pakistan's first female band, ''Symphony'', formed in 1993.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 July 2020 |title=Did you know Ahad Raza Mir's mother is a musician? |url=https://www.somethinghaute.com/did-you-know-ahad-raza-mirs-mother-is-a-musician/ |website=Something Haute}}</ref> He has a younger brother, Adnan Raza Mir, who has launched his acting career in 2023 with the comedy drama ''[[Fairy Tale (Pakistani TV series)|Fairy Tale]]'' on [[Hum TV]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=15 March 2023 |title=Ahad Raza Mir's Brother Adnan Raza Mir Debut Drama Fairy Tale Trailer |url=https://bolnews.com/entertainment/lollywood/2023/03/ahad-raza-mirs-brother-adnan-raza-mir-debut-drama-fairy-tale-trailer |website=[[BOL News]]}}</ref> Singer and actor [[Haroon Shahid]] is his cousin.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 July 2019 |title=Actor Haroon Shahid and wife welcome a baby girl |url=https://www.samaaenglish.tv/news/1808702/actor-haroon-shahid-and-wife-welcome-a-baby-girl |website=[[Samaa TV]] |quote=He's the cousin of actor-singer Ahad Raza Mir.}}</ref>

Mir attended [[Central Memorial High School]]’s Performing and Visual Arts Program in Calgary, Alberta, and graduated from the [[University of Calgary]] with a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://hellopakistanmag.com/hello-pakistan/ahad-raza-mir-reveals-his-future-plans-love-for-acting-and-ideal-woman/|title=Hello! Exclusive: Ahad Raza Mir Reveals His Future Plans, Love for Acting And Ideal Woman|date=November 25, 2017|access-date=August 23, 2018|language=en-US|archive-date=1 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191101110554/http://hellopakistanmag.com/hello-pakistan/ahad-raza-mir-reveals-his-future-plans-love-for-acting-and-ideal-woman/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":0" /><ref name="MIRHIP">{{Cite news |last=Arif |first=Azqua |date=August 8, 2017 |title="I wish to show the public who 'Ahad' really is and be my own self" |language=en-US |work=HIP |url=https://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1153234 |access-date=August 6, 2018 |archive-date=15 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190115234500/https://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1153234 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Career ==

=== Beginnings and stage roles (2010–2016) ===
Mir started his career in 2010 at age 17, playing a brief role as the son of [[Sania Saeed]] and [[Faisal Rehman]] in the [[Hum TV]]'s romantic drama ''Khamosiyan''.{{citation needed|date=April 2026}}  Mir started his career on stage, performing, directing and writing in several musicals and plays across Canada. Mir wanted to move to Toronto, but instead decided to go back to Pakistan to work in films and television.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Ahad Raza Mir: "I love both the East and the West for what they are."|url=https://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1153452/ahad-raza-mir-i-love-both-the-east-and-the-west-for-what-they-are|last=Hyder|first=Hira|date=September 9, 2017|work=HIP|access-date=August 6, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref>

===''Yaqeen Ka Safar'' and rise to prominence (2017–present)===

In 2017, Mir started auditioning for [[Hum TV]]'s production house [[MD Productions]], and was cast as a leading role in ''[[Yaqeen Ka Safar]]'' where he played Dr. Asfand Yaar, a grief-stricken brother alongside [[Sajal Aly]] and [[Hira Mani]]. He then had a supporting role in the social drama ''[[Sammi (2017 TV series)|Sammi]]'' opposite [[Mawra Hocane]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1179037|title=How Yakeen ka Safar's Asfandiyar is the leading man Pakistani dramas desperately needed|last=Kari|first=Maria|date=December 26, 2017|work=Dawn|access-date= August 6, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.somethinghaute.com/ahad-raza-mir-dr-asfandyars-appeal/| title= Ahad Raza Mir tells us the secret behind Dr Asfandyar's appeal|date=November 1, 2017|first=Mariam|last=Tahir|work= Something Haute| access-date=August 6, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=There's more to Dr Asfi than the romantic element, says Ahad Raza Mir of Yakeen ka Safar|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1178605|last=Haider|first=Sadaf |date=October 13, 2017|work=Dawn|access-date=August 6, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> His performance earned him [[Lux Style Awards|Lux Style Award for Best Actor]], and won three [[Hum Awards]] including [[Hum Award for Best Actor Popular|the Hum Award for Best Actor]].<ref>{{Cite news| title=Hum Awards 2018: Yakeen Ka Safar wins big|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1180551|author=Images Staff| date=2018-07-29| work=Images|access-date=2018-08-06|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://tns.thenews.com.pk/coming/#.W342NJMzYWo|title=The up and coming|first=Ahmed|last=Sarym|website=The News On Sunday|language=en-US|date=March 12, 2017|access-date=August 23, 2018|archive-date=11 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190811041451/http://tns.thenews.com.pk/coming/#.W342NJMzYWo|url-status=dead}}</ref> Reviewing ''Yakeen Ka Safar'', Sadaf Pervez of ''[[Express Tribune]]'' noted that Mir "shines" with his performance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/article/59539/yaqeen-ka-safar-is-honest-and-original-and-has-changed-the-paradigm-of-pakistani-dramas?|title=Yaqeen Ka Safar is honest and original, and has changed the paradigm of Pakistani dramas|date=2017-11-04|newspaper=Express Tribune|access-date=2021-06-13|author=Sadaf Pervez}}</ref>

Coming from an influential film making family, Ahad was accused of [[nepotism]]. Responding to such claims Mir stated that he wanted "people to take [him], as an actor, very seriously" and that he is “here to give Pakistan some good cinema and TV”.<ref name="TMF">{{Cite news|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1650944/4-raza-mir-factor/|title=The 'Raza Mir' Factor |date=June 3, 2018|work=The Express Tribune|first=Ahmed|last=Sarym|access-date=August 6, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/urdu/entertainment-42673706|title='اداکاری میری میراث ہے'|first=Fifi|last=Haroon|date=January 15, 2018|work=[[BBC Urdu]]|access-date=August 6, 2018| language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news| url=https://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1154289/pakistan-has-more-celebrities-and-less-actors-ahad-raza-mir|title="Pakistan has more celebrities and less actors," Ahad Raza Mir|last=Khan|first=Saira|date=January 17, 2018 |work=HIP|access-date=August 6, 2018|language =en-US}}</ref>

In 2018, Mir made his film debut with [[Haseeb Hassan]]'s military-drama ''[[Parwaaz Hay Junoon]]'', co-starring [[Hamza Ali Abbasi]] and [[Hania Aamir]], which was released on [[Eid al-Adha]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Catching up with Ahad Raza Mir|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/218523-Catching-up-with-Ahad-Raza-Mir|first=Buraq|last=Shabbir|date=July 24, 2017|work=The News International|access-date=November 10, 2017|language=en-US}}</ref> Mir replaced [[Osman Khalid Butt]] in a role of Flight Lieutenant Saad, who opted out due to his other commitments.<ref>{{cite news|title=Osman Khalid Butt is no longer part of Parwaaz Hay Junoon|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1176947| first=Irfan|last=ul Haq|work=Dawn Images|date=19 January 2017|access-date=25 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1151669|title=Ahad Raza Mir replaces Osman Khalid Butt in Parwaaz Hay Junoon|date=January 18, 2017|work=HIP|access-date=August 6, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> The same year, Mir reunited with Sajal Aly and Mawra Hocane in Hum TV's [[Mohammed Ehteshamuddin]]-directed period drama ''[[Aangan (2018 TV series)|Aangan]]'' where he played a poet, Jameel.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/238391-Ahsan-Khan-and-Mawra-Hocane-pair-up-for-Ehteshamuddins-Aangan|title=Ahsan Khan and Mawra Hocane pair up for Ehteshamuddin's Aangan|date=October 20, 2017|access-date=November 10, 2017|work=The News International|language=en-US}}</ref> The series was one of the most hyped dramas of 2018 but it has been a huge disappointment which in result was panned by audience.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://tns.thenews.com.pk/ahad-raza-mir-really/#.W2hU5_4zYWo|title=All that Ahad Raza Mir really is|website=The News On Sunday|first=Buraq|last=Shabbir|language=en-US|date=April 1, 2017|access-date=August 6, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180414010404/http://tns.thenews.com.pk/ahad-raza-mir-really/#.W2hU5_4zYWo|archive-date=April 14, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> 
 
In 2019, [[The Shakespeare Company]], in a joint production with Vertigo Theatre in Canada, signed Mir to play [[Prince Hamlet|Hamlet]] in their production becoming one of the first South Asian actor to play the role professionally in Canada.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newspakistan.tv/pakistani-actor-ahad-to-play-hamlet-in-canada/|title=Pakistani actor Ahad to play Hamlet in Canada! - News Pakistan|website=News Pakistan|language=en-US|first=Aiman|last=Iman|date=August 17, 2018|access-date=August 18, 2018|archive-date=27 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220227214438/https://www.newspakistan.tv/pakistani-actor-ahad-to-play-hamlet-in-canada/|url-status=dead}}</ref> His performance won him the Betty Mitchell Award for Outstanding Performance by an Actor in a Drama.<ref name="hamlet1"/><ref name="hamlet2">{{Cite news|url=http://www.aaj.tv/2019/06/ahad-raza-mir-bags-international-nomination-for-hamlet/|title=Ahad Raza Mir bags International nomination for hamlet|date=12 June 2019|work=AAJ Tv|access-date=15 June 2019|archive-date=13 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190613130634/http://www.aaj.tv/2019/06/ahad-raza-mir-bags-international-nomination-for-hamlet/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url= https://tribune.com.pk/story/1782143/4-ahad-raza-mir-play-hamlet-shakespearean-play/|title=Ahad Raza Mir to play Hamlet in Shakespearean play |date=August 16, 2018|work=The Express Tribune|access-date=August 18, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.somethinghaute.com/ahad-raza-mir-will-be-returning-to-toronto-for-hamlet/|title=Ahad Raza Mir will be returning to Toronto for Hamlet|date=August 18, 2018 |work= Something Haute|access-date=August 18, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://calgaryherald.com/entertainment/theatre/ahad-mir-will-return-to-calgary-to-play-hamlet|title=Rising star to return to Calgary to play Hamlet|date=June 10, 2018|first=Louis|last=B. Hobson|work=Calgary Herald|access-date=August 18, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/356957-ahad-raza-mir-comes-clean|title=Ahad Raza Mir comes clean|last=Sarym|first=Ahmed|access-date=August 18, 2018|language=en}}</ref>

In the same year, he played an army officer Saad Faraz in [[Inter-Services Public Relations|ISPR]] based ''[[Ehd-e-Wafa]]'' opposite [[Alizeh Shah]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2046270/4-okb-ahad-raza-mir-shine-teaser-upcoming-military-drama-ehd-e-wafa/|title=OKB, Ahad Raza Mir shine in teaser of upcoming military drama 'Ehd-e-Wafa'|last=Tribune.com.pk|date=31 August 2019|website=The Express Tribune|language=en|access-date=1 September 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/630687-ehd-e-wafa-concludes-shines-light-on-bond-of-friendship|title=Ehd e Wafa concludes; shines light on bond of friendship|publisher=[[The News International]]|access-date=August 17, 2021|date=March 18, 2020}}</ref> He then starred as Amaanullah Khan opposite Sajal Ali in suspense thriller ''[[Yeh Dil Mera]]''. For both these performances, he received Lux Style Award for Best TV Actor - Critics nominations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/ahad-and-sajals-yeh-dil-mera-might-be-the-complete-opposite-of-a-classic-love-story-between-a-boy-and-a-girl/|title=Yeh Dil Mera might be the complete opposite of a classic love story between a boy and a girl|website=Daily Pakistan Global|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-27|archive-date=26 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191026083848/https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/ahad-and-sajals-yeh-dil-mera-might-be-the-complete-opposite-of-a-classic-love-story-between-a-boy-and-a-girl/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/627242/yeh-dil-mera-is-a-psychological-thriller/|title='Yeh Dil Mera' is a psychological thriller|website=Daily Times|date=16 June 2020|access-date=25 August 2021|author=Haneen Moosa}}</ref> Mir made his web debut co-starring Sajal Ali in ''[[Dhoop Ki Deewar]]'' as Vishal Malhotra. The series was released on [[ZEE5]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gulfnews.com/entertainment/tv/how-dhoop-ki-deewar-reels-in-fans-from-pakistan-and-india-with-a-story-about-love-1.80221774|title=How 'Dhoop Ki Deewar' reels in fans from Pakistan and India with a story about love|work=Gulf News|language=en|first=|last=|date=26 June 2021 |access-date=26 October 2021}}</ref>

After a hiatus of three-years, Mir played a college chemistry student Adam Sultan in the 2022 Ramadan special ''[[Hum Tum (2022 TV series)|Hum Tum]]'', opposite [[Ramsha Khan]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/874312|title=Ramsha and Ahad Raza Mir pair up for an upcoming Ramadan play|date=25 January 2022|accessdate=13 April 2022|work=Daily Times}}</ref> The series and his portrayal was praised across [[Pakistan]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1189762|title=Teasers are out for Ahad Raza Mir and Ramsha Khan's Ramazan special Hum Tum|work=DAWN Image|date=21 March 2022 |accessdate=21 March 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1189870|title=Ramazan special Hum Tum is breaking gender stereotypes and Pakistani Twitter loves it|work=DAWN Image|date=5 April 2022 |accessdate=25 April 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://propakistani.pk/lens/hum-tum-netizens-love-the-chaotic-pairing-of-ramsha-and-ahad/ |title=Hum Tum: Netizens are in love with the chaotic pairing of Ramsha Khan and Ahad Raza Mir |access-date=24 August 2022 |work=Pro Pakistani|date=4 April 2022 }}</ref> His chemistry with Khan was appreciated and they won the [[Hum Award for Best Onscreen Couple Popular]] and he received nomination for [[Hum Award for Best Actor Popular]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.samaa.tv/2087321717-hum-awards-2024-yumna-zaidi-sehar-khan-among-top-winners |title=Hum Awards 2024: Yumna Zaidi, Ramsha Khan, Ahad Raza Mir and Sehar Khan among top winners! |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=2 October 2024 |work=samaa.tv}}</ref>

The same year, he made his [[Netflix]] debut with the series ''[[Resident Evil (TV series)|Resident Evil]]'', as Arjun Batra.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://slate.com/culture/2022/07/netflix-resident-evil-series-review.html|title=Netflix's Resident Evil Is Surprisingly Good. There's One Scene That Proves It|date=July 21, 2022|access-date=July 25, 2022|work=Slate|last=Drezner|first=Daniel|archive-date=July 25, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220725003319/https://slate.com/culture/2022/07/netflix-resident-evil-series-review.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He next appeared in British series ''[[World on Fire (TV series)|World on Fire]]'',  as Rajib Pal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BBC releases the first-look images for World on Fire season 2 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/mediacentre/2023/world-on-fire-series-two-first-look-images/ |access-date=10 September 2023|date=31 May 2023 |website=BBC UK |language=en}}</ref> Mir will next appear in Pakistan's first [[Netflix]] original ''[[Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fawad Khan, Sanam Saeed, Mahira Khan, Ahad Raza Mir to star in Netflix's first Pakistan-themed original |url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/asia/fawad-khan-pakistan-netflix-jo-bachay-hain-sang-samait-lo-1235701929/ |access-date=28 December 2023 |website=Variety |date=23 August 2023 |language=en}}</ref> which is expected to be released in late 2026.

In December 2024, Ahad played the lead role in [[Hum TV]]'s ''[[Meem Se Mohabbat]]'' along with [[Dananeer Mobeen]].<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Salamat |first1=Sajid |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/1223929/dananeer-set-to-play-lead-role-in-meem-se-mohabbat/|title=Dananeer set to play lead role in 'Meem Se Mohabbat'|date=5 September 2024|website=Daily Times}}</ref> Mir portrayed Talha Ahmed, a wealthy CEO and uncle to a young orphaned child.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/tns/detail/1263985-does-love-really-conquer-all|title=Does love really conquer all? &#124; Shehr &#124; thenews.com.pk|website=www.thenews.com.pk}}</ref> In 2026, Ahad played the lead role in [[Green Entertainment]]'s ''Aik Mohabbat Aur'' along with [[Maya Ali]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://niche.com.pk/ahad-raza-mir-and-maya-ali-are-giving-romance-a-new-mood-in-aik-mohabbat-aur/|title=Ahad Raza Mir and Maya Ali are giving romance a new mood in 'Aik Mohabbat Aur'|date=4 June 2026|website=Niche Lifestyle}}</ref> 

== Other work ==

=== Music ===
In Canada, Mir has mostly been involved in [[musical theatre]], being the first South Asian to win a "Best Actor in a Musical" award at the Canadian Critics’ Awards.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Ajaz |first=Mahwash |date=1 November 2017 |title=Everything you ever wanted to know about Ahad Raza Mir – in his own words |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1546781/everything-ever-wanted-know-ahad-raza-mir-words |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250406193138/https://tribune.com.pk/story/1546781/everything-ever-wanted-know-ahad-raza-mir-words |archive-date=6 April 2025 |website=[[The Express Tribune]] |quote=We saw you singing a bit in Yaqeen Ka Safar... [Ahad] I’m the first desi actor to win ‘best actor in a musical’ at the Canadian Critics’ Awards... Every month I try to learn something new. Last month I tried learning a West African drum called djembe. I try to learn different languages, painting etc.}}</ref> He can play a number of musical instruments, including guitar, bass guitar, drums and keyboards.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 August 2018 |title=On Board With The Team And Cast Behind Parwaaz Hai Junoon |url=https://theglossmag.net/on-board-with-the-team-and-cast-behind-parwaaz-hai-junoon/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241101223256/https://theglossmag.net/on-board-with-the-team-and-cast-behind-parwaaz-hai-junoon/ |archive-date=1 November 2024 |website=Gloss Magazine |quote=[Ahad Raza Mir] I did my BFA from Canada with a lot of musical theatres, played a number of instruments like the guitar, the bass guitar, the drums, keyboards.}}</ref> He has also learned to play the [[djembe]], a [[West Africa|West African]] drum.<ref name=":0" />

In 2017, he played the guitar and sang for ''Yaqeen Ka Safar''.<ref name=":0" />

In 2018, Mir made his ''[[Coke Studio Pakistan|Coke Studio]]'' debut as a featured artist in its [[Coke Studio Pakistan (season 11)|eleventh-season]], where he performed the song "[[Ko Ko Korina]]" with [[Momina Mustehsan]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sabeeh |first=Maheen |date=July 30, 2018 |title=How Ahad Raza Mir made it to Coke Studio 11 |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/348310-how-ahad-raza-mir-made-it-to-coke-studio-11 |access-date=August 6, 2018 |language=en}}</ref> Their rendition of the classic song was widely criticized. Within a few days of the video being released on [[YouTube]], it became the most-disliked video in the music show's history.<ref>{{cite web |author=Priyamvada Grover |date=9 November 2018 |title=Ko Ko Korina: Why Pakistan is decrying a Coke Studio cover |url=https://theprint.in/culture/ko-ko-korina-why-pakistan-is-decrying-a-coke-studio-cover/143885/ |access-date=1 December 2018 |website=theprint.in}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Ghazala Sulaiman |date=23 October 2018 |title=Momina Mustehsan Vs Shireen Mazari's 'Ko Ko Korina' Twitter War: Ahad Raza Mir & Sajal Break Silence! |url=https://www.brandsynario.com/momina-mustehsan-vs-shireen-mazaris-ko-ko-korina-twitter-war-sajal-ali-breaks-silence/ |access-date=23 October 2018 |publisher=Brandsynario}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Ghazala Sulaiman |date=23 October 2018 |title=Momina Mustehsan Vs Shireen Mazari's 'Ko Ko Korina' Twitter War: Ahad Raza Mir & Sajal Break Silence! |url=https://www.brandsynario.com/momina-mustehsan-vs-shireen-mazaris-ko-ko-korina-twitter-war-sajal-ali-breaks-silence/ |accessdate=23 October 2018 |publisher=Brandsynario}}</ref>

=== Production ===
In 2018, Mir announced that he will be producing the film ''Kalasha'', about the [[Kalash people]], featuring actor [[Aijaz Aslam]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kalasha will feature Aijaz Aslam and Angeline Malik |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/374510-kalasha-will-feature-aijaz-aslam-and-angeline-malik |access-date=11 September 2024 |website=[[The News International]]}}</ref>

== Personal life==
Mir obtained the [[Canadian citizenship]] in 2015.<ref name=":0" /> His hobbies include painting and learning languages.<ref name=":0" />

On 6 June 2019, Mir got engaged to actress [[Sajal Aly]], and married her in a private ceremony on 14 March 2020 in [[Abu Dhabi]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gulfnews.com/entertainment/pakistani-cinema/ahad-raza-mir-sajal-ali-finally-announce-engagement-1.64496337|title=Ahad Raza Mir, Sajal Ali finally announce engagement|date=June 10, 2019|website=gulfnews.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/277296-sajal-ali-and-ahad-raza-mir-getting-married-today-in-uae|title=Sajal Ali and Ahad Raza Mir get married in UAE|date=March 14, 2020|website=geo.tv}}</ref> The couple separated and eventually divorced on 22 March 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Reporter |first=Masala |date=22 March 2022 |title=Sajal Aly, Ahad Raza Mir part ways; couple officially divorced |pages=1 |work=Masala News |publisher=Masala News |url=https://www.masala.com/celebrities/sajal-aly-ahad-raza-mir |access-date=22 March 2022}}</ref>

==Public image and recorgnition==
''[[Dawn (newspaper)|Images Dawn]]'' named Mir in their "Standout performances: Male" list of 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1184358|title=What made a good drama in 2019? Here are the top picks|website=Images Dawn|language=en|date=7 January 2020|accessdate=21 February 2022}}</ref> Mir has been placed in the [[Hello Magazine|Hello Pakistan]]'s HOT100 list, in the "Trailblazers" category, in the year 2020 and 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hmagpak.com/17-Dec-2020/hot-100?version=amp|title=HELLO! HOT 100 - 2020|accessdate=26 December 2020|website=Hello Magazine Pakistan|date=17 December 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/14-Dec-2022/headliners-trailblazers-trendsetters-celebs-who-made-it-to-hellopakistan-s-hot100-list-of-2022%3fversion=amp|title=Headliners, trailblazers, trendsetters - Celebs who made it to Hello Pakistan's #HOT100 list|accessdate=16 December 2022|website=Daily Pakistan|archive-date=15 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221215012342/https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/14-Dec-2022/headliners-trailblazers-trendsetters-celebs-who-made-it-to-hellopakistan-s-hot100-list-of-2022?version=amp|url-status=dead}}</ref> The actor serves as an ambassador for a number of brands including [[Nestlé]], [[Mountain Dew]], [[Xiaomi]], [[Coca-Cola]] and [[Lays]], among others.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2342760/xiaomi-vows-to-make-lives-better-with-its-innovative-redmi-and-smart-air-purifier-series?amp=1|title=Xiaomi roped in the heartthrob Ahad Raza Mir as its brand ambassador for the Redmi series|accessdate=16 October 2022|website=The Express Tribune|date=9 February 2022 }}</ref> In 2021, he was appointed the ambassador of the Pakistan Pavilion, at the Expo 2020 [[Dubai]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.khaleejtimes.com/local-events/the-world-owes-the-uae-for-putting-expo-2020-together-ahad-raza-mir?amp=1|title=The world owes the UAE for putting Expo 2020 together: Ahad Raza Mir|accessdate=28 November 2021|website=Khaleej Times}}</ref> Mir was placed at 42nd position in ''[[Eastern Eye]]''{{'}}s "Top 50 Global Asian Celebrities" list of 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.easterneye.biz/top-50-asian-stars-of-2023/|title=Shah Rukh Khan tops Global Asian Celebrity List 2023; check the complete list|accessdate=16 December 2023|website=Eastern Eye}}</ref>

'''Anmol Baloch''' (born 10 January 1999) is a [[Pakistani]] television actress and model.<ref>{{cite web |title=Anmol Baloch - Interview |url=https://socialdiary.pk/anmol-baloch/ |website=Social Diary |date=January 2019 |publisher=[[Pakistan Observer]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=30 minutes with Anmol Baloch |url=https://www.goodtimes.com.pk/30-minutes-with-anmol-baloch/ |website=Good Times |date=16 December 2018 |publisher=[[Daily Times (Pakistan)|Daily Times]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Qamar |first1=Alina |title="I want the girls watching me to feel they can do anything," - Anmol Baloch |url=http://magtheweekly.com/detail/9434-i-want-the-girls-watching-me-to-feel-they-can-do-anything-anmol-baloch |website=Mag The Weekly |publisher=[[Jang Media Group]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=60 Seconds with Anmol Baloch |url=http://magtheweekly.com/detail/10528-60-seconds-with-anmol-baloch |website=Mag The Weekly |publisher=[[Jang Media Group]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref>
She is known for her roles as Ushna in ''[[Aik Sitam Aur]]'', Abeer in the series ''Sirf Tum'',<ref>{{cite web |title=Actress Anmol Baloch to star in 'Qurbatain' |url=https://www.24newshd.tv/17-Jul-2020/actress-anmol-baloch-to-star-in-qurbatain |website=[[24 News HD]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Catch Anmol Baloch, Shahbaz Shigri in Qurbatain |url=https://www.samaa.tv/entertainment/2020/07/catch-anmol-baloch-shahbaz-shigri-in-qurbatain/ |website=[[Samaa TV]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Anmol Baloch shines in her latest TV drama 'Qurbatain' |url=https://nation.com.pk/18-Jul-2020/anmol-baloch-shines-in-her-latest-tv-drama-qurbatain |website=[[The Nation (Pakistan)|The Nation]] |date=17 July 2020 |publisher=[[Nawa-i-Waqt]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> and Mehr-un-Nissa in ''[[Iqtidar]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Happy birthday to 'Aik Larki Aam Si' Anmol Baloch |url=https://www.24newshd.tv/10-Jan-2021/happy-birthday-to-aik-larki-aam-si-anmol-baloch |website=[[24 News HD]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Actress Anmol Baloch celebrates birthday |url=https://nation.com.pk/11-Jan-2021/actress-anmol-baloch-celebrates-birthday |website=[[The Nation (Pakistan)|The Nation]] |date=11 January 2021 |publisher=[[Nawa-i-Waqt]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref>

==Career==
===2016-2020===
Baloch started out as a model but later ventured into acting. In 2016, she made her debut in the [[A-Plus Entertainment]] television series ''Kambakht Tanno''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kambakht Tanno |url=http://a-plus.tv/dramas/kambakht-tanno/ |website=[[A-Plus TV]] |access-date=3 March 2021 |archive-date=17 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200217191947/http://a-plus.tv/dramas/kambakht-tanno/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2017, she appeared in the [[Geo Entertainment]] television series ''[[Bedardi Saiyaan]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bedardi Saiyaan |url=https://harpalgeo.tv/program/bedardi-saiyaan |website=[[Geo Entertainment]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> She also appeared in TV One's ''Jalti Barish''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jalti Barish |url=https://www.tvonepk.tv/drama/serial/jalti-barish |website=TVOne |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> In 2018, she guest starred in [[Express Entertainment]]'s anthology television series ''[[Kabhi Band Kabhi Baja]]'' in the episode ''Laila Ka Jadoo''.<ref>{{cite web |title= Kabhi Band Kabhi Baja Episode 16 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yeEt93orBX8 |website=[[YouTube]] |publisher=[[Express Entertainment]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> She also starred in Hum TV's ''[[Aik Larki Aam Si]]'' as Anmol the same year.<ref>{{cite web |title=Aik Larki Aam Si |url=https://www.hum.tv/dramas/aik-larki-aam-si/ |website=[[Hum TV]] |access-date=3 March 2021 |archive-date=21 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921135614/https://www.hum.tv/dramas/aik-larki-aam-si/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Mansoor |first1=Rabail |title=Aik Larki Aam Si Drama on HUM TV: Timings, Cast, OST & Plot |url=https://www.brandsynario.com/aik-larki-aam-si-drama-on-hum-tv-timings-cast-ost-plot/ |website=Brandsynario |date=29 June 2018 |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> In 2019, she had a main role in the Hum TV television film ''[[Pyaar Kahani]]'' alongside [[Asim Azhar]] and [[Hania Amir]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Hania Amir, Asim Azhar to star in telefilm Pyar Kahani |url=https://www.samaa.tv/entertainment/2019/07/hania-amir-asim-azhar-to-star-in-telefilm-pyar-kahani/ |website=[[Samaa TV]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Ghafoor |first1=Usman |title=Asim Azhar and Hania Aamir pair up for TV movie |url=https://gulfnews.com/entertainment/pakistani-cinema/asim-azhar-and-hania-aamir-pair-up-for-tv-movie-1.65235484 |website=[[Gulf News]] |date=15 July 2019 |publisher=[[Al Nisr Publishing]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> She appeared in the Hum TV historical television series ''[[Deewar-e-Shab]]'' which was nominated for the [[1st Pakistan International Screen Awards]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nominations for the first ever Pakistan International Screen Awards are out |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1184279 |website=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn Images]] |date=24 December 2019 |publisher=[[Dawn Media Group]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Ul Haq |first1=Irfan |title=Bushra Ansari, Asma Abbasi and Zara Noor Abbas are starring together in Hum TV's next period play |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1181661 |website=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn Images]] |date=15 January 2019 |publisher=[[Dawn Media Group]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> She played the main role of Sajeeda in the Pakistani-Malaysian co-produced television series ''[[Sara Sajeeda]]''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Shamsudin |first1=Rudy Imran |title=Penerbit geram dengan pelakon 'kekwat' |url=https://www.hmetro.com.my/rap/2019/10/503281/penerbit-geram-dengan-pelakon-kekwat |website=[[Harian Metro]] |date=3 October 2019 |publisher=The New Straits Times Press (M) Berhad |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> In 2020, she guest starred in the A-Plus Entertainment television series [[Haqeeqat (2019 TV series)|''Haqeeqat'']] in the episode "Badnaam Mohabbat".<ref>{{cite web |title=Badnaam Mohabbat - Haqeeqat |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HZ6G-P2EjXs |website=[[YouTube]] |publisher=[[A-Plus Entertainment]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> She starred in the Express Entertainment television series ''[[Saza e Ishq]]'' as Rameen alongside [[Azfar Rehman]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Saza e Ishq |url=https://www.expressentertainment.tv/dramas/saza-e-ishq/ |website=[[Express Entertainment]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Khalid |first1=Almas |title=نیا ڈرامہ ''سزا عشق'' جلد آن ایئر کردیا جائے گا |url=https://www.roznama92news.com/%D9%86%DB%8C%D8%A7-%D8%B1%D8%A7%D9%85-%D8%B3%D8%B2%D8%A7-%D8%B9%D8%B4%D9%82-%D8%AC%D9%84%D8%AF-%D9%86-%D8%A7%DB%8C%D8%B1-%DA%A9 |website=[[92 News|Roznama 92]] |publisher=[[92 News]]}}</ref> Baloch played the main role of Areeba in the Hum TV television series ''[[Qurbatein]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Qurbatein |url=https://www.hum.tv/dramas/qurbatain/ |website=[[Hum TV]] |access-date=3 March 2021 |archive-date=17 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017162154/https://www.hum.tv/dramas/qurbatain/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===2021-present===
Baloch played the negative role in the [[ARY Digital]] television series ''Khwaab Nagar Ki Shehzadi''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hasnain |first1=Alefyah |title='Khwaab Nagar Ki Shehzadi' Begins With A Promising Start! |url=https://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1159101 |website=Hip in Pakistan |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Fans are loving 'Khwaab Nagar Ki Shehzadi' and here are the reasons! |url=https://arynews.tv/en/knks-maid-story-viral/ |website=[[ARY News]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Shafi |first1=Faisal |title=10 Best Upcoming Pakistani Dramas 2021 |url=https://www.desiblitz.com/content/10-best-upcoming-pakistani-dramas-2021 |website=DesiBlitz |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> She played the lead role in A-Plus Entertainment television series ''Noor'' alongside [[Usama Khan]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Noor - Coming Soon |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nnp64rhaTuk |website=[[YouTube]] |publisher=[[A-Plus Entertainment]] |access-date=3 March 2021}}</ref> in 2022, She played lead in ''[[Aik Sitam Aur]]'' on ARY Digital and negative lead in ''Siyani'' on Geo TV. In 2023, she played lead roles in ''Mann Aangan'' on ARY Digital, ''Sirf Tum'' and ''Shiddat'' on Geo TV. In 2024-25 she played lead role in Green Entertainment television's series ''[[Iqtidar]].''

'''Armeena Rana Khan''' ({{langx|ur|{{nq|ارمینہ رانا خان}}}} {{IPA|ur|əɾˈmiːnaː ˈxaːn|pron}}) is a Pakistani-Canadian film and television actress and model.

She was born in [[Toronto]] to Pakistani parents, was raised in [[Manchester]] and earned a Bachelor's degree in business administration from the [[University of Manchester]]. She rose to prominence with the role of an [[antagonist]] in the romantic television series ''[[Muhabbat Ab Nahi Hugi]]'' (2014), garnering her a [[Hum Award for Best Actor in a Negative Role|Best Villain]] nomination at the  [[Hum Awards]]. She followed it by garnering widespread critical acclaim for her starring roles in the romantic series— ''[[Ishq Parast]]'' (2015) and ''[[Karb]]'' (2015).<ref name="tribune/18july2017">{{cite news |title=Sorry guys, Armeena Khan is officially off the market! - The Express Tribune |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1460485/sorry-guys-armeena-khan-officially-off-market-now/ |access-date=24 February 2018 |work=The Express Tribune |date=18 July 2017}}</ref><ref name="thenews/1nov2016">{{cite news |last1=raza |first1=Nida |title=Armeena Rana Khan |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/you/161293-Armeena-Rana-Khan |access-date=24 February 2018 |work=The News International |date=1 November 2016 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mohabbatein Chahatein: In conversation with Armeena Khan - BBC URDU - YouTube | date=25 November 2020 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xr2rLIufDpQ&ab_channel=BBCNews%D8%A7%D8%B1%D8%AF%D9%88 |access-date=22 December 2020 |via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=8 October 2020 |title=It is always good to be back on HUM TV: Armeena Khan talks about her new project {{!}} HUM TV - Watch Dramas Online |newspaper=Hum Tv |url=https://www.hum.tv/spotlight-it-would-take-more-than-a-pandemic-to-keep-me-away-armeena-khan/ |access-date=22 December 2020 |language=en-US}}</ref>

She, in 2015 and 2016, played a [[girl next door]] in the [[Bin Roye|film]] and [[Bin Roye (TV series)|television adaption]] of the novel ''[[Bin Roye Ansoo (novel)|Bin Roye Ansoo]]'', the former earned her a nomination for the [[Lux Style Award|Lux Style Award for Best Supporting Actress]]. She then starred as the female lead in the romantic comedy ''[[Janaan]]'' and the war drama ''[[Yalghaar]]'', both of which rank among the [[List of highest-grossing Pakistani films|highest-grossing Pakistani films of all time]], and has since played a woman caught in a romantic triangle in ''[[Rasm E Duniya]]'' (2017) and a troubled wife the social drama ''[[Daldal (TV series)|Daldal]]'' (2017).

==Early life and background==
Khan was born in [[Toronto]], [[Ontario]], to Pakistani parents. Her father is a businessman, and her mother is a homemaker. She has one brother and two sisters. She is of [[Pashtuns|Pashtun]] and [[Punjabi people|Punjabi]] origins.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Alavi |first1=Omair |title=And then there was Armeena |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1196207 |access-date=18 January 2021 |work=Dawn|location=Pakistan |date=26 July 2015 |language=en}}</ref> Khan did her schooling from Toronto, however, the family later relocated to [[Manchester]], where she attended the [[University of Manchester]], earning an Honors degree in Business Administration. She later studied method acting at the [[Ealing Studios]] and the [[Pinewood Studios]]. According to the actress, she holds [[dual citizenship]] of Pakistan and Canada.<ref name="thenews/1nov2016" /><ref name="dailytimes/18nov2016" /> Khan is fluent in English and Urdu and can read Arabic.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ahmad |first1=Fouzia Nasir |title=THE TUBE |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1594301 |access-date=4 February 2021 |work=Dawn |date=6 December 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

Khan pursued modelling in 2010 before becoming an actress. During this time, she worked in commercials for various brands and products, including [[Nishat Linen]], [[Faysal Bank]] and [[Sprite (drink)|Sprite]].{{cn|date=January 2026}}

== Acting career  ==
[[File:Armeena Khan (cropped).jpg|thumb|150px|Khan promoting ''[[Huff! It's Too Much]]'' in 2013]]
Her first acting role was for the British short film "Writhe", in which Khan played the role of a serial killer. The film was selected for the 2013 [[Cannes Film Festival]]. Khan claimed that she was the first Pakistani actress to walk at Cannes in 2013.<ref name="thenews/1nov2016" /><ref name="dawn/26july2015">{{cite news |last1=Alavi |first1=Omair |title=And then there was Armeena |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1196207 |access-date=24 February 2018 |work=Dawn|location=Pakistan |date=26 July 2015}}</ref> She then appeared in another short film, titled ''Stranger Within Me'' which was screened at the [[2014 Cannes Film Festival]].<ref name="thenews/1nov2016" /><ref name="thenews/21jan2018">{{cite news |title=Honestly, Armeena {{!}} TNS - The News on Sunday |url=http://tns.thenews.com.pk/honestly-armeena/ |access-date=24 February 2018 |work=The News International |date=21 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180225205541/http://tns.thenews.com.pk/honestly-armeena/#.WpELX5P1X6Y |archive-date=25 February 2018 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="magtheweekly/5jan2018">{{cite news |title=The Hit Dozen Of 2017 |url=http://www.magtheweekly.com/detail/1290-the-hit-dozen-of-2017 |access-date=24 February 2018 |work=Mag The Weekly |date=5 January 2018 |language=en}}</ref> Khan starred alongside [[Azfar Rehman]] in the sitcom ''Happily Married'' which aired in 2013 on [[ARY Digital Network|ARY Digital]]. The year 2013 witnessed the broadcasting of Khan's first serious acting performances with the airing of ''Shab-e-Arzu ka Alam'', in which she plays the lead role alongside [[Mohib Mirza]]. But it was the television series ''[[Muhabbat Ab Nahi Hugi]]'' that proved to be a breakthrough for her,<ref name="thenews/1nov2016" />  and for which she was also nominated for Hum Awards 2015.<ref name=":0"/> She then moved on to continue with other TV serials ''[[Ishq Parast]]'' and ''[[Karb]]'' playing the lead role alongside [[Adnan Siddiqui]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://magazine.thenews.com.pk/mag/detail_article.asp?id=10261&magId=11 |title=Armeena Khan signed up for |work=The News International |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150520235433/http://magazine.thenews.com.pk/mag/detail_article.asp?id=10261&magId=11 |archive-date=20 May 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> She made her [[Bollywood]] debut in 2013 with ''[[Huff! It's Too Much]]'' with a lead role in the film.<ref name="timesofindia/8nov2013">{{cite news |title=Huff! It's Too Much: A candyfloss romance with a real touch - Times of India |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/Huff-Its-Too-Much-A-candyfloss-romance-with-a-real-touch/movie-review/25383114.cms |access-date=24 February 2018 |work=The Times of India |date=8 November 2013}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite news |title=HUM TV Awards 2015: the nominations are in |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1173462 |work=Dawn}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Civilisations are known by their cultural legacies: Khan |url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/563597/civilisations-are-known-by-their-cultural-legacies-khan/ |website=The Express Tribune|date=15 June 2013}}</ref>

She became a well-known actress in the country with the 2015 romantic drama film ''[[Bin Roye]]''<ref name="thenews/1nov2016" /> as the lead cast along with [[Mahira Khan]] and [[Humayun Saeed]],<ref name="auto2">{{cite news |url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/867605/mahira-khan-and-humayun-saeeds-bin-roye-likely-to-steal-your-hearts/ |title=Mahira Khan and Humayun Saeed's Bin Roye likely to steal your hearts |date=10 April 2015 |work=The Express Tribune |access-date=1 April 2021}}</ref> and was later turned into a drama serial with the [[Bin Roye (TV series)|same name]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/881283/i-cant-wait-to-see-my-films-rule-the-box-office-humayun-saeed/ |title=I can't wait to see both my films rule the box office: Humayun Saeed |date=5 May 2015 |access-date=1 April 2021 |work=The Express Tribune |last=Hassan |first=Sameen}}</ref> Produced by [[Momina Duraid]], the film and the television version were based on the novel ''[[Bin Roye Ansoo (novel)|Bin Roye Aansu]]'' by [[Farhat Ishtiaq]].<ref name="auto2"/><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://awamiweb.com/ishq-parast-ary-digital-drama-cast-new-77429.html |title=Ishq Parast ARY Digital Drama Cast Is New |date=8 February 2015 |work=Awami Web |access-date=26 March 2018 |language=en-US}}</ref> That same year, she featured alongside [[Osman Khalid Butt]] in the music video "[[Sajna]]". Sung by [[Uzair Jaswal]] and produced by his brother [[Yasir Jaswal]], the single was well received upon release and earned her nationwide recognition.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hum Awards 2016 Complete Nominations List |url=http://www.brandsynario.com/hum-awards-2016-complete-nominations-list/ |work=Maheen Nusrat |publisher=Brandsynario |date=6 April 2016 |access-date=6 April 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Hum Awards 2016 Complete Nominations List |url=http://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/112163-What-to-expect-at-the-Hum-Awards-2016 |work=[[The News International]] |date=13 April 2016 |access-date=14 April 2016}}</ref> Her other big screen projects include the epic-war drama ''[[Yalghaar]]'',<ref>{{cite news |last=Tapal |first=Nida |date=10 September 2014 |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1125718/hassan-rana-talks-yalghaar-shaan-and-future-of-pakistans-cinema |title=Hassan Rana talks Yalghaar, Shaan and future of Pakistan's cinema |access-date=1 April 2021 |work=Dawn}}</ref> a film by [[Hassan Waqas Rana]] which is being termed as the most expensive film in the history of Pakistani cinema, and ''[[Janaan]]'', a romantic comedy which is directed by [[Azfar Jafri]] and co produced by [[Hareem Farooq]], [[Reham Khan]] and Imran Raza Kazmi. In November 2016, she was signed for ''[[Rasm E Duniya]]'', a television drama that aired on [[ARY Digital]].<ref name="dailytimes/18nov2016">{{cite news |title=Armeena Rana Khan signs her next television project - Daily Times |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/45331/armeena-rana-khan-signs-her-next-television-project/ |access-date=24 February 2018 |work=Daily Times |date=18 November 2016}}</ref> In 2019, Khan played the leading role in the patriotic war film ''[[Sherdil]]''.<ref name="Daily Pakistan Global">{{cite news |title=Here's all you need to know about movie 'Sherdil' |url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/heres-all-you-need-to-know-about-movie-sherdil/ |access-date=24 February 2018 |work=Daily Pakistan Global}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1147074 |title=Adnan Siddiqui's 'Karb' looks like a bore |last=Ahmad |first=Ayesha |date=28 April 2015 |work=HIP |access-date=26 March 2018 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/45331/armeena-rana-khan-signs-her-next-television-project/ |title=Armeena Rana Khan signs her next television project - Daily Times |date=18 November 2016 |work=Daily Times |access-date=26 March 2018 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1154278 |title=Armeena Khan talks about Daldal with BBC Asian Network |last=Khan |first=Saira |date=16 January 2018 |work=HIP |access-date=26 March 2018 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2025, she made her television comeback after 4 years for [[Hum TV]] drama series '' Meri Tanhai''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://jang.com.pk/en/27197-azaan-sami-khan-shares-update-about-his-new-drama-meri-tanhai-news|title=Azaan Sami Khan shares Update about his new Drama Meri Tanhai|website=[[Daily Jang]]|date=14 December 2024|access-date=1 January 2025|language=en-PK}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
She announced her engagement to [[British Pakistani]] businessman Fesl Reza-Khan<ref name="eye">{{cite web|url=https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/uk-gorton-and-denton-by-election-meet-frontrunners-green-party-candidate|title=Meet the frontrunners to be Green candidate in crucial UK by-election|accessdate=30 January 2026|website=Middle East Eye|last=Mulla|first=Imran|date=29 January 2026}}</ref> on [[Twitter]] in July 2017.<ref name="tribune/18july2017" /> She revealed that Fesl had proposed to her on the beach in [[Cuba]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1460485/sorry-guys-armeena-khan-officially-off-market-now/ |title=Sorry guys, Armeena Khan is officially off the market! |date=18 August 2017 |work=The Express Tribune |access-date=18 July 2017 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1462311/fan-accuses-armeena-khan-already-married/ |title=Fan accuses Armeena Khan of already being married once before |date=24 August 2016 |work=The Express Tribune |access-date=31 March 2018 |language=en-US}}</ref> Khan married Fesl in a Nikah ceremony in London on 14 February 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.samaa.tv/entertainment/2020/02/armeena-rana-khan-fesl-khan-are-married/ |title=Armeena Rana Khan, Fesl Khan are married! |date=15 February 2020 |publisher=Samaa TV |access-date=15 February 2020 |language=en-US}}</ref> The couple became parents to a girl, Amelie Isla, in December 2022.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.samaa.tv/entertainment/2020/02/armeena-rana-khan-fesl-khan-are-married/ |title=Armeena Khan welcomes a baby girl, names her 'Amelie Isla' |date=26 December 2022 |publisher=Tribune |access-date=15 February 2023 |language=en-US}}</ref> Fesl joined the [[Green Party of England and Wales]] in 2023; as of 2026 he serves as the party's International Co-ordinator and is the co-chair of Muslim Greens.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Executive (GPEx)|url=https://greenparty.org.uk/about/people/national-executive/|website=Green Party|access-date=2026-01-30|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name="eye"/> As a result of the [[2026 Manchester City Council election]], he was elected one of the three councillors for Levenshulme.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/manchester-local-election-results-2026-33864743 |title=Manchester local election results 2026 in full |date=8 May 2026 |publisher=Manchester Evening News |access-date=11 May 2026|language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Balaji Telefilms''' is an Indian company that produces [[Indian soap opera]]s in several Indian languages. It also produces reality TV, comedy, game shows, entertainment, and factual programming. Balaji Telefilms is promoted by [[Ekta Kapoor]] and [[Shobha Kapoor]] and is a [[public company]] listed at [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] and [[National Stock Exchange of India]].

In the 2000s, the company produced some historic blockbusters, which included ''[[Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi]]'',<ref>{{cite web | title = "25 Years of Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi " |publisher=Kovid Gupta Films| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sSYew-BvtNM|date=2025| accessdate =29 April 2025|via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> ''[[Kahaani Ghar Ghar Kii]]'', ''[[Kaahin Kissii Roz]]'', ''[[Kasautii Zindagii Kay (2001 TV series)|Kasautii Zindagii Kay]]'', ''[[Kahin to Hogaa|Kahiin to Hoga]]'', ''[[Kutumb]]'', ''[[Kkusum]]'', ''[[Kabhii Sautan Kabhii Sahelii]]'', ''[[Kis Desh Mein Hai Meraa Dil]]'' and ''[[Kasamh Se]]'' amongst several others.

==History==
The company was registered as 'Balaji Telefilms Private Limited' on 11 November 1994 in [[Mumbai]], [[India]], with the objective of creating [[Indian serial|serials]] and other entertainment content by [[Ekta Kapoor]] and [[Shobha Kapoor]]. Balaji has specialized in [[TV format|formatted programming]] that can be adapted for languages around the nation as well as abroad. The most notable success includes ''[[Kasautii Zindagii Kay (2001 TV series)|Kasautii Zindagii Kay]]'' where she introduced the biggest fictional characters like [[Prerna Sharma (character)|Prerna]] and [[Komolika (character)|Komolika]] and ''[[Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi]]''. Other examples include ''[[Kahaani Ghar Ghar Kii]]'', ''[[Kaahin Kissii Roz]]'', ''[[Kahiin to Hoga]]'', ''[[Kkusum]]'', ''[[Kutumb (TV series)|Kutumb]]'', ''[[Kohi Apna Sa]]'', ''[[Kasamh Se]]'', ''[[Kis Desh Mein Hai Meraa Dil]]'', ''[[Pavitra Rishta]]'', ''[[Parichay (TV series)|Parichay]]'', ''[[Kya Hua Tera Vaada]]'', ''[[Jodha Akbar (TV series)|Jodha Akbar]]'', ''[[Tere Liye (TV series)|Tere Liye]]'', ''[[Bade Achhe Lagte Hain]]'', ''[[Yeh Hai Mohabbatein]]'', ''[[Naagin (2015 TV series)|Naagin]]'', ''[[Kasam Tere Pyaar Ki]]'', ''[[Kumkum Bhagya]]'', ''[[Bhagya Lakshmi]]'' and ''[[Kundali Bhagya]]''. The later five are dubbed and re-produced in several languages across [[India]] and [[Asia]]. In recent years the company has been expanding its [[reality show]] output with shows such as titles such as ''Box Cricket League'' on [[Set india|Sony TV]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Balaji Telefilms in association with Marinating Films to create Box Cricket League for Sony TV |url=https://www.exchange4media.com/advertising-news/balaji-telefilms-hands-over-sales-mandate-of-box-cricket-league-to-aidem-ventures-62906.html |website=Exchange4Media}}</ref>

Balaji was incorporated as a public limited company on 29 February 2000, and its name was changed to 'Balaji Telefilms Ltd' on 19 April 2000.<ref name="History">{{Cite web|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/balaji-telefilms-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-3376.cms|title=Balaji Telefilms History &#124; Balaji Telefilms Information|website=The Economic Times}}</ref> The company made public issue of 28,00,000 equity shares of {{INR}}10 each at a premium of {{INR}}120 aggregating {{INR}}36.40 crore. The issue included a book-built portion of 25,20,000 equity shares and a fixed price portion of 2,80,000 equity shares.<ref name="History"/> In the same year, Nine Network Entertainment India Pvt. Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Nine Broadcasting India Pvt. Ltd., merged with Balaji Telefilms Ltd.<ref name="History"/> During 2000–04 the stock market capitalization grew sixteenfold to {{INR}}571 crores when Star India acquired a 26% stake in the business.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/Star-arm-to-buy-26-pc-in-Balaji/articleshow/820007.cms|title=Star arm to buy 26 pc in Balaji – Times of India|website=The Times of India|date=19 August 2004 }}</ref> In 2005, Balaji Telefilms had 21 Hindi television shows on air at the same time, a record in the industry.

Balaji Telefilms started a media training institute in 2010. Known as ICE Institute of Creative Excellence,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ekta Kapoor's Acting Schools in Delhi & Mumbai, India – ICE Institute |url=https://www.theiceinstitute.com/ |access-date=30 December 2022 |website=Ekta Kapoor's Acting Institute |language=en-US}}</ref> it trains students in acting, cinematography, direction, modelling, etc.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.balajitelefilms.com/indus-balaji-fund.php|title=Balaji Telefilms Limited : Television, Motion Pictures|website=balajitelefilms.com|access-date=16 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiantelevision.com/release/y2k12/may/mayrel25.php|title=Balaji Telefilms launches training academy in filmmaking|date=15 May 2012|website=Indian Television Dot Com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tellychakkar.com/movie/movie-news/ekta-kapoors-ice-sets-campus-delhi|title=Ekta Kapoor's ICE sets up campus in Delhi|first=Tellychakkar|last=Team|website=Tellychakkar.com}}</ref>
<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiainfoline.com/article/news-top-story/balaji-telefilms-to-start-chain-of-acting-editing-schools-113101802393_1.html|title=Balaji Telefilms to start chain of acting, editing schools|website=indiainfoline.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiawest.com/entertainment/bollywood/institute-of-creative-excellence-launches-delhi-campus/article_097ce613-5504-5cd1-a8eb-be9d6d4dc056.html|title=Institute of Creative Excellence Launches Delhi Campus|first=R. M. Vijayakar, Special to|last=India-West|website=India West}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.firstpost.com/fwire/now-ekta-kapoor-in-front-of-the-camera-293541.html|title=Now, Ekta Kapoor in front of the camera|website=Firstpost|date=30 April 2012 }}</ref>

In 2014, the company and Ekta Kapoor were subject to protests in [[Jaipur]] led by the [[Shri Rajput Karni Sena]] (SRKS), a [[Hindutva]] group. These occurred because of perceived communal slights in the ''Jodha Akbar'' television series.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.newindianexpress.com/entertainment/television/Rajput-Karni-Sena-Shout-Slogans-at-Ekta-Kapoor-During-Jaipur-Lit-Fest/2014/01/21/article2011905.ece |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140122062530/http://www.newindianexpress.com/entertainment/television/Rajput-Karni-Sena-Shout-Slogans-at-Ekta-Kapoor-During-Jaipur-Lit-Fest/2014/01/21/article2011905.ece |url-status=dead |archive-date=22 January 2014 |title=Rajput Karni Sena Shout Slogans at Ekta Kapoor During Jaipur Lit Fest |agency=IANS |date=21 January 2014 |work=The New Indian Express |access-date=14 April 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/other-states/journalists-demand-arrest-of-karni-sena-president/article5730441.ece |work=The Hindu |date=27 February 2014 |title=Journalists demand arrest of Karni Sena president |first=Mahim Pratap |last=Singh |access-date=15 April 2015}}</ref>

In 2015, Balaji Telefilms produced a finite series, ''[[Naagin (2015 TV series)|Naagin]]'', which became the most viewed show on Indian television since its inception. The show won multiple awards and returned for its second and third season, which also generated high ratings. The fourth season of series was broadcast starting in December 2019 but it was not doing well on television so it was replaced by the fifth season of the series in August 2020.<ref name="Naagin-1-Launch">{{cite web |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/entertainment/photo/ekta-kapoors-naagin-launched-mouni-roy-adaa-khan-arjun-bijlani-bring-saga-of-love-and-revenge-376608-2015-10-27 |title=Ekta Kapoor's Naagin launched: Mouni, Adaa, Arjun bring saga of love and revenge |date=27 October 2015 |website=India Today}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/tv/news/hindi/arjun-bijlani-back-with-mouni-roy-in-naagin-season-2/articleshow/54562640.cms|title=Arjun Bijlani back with Mouni Roy in Naagin season 2 – Times of India|website=The Times of India}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dnaindia.com/entertainment/report-all-you-need-to-know-about-naagin-season-2-2187633 |title=All you need to know about Naagin season 2! – Latest News & Updates at Daily News & Analysis |date=10 March 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/television/soaps/story/watch-naagin-season-2-will-be-back-in-october-watch-the-trailer-lifetv-12677-2016-06-06 |title=Naagin Season 2 will be back in October; watch the trailer |date=6 June 2016 |website=India Today}}</ref>

In 2017, [[Reliance Industries]] acquired a 25% stake in Balaji Telefilms for Rs413 crore. The deal gave RIL access to Balaji Telefilms' content for use by telecom unit Reliance Jio.<ref name="RIL buys 25% stake in Balaji Telefilms for Rs 413 crore">{{cite news |last1=Choudhary |first1=Vidhi |title=RIL buys 25% stake in Balaji Telefilms for Rs413 crore |url=http://www.livemint.com/Companies/bKu1z9YYSqfVqo8HT4N1xM/RIL-buys-25-stake-in-Balaji-Telefilms-for-Rs413-crore.html |access-date=21 July 2017 |publisher=LiveMint}}</ref>

'''''Dastaan''''' ({{langx|ur|{{Nastaliq|داستان}}}}, {{Literal translation|The tale}}) is a Pakistani television series based on the 1971 novel ''[[Bano (novel)|Bano]]'' by [[Razia Butt]].<ref name="history">{{Cite news|url=https://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/8103/dastaan-history-on-tv/|title=Dastaan: History on TV|access-date=2018-07-24|language=en-US|date=September 24, 2011|first=Taneeya|last=Hasan|work=[[Express Tribune]]|archive-date=24 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180724213312/https://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/8103/dastaan-history-on-tv/|url-status=live}}</ref> Dramatized by author and screenwriter [[Samira Fazal]], it originally aired on [[Hum TV]] in 2010. It is set amidst the [[partition of India]] and the [[Independence Day (Pakistan)|establishment of Pakistan]], taking place between [[Dominion of Pakistan|1947 and 1956]]. It depicts the story of Bano, a Muslim girl from a close-knit family living in [[Ludhiana]], [[Punjab Province (British India)|Punjab Province]]; the plot revolves around the trials and tribulations that she faces after she decides to dedicate her life to the [[All-India Muslim League]].

Director [[Haissam Hussain]] stated in an interview that production for the drama began months in advance and that the filming only took a little over two months.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://vidpk.com/41855/Morning-With-Hum-Momina-Duraid--Haissam-Hussain--Mehreen-Raheel--Sanam-Baloch-P-2|title=Morning With Hum|url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101210060120/http://vidpk.com/41855/Morning-With-Hum-Momina-Duraid--Haissam-Hussain--Mehreen-Raheel--Sanam-Baloch-P-2/ |archive-date=10 December 2010}}/</ref>

== Plot ==
Based on the true events of the [[Partition of India|partition of India in 1947]], the series depicts the events of rioting and chaos in 1947.

Based on the novel [[Bano (novel)|Bano]], ''Dastaan'' begins with the wedding of Suraiya and Salim. Suraiya's nephew Hassan was the son of Rasheeda. When Hassan's father died, he and his mother were kicked out of his father's house by his paternal family which was in [[Jalandhar]], and they moved back to Rasheeda's maternal house in [[Ludhiana]].

Bano, Suraiya, Faheem, Salim and Hassan were childhood friends, and all grew up together. When Hassan went to the university, he left home and went to Islamia College in [[Peshawar]]. Hassan returns for Saleem and Suraiya's wedding, where Hassan and Bano meet for the first time as adults after three years. The whole family gathered for the wedding, including Hassan's aunt Jameela from [[Amritsar]], his aunt Sultana and her daughter Rabia from [[Lahore]] or [[Rawalpindi|Pindi]].

Hassan spent most of his time at the wedding preaching the Quaid's message and the rest of it teasing his cousin Rabia and flirting with Bano. Although Rabia was only 14 years old and Hassan thought of her as a younger sister, she started developing feelings for him. As Hassan starts teasing and flirting with Bano, they slowly begin to develop feelings for each other, with Hassan visiting [[Ludhiana]] every now and then.

He is a final year engineering student at the [[Islamia College (Lahore)|Islamia College]], an active supporter of the [[All-India Muslim League]], and the leader of the Ludhiana Branch. He strongly believes in the establishment of Pakistan and is an avid follower of [[Muhammad Ali Jinnah|Qaid-E-Azam]], the head of the Muslim League and [[Pakistan Movement]]. Saleem is an activist of the [[Indian National Congress]], with all his friends being [[Hindu]]. He strictly believes that the creation of Pakistan will not help but lessen the position of Muslims in India.

The political debate between Saleem and Hassan begins as friendly competition, but it intensifies as conditions worsen throughout India for Muslims. Saleem, hot-tempered and rash, begins bringing political debates into family life and eventually forbids Suraiya from visiting Hassan, her nephew. But Hassan is not dissuaded. He continues to spread the message of Pakistan throughout Saleem's family, causing Saleem's anger to explode on many occasions. Other than Saleem, his entire family becomes strong supporters of the Muslim League, especially Bano, who makes posters and signs for the Pakistan Movement.

Bibi tells Suraiya that a marriage proposal has come for Bano from [[Patiala]]. Suraiya panics and tells her sister Rashida that Bano and Hassan like each other and have become close. She tells her that if they don't get married, then Bano will commit suicide, and Hassan will not marry anyone else either. Upon hearing this, Rashida takes her brother and sister-in-law and asks for Bano's hand in marriage for Hassan. Saleem overhears this and politely tells them they can leave because a proposal has come for Bano. Bano's parents become angry and ask Saleem who he has in mind, and Saleem tells them about his Hindu friend Ram. His parents immediately agree to Bano's proposal with Hassan. Hassan and Bano eventually become engaged, and Saleem decides to leave behind his rivalry with Hassan for Bano's sake. Soon, Hassan gets a job in [[Rawalpindi]] and has to leave immediately. He leaves Ludhiana with the promise that they will return four months later for the wedding. Meanwhile, Suraiya is four months pregnant.

During this time, tensions between [[Hindus]] and [[Muslims]] escalate dramatically, and violence breaks out all across India. Hate crimes against Muslims become common, and fighting spreads to all states, getting threateningly closer to Ludhiana. As the riots become more pronounced, Muslims retaliate, leaving nobody safe. Saleem seems to be under the impression that his Hindu friends and their families will be able to protect his family from rioters. However, he soon feels they are distant and aloof and realises he is wrong.

On a fateful night, a group of [[Sikhs]] and Hindus attack the family's home. All the men (which includes many other Muslims who sought refuge in their house) stay on the bottom floor with their swords and knives intending to fight. All the women (including Bano, Suraiya, and Bano's mother, Bibi, Sakina Khala and her daughters) are hiding on the roof of their house. All the men get killed brutally, while the women were raped and killed. Some women committed suicide to save themselves from that fate. Bano and Bibi, however, survive and are 'rescued' by Salim's Hindu friends.

Saleem's friend, Ram, tries to rape Bano, but his other friend saves her by killing Ram out of guilt. Bano and Bibi manage to escape Ludhiana, where they seek shelter in a refugee camp for Muslims. The [[Muslim]] refugees are led by a young brave Muslim man who lost his entire family. Thirsty and hungry, they try to walk to Pakistan, encountering poisoned wells along the way. Eventually, Hindu rioters attack this caravan. Bano and Bibi are separated, and both are gang raped. Bano crawls toward her mother's lifeless body, seeing her [[Ta'wiz]] necklace. Bano, grief-stricken and in shock, wears it and lies next to her body.

A Sikh man stumbles upon Bano and her dead mother, and he helps nurse her back to health. He then boards her on a train, heading from [[Jalandhar]] towards [[Lahore]] and leaves. It was common for trains to arrive in Lahore full of dead Muslims with only a few survivors and vice versa. Soon this train is attacked by rioters. Basant Singh, a rioter, chases after Bano on the train. She falls unconscious, and Basant Singh kidnaps her, bringing her to his home in [[Kapurthala]]. Bano awakens in the house where he and his mother live. At first, she refuses to tell them her name, so Basant Singh calls her Sundar [[Kaur]], meaning "beautiful lioness" in [[Punjabi language|Punjabi]]. He gives her the impression that he will take her to Pakistan once there is no danger. He also tells her she can write to Hassan, and he'll deliver the letters. Bano believes his lies and cannot wait to go to Pakistan.

Nearly a year later, Basant has not lived up to his promise, claiming that the roadways are blocked and travelling to Pakistan is too dangerous. Eventually, Bano learns of his plan to forcibly marry and convert her, and she attempts to run away again. This time though, when Basant catches her, he doesn't treat her gently as he did the first time. He spends the next five years beating, raping, and emotionally torturing Bano after forcibly marrying and converting her. However, she doesn't give up and makes his blood boil by shouting abuses at him and never forgetting that she is a Muslim. One day, Basant dies as he tries to save their infant son Bhagat Singh as he's about to fall from the roof. Bano takes her son and migrates to Pakistan.

In Pakistan, Hassan undergoes severe depression after realising that Suraiyyah, Bano and their other relatives must have been brutally raped and killed. He goes from a friendly extrovert to a miserable reserved person. For the next five years, his mother did not see him laugh. Seeing this, she asks him to get married, but he disagrees as he believes himself to be married to Bano. One day, Sultana, his aunt, with her children, visit them. Hassan is excited after a long time to meet his only surviving family, especially Rabia. Expecting the same fourteen-year-old child with ponytails whom he could tease again, he's astonished when he encounters a young woman instead. Hassan becomes distant from her as he senses her feelings. However, it's been five years since Bano's 'death', and he needs to move on. Later Rabia and her mother moved from [[Karachi]] to [[Lahore]] to meet Hassan and her mother. He tries to find Bano in Rabia and soon gets engaged to her.

Bano ends up in a shelter for refugees. The caretaker woman writes a letter to Hassan asking him to come and take Bano.

Hassan receives the letter and takes Bano and the child home. Hassan decides to marry Bano and wants to break off his engagement to Rabia. Rabia and her mother learn this and visit Hassan's house. Rabia's mother tells Rabia to take care of Bano to please Hassan. However, one day, he overhears a conversation between his parents about Rabia taking care of Bano so Hassan can see the goodness in her. He argues with Rabia, but Rabia insists that her love is truer than Bano's. Bano overhears this and interrupts them telling them that if they truly want to do something for her, they should get married. The next day, Hassan finds out that Bano has left the house. Hassan spends many days and weeks searching for Bano. He blames Rabia for this. Bano is living with a family where she does their household chores. She gets a job in a modern family where she realises Pakistan is not how she thought it would be. They fire her from the job. One day Hassan sees her in the mosque, and he runs after her to get her back home, but Bano asks her friend to go to Hassan and ask him to forget Bano. Hassan then goes home and agrees to marry Rabia as Bano had wished for their marriage. One day she goes to a birthday party where she meets a gentleman with similar thoughts to those of Bano. He offers Bano to come and work in his office, where they work for the welfare of people. Bano is happy and accepts his proposal.

One day, Rabia learns of Bano's whereabouts, and she begs her to marry Hassan. Eventually, Bano agrees and promises that she will come. She goes to her office, where the same gentleman leads her to the storage room and attempts to abuse her, but she stabs him to death. The police arrest her. Bano goes to a mental asylum for recovery. Later, Hassan and Rabia, now husband and wife, visit Bano.

==Soundtrack==
The ''Dastaan'' theme, "Aasmanon Se", was [[Composer|composed]] and [[Singing|sung]] by Sohail Haider and was written by Sahir Altaf. A frequent background music on the show played during scenes asserting Pakistani [[independence]] and Pakistani pride is based on the tune of [[List of songs about Pakistan|Aye Watan Pyare Watan]] by [[Ustad Amanat Ali Khan]].

== Production ==
===Development and background===
When asked to choose [[Razia Butt]]'s novel ''[[Bano (novel)|Bano]]'' as the inspiration for ''Dastaan'', Haissam Hussain revealed that, about three years ago, he had directed a telefilm by [[Umera Ahmad]], ''[[Mutthi Bhar Mitti]]'', which received a great response. Consequently, he and producer Momina Duraid decided to work on a project based on the theme of [[Partition of India|Partition]]. Razia Butt's novel ''Bano'' provided the perfect opportunity to pursue this theme.<ref>{{cite web | url= https://tribune.com.pk/story/268234/%E2%80%98dastaan%E2%80%99-reflecting-the-indo-pak-divide | title= Dastaan': Reflecting the Indo-Pak divide | accessdate= February 8, 2021 | publisher= [[Express Tribune]] | date= October 6, 2011 | first= Saadia | last= Qamar | archive-date= 11 March 2022 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220311155542/https://tribune.com.pk/story/268234/%E2%80%98dastaan%E2%80%99-reflecting-the-indo-pak-divide | url-status= live }}</ref>

Duraid revealed that she had read the novel ''Bano'' in her childhood and initially wanted to create a play about the Partition era. However, she was discouraged, as many believed it would be unsuccessful due to a perceived lack of interest in Partition-themed dramas.<ref>{{cite web| url= https://aurora.dawn.com/news/1141908| title= "We should make trends, and then break trends"| date= 28 August 2018| accessdate= February 8, 2021| publisher= aurora.dawn| archive-date= 27 February 2022| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220227213910/https://aurora.dawn.com/news/1141908| url-status= live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1164419 | title=Humsafar was rejected by two production houses: Momina Duraid | accessdate=February 8, 2021 | work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] | first=Zoya | last=Anwer | date=February 18, 2015 | archive-date=26 October 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201026213514/https://www.dawn.com/news/1164419 | url-status=live }}</ref> Undeterred, Duraid decided to adapt the novel ''Bano'' into a play. She met with Razia Butt, the novel's author, who entrusted Duraid with her work, saying, "I'm giving you my precious thing, make it good."

===Production locations===

The [[principal photography]] takes place at a number of locations, primarily in [[Lahore, Pakistan|Lahore]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/amp/76163-snip-snap-fawad-khan-and-sanam-balochs-dastaan-gets-an-indian-makeover|title=Snip snap: Fawad Khan and Sanam Baloch's Dastaan gets an Indian makeover|date=27 March 2015|work=[[The News International]]|language=en-US}}</ref> It starts out at a neighborhood of Lahore, which was portrayed as [[Ludhiana]], India. The location changed with every couple of episodes as the story corresponds. Other locations include [[Karachi]], [[Rawalpindi]], and [[Kapurthala]]. Other notable locations include the [[Islamia College (Lahore)|Islamia College]], [[Badshahi Mosque]] and [[Lahore Junction railway station]].

== Release ==

===International broadcast===
''Dastaan'' was aired in [[Middle East]] on [[MBC Bollywood]] under the title ''حب عبر الحدود'' (transl. ''Love Across Borders'').<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/76163-snip-snap-fawad-khan-and-sanam-balochs-dastaan-gets-an-indian-makeover | title = Snip snap: Fawad Khan and Sanam Baloch's Dastaan gets an Indian makeover | accessdate = February 8, 2021 | publisher = [[The News International]] | archive-date = 11 March 2022 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20220311154009/https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/76163-snip-snap-fawad-khan-and-sanam-balochs-dastaan-gets-an-indian-makeover | url-status = live }}</ref> It aired in India on [[Zindagi (TV channel)|Zindagi]] as [[Waqt Ne Kiya Kya Haseen Sitam (TV series)|''Waqt Ne Kiya Kya Haseen Sitam'']] from March 23, 2015. Previously, the show was to be titled ''Lakeerein.''<ref>{{cite web | url = https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/play/from-the-other-side/ | title = Fawad Khan's Pakistani show 'Waqt Ne Kiya Kya Haseen Sitam' is a partition love story | accessdate = February 8, 2021 | publisher = [[Indian Express]] | first = Somya | last = Lakhani | date = 27 March 2015 | archive-date = 29 April 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150429141936/http://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/play/from-the-other-side/ | url-status = live }}</ref> In [[UK|the UK]], the show was broadcast on [[Hum Europe]], premiering on September 19, 2015.<ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.bizasialive.com/hum-tv-to-air-fawad-khan-drama-dastaan-in-uk/ | title= Hum TV to air Fawad Khan drama 'Dastaan' in UK | date= 12 September 2015 | accessdate= February 8, 2021 | publisher= bizasialive | archive-date= 11 March 2022 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220311155538/https://www.bizasialive.com/hum-tv-to-air-fawad-khan-drama-dastaan-in-uk/ | url-status= live }}</ref>

===Home media and digital release===
The show was available for online streaming on [[Iflix]] from 2017 to 2019 and on the Indian streaming platform [[Eros Now]]. Hum TV uploaded the series on its official [[YouTube]] channel in May 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ماضی کا مقبول ڈرامہ 'داستان' آن لائن ریلیز|url=https://www.dawnnews.tv/news/1104256/|date=September 2020|access-date=6 September 2020|archive-date=8 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211208000511/https://www.dawnnews.tv/news/1104256/|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Reception==

=== Critical reception ===
''Dastaan'' was widely appreciated by the viewers and received positive reviews from critics due to its subject, genre, performances and direction.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1582900/mahira-khan-gushes-fawad-sanams-blockbuster-drama-dastaan-twitter-agrees|title=Mahira Khan gushes over Fawad, Sanam's blockbuster drama 'Dastaan' and Twitter agrees|access-date=8 February 2021|work=[[Express Tribune]]|date=13 December 2017|first=Entertainment|author=Entertainment Desk|language=en-US|archive-date=11 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220311155537/https://tribune.com.pk/story/1582900/mahira-khan-gushes-fawad-sanams-blockbuster-drama-dastaan-twitter-agrees|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="history"/><ref>{{cite web|date=20 July 2016|url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/68995/20-pakistani-tv-dramas-that-you-should-watch-if-you-havent/|title=20 Pakistani TV dramas that you should watch if you haven't|website=Daily Times|access-date=22 May 2021|archive-date=24 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210924011239/https://dailytimes.com.pk/68995/20-pakistani-tv-dramas-that-you-should-watch-if-you-havent/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tvkahani.com/five-characters-well-remember-forever/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130218174055/http://www.tvkahani.com/five-characters-well-remember-forever/|title=Five Characters We'll Remember Forever|date=12 February 2013|access-date=|archive-date=18 February 2013|work=TV Kahani}}</ref> In a poll by ''[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]]'', ''Dastaan'' was rated as the second best drama of 2010, after ''Dolly ki Ayegi Baraat'', which aired on Geo Entertainment, and [[Sanam Baloch]] was voted best actress for ''Dastaan'', with [[Mehreen Raheel]] in third place, while [[Samira Fazal]] was voted third best writer, also for ''Dastaan.''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/593734/opinion-poll-who-ruled-2010|title=Opinion Poll: Who ruled 2010?|first=From|last=InpaperMagazine|date=26 December 2010 |work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] |access-date=2 May 2020|archive-date=14 October
