TV Kahani. The review said: "Please, do yourself a favor and watch this one. You will learn and be entertained at the same time."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tvkahani.com/reviews-dastaan-hum-tv-review/|title=Reviews: Dastaan HUM TV Review|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140131085246/http://www.tvkahani.com/reviews-dastaan-hum-tv-review/|archive-date=31 January 2014|work=TV Kahani|date=18 October 2012}}</ref> ''[[The News International]]'' praised it for illustrating minority representation with sensitivity.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/tns/detail/562533-burden-representation|title=The burden of representation|date=22 January 2017|access-date=22 November 2022|work=The News International|archive-date=22 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221122141800/https://www.thenews.com.pk/tns/detail/562533-burden-representation|author=Sadaf Haider}}</ref>

''[[DAWN Images]]'' ranked it as most iconic TV drama of Pakistan, praising the direction and for balancing the historical details and political sensitivities.<ref name="Iconic">{{Cite web |last=Haider |first=Sadaf |date=March 28, 2020 |title=10 iconic Pakistani TV dramas you should binge-watch this weekend |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1176410 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808000607/https://images.dawn.com/news/1176410 |archive-date=8 August 2017 |accessdate=2021-02-08 |publisher=Dawn Images}}</ref> ''[[People Magazine]] Pakistan'' included it amaong the best work on partition of the Indian subcontinent.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://peoplepakistan.com/2020/08/best-content-based-on-indo-pak-partition/ |title=Best Content Based On Indo-Pak Partition |date=13 August 2020 |work=People Magazine |archive-date=18 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210418142959/https://peoplepakistan.com/2020/08/best-content-based-on-indo-pak-partition/ |url-status=live |access-date=3 July 2024}}</ref>

===Reaction from India===
A notice was issued by Justice Mukul Mudgal against Zindagi on account of complaints received by the [[Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (India)|Indian Ministry of Broadcasting and Information]]. It stated that the show had depicted Indians in a bad light.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/tv/news/hindi/Notice-to-Zindagi-channel-on-pro-Pak-serial/articleshow/47218707.cms|title=Notice to Zindagi channel on 'pro-Pak' serial - Times of India|website=The Times of India|last1=Dhawan|first1=Himanshi|access-date=2 May 2020|archive-date=6 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190906205434/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/tv/news/hindi/Notice-to-Zindagi-channel-on-pro-Pak-serial/articleshow/47218707.cms|url-status=live}}</ref>

<!-- As per [[WP:MOSBEGIN]] the lead paragraph shall be illustrated in the way provided below, this paragraph has been compared by [[WP:MOSBEGIN]] illustrated point, removal of item such as premier dates, timings, stories, leading crew members etc will be wrong, these details are required by wikipedia and are provided, they should not be removed. '''''Diyar-e-Dil''''' ({{langx|ur|{{Nastaliq|دیارِدل}}}}; {{lit|''The Dominion of the Heart''}}) (also known as ''Dayar-e-Dil'')<ref>{{cite web|title=Diyar-e-Dil – The City of Heart|url=http://blogs.humnetwork.com/dayaar-e-dill-city-of-heart/|publisher=[[Hum TV]]|date=16 March 2015|access-date=5 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150325045218/http://blogs.humnetwork.com/dayaar-e-dill-city-of-heart/|archive-date=25 March 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> is a Pakistani television [[Pakistani drama|drama serial]], that originally aired on [[Hum TV]] from 17 March 2015 to 27 October 2015, in [[List of Diyar-e-Dil episodes|33 episodes]].<ref name="Hum TV Programming schedule">{{cite web|title=Hum TV Programming schedule|url=http://www.hum.tv/schedule.php|publisher=[[Hum TV]]|access-date=24 September 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151007033151/http://www.hum.tv/schedule.php|archive-date=7 October 2015|df=dmy-all}}</ref><ref name="timings" />''Diyar-e-Dil'' follows the lives of a dysfunctional family led by [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters#Protagonist|Agha Jaan]] and his grandchildren, [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters#Protagonists|Wali]] and [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters#Protagonists|Faarah]]. The story is told in a heavily serialized manner. It revolves around the lives of [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters#Protagonists|Wali]] and [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters#Protagonists|Faarah]], who were forced to commit to each other for the cause of reuniting their family, which had fallen apart long ago because of Agha Jaan's eldest son [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters#Protagonists|Behroze]], when he called off his long engagement to marry his late love interest.

''Diyar-e-Dil'' features an ensemble cast with [[Abid Ali (actor)|Abid Ali]] as [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters#Protagonist|Bakhtiyar Ahmed Khan]], [[Osman Khalid Butt]] and [[Maya Ali (actress)|Maya Ali]] as his grandchildren [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters#Protagonists|Wali Suhaib Khan]] and [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters#Protagonists|Faarah Wali Khan]], [[Meekal Zulfiqar]], [[Ali Rehman Khan]] as his children [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters#Protagonists|Behroze Bakhtiyar Khan]] and [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters#Protagonists|Suhaib Bakthiyar Khan]] and [[Sanam Saeed]], [[Hareem Farooq]] as his daughters-in-law [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters#Protagonsts|Ruhina Behroze Khan]] and [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters#Protagonists|Arjumand Suhaib Khan]].<ref name=Akhtar>{{cite web|title=Diyar-e-dil: The only drama portraying the true dynamics of a tribal family in Pakistan|date=16 October 2015|access-date=11 December 2015|work=Almas Akhtar|publisher=Express Tribune|url=http://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/29829/diyar-e-dil-the-only-drama-portraying-the-true-dynamics-of-a-tribal-family-in-pakistan/}}</ref><ref name="Shoting for ded"/> It also stars [[Behroze Sabzwari]], [[Tara Mahmood]], Ahmad Zeb and [[Mariyam Nafees]] in recurring roles.<ref name=HIP>{{cite web|title=Still waiting for Diyar-e-Dil to take off|publisher=HIP|access-date=6 December 2015|url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1147046|work=Rozina Bhutto|date=22 April 2015}}</ref> It was created by [[Momina Duraid]], and aired on Hum TV as part of night programming under Duraid's [[MD Productions|production company]]. It was written by [[Farhat Ishtiaq]] based on her [[Dayar-e-Dil (novella)|novel of the same name]] and directed by [[Haseeb Hassan]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Diyar-i-dil-An upcoming drama serial by Farhat Ishtiaq|url=http://gossip.pk/2014/08/13/dayar-e-dil-upcoming-drama-based-farhat-ishtiaq-novel/|access-date=13 January 2015|archive-date=14 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150614050133/http://gossip.pk/2014/08/13/dayar-e-dil-upcoming-drama-based-farhat-ishtiaq-novel/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The show is set in [[Skardo|Skardu]], [[Gilgit–Baltistan]] and [[Karachi]], [[Sindh]]. ''Diyar-e-Dil'' premiered in Pakistan, the UK, USA and UAE on 17 March 2015, with prime slot on Tuesdays.<ref name=DDtimings>{{cite web|title=Hum TV to launch 'Dayar-E-Dil' in Tuesday slot|url=http://www.media247.co.uk/bizasia/hum-tv-to-launch-dayar-e-dil-in-tuesday-slot-2015|publisher=Media24/7|date=16 March 2015|access-date=5 April 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150411042511/http://www.media247.co.uk/bizasia/hum-tv-to-launch-dayar-e-dil-in-tuesday-slot-2015|archive-date=11 April 2015|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

''Diyar-e-Dil'' was 2015's highest rated and most acclaimed program of Pakistan.<ref name="A legacy of love: Diyar-e-Dil">{{cite web|title=A legacy of love: Diyar-e-Dil|url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1146854/|work=Sheeba Khan|publisher=HIP|date=20 March 2015|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref><ref name="Diyar-e-Dil hits home by stressing">{{cite news |title=Diyar-e-Dil hits home by stressing family values |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1189967/diyar-e-dil-hits-home-by-stressing-family-values |first=Sdaf |last=Haider |work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] |date=25 June 2015 |access-date=25 September 2015}}</ref> It received critical appraisal for being visually-appealing for the male audience, due to the maintenance of their relationships in the story,<ref name="dawn.com"/> and was praised for its direction, cinematography and visuals.<ref name="Dawn News">{{cite news |title=''Diyar-e-Dil'' opens with a bang and is a visual treat |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1170348/review-diyar-e-dil-opens-with-a-bang-and-is-a-visual-treat |first=Sadaf |last=Haider |work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] |date=19 March 2015 |access-date=7 April 2015}}</ref> It was the most awarded show at [[4th Hum Awards]], and won awards for [[Hum Award for Best Drama Serial|Best Drama Serial - Jury]] and [[Hum Award for Best Drama Serial Popular|Best Drama Serial - Popular]]. At [[15th Lux Style Awards]], it won two awards including [[Lux Style Award for Best TV Play|Best TV Play]] out of six nominations.

==Premise==
{{main|Dayar-e-Dil (novella)|l1=Synopsis of Diyar-e-Dil|List of Diyar-e-Dil episodes}} 
''Diyar-e-Dil'' depicted the story of [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters|Bakhtiyar Khan / Agha Jan]] ([[Abid Ali (actor)|Abid Ali]]) and his family. Agha Jan's family parted ways a long time ago due to the rebelliousness of his son, [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters|Behroze Bakhtiyar Khan]] ([[Meekal Zulfiqar|Mekal Zulfiqar]]) as he refused to marry a woman of his father's choice [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters|Arjumand Bedar Khan]] ([[Hareem Farooq]]) and went on to marry his college love interest [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters|Ruhina Arsalan]] ([[Sanam Saeed]]) instead. After getting disowned by his father, Behroze left his city to marry Ruhina, while Arjumand was forced to marry Behroze's younger brother, [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters|Suhaib Bakhtiyar Khan]] ([[Ali Rehman Khan]]). Soon after his marriage when Behroze came back to apologise to Agha Jaan, he and his wife were insulted and banished for life. This left the two bitter towards Agha Jaan’s family and they chose to continue their a newly married journey in away from his city. The two couples navigated various problems in their marriage, which for Behroze and Ruhina were financial problems, and for Sohaib and Arjumand were emotional disconnect. The series then focused on the transitioning of their life after marriage and showed how Suhaib and Arjumand grew close and fell in love after the birth of their son [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters|Wali Suhaib Khan]] ([[Osman Khalid Butt]]).  As Behroze and Ruhina gradually achieve financial stability, their lives begin to improve, and they welcome their daughter, [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters|Faarah Behroze Khan]] ([[Maya Ali (actress)|Maya Ali]]).

After twenty years, Behroze became a successful businessman, while Suhaib and Arjumand raise both their children with Agha Jan. Both the couples were settled and satisfied.  Despite the estrangement, Sohaib continues looking after his elder brother in hopes of reuniting the family. After Sohaib’s untimely death, Behroze finally came back home and reconciled with Agha Jaan. Their children were married, fulfilling Suhaib's last wish to reunite the family. Behroze and his family returned back to Lahore with Faarah’s rukhsati (the formal departure to her husband’s home) set to take place four years later, after she completes her graduation. However, Ruhina opposed this decision and, influenced by her brother [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters|Tajamul Arsalan]]’s ([[Behroze Sabzwari]])  manipulation, left Behroze, making her return conditional on him choosing between her and his father. As a result, Behroze was left heartbroken and died of grief. With the grief of her father's death, Farah never managed to connect with Agha Jaan and Wali, and if she ever managed to, she was pulled back by her mother. Her mother now pressured Agha Jaan to give them a monthly allowance for (Faarah’s care) that she spent on her brother and his wife. With constant persuasion of her mother, maternal uncle and cousin, Faraah demanded for a divorce from Wali along with her inheritance, which further increased tensions within the family and became the cause of Agha Jaan's developing illness. Faarah told her mother she did not want her inheritance to be used bh her mother, and that it was added to her divorce agreements without her choice, due to which Ruhi left the house in anger, leaving her daughter alone.

After Agha Jaan's second heart attack, Wali, driven by rage, kidnapped Faarah from her house and drove her to his summer resort, locking her in a room so she would not be able to escape. Once Faarah calmed down, Wali made an agreement with her; that if she agreed to live with Agha Jaan for three months, he would give her a divorce so she could marry her cousin Moeez (Ahmad Zeb) whom he thought she loved. Following the agreement Faarah grew attachment to the household. One night broke down infront of Agha Jan when she developed affection towards him, and realised her mistakes and lies told by her uncle [[List of Diyar-e-Dil characters|Tajamul Arsalan]] ([[Behroze Sabzwari]]) and mother. She eventually developed a soft corner for Wali, befriended his sister and chose to spend the rest of her life with Agha Jan. Tajamul and Moeez's truth was revealed to Ruhi after which she regretted her doings and was locked up by Moeez. He kidnapped Faarah to retain her inheritance to invest in his business, where Wali saved her and gets wounded of gun shot. Moeez ended up in jail, while Ruhi breaks all ties from her brother and reunites with Agha Jaan and her in-laws apologizing for her doings. Faarah admits her love for Wali the day her three-month contract was due, the two reconciled removing all the misconceptions they had in their hearts and complete the valley of heart (Diyar-e-Dil) paved by their fathers a long time ago.

==Background and production==
===Concept and development===
[[File:HaseebHasan.jpg|left|thumb|220px|Director of series, [[Haseeb Hassan]]]]

''Diyar-e-Dil'' was developed by [[Hum TV]]'s senior producer [[Momina Duraid]] of [[Moomal Productions|MD Productions]], the channel hired the award-winning director [[Haseeb Hassan]] to direct the series.<ref name='11 can'>{{cite web|title= 11 Pakistani dramas you can't miss the year|publisher= Express tribune|access-date=22 September 2015|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/853244/11-pakistani-dramas-you-cant-miss-this-year/|author=Alishba Nisar|date=18 March 2015}}</ref> Story of serial is based on award-winning writer [[Farhat Ishtiaq]]'s novel of the same name ''[[Dayar-e-Dil (novella)|Dayar-e-Dil]]'' with few variations.<ref>{{cite web|title=In Conversation With Real Brains Behind Bin Roye & Diyar-e-Dil|publisher=[[Hum TV]]|access-date=22 September 2015|date=15 June 2015|url=http://blogs.humnetwork.com/in-conversation-with-the-real-brains-behind-bin-roye-diyar-e-dil-farhat-ishtiaq-the-writer/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925102123/http://blogs.humnetwork.com/in-conversation-with-the-real-brains-behind-bin-roye-diyar-e-dil-farhat-ishtiaq-the-writer/|archive-date=25 September 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Dayar-e-Dil, A Drama Based on Farhat Ishtiaq Novel"/> Screenplay is also written by Ishtiaq while script composing is done by Muhammad Wasi-ul-Din. Farhat has previously worked twice with Momina, when she wrote mega-hit drama serial in Pakistan television history ''[[Humsafar]]''<ref>{{cite news |title= Popular Pakistani television drama Humsafar reaches Toronto fans via web| url =https://www.thestar.com/living/article/1132592--popular-pakistani-television-drama-humsafar-reaches-toronto-fans-in-via-web// |access-date= 29 February 2012 | work=The Star |date=16 February 2012}}</ref> and ''[[Mata-e-Jaan Hai Tu]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/335449/mata-e-jaan-hai-tu-composition-he-wrote/|title=Mata-e-Jaan Hai Tu drama serial's composition|newspaper=[[The Express Tribune]]|date=12 February 2012|access-date=25 February 2012}}</ref>

Song composition is done by Shany Haider while background music is given by Bilal Allah Ditta, who chose Zeb Bangash and Momin Durrani<ref>{{cite news|title=Musin and Momin Durrani go hand-in-hand|access-date=22 September 2015|date=21 June 2015|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/907432/music-and-momin-durrani-go-hand-in-hand/|newspaper=Express Tribune|author=Hasan Ansari}}</ref> for singing. The show approximately airs weekly episode for 35–40 minutes (minus commercials) every Tuesday.<ref name="DDtimings"/>
[[File:Dayar-e-Dil full cast.jpg|thumb|right|260px|''Diyar-e-Dill'' cast and crew in [[Skardo]] at [[Khaplu Palace]].]]
There were several discussions laid on its time slot, previously it was announced that the show will air on Friday's replacing ''[[Sadqay Tumhare]]'',<ref name='Dayar-e-Dil, A Drama Based on Farhat Ishtiaq Novel'>{{cite web|title=Dayar-e-Dil, A Drama Based on Farhat Ishtiaq Novel|url=http://trends4ever.com/pakistani-dramas/dayar-e-dil-a-drama-based-on-farhat-ishtiaq-novel.php#.VgFpWYuGklI|access-date=22 September 2015|archive-date=11 July 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220711074641/http://trends4ever.com/pakistani-dramas/dayar-e-dil-a-drama-based-on-farhat-ishtiaq-novel.php#.VgFpWYuGklI|url-status=dead}}</ref> and was also reported that the series will originally start its airing in April or May. However, due to promotional reasons the show was given a time slot of Tuesday, 8:00&nbsp;pm and the pilot episode was released on 17 March 2015,<ref name="DDtimings"/> replacing channel's drama series ''[[Zid (TV series)|Zid]]'' to Sundays.

===Writing===
The drama serial screenplay is also written by Ishtiaq. She explained that [[Momina Duraid]] gave her a full freedom of writing, while writing she discuss the story-line with Duraid and with mutual ideas and aspects Farhat wrote the scripts and made changes in several drafts of screenplay. Farhat said, "I did everything I wanted to and as I wanted to. I had the havelis [hilly]  scenes planned out but was a bit scared ''ke'' it might be too much, but Momina made it happen and exactly like I had imagined it." Farhat wrote thirty plus episodes which she explained that "it isn't because it was the demand of the channel or producer, it is because that’s how I wrote it. You will see that it will not drag. But to do justice to the story (which revolves around 3 generations), the characters and their feelings, thirty plus episodes had to be written, otherwise ''bohut kuch reh jata''."<ref name="DDdev">{{cite web|last1=Khan |first1=Sheeba |title=Farhat Ishtiaq and Haseeb Hassan talk Diyar-e-Dil - The director and writer of the drama say they are working with a 'dream team'. |work=HIP |url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1146877/|date=23 March 2015|access-date=25 September 2015}}</ref>

In an interview with ''[[Hum TV]]'' Farhat states that, "Diyar-e-Dil as a novel was not my best thing. It could have been written better which I tried to do in the script. I personally feel ''Diyar-e-Dil''s script is far better than the original novel. I'm planning to rewrite ''Diyar-e-Dil'' novel with all the additions that I've made for the script. In my opinion ''Diyar e-Dil'' script is my best script till date. ''Diyar e Dil'' critics can disagree with me." Commenting on characters, she emphasized that they are based on, "Family ties, relationships and love. It was a journey which my characters took to find out whether love is enough for us or do we need blood relations also? Can a person survive without his/her parents, siblings and family? My characters chose different paths and some of them later regret their decisions. How one generation's mistakes bring troubles to the next generation was also a big problem which my characters faced."<ref>{{cite web|title=In Conversation with the Real Brains Behind Bin Roye & Diyar-e-Dil – Farhat Ishtiaq (The Writer)|url=http://blogs.humnetwork.com/in-conversation-with-the-real-brains-behind-bin-roye-diyar-e-dil-farhat-ishtiaq-the-writer/|work=Zeresch Gil|publisher=[[Hum Network]]|date=15 June 2015|access-date=24 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925102123/http://blogs.humnetwork.com/in-conversation-with-the-real-brains-behind-bin-roye-diyar-e-dil-farhat-ishtiaq-the-writer/|archive-date=25 September 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====Novella====
{{main|Dayar-e-Dil (novella)}} 
The entire story of the series is based on Ishtiaq's novella. While developing screenplay Farhat made several changes, in an interview she said, "There are some differences, but they are very positive. I wrote several drafts of this novel back in 2006. While adapting I took some scenes and situations from my earlier drafts of the novel. Interestingly Momina and I think on the same wavelength. She came up to me once and said Farhat, it would be great if the story had this and this and I said, that is what I had written in the earlier drafts and we just used those. In the novel, there were flashbacks here the story is very linear. Now we have a very strong linear story and I have strengthened the characters even more. I have really enjoyed this script and it was very difficult for me. There are so many characters and each with their feelings that I had to do justice to the feelings of all the characters. I Enjoyed the difficulty as I had also challenged myself."<ref>Farhat Ishtiaq (2015), Interview with HIP TV, {{cite web|last1=Khan |first1=Sheeba |title=Farhat and Haseeb talk DD|work=HIP |date=23 March 2015 |url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1146877}}</ref> Few characters were added, who only introduced namely in novel. Characters like, Laila, Ibrahim Feroze and parents of Arjumand, Yasmin and Bedar were expanded. Arjumand’s character itself had a less appearance in book while in serial it is one of leading character. Ruhina's miscarriage was also not written in the novel.

On 12 October 2014, actress [[Sanam Saeed]] joined the ongoing filming thereby confirming her role for ''Diyar-e-Dil''.<ref name="behind the scenes of Diyar e Dil"/> Saeed was offered the role of Ruhina <ref name="behind the scenes of Diyar e Dil"/> after the success of her role of Kashaf Murtaza in channel’s series ''[[Zindagi Gulzar Hai]]. ''<ref name="ZindagiTreat">{{cite news |title=Zindagi channel treats Indian viewers to the best Pakistani dramas on offer |work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] |date=20 July 2014 |access-date=24 September 2015 |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1122357}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The award for best Pakistani drama of 2013 goes to.|first=Sadaf |last=Haider |publisher=tribune|access-date=24 September 2015|date=30 December 2015|url=http://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/20351/the-award-for-best-pakistani-drama-of-2013-goes-to/}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Pakistani dramas in India|date=4 July 2014|access-date=24 September 2015|author=Arisha Meeraj|newspaper=Tribune|url=http://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/23091/pakistani-dramas-in-india-yay/}}</ref> Alongside Saeed, Mikaal Zulfiqar was cast to play the role of Behroze.<ref>{{cite news |work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] |date=1 December 2014 |title=I am too nice for 'Bigg Boss': Meekal Zulfiqar |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1148089}}</ref> Both marked their second appearance together as a couple after their TV Series Ek Kasak Reh Gayi. Actors [[Ali Rehman Khan]] and [[Hareem Farooq]] were cast to portray the roles of Arjumand and Suhaib after their success in shows ''[[Rishtay Kuch Adhooray Se]]'' and ''[[Mausam (TV series)|Mausam]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hareem Farooq|author=Nida Ahmad|date=31 January 2015|access-date=6 December 2015|url=http://www.fashionstown.com/pakistani-actress-hareem-farooq-dramas-pics-biography/}}</ref> It was their first appearance together as a couple. Production also chose [[Behroze Sabzwari]], Tara Mehmood, Azra Mansoor, [[Rasheed Naz]], Ahmed Zeb and [[Eshita Mehboob]] for the supporting roles of Tajamul, Zuhra, Yasmeen, Beddar, Moeez and Laila respectively.

[[Principal photography]] and filming began in late September 2014 and finished in early April 2015 <ref name="Shoting for ded">{{cite news |title=Shoting continues for Diyar-e-dil |url=http://dawnnews.altervista.org/shooting-continues-for-diyar-e-dil/?doing_wp_cron=1423134352.7484579086303710937500 |work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] |date=8 October 2014 |access-date=23 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151124162132/http://dawnnews.altervista.org/shooting-continues-for-diyar-e-dil/?doing_wp_cron=1423134352.7484579086303710937500 |archive-date=24 November 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="autogenerated1">{{cite web|title=Dayar e Dil Cast on the sets at Khaplu!|url=http://showbizpak.com/dayar-e-dil-upcoming-drama-on-hum-tv/|work=Sawara Khan|publisher=Showbiz PK|date=6 October 2014|access-date=5 April 2015|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304033411/http://showbizpak.com/dayar-e-dil-upcoming-drama-on-hum-tv/|url-status=dead}}</ref> with approximately 33 episodes.<ref name="DDdev"/> Shooting was extensively done in hilly areas of Pakistan, production house choose [[Khaplu Palace]] for pivotal shooting location, in [[Skardo]], [[Gilgit–Baltistan]]<ref name="autogenerated1"/> which was set as a Mansion. Episodes were also shot in [[Shangrila Resort]] and [[Shangrila Lake]] was shown in drop up scenes.<ref name="autogenerated1"/> 
In early March, channel released [[Promo (media)|promos]] of serial which were heavily praised for their shooting locations and cast. Series’s original sound track (OST) was recorded in January and was released in March 2015. The series was officially set to premier in May with Friday as prime time-slot. Teasers were released in February along with the OST of serial.

The [[title song]] of ''Diyar-e-Dil'' was composed by musician Shani Arshad who also did background music with Bilal Allah Ditta.The soundtrack consists of two songs, one in Urdu language and the other in Persian language. Lyrics for songs were written by [[Sabir Zafar]]. The lines of the song are frequently used during the course of the show. The songs are sung by [[Zeb and Haniya|Zebunnisa Bangash]] of duo [[Zeb and Haniya]] and Momin Durrani.  The original sound track was released on 14 March 2015 with the teaser trailer of serial. The song along with production is produced by [[Momina Duraid]] under her production company [[Momina Duraid Productions|M.D Productions]].

==Release and distribution==
===Broadcast===

Hum TV originally scheduled the series for Fridays slot, but ''Diyar-e-Dil'' aired an hourly episode on Tuesdays at 8:00&nbsp;p.m (Pakistan Standard Time).<ref name="Hum TV Programming schedule"/> During [[Ramadan]] the show timings were shifted to 9:00 pm. Series has also aired internationally, for North America, New Zealand, Australia and Middle East on [[Hum TV|Hum TV World]]. It aired on [[Hum Europe]] in UK and Europe,<ref name="timings">{{cite web|title=Diyar-e-dil|url=http://www.hum.tv/hum-europe/|access-date=27 December 2015}}</ref> on [[Hum TV|Hum TV USA]] in USA<ref name="timings"/> and [[Hum TV|Hum TV Mena]] on UAE.<ref name="timings"/> Later in 2021, show was dubbed in Pashto and was released on Hum Pashto 1. In 2022, it began airing in India under [[Zee Entertainment Enterprises]]'s distribution on their channel [[Zindagi (TV Channel)|Zee Zindagi]].

===Digital release and availability===
''Diyar-e-Dil's'' episodes went available on Hum TV's YouTube channel till its syndication. Furthermore In January 2017, it had its digital release on the [[iflix]] app, but was taken off the same year as per contracted. It was also made available on the [[Eros Now]] app. On August 16, 2020, the series was digitally released again on [[Hum TV]]'s [[YouTube]] channel, the same month, it also began streaming digitally in India under channel [[Zindagi (TV Channel)|Zee Zindagi]] on the [[ZEE5]] app.

===Critical reception===

Actors [[Abid Ali (actor)|Abid Ali]] and [[Osman Khalid Butt]] received immense acclaim for their portrayals. Sadaf Haider of the ''[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]]'' praised the series' direction, cinematography, characterisation and production saying, "As with any excellent start the only fear is whether team ''Diyar-e-Dil'' can maintain the standards it has now set. This serial is a must watch for any drama fan. Farhat Ishtiaq is a great storyteller but this time she has honed her script-writing skills too and Haseeb Hassan has managed to translate this with seamless ease to our screens."<ref name="Dawn News"/> She said that, "In many dramas we are shown protagonists, especially women who adapt with unnatural ease to each change of fortune. Director Haseeb Hassan has done a fabulous job of weaving this inter-generational story together combining beautiful cinematography and a fast paced, well-edited narrative to make a highly entertaining serial thus far."<ref name="dawn.com">{{cite news |title=In Diyar-e-Dil, male relationships finally get their due |date=24 April 2015 |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1177932 |work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] |access-date=24 April 2015}}</ref> In an issue of ''[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]]'' June 25, Sadaf said, "As a story, ''Diyar-e-Dil'' covers very traditional grounds: the honour and obedience we owe to our parents and the importance of family. These values are deeply ingrained in our culture, something the writer never questions but reinforces with each turn."<ref name="Diyar-e-Dil hits home by stressing"/>

Aruba Adil of ''[[Aaj News]]'' praises it story line and consensus that, "''Diyar-e-Dil'' is different from other soap drama serials". She went to state five reasons that makes it different including, location, cast, realistic relationships, subtle love stories and unpredictable ending.<ref>{{cite web|title=5 reasons Diya-re-Dil is different from other soap dramas|url=http://www.aaj.tv/2015/07/5-reasons-diya-re-dil-is-different-from-other-soap-drama-serials/|work=Aruba Adil|date=29 July 2015|access-date=24 September 2015|archive-date=12 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180812062500/http://aaj.tv/2015/07/5-reasons-diya-re-dil-is-different-from-other-soap-drama-serials/|url-status=dead}}</ref> After the premier of series first episode it was listed among the top eleven drama serials of 2015 on place four.<ref name="Alishba Nasir"/> It has been ranked on many media outlets of top list drama serials of twenty-fifteen.<ref>{{cite web|title=Top 5 Pakistani Dramas Of 2015|url=http://style.pk/top-5-pakistani-dramas-of-2015/|work=Hira|publisher=[[The Express Tribune]]|date=3 August 2015|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref> Sheeba Khan of ''HIP'' states the serial is, "As great as the script was, the direction was equally fantastic. Haseeb Hassan took the script and visualized it for us with absolute perfection. The cinematography and presentation was beautiful and it was nice to see the beauty of Pakistan, rather than the US or UK."<ref name="A legacy of love: Diyar-e-Dil"/> 
Commenting on the leads of serial she said, " We got to see more of Wali and Faara along with the dining table in the haveli. It was nice to see the lead pair's banter. With all the hatred Wali says he has of Faara, you can see how completely he is in love with her. In their last scene together, you could see how the hurt in his eyes when Faara tells him off, again!".<ref>{{cite web|title=Wali and Faara are owning the serial! Eik taraf behen, to doosri taraf begum; what does the 'Khan' do? |url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1147708/wali-and-faara-are-owning-the-serial|work=Sheeba Khan|publisher=HIP|date=20 August 2015|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref> Writing for ''BrandSynario'', Ghazal Sulaiman praises the chemistry between Sanam and Meekal and said, "All praises for ''Diyar-e-Dil'', this drama seems to have all the elements to be HUM TV’s next hit. With an outstanding entry in the season, the drama is pacing fast and is successfully keeping the viewers hooked. Moreover, the drama’s crisp editing and exceptional direction will make you head over heels in love with the natural scenic beauty of Baltistan."<ref>{{cite web|title=Wali and Faara are owning the serial!|url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1147708/wali-and-faara-are-owning-the-serial|work=Sheeba Khan|publisher=HIP|date=20 August 2015|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref>

Almas Akhtar of ''[[The Express Tribune]]'' praised the series story line, setting, location, casting and concept saying, "''Diyar-e-dil'' the only drama portraying the true dynamics of a tribal family in Pakistan" she further added that the series also portray Male bonding thus attracting male viewers .<ref name="Akhtar"/> With the popularity of serial, the portrayal of Wali by Osman was declared the best character of the year alongside [[Zindagi Gulzar Hai#Cast|Kashaf Murtaza]] by [[Sanam Saeed]] in 2012 drama serial ''[[Zindagi Gulzar Hai]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title=What do Pakistani TV audiences want to see? Favourite characters Kashaf and Wali give us a hint (Heroes and heroines of recent TV favourites hark back to the original 'It' couple of the '80s) |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1174176/what-do-pakistani-tv-audiences-want-to-see-favourite-characters-kashaf-and-wali-give-us-a-hint |work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] |date=5 November 2015 |access-date=10 November 2015}}</ref> Buraq Shabbir of ''[[The News International|The News]]'' also lauded the serial and said, "The themes of love, respect, and [[family values]] are recurrent through ''Diyar-e-Dil''. The show does a neat job of exploring various emotions and how damaging it can be if one is arrogant and angry and spends time in a negative structure."<ref>{{cite web|title=Diyar-e-Dil: Of love, pride and family values|url= http://tns.thenews.com.pk/love-pride-family-values/#.VlA_6HYrLIU|author=Buraq Shabbir|publisher=[[News on Sunday]]|date=15 November 2015|access-date=21 November 2015}}</ref>

'''Fahad Sheikh''' is a Pakistani television actor, best known for his lead role as Ahmer in the 2020 [[ARY Digital]] television series ''[[Jalan (TV series)|Jalan]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-07-15|title=Actor Fahad Sheikh tackles his role effortlessly in 'Jalan'|url=https://www.24newshd.tv/15-Jul-2020/actor-fahad-sheikh-tackles-his-role-effortlessly-in-jalan|access-date=2020-12-21|website=24 News HD|language=en}}</ref><ref name="dawn" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2020-11-30|title='Jalan' star Fahad Sheikh says Fahad Mustafa is his mentor|url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/696033/jalan-star-fahad-sheikh-says-fahad-mustafa-is-his-mentor/|access-date=2020-12-21|website=Daily Times|language=en-US}}</ref> He was also seen in drama serial drama serial ''[[Azmaish]]'' and ''[[Dunk (2020 TV series)|Dunk]]''. Before ''Jalan'' he appeared in dramas such as ''[[Badbakht]]'', ''[[Khudparast]]'', and ''[[Bandish (2019 TV series)|Bandish]]''.

He was also seen in a short film<ref>{{Cite web|title=See Prime's new film is a tale of lost lovers|url=https://www.samaa.tv/entertainment/2020/12/see-primes-new-short-film-is-a-tale-of-lost-lovers/|access-date=2020-12-21|website=Samaa TV|language=en-US}}</ref> "Nam Kya Rakha?" starring [[Hajra Yamin]] and Faizan Shaikh.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-12-14|title=See Prime releases original sound tracks from short films|url=https://nation.com.pk/15-Dec-2020/see-prime-releases-original-sound-tracks-from-short-films|access-date=2020-12-21|website=The Nation|language=en}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Fahad was born in [[Lahore]] into a mixed [[Punjabi Muslims|Punjabi]] and [[Kashmiri people|Kashmiri]] (through his maternal grandmother) family.<ref>{{cite video |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R1KOfrk9xic |title=Fahad Sheikh {{!}} Imran Ashraf {{!}} Mazaq Raat Season 2 {{!}} Ep 171 {{!}} Honey Albela {{!}} Sakhawat Naz |date=17 September 2024 |publisher=[[Mazaaq Raat]] |access-date=17 January 2026 |quote=Listen from 9:30 onward}}</ref> Before entering the entertainment industry he had played professional cricket, representing the [[Pakistan national under-19 cricket team|Pakistan national under-19 team]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-06 |title=Fahad Sheikh was a part of Pakistan cricket team? See throwback picture |url=https://arynews.tv/viral-fahad-sheikh-reminisces-u-19-cricket-days-with-old-picture |access-date=2026-01-17 |website=arynews.tv |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Fahad faced challenges early on in his career due to criticisms about his height, Urdu pronunciation and demeanor.<ref name="dawn" /> His break came with his role in the drama ''[[Jalan (TV series)|Jalan]]'', which led to subsequent acting offers in Pakistani television.<ref name="dawn" /> Before starting his career as an actor, Fahad hosted ''Gyara Number'', a television show in [[Lahore]] and was managing his clothing business.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2021-07-19 |title=Don't rush into marriage: Yashma Gill |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2311363/everyone-desires-companionship-but-dont-rush-into-marriage-yashma-gill |access-date=2024-10-31 |website=The Express Tribune |language=en}}</ref> Fahad attributes much of his success to the guidance and support of [[Fahad Mustafa]], who has acted as a mentor, helping him navigate the industry.<ref name="dawn" /><ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
Fahad married Mehreen Sheikh, the daughter of Pakistani actress [[Shahida Mini]], in 2012.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2023-08-14 |title=اداکار فہد شیخ کے ہاں دوسرے بچے کی پیدائش |url=https://www.dawnnews.tv/news/1209646 |access-date=2024-11-01 |website=Dawn News Urdu |language=ur}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2024-03-02 |title=ساس سے پہلی بار ملاقات پر شدید خوفزدہ تھا اداکار فہد شیخ {{!}} The Express News |url=https://www.express.pk/story/2612548/pakistan?amp=1 |access-date=2024-11-01 |website=ایکسپریس اردو}}</ref> The couple has two children.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

'''Fakhar-e-Alam''' ([[Punjabi language|Punjabi]], {{langx|ur|فخر عالم}}) (born 19 January 1976) is a Pakistani actor, singer, songwriter, TV host, [[VJ (media personality)|video jockey]], rapper and producer<ref name=Dawn/><ref name="TOI">{{cite news |last=Joy |first=Prathibha |date=20 September 2011 |title=I'm doing good cinema: Manjari Fadnis |newspaper=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/regional/news-interviews/Im-doing-good-cinema-Manjari-Fadnis/articleshow/10041262.cms |url-status=dead |access-date=15 August 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120418081839/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2011-09-20/news-interviews/30176232_1_manjari-fadnis-kannada-films-muthirai |archive-date=18 April 2012}}</ref> famous for introducing the [[Bhangra (music)|bhangra]]-[[Pakistani rap|rap]] fusion genre of music in Pakistan. He is considered a pioneer of [[Bhangra (music)|bhangra]]-rap music of Lahore in the 1990s. He currently hosts TV shows, sports broadcasts, and high-profile national and international productions. 

He also served as the chairman of the Sindh Board of Film Censors from 2013 to 2016.<ref name="Tribune">{{Cite web |last=Qamar |first=Saadia |date=2013-09-20 |title=Fakhr-e-Alam: The new face of Sindh's Censor board |url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/607019/fakhr-e-alam-the-new-face-of-sindhs-censor-board |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=[[The Express Tribune]] |language=en}}</ref>

In 2018, he became the first and, to date, the only Pakistani in world history to [[circumnavigate]] the globe in a solo flight, in what he called Mission Parwaaz. He was aiming for a 28-day schedule and was planning on flying to 30 airports around the world.<ref name=Dawn2>{{cite news |date=4 November 2018 |title=Fakhre Alam becomes the first Pakistani to circumnavigate the globe solo |newspaper=Dawn newspaper |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1181186/fakhre-alam-becomes-first-pakistani-to-circumnavigate-the-globe-solo|access-date=13 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230203040250/https://images.dawn.com/news/1181186/fakhre-alam-becomes-the-first-pakistani-to-circumnavigate-the-globe-solo|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 February 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life ==
=== Family background ===
Fakhar-e-Alam was born on 19 January 1976 in Lahore, Pakistan.<ref name=PakistanHerald>{{cite web|url=http://pakistanherald.com/Profile/Fakhar-e-Alam-797|url-status=dead|archive-date=1 July 2022|access-date=13 December 2024|title=Fakhar-e-Alam profile|website=PakistanHerald website|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220701233522/http://pakistanherald.com/Profile/Fakhar-e-Alam-797}}</ref><ref name="VIDPK" /> His maternal grandmother [[Akleem Akhtar]], also known as ''General Rani'', was a [[socialite]] close to dictator General [[Yahya Khan]], who ruled Pakistan from 1969 to 1971, while his mother Aroosa Alam is a journalist.<ref name=Telegraph>{{Cite news |last=Desai |first=Ashok |date=27 March 2007|title=THE RANI GENERAL FILES - The legacy of Akleem Akhtar lives on in her daughter|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/opinion/the-rani-general-files-the-legacy-of-akleen-akhtar-lives-on-in-her-daughter/cid/1027330|access-date=13 December 2024|newspaper=Telegraph India newspaper|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200610195214/https://www.telegraphindia.com/opinion/the-rani-general-files-the-legacy-of-akleen-akhtar-lives-on-in-her-daughter/cid/1027330|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 June 2020|quote=I do not know what happened to her numerous children, except one — Aroosa Alam. Aroosa did not show early promise. She married and had a son in 1976, Fakhr-e-Alam, who became more famous than her.}}</ref>  Akleem Akhtar ('The Rani General') garnered the reputation of being the "most powerful woman in Pakistan" due to her role as the "muse and mistress" of General [[Yahya Khan]].<ref name=Telegraph/><ref name="theprint/22aug18" />

In 2017, [[Sukhpal Singh Khaira]], Leader of the Opposition in India's Punjab Legislative Assembly, alleged that Fakhar-e-Alam's mother Aroosa had affiliations with the ISI and served as a Pakistani spy. It was claimed that she resided at the official residence of India's Punjab Chief Minister [[Amarinder Singh]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Amarinder's Pak guest stirs up row |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/amarinders-pak-guest-stirs-up-row/articleshow/2653960.cms |access-date=17 April 2024 |work=The Times of India |date=27 December 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Captain Amarinder Singh's Friend Aroosa Alam is Pakistani Spy, Claims AAP MLA Sukhpal Singh Khaira  |url=https://www.india.com/news/india/captain-amarinder-singhs-friend-aroosa-alam-is-pakistani-spy-claims-aap-mla-sukhpal-singh-khaira-2695135/ |access-date=17 April 2024 |work=india.com website|language=en}}</ref> Additionally, she was colloquially referred to as the 'First Lady of Punjab' due to her relationship with the Amarinder Singh and was reported to have close ties with the Pakistani military establishment.<ref name="theprint/22aug18">{{cite news|author=Shobhaa De|title=When attacking Sidhu, keep in mind Punjab's most famous live-in couple |url=https://theprint.in/opinion/when-attacking-sidhu-keep-in-mind-punjabs-most-famous-live-in-couple/103060/|access-date=17 April 2024|work=ThePrint newspaper|date=22 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180822160014/https://theprint.in/opinion/when-attacking-sidhu-keep-in-mind-punjabs-most-famous-live-in-couple/103060/|url-status=dead|archive-date=22 August 2018}}</ref>

=== Education ===
In 2022, after doing an online course from the [[Harvard Business School]], he earned an [[Alternative Investments]] certificate at the age of 46.<ref name=Dawn>{{Cite news |date=21 September 2022|title='Never too old to learn': Fakhr-e-Alam awarded Alternate Investments certificate from Harvard Business School|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1190882 |newspaper=Images magazine (Dawn Group of Newspapers) website|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220925175804/https://images.dawn.com/news/1190882|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 September 2022|access-date=13 December 2024}}</ref>

==Career==
=== Music ===
Fakhar-e-Alam started his career as Pakistan's first rap artist with the music album "RAP UP" in 1993. The same year, he debuted as a presenter in Pakistan's first pop chart television show, "Music Channel Charts". After the success of "Music Channel Charts", he was offered the position of a presenter for "Pepsi Top of the Pops".<ref name="VIDPK">{{cite web|url=http://vidpk.com/p/739/Fakhr-e-Alam/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170324085153/http://vidpk.com/p/739/Fakhr-e-Alam/ |date=9 November 2011|archive-date=24 March 2017|access-date=13 December 2024|title=Profile of Fakhr-e-Alam|website=VIDPK.com website|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He met great success with his single "Bhangra Pao", a fusion of [[Bhangra (music)|bhangra]] and [[Rap music|rap]] music, in 1993. He received a gold disc for his debut album and is considered one of EMI Records' most successful artists. The single was also broadcast on [[MTV]].<ref name=PakistanHerald/><ref name="VIDPK" />

=== Acting ===
He has acted in movies such as ''Very Good Dunya Very Bad Log'' (1998)<ref name="VIDPK" /> and in television serials such as ''Do Biwiyan Ek Bechara'' (2018).

=== Production ===
When he arrived in Karachi in 2004, Fakhar-e-Alam was offered a CEO position in an electronic media marketing company. He accepted the offer and stayed with the company for three months. He then launched his own production house called Industree Productions''.''

=== Philanthropy ===
Fakhar-e-Alam was actively involved in humanitarian activities and relief work after the [[2005 Kashmir earthquake]].<ref name="VIDPK" /> 

=== Hosting ===
Fakhr-e-Alam's show ''Aaghaz-e-Safar'', based on real-life stories of Pakistanis, aired on 18 April 2014. The show was produced and directed by [[Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy]], a two-time Pakistani [[Academy Awards|Oscar]] winner. It was the first time Obaid-Chinoy produced for a Pakistani TV channel. The show aired on [[AAJ TV]] in Pakistan.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Syed |first=Madeeha |date=2014-04-11|title=Aaghaz-e-Safar: "This show will be groundbreaking" |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1099186 |access-date=2022-09-17 |newspaper=Dawn newspaper|language=en}}</ref>

In 2016, after the murder of a popular [[qawwal]], [[Amjad Sabri]], in [[Karachi]], Fakhr-e-Alam led a movement pressing for better government security for artists.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2016-06-24 |title='No difference between politicians and us': Fakhr-e-Alam demands better security for artists |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1175676 |access-date=2022-09-17 |newspaper=Images magazine (Dawn Group of Newspapers) |language=en}}</ref>

On 1 August 2017, he became the second Pakistani celebrity invited to speak at [[Googleplex]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Murtaza |first=Syed M. |title=Fakhr e Alam becomes first Pakistani to speak at Google/Facebook  |url=https://archive.pakistantoday.com.pk/2017/08/02/fakhr-e-alam-first-pakistani-to-speak-at-googlefacebook/ |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=Pakistan Today newspaper|date=2 August 2017 |language=en-GB}}</ref> 

In May 2021, he was announced as the host of ''[[60 Hours to Glory]]'', a military reality show featuring several international teams. It was broadcast on [[Hum TV]], [[Hum News]], and [[PTV Home]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Haq |first=Irfan Ul |date=2021-06-04 |title=Fakhre Alam teases new military reality show 60 Hours to Glory |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1187751 |access-date=2022-09-17 |newspaper=Dawn newspaper |language=en}}</ref> On 27 June 2021, he was bestowed with the UAE [[golden visa]], making him the first Pakistani celebrity to receive it.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gokulan |first=Dhanusha |date=27 June 2021 |title=Fakhr-e-Alam is first Pakistani celebrity to get UAE Golden Visa |url=https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/fakhr-e-alam-becomes-first-pakistani-celebrity-to-receive-10-year-uae-golden-visa |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=Khaleej Times newspaper|language=en}}</ref>

On 2 October 2021, Fakhr-e-Alam announced a partnership with [[Dubai]]-based [[esports]] organisation [[Galaxy Racer]]. As a result of the deal, the two parties will collaborate to create Galaxy Racer Pakistan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-10-02 |title=Fakhr-e-Alam takes $40 million stake in Galaxy Racer |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/824030/fakhr-e-alam-takes-40-million-stake-in-galaxy-racer/ |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=Daily Times newspaper |language=en-US}}</ref> Later that month, he hosted the sports show ''The Pavilion'' on [[A Sports]] as part of its coverage of the [[2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2021-11-09 |title=Who is Shaniera Akram going to cheer for during the Pakistan versus Australia T20 match? |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1188763 |access-date=2022-09-17 |newspaper=Images magazine (Dawn Group of Newspapers)|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=1 November 2021 |title=Watch: Pakistan greats Wasim, Waqar and Misbah's showtime banter will leave you in splits |url=https://www.khaleejtimes.com/entertainment/watch-pakistan-greats-wasim-waqar-and-misbahs-showtime-banter-will-have-you-in-splits |access-date=2022-09-17 |website=Khaleej Times newspaper|language=en}}</ref>

Alam hosted ''The Pavilion'' for the [[2023 Cricket World Cup]], which has become a global hit and recognized as the biggest cricket show in cricketing world. It has gained massive popularity especially within [[India]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-17 |title=This World Cup's sleeper hit: The Pavilion, a simple, informal show from Pakistan |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/sports/cricket/the-sleeper-hit-this-world-cup-a-simple-informal-show-from-pakistan-9029938/ |access-date=2024-01-02 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

'''''Hum Log''''' (English: ''We People'') is an Indian television soap opera and also the first serial drama series in [[Hindi]]. It began telecast on 7 July 1984 on [[Doordarshan]], the only television channel in India at the time.<ref name=bbc/> It is the story of an Indian middle-class family of the 1980s and their daily struggles and aspirations.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/an-episode-in-history/485943/ |title=An episode in history |date=7 July 2009 |publisher=[[Indian Express]] |accessdate=8 July 2009 |archive-date=15 July 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090715005740/http://www.indianexpress.com/news/an-episode-in-history/485943 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/tv/hum-log-revisiting-that-80-s-show/story-u4gx5IBZV3kuez0bI3q07K.html|title=Hum Log: Revisiting that 80's show|date=21 July 2014|website=Hindustan Times|language=en|access-date=19 August 2019|archive-date=19 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190819234535/https://www.hindustantimes.com/tv/hum-log-revisiting-that-80-s-show/story-u4gx5IBZV3kuez0bI3q07K.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Hum Log is also the first Indian show to be sponsored.<ref name="g302">{{cite web | title=Cast of Hum Log had a reunion to celebrate its 30th anniversary | website=The Times of India | date=10 August 2014 | url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/tv/news/hindi/cast-of-hum-log-had-a-reunion-to-celebrate-its-30th-anniversary/articleshow/39951844.cms | access-date=11 March 2026}}</ref>

It was created on the lines of a Mexican television series, ''[[Ven conmigo (telenovela)|Ven Conmigo]]'' (1975), using the education-entertainment methodology. The idea of the TV series came to then [[Minister of Information and Broadcasting (India)|Information and Broadcasting Minister]], [[Vasant Sathe]], after a Mexican trip in 1982. Soon the idea for ''Hum Log'' was developed in collaboration with writer [[Manohar Shyam Joshi]], who scripted the series, and filmmaker, P. Kumar Vasudev, who went on direct the series.<ref name=exp>{{cite web |title=Sister Act |work=[[Indian Express]] |url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/sister-act/505763/ |author=Alaka Sahani |date=23 August 2009 |accessdate=26 January 2016 |archive-date=5 February 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160205120632/http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/sister-act/505763/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The title score was composed by  music director [[Anil Biswas (composer)|Anil Biswas]].

At the end of every episode, [[Ashok Kumar]] discussed the ongoing story and situations with the audience using Hindi couplets and limericks. In later episodes, introduced the actors who played various characters in the serial and end his monologue with the various Indian language versions of the words "Hum Log".

The series was broadcast in the UK on the cable channel [[Indra Dhnush]] in 1992.<ref name="SatJUL1992">''Satellite Times'', July 1992</ref>

==Development and production==
In 1984, Mexican television writer Miguel Sabido, who had written the Mexican telenovela on [[educational entertainment]], ''[[Ven conmigo (telenovela)|Ven conmigo]]'' (Come with Me, 1975) on adult literacy, was invited to India. Working with local writer, he helped created the series which tackled social issues like family planning, caste harmony, empowerment of women,  national integration, dowry, alcoholism and drug abuse.<ref name=bbc>{{cite web |title=How soap operas changed the world |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/magazine-17820571 |author=Stephanie Hegarty |date=27 April 2012 |accessdate=26 January 2016 |archive-date=31 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160131094916/http://www.bbc.com/news/magazine-17820571 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Adult Literacy, Birth Control Addressed in Dramas : Third World Soaps Tackle Social Problems |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1987-09-20-mn-8914-story.html |access-date=26 January 2016 |newspaper=[[LA Times]] |date=20 September 1987 |author=Jeff Crider |archive-date=31 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160131143534/http://articles.latimes.com/1987-09-20/news/mn-8914_1_soap-operas |url-status=live }}</ref> ''Ven conimgo'' was in turned based on the Peruvian telenovela, ''[[Simplemente María (1969 telenovela)|Simplemente María]]'' (Simply Maria, 1969-1971).<ref name=bbc/>

The cast would meet for rehearsals at 3 pm at Himachal Bhavan, near [[Mandi House]] in Delhi, and thereafter a van would take them to a studio in suburb [[Gurgaon]] where it was shot.<ref name=exp/>

==Reception==
During its 17-month run, Ashok Kumar received over 400,000 letters from young viewers, asking him to convince their parents in marriage of their choice. The viewership of each episode was more than 50 millions.<ref name=bbc/>

'''Hum Sitaray''' is a [[Pakistani]] entertainment channel launched by [[Hum Network Limited]] on 14 December 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1573951|title=Unusual movement of share price alarms Hum Network|first=Kalbe|last=Ali|date=12 August 2020|website=DAWN.COM}}</ref> It is a major entertainment channel in Pakistan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://aurora.dawn.com/news/1140730|title=The business of entertainment|first=Marylou|last=Andrew|date=1 November 2014|website=Aurora Magazine}}</ref>

== History ==
The channel launched on 14 December 2013 with original programming - this had become a trend for Pakistani entertainment to have 2 channels under 1 company (ex. [[Geo Kahani]], [[ARY Zindagi]]) but due to bad ratings, the channel turned to airing reruns from 2015 onwards with little original programming and since 2016 it has been airing only reruns from [[Hum TV]]. Hum Sitaray dubbed the entire Season 1 of the Turkish Historical Drama Dilliris Ertuğrul.{{citation needed|date=April 2020}}

'''Humayun Saeed''' (born 27 July 1971) is a Pakistani [[actor]] and [[Film producer|producer]].<ref name="dawn">{{cite news|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1139177|title=Humayun Saeed, wife injured in Bangkok car crash|newspaper=Daily Dawn.com|date=20 October 2014|access-date=19 June 2015}}</ref> Describing himself as a [[Method acting|method actor]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 December 2020 |title=Throwback 2020 - The Man of the Moment, Humayun Saeed. |url=https://www.hmagpak.com/24-Dec-2020/throwback-2020-the-man-of-the-moment-humayun-saeed |website=H Magazine |quote=If you could call this a method, then maybe I am a method actor.}}</ref> Saeed is primarily known for his work on Pakistani television and cinema and is the recipient of several accolades, including [[Lux Style Awards]] and [[ARY Film Awards]].<ref name="auto6">{{cite web|last1=Mughal|first1=Danish|title=ARY Film Awards 2016 Winners List -|url=http://www.pakium.pk/2016/04/18/ary-film-awards-2016-winners-list|date=17 April 2016}}</ref> Saeed also runs the Six Sigma Plus media production house  which produces television drama serials and commercial movies.

==Early life and family==
Saeed was born on 27 July 1971 in [[Karachi]] into a [[Punjabi Muslim|Punjabi]] family.<ref>Syeda Areeba Rasheed (30 June 2018), [https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Humayun+Saeed+Carries+On.-a0543904531 "Humayun Saeed Carries On"], ''Slogan'' magazine (June 2018), vol. 23, no. 6, p. 33. [https://web.archive.org/web/20230824075717/https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Humayun+Saeed+Carries+On.-a0543904531 Archived] from the original on 24 August 2023. "Born in Karachi on July 27,1971, Saeed belongs to a liberal and well-educated Punjabi family."</ref>

He earned a bachelor's degree in commerce from [[St. Patrick's College (Karachi)|St. Patrick's College, Karachi]] and before entering the entertainment industry he used to work as a [[general manager]] at a garment factory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dass |first=Camillia |date=12 January 2022 |title=Who Is Humayun Saeed, the Actor Starring as Princess Diana’s Love Interest on ‘The Crown’? |url=https://www.tatlerasia.com/lifestyle/entertainment/pakistani-actor-humayun-saeed-princess-diana-love-interest-the-crown-netflix |website=[[Tatler Asia]] |quote=Saeed did not start his career out by taking on acting school. Rather, he enrolled in St. Patrick’s college in Karachi and earned his bachelor’s degree in commerce. He then started working at a garment factory as a general manager.}}</ref>

Saeed has four younger brothers, with Salman Saeed also being an actor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fatima |first=Komal |date=9 November 2020 |title=Meet All Four Brothers of Legend Humayun Saeed |url=https://www.bolnews.com/entertainment/2020/11/meet-all-four-brothers-of-legend-humayun-saeed/ |website=[[Bol News]] |quote=Humayun’s brother Salman Saeed is also an actor.}}</ref>

==Career==
===Television===
Saeed began his career as a television producer in the early 90s. After stepping into showbiz, Saeed's was cast in the TV shows for acting roles. He made his acting debut in 1995 with ''Karoron Ka Aadmi'' produced by Nadeem A Khan.<ref>Ayesha Anis (27 July 2018), [https://dailytimes.com.pk/273970/7-facts-you-didnt-know-about-humayun-saeed/ "7 facts you didn’t know about Humayun Saeed"], ''Daily Times''. Retrieved 7 March 2019.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Karoron ka Aadmi produced by Nadeem A Khan |url=https://ptv2.tripod.com/k/karoron.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231224104610/https://ptv2.tripod.com/k/karoron.htm |archive-date=24 December 2023}}</ref> 

Saeed continued doing TV productions. He partnered with [[Sultana Siddiqui]] in the late 90s and then [[Abdullah Kadwani]] in 2000s for [[7th Sky Entertainment]]. Later, he started his own production house along with Shehzad Nasib under the banner [[Six Sigma Plus]]. Since then he has produced content for Pakistani television viewers.<ref>{{cite news|title=Catching up with Humayun Saeed {{!}} TNS – The News on Sunday|url=http://tns.thenews.com.pk/catching-humayun-saeed/#.V8M1R_l97IU|work=tns.thenews.com.pk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rehman |first=Maliha |date=2016-05-29 |title=First person: Hero evergreen |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1261034 |access-date=2022-04-07 |website=DAWN.COM |language=en}}</ref>

Saeed's initial TV work as an actor includes ''[[Mehndi (drama)|Mehndi]]'', ''[[Doraha (TV series)|Doraha]]'', ''Kabhi Kabhi Pyar Mein'', ''[[Kaafir (Pakistani TV series)|Kaafir]]'', ''[[Uraan (2010 TV series)|Uraan]]'', ''Hum Se Juda Na Hona'', ''Ladies Park'' and guest roles in ''[[Meri Zaat Zarra-e-Benishan]]'' and ''[[Daam]]''. In 2005, Saeed starred in the music video ''Iss Baar Milo''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pakipop.com/evaluation/rough_cut.html|title=Pakipop.com > Evaluation > Hadiqa Kiani & Aamir Zaki - Rough Cut|website=www.pakipop.com|access-date=2017-10-13|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171123084122/http://www.pakipop.com/evaluation/rough_cut.html|archive-date=23 November 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=HadiqaKianiTV|title=Hadiqa Kiani - Iss Baar Milo|date=2009-06-23|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k-55obN0nU8 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211222/k-55obN0nU8 |archive-date=2021-12-22 |url-status=live|access-date=2017-10-13}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://newslinemagazine.com/magazine/interview-hadiqa-kiyani/|title=Interview: Hadiqa Kiyani {{!}} Newsline|work=Newsline|access-date=2017-10-13|language=en-US}}</ref> 

In January 2022, Saeed was cast as [[Hasnat Khan|Dr. Hasnat Khan]] (known for his romantic involvement with [[Diana, Princess of Wales|Princess Diana]]), in the [[The Crown (season 5)|fifth season]] of [[The Crown (TV series)|''The Crown'']].<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Ramach|first1=Naman|last2=ran|date=2022-01-09|title='The Crown': Pakistani Star Humayun Saeed Cast as Princess Diana's Companion Dr. Hasnat Khan in Hit Netflix Series (EXCLUSIVE)|url=https://variety.com/2022/streaming/news/the-crown-humayun-saeed-hasnat-khan-princess-diana-1235149744/|access-date=2022-01-09|website=Variety}}</ref>

===Films===
Saeed made his film debut in 1999 with Samina Peerzada's movie ''[[Inteha (1999 film)|Inteha]]'', in which he played a negative role. For his performance, he receive the National Award for Best Actor.<ref>{{cite news|title=The Evil in Us All {{!}} TNS – The News on Sunday|url=http://tns.thenews.com.pk/evil-us/#.V8MzWPl97IU|work=tns.thenews.com.pk|access-date=28 August 2016|archive-date=25 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160825012336/http://tns.thenews.com.pk/evil-us/#.V8MzWPl97IU|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Humayun Saeed: A Man for All Reasons {{!}} TNS – The News on Sunday|url=http://tns.thenews.com.pk/a-man-for-all-reasons-humayun-saeed/#.V8FKoPl97IU|work=tns.thenews.com.pk}}</ref> Owing to the decline of the Pakistani film industry at that time, he appeared in only a limited number of films until the revival of cinema in 2013. Since then, he has appeared in many films, including ''[[Main Hoon Shahid Afridi]], [[Bin Roye]]'',<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-07-29 |title=Humayun Saeed hosts party to celebrate success of Bin Roye AND Wrong No. |url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/928029/humayun-saeed-hosts-party-to-celebrate-success-of-bin-roye-and-wrong-no |access-date=2022-04-07 |website=The Express Tribune |language=en}}</ref> ''[[Jawani Phir Nahi Ani]]'' and ''[[Punjab Nahi Jaungi]].'' In 2018, he starred in ''[[Jawani Phir Nahi Ani 2]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1180805|title=It was a conscious decision to make JPNA 2 different from the prequel: Humayun Saeed|date=5 September 2018|access-date=8 September 2018|work=Dawn Images|author=Ahmed Sarym}}</ref> In 2022, he appeared in Nadeem Baig's ''London Nahi Jaunga''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/586570-5-of-the-most-anticipated-films-of-2020|title=5 of the most anticipated films of 2020|website=www.thenews.com.pk|language=en|access-date=2019-12-28}}</ref>

== Awards and nominations ==
Saeed has received numerous award nominations and honours including a minimum of 5 [[Lux Style Awards]]. He received special recognition awards at Pakistan Achievement Awards ''2015'' UK and Europe<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-11-19 |title=Javed Sheikh and Humayun Saeed honoured in London |url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/994439/javed-sheikh-and-humayun-saeed-honoured-in-london |access-date=2022-04-07 |website=The Express Tribune |language=en}}</ref> and at fourth [[Hum Awards]] in 2016 for his invaluable contribution towards revival of Pakistani cinema.<ref>{{cite news|title=10 best and worst moments of Hum TV awards 2016 – The Express Tribune|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/1090800/10-best-and-worst-moments-of-humtv-awards-2016|date=24 April 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nation.com.pk/25-Apr-2016/star-power-charms-audiences-at-hum-awards|title=Star power charms audiences at HUM Awards|date=24 April 2016|website=The Nation}}</ref> Saeed's film ''[[Jawani Phir Nahi Ani]]'' swept the [[ARY Film Awards]] ceremony with total of 17 awards, also earning him the award for the best male actor in a leading role.<ref name="auto6"/> He was awarded the [[Pride of Performance]] by the [[President of Pakistan]] on 23 March 2021.<ref>{{cite web | author=Web Desk | title=Pakistan Day: Ali Zafar, Humayun Saeed, Bushra Ansari, others honoured with civil awards | website=The News International | date=2021-03-23 | url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/808732-pakistan-day-ali-zafar-humayun-saeed-bushra-ansari-others-honoured-with-civil-awards | access-date=2021-06-03}}</ref>

'''''Ijazat''''' ({{translation|Permission}}) is a Pakistani television series that premiered on [[ARY Digital]] on 6 May 2010. It is produced by [[Samina Humayun Saeed]] and Shehzad Naseeb under banner [[Six Sigma Plus]] and directed by [[Misbah Khalid]]. [[Humayun Saeed]] and [[Ayesha Khan (Pakistani actress)|Ayesha Khan]] played the lead roles in the series.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fashiontimesmagazine.com/why-are-pakistani-dramas-obsessed-with-infidelity/|title=Why are Pakistani Dramas Obsessed with Infidelity?|date=30 October 2022|work=Fashion Times Magazine|archive-date=11 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221111072755/https://fashiontimesmagazine.com/why-are-pakistani-dramas-obsessed-with-infidelity/|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/537463/newspaper/newspaper/column|title=Infocus: Of love, intrigue and heartbreak|date=23 May 2010|work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]]|author=Khursheed Hyder|access-date=}}</ref>

In an interview with [[Mag The Weekly]], Saeed hinted about a potential sequel of the serial.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.magtheweekly.com/11-17feb2012/cover.asp |title=Cover Story |magazine=Mag The Weekly |issue=11-12 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120423111131/http://www.magtheweekly.com/11-17feb2012/cover.asp |archive-date=23 April 2012}}</ref>

== Plot ==
The story revolves around a happily married couple, Hamza and Muqadas. Muqadas is a loving wife and daughter-in-law. Her husband Hamza who is a struggling actor also loves her. Hamaz's life changes when he encounters a woman, Nijaat, who is eager to join the showbiz industry. She is married to a simple looking yet wealthy man. After an extramarital affair with Hamza, she divorces her husband and marries him. At the end, Muqadas also divorces Hamaz and he is left alone with his guilt.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://galaxylollywood.com/2021/08/21/extramarital-affairs-divorces-these-8-dramas-are-narrating-the-same-story/|title=Extramarital Affairs & Divorces: These 8 Dramas Are Narrating The Same Story|date=21 August 2021|access-date=11 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240910021243/https://galaxylollywood.com/2021/08/21/extramarital-affairs-divorces-these-8-dramas-are-narrating-the-same-story/|archive-date=10 September 2024|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Jana Malik''' ({{langx|ur|{{nq|جاناں ملک}}}}; born 26 April 1974) is a [[Pakistani]] actress who appears in television serials.<ref name=tv>{{cite web|title=Biography of actress Jana Malik|url=http://www.tv.com.pk/celebrity/Jana-Malik/118|publisher=tv.com.pk|accessdate=12 March 2013}}</ref><ref name=tnt>{{cite news|title=Pakistan's television artist Jana Malik |url=http://www.thenewstribe.com/2012/05/27/quality-my-priority-jana-malik/ |accessdate=12 March 2013 |newspaper=thenewstribe.com |date=27 May 2012 |url-status=usurped |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120531191723/http://www.thenewstribe.com/2012/05/27/quality-my-priority-jana-malik/ |archivedate=31 May 2012 }}</ref> Jana Malik is also known as Janan or Jana. She is best known for playing the supporting character of Pashi, the snake charmer, in the supernatural series [[Naagin (Geo Kahani)|''Naagin'']], which aired on [[Geo Kahani]]. She was seen in the television serials ''Mar Jain Bhi To Kya'', ''[[Parlour Wali Larki]]'', and ''[[Ek Tamanna Lahasil Si]]'' and is well known for her lead role in the serial ''Aiteraaf''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Malik's works in serials and a little history|url=http://www.sayever.com/beautiful-pakistani-actress-jana-malik-latest/|publisher=sayever.com|accessdate=12 March 2013|archive-date=22 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200322173333/http://www.sayever.com/beautiful-pakistani-actress-jana-malik-latest/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was also part of the cast in the Urdu films [[Muhafiz (1998 film)|''Muhafiz'']], and ''Zor'' in 1998.

== Personal life ==
She was born in [[Lahore]] on 26 April 1974.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://urdu.arynews.tv/i-am-an-avid-reader-exclusive-talk-with-janaa-malik/|title=مجھے ٹی وی دیکھنے کا زیادہ شوق نہیں، اداکارہ جاناں ملک|date=2 October 2016|website=ARY News}}</ref>

She was married to [[Nouman Javaid]] on 2 September 2016. The couple divorced in March 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://dunyanews.tv/en/Entertainment/379702-Jana-Malik-happy-with-divorce-expresses-good-wish|title=Jana Malik happy with divorce, expresses good wishes for Nouman|website=Dunya News|date=19 March 2017}}</ref>

== Career ==
Jana started her career as an actress in [[Pakistan Television Corporation|PTV]] when she was thirteen years old.<ref name="tv" /> She made her debut with the serial ''Reizgar'' aired on [[PTV Home]]. After that, she was seen in ''Maigh Malhaar'' and then acted in a children's musical show ''Aangan Aangan Tarey'' on PTV.<ref name="tv" /> She also appeared in an [[Urdu]] language film [[Muhafiz (1998 film)|''Muhafiz'']] in 1998 with [[Nadeem Baig (Pakistani actor)|Nadeem]] and [[Saud (actor)|Saud]]. She is being seen on different TV channels and in television serials. She played a lead role in ''Aiteraaf'' in 2011 on ARY Digital. The next serials in which she starred in include ''[[Kis Din Mera Viyah Howay Ga]]'', ''[[Ek Tamanna Lahasil Si]]'', ''[[Mor Mahal]]'' and ''[[Marzi (Geo Tv)|Marzi]].'' From 2017 to 2019, she starred in [[Geo Kahani]]'s hit series ''[[Naagin (Geo Kahani)|Naagin]].''<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bizasialive.com/overnights-geo-tv-surges-ahead-zee-tv-sony-tv-hum-tv/|title=Overnights: Geo TV surges ahead of ZEE TV, Sony TV & Hum TV|date=2017-09-05|work=BizAsia {{!}} Media, Entertainment, Showbiz, Events and Music|access-date=2018-05-18|language=en-GB}}</ref>

'''Khushhal Khan Khattak''', known professionally as '''Khushhal Khan''', is a Pakistani television actor, model and boxer. Khan is known for portraying Saim Ibrahim in ''[[Muhabbat Gumshuda Meri]]'', Faraz in ''Mushkil'' and Shahmir Adam in ''[[Duniyapur (TV series)|Duniyapur]]''. He is the recipient of a [[Hum Awards|Hum Award]]. In 2025, he played Mir Meeran Zamaan in ARY Digital's ''[[Biryani (TV series)|Biryani]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1187806|title=Teen web-series Midsummer Chaos finally is ready to air|website=Dawn Images|date=12 June 2021|access-date=19 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sumiya |date=2022-02-08 |title=Khushhal Khan Biography, Age, Wife, Family, Dramas |url=https://www.magpakistan.com/khushhal-khan-biography-age-wife-family-dramas/ |access-date=2022-07-25 |website=Mag Pakistan |language=en-US |archive-date=25 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220725110201/https://www.magpakistan.com/khushhal-khan-biography-age-wife-family-dramas/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Early life and family ==
Khan belongs to a [[Pashtuns|Pashtun]] [[Khattak]] family originally from [[Nowshera, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa|Nowshera]] village Ameer and lives in [[Islamabad]]. His family traces its roots to [[Khushal Khattak]], the 17th-century political figure, poet and one of the most influential names in [[Pashto literature and poetry|Pashto literature]].{{citation needed|date=April 2026}}

== Career==

=== Model ===
Khan began modeling and earned a name for himself in the profession. In 2020, Khan received a Hum Style Awards Rising Model award.<ref name="gl" />

=== Actor ===
He made his acting debut in the same year with ''[[Qissa Meherbano Ka]]''.<ref>{{cite web|date=2021-08-10|url=https://galaxylollywood.com/2021/08/10/qissa-meherbano-ka-a-family-story-caught-up-amidst-lies-love-and-deceit/|title='Qissa Meherbano Ka': A Story About Family, Lies, Love And Deceit|website=Galaxy Lollywood|author=Ifrah Butt|archive-date=10 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210810180007/https://galaxylollywood.com/2021/08/10/qissa-meherbano-ka-a-family-story-caught-up-amidst-lies-love-and-deceit/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He went on to appear in the dramas ''[[Bebasi]]'' (2021), ''Mushkil'' (2022), ''[[Wehshi (TV series)|Wehshi]]'' (2022) and the telefilm ''[[Aik Hai Nigar]]'', also in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Saboor Aly, Khushhal Khan's 'Mushkil' poster revealed|url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/967678/saboor-aly-khushhal-khans-mushkil-poster-revealed/amp|work=Daily Times|date=8 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.somethinghaute.com/aik-hai-nigar-an-inspirational-biopic-with-powerful-messages/|title=Aik Hai Nigar: An inspirational biopic with powerful messages|website=Something Haute|date=2021-10-26}}</ref>

Khan received recognition in 2023, with his portrayal of Saim in ''[[Muhabbat Gumshuda Meri]]'' opposite [[Dananeer Mobeen]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Bukhari|first=Kehkashan|date=6 June 2023|title=Muhabbat Gumshuda Meri Reminds Viewers of Raj and Simran from DDLJ|url=https://galaxylollywood.com/2023/06/06/muhabbat-gumshuda-meri-reminds-viewers-of-raj-and-simran-from-ddlj/|website=Galaxy Lollywood|access-date=1 November 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youlinmagazine.com/story/muhabbat-gumshuda-meri-a-refreshing-tale-of-teenage-romance/MjUyOA==|title=Muhabbat Gumshuda Meri: A Refreshing Tale of Teenage Romance|publisher=Youlin Magazine}}</ref> The drama won him the [[Hum Award for Best Actor Popular]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.samaa.tv/2087321717-hum-awards-2024-yumna-zaidi-sehar-khan-among-top-winners |title=Hum Awards 2024: Yumna Zaidi, Ramsha Khan, Ahad Raza Mir and Sehar Khan among top winners! |date=1 October 2024 |access-date=2 October 2024 |work=samaa.tv}}</ref> In 2024, Khan made his film debut with ''Poppay Ki Wedding'' and appeared in the web series ''[[Barzakh (TV series)|Barzakh]]'' in a special appearance. He then played the titular role in the mini-drama series ''Yahya''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://jang.com.pk/en/11311-khushal-khans-poppay-ki-wedding-coming-to-cinemas-on-may-10-news|title=Khushal Khan's 'Poppay Ki Wedding' coming to cinemas on May 10|date=May 8, 2024|website=Daily Jang}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Ajaz |first1=Mahwash |title=Barzakh Review: Pakistani actor Fawad Khan stands out in a puzzling tale of love and longing |url=https://www.khaleejtimes.com/reviews/movie-reviews/barzakh-review-fawad-khan-stands-out-in-a-puzzling-tale-of-love-and-loss |access-date=21 July 2024 |work=[[Khaleej Times]] |language=en}}</ref>

Khan has since received praise for portraying Shahmir opposite [[Ramsha Khan]], in ''[[Duniyapur (TV series)|Duniyapur]]''. The series is the costliest drama made in the history of Pakistani television.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1860190|title=Spotlight: The Badlands of Duniyapur |first=Mohammad|last=Kamran Jawaid|date=September 22, 2024|website=DAWN.COM}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://jang.com.pk/en/21512-khushhal-khan-ramsha-khans-chemistry-in-duniyapur-wows-fans-news|title=Khushhal Khan, Ramsha Khan's chemistry in 'DuniyaPur' wows fans|date=September 26, 2024|website=Daily Jang}}</ref>

In 2025, Khan appeared in Green Entertainment's Ramadan special television series ''[[Ishq Di Chashni]]'', along with [[Sehar Khan]].<ref name="DWGMT">{{Cite web|url=https://www.bollywoodlife.com/photos/sajal-aly-dil-wali-gali-mein-sehar-khan-khushhal-ishq-di-chashni-sarah-khan-shair-and-other-top-5-upcoming-pakistani-drama-on-ramadan-3092273/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250301081945/https://www.bollywoodlife.com/photos/sajal-aly-dil-wali-gali-mein-sehar-khan-khushhal-ishq-di-chashni-sarah-khan-shair-and-other-top-5-upcoming-pakistani-drama-on-ramadan-3092273/|url-status=dead|archive-date=1 March 2025|title=Dil Wali Gali Mein to Ishq Di Chashni; Top 5 upcoming Pakistani dramas that will make your Ramadan 2025 more lively|date=Feb 23, 2025|website=www.bollywoodlife.com|access-date=Feb 28, 2025}}</ref> The same year, he reunited with [[Ramsha Khan]] for ARY Digital's drama ''[[Biryani (TV series)|Biryani]]''.<ref name="PDBIA">{{Cite news |last=Hussain |first=Sana |date=3 October 2025 |title=Pakistani drama 'Biryani' is a love story with all the right ingredients |url=https://asianews.network/pakistani-drama-biryani-is-a-love-story-with-all-the-right-ingredients/ |work=Asia News Network |location=Islamabad |access-date=29 June 2026}}</ref>

=== Boxing ===
In January 2025, Khan made his [[amateur boxing]] debut during the International Boxing Event held in [[Lahore]], as part of the co-main event fight, triumphing over his opponent Bashar Khan with a [[knockout]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 January 2025 |title=Actor Khushhal Khan Wins Big At his First Amateur Boxing Match |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2524791/actor-khushhal-khan-wins-big-at-his-first-amateur-boxing-match |website=[[The Express Tribune]]}}</ref>
