'''Rabia Iqbal Khan''' ({{Langx|ur|{{nq|رابعہ اقبال خان}}}}) known by her [[stage name]] '''Kubra Khan''' ({{Langx|ur|{{nq|کبریٰ خان}}}}; born 16 June 1993), is a Pakistani actress who works in [[Urdu]] television and films. She made her debut in 2014 with the film ''[[Na Maloom Afraad]]''. Khan is described among the nation's highest-paid actresses by the media.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/web-stories/entertainment/highest-paid-pakistani-actresses-kubra-khan-mehwish-hayat-mahira-khan-saba-qamar-hania-amir-1692720884774 |title=From Mahira Khan to Kubra Khan: Highest paid Pakistani actresses |work=[[Daily News and Analysis|DNA India]] |access-date=2022-11-22 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.news18.com/web-stories/entertainment/9-highest-paid-pakistani-actresses-434133/ |title=Check out the list of the 9 Highest paid Pakistani actresses |work=[[News18 India]] |access-date=2022-12-21 |language=en-US}} oo</ref>

Khan has appeared in  successful films such as ''[[Jawani Phir Nahi Ani 2]]'', ''[[Parwaaz Hai Junoon]]'' (both 2018), and ''[[London Nahi Jaunga]]'' (2022).<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://cn.thenews.com.pk/magazine/you/208750-Watch-out-for-the-Show-Queens |title=Watch out for the 'Show Queens' |last=Zakir |first=Fatima |website=The News International |language=en |access-date=29 April 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180430113851/http://cn.thenews.com.pk/magazine/you/208750-Watch-out-for-the-Show-Queens |archive-date=30 April 2018 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Na Maloom Afraad's actress will make Bollywood debut |url=http://nation.com.pk/entertainment/10-Nov-2014/na-maloom-afraad-s-actress-will-make-bollywood-debut |publisher=[[the Nation]] |date=10 November 2014 |access-date=26 July 2015}}</ref> She made her television debut with ''[[Sang-e-Mar Mar]]'' (2016) followed by several dramas including ''[[Alif Allah Aur Insaan]]'' (2017), ''[[Alif (TV series)|Alif]]'' (2019), ''[[Hum Kahan Ke Sachay Thay]]'' and ''[[Sinf-e-Aahan]] (''both in 2021), ''[[Jannat Se Aagay]]'' (2023)<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.mangobaaz.com/this-contestant-dragged-judge-kubra-khan-for-critiquing-his-singing-when-she-cant-sing-herself-and-it-got-awkward-real-fast |title=This Contestant Dragged Judge Kubra Khan For Critiquing His Singing When She Can't Sing Herself And It Got Awkward Real Fast |last=Zia |first=Iman |date=20 June 2019 |website=MangoBaaz |access-date=7 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/266012-catching-up-with-kubra-khan |title=Catching up with Kubra Khan |last=Saeed |first=Mehek |website=The News International |language=en |access-date=29 April 2018}}</ref> and ''[[Noor Jahan (2024 TV series)|Noor Jahan]]'' (2024).

==Early life==

Born near [[Multan]], [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]] on 16 June 1993, her family moved to the [[United Kingdom]] when she was 6 months old, and initially was a model, having been spotted by [[Ahmad Ali Butt|Ahmed Ali Butt]]'s future wife Fatima Khan and later by Butt's brother, before becoming an actress.<ref name="March issue">{{cite web |url=http://www.hum.tv/did-you-know-kubra-khan-was-offered-the-lead-role-in-verna |last=Alavi |first=Omair |title=Did you know: Kubra Khan was offered the lead role in 'Verna' |date=12 March 2018 |website=GLAM Magazine |archive-date=17 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190517235459/https://www.hum.tv/did-you-know-kubra-khan-was-offered-the-lead-role-in-verna/ |url-status=dead |access-date=16 October 2019}}</ref>

==Career==
Khan's acting debut as well as cinematic debut was marked in 2013 by action-comedy ''[[Na Maloom Afraad]]'', where she portrayed Hina, a bank-worker and love interest of the film's main lead, [[Mohsin Abbas Haider]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=From Na Maloom To Being Somebody!-Nabeel Qureshi talks about his successful journey into films |url=http://tns.thenews.com.pk/nabeel-qureshi-about-his-success/ |publisher=The News Sunday |date=21 December 2014 |access-date=25 July 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150404055455/http://tns.thenews.com.pk/nabeel-qureshi-about-his-success/ |archive-date=4 April 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> A reviewer from the ''[[Gulf Times]]'' found her presence as "almost angel-like" but criticised her unfit and preachy monologue.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gulf-times.com/story/411043/Pakistani-film-Na-Maloom-Afraad-a-possible-game-ch |title=Pakistani film Na Maloom Afraad a possible game-changer |date=5 October 2014 |archive-date=7 March 2016 |work=Gulf Times |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160307160149/https://www.gulf-times.com/story/411043/Pakistani-film-Na-Maloom-Afraad-a-possible-game-ch}}</ref> In 2015, Khan appeared in the Bollywood movie ''[[Welcome 2 Karachi]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title=Na Maloom Afraad's Kubra Khan to make Bollywood debut with 'Welcome to Karachi' |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1143510/na-maloom-afraads-kubra-khan-to-make-bollywood-debut-with-welcome-to-karachi |newspaper=[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]] |date=10 November 2014 |access-date=26 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Rabia Khan reason behind Irrfan's exit from Vashu's film |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/Rabia-Khan-reason-behind-Irrfans-exit-from-Vashus-film/articleshow/45001791.cms |work=[[The Times of India]] |date=1 November 2014 |access-date=26 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Na Maloom Afraad se Welcom to Karachi! |url=https://www.dawnnews.tv/news/1012130/ |publisher=[[Dawn News]] |date=25 November 2014 |access-date=26 July 2015}}</ref>

She made her television debut in ''[[Sang-e-Mar Mar]]'', which aired on [[Hum TV]] in 2016. Sadaf Haider of the ''[[DAWN Images]]'' termed her as one of the breakout star of the serial, noting her "beautifully controlled performance as Shireen".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1177229 |title=TV drama Sang-e-Marmar is a necessary critique of Pakistan's obsession with 'ghairat' |date=10 March 2017 |author=Sadaf Haider |work=DAWN Images}}</ref> She next appeared in the spiritual-romance ''[[Khuda Aur Muhabbat season 2]]'' as a materialistic girl who later develops spiritualism.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2357145/kubra-khan-talks-about-her-characters-never-finding-love-in-projects? |title=Kubra Khan talks about her characters never finding love in projects |date=18 May 2022 |work=The Express Tribune}}</ref> Khan then essayed the justice seeking [[marital rape]] victim in the drama ''[[Andaaz-e-Sitam]]''.<ref name="face">{{cite news|url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/15351/the-changing-face-of-pakistani-dramas/ |title=The changing face of Pakistani dramas |date=24 April 2017 |author=Mahwash Ajaz |work=Daily Times |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316235322/https://dailytimes.com.pk/15351/the-changing-face-of-pakistani-dramas/ |archive-date=16 March 2018}}</ref> She concluded the year with a similar role of a [[Effects and aftermath of rape|rape victim]] in social drama ''[[Muqabil]]'',<ref name="face" /> for which she received [[Lux Style Award for Best TV Actress]] nomination at the [[17th Lux Style Awards]].<ref name="nominations">{{Cite web|date=2018-01-13|title=Lux Style Awards 2018: And the nominations are...|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/1607894/lux-style-awards-2018-nominations|access-date=2021-07-08|work=The Express Tribune|language=en}}</ref>

She had her first appearance in 2017 in spiritual drama ''[[Alif Allah Aur Insaan]]'' as an arrogant and pride daughter of a feudal family. She expressed dissatisfaction with her performance.<ref name="hate">{{cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2427800/no-regard-for-mental-health-kubra-says-pakistani-people-have-trend-of-belittling-trolling-people? |title=No regard for mental health: Kubra says Pakistani people have trend of belittling, trolling people |date=25 July 2023 |access-date=9 November 2024 |work=The Express Tribune}}</ref> She then played a girl next door in romantic-comedy ''Shadi Mubarak Ho''. Her next portrayal was a brief appearance as a ballsy London-based punjabi window in social drama ''[[Daldal]]''.

In 2018, she appeared in the Pakistani films ''[[Jawani Phir Nahi Ani 2]]'' and ''[[Parwaaz Hai Junoon]]'', both of which released on 22 August [[Eid-al-Adha]]. While reviewing her performance in ''Jawani Phir Nahi Ani 2'', Mohammad Kamran Jawaid of ''[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]]'' opined that her "cutesy aura befitting her role".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1430117/the-icon-review-the-power-of-three |title=The Icon Review: The Power Of Three |author=Mohammad Kamran Jawaid |date=2 September 2018}}</ref>

She returned to television in 2019 with spiritual-romance ''[[Alif (TV series)|Alif]]'', portraying Husn-e-Jahan, a renowned Pakistani cinema actress who abandoned her career to marry a calligrapher's son. Describing the project as "most memorable" for her, Khan reflected that she gave "heart and soul to ''Alif''."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2472571/i-gave-it-my-heart-and-soul-kubra-khan-declares-alif-her-most-memorable-project?a |title=I gave it my heart and soul: Kubra Khan declares 'Alif' her most memorable project |date=20 June 2024 |work=The Express Tribune}}</ref>

In 2022, she portrayed Mashal Tahir, an emotionally fragile and insecure university student in psychological-drama ''[[Hum Kahan Ke Sachay Thay]]'' based on the eponymous novel by Umera Ahmad. Maria Kari of the ''[[DAWN Images]]'' found that as Mashal, Khan "packs a punch".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1189166|title=Review: Hum Kahan Ke Sachay Thay was a total disappointment|date=5 January 2022|work=DAWN Images}}</ref> Khan then depicted a journalist with her childhood trauma in mystery-drama ''[[Sang-e-Mah]]'', pairing opposite [[Atif Aslam]]. Her on-screen chemistry with Aslam was praised critically,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2341594/atif-aslam-and-kubra-khan-the-new-onscreen-couple-in-town|title=Atif Aslam and Kubra Khan: The new onscreen couple in town|date=2 February 2022|work=The Express Tribune|access-date=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.somethinghaute.com/best-of-2022-on-screen-couples-that-won-our-hearts/|title=Best of 2022: On screen couples that won our hearts|date=22 December 2022|author=Syeda Zehra|access-date=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221222103202/https://www.somethinghaute.com/best-of-2022-on-screen-couples-that-won-our-hearts/|archive-date=22 December 2022}}</ref> despite her performance being overlooked.<ref name="hate" /> The same year, she returned to cinema screens, starring alongside [[Humayun Saeed]] in romantic-comedy ''[[London Nahi Jaunga]]'' as an educated rural Punjabi girl.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/586570-5-of-the-most-anticipated-films-of-2020 |title=5 of the most anticipated films of 2020 |website=The News International |language=en |access-date=28 December 2019}}</ref> Rafay Mahmood of ''[[The Express Tribune]]'' found her as a "a real surprise package" who "ruled the screen and camera, equally".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2366856/review-london-nahi-jaunga-is-a-thoroughly-entertaining-apology-by-khalil-ur-rehman-qamar |title=Review: 'London Nahi Jaunga' is a thoroughly entertaining apology by Khalil ur Rehman Qamar |author=Rafay Mahmood |date=20 July 2022 |access-date=9 November 2024}}</ref> The performance earned her a nomination of Best Film Actress at the [[22nd Lux Style Awards]]<ref name="pasoori">{{Cite web |date=2023-09-27 |title=Lux Style Awards 2023 nominations out now: Pasoori, Joyland, Mere Humsafar reign supreme |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2438044/lux-style-awards-2023-nominations-out-now-pasoori-joyland-mere-humsafar-reign-supreme? |access-date=2023-10-04 |website=The Express Tribune |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, Khan starred as Jannat Ali Khan in ontology drama ''[[Jannat Se Aagay]]'' as a TV show host whose personal life gets affected due to her stardom, earning decent reviews; Gaitee Ara Siddiqi of ''[[The News International]]'' stated that she has done "a commendable job" suggesting improvement in dialogue delivery.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/tns/detail/1101783-the-ratings-challenge |title=The 'ratings' challenge |author=Gaitee Ara Siddiqi |date=20 August 2023 |work=The News International |access-date=10 November 2024}}</ref> In 2024, she appeared in television series ''[[Noor Jahan (2024 TV series)|Noor Jahan]]'' as Noor Bano Shah.<ref name="dailytimes.com.pk">{{Cite web |date=2024-09-11 |title=I got irritated in the first 15 minutes: Kubra |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/1200702/i-got-irritated-in-the-first-15-minutes-kubra/ |access-date=2022-06-13 |website=Daily Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

She will next seen as [[Homai Vyarawalla]] in Aur Digital's drama ''Fatima Jinnah''.<ref>{{Citation |title=Fatima Jinnah - a Sister |type=Biography, Drama, History |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt36058979/ |access-date=2025-09-16 |others=Samar Jafri, Kubra Khan, Samina Ahmed}}</ref>

== Controversy==
In 2023, reports emerged alleging that the Pakistan Army, under the direction of former COAS [[Qamar Javed Bajwa]] and former DG Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) [[Faiz Hameed]], employed actresses to entrap and blackmail politicians in the country. These claims were made by retired Major [[Adil Raja]], who suggested that actresses were used to produce compromising videos and were housed in safe houses connected to the ISI. One of the actresses named in the allegations was Kubra Khan who denied these claims, describing them as unfounded.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kubra, Sajal, Mehwish break silence on allegations by Adil Raja |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2393965/enough-is-enough-kubra-sajal-and-mehwish-hayat-wont-let-anyone-drag-their-names-through-the-mud |access-date=23 August 2024 |work=The Express Tribune |date=3 January 2023 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Sex and Spies: Has Pakistan army been using actors to honey trap politicians? |url=https://www.firstpost.com/explainers/sex-and-spies-has-pakistan-army-been-using-actors-to-honey-trap-politicians-11925792.html |access-date=23 August 2024 |work=Firstpost |date=4 January 2023 |language=en-us}}</ref>

In response to the allegations, Khan also threatened legal action against Adil Raja for defamation.<ref>{{cite news |author=Images Staff |title=Kubra Khan threatens to sue YouTuber Adil Raja for defamation |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1191350 |access-date=23 August 2024 |work=Images |date=3 January 2023 |language=en}}</ref> Raja subsequently issued an apology to Khan, clarifying that his intention was not to target women but to highlight broader systemic issues.<ref>{{cite news |title=Adil Raja apologizes to Kubra Khan for distress caused by his allegations |url=https://thefrontierpost.com/adil-raja-apologizes-to-kubra-khan-for-distress-caused-by-his-allegations/ |access-date=23 August 2024 |work=thefrontierpost}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In January 2025, Khan and her longtime friend [[Gohar Rasheed]] announced their upcoming wedding.<ref>{{cite web |title=Did Kubra Khan and Mirza Gohar Rasheed just announce they're getting married?! |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1193174/did-kubra-khan-and-mirza-gohar-rasheed-just-announce-theyre-getting-married |website=Images |access-date=27 January 2025 |language=en |date=25 January 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Did Kubra and Gohar just soft-launch some big news? |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2524677/did-kubra-and-gohar-just-soft-launch-some-big-news |website=The Express Tribune |language=en |date=26 January 2025}}</ref>

'''Mahira Hafeez Khan''' ({{IPA|hns|maɦiːraː hafiːz kʰan|pron}}; born 21 December 1984) is a Pakistani actress known for her work in films and television. One of the highest-paid actresses in Pakistan, she has received [[Mahira Khan#Awards and nominations|several accolades]], including seven [[Lux Style Awards]] and eight [[Hum Awards]].<ref name="india.com">{{cite news|title=Mahira Khan: 7 things to know about Humsafar's pretty Khirad Hussain|url=http://www.india.com/top-n/mahira-khan-7-things-to-know-about-humsafars-pretty-khirad-hussain-172850/|accessdate=13 November 2016|work=India.com|date=15 October 2014|ref=india.com}}</ref>

After working as a video jockey for various television shows, Khan made her acting debut in 2011 with a supporting role in [[Shoaib Mansoor]]'s [[Blockbuster (entertainment)|blockbuster]] social drama ''[[Bol (film)|Bol]]'' (2011). She then played a troubled wife in the highly successful romantic television drama ''[[Humsafar]]'' (2011), which won her the [[Lux Style Awards|Lux Style Award for Best Television Actress]]. She gained wider recognition for portraying a range of unconventional characters in several [[Pakistani dramas|top-rated television series]], including the spiritual drama ''[[Shehr-e-Zaat]]'' (2012), the biographical romance ''[[Sadqay Tumhare]]'' (2014), the romantic drama ''[[Bin Roye (TV series)|Bin Roye]]'' (2016), the psychological thriller ''[[Hum Kahan Ke Sachay Thay]]'' (2021), and the revenge period drama ''[[Mitti De Baway]]'' (2026), all of which earned her multiple Best Actress awards and nominations.

Khan established herself by starring as the female lead in two of [[List of highest-grossing Pakistani films|Pakistan's highest-grossing productions]], the 2015 romantic drama ''[[Bin Roye]]'' and the 2016 coming-of-age musical drama ''[[Ho Mann Jahaan]]''. Her first project in [[Hindi cinema]] came with the crime thriller ''[[Raees (2017 film)|Raees]]'' (2017), which ranks among the [[List of Indian films of 2017|highest-grossing Indian films]] of 2017. She received critical acclaim for her portrayal of a rape victim in the revenge drama ''[[Verna (film)|Verna]]'' (2017), and an aspiring actress in the musical drama ''[[Superstar (2019 film)|Superstar]]'' (2019). After a short break, she appeared in the 2022 action films ''[[Quaid-e-Azam Zindabad]]'' and ''[[The Legend of Maula Jatt]]'', both of which became major box-office successes. Her subsequent releases, ''[[Love Guru (2025 film)|Love Guru]]'' (2025) and ''[[Aag Lagay Basti Mein]]'' (2026), both became among the highest-grossing Pakistani films of all time, further establishing her as a leading figure in the country's commercial cinema. She also produced the sports-based web series ''[[Baarwan Khiladi]]'' (2022).

Outside of acting, Khan supports social causes related to women's rights and the refugee crisis. She has worked with [[UNICEF]] since 2019 and was appointed as the national and global [[UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador]] for [[Afghan refugees in Pakistan]] the same year. She has also co-hosted several award ceremonies and is a prominent celebrity endorser for major brands and products. Khan is known to be private about her personal life, which often attracts media attention.

==Early life and education==
Mahira Khan was born on 21 December 1984 into a [[Muhajir (Pakistan)|Muhajir]] family in [[Karachi]], [[Sindh]], Pakistan.<ref name="india.com"/> In an [[The Reham Khan Show|online interview]] with [[Reham Khan]], she said that her parents are [[Urdu]]-speaking [[Pashtun|Pathans]]. Her father, Hafeez Khan, was born in [[Delhi]] during the [[British Raj]] and migrated to Pakistan after the [[partition of India]].<ref name="india.com/12dec2016">{{cite news|title=Mahira Khan: 8 things to know about Shah Rukh Khan's beautiful Raees actress from Pakistan|url=http://www.india.com/buzz/mahira-khan-8-things-to-know-about-shah-rukh-khans-beautiful-raees-actress-from-pakistan-1702407/|accessdate=13 December 2016|work=India.com|date=12 December 2016}}</ref> She has a younger brother, Hissan Khan, who is a journalist and entrepreneur.<ref name="Brother">{{cite news |title=Mahira Khan pens heartfelt wish for brother Hissan as she celebrates his birthday |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/952454-mahira-khan-pens-heartfelt-wish-for-brother-hissan-as-she-celebrates-his-birthday |work=The News |date=22 April 2022 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

She received her early education at [[Foundation Public School]], where she completed her [[A'Level|A-Levels]].<ref name="mahirabio">{{cite news|url=http://www.dailytimes.com.pk/entertainment/01-Nov-2015/mahira-khan-what-you-may-not-know-about-her|title=Mahira Khan — what you may not know about her|newspaper=Daily Times|date=1 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160128064810/http://www.dailytimes.com.pk/entertainment/01-Nov-2015/mahira-khan-what-you-may-not-know-about-her|archive-date=28 January 2016}}</ref> At the age of seventeen, she moved to [[California]] in the [[United States]] for higher education and enrolled at [[Santa Monica College]]. Mahira was the first woman in her family to travel abroad alone.<ref name="newsline/march2012">{{cite news|title=Profile: Mahira Khan {{!}} Newsline|url=http://newslinemagazine.com/magazine/profile-mahira-khan/|accessdate=14 December 2016|work=Newsline|date=March 2012}}</ref> She later said that living in the United States on her own helped her become "strong and independent."<ref name="The News on Sunday">{{cite web|url=http://tns.thenews.com.pk/unusual-shining-star/|title=Mahira Khan: the unusual, shining star|work=The News on Sunday|accessdate=15 October 2014}}</ref> She then enrolled at the [[University of Southern California]] for a master's degree in English literature. During this period, she worked part-time as a cashier at [[Rite Aid]]. Reflecting on the experience, she said: "I used to mop floors, clean floors, run the till and shut the store at night."<ref name="india.com"/> After completing her first year, Khan decided to pursue her interest in acting and left her studies, returning to Pakistan.<ref name=mahirabio/>

==Career==
=== Early work (2006–2011) ===
Khan began her career in 2006 as a [[VJ (media personality)|video jockey]] at [[MTV Pakistan]], where she hosted the live show ''Most Wanted'' five days a week.<ref name="dawn.com/22Oct2013">{{cite news |title=In conversation with Mahira Khan |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1050749 |newspaper=Dawn |date=22 October 2013 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref> She later hosted ''Weekend with Mahira'' on [[AAG TV]] in 2008, which featured interviews with celebrities.<ref name="tribune.com/14Jan2012">{{cite news |title=Mahira Khan: From VJ to TV actor |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/321294/mahira-khan-from-vj-to-tv-actor |newspaper=The Express Tribune |date=14 January 2012 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

In 2011, she made her film debut with a supporting role in [[Bol (film)|''Bol'']], directed by [[Shoaib Mansoor]]. She played Ayesha, a friend of the lead character, and the film became one of Pakistan's highest-grossing films at the time.<ref name="BolBoxOffice">{{cite news |title='Bol' smashes Pakistani box office records |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/archive/print/618088-bol-smashes-pakistani-box-office-records |work=The News |date=11 June 2011 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref> The success of the film marked her transition from television presenter to actor.<ref name="tribune.com/14Jan2012" />

=== Breakthrough and television success (2011–2016) ===
[[File:Mahira Khan.jpg|thumb|upright=0.9|right|Khan at an event for [[Zindagi TV]] in 2016]]
Khan gained nationwide fame with the television drama ''[[Humsafar]]'' (2011), in which she played Khirad Ehsan opposite [[Fawad Khan]]. The serial, based on [[Farhat Ishtiaq]]'s novel, became a cultural phenomenon in Pakistan and among South Asian audiences abroad.<ref name="tribune.com/14Jan2012" /> Her performance earned her the [[12th Lux Style Awards#Television|Lux Style Award for Best Television Actress]] and established her as a leading name in Pakistani television.<ref name="dawn.com/22Oct2013" />

Following the success of ''Humsafar'', she starred in the spiritual romance ''[[Shehr-e-Zaat]]'' (2012), portraying Falak, a woman on a journey of self-discovery and faith. The serial received critical acclaim and earned her the [[1st Hum Awards#Winners and nominees|Hum Award for Best Actress]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Shehr-e-Zaat: Mahira Khan shines in a story of self-realisation |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/425997/shehr-e-zaat-mahira-khan-shines-in-a-story-of-self-realisation |newspaper=The Express Tribune |date=27 August 2012 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

In 2014, she appeared in the biographical romance ''[[Sadqay Tumhare]]'', written by [[Khalil-ur-Rehman Qamar]], playing Shano. The drama, based on Qamar's real-life love story, was another success and earned her the [[3rd Hum Awards#Winners and nominees|Hum Award for Best Actress]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Mahira Khan wins Best Actress for Sadqay Tumhare |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/858414/hum-awards-2015-mahira-khan-wins-best-actress-for-sadqay-tumhare |newspaper=The Express Tribune |date=30 March 2015 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

Her next major television appearance was ''[[Bin Roye (TV series)|Bin Roye]]'' (2016), adapted from Farhat Ishtiaq's novel of the same name. She reprised her film role for the serial version, which became a commercial success and reinforced her reputation as one of Pakistan's leading actresses.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bin Roye: Mahira Khan lights up the screen once again |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1194483 |newspaper=Dawn |date=18 July 2015 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

=== Film Stardom and Television Return (2015–present) ===
Khan made her return to cinema with ''[[Bin Roye]]'' (2015), opposite [[Humayun Saeed]] and [[Armeena Khan]]. The film was both critically and commercially successful, earning her the [[15th Lux Style Awards#Winners and nominees|Lux Style Award for Best Actress (Film)]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Bin Roye makes box office history in Pakistan |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/924788/bin-roye-makes-box-office-history-in-pakistan |newspaper=The Express Tribune |date=25 July 2015 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref> 

She next appeared in ''[[Ho Mann Jahaan]]'' (2016), a coming-of-age musical drama, alongside [[Adeel Hussain]], [[Sheheryar Munawar]], and [[Sonya Jehan]]. The film performed well at the box office and earned her another [[16th Lux Style Awards#Winners and nominees|Lux Style Award for Best Actress (Film)]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ho Mann Jahaan opens to positive reviews |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1020858/ho-mann-jahaan-opens-to-positive-reviews |newspaper=The Express Tribune |date=1 January 2016 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

In 2017, she made her Hindi film debut in India with [[Rahul Dholakia]]'s gangster action film ''[[Raees (2017 film)|Raees]]'' opposite [[Shah Rukh Khan]]. The film was a moderate commercial success, nonetheless, ranking among the highest-grossing Indian films of the year.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mahira Khan shines in Bollywood debut Raees |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1310762 |newspaper=Dawn |date=27 January 2017 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref> Due to political tensions between India and Pakistan, she was unable to participate in the film’s promotional activities in India.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mahira Khan banned from promoting Raees in India |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1308994/mahira-khan-banned-promoting-raees-india |newspaper=The Express Tribune |date=24 January 2017 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

Later that year, she starred in the social-drama ''[[Verna (film)|Verna]]'', directed by [[Shoaib Mansoor]], playing a rape survivor seeking justice. Her performance received widespread praise and a [[17th Lux Style Awards#Winners and Nominees|Lux Style Award for Best Actress (Film)]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Mahira Khan's fearless performance in Verna wins praise |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1562824/4-mahira-khans-fearless-performance-verna-wins-praise |newspaper=The Express Tribune |date=18 November 2017 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

In the 2018 romantic comedy ''[[7 Din Mohabbat In|Saat Din Mohabbat In]]'', Mahira Khan played Neeli, a wry and humorous mohallah girl, marking her first venture into the comedy genre. While the film received mixed reviews, with some critics praising her comic timing and versatility, others found the acting unconvincing. Despite the polarized reception, the film was a commercial success.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mahira Khan and Sheheryar Munawar starrer 'Saat Din Mohabbat In' begins shooting |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1178116#1 |work=Dawn Images |date=2017-02-07 |access-date=2026-08-31}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Eid hit Saat Din Mohabbat In continues to enthrall fans |url=https://inp.net.pk/article-detail/inp-wealthpk/eid-hit-saat-din-mohabbat-in-continues-to-enthrall-fans |work=INP |date=2018-06-22 |access-date=2026-08-31}}</ref>

In 2019, she appeared in the romantic musical ''[[Superstar (2019 film)|Superstar]]'' opposite [[Bilal Ashraf]]. The film was commercially successful and her performance was positively reviewed. She received [[19th Lux Style Awards#Winners and nominees|Lux Style Award for Best Actress (Film)]] in both critics and viewers choice categories.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mahira Khan's Superstar reigns at the box office |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2048823/4-mahira-khans-superstar-reigns-box-office |newspaper=The Express Tribune |date=17 August 2019 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

Mahira Khan returned to television in 2021 with ''[[Hum Kahan Ke Sachay Thay]]'', ending a five-year hiatus with her role as Mehreen, a psychologically complex character. The drama, written by [[Umera Ahmed]] and directed by [[Farooq Rind]], explored themes of trauma, abuse, and family politics. While the series received mixed reactions for its dark narrative, Khan's performance was widely praised for its depth, with critics calling her portrayal "sensational" and "incredible". The project reaffirmed her ability to anchor challenging, emotionally demanding roles.<ref name="mahira_khan_returns">{{cite web |first=Irfan Ul |last=Haq |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1187972 |title=Mahira Khan returns to our television screens after five-year hiatus with Hum Kahan Kai Sachey Thay |date=9 July 2021 |website=[[Dawn News|Dawn Images]] |access-date=11 July 2021}}</ref> Mahira Khan also starred in the telefilm ''[[Aik Hai Nigar]]'', a biopic of Lieutenant General [[Nigar Johar]], Pakistan's first female three-star general. The film was released on October 23, 2021, and was directed by [[Adnan Sarwar]], with a script by Umera Ahmed. Mahira Khan also co-produced the project, describing it as an "honour" to portray a woman she deeply admired.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/878276-mahira-khan-plays|title=Mahira Khan plays 'Pakistan's first female Three star General' in 'Ek Hai Nigar'|website=www.thenews.com.pk|date=14 August 2021|access-date=}}</ref><ref name="October 23">{{Cite web |author=Images Staff |date=14 October 2021 |title=Mahira Khan's Aik Hai Nigar to release on October 23 |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1188591 |access-date=28 October 2021 |website=Images |language=en}}</ref>

After a brief hiatus, she returned to the screen in 2022 with ''[[Quaid-e-Azam Zindabad]]'', an action-comedy film opposite [[Fahad Mustafa]], which became one of the year's highest-grossing Pakistani films.<ref>{{cite news |title=Quaid-e-Azam Zindabad scores big at box office |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2369107/quaid-e-azam-zindabad-scores-big-at-box-office |newspaper=The Express Tribune |date=25 July 2022 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

The same year, she starred in the epic action film ''[[The Legend of Maula Jatt]]'' alongside [[Fawad Khan]], [[Hamza Ali Abbasi]], and [[Humaima Malick]]. The film became the [[List of highest-grossing Pakistani films|highest-grossing Pakistani film of all time]] and was lauded for its production, direction, and performances.<ref>{{cite news |title=The Legend of Maula Jatt becomes Pakistan's highest-grossing film |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1715960 |newspaper=Dawn |date=17 October 2022 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref> Khan's portrayal of Mukkho received widespread praise from both critics and audiences.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mahira Khan delivers strong performance in The Legend of Maula Jatt |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2382829/mahira-khan-delivers-strong-performance-in-the-legend-of-maula-jatt |newspaper=The Express Tribune |date=20 October 2022 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref> She also appeared as the narrator in ''[[Razia (TV series)|Razia]]'', a 2023 socio-comedy mini series.<ref name=tribune>{{cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2430827/i-said-yes-in-a-heartbeat-mahira-khan-grateful-to-be-part-of-razia|title=I said yes in a heartbeat: Mahira Khan grateful to be part of 'Razia'|date=15 August 2023|access-date=16 August 2023|work=Express Tribune}}</ref>

In 2025, Mahira Khan starred in two major film releases. The romantic comedy ''[[Love Guru (2025 film)|Love Guru]]'', directed by [[Nadeem Baig (director)|Nadeem Baig]] and co-starring Humayun Saeed, emerged as the year's biggest commercial success, earning over Rs. 8 billion globally and setting new box office benchmarks.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cinema 2025: Pakistani films which shattered box office records |url=https://www.samaa.tv/2087343961-cinema-2025-pakistani-films-which-shatter-box-office-records#1 |work=Samaa TV |date=2025-12-31 |access-date=2026-08-31}}</ref> Her second film, ''[[Neelofar (film)|Neelofar]]'', directed by Ammar Rasool, was a romantic drama where she played a blind girl opposite Fawad Khan. This marked their third on-screen collaboration together following their appearances in ''[[Humsafar]]'' and ''[[The Legend of Maula Jatt]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|date=28 December 2020|title=13 Iconic On-Screen Pakistani Couples Who Made Us Fall in Love|work=Brandsynario|url=https://www.brandsynario.com/10-iconic-on-screen-pakistani-couples-who-made-us-fall-in-love/|access-date=16 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=9 December 2020|title=Inside Mahira and Fawad Khan's upcoming film 'Neelofar': See BTS photos|work=The News|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/756057|access-date=7 January 2022}}</ref>. The film was praised for its poetic storytelling, visual aesthetics, and the chemistry between the leads.<ref>{{cite news |title=Star-studded event premieres Neelofar |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2579787/star-studded-event-premieres-neelofar |work=The Express Tribune |date=2025-04-14 |access-date=2026-08-31}}</ref>

In 2026, Mahira starred in ''[[Aag Lagay Basti Mein]]'', which became the second highest-grossing Pakistani film of all time by crossing the Rs. 100 crore mark worldwide.<ref>{{cite news |title=Aag Lagay Basti Mein hits Rs101 crore worldwide |url=https://www.24newshd.tv/31-Jul-2026/aag-lagay-basti-mein-hits-rs101-crore-worldwide |work=24 News HD |date=2026-07-31 |access-date=2026-08-31}}</ref> This achievement means Mahira Khan now stars in three of the [[List of highest-grossing Pakistani films|top-grossing Pakistani films]], alongside ''The Legend of Maula Jatt'' and ''Love Guru'', solidifying her position as a leading figure in the country's commercial cinema.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mahira Khan Stars in Top 3 Highest-Grossing Films in Pakistan's History |url=https://eng.jeeveypakistan.com/?p=68551 |work=Jeevey Pakistan |date=2026-05-20 |access-date=2026-08-31}}</ref> Mahira Khan received positive response for her performance as Billo in ''[[Mitti De Baway]]'', a character who transforms from a lovestruck young woman into a ruthless, authoritative spiritual guide. Critics and audiences praised her nuanced portrayal of a figure who is both victim and oppressor. In addition to starring opposite [[Wahaj Ali]], she also produced the period revenge saga, which aired on [[Green Entertainment]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Mahira Khan, Wahaj Ali's 'Mitti De Baway' trailer wins praise from celebrities |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2626226/mahira-khan-wahaj-alis-mitti-de-baway-trailer-wins-praise-from-celebrities |work=The Express Tribune |date=2026-10-20 |access-date=2026-10-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mitti De Baway Episode 6: Public Applauds Script & Performances |url=https://reviewit.pk/mitti-de-baway-episode-6-public-applauds-script-performances/ |website=Reviewit.pk |date=2026-10-21 |access-date=2026-10-22}}</ref>

=== Other work ===
Apart from acting, Khan has also worked as a singer and producer. She once mentioned that director Shoaib Mansoor encouraged her to sing for his film ''[[Verna (film)|Verna]]'' (2017).<ref>{{cite news |title=Shoaib Mansoor feels I'm better at singing than acting: Mahira Khan |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1177070/shoaib-mansoor-feels-im-better-at-singing-than-acting-mahira-khan |work=Images (Dawn) |date=8 February 2017 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

In 2021, she started her own company, Soul Fry Films, and produced the web series ''[[Baarwan Khiladi]]'' (2022) with Nina Kashif.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mahira Khan turns producer with Baarwan Khiladi |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/tns/detail/785510-mahira-khan-turns-producer-with-baarwan-khiladi |work=The News |date=7 February 2021 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Mahira Khan's production debut "Baarwan Khiladi" to premiere on Tapmad TV |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/720096/mahiras-production-debut-baarwan-khiladi-to-premiere-on-tapmad-tv/ |work=Daily Times |date=3 February 2021 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

She has also appeared in brand campaigns and spoken about the importance of Pakistan–India collaborations in film and local digital content.<ref>{{cite news |title=Collaborations between India and Pakistan are extremely important: Mahira Khan |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1557054/think-collaborations-india-pakistan-extremely-important-mahira-khan |work=The Express Tribune |date=8 February 2018 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life and off-screen work==
While studying in the United States, Khan met businessman Ali Askari in 2005.<ref name="The News on Sunday"/> She moved back to Pakistan the following year and married him in 2007.<ref name=mahirabio/> The couple have a son, Azlaan, who was born in 2010. Khan and Askari divorced in 2015{{Citation needed|date=September 2026}} and share custody of their son.<ref name=mahirabio/> In 2019, she began dating entrepreneur Salim Karim, which she confirmed in an [[Tonite with HSY|online interview]] with [[Hassan Sheheryar Yasin]] in 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Raees actress Mahira Khan feels her boyfriend Salim Karim is a blessing |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/movies/celebrities/story/raees-actress-mahira-khan-feels-her-boyfriend-salim-karim-is-a-blessing-1688829-2020-14-6 |accessdate=14 June 2020 |date=14 June 2020 |work=India Today}}</ref> She married Karim in an intimate ceremony on 2 October 2023 in [[Bhurban]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Pakistani actor Mahira Khan looks ethereal as she marries businessman Salim Karim; watch video |url=https://www.livemint.com/news/world/pakistani-actor-mahira-khan-looks-ethereal-as-she-marries-businessman-salim-karim-video-11696242142116.html |access-date=3 October 2023 |work=Live Mint |date=2 October 2023 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Pakistani Actress Mahira Khan Marries Businessman Salim Karim In An Intimate Ceremony. Video Inside |url=https://www.ndtv.com/entertainment/pakistani-actress-mahira-khan-marries-businessman-salim-karim-in-an-intimate-ceremony-video-inside-4441944 |access-date=3 October 2023 |work=NDTV |date=2 October 2023 |language=en}}</ref> In September 2026, Khan announced that she is pregnant with her and Karim's first child.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Usman |first=Muhammad |date=2026-09-13 |title=Mahira Khan confirms pregnancy, shares heartfelt message with fans |url=https://www.thenews.pk/story/1437203-mahira-khan-confirms-pregnancy-shares-heartfelt-message-with-fans |access-date=2026-09-13 |website=www.thenews.pk |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Pakistani actress Mahira Khan announces second pregnancy at 41 in a stunning white dress, expecting baby with Salim Karim |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/life-style/fashion/celeb-style/pakistani-actress-mahira-khan-announces-second-pregnancy-at-41-in-a-stunning-white-dress-expecting-baby-with-salim-karim/articleshow/134174897.cms |access-date=2026-09-13 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

Khan has also taken part in charitable work. She visited Dubai (along with [[Maya Ali]] and then Prime Minister [[Imran Khan]]) and Los Angeles to raise funds for the [[Shaukat Khanum Memorial Hospital]] in 2018 and 2019.{{cn|date=May 2026}} She has worked with the [[United Nations Children's Fund|UNICEF]] since 2019,<ref>{{cite web |title=Mahira among top 10 'Sexiest Asian Women' along with Priyanka, Sonam |url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/1008215/mahira-among-top-10-sexiest-asian-women-along-with-priyanka-sonam/ |newspaper=The Express Tribune |date=11 December 2015 |accessdate=12 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151213181418/http://tribune.com.pk/story/1008215/mahira-among-top-10-sexiest-asian-women-along-with-priyanka-sonam/ |archive-date=13 December 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> and was appointed as a national and global [[UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador]] for [[Afghan refugees in Pakistan]] in the same year. Her work was praised by the UN Secretary-General [[António Guterres]] during his visit to Pakistan in February 2020. Khan often speaks on issues such as women's rights, child safety, and gender-based violence. On [[International Women's Day|Women's Day]] in 2020, she collaborated with [[Shoaib Mansoor]] on the music video "Dua-e-Reem".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.somethinghaute.com/mahira-khan-and-shoaib-mansoor-reunite-for-dua-e-reem/|title= Mahira Khan and Shoaib Mansoor reunite for 'Dua-e-Reem'|author=|work=Something Haute|date= 3 March 2020|accessdate=9 March 2020}}</ref> The song, a modern take on [[Lab Pe Aati Hai Dua]] by [[Allama Iqbal]], was set in the [[British Raj|pre-partition era]] and featured her as a young woman reflecting on justice and equality after marriage.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/276288-dua-e-reem-shoaib-mansoor-releases-song-featuring-mahira-khan-on-womens-day|title= Dua-e-Reem: Shoaib Mansoor releases song featuring Mahira Khan on Women's Day|author=|work=Geo News|date= 8 March 2020|accessdate=8 March 2020}}</ref> The song was widely praised and became popular across the [[Indian subcontinent]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Sabeen |first1=Laiba |url=https://www.oyeyeah.com/music/mahira-khan-is-the-voice-of-all-young-brides-in-dua-e-reem/|title=Mahira Khan is the voice of all young brides in Dua E Reem|work=Oye Yeah!|date=9 March 2020 |accessdate=9 March 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/lifestyle/a-womans-dua-rises-against-domestic-violence-marital-rape-6451224/|title= A Pakistan woman's 'dua' against domestic violence, marital rape, echoes in India|author=|work=Indian Express|accessdate=9 March 2020}}</ref>

In 2018, Khan and her brother Hissan<ref name="Brother" /> launched a clothing line, Mashion!.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1155475|title=Mahira Khan is Launching Her Own Clothing Line, Mashion! |author=|work=HIP Pakistan|accessdate=13 August 2018}}</ref> Later that year, the two founded a media platform of the same name that focuses on empowering women and spreading awareness about mental health in Pakistan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://startupguide.com.pk/mahira-khan-hassaan-khan-on-changing-the-game-with-mashion/|title=Mahira Khan & Hassaan Khan On Changing the Game with Mashion |author=|work=Startup Guide|date=21 January 2019 |accessdate=21 January 2019}}</ref> In 2020, she hosted ''Khandani Kitchen'', a [[YouTube]] show by Mashion featuring male celebrities cooking traditional dishes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mashion.pk/adnan-siddiqui-teaches-mahira-khan-how-to-cook-the-perfect-eid-meal/|title=Adnan Siddiqui Teaches Mahira Khan How To Cook The Perfect Eid Meal|author=|work=Mashion|date=2 August 2020 |accessdate=2 August 2020}}</ref> In September 2020, she joined the [[Commonwealth of Nations]] campaign "No More", raising awareness about sexual and domestic violence.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dunyanews.tv/en/Entertainment/563554-Mahira-Khan-joins-Commonwealth-saying-no-more-sexual-domestic-violence|title=Mahira Khan joins Commonwealth in saying no more to sexual, domestic violence|author=|work=Dunya News|date=14 February 2008 |accessdate=12 September 2020}}</ref>

On 6 November 2024, Khan received the Lifetime Achievement Award from the [[UK Parliament]] for her work as a cultural ambassador and her contributions to women's empowerment.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-11-07 |title=Mahira Khan wins Lifetime Achievement Award by UK Parliament |url=https://jang.com.pk/en/24618-mahira-khan-wins-lifetime-achievement-award-by-uk-parliament-news#:~:text=Mahira%20Khan%20wins%20Lifetime%20Achievement%20Award%20by%20UK%20Parliament,-The%20prestigious%20award&text=Pakistani%20actress%20Mahira%20Khan%20won,work%20as%20a%20cultural%20ambassador. |access-date=2024-12-27 |website=Daily Jang |language=en}}</ref>

WIKIPEDIA REVISION DOCUMENT: Mani (actor)
======================================================================

{{Short description|Pakistani television actor}}
{{Use Pakistani English|date=January 2020}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=January 2020}}

'''Salman Saqib Sheikh''' ({{langx|ur|{{nq|سلمان ثاقب شیخ}}}}), credited as '''Mani''', is a Pakistani actor, producer, screenwriter, politician and host. Mani is mostly known for his comic roles. He started his career as an anchor and roadshow host before becoming a sitcom and comedy actor.

He is known for his roles in ''[[Meri Teri Kahani]]'', [[Bandish (2019 TV series)|''Bandish'']] and the telefilm ''Dil Toh Bacha Hai''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2068646/4|title=Mani jokes about his 'first' marriage in an interview|work=[[The Express Tribune]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2018/10/24/mani-clarifies-stance-over-controversial-metoo-comments/|title=Mani clarifies stance over controversial #MeToo comments {{!}} Pakistan Today|website=www.pakistantoday.com.pk|access-date=2020-01-19}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1181764|title=Review: This black magic TV drama is a Pakistani horror fan's delight|last=Khan|first=Sheeba|date=2019-02-02|website=[[Dawn (newspaper)|DAWN]]|language=en|access-date=2020-01-19}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Mani was born on 22 March 1977 and was raised in a locality of [[Gulshan-e-Iqbal]]<ref>{{cite web |title=Gulshan-e-Iqbal |url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulshan-e-Iqbal |website=Wikipedia |publisher=Wikipedia |language=en |date=9 March 2024}}</ref>{{Circular reference|date=February 2025}} in [[Karachi]]. During an interview with [[Samina Peerzada]], Mani explains that despite his father Saquib Sheikh and elder sister Ayesha Mirza being actors, he was interested in sports during his early years and did not think to venture into television. His initial interest grew after a minor appearance in theatre, with the theatre group ''Katha'' stars [[Sania Saeed]] and [[Nadia Jamil]].

== Media career ==

=== Early career as actor and scriptwriter ===
He started his career in television as a junior anchor and host before becoming an actor. He wrote scripts for [[Fakhar-e-Alam]]'s show ''Boom Boom Bastic'' which aired on [[PTV Home|PTV]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mani On Rewind With Samina Peerzada {{!}} Part I|url=https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=tTszCyDV-sQ}}</ref> In the early 2000s, he also worked on various shows, including Sarak Chapp, which aired on Geo TV and ATV. Mani among Azfar Ali also created the ''Azfar Mani Show'' on [[AAG TV]].<ref>[[AAG TV]]</ref> The show experienced significant growth within the community and among the general public. This airing made them popular among Pakistani TV channels.

Mani also participated in campaigns run by [[Shaukat Khanum Cancer Hospital]]<ref>[[Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital and Research Centre|Shaukat Khanum Cancer Hospital]]</ref> which experienced a great turnout due to his popularity in Pakistan at the time. He was also cast in various commercials and campaigns for Pepsi, Tepal, Ufone, and Mobilink.

=== Host ===
In 2001, he hosted the first ever [[Street performance|Road Show]] in Pakistan's Television history called ''Streets.'' Aired on Indus Vision, the show conducted street interviews on contemporary issues. He was one of the first to introduce Road Shows to Pakistan, succeeding commercially due to its authentic nature. He also hosted two other road shows called ''Road Romeo'' and ''Sarrak Chhap'' aired on [[ATV (Pakistan)|ATV]] and [[Jang Media Group|Geo TV]] respectively.

Mani is also known as the pioneer of roadshows<!-- source? -->. He was a part of what is now known as the golden era of Pakistani Television. Mani was a part of the show ''Sub Set Hai'' including himself, [[Adnan Shah Tipu]], [[Salma Hassan]], and Azfar Ali. The show was met with great audience reception throughout the Indian subcontinent. Mani had been part of various music channels, such as Indus Music and The Music.

A similar show ''Ulta Seedha'', penned by [[Faisal Qureshi (television personality)|Faisal Qureshi]], co-hosted by Mani, was also aired on [[Jang Media Group|Geo TV]]. Mani then hosted the first [[talk show]] ''Casual'' for newly founded [[Hum TV]] in 2006. Hira and Mani started the show at Hum TV, specifically the ''Hum 2 Humara Show''. Both of them served as the show's hosts. They upheld their reputation as an ideal couple, receiving widespread affection from the audience. The show aired for about three years, during which time different actors and actresses came together on the TV show.

=== Production ===
Mani produced a sports show ''Champions'' on [[ARY Digital]]. He also produced sitcoms ''Zerooos'' and ''Khala Surayya'' aired on Geo TV.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Mani On Rewind With Samina Peerzada {{!}} Part II |url=https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=Zei8BLyEVFg}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-07-08 |title=Mani makes new accounts on social media to bully politicians |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2309433/mani-makes-new-accounts-on-social-media-to-bully-politicians |access-date=2023-02-22 |website=The Express Tribune |language=en}}</ref>

== Political career ==
Besides being an actor, Mani is also very active in politics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-25 |title=Mani shares hilarious ideas up his sleeve to save Pakistan |url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/25-Jul-2022/mani-shares-hilarious-ideas-up-his-sleeve-to-save-pakistan |access-date=2023-02-22 |website=Daily Pakistan Global |language=en}}</ref> He actively supported [[Imran Khan]]'s [[Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf]] and attended several processions<ref>{{Cite web |author=Web Desk |date=2020-12-12 |title=Politics affected my acting career - Mani |url=https://www.behtareen.pk/politics-affected-acting-career-mani/ |access-date=2023-02-22 |website=Behtareen |language=en-US}}</ref> across Pakistan<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-07-26 |title=Hand Pakistan over to Imran Khan: Mani |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/972133/hand-pakistan-over-to-imran-khan-mani/ |access-date=2023-02-22 |website=Daily Times |language=en-US}}</ref> before joining the [[Pak Sarzameen Party]] in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-07-09 |title=Pak Sarzameen Party welcomes new entrants |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/265240/pak-sarzameen-party-welcomes-new-entrants/ |access-date=2021-05-01 |website=Daily Times |language=en-US}}</ref> He and his wife, [[Hira Mani]], have criticized Imran Khan and Altaf Hussain on several occasions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hira Mani takes a jab at PM Imran Khan, saying he should allow people to worry |url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/397263-hira-mani-takes-jibes-at-pm-saying-he-should-allow-people-to-feel-worry |access-date=2023-02-23 |website=www.geo.tv |language=en}}</ref> He also participated in the polio campaign for UNICEF.

== Personal life ==
He married fellow actress [[Hira Salman]] in 2008. Hira Salman, commonly known as [[Hira Mani]], in her interview at Speak Your Heart With Samina Peerzada on 19 Oct 2018 [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cFKxlM96EqE] explained how she met Mani. She had secretly gotten Mani's phone number from his then girlfriend and phoned him under the alias of Mariam. During this time she was engaged to a Banker in Dubai whom she later left to be with Mani.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-12-12 |title=I give my all to reach my wife's acting level: Mani |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2275676/i-give-my-all-to-reach-my-wifes-acting-level-mani |access-date=2023-02-22 |website=The Express Tribune |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-qGZHXUS3ss |title=Mani {{!}} HIRA aur MERA comparison hee nahy hai {{!}} Exclusive interview {{!}} Part 04 of 04 |date=2020-11-28 |last=RAVA Entertainment |access-date=2026-02-12 |via=YouTube}}</ref> Their marriage ceremony took place on 18 April 2008. They frequently work together in most of their projects after marriage.<ref name="Dailyp">{{Cite web |title=Hira Mani stole Mani from her friend, broke off her own engagement for him |url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/hira-mani-stole-mani-from-her-friend-broke-off-her-own-engagement-for-him/ |access-date=2019-02-13 |website=[[Daily Pakistan]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Hira Mani gives success credit to husband Salman Sheikh |url=https://dunyanews.tv/en/Entertainment/528481-Hira-Mani-gives-success-credit-husband-Salman-Sheikh |access-date=2020-01-19 |website=Dunya News}}</ref><ref name="express2">{{Cite web |date=2018-03-04 |title=I'm proud to be labelled as 'Mani's wife': Hira Mani |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1650803/4 |access-date=2019-02-13 |website=[[The Express Tribune]] |language=en-US}}</ref> together they have two sons: Muzammil (born in 2009) and Ibrahim (born in 2014).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Syeda Hira Salman (@hiramaniofficial) • Instagram photos and videos |url=https://www.instagram.com/hiramaniofficial/ |access-date=2019-06-16 |website=www.instagram.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-08-17 |title=My purpose is to act, no matter what the medium is: Hira |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/449419/my-purpose-is-to-act-no-matter-what-the-medium-is-hira/ |access-date=2020-01-20 |website=Daily Times |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Yaqeen Ka Safar is honest and original, and has changed the paradigm of Pakistani dramas |url=https://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/59539/yaqeen-ka-safar-is-honest-and-original-and-has-changed-the-paradigm-of-pakistani-dramas/ |access-date=2020-01-19 |website=[[The Express Tribune]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Mawra Hussain''' ({{Langx|ur|{{nq|ماورہ حسین}}}}; born 28  September 1992), known professionally as '''Mawra Hocane''', is a [[Pakistani people|Pakistani]] actress who primarily works in [[Urdu]] television.<ref name="Dunya News"/> She made her acting debut in 2011 with ''[[Khichari|Khichari Salsa]]''.<ref name="Name">{{cite web |author=Hassan Choudary |title=Unraveling the mystery: Here's why Mawra and Urwa's surname is 'Hocane' |url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/975067/unraveling-the-mystery-heres-why-mawra-and-urwas-surname-is-hocane/ |newspaper=[[The Express Tribune]] |date=19 October 2015 |access-date=10 December 2015 |archive-date=25 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181225220123/https://tribune.com.pk/story/975067/unraveling-the-mystery-heres-why-mawra-and-urwas-surname-is-hocane/ |url-status=live}}</ref> She made her [[Bollywood]] debut with the romantic tragedy, ''[[Sanam Teri Kasam (2016 film)|Sanam Teri Kasam]]'' (2016) and her [[Pakistani]] film debut with the comedy drama ''[[Jawani Phir Nahi Ani 2]]'' (2018).<ref name="ramp">{{cite news |url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/mawra-hocane-making-history-in-pakistani-fashion-industry/ |title=Mawra Hocane making history in Pakistani fashion industry |website=dailypakistan.com |publisher=Daily Pakistan Global |date=12 December 2018 |access-date=19 December 2018 |archive-date=19 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181219182648/https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/mawra-hocane-making-history-in-pakistani-fashion-industry/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

Hocane has received praise for her portrayals of Nadia in ''[[Ek Tamanna Lahasil Si]]'' (2012), Haya in ''[[Aahista Aahista (TV series)|Aahista Aahista]]'' (2014), Sammi in ''[[Sammi (TV series)|Sammi]]'' (2017), Anaya Aziz in ''[[Sabaat]]'' (2020), and Mehrbano in ''[[Qissa Meherbano Ka]]'' (2021).<ref name="indc">{{cite news |title=Here's what Indian critics had to say about Mawra Hocane's Bolly debut, Sanam Teri Kasam |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1174807 |access-date=18 November 2016 |work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|DAWN Images]] |date=10 February 2016 |archive-date=15 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161215132617/http://images.dawn.com/news/1174807 |url-status=live}}</ref> She won [[Hum Award for Best Actress]] for her performance in ''[[Neem (TV series)|Neem]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1190835/portion-of-hum-awards-ticket-sale-proceeds-to-be-donated-to-flood-relief-efforts|title=Portion of HUM Awards ticket sale proceeds to be donated to flood relief efforts|accessdate=September 12, 2022|work=Dawn Images|date=12 September 2022 }}</ref>

== Early life and family ==
Hocane was born as Mawra Hussain on 28 September 1992 in [[Karachi, Sindh]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/1004483/mawra-hocane-marks-30th-birthday-with-adorable-reel/ |title=Mawra Hocane marks her 30th birthday with an adorable reel |work=Daily Times |access-date=28 September 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="MawraHBD">{{Cite news |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2379031/celebrating-mawra-hocanes-30th-birthday-with-her-top-five-roles%3famp=1 |title=Celebrating Mawra Hocane's 30th birthday with her top five roles |work=The Express Tribune |access-date=28 September 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref> Actress [[Urwa Hocane]] is her elder sister, while actor [[Farhan Saeed]] is her brother-in-law.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1586337/4-urwa-hocane-farhan-saeed-celebrate-year-matrimony-sizzling-photoshoot/ |title=Urwa Hocane, Farhan Saeed celebrate a year of matrimony with sizzling photoshoot |date=2017-12-17 |work=The Express Tribune |access-date=2018-11-23 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In 7th grade, she started spelling her family name as "Hocane" to give it a unique form.<ref name="Name" /> She holds a degree in law from the [[University of London]], which she finished after returning to school.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mawra Hocane goes back to law school to 'finish what she started' |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1177115/mawra-hocane-goes-back-to-law-school-to-finish-what-she-started |access-date=17 February 2017 |work=Images Dawn |date=17 February 2017 |archive-date=17 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170217120952/http://images.dawn.com/news/1177115/mawra-hocane-goes-back-to-law-school-to-finish-what-she-started |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="deg1" />

== Career ==
Hocane performed as a theatre artist before working as a [[VJ (media personality)|VJ]] at [[ARY Musik]].<ref name="MawraHBD" /> She made her acting debut in 2011 with the drama ''Khichari Salsa''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/1283037/mawra-hocane-debuts-in-indian-music-video/ |title=Mawra Hocane debuts in Indian music video |date=5 April 2025 |work=www.dailytimes.com.pk}}</ref> She acted in the dramas ''[[Aahista Aahista (TV series)|Aahista Aahista]]'', ''[[Ik Tamanna Lahasil Si]],'' and ''[[Nikhar Gaye Gulab Sare]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gulfnews.com/entertainment/mawra-hocane-i-chose-not-to-be-just-the-heros-eye-candy-1.1664868|title=Mawra Hocane: I chose not to be just the hero's eye candy|work=Gulf News|date=3 February 2016|access-date=29 December 2023|author1=Manjari Saxena|author2=Deputy tabloid}}</ref> In 2014, she portrayed the titular role of Bushra in ARY Digital's ''[[Mein Bushra]]'' as a determined and capable daughter of a strict father. Hocane termed the project among her favourites.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1487044 |title=THE ICON INTERVIEW: THE 'HOCANE' PHENOMENON |date=9 June 2019 |access-date=22 June 2024 |work=Dawn (newspaper)}}</ref>

[[File:Mawra Hocane on the sets of 'Sanam Teri Kasam' at Filmalaya02 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Hocane on ''[[Sanam Teri Kasam (2016 film)|Sanam Teri Kasam]]'' set]]

Hocane made her [[Hindi film]] debut with the romantic tragedy ''[[Sanam Teri Kasam (2016 film)|Sanam Teri Kasam]]'' opposite [[Harshvardhan Rane]].<ref name="tr">{{cite news |url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/898115/not-one-not-two-mawra-hocane-has-signed-three-bollywood-films/ |title=Not one, not two, Mawra Hocane has signed three Bollywood films! |work=The Express Tribune |date=5 June 2015 |access-date=3 October 2015 |first=Hassan |last=Choudary |archive-date=26 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181226044755/https://tribune.com.pk/story/898115/not-one-not-two-mawra-hocane-has-signed-three-bollywood-films/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Harshvardhan Rane and Mawra Hocane promote 'Sanam Teri Kasam'; see pics |url=https://www.mid-day.com/entertainment/bollywood-news/article/harshvardhan-rane-and-mawra-hocane-promote--sanam-teri-kasam--16897152 |work=Mid Day |date=26 January 2016 |access-date=28 January 2016}}</ref> She portrayed a South Indian girl who works as a librarian.<ref>{{cite web |title=Eros releases first look of Harshvardhan and Mawra's "Sanam Teri Kasam" |url=http://www.dailytimes.com.pk/entertainment/07-Dec-2015/eros-releases-first-look-of-mawra-s-sanam-teri-kasam |website=Daily Times |access-date=8 December 2015 |date=7 December 2015}}</ref> ''[[Hindustan Times]]'' noted, "Mawra is a delight to watch as Saru. She slips into the demure character with ease and her get-up certainly adds to her persona.", while ''[[News18]]'' mentioned her as "one of the most incredible performer."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sanam Teri Kasam Movie Review: Intense and emotional |work=Hindustan Times |date=5 February 2016 |access-date=10 February 2016 |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/movie-reviews/sanam-teri-kasam-review-intense-and-emotional/story-RXorjaHSqxtBYsC2b2UdSP.html}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title='Sanam Teri Kasam' review: It doesn't do justice to Mawra Hocane, Harshvardhan Rane's potential as actors |work=News18 |date=6 February 2016 |access-date=11 February 2016 |url=https://www.news18.com/news/movies/sanam-teri-kasam-review-this-cliched-love-story-doesnt-do-justice-to-mawra-hocane-harshvardhan-ranes-potential-as-actors-1199832.html}}</ref>

In 2018, she made her Pakistani film debut with the romantic comedy ''[[Jawani Phir Nahi Ani 2]]'' opposite [[Fahad Mustafa]].<ref name="jpna2">{{Cite news |date=20 October 2017 |title=Mawra Hocane joins cast of 'Jawani Phir Nahi Aani 2' |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1536305/mawra-hocane-joins-cast-jawani-phir-nahi-aani-2/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171021030051/https://tribune.com.pk/story/1536305/mawra-hocane-joins-cast-jawani-phir-nahi-aani-2/ |archive-date=21 October 2017 |access-date=20 October 2017 |work=The Express Tribune}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://gulfnews.com/1.2131059|title='Jawani Phir Nahi Ani 2' set to up the glamour|author=Usman Ghafoor|date=27 November 2017|access-date=4 December 2017|work=Gulf News}}</ref> The film is the [[List of highest-grossing Pakistani films|second-highest-grossing Pakistani film]] worldwide. ''[[Pakistan Today]]'' noted, "Mawra is a good addition to the film and she nailed her character of a spoilt, young heiress."<ref>{{cite news|title=Step onto the rollercoaster as the JPNA boys take you on yet another crazy ride|url=https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2018/08/22/step-onto-the-rollercoaster-as-the-jpna-boys-take-you-on-yet-another-crazy-ride/|date=22 August 2018|access-date=23 August 2018|work=Pakistan Today|author=Saman Shafiq}}</ref>

From 2018 to 2019, she narrated and appeared in the period drama ''[[Aangan (Hum TV series)|Aangan]]'' based on [[Khadija Mastoor]]'s [[Aangan (novel)|novel of the same name]]. Hocane portrayed a resilient [[Hindustani people|Hindustani]] who endures bitter experiences in love.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1181512|title=Playing Aaliya has made me a stronger woman: Mawra Hocane on her Aangan character|date=20 December 2018|work=images.dawn.com|author=Images Staff}}</ref> In 2019, she appeared as the juvenile and bubbly Sunehri in ''[[Daasi (TV series)|Daasi]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1183569 |title=Mawra Hocane and Adeel Hussain are pairing up for Hum TV's Daasi |last=Haq |first=Irfan Ul |date=26 August 2019 |website=DAWN |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200612032355/https://images.dawn.com/news/1183569 |archive-date=12 June 2020 |access-date=9 September 2019}}</ref> Her next role of a headstrong and ambitious university student in ''[[Sabaat]]'' earned her dual nominations of Best TV Actress at the [[20th Lux Style Awards]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/593990/mawra-hocane-talks-about-her-chemistry-with-ameer-gilani/ |title=Mawra Hocane talks about her chemistry with Ameer Gilani |date=12 April 2020 |website=Daily Times |access-date=25 April 2020 |archive-date=2 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200702224810/https://dailytimes.com.pk/593990/mawra-hocane-talks-about-her-chemistry-with-ameer-gilani/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2021, she played the title role of a victim of domestic abuse and [[marital rape]] in the drama ''[[Qissa Meherbano Ka]]''.<ref>{{cite August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220818101429/https://images.dawn.com/news/1189589/|url-status=live}}</ref> Her first role in 2023 was of a determined philanthropist Zimal Riyasat in the romance-drama ''[[Neem (TV series)|Neem]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2407309/after-sabaat-ameer-gilani-mawra-hocane-set-to-star-in-neem? |work=Express Tribune Award for Best Actress]], at the [[9th Hum Awards]].<ref name="win">{{cite web|url=https://jang.com.pk/en/21732-mawra-hocane-wins-best-actor-female-2023-award-for-outstanding-performance-in-neem-news role in 2024 in the comedy ''Let's Try Mohabbat'', where she portrayed a newlywed bride who changes the perspectives of her in-laws with her arrival.<ref>{{cite web gynecologist Dr. Zara who copes with her troubled marriage.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.khaleejtimes.com/entertainment/pakistani-tv-actress-mawra-hocane-on-playing-a-doctor-in-jafaa |title=Pakistani TV actress Mawra Hocane on playing a doctor in 'Jafaa' |author=Mahwash Ajaz|date=10 July 2024|access-date=15 July 2024|work=[[The Khaleej Times]]|url-status=live web|url=https://www.filmfare.com/news/bollywood/mawra-ameer-gilanis-agar-tum-sath-ho-more-pak-dramas-to-watch-this-week-71726.html |title=Mawra, Ameer Gilani's Agar Tum Sath Ho & More Pak Dramas To 2025 |author=Mahwash Ajaz |work=[[The Nation (newspaper)|The Nation]]}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Hocane met actor [[Ameer Gilani]] on the sets of ''[[Sabaat]]'' in 2020. On 5 February 2025, Hocane married Gilani in a traditional [[Muslim wedding]] in [[Lahore]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/bollywood/sanam-teri-kasam-star-mawra-hocane-ties-the-knot-with-pakistani-actor-ameer-gilani-shares-dreamy-wedding-pictures-101738759653795-amp.html |title=Sanam Teri Kasam star Mawra Hocane ties the knot with Pakistani actor Ameer Gilani, shares dreamy wedding pictures |work=Hindustan Times |access-date=5 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1193213/mawra-hocane-and-ameer-gilani-just-got-married |title=Mawra Hocane and Ameer Gilani just got married! |work=Images Dawn |access-date=5 February 2025}}</ref>

== Other work and media image ==
[[File:Mawra Hocane during Promotions of 'Sanam Teri Kasam' at Eros office02 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Hocane at an event in 2016]]

Hocane has established herself as one of the leading Urdu television actresses.{{According to whom|date=February 2025}} In 2016, Hocane ranked 6th in "HIP Top 10" list for her "strong and vocal personality".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1151496 |title=HIP Top 10: Mawra Hocane the Rising Star |work=HIP in Pakistan |date=30 December 2016 |access-date=11 August 2019 |archive-date=25 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230625075429/https://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1151496 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Hocane modelled in "Hum Bridal Couture Week" in 2018, for designer Nilofer Shahid. She was the show stopper for designer [[Hassan Sheheryar Yasin|HSY creation]].<ref name="ramp" /> She has also done various photoshoots for "Eid Collections" and for designers.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://propakistani.pk/lens/mawra-hocane-looks-dreamy-in-these-perfect-for-eid-dresses/ |title=Mawra Hocane looks dreamy in her these Perfect-for-Eid dresses photoshoot |work=Pro Pakistani |date=3 April 2023 |access-date=21 April 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bolnews.com/2023/06/21/pakistani-celebrity/mawra-hocane-dazzles-in-pink-attire-in-latest-photoshoot/index.html/amp |title=Mawra Hocane dazzles in a pink attire in her latest photoshoot |work=Bol News |date=21 June 2023 |access-date=23 June 2023 |archive-date=25 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230625075430/https://www.bolnews.com/2023/06/21/pakistani-celebrity/mawra-hocane-dazzles-in-pink-attire-in-latest-photoshoot/index.html/amp |url-status=dead }}</ref> She serves as an ambassador for a number of brands such as [[Glow & Lovely]] and [[Lay's]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/10-Oct-2020/market-leader-fair-lovely-now-glow-lovely-rebrands-and-changes-brand-narrative%3fversion=amp|title=Glow & Lovely: Brand name changed but Mawra Hocane is still the brand ambassador|website=Daily Pakistan|language=en|accessdate=20 January 2021|archive-date=25 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230625113621/https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/10-Oct-2020/market-leader-fair-lovely-now-glow-lovely-rebrands-and-changes-brand-narrative%3Fversion=amp|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Hocane launched her clothing line named "UXM", in collaboration with her sister [[Urwa Hocane]], in June 2019.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1989053/4-sister-act-urwa-mawra-unveil-new-clothing-line/?amp=1 |title=Sister act: Urwa and Mawra unveil their new clothing line |work=The Express Tribune |date=10 June 2019 |access-date=11 June 2019}}</ref> In 2022, she also launched her own [[YouTube]] channel named "M Live".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1191041 |title=Mawra Hocane launches her own YouTube channel! |work=Images Dawn |date=20 October 2022 |access-date=11 November 2022}}</ref>

Hocane once tweeted in support of 2015 Indian film ''[[Phantom (2015 film)|Phantom]]'', which was banned in Pakistan, prompting social media harassment.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/947050/shaan-calls-for-a-ban-on-mawara-hocane-for-supporting-phantom/ |title=Shaan calls for a ban on Mawra Hocane for supporting Phantom |work=The Express Tribune |access-date=2 November 2015 |archive-date=2 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151102094210/http://tribune.com.pk/story/947050/shaan-calls-for-a-ban-on-mawara-hocane-for-supporting-phantom/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1203410 |title=How Phantom, Faisal Qureshi and Shaan vs Mawra exposed sexism in our midst |work=DAWN |type=Blog |access-date=2 November 2015 |archive-date=19 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151019182521/http://www.dawn.com/news/1203410 |url-status=live}}</ref>
