'''Momina Duraid''' ({{langx|ur|{{nq|مُومِنہ دُرید}}}}) is a [[Pakistani]] director and producer. She is a senior producer and creative head of television network [[Hum TV]] and CEO of her own production company [[MD Productions]]. She has produced and created several series including ''[[Dastaan (2010 TV series)|Dastaan]]'' (2010), ''[[Qaid-e-Tanhai]]'' (2010–11), ''[[Humsafar]]'' (2011–12), ''[[Shehr-e-Zaat]]'' (2012), ''[[Zindagi Gulzar Hai]]'' (2012–13), ''[[Diyar-e-Dil]]'' (2015), ''[[Sadqay Tumhare]]'' (2015), ''[[Mann Mayal]]'' (2016), ''[[Udaari]]'' (2016), ''[[Bin Roye (TV series)|Bin Roye]]'' (2016), ''[[Yaqeen Ka Safar]]'' (2017), ''[[Suno Chanda]]'' (2018) and ''[[Ehd-e-Wafa]]'' (2019).

In 2015, Momina ventured into film direction and co-directed ''[[Bin Roye]]''. Later that year, she founded film production house, [[Hum Films]]. She is married to Duraid Qureshi and is a daughter-in-law of [[Hum Network]] president and founder, [[Sultana Siddiqui]]. In 2015, she was named among the [[Pond's]] list of ''Miracle Journey: The 100 Most Inspirational Women''.<ref name="kdawn">{{Cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1529211|title=THE ICON INTERVIEW: FIFTEEN YEARS IN THE FAMILY|date=19 January 2020|access-date=18 January 2022|author=Mohammad Kamran Jawaid|archive-date=13 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210913095658/https://www.dawn.com/news/1529211}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=The Wonderful Women of Pakistan|url=http://tns.thenews.com.pk/wonderful-women-of-pakistan/#.WHoJ5fl97IU|work=Aamna Haider Isani|publisher=The News On Sunday|date=18 January 2015|access-date=14 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170116165050/http://tns.thenews.com.pk/wonderful-women-of-pakistan/#.WHoJ5fl97IU|archive-date=16 January 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.entertainmentpk.com/find-out-who-will-be-romancing-whom-in-ehd-e-wafa/|title=Find Out: Who will be romancing whom in Ehd e Wafa {{!}} Entertainment Pakistan|date=2019-08-31|language=en-US|access-date=2019-09-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190901181039/https://www.entertainmentpk.com/find-out-who-will-be-romancing-whom-in-ehd-e-wafa/|archive-date=2019-09-01|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Career==
Before joining the media industry, Momina was working as a marketing executive at a bank,<ref name="MominaDawn">{{cite web|title=Humsafar was rejected by two production houses: Momina Duraid|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1164419|work=Zoya Anwer|publisher=Dawn News|date=19 February 2016|access-date=14 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161018025846/http://www.dawn.com/news/1164419|archive-date=18 October 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> she said, "Media was the last thing I thought I would do. My mother-in-law, [[Sultana Siddiqui]], has been definitely associated with the industry as she worked for PTV but at the beginning, I was only looking after finances. I didn't know that I would be stepping into the creative side of things."<ref name="MominaDawn"/> She produced [[Samira Fazal]]'s ''Mere Paas Paas'' as her first independent drama series, that earned her critical acclaim. In 2010 she produced [[Partition of India|partition]] based drama series ''[[Dastaan (2010 TV series)|Dastaan]]'' based on the novel ''[[Bano (novel)|Bano]]'' by [[Razia Butt]], the series starred then newcomer [[Fawad Khan]] with [[Sanam Baloch]] playing the title character of Bano.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dastaan: History on TV|url=http://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/8103/dastaan-history-on-tv/|first=Taneeya|last=Hasan|newspaper=The Express Tribune|date=24 September 2011|access-date=14 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171007171820/https://www.dawn.com/news/1181504|archive-date=7 October 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Dastaan'' received extravagant reception from critics and became one of the most acclaimed series of all time.<ref>{{cite web|title=20 Pakistani TV dramas that you should watch if you haven't|url=http://dailytimes.com.pk/life-and-style/20-Jul-16/20-pakistani-tv-dramas-that-you-should-watch-if-you-havent|work=Saadia Qamar|publisher=The Daily Times|date=20 July 2016|access-date=14 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161024164347/http://dailytimes.com.pk/life-and-style/20-Jul-16/20-pakistani-tv-dramas-that-you-should-watch-if-you-havent|archive-date=24 October 2016|url-status=live}}</ref> At [[1st Hum Awards]] ceremony serial was awarded [[Hum Honorary Most Challenging Subject Award]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Hum award Winners List|url=http://dailymailnews.com/0413/30/ShowBiz/index.php?id=1|publisher=dailymailnews.com|access-date=14 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131014173834/http://dailymailnews.com/0413/30/ShowBiz/index.php?id=1|archive-date=14 October 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> and received five nominations at [[10th Lux Style Awards]], winning Best Director for [[Haissam Hussain]]<ref>{{cite web|title=LSA 2011 Nominations and winners|url=http://lux.com.pk/lsa2011/10YearsOfLSA/PR_2011.aspx|publisher=Lux|access-date=13 December 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426050832/http://lux.com.pk/lsa2011/10YearsOfLSA/PR_2011.aspx|archive-date=26 April 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> Momina then produced number of series and founded her own production company [[Momina Duraid Productions]] and became the senior producer of [[Hum TV]].<ref name="DastaanTribune">{{cite web|title='Dastaan': Reflecting the Indo-Pak divide|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/268234/dastaan-reflecting-the-indo-pak-divide/|first=Saadia|last=Qamar|newspaper=The Express Tribune|date=6 October 2011|access-date=14 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161026123906/http://tribune.com.pk/story/268234/dastaan-reflecting-the-indo-pak-divide/|archive-date=26 October 2016|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2011, Momina convinced [[Farhat Ishtiaq]] to dramatize her novel ''[[Humsafar (novel)|Humsafar]]'' into a [[Humsafar|television series]], which was previously rejected by two production houses.<ref name="MominaDawn"/> After its release ''Humsafar'' gained instant popularity and received an overwhelming response from critics and people all over the world.<ref>{{cite web|title= Humsafar: Here's what the noise is about|date= 14 December 2011|url= http://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/9343/humsafar-heres-what-the-noise-is-about//|access-date= 29 February 2012|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120229202107/http://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/9343/humsafar-heres-what-the-noise-is-about/|archive-date= 29 February 2012|url-status= live}}</ref> Critics regarded ''Humsafar'' as revival of drama industry.<ref>{{cite web|title= Mohabbaton ka safar|date= 24 February 2012|url= http://tribune.com.pk/story/341284/humsafar--mohabbaton-ka-safar/|access-date= 29 February 2012|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120229191120/http://tribune.com.pk/story/341284/humsafar--mohabbaton-ka-safar/|archive-date= 29 February 2012|url-status= live}}</ref> Sabahat Zakariya of ''Dawn News'' wrote, "If [[Haseena Moin]] was the benchmark of mass popularity back then, then ''Humsafar'' is an indicator of our endemic regressiveness."<ref>{{cite news|title= Drama Serials:Golden Age?|url= https://www.dawn.com/news/699862/drama-serials-golden-age|access-date= 3 March 2012|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20141006075838/http://www.dawn.com/news/699862/drama-serials-golden-age|archive-date= 6 October 2014|url-status= live}}</ref> The series has a [[cult following]] with huge fan following especially in India, Europe and North America.<ref>{{cite news|title= Popular Pakistani television drama Humsafar reaches Toronto fans via web|url= https://www.thestar.com/living/article/1132592--popular-pakistani-television-drama-humsafar-reaches-toronto-fans-in-via-web//|access-date= 29 February 2012|work= The Star|date= 16 February 2012|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120219230621/http://www.thestar.com/living/article/1132592--popular-pakistani-television-drama-humsafar-reaches-toronto-fans-in-via-web|archive-date= 19 February 2012|url-status= live}}</ref> The series lead actors [[Mahira Khan]] and [[Fawad Khan]] went on to become most popular actors in Pakistani film and television industry.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thank God for Fawad Khan and Mahira Khan!|url=http://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/42029/thank-god-for-fawad-khan-and-mahira-khan/|first=Sadaf|last=Haider|newspaper=The Express Tribune|date=16 March 2013|access-date=26 March 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161021125548/http://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/42029/thank-god-for-fawad-khan-and-mahira-khan/|archive-date=21 October 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Hum TV]] honored the craft and crew of serial giving them a special [[Hum Honorary Phenomenal Serial Award]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hum Honorary TV Award|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/792549/awards-celebrate-showbiz-achievements|publisher=[[Dawn News]]|date=16 March 2013|access-date=26 March 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130715073019/http://dawn.com/news/792549/awards-celebrate-showbiz-achievements|archive-date=15 July 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2015, Momina co-directed her first film ''[[Bin Roye]]'' under her production house [[Hum Films]], that earned her rave reviews,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-33604804 | title=Could Pakistan rival India's Bollywood? | publisher=[[BBC Asian Network]] | work=Haroon Rashid | date=21 July 2015 | access-date=24 July 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150723210516/http://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-33604804 | archive-date=23 July 2015 | url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/922693/the-box-office-eidi/|title=The box office Eidi|date=17 July 2015 |access-date=2017-01-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161018090356/http://tribune.com.pk/story/922693/the-box-office-eidi/|archive-date=2016-10-18|url-status=live}}</ref> and became the third [[List of highest-grossing Pakistani films|highest-grossing Pakistani film]] of all time.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://m.gulfnews.com/life-style/celebrity/desi-news/bin-roye-rides-pakistani-new-wave-1.1551281|title='Bin Roye' rides Pakistani new wave|newspaper=Gulf News|access-date=23 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817100529/http://m.gulfnews.com/life-style/celebrity/desi-news/bin-roye-rides-pakistani-new-wave-1.1551281|archive-date=17 August 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>  After the release of ''Bin Roye'', Hum Films has distributed and produced over fifteen films both domestically and internationally.

In 2016, seven of ten-scheduled drama series that Momina produced including, ''[[Dastaan (2010 TV series)|Dastaan]]'' (2010), ''[[Humsafar]]'' (2011–12), ''[[Zindagi Gulzar Hai]]'' (2012–13), ''[[Sadqay Tumhare]]'' (2015) are set to release on [[online streaming]] service [[Netflix]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Netflix to air hit Pakistan TV shows|url=https://www.samaa.tv/entertainment/2016/12/netflix-to-air-hit-pakistan-tv-shows/|work=Muhammad Farooq Dhedhi|publisher=Samaa TV|date=19 December 2016|access-date=14 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170116165842/https://www.samaa.tv/entertainment/2016/12/netflix-to-air-hit-pakistan-tv-shows/|archive-date=16 January 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Netflix to stream popular Pakistani shows|url=http://www.media247.co.uk/bizasia/netflix-to-stream-popular-pakistani-shows-2016|work=Raj Baddhan|publisher=Biz Asia|date=19 December 2016|access-date=14 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170116164215/http://www.media247.co.uk/bizasia/netflix-to-stream-popular-pakistani-shows-2016|archive-date=16 January 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Neelam Muneer''' ([[Pashto]]/{{langx|ur|{{nq|نیلم منیر خان}}}}; born 20 March 1992) is a [[Pakistani]] actress and model who appears in television dramas and films.<ref>{{Cite web == Early life ==
Neelam Muneer Khan was born in [[Mardan]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]] but was brought up in [[Karachi]].<ref name="bol">{{cite news |url=https://www.bolnews.com/latest/2020/11/neelam-muneer-the-goddess-of-beauty/ |title=Neelam Muneer: The Goddess Of Beauty |date=4 November 2020 |access-date=14 December 2021 |work=[[Bol News]]}}</ref> Her father died when she was three years old. Her mother raised Neelam and her three sisters as a single parent. While in school, she started modelling and later completed her graduation privately.{{cn|date=April 2026}} She was initially approached by [[Shamoon Abbasi]] for a television series.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.masala.com/i-declined-a-movie-offer-with-priyanka-chopra-due-to-waar-says-pakistani-actor-shamoon-abbasi-288201 |title="I declined a movie offer with Priyanka Chopra due to 'Waar'" Says Pakistani Actor Shamoon Abbasi |website=Masala.com |language=en |access-date=2020-04-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://arynews.tv/en/shamoon-abbasi-priyanka-chopra-bollywood/ |title=Shamoon Abbasi reveals why he refused a role opposite Priyanka Chopra |date=2019-07-08 |website=ARY NEWS |language=en-US |access-date=2020-04-07}}</ref> Eventually, she entered the television industry with director Kazim Pasha's drama serial ''Thora Sa Aasmaan'', which aired on [[PTV Home]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://galaxylollywood.com/2019/12/25/neelam-muneer-reveals-all-about-struggling-in-showbiz-since-9th-grade/ |title=Neelam Muneer Reveals All About Struggling In Showbiz Since 9th Grade |date=2019-12-25 |website=Galaxy Lollywood |language=en-US |access-date=2019-12-28 |last1=H |first1=Faisal Ali |archive-date=28 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191228122507/https://galaxylollywood.com/2019/12/25/neelam-muneer-reveals-all-about-struggling-in-showbiz-since-9th-grade/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Career ==

=== Television ===
Muneer made her acting debut with the drama series ''Thoda Sa Aasmaan''. Later, she appeared in ''Meri Subha Ka Sitara'' on Geo TV, ''[[Qaid-e-Tanhai]]'', [[List of programs broadcast by Hum TV#Telefilms|''Aankh Macholi'']],<ref name="Tribune">{{cite news |url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/1094225/neelam-muneer-has-her-hands-full/ |title=Neelam Muneer khan has her hands full |date=30 April 2016 |work=[[The Express Tribune]] |access-date=2 June 2016}}</ref> ''Shehr-e-Dil Ke Darwazey'', on Hum TV, ''Jal Pari'', [[Ashk (drama)|''Ashk'']] on Geo TV and [[Urdu 1]]'s serial ''[[Meri Saheli Meri Humjoli]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://arynews.tv/en/this-hilarious-instagram-post-by-neelum-muneer-will-make-your-day/ |title=This Instagram post by Neelum Muneer will leave you in titters|date=4 August 2016 }}</ref> She also appeared in the Geo TV serials ''[[Meri Behen Maya]]'' and ''[[Daray Daray Naina]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/988028/when-neelam-muneer-met-kareena-kapoor/ |title=When Neelam Muneer met Kareena Kapoor - The Express Tribune |date=9 November 2015}}</ref> In 2018, she played the leading role in social drama ''[[Umm-e-Haniya]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1179316 |title=Neelum Muneer's next TV drama puts the spotlight on abandoned babies |date=2018-01-24 |website=Images |language=en |access-date=2019-10-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/273721-umm-e-haniya-tackles-familial-and-societal-issues |title=Umm-e-Haniya tackles familial and societal issues |website=www.thenews.com.pk |language=en |access-date=2019-10-06}}</ref> The same year, she portrayed the role of Ulfat in the highly acclaimed drama series ''[[Dil Mom Ka Diya]]'', which became one of the most watched shows in the history of [[Pakistani television]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/403371-dil-mom-ka-diya-concludes-leaves-viewers-in-awe |title=Dil Mom Ka Diya concludes; leaves viewers in awe |last=Shabbir |first=Buraq |website=www.thenews.com.pk |language=en |access-date=2019-10-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/376383/neelam-muneer-thanks-fans-for-showing-love-for-ulfat/ |title=Neelam Muneer thanks fans for showing love for 'Ulfat' |date=2019-04-13 |website=Daily Times |language=en-US |access-date=2019-12-14}}</ref> The series earned her a nomination at the 18th Lux Style Awards for Best TV Actress.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1182224 |title=Lux Style Awards 2019 nominations are out! |date=2019-03-30 |website=Images |language=en |access-date=2019-10-05}}</ref> From 2019 to 2020, she appeared in ''[[Kahin Deep Jaley]]'' opposite [[Imran Ashraf]] where she portrays an innocent girl, Rida, whose cousin's jealousy and hatred caused many misfortunes and hardships for her.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/479049-neelam-muneer-on-her-next-with-imran-ashraf |title=Neelam Muneer on her next with Imran Ashraf |website=www.thenews.com.pk |language=en |access-date=2019-10-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/525307-imran-ashraf-neelum-muneer-take-up-new-roles-in-this-romance |title=Imran Ashraf & Neelum Muneer take up new roles in this romance |website=www.thenews.com.pk |language=en |access-date=2019-10-05}}</ref>

In 2020, she appeared in ''[[Bikhray Moti]]'', a serial co-produced by Humayun Saeed and Samina Humayun Saeed alongside Yasir Nawaz and Wahaj Ali. In this serial, Muneer played Ayeza, a strong and independent girl.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wahaj Ali to come back on screens with NeelamMunir for Bikhraymoti |url=https://nation.com.pk/19-May-2020/wahaj-ali-to-come-back-on-screens-with-neelammunir |date=2020-05-19 |website=The Nation |language=en |access-date=10 March 2021}}</ref>

=== Film ===
In 2017, Muneer made her film debut with the comedy thriller ''[[Chupan Chupai]]'' opposite [[Ahsan Khan (actor)|Ahsan Khan]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.brandsynario.com/pakistani-movie-chupan-chupai-starring-ahsan-khan-neelam-muneer/ |title=Pakistani Movie Chupan Chupai Starring Ahsan Khan & Neelam Muneer: BTS Shots - Brandsynario |date=6 December 2016 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/164988/neelam-muneer-embraces-simple-fashion-looks-chupan-chupai-promotions/ |title=Neelam Muneer embraces simple fashion looks for 'Chupan Chupai' promotions |date=2017-12-22 |website=Daily Times |language=en-US |access-date=2020-02-18}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/153865/never-said-neelam-beautiful-mahira-talented-saba-ahsan/ |title=I never said Neelam was more beautiful than Mahira or more talented than Saba: Ahsan |date=2017-12-06 |website=Daily Times |language=en-US |access-date=2020-04-07}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/155897/neelam-muneer-looking-forward-release-first-feature-film/ |title=Neelam Muneer looking forward to the release of her first feature film |date=2017-12-09 |website=Daily Times |language=en-US |access-date=2020-04-07}}</ref> Rahul Aijaz of ''[[The Express Tribune]]'' thought Muneer "serves her limited function of sprinkling masala in the film."<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1595962/4-chupan-chupai-review-birth-new-film-stars/ |title='Chupan Chupai' review: The birth of new film stars |work=The Express Tribune}}</ref> The film earned her a nomination for Best Film Actress at the 17th Lux Style Awards.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1179502 |title=Who won big at Lux Style Awards 2018? |date=2018-02-21 |website=Images |language=en |access-date=2019-10-05}}</ref> She next starred in the romantic-comedy film ''[[Wrong No. 2]]'' opposite [[Sami Khan]], a sequel to the 2015 film ''[[Wrong No.]]'' The film was released on [[Eid al-Fitr]], 2019. Her performance in the film was better received.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1182957 |title=Review: Wrong No 2 is more than a silly comedy film |date=2019-06-07 |website=Images |language=en |access-date=2019-12-28}}</ref> Both ''Chuppan Chuppai'' and ''Wrong No. 2'' proved to be commercial successes.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/272072-chupan-chupai-surpasses-with-7crore-target-in-25-days |title='Chupan Chupai' surpasses with 7 crore target in 25 days |website=www.thenews.com.pk |language=en |access-date=2019-10-05}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/527707-wrong-no-2-crosses-the-200-million-mark |title=Wrong No. 2 crosses the 200 million mark |last=NewsBytes |website=www.thenews.com.pk |language=en |access-date=2019-10-05}}</ref> Muneer performed an item number in the film ''[[Kaaf Kangana]].''<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1183885 |title=Kaaf Kangana's item number might be my first and last, says Neelam Muneer |date=2019-10-22 |website=Images |language=en |access-date=2019-12-14}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2084801/4-neelam-muneer-says-item-song-ispr-film/ |title=Neelam Muneer seeks to justify her 'item' song for Kaaf Kangna |date=2019-10-22 |website=The Express Tribune |language=en |access-date=2020-04-07}}</ref>

In 2022, she played dual roles of twins in [[Yasir Nawaz]]'s murder mystery film [[Chakkar (film)|''Chakkar'']].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-24 |title=Neelam Muneer to play a dual role in upcoming film 'Chakkar' |url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/2354030/it-wasnt-a-piece-of-cake-neelam-muneer-on-struggles-of-playing-a-dual-role-for-chakkar |access-date=2022-05-08 |website=The Express Tribune|language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In January 2025, Neelam tied the knot with the [[Emiratis|UAE resident]], Mohammad Rashid, who works as an officer of [[Dubai Police Force|Dubai Police’s]] Crime Investigation Department. They had a love marriage, and their wedding ceremony was held in [[Dubai]], United Arab Emirates.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thecurrent.pk/exclusive-identity-of-neelam-muneers-husband-revealed|title=EXCLUSIVE: Identity of Neelam Muneer's husband revealed|date=4 January 2025|website=The Current Pk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/04-Jan-2025/who-is-neelam-muneers-husband-know-his-name-profession-and-other-details|title=Who is Neelam Muneer's husband? Know his name, profession, and other details|first=Life|last=Style|date=4 January 2025|website=[[Daily Pakistan]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.samaa.tv/2087326727-neelam-muneer-is-officially-married-husband-revealed|title=Actress Neelam Muneer is officially married, reveals husband|date=4 January 2025|website=[[Samaa TV]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://jang.com.pk/en/28527-neelam-muneer-reveals-husband-as-she-shares-romantic-nikah-pictures-news|title=Neelam Muneer reveals husband as she shares romantic Nikah pictures|date=3 January 2025|website=[[Daily Jang]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Who Is Neelam Muneer's Husband? |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2520037/who-is-neelam-muneers-husband |website=The Express Tribune |language=en |date=4 January 2025}}</ref> Rashid owns businesses, including a travel and tourism agency and a few restaurants, in Dubai, where he has been residing since 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 January 2025 |title=What does Neelam Muneer's husband do in Dubai? |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2521878/what-does-neelam-muneers-husband-do-in-dubai?amp=1 |website=[[The Express Tribune]]}}</ref> As per his brother Samar Ranjha, the family is originally from [[Mianwal Ranjha]], a village in [[Mandi Bahauddin District|Mandi Bahauddin]], [[Punjab, Pakistan]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2025-01-14 |title=Neelam Muneer husband Muhammad Rashid's occupation revealed |url=https://arynews.tv/muhammad-rashid-neelam-muneer-husband-details-revealed |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261011150439/https://arynews.tv/muhammad-rashid-neelam-muneer-husband-details-revealed |archive-date=2026-10-11 |access-date= |website=[[ARY News]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-14 |title=Everything you need to know about Neelam’s husband {{!}} Daily National Courier |url=https://www.dailynationalcourier.com/news/everything-you-need-to-know-about-neelams-husband |access-date=2026-06-09 |website=www.dailynationalcourier.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Raeed Muhammad Alam''' is a Pakistani actor, model, director and producer.<ref name=TheNewsInternational/> 

He has appeared in several television serials, such as ''[[Jo Tu Chahey]]'', ''[[Mujhay Jeenay Do]]'', ''[[Dil Ruba]]'' and ''[[Fitrat (TV series)|Fitrat]]''.<ref name="yung" />

==Early life==
He completed his MBA in marketing from [[Hamdard University]].<ref name="TheNewsInternational">{{cite web |last=Khan |first=Asif |date=1 August 2017 |title=Raeed Alam |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/you/220283-Raeed-Alam |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231225185745/https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/you/220283-Raeed-Alam |archive-date=25 December 2023 |website=[[The News International]]}}</ref>

==Career==
===Modeling and acting===
Raeed started his career from modeling in 2010.<ref name="yung">{{cite web |last=Nasreen |first=Gul |date=16 November 2021 |title=THE YOUNG TALENT |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/you/908157-the-young-talent |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231225190623/https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/you/908157-the-young-talent |archive-date=25 December 2023 |access-date= |website=[[The News International]]}}</ref> 

He first acted in a commercial of Sony Ericsson directed by Saqib Malik. Many more commercials followed, including those for National Food, Jazz, Pepsi, Djuice, Sprite and Rani Pulpy.<ref name="TheNewsInternational" /> 

Later he worked in several dramas including ''[[Badnaam (TV series)|Badnaam]]'', ''[[Kuch Na Kaho (TV series)|Kuch Na Kaho]]'', ''[[Mujhay Jeenay Do]]'', ''[[Jo Tu Chahey]]'' and ''[[Dil Ruba]]''.<ref name="TheNewsInternational" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://nation.com.pk/08-Sep-2017/mujhay-jeenay-do-to-air-from-11th|title=Mujhay Jeenay Do to air from 11th|website=The Nation|date=28 April 2021}}</ref><ref name="SocialDairy">{{cite web|url=https://socialdiary.pk/social-diary-exclusive-a-metaphoric-rise-to-stardom-raeed-muhammad-alam|title=Social Diary Exclusive A Metaphoric Rise to Stardom Raeed Muhammad Alam|website=Social Diary|date=1 May 2021}}</ref>

===Direction and production===
He worked as assistant with director Saqib Malik for seven years.<ref name="TheNewsInternational" /> 

He also directed two music videos 'Teri Yaad' and one for Persian singer Shadi G.<ref name="TheNewsInternational" /> 

In 2018 he started his own production house called DNA Films.<ref>{{cite web |last=Khan |first=Sidra |date=4 May 2018 |title=Raeed & Hina - Stars of the millennials |url=https://magtheweekly.com/detail/2605-raeed-hina-stars-of-the-millennials |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231225190740/https://magtheweekly.com/detail/2605-raeed-hina-stars-of-the-millennials |archive-date=25 December 2023 |website=Mag - The Weekly}}</ref>

'''''Raju Rocket''''' is a 2012 Pakistani [[Comedy drama|comedy]] [[Drama (film and television)|drama]] serial aired on the [[Hum TV]]. The serial was first aired on 27 August 2012; and was directed by ''Saima Waseem'' and written by ''Imran Ali Safir'', starring [[Danish Taimoor]], [[Sumbul Iqbal]], [[Madiha Rizvi]], [[Rubina Ashraf]], [[Nadia Afghan]] and [[Qazi Wajid]].<ref>{{Cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140818142008if_/http://hum.tv/program_page.php?page_id=30&program_id=67&playlist_id=4C5A690FBF2EE6BD|url=http://hum.tv/program_page.php?page_id=30&program_id=67&playlist_id=4C5A690FBF2EE6BD|title=Raju Rocket|archive-date=18 August 2014|access-date=6 April 2022}}</ref>

It with peaked with 8.0 TRP, becoming the second most watched drama in the Pakistan history after [[Humsafar]] which got 9.8 TRP.

'''''Ranjha Ranjha Kardi''''' ({{literal translation|While repeating her beloved's name}}) is a 2018 [[Pakistani dramas|Pakistani drama]] serial that aired on [[Hum TV]]. It is directed by [[Kashif Nisar]] and written by [[Faiza Iftikhar]], starring [[Iqra Aziz]], [[Imran Ashraf]] and [[Syed Jibran]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nawaiwaqt.com.pk/11-Jun-2018/844340|title=ڈرامہ سیریل ''رانجھا رانجھا کردی'' کی ریکارڈنگ لاہور میں شروع|date=11 June 2018|work=[[Nawa-i-Waqt]]}}</ref> It emerged as one of the most iconic dramas in Pakistan television history.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.oyeyeah.com/entertainment/ranjha-ranjha-kardi-last-episode/amp/ | publisher=oyeyeah.com | title=Ranjha Ranjha Kardi ends on a beautiful note| date=2019-06-04}}</ref> The serial is produced by [[Momina Duraid]] under their banner [[MD Productions]] in collaboration with SBCH Productions.

== Plot ==
{{long plot|date=June 2019}}
The drama serial revolves around Noori, a young woman from a poor background. Her parents live by picking garbage from streets, therefore she is uncomfortable with the environment around her. She rejects her parents' lifestyle and wishes for a better and respectable life. To fulfill this wish of hers, she moves to a city and starts a respectable living by working in a factory. In this journey, she learns of Sahir and Bhola. Sahir is a greedy young man, who works in a shop and wishes for a better future; whereas, mentally weak and childlike Bhola owns a mansion and agricultural land in a village, (which his paternal uncle, Nusrat Chacha, takes care of). Bhola is loved deeply by his mother,&nbsp;Fehmida. Sahir and Bhola both get attached to Noor Bano's life, one which is by total deceit and the other is an ordeal.

Sahir is not serious about Noori, but she is always daydreaming about her marriage with Sahir. Noori somehow convinces him to marry her, to which he nonchalantly agrees. One day, when Noori comes to visit Sahir, she sees that there is some investigation going on and becomes worried when Sahir is found guilty of stealing money from the shop he works in. The police demanded ransom for Sahir's release and Noori is thinking of the ways she could get the money. When Noori asks her baji for money, she refuses and her husband also sexually harasses Noori by offering her money to be with him. Noori confronts the factory owner and says she does not want his money and quits working at the factory.

She steals her Baji's jewelry to pay for Sahir's release. Afterward, Sahir gets released, whereas Noori is jailed for stealing the jewellery. Noori's father makes a deal with Shokha, an aged smuggler, to free his daughter and marry her. On the other hand, Noori threatens her former boss to either take back the case or she will expose him. The Haji (former boss) does it and Noori is free. However, she still has to get rid of Shokha, so she runs away and goes to Sahir, who is arranging to leave the city. Sahir refuses to marry her, (as he was not sincere with his intentions), saying that she had spent a night in the lock-up and who knows if any lustful policeman had disgraced her. Noori, heartbroken, returns to her mentor, Amma Jannate's house. She asks Amma Jannate to help her because she does not want to marry Shokha and is considering suicide. Amma Jannate tells her the only way out is to wed, which will also fulfill her desire of living a respectable life.

The person Amma Jannate is talking about is actually Bhola, but Noori is not aware of it until after her marriage. Has all this happened to her for good and a better future? Initially, Noori can not stand him, even feeling for Bhola. She then realizes that Sahir is a Cunning and Deceitful greedy man and she would not want anyone else to have him as a life partner so in an attempt to break Komal and Sahir's alliance, she exposes him to everyone and succeeds. It is revealed that 23 years before Bhola's mother made a wish at the Mazaar that she will sacrifice him and give him to a Peer. And it was her belief that if you aren't having any children but as soon as you have your first child and you leave it at the Mazaar you will have many more, but her heart doesn't listen and she doesn't leave him at the Mazaar and then she never had any other children and Bhola became mentally ill and her husband died. She misunderstands the situation as the Peer being angry and that is the cause of the whole problem and says that if Bhola and Noori have any children she will leave the first one at the Mazaar but her daughter-in-law Noori explains to her that this can happen to anyone and we should not associate partners with Allah (God) and that if you have a child that is because of God and not a Peer at a Mazaar and that she is doing Shirk. Noori tries to get away from Bhola, but later she develops love, care, and empathy for him, due to his innocence and pure love for her. This intense story develops from there, and so does Noori and Bhola's unconventional romantic relationship. It ends with Bhola's mental condition becoming mostly fine and then she has a baby boy whom Bhola refuses to meet as he is afraid of him being like Bhola, but when Noori convinces him to see his baby, he kisses him on the forehead and starts to cry.

== Themes ==
The series shed light on various societal issues like [[marital rape]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.samaa.tv/lifeandstyle/2019/04/iqra-aziz-talks-about-marital-abuse-in-ranjha-ranjha-kardi/ |title=Iqra Aziz talks about marital abuse in 'Ranjha Ranjha Kardi' |date=19 April 2019 |archive-date=20 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420134858/https://www.samaa.tv/lifeandstyle/2019/04/iqra-aziz-talks-about-marital-abuse-in-ranjha-ranjha-kardi/ |work=Samaa TV }}</ref>

== Production ==
[[Imran Ashraf]] was selected to portray the lead role of a mentally challenged person ''Bhola'', while talking to ''[[The News International]]'' he shared that, for the preparation of the role, he observed and studied such people and their body language.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/487170-the-risk-and-reward-of-playing-disabled-characters|title=The risk and reward of playing disabled characters|work=The News International|date=20 June 2019}}</ref> Alongside Ashraf, [[Iqra Aziz]] was chosen to portray the female lead of Noori which was previously rejected by [[Zara Noor Abbas]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1487009|title=Spotlight: Zara Leading|date=9 June 2019|work=Dawn com|author=Ahmed Sarym|access-date=2 July 2023}}</ref>

== International broadcast ==

The series aired in India on [[Zindagi (TV channel)|Zindagi]], started from December 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.medianews4u.com/zindagi-unveils-december-line-up-to-air-saari-raat-on-11th-december/|title=Zindagi unveils December line-up; to air Saari Raat on 11th December|date=7 December 2022|work=Media News 4 U|access-date=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221224133803/https://www.medianews4u.com/zindagi-unveils-december-line-up-to-air-saari-raat-on-11th-december/|archive-date=24 December 2022}}</ref>

== Reception ==
[[File:Imran Ashraf.jpg|thumb|upright|[[Imran Ashraf]]'s performance received critical acclaim, and he was awarded the [[Lux Style Award]] for Best TV Actor (Viewer's choice)<ref name="win"/>]] The show's first episode has over 10 million views<ref>{{Citation|last=HUM TV|title=Ranjha Ranjha Kardi Episode #01 HUM TV Drama 3 November 2018|date=2018-11-03|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eEbT-p8KOO8|access-date=2019-04-17}}</ref> on YouTube and the TRPs of the show several times were the highest for the timeslot.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BwRuWUQHmix/?igshid=zjm6hgq7mu4x|title=#RanjhaRanjhaKardi {{!}} Top Rated, Saturday at 8:00 PM on #HUMTV}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/Bvttu4RHMSO/?igshid=zi5je6zmgthp|title=#RanjhaRanjhaKardi {{!}} Top rated! Saturdays at 8:00 PM on #HUMTV}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/BuFsk85Hzaq/?igshid=18f3rgzshazhx|title=Stealing the limelight {{!}} #RanjhaRanjhaKardi #HUMTV}}</ref> The drama and its story has gained critical acclaim for various things; [[Imran Ashraf]]'s performance as Bhola, [[Iqra Aziz]]'s performance as Noori, [[Asma Abbas]]'s performance as Amma Jee,<ref>{{cite web|title=6 actors that ruled television in 2019|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1184426/6-actors-that-ruled-television-in-2019|date=15 January 2020|author=Maria Kari|work=Dawn Images}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=10 March 2019|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/tns/detail/567398-inspirational-female-characters-television|title=Inspirational female characters on television|website=The News International|access-date=12 October 2023|author=Buraq Shabbir}}</ref> dealing with hidden social issues, such as awareness about mentally challenged people, wrong perceptions of society on castes and social status, misinterpretation of Islam and made up religious practices, and  messages on sensitive issues.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://tns.thenews.com.pk/road-less-travelled/#.XP7IGzdRUwB |title = The road less travelled|date = 2019-03-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.entertainmentpk.com/ranjha-ranjha-kardi-concludes-a-performance-to-be-remembered-by-imran-ashraf-others/ |title = Ranjha Ranjha Kardi Concludes: A Performance to be remembered by Imran Ashraf & others! &#124; Entertainment Pakistan|date = 2019-06-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/amp/436874-ranjha-ranjha-kardi-continues-to-impress-on-many-levels | title=Ranjha Ranjha Kardi continues to impress on many levels| date=26 February 2019|work=The News International}}</ref>

WIKIPEDIA REVISION DOCUMENT: Razia Butt

{{Short description|Pakistani novelist and playwright (1924-2012)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=February 2014}}
{{Infobox writer
| name          = Razia Butt<br />رضیہ بٹ
| image         = Razia Butt.jpg
| pen_name      = 
| birth_name    = 
| birth_date    = {{Birth date|df=yes|1924|05|19}}
| birth_place   = [[Rawalpindi]], [[Punjab (British India)|Punjab]], [[British India]]
| death_date    = {{Death date and age|df=yes|2012|10|04|1924|05|19}}
| death_place   = [[Lahore]], [[Punjab, Pakistan]]
| occupation    = Writer, playwright, novelist
| genre         = Fiction
| subject       = Socialism, [[Romance novel|romance]]
| notable_works = [[Saiqa (TV)|Saiqa]], Naila, [[Bano (novel)|Bano]], Najia
| influences    = 
| influenced    = 
| signature     = 
| website       = 
}}
'''Razia Butt''' ({{langx|ur|{{Nq|رضیہ بٹ}}}}) was an [[Urdu]] novelist and playwright from Pakistan. One of the famous [[popular fiction]] writer of the 1960s and 1970s, she is often compared with English writer [[Barbara Cartland]] due to her popularity among the household readers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1652895/popularity-literary-finesse-and-some-urdu-bestsellers|title=Popularity, literary finesse and some Urdu bestsellers|date=2021-10-19|website=dawn.com}}</ref><ref name="sht"/><ref>{{cite web|author=Abbas Akhtar |url=http://vidpk.com/12317/Writer--Novelist-Razia-Butt-in-Brunch-w-Bushra-P-35/ |title=Writer & Novelist Razia Butt in Brunch w/ Bushra P-3/5 |publisher=Vidpk.com |date=18 May 2008 |accessdate=21 October 2012}}</ref>

Some of her works have been adapted into television serials and films, including ''[[Bano (novel)|Bano]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/article/8103/dastaan-history-on-tv?|title=Dastaan: History on TV|date=2011-09-24|website=Express Tribune}}</ref>

==Background==
Razia Niaz was born in [[Rawalpindi]] on 19 May 1924.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.samaa.tv/newsdetail.aspx?ID=54797 |title=Great Urdu novelist Razia Butt passes away aged 89 |publisher=Samaa Tv |date= |accessdate=21 October 2012}}</ref> She spent most of her childhood in [[Peshawar]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.paklinks.com/gs/culture-literature-and-linguistics/578971-razia-butt-is-no-more.html |title=Razia Butt is no more |publisher=Paklinks.com |date=5 October 2012 |accessdate=21 October 2012 |archive-date=22 February 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222143253/http://www.paklinks.com/gs/culture-literature-and-linguistics/578971-razia-butt-is-no-more.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Career==
Her writings first appeared in a literary journal around 1940 when she was in her teens.<ref>Rayan Khan (July 10, 2011). [http://tribune.com.pk/story/206755/rasheed-butt-the-life-and-times-of-a-calligrapher/ Rasheed Butt: The life and times of a calligrapher], ''[[The Express Tribune]]''</ref> She later developed her first published story into a novel, ''Naila''.<ref name="sht">{{cite web|author=عارف وقار بی بی سی اردو ڈاٹ کام، لاہور |url=https://www.bbc.com/urdu/entertainment/2012/10/121005_novel_razia_butt_died_tk |title=BBC Urdu – فن فنکار – ناول نگار رضیہ بٹ انتقال کر گئیں |publisher=Bbc.co.uk |date=1 January 1970 |access-date=21 October 2012}}</ref> Butt also wrote radio plays. Films such as ''[[Naila (film)|Naila]]'', and ''[[Saiqa (film)|Saiqa]]'' and television serials such as ''[[Saiqa (TV series)|Saiqa]]'' and ''[[Dastaan (2010 TV series)|Dastaan]]'' are based on her novels.<ref name="sht"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Gul |first1=Aijaz |title=Lok Virsa to screen classical film 'Saiqa' tomorrow |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/414451-lok-virsa-to-screen-classical-film-saiqa-tomorrow |website=The News|date=January 4, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/article/8103/dastaan-history-on-tv|title =Dastaan: History on TV|publisher=[[Express Tribune]]|date=September 24, 2011|first=Taneeya|last=Hasan}}</ref>

Married in 1946, Razia Butt resumed writing in 1950s after a break of some years. She wrote 51 novels and 350 short stories.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thenewstribe.com/2012/10/05/novelist-razia-butt-passes-away-at-89/#.UIMcj47e7dk |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121007223254/http://www.thenewstribe.com/2012/10/05/novelist-razia-butt-passes-away-at-89/#.UIMcj47e7dk |url-status=usurped |archive-date=7 October 2012 |title=Novelist Razia Butt passes away at 89 |publisher=The News Tribe |date=5 October 2012 |accessdate=21 October 2012}}</ref>

Butt wrote an autobiography, ''Bichhray Lamhe''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/754264/novelist-razia-butt-is-no-more |title=Novelist Razia Butt is no more |publisher=Dawn.Com |date=5 October 2012 |access-date=21 October 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=شائستہ جلیل، کراچی |url=http://www.urduvoa.com/content/noted-urdu-novelist-razia-dies/1520721.html |title=مشہور ناول نگار رضیہ بٹ انتقال کرگئیں |publisher=Urduvoa.com |date=4 October 2012 |accessdate=21 October 2012}}</ref>

==Death==
Razia Butt died in [[Lahore]] on 4 October 2012 after a protracted illness.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nation.com.pk/05-Oct-2012/novelist-razia-butt-dies-at-89 |title=Novelist Razia Butt dies at 89 |publisher=The Nation |date=5 October 2012 |access-date=21 October 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://centralasiaonline.com/en_GB/articles/caii/newsbriefs/2012/10/05/newsbrief-03 |title=Fiction writer Razia Butt dies |publisher=Central Asia Online |date=5 October 2012 |accessdate=21 October 2012}}</ref>

WIKIPEDIA REVISION DOCUMENT: Saba Qamar

{{Short description|Pakistani actress (born 1984)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=January 2025}}
{{Use Pakistani English|date=January 2025}}
{{Infobox person

| native_name        = <!--{{lang|ur|{{nq|صبا قمر زمان}}}}-->
|image               = File:Saba_Qamar_(cropped).jpg
|caption             = Qamar at the Masala Awards in 2017
| birth_name         = Saba Qamar Zaman
| birth_date         = {{birth date and age|df=y|1984|4|5}}
| birth_place        = [[Hyderabad, Sindh|Hyderabad]], [[Sindh]], Pakistan
| awards             = [[List of awards and nominations received by Saba Qamar|Full list]]
| honours            = 
| signature          = [[File:Sabaqamarsignature.jpg|100px]]

| years_active       = 2004–present
| works              = [[Saba Qamar filmography|Full list]]}} 
'''Saba Qamar Zaman''' (born 5 April 1984) is a Pakistani actress who works predominantly in [[Urdu]] [[Film|films]] and [[Television show|television series]]. Qamar is one of Pakistan's most popular and highest-paid [[actresses]].<ref name="Paid1">{{Cite news |url=https://www.dnaindia.com/web-stories/entertainment/highest-paid-pakistani-actresses-kubra-khan-mehwish-hayat-mahira-khan-saba-qamar-hania-amir-1692720884774 |title=From Mahira Khan to Iqra Aziz: Highest paid Pakistani actresses |work=[[Daily News and Analysis|DNA India]] |access-date=22 November 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Paid2">{{Cite news |url=https://www.news18.com/web-stories/entertainment/9-highest-paid-pakistani-actresses-434133/ |title=Check out the list of the 9 Highest paid Pakistani actresses |work=[[News18 India]] |access-date=21 December 2022 |language=en-US}}</ref> She is a recipient of [[List of awards and nominations received by Saba Qamar|several accolades]] including two [[Lux Style Awards]] and three [[PTV Awards]] alongside a [[Filmfare Award|Filmfare]] nomination.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.filmfare.com/awards/filmfare-awards-2018/nominations|title=Filmfare Awards 2018 – Winners & Nominees|publisher=[[Filmfare Awards]]|date=20 January 2018|access-date=15 July 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190715124831/https://www.filmfare.com/awards/filmfare-awards-2018/nominations?year=2017|archive-date=15 July 2019}}</ref>
The [[Government of Pakistan]] has honoured her with the [[Tamgha-e-Imtiaz]] in 2012 and the [[Pride of Performance]] in 2016.

Qamar first received positive media attention for the role of ''Ruqsana Inayat'' in the historical [[drama]] ''[[Jinnah Ke Naam]]'' (2009). This was followed by further success in several television series, including the pre-partition drama ''[[Dastaan (2010 TV series)|Dastaan]]'', the melodrama ''[[Uraan (2010 TV series)|Uraan]]'' (both 2010), the romantic dramas ''[[Maat (TV series)|Maat]]'' and ''[[Pani Jaisa Piyar]]'' (both 2011), the socio ''[[Thakan]]'' (2012), thriller ''[[Sannata]]'', the romantic ''[[Bunty I Love You]]'' (both 2013), family drama ''[[Digest Writer]]'' (2014), crime thriller ''[[Sangat (TV series)|Sangat]]'' (2015) and ''[[Besharam (TV series)|Besharam]]'' (2016), receiving Best Actress nominations for these. She has also appeared in biographical film ''[[Manto (2015 film)|Manto]]'' (2015), romantic comedy ''[[Lahore Se Aagey]]'' (2016), and the Indian [[Hindi Cinema|Hindi]]-language educational drama ''[[Hindi Medium]]'' (2017), for which she received a nomination of [[Filmfare Award for Best Actress]].

Qamar has portrayed [[Fouzia Azeem]] and [[Noor Jehan]] in the 2017 biographical dramas ''[[Baaghi (TV series)|Baaghi]]'' and ''[[Main Manto]]'', and a strong-headed woman in the 2019 courtroom drama ''[[Cheekh]]''. The first of these earned her a Lux Style Award for Best TV Actress. She also features in listings of the nation's popular personalities.
In addition to acting, Qamar is involved with several humanitarian causes and is vocal about issues faced by women and children and has participated in concert tours and stage shows. She has featured as a host and comedian on the political satire ''[[Hum Sab Umeed Se Hain]]'' (2009–2015). Despite maintaining privacy, her off-screen life is the subject of substantial media coverage.

== Early life ==
Saba Qamar Zaman was born on 5 April 1984 in [[Hyderabad, Sindh|Hyderabad]], [[Sindh, Pakistan|Sindh]], Pakistan.<ref>{{cite news |title=Happy Birthday Saba Qamar! |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/300936-happy-birthday-saba-qamar |work=[[The News International]] |date=5 April 2018 |access-date=8 April 2018}}</ref> She has five siblings: three elder and one younger brother who died on 15 November 2022<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/1027723/saba-qamars-brother-passes-away/|title=Saba Qamar's brother passes away|date=15 November 2022|access-date=11 May 2023}}</ref> and one elder sister. She lost her father at a very young age and spent most of her childhood in [[Gujranwala]] with her grandmother. She got her early education in Gujranwala, then moved to [[Lahore]] to pursue further studies. Her family is settled in [[Karachi]].<ref name=sq1>{{cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1024808/first-person-scent-of-a-woman|title=First person: Scent of a woman|date=21 April 2013}}</ref><ref name="hindustantimes.com">{{Cite web|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/bollywood/saba-qamar-english-is-a-status-symbol-in-our-society/story-XRIX93wnEObz3VgiqWR7dM.html|title=Saba Qamar: English is a status symbol in our society|date=15 April 2017|website=[[Hindustan Times]]|language=en|access-date=22 December 2018}}</ref>

== Acting career ==
=== Beginnings and breakthrough (2004–2011) ===
Qamar started her career with [[Pakistan Television Corporation|PTV]] television series ''Mein Aurat Hoon'' in 2004.<ref name="pride">{{Cite news|url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/278239/pride-of-pakistan-saba-qamar/|title=Pride of Pakistan Saba Qamar - Daily Times|date=5 August 2018|work=[[Daily Times (Pakistan)|Daily Times]]|access-date=14 November 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=Daily.pak/> She then appeared in telefilm ''Ishq'' directed by Dilawar Malik opposite Bilal Qureshi for [[Geo Entertainment]]. Later that year she appeared as model for [[Abrar-ul-Haq]] music video ''Boliyan'' from the award-winning album [[Nachan Main Audhay Naal]]. In 2005, Qamar played lead role in [[ATV (Pakistan)|ATV]]'s ''[[Chaap]]'' opposite [[Sami Khan]]. She then replaced Sophia Mirza in comedy drama ''Sussar In Law'' as Tania and made special appearances in ''Hera Pheri & Company'' as Sonia in Episode 40- 41 and in Punjabi anthology series ''Jag Beeti'' in Episode ''Faisla'' as Erum for [[Pakistan Television Corporation|PTV]]. In 2006, she starred in several classic [[Pakistan Television Corporation|PTV]] series including ''Kahin Tum Kahin Hum'', ''Phool'', ''Apno Ka Sath'' and ''Dhoop Mein Andhera Hai''.<ref name="dhoop">{{Cite news|url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/12832/saba-qamar-to-play-qandeel-baloch-in-biopic/|title=Saba Qamar to play Qandeel Baloch in biopic - Daily Times|date=7 May 2017|work=[[Daily Times (Pakistan)|Daily Times]]|access-date=15 November 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> She later did supporting roles in ''[[Gharoor]]'' and ''Taqdeer'' for [[Pakistan Television Corporation|PTV]] and Banjar for [[Geo Entertainment]].
She was paired with [[Ahsan Khan]] in both ''Banjar'' and ''[[Gharoor]]''. Qamar later portrayed the role of Sana Hamdani in her first and only lead appearance opposite [[Fawad Khan]] in telefim ''Kal'' aired on PTV.

In 2007, Qamar appeared in two major [[ATV (Pakistan)|ATV]]'s serials ''[[Khuda Gawah (TV series)|Khuda Gawah]]'' which was the remake of 1992 Indian film of the [[Khuda Gawah (film)|same name]] and ''Muhabbat Ab Nahi Hogi''. Later that year Qamar appeared in series of comedy dramas including [[Aaj TV]]'s ''Mirch Masala'' with [[Veena Malik]] and [[Shamil Khan]] and [[Pakistan Television Corporation|PTV]]'s ''Unbiyaanable'', ''Maamo'' and ''No.1''.
In 2008, Qamar starred in melodrama ''Woh Subha Kab Aayegi'', comedy series ''Not Responding'' and ''Nawab Manzil'' for [[ATV (Pakistan)|ATV]]. She then did four supporting roles for [[Pakistan Television Corporation|PTV]] including ''Chubhan'', ''Na Janay Kyun'', ''Phool Aur Kantey'' and ''Bint-e-Adam''. Her role in social drama ''Bint-e-Adam'' was of a rich brat who falls for a boy from a poor background, played by [[Ahsan Khan]] and marries him against her cruel father's wishes. ''Bint e Adam'' was a major critical and commercial hit, however, critics noted that her role was "limited" from an acting point of view.
In 2009, she appeared in biographical drama ''[[Jinnah Ke Naam]]'', which was the production of [[PTV Home]] in the direction of Tariq Mairaj.<ref name=gawah>{{Cite news|url=https://www.india.com/showbiz/hindi-medium-actress-saba-qamar-looks-hot-and-sexy-in-recent-photoshoots-check-pics-3157385/|title=Hot Damn! We Get Can't Take Our Eyes Off Saba Qamar's Latest Pictures|last=Vaid|first=Kritika|date=10 July 2018|work=India.com|access-date=15 November 2018|language=en}}</ref><ref name=jinnah>{{Cite web|url=https://www.india.com/showbiz/11-pakistani-actresses-bollywood-should-welcome-with-an-open-heart-751940/|title=11 Pakistani actresses Bollywood should welcome with an open heart!|last=Mishra|first=Rashmi|date=2 December 2015|website=India.com|language=en|access-date=22 December 2018}}</ref> She played the role of Ruqsana Inayatullah and the series was a tribute to the founder of Pakistan, [[Muhammad Ali Jinnah]]. In an earlier interview with ''[[The Express Tribune]]'', Qamar confessed, "For me, acting is being able to express the feelings, emotions and expressions of different people and characters".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1715439/4-baaghi-people-finally-understood-qandeel-wronged-saba-qamar/|title=After 'Baaghi', people finally understood Qandeel was wronged: Saba Qamar|date=21 May 2018|work=[[The Express Tribune]]|access-date=14 November 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> In the same year Qamar appeared in two [[Geo Entertainment]] serials ''Teri Ik Nazar'' and ''Nadia Naam Ki Larki''. She then did [[PTV Home]] serials ''Hum Tu Karain Kamal'', ''[[Mishaal]]'' and ''[[Tinkay]]''. She won the [[PTV Awards]] for the best TV actress in both public and jury choice categories at the 16th Annual PTV awards, held on 23 July 2011 for her role in ''[[Tinkay]]''.

In 2010, she appeared in a supporting role of Surraya in [[Hum TV]]'s [[Partition of India|pre partition]] television series ''[[Dastaan (2010 TV series)|Dastaan]]'', an adaptation of [[Razia Butt]]'s novel ''[[Bano (novel)|Bano]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/8103/dastaan-history-on-tv/|title=Dastaan: History on TV|work=[[The Express Tribune]]|access-date=14 November 2018}}</ref><ref name="geonews">{{Cite news|url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/177421-saba-qamar-shares-humiliating-experience-at-international-airport|title=Saba Qamar shares 'humiliating' experience at international airport|work=[[Geo News]]|access-date=14 November 2018}}</ref> She was seen opposite [[Ahsan Khan]], [[Sanam Baloch]] and [[Fawad Khan]]. Series proved to be the break-through for her and she won the Best TV Actress trophy at the [[Pakistan Media Awards]] (2010).<ref name=pride/><ref name="Daily.pak">{{Cite news|url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/saba-qamar-is-definitely-a-force-to-be-reckoned-with-and-heres-why/|title=Saba Qamar is definitely a force to be reckoned with and here's why!|work=[[Daily Pakistan]]|access-date=14 November 2018|archive-date=23 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190423055444/https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/saba-qamar-is-definitely-a-force-to-be-reckoned-with-and-heres-why/}}</ref>
She then played lead role of Pooja Mohan Das in Indus Vision's partition based drama ''Kanpur Se Katas Tak''.
Qamar later appeared in two [[A-Plus TV|A-Plus]] dramas including ''[[Aankh Salamat Andhay Log]]'' and ''Rait Kay Dairay''. She then appeared in soap ''Chaand Ki Goud Mein'' and social drama ''[[Uraan (2010 TV series)|Uraan]]'' for [[Geo Entertainment]].
Qamar later played lead roles in [[PTV Home]] serial ''Lahore Junction'' opposite [[Shamil Khan]] and [[ATV (Pakistan)|ATV]]'s ''Amar Bel'' opposite [[Kashif Mehmood]] and ''Ghao'' opposite [[Sami Khan]].
Qamar later that year portrayed role of blind girl Naila Habib in [[Geo Entertainment]] anthology series ''Taaluq''.

Qamar then appeared in [[Sarmad Khoosat]]'s romantic series ''[[Pani Jaisa Piyar]]'' (2011), where she played the character of Sana who has been engaged to Adarsh, the son of her mother's best friend ever since she was a child. Adarsh, however, has been unaware of this engagement, as his parents thought that he needed to focus more on his [[education]] than [[wedding]] plans. It was followed by a role in PTV's ''[[Tera Pyar Nahi Bhoole]]''.<ref name=pride/> She was paired opposite Ahsan Khan in both the series.<ref name="deccan">{{Cite news|url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/entertainment/television/060716/home-is-the-best-place-to-learn-acting-saba-qamar.html|title=Home is the best place to learn acting: Saba Qamar|date=6 July 2016|work=[[Deccan Chronicle]]|access-date=14 November 2018}}</ref>
She then played characters in [[PTV Home]]'s serials ''Khalida Ki Walida'', ''Main Aisa Kyun Hoon'', ''Nazar'' and ''Two In One''.
Later that year, she appeared in ''[[Maat (TV series)|Maat]]'' where she played the self-obsessed Saman opposite [[Adnan Siddiqui]] and [[Aamina Sheikh]].<ref name="uraan">{{Cite news|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/bollywood/hindi-medium-actor-saba-qamar-had-appeared-on-indian-tv-with-fawad-khan-do-you-remember-watch-video-4664974/|title=Hindi Medium actor Saba Qamar had appeared on Indian TV with Fawad Khan. Do you remember? Watch video|date=20 May 2017|work=[[The Indian Express]]|access-date=15 November 2018}}</ref> 
The series was a critical and commercial hit and became the [[Pakistani dramas|thirteenth highest-rated Pakistani television series]] and garnered her the [[4th Pakistan Media Awards|Pakistan Media Award]] for Best Actress.<ref name=pride/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.timesnownews.com/entertainment/fashion/article/hindi-medium-heroine-saba-qamars-latest-photo-shoot-is-too-hot-to-handle/251282|title=Hindi Medium heroine Saba Qamar's latest photo shoot is too hot to handle {{!}} Entertainment News|work=[[Times Now]]|access-date=14 November 2018}}</ref><ref name="tns">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/159113-There-is-no-vulgarity-in-Kalabaaz|title="There is no vulgarity in 'Kalabaaz'"|last=Shabbir|first=Buraq|website=The News International|access-date=14 November 2018}}</ref> That same year, Qamar collaborated with [[Sami Khan]] in two projects, ''[[Jo Chale To Jaan Se Guzar Gaye]]'' and ''[[Main Chand Si]]'' receiving further praise.<ref name=deccan/><ref name="crossing">{{Cite news|url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/91421/crossing-borders-saba-qamar-to-make-bollywood-debut-alongside-irrfan-khan/|title=Crossing borders: Saba Qamar to make Bollywood debut alongside Irrfan Khan - Daily Times|date=10 April 2016|work=Daily Times|access-date=14 November 2018}}</ref> She then appeared in the [[Hum TV]] Eid telefilm ''Balay Ki Balli'' as Vaneeza. Later she was cast opposite [[Saleem Sheikh]] in the [[A-Plus TV|A-Plus]] sitcom ''Ghar Ki Baat Hai''. Lastly she was seen as Neelofar in [[PTV Home]]'s anthology series ''[[Faseel-e-Jaan Se Aagay]]'' in Episode ''Matti Ka Qarz''.

=== Critical acclaim and professional expansion (2012–2015) ===

Qamar next appeared in Ameen Iqbal's ''[[Thakan]]'' (2012), where she played the role of Sadaf who works extremely hard like a machine day and night to run her family but no one except her grandfather feels sympathy for her or even cares about her.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/68995/20-pakistani-tv-dramas-that-you-should-watch-if-you-havent/|title=20 Pakistani TV dramas that you should watch if you haven't - Daily Times|date=20 July 2016|work=Daily Times|access-date=14 November 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/zindagi-brings-two-new-shows/|title=Zindagi brings two new shows|last=Bhadani |first=Priyanka |date=29 August 2014|work=[[The Indian Express]]|access-date=14 November 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://zeenews.india.com/entertainment/idiotbox/zindagi-presents-%E2%80%98selfish%E2%80%99-saman-of-%E2%80%98maat%E2%80%99-in-new-avatar-in-%E2%80%98thakan%E2%80%99_1462332.html|title=Zindagi presents 'selfish' Saman of 'Maat' in new avatar in 'Thakan'|date=30 August 2014|work=[[Zee News]]|access-date=8 July 2018}}</ref>
She then starred in [[ARY Digital]]'s two Eid Telefilms ''Pyaar Mein Twins'' and ''Love Ki Kichri''. It was followed by the leading roles in the Amna Nawaz Khan-written ''[[Na Kaho Tum Mere Nahi]]'' (2012) and [[Faiza Iftikhar]]'s ''[[Yahan Pyar Nahin Hai]]'' (2012)<ref name=geonews/><ref name=tns/><ref name=nakaho>{{Cite news|url=https://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/16495/na-kaho-tum-mere-nahin-another-drama-serial-for-an-unhappy-wife/|title=Na Kaho Tum Mere Nahin: Another drama serial for an unhappy wife|work=The Express Tribune|access-date=26 July 2018}}</ref> The latter of which earned her a nomination for [[Hum Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]] at [[Hum Awards]]. She starred in another [[PTV Home]] serial ''Bhool''. It was shot in 2008 but got delayed and finally released in 2012. She gained recognition for portraying a range of characters in the serials like ''Shikwa Na Shikayat'' (2012), ''[[Shehryar Shehzadi]]''<ref name=sq1 /> (2012), special appearance in [[ARY Digital]]'s ''[[Timmy G]]'' (2012), ''[[Kaash Aisa Ho]]''<ref name=sq1 /> (2013), ''[[Miss Fire]]'' (2013), ''[[Sannata]]''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blush.com.pk/a-review-of-the-dark-deep-drama-sannata/|title=A Review of the Dark, Deep Drama- Sannata|date=23 November 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191022191126/http://blush.com.pk/a-review-of-the-dark-deep-drama-sannata/|author=Maila|archive-date=22 October 2019|work=Blush.com.pk}}</ref> (2013), and ''[[Ullu Baraye Farokht Nahi]]''<ref name=images/> (2013), some of which garnered her several best actress nominations.<ref name=crossing/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/326404-zahid-ahmed-on-his-upcoming-eid-telefilm-with-saba-qamar|title=Zahid Ahmed on his upcoming Eid telefilm with Saba Qamar|last=NewsBytes|website=The News International|access-date=20 February 2019}}</ref><ref name="tns2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/350116-saba-qamar-talks-about-her-upcoming-film-and-tv-projects|title=Saba Qamar talks about her upcoming film and TV projects|last=Shabbir|first=Buraq|website=The News International|access-date=14 November 2018}}</ref> Qamar won her first Hum Awards for the Best TV Actress for her role as Diana in ''[[Bunty I Love You]]'', at the [[3rd Hum Awards]].<ref name=3rdhum>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1175086|title=HUM TV Awards 2015: 'Sadqay Tumhare' a clear winner|date=10 April 2015|work=[[Dawn (newspaper)|DAWN]]|access-date=14 November 2018}}</ref>

That same year, Qamar worked in the television film ''[[Aina (2013 film)|Aina]]'' (2013), opposite [[Faysal Qureshi (actor)|Faysal Qureshi]]. The film, a remake of the [[Aina (1977 film)|1977 film of the same name]], was well received by the audience and she was nominated for the Best Actress award at the Tarang Housefull Awards.<ref name="pride"/> After two consecutive years of poorly received serials, Qamar's career prospects began to improve in 2014; she appeared in six projects: ''[[Jaanam]]'', ''Bay Emaan Mohabbat'', ''Na Katro Pankh Mere'' in her first time pairing with [[Danish Taimoor]], ''[[Bunty I Love You]]'', ''[[Izteraab]]'', and ''[[Digest Writer]]''.<ref name=geonews/><ref name=emaan>{{Cite web|url=https://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/25599/14-pakistani-dramas-that-ruled-our-television-screens-in-2014/|title=14 Pakistani dramas that ruled our television screens in 2014|date=2 January 2015 |access-date=22 December 2018}}</ref><ref name=jaanam>{{Cite web|url=http://todaynews.pk/jaanam-episode-18-aplus-tv-8th-january-2015/|title=Jaanam on Aplus|last=Adnan|date=8 January 2015|website=TodayNews.PK|access-date=22 December 2018}}</ref> The romantic drama ''Jaanam'' (alongside [[Adnan Siddiqui]]) and the romance ''Bay Emaan Mohabbat'' (alongside [[Agha Ali]] and [[Adnan Shah Tipu]]) earned little praise, but the family drama ''[[Bunty I Love You]]'' (a story about a girl who got married aged 17 to a much older man, later dreams of living a free life after his death) was Qamar's first critical success since ''[[Maat]]''.<ref name="D.Pakistan">{{Cite news|url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/you-should-watch-these-five-performances-of-saba-qamar-on-her-birthday/|title=You should watch these five performances of Saba Qamar on her birthday!|work=[[Daily Pakistan]]|access-date=25 July 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=pride/> Directed by [[Siraj-ul-Haque]], the series was generally well received. Reviewer from ''[[Daily Pakistan]]'' considered it along with ''[[Digest Writer]]'' as "one of the best performances of Qamar".<ref name="D.Pakistan"/> The series received five nominations at Hum Awards including Qamar for best actress.{{citation needed|date=December 2022}} She next appeared in ''[[Izteraab]]''. Her performance as the working women did not go well and despite the strong cast, story, production house and promotions, the drama turned out to be a major critical and commercial [[Box-office bomb|Disaster]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1174340|title=Do Pakistani TV dramas depict working women as selfish, unfavourable characters?|last=Haider|first=Sadaf|date=8 January 2016|website=Images|access-date=24 December 2018}}</ref> She then appeared for [[Wajahat Rauf]]'s directed anthology series ''[[Shareek-e-Hayat]]'' for [[Hum TV]].

Qamar appeared in three series in 2015. She first reunited with [[Muhammad Younis Butt]] and Fawad Wyne in the comedy series ''S.H.E'' where she played a role of lady [[Station house officer|S.H.O]] Bajirao Mastani.<ref name="blogs.tribune.com.pk">{{Cite web|url=https://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/16495/na-kaho-tum-mere-nahin-another-drama-serial-for-an-unhappy-wife/|title=Na Kaho Tum Mere Nahin: Another drama serial for an unhappy wife|date=21 March 2013|website=The Express Tribune|language=en-US|access-date=22 December 2018}}</ref> She then starred alongside [[Adeel Chaudhry]] in Fahim Burney's directorial ''[[Kaisay Tum Se Kahoon]]'' which tells the story of star-crossed lovers who are reincarnated.<ref name="sitara">{{Cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1079727/heres-the-ultimate-list-of-pakistani-dramas-you-must-watch-in-2016/|title=Here's the ultimate list of Pakistani dramas you must watch in 2016|date=11 April 2016|website=The Express Tribune|language=en-US|access-date=22 December 2018}}</ref><ref name="digest">{{Cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1651457/4-gohar-rasheed-saba-qamar-share-screen-space-two-years/|title=Gohar Rasheed, Saba Qamar to share screen space after two years|date=5 March 2018|website=The Express Tribune|language=en-US|access-date=22 December 2018}}</ref><ref name="images">{{Cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1176410|title=10 iconic Pakistani TV dramas you should binge-watch this weekend|last=Haider|first=Sadaf|date=21 October 2016|website=Images|language=en|access-date=22 December 2018}}</ref> It was her third consecutive appearance in [[Momina Duraid]]'s production. Although the series did not do well in terms of ratings, but her performance was praised by the critics.<ref name=crossing/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1147613|title='Kaise Tum Se Kahoon' needs more than Saba Qamar's good looks|last=Ahmad|first=Ayesha|date=28 July 2015|website=HIP|access-date=24 December 2018|archive-date=4 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180704124025/https://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1147613}}</ref> The following year, Qamar collaborated with [[Mikaal Zulfiqar]] for the third time (alongside [[Zahid Ahmed (Pakistani cricketer)|Zahid Ahmed]], [[Kiran Haq]], and [[Sonia Mishal]]) in [[Kashif Nisar]]'s ''[[Sangat (TV series)|Sangat]]'' where she played a role of Aisha, a rape survivor who faced difficulties when her husband came to know that he was not the biological father of a daughter they have.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1202747|title=First look: Will Sangat deal with sexual violence any better than typical TV?|last=Siddique|first=Sadaf|date=25 August 2015|work=DAWN.COM|access-date=10 June 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1174079|title=In Sangat, the rapist is both hero and villain — and that's a problem|last=Haider|first=Sadaf|date=4 November 2015|work=DAWN|access-date=12 July 2018}}</ref> The series earned her the nomination for Best Actress in both [[Hum Award for Best Actress|Jury]] and [[Hum Award for Best Actress Popular|Popular]] categories at the [[Hum Awards]].

Qamar then made her acting debut in [[Lollywood]] as a leading actress in the acclaimed biographical drama ''[[Manto (2015 film)|Manto]]'' (2015).<ref name="manto">{{cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1198981|title=Must watch: Literary genius Manto comes to life in much-awaited biopic|date=7 August 2015|website=DAWN|publisher=Dawn News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1678229/4-happy-birthday-saba-qamar-5-times-actor-proved-mettle-onscreen/|title=Happy Birthday Saba Qamar: 5 times the actor proved her mettle onscreen {{!}} The Express Tribune|date=5 April 2018|work=The Express Tribune|access-date=23 July 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> Directed by [[Sarmad Khoosat]], the film was made on a big budget and performed poorly at the box office with a lifetime collection of Rs 5.05 million, however, it was critically praised and Qamar's portrayal of the singer [[Noor Jehan]] was well received by the critics, and earned her a nomination at the [[ARY Film Awards|ARY Films Awards for Best Supporting Actress]].<ref name=aryfilm>{{Cite news|url=https://arynews.tv/en/ary-film-awards-2016-nominations-out/|title=ARY Film Awards 2016 nominations are out! - ARYNEWS|date=7 February 2016|work=[[ARY News]]|access-date=16 November 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=manto-lives-in-sarmad-khoosats-darkly-perfect-biopic-a-great-writer-gets-his-due|date=16 September 2015 |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1173852/manto-lives-in-sarmad-khoosats-darkly-perfect-biopic-a-great-writer-gets-his-due|publisher=[[Dawn News]]|access-date=19 October 2015}}</ref> The film was later adapted into a television series with the same cast in 2017, titled ''[[Main Manto]]'', and was aired on Geo TV.<ref name="mmanto">{{Cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1179406|title=TV drama Manto shows an artist besieged by opposition on all sides|last=Siddique|first=Sadaf|date=8 February 2018|website=DAWN|language=en|access-date=21 December 2018}}</ref>

=== Established actress (2016–2019) ===
In 2016, Qamar played the role of a struggling actress in the period drama ''[[Mein Sitara]]'', (serial based on [[lollywood]] golden era)<ref name=meinsitara>{{Cite news|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1074372/mein-sitara-serial-on-lollywoods-golden-era-a-dark-horse-among-pakistani-dramas/|title=Mein Sitara: Serial on Lollywood's golden era a dark horse among 2017|work=The Express Tribune|access-date=14 November 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> Qamar played a rockstar opposite [[Yasir Hussain]], in the travel comedy ''[[Lahore Se Aagey]]'' (2016).<ref>{{Cite receiving [[Nigar Awards]] for Best Film Actress.<ref name=16thlux/> Later that year, she played a leading role in the psycho–thriller ''[[8969]]'', a critical and commercial failure.<ref name="Dawn8969">{{Cite news|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1176548|title=Saba Qamar's upcoming release 8969 is 'the biggest mistake of her career'|last=Alavi|first=Omair|date=8 November
