Qamar was offered an Indian film opposite [[Randeep Hooda]], and supporting roles in ''[[Once Upon a Time in Mumbaai]]'' (2012) and ''[[Heroine (2012 film)|Heroine]]'' (2012), which she declined.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/630861/bollywood-not-on-the-cards-for-saba-qamar/|title=Bollywood not on the cards for Saba Qamar|date=12 November 2013|website=The Express Tribune|language=en-US|access-date=19 December 2018}}</ref> After the [[2016 Uri attack]], relations between India and Pakistan deteriorated; the Indian Motion Picture Producers Association (IMPPA) and the Film Producers Guild of India banned Pakistani artists from working in India until the situation normalised.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.ibtimes.co.in/imppa-passes-resolution-temporarily-ban-pakistani-artists-india-twitter-reacts-695956|title=IMPPA passes resolution to temporarily ban Pakistani artists in India|date=29 September 2016|work=International Business Times, India|access-date=13 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170801200048/http://www.ibtimes.co.in/imppa-passes-resolution-temporarily-ban-pakistani-artists-india-twitter-reacts-695956|archive-date=1 August 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> The comedy-drama ''[[Hindi Medium]]'' (2017), in which Qamar played the lead female role of Meeta Batra, a [[nouveau riche]] opposite [[Irrfan Khan]], marked her first project in the [[Bollywood|Hindi cinema]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1177420/you-cant-judge-someones-capabilities-based-on-the-language-they-know-shares-saba-qamar|title=You can't judge someone's capabilities based on the language they know, shares Saba Qamar|author=Images Staff|date=13 April 2017|website=DAWN|access-date=6 August 2017}}</ref><ref name=break>{{Cite news|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1179819|title=Saba Qamar's Hindi Medium breaks Indian film records in China|author=Images Staff|date=9 April 2018|work=DAWN|access-date=19 July 2018|language=en-US}}</ref>

[[File:Saba Qamar with Irfan khan.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Qamar with co-star [[Irrfan Khan]] on the sets of ''[[Hindi Medium]]'' in 2017|alt=Saba Qamar with Irrfan Khan]]

Critical reception of the film was positive. A reviewer for ''[[The Times of India]]'' wrote, "Saba, as the dominating wife is sheer delight onscreen".<ref>{{Citation|title=Hindi Medium Review {4/5}: This class isn't part of the usual Bollywood curriculum, and we suggest that you sign up for it. Admissions open to all.|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/movie-reviews/hindi-medium/movie-review/58716386.cms|work=[[The Times of India]]|access-date=20 December 2018}}</ref> In a scathing review, Sreehari Nair of ''[[Rediff.com]]'' labelled the film "fascinatingly frustrating" and called Qamar "natural actress, sexual daring".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rediff.com/movies/report/review-hindi-medium-is-a-fascinatingly-frustrating-film/20170518.htm|title=Review: Hindi Medium is a fascinatingly frustrating film|website=[[Rediff.com]]|access-date=20 December 2018}}</ref> The film earned over ₹334.36 million worldwide, a majority of which came from the Chinese box office.<ref name="boi">{{Cite web|url=http://boxofficeindia.com/movie.php?movieid=3526|title=Hindi Medium - Movie|website=[[Box Office India]]|access-date=28 July 2017}}</ref><ref name=boxx>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bollywoodhungama.com/movie/hindi-medium/box-office/|title=Hindi Medium Box Office Collection till Now |date=19 May 2017|website=[[Bollywood Hungama]]|language=en|access-date=13 January 2019}}</ref> Qamar received several Best Actress nominations at various award ceremonies, including a [[Filmfare Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]] nomination at [[Filmfare Awards|Filmfare]]. Later that year, Qamar was declared as the top Bollywood debutante of 2017 by ''[[Eastern Eye]]''.<ref name=filmf>{{Cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1611918/4-saba-qamar-nominated-best-actor-female-upcoming-filmfare-awards/|title=Saba Qamar nominated for Best Actor (Female) at upcoming Filmfare Awards|date=18 January 2018|website=The Express Tribune|language=en-US|access-date=20 December 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2017/12/24/mahira-khan-saba-qamar-lead-bollywoods-debutantes-list-of-2017/|title=Mahira Khan, Saba Qamar lead Bollywood's debutantes list of 2017 {{!}} Pakistan Today|date=24 December 2017|website=Pakistan Today|access-date=20 December 2018}}</ref><ref name="auto4">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thequint.com/entertainment/bollywood/best-bollywood-debut-2017|title=Take a Look at the Newcomers Who Made a Mark In 2017|date=12 December 2017|website=[[The Quint]]|language=en|access-date=20 December 2018}}</ref>

In 2017, Qamar worked in the [[biographical]] drama series ''[[Baaghi (TV series)|Baaghi]]'', in the role of Pakistani controversial figure [[Qandeel Baloch]].<ref name="The face of Baaghi – Saba Qamar">{{Cite web|url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/the-face-of-baaghi-saba-qamar/|title=The face of "Baaghi" – Saba Qamar|website=Daily Pakistan Global|date=17 December 2017 |language=en-US|access-date=14 December 2018}}</ref> The series was a critical and commercial success, becoming one of the highest-grossing Pakistani drama of 2017.<ref name="The face of Baaghi – Saba Qamar"/> Qamar's performance was widely praised by the critics and her portrayal of the actress and singer was applauded even before its release. Neeha of ''[[The Nation (Pakistan)|The Nation]]'' wrote, "Without a doubt, Qamar has done an outstanding job",<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nation.com.pk/04-Feb-2018/if-baaghi-is-based-on-a-true-story-then-qandeel-baloch-did-not-deserve-this|title=If Baaghi is based on a true story then Qandeel Baloch did not deserve this|date=4 February 2018|website=The Nation|language=en|access-date=14 December 2018}}</ref> whereas reviewer from ''[[The Express Tribune]]'' said she "slayed the social media star with such finesse".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1461245/baaghi-trailer-saba-qamar-made-us-relive-qandeels-life/|title='Baaghi' trailer is out and Saba Qamar made us relive Qandeel's life|date=19 July 2017|website=The Express Tribune|language=en-US|access-date=14 December 2018}}</ref> The series earned her a Lux Style Awards for Best Actress (Television) and [[International Pakistan Prestige Awards|IPPA Awards]] for Best Actress.<ref name=luxbaaghi>{{cite web|url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/182910-here-are-the-winners-from-the-lux-style-awards-2018|title=Here are the winners from the Lux Style Awards 2018|website=Geo News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2018/02/21/winners-of-the-lux-style-awards/|title=Winners of the Lux Style Awards {{!}} Pakistan Today|date=21 February 2018|website=Pakistan Today|access-date=22 December 2018}}</ref>

In 2018, Qamar appeared in three short films. She first paired with [[Ahsan Khan]] in [[Siraj-ul-Haque]] directorial [[Moomal Rano]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/280156-saba-qamar-and-ahsan-khan-starrer-moomal-rano-to-premiere-in-pakistan|title=Saba Qamar and Ahsan Khan starrer Moomal Rano to premiere in Pakistan|last=NewsBytes|website=The News International}}</ref> The film was made as part of the Zeal For Unity initiative to bridge cultural barriers between India and Pakistan. It was critically praised and was nominated for Best Film at the 2018 European Festival.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://dunyanews.tv/en/Entertainment/462758-Nomination-Moomal-Rano-European-festival-Saba|title=Nomination of film 'Moomal Rano' for European festival an honor: Saba|work=[[Dunya News]]|access-date=16 November 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1649955/4-saba-qamar-ahsan-khans-moomal-rano-hit-screens-soon/|title=Saba Qamar, Ahsan Khan's 'Moomal Rano' appears to be Pakistan's version of 'Romeo and Juliet' {{!}} The Express Tribune|date=3 March 2018|work=The Express Tribune|access-date=16 November 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=moomal>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2018/02/10/ahsan-khan-and-saba-qamars-moomal-rano-to-finally-see-the-light-of-the-day/|title=Ahsan Khan and Saba Qamar's Moomal Rano to finally see the light of the day|date=10 February 2018|website=[[Pakistan Today]]|language=en-GB|access-date=16 November 2018}}</ref> It was released by digital platform [[ZEE5|Zee5]]. She then appeared in Fahim Burney's ''[[Dil Diyan Gallan]]'', opposite [[Zahid Ahmed (actor)|Zahid Ahmed]] where she played the character of Raniya.<ref name=dild>{{Cite news|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1180250|title=Saba Qamar and Zahid Ahmed are reuniting for a cute love story this Eid|last=Haq|first=Irfan Ul|date=12 June 2018|work=DAWN|access-date=23 June 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> She was then paired with [[Farhan Saeed]] for the first time in telefim ''[[Iss Dil Ki Essi Ki Tessi]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1773161/4-saba-qamar-farhan-saeed-star-iss-dil-ki-essi-ki-tessi/|title=Saba Qamar, Farhan Saeed to star in 'Iss Dil Ki Essi Ki Tessi' {{!}} The Express Tribune|date=4 August 2018|work=The Express Tribune|access-date=13 September 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> Qamar later appeared as model for [[Shuja Haider]]'s two music videos ''Jeewan Daan'' and ''Funn Mitti Se''.
In 2019, Qamar worked in crime drama ''[[Cheekh]]'' where she played a headstrong girl who fights for justice. It is considered both critical and commercial blockbuster.

=== Further success (2020-present) ===

In 2020, she narrated [[Zara Abid]]'s debut short film ''Sikka'' released on Qissa Nagri [[YouTube]] channel.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Short Film Sikka – A tribute to Zara Abid Model – Showbiz and Fashion|date=24 May 2020 |url=https://showbizfashion.pk/short-film-sikka-a-tribute-to-zara-abid-model/|access-date=10 April 2021|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Sikka">{{cite news|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2228795/4-zara-abids-debut-short-film-sikka-hits-youtube/|title=Watch: Zara Abid's debut short film 'Sikka' hits YouTube|work=The Express Tribune|date=26 May 2020|access-date=26 May 2020}}</ref>
She later collaborated with [[Bilal Saeed]] for music video ''Qubool'' which she also directed.
In 2021, Qamar portrayed the role of Naheed Ahmed Tasnim in telefim ''[[Hangor S-131]]'' aired on [[ARY Digital]]. In the same year Qamar appeared as model for [[Abrar-ul-Haq]]'s and [[Mustafa Zahid]]'s music videos ''Begum Shak Karti Hai'' and ''Chingaariyan'' respectively.
In 2022, Qamar made her film comeback after five year hiatus with [[Sarmad Khoosat]]'s ''[[Kamli (2022 film)|Kamli]]'' and Saqib Khan's ''[[Ghabrana Nahi Hai]]''. Qamar got several accolades for ''Kamli'' including ''IVIF'' and ''Lux Style Awards'' for Best Film Actress.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/chandigarh-hosts-4th-edition-of-south-asias-first-internationally-travelling-film-festival/articleshow/95496713.cms | title=Chandigarh hosts 4th edition of South Asia's first internationally travelling film festival | newspaper=The Times of India | date=14 November 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/526402-saba-qamar-to-star-in-sarmad-khoosats-second-production-kamli|title=Saba Qamar to star in Sarmad Khoosat's second production, Kamli|website=www.thenews.com.pk|language=en|access-date=15 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.masala.com/saba-qamar-starrer-pakistani-film-finally-gets-a-title-318416.html|title=Saba Qamar-starrer Pakistani Film Finally Gets a Title|website=Masala.com|language=en|access-date=15 February 2020}}</ref>
She later received praise for portraying Maya Nisar in [[ARY Digital]]'s hit crime thriller ''[[Fraud (TV series)|Fraud]]'' collaborating with [[Ahsan Khan]] and [[Mikaal Zulfiqar]]. 
In the same year Qamar made her OTT debut with [[Zee5]] critical and commercially successful web series ''[[Mrs and Mr Shameem]]'' and Urduflix Original ''Naina Ki Sharafat''. She then appeared as model for [[Asim Azhar]]'s music video ''Kabhi Main Kabhi Tum'' opposite [[Fahad Mustafa]].{{citation needed|date=March 2024}}

In 2023, Qamar portrayed taxi driver Rania in short series ''[[Sar-e-Rah]]'' winning Best Actress award by [[USAID]].<ref name="auto1">{{cite web | url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/1075897/usaid-honours-pakistani-women-with-sar-e-rah/ | title=USAID honours Pakistani women with 'Sar-e-Rah' | date=22 March 2023 }}</ref>  It was produced by IDream Entertainment in collaboration with [[USAID]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.youlinmagazine.com/article/drama-review-sar-e-rah/MjQ3Mg== | title=Drama Review: Sar-e-Rah - Hurmat Majid - Youlin Magazine }}</ref> In the same year she joined hands with Pakistan Polio Eradication Programme on polio awareness, starring in ''Yehi Waqt Hai'' [[YouTube]] mini series along with [[Haroon Shahid]], [[Kiran Haq]] and [[Agha Mustafa Hassan]]. She received widespread acclaim for playing antagonist Gul Meher in [[Express Entertainment]]'s mini-series ''[[Gunah (TV series)|Gunah]]'' directed by [[Adnan Sarwar]] opposite [[Juggan Kazim]], [[Rabia Butt]] and [[Sarmad Khoosat]]. Qamar next collaborated with Green Entertainment for three projects including the classic romantic drama ''Tumhare Husn Ke Naam'', the crime mystery ''Serial Killer'' and the social drama ''Pagal Khana''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saba Qamar Drama, Serial Killer, Is A Love Letter To Film Noir |url=https://dramaflash.com/saba-qamar-drama-is-a-love-letter-to-film-noir/ |access-date=9 January 2024 |website=Drama Flash |date=7 January 2024 |language=en-US}}</ref>
In 2025, Qamar made her [[Hum TV]]  comeback after seven years with [[Saife Hassan]]'s directorial telefilm ''Mohabbat Youn Bhi Honi Thi'' opposite [[Ahsan Khan]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hum.tv/blog/hum-tv-unveils-first-teaser-for-mohabbat-youn-bhi-honi-thi/|title=HUM TV Unveils First Teaser for "Mohabbat Youn Bhi Honi Thi"|date=16 December 2024|website=Hum TV}}</ref>
Qamar next appeared opposite [[Faysal Quraishi]] in [[Geo Entertainment]]'s courtroom serial ''[[Case No. 9]]'' and Green Entertainment's ''Pamaal'' opposite [[Usman Mukhtar]].{{cn|date=February 2026}}

== Other work and media image ==

In 2009, Qamar joined the political satire show ''[[Hum Sab Umeed Se Hain]]'', as a host and presenter where she also did the [[parody]] of politicians and actors. The show was extremely popular and was at the number one spot in ratings in Pakistan. She decided to quit the show and was replaced by [[Meera (Pakistani actress)|Meera]] in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.desiblitz.com/content/saba-qamars-journey-to-bollywood-hum-sab-umeed-say-hain-to-hindi-medium|title=Saba Qamar's Bollywood Journey ~ Hum Sab Umeed Say Hain to Hindi Medium|date=16 May 2017|website=DESIblitz|language=en|access-date=19 December 2018}}</ref> In January 2018, she appeared in photoshoot for Mahid Khawar's creation "Padmavat" where she dressed up like [[Rani Padmini|Rani Padmavati]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/is-that-saba-qamar-or-deepika-padukone/|title=Is that Saba Qamar or Deepika Padukone?|website=Daily Pakistan Global|date=26 January 2018 |language=en-US|access-date=26 December 2018}}</ref> 
In May 2018, she showcased golden bridal couture for designer Nilofer Shahid. She was showstopper for Rimple and Harpreet Narula's first Pakistan show on ''Shaan-E-Pakistan''.<ref>{{Cite [[Sunsilk]],<ref>{{Citation|title=Saba Qamar Sunsilk commercial|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VEhf3YVV9TE |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/VEhf3YVV9TE Qamar is considered one of the nation's most popular and highest-paid actresses.<ref name="D.Pakistan"/><ref name="pride"/><ref name="ndtv">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ndtv.com/entertainment/pakistani-actress-saba-qamars-colleagues-defend-her-after-shes-trolled-for-smoking-in-pic-1888665|title=Pakistani Actress Saba Qamar's Colleagues Defend Her In addition to acting, Qamar has supported charitable organisations for various causes.<ref name="pride"/> She is involved with several humanitarian causes and is vocal about issues faced by women and children.<ref name=women/> In June 2018, she did a special appearance in [[Shuja Haider]]'s music video "Jeevan Daan" to raised awareness against child abuse.<ref name=women>{{Cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/1735110/4-saba-qamar-star-music-video-child-abuse/|title=Saba Qamar to star in music video about child abuse|date=14 June 2018|website=The Express Tribune|language=en-US|access-date=21 December 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/shuja-haiders-song-for-a-social-cause-jevaan-daan-featuring-this-pakistani-supermodel-is-out/|title=You will cry: This song by Shuja haider featuring Saba Qamar is what you need to play right now|date=29 June 2018|newspaper=Daily Pakistan Global|language=en-US|access-date=21 December 2018|archive-date=22 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181222082006/https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/shuja-haiders-song-for-a-social-cause-jevaan-daan-featuring-this-pakistani-supermodel-is-out/}}</ref> The song was socially relevant and highlights issues concerning children and women.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/336431-shuja-haiders-latest-single-highlights-oppression-of-children|title=Shuja Haider's latest single highlights oppression of children|last=Shabbir|first=Buraq|website=The News International|language=en|access-date=21 December 2018}}</ref> In August 2018, Qamar expressed in an interview, "I encourage and urge people to invest in good education as it will shape the future of our children and our society".<ref name="pride"/> On [[Independence Day (Pakistan)|Independence Day]] in 2018, ''[[Daily Times (Pakistan)|Daily Times]]'' named Qamar "Pride of Pakistan".<ref name="pride"/>

[[Saba Qamar]] is a [[Pakistani]] actress who works predominantly in [[Urdu]] films and television. Qamar started her career with [[PTV Home]]'s classic television series ''Main Aurat Hoon'' in 2004. She made her [[Lollywood]] debut with [[Sarmad Khoosat]]'s directorial film ''[[Manto (2015 film)|Manto]]'' in 2015 and [[Bollywood]] debut with [[Saket Chaudhary]]'s directorial film ''[[Hindi Medium]]'' in 2017.<ref name="pride">{{Cite news|url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/278239/pride-of-pakistan-saba-qamar/|title=Pride of Pakistan Saba Qamar - Daily Times|last=|first=|date=2018-08-05|work=[[Daily Times (Pakistan)|Daily Times]]|access-date=2018-11-14|language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Sabreen Hisbani Baloch''' ({{langx|ur|{{Nastaliq|سبرین حسبانی }}}}; {{Langx|sd|صابرين حسباني}}; born 10 September 1978) is a Pakistani-Canadian actress. She also has worked in several acclaimed drama serials including ''[[Kitni Girhain Baaki Hain]]'', ''[[Nikhar Gaye Gulab Sare]]'', ''[[Saat Pardon Mein]]'', ''[[Sanjha]]'', ''[[Aun Zara|Aunn Zara]]'', and ''[[Laa (TV serial)|Laa]]''. With the former two earned her a widespread acclaim and recognition. She was nominated as a [[Hum Award for Best Supporting Actress|Best Supporting Actress]] at [[3rd Hum Awards]] for ''Laa'' while she won the award at [[4th Pakistan Media Awards]] for ''Aunn Zara'' in the same category.

In 2024, Sabreen Hisbani made her debut in live theatre with a Sindhi play titled ''Salgirah''. The production explored the emotional landscape of a couple in a long-term marriage who, after years of routine, confront their unmet expectations and societal pressures. She performed in a sold-out show that received high praise from fans. The performance took place at the Arts Council [[Karachi]] on 17 October 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=World Culture Festival: 'Salgirah' on marital complexities elicits emotions |url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/569543-world-culture-festival-salgirah-on-marital-complexities-elicits-raw-emotions-from-audience |access-date=2024-10-19 |website=www.geo.tv |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Sabreen was born on 10 September 1978, in [[Karachi]], to Maria and Ghulam Murtaza Baloch. Her mother was a [[Folk music|Lok]] Sindhi singer. She has two sisters and two brothers, who include famous host and acclaimed actress [[Sanam Baloch]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Sabreen Hisbani Biography, pictures |url=http://pakistani.pk/sabreen-hisbani/|publisher=Showbiz|date=2 October 2014|access-date=6 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Sabreen Hisbani Is Still Single: A Sister of Sanam Baloch|url=http://www.magmedianews.com/sabreen-hisbani-is-still-single-a-sister-of-sanam-baloch/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150411065756/http://www.magmedianews.com/sabreen-hisbani-is-still-single-a-sister-of-sanam-baloch/|url-status=usurped|archive-date=11 April 2015|publisher=Magmedia|date=5 April 2015|access-date=6 August 2015}}</ref> She was a flight attendant for PIA then began her career in 2005 in the [[Pakistan Television Corporation|PTV]] drama serial ''Masuri'', which gives her wide acclaim, she successfully established herself as an actress in industry. Since she has appeared in drama serials, sitcoms, telefims and has appeared on number of talk shows and programs. In addition she hosted the 17th PTV Karachi Center Awards.<ref>{{cite web|title=PTV awards: A tribute to Sufi folk music|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/291679/ptv-awards-a-tribute-to-sufi-folk-music/|publisher=[[The Express Tribune]]|date=14 November 2011|access-date=6 August 2015}}</ref>

== Career ==

=== 2005–2012: Early acting roles ===
Sabreen made her acting debut in ''Masuri'' (2005) as a recurring role, for which she was nominated for the [[Lux Style Award for Best TV Actress|Lux Style Award for Best Television Actress]]. Later in 2008, she got a big breakthrough with the [[Jang Media Group|Geo TV]] [[Soap opera]] ''Meri Adhoori Mohabbat'' (2008) starring alongside [[Humayun Saeed]]. The soap became a massive hit in the networks history. For the next couple of years, Sabreen continued starring in telefilms, and recurring roles.

=== 2013–2019: Mainstream success ===
In the 2013 series, [[Aunn Zara]], Hisbani plays ''Nighat'', Aunn's protective Phupho.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dawn.com |date=2013-09-27 |title='Aunn Zara' - A drama review |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1045819 |access-date=2024-07-07 |website=DAWN.COM |language=en}}</ref> In the series, Sabreen plays a supporting role in an ensemble cast. Her performance was critically acclaimed and she won the [[Pakistan Media Awards|Pakistan Media Award for Best Supporting Actress.]] The show earned her a respectful place in the industry. The same year, Sabreen would go on to do another massive hit [[Meri Beti]] (2013–2014) for [[ARY Digital]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-08-19 |title=Sabreen Hisbani: “Saba in Meri Beti is very much like me!” |url=https://pr24x7networkltd.wordpress.com/2016/08/19/sabreen-hisbani-saba-in-meri-beti-is-very-much-like-me/ |access-date=2024-07-07 |website=pr24x7networkltd |language=en }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Both [[Aunn Zara]] and [[Meri Beti]] would go on to be instant classics that are still known as some of Pakistan's best television shows.

In the 13 episode [[Hum TV]] [[Miniseries]], [[Laa (TV serial)|Laa]] (2014), Sabreen portrayed ''Laila.'' The series was nominated for multiple awards, and Sabreen herself was nominated for the 2014 [[Hum Award for Best Supporting Actress]]. Later in the years Sabreen continued to star in series such as [[Mera Dard Na Janay Koi]] (2015–2016), [[Mujhe Kucch Kehna Hai (TV series)|Mujhe Kucch Kehna Hai]] (2015–2016), and [[Mubarak Ho Beti Hui Hai]] (2017).

In 2017, Sabreen became a recurring role in [[Mohabbat Tumse Nafrat Hai]], and later that year, she starred in [[Gumrah (TV series)|Gumrah]] (2017–2018) and [[Parchayee]] (2017–2018). Both shows were airing back-to-back on the same network, [[Hum TV]]. Both were very successful for the network and gained positive reviews from the audience.

On 9 February 2018, Sabreen's debut film, [[Azad (2018 film)|Azad (2018)]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pakistani feature-film 'Azad' lands in cinemas today |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/279019-pakistani-feature-film-azad-lands-in-cinemas-today |access-date=2024-07-07 |website=www.thenews.com.pk |language=en}}</ref> ''Azad'' is a melodrama film directed and written by [[Rehan Sheikh]], who co-produced with Hasan Naeem under the production banner of Bling Studios and Roomi Films. The film features Sabreen Hisbani, [[Sanam Saeed]], [[Salman Shahid]], Rehan Sheikh, [[Nimra Bucha]] and [[Zahid Ahmed (actor)|Zahid Ahmed]], and [[Sajjad Kishwar]].

In early 2019, it was announced that Sabreen Hisbani and [[Alyy Khan]] were going to be starring in an upcoming [[Jang Media Group|Geo TV]] series, ''Saibaan.'' The first episode aired on 3 March 2019. Later that year, [[Mujhe Beta Chahiye]] was released on [[A-Plus TV]]. The series ended in December 2019.

In 2020, Sabreen made an Instagram account and shared posts that confirmed she had moved to Canada. She has stayed active on social media since then. Later in the year, It was rumored that Sabreen had left the industry overall and has moved on to pursue other ventures. Sabreen continued to update fans on her life using Instagram for years after.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sumiya |date=2022-02-07 |title=Sabreen Hisbani Biography, Husband, Daughter, & Drama List |url=https://www.magpakistan.com/sabreen-hisbani-biography-husband-daughter-drama-list/ |access-date=2024-07-07 |website=Showbiz Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== 2024–present: Media comeback ===
On 3 July 2024, Sabreen Hisbani and Umer Alam shared a post on Instagram of them together. The caption reads, "''Fortunate enough to share screen with Sabreen Hisbani. In our new Project for Hum TV, who’s making a comeback after 4 years, produced by MD Productions."'' <ref>{{Cite web |last=Abdullah |first=Rao |date=2024-07-03 |title=Sabreen Hisbani Set to Make TV Comeback |url=https://www.bolnews.com/showbiz/2024/07/sabreen-hisbani-set-to-make-tv-comeback/ |access-date=2024-07-07 |website=BOL News |language=en-US}}</ref>

The post confirms that Sabreen is returning to Pakistani Television in her new project for [[Hum TV]]. The title, characters, and full cast list is yet to be announced. Filming in currently underway in [[Karachi|Karachi, Pakistan]] and the series is set to release later this year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mohabbat Reza Reza |url=https://hum.tv/dramas/mohabbat-reza-reza/ |access-date=2024-10-20 |website=Hum TV |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Sai Paranjpye''' (born 19 March 1938) is an Indian film director and screenwriter. She is the director of the award-winning movies ''[[Sparsh (film)|Sparsh]]'', ''[[Katha (1983 film)|Katha]]'', ''[[Chashme Buddoor (1981 film)|Chasme Buddoor]]'' and ''[[Disha (film)|Disha]]''. She has written and directed many Marathi plays such as ''Jaswandi'', ''Sakkhe Shejari'', and ''Albel''.

She has won four [[National Film Awards]] and two [[Filmfare awards]]. The [[Government of India]] awarded Paranjpye the [[Padma Bhushan]] in 2006 in recognition of her artistic talents.<ref name=Padma>[http://india.gov.in/myindia/padmabhushan_awards_list1.php Padma Bhushan Awardees] Ms. Sai Paranjpye, Arts, Maharashtra, 2006.</ref>

==Early years==
Sai Paranjpye was born on 19 March 1938 in Lucknow to [[Russian people|Russian]] Youra Sleptzoff and [[Shakuntala Paranjpye]].<ref name=ASHA>{{Cite web|url=http://www.asha-foundation.org/women/women/sai_paranjpe.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071217041336/http://www.asha-foundation.org/women/women/sai_paranjpe.php|url-status=dead|title=Sai Paranjpye at ASHA|archive-date=17 December 2007}}</ref> Sleptzoff was a Russian watercolor artist and a son of a Russian general. Shakuntala was an actor in Marathi and Hindi films in the 1930s and 1940s, including [[V. Shantaram]]'s Hindi social classic, ''[[Duniya Na Mane]]'' (1937). Later she became a writer and a social worker, was nominated to [[Rajya Sabha]], Upper House of [[Indian Parliament]] and was awarded the [[Padma Bhushan]] in 1991.<ref>[http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Davis/Names/Paranjpye_Shakuntala.html Shakuntala Profile] History, names Paranjpye.</ref>

Sai's parents divorced shortly after her birth. Her mother raised Sai in the household of her own father, Sir [[R. P. Paranjpye]], who was a renowned mathematician and educationist and who served from 1944 to 1947 as India's [[High Commissioner]] in [[Australia]]. Sai thus grew up and received education in many cities in India, including [[Pune]], and for a few years in [[Canberra]], Australia.<ref>[http://www.booksandcollectibles.com.au/book.php3?book_id=219880988& Three Years In Australia] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120209012029/http://www.booksandcollectibles.com.au/book.php3?book_id=219880988& |date=9 February 2012 }} Item: 13460, booksandcollectibles.</ref><ref name="IndianExpress-Das-Writer-2019">{{Cite news|last=Das|first=Arti|date=2019-03-23|title=I am a first-class writer and a second-class director: Sai Paranjpye|language=en-IN|work=The Hindu|url=https://www.thehindu.com/entertainment/movies/i-am-a-first-class-writer-and-a-second-class-director-sai-paranjpye/article26606850.ece|access-date=2021-03-20|issn=0971-751X}}</ref> As a child, she used to walk up to the home of her uncle Achyut Ranade, a noted filmmaker of the '40s and '50s, on Fergusson Hill in Pune, who would tell stories as if he were narrating a screenplay.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080802155958/http://www.hindu.com/mp/2008/07/14/stories/2008071450150100.htm Cinema with sense], ''[[The Hindu]]'', 14 July 2008.</ref> Sai took to writing early in her life: Her first book of fairy tales – ''Mulānchā Mewā'' (in Marathi), was published when she was eight.<ref name=Pune/><ref>{{cite book |title=The cinemas of India|last=Thoraval |first=Yves|year=2000 |publisher=Macmillan India |isbn=0-333-93410-5|pages=203–204 }}</ref><ref name=indo>[http://cities.expressindia.com/fullstory.php?newsid=131515 Miss Chamko goes Chaka Chak]{{dead link|date=February 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}, ''[[Indian Express]]'', 30 May 2005.</ref>

Paranjpye graduated from the [[National School of Drama]] (NSD), [[New Delhi]] in 1963.<ref>[http://www.nsd.gov.in/Annual_Report_2005-06.pdf NSD Alumni] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718213711/http://www.nsd.gov.in/Annual_Report_2005-06.pdf |date=18 July 2011 }} [[National School of Drama]] (NSD) Annual Report 2005-2006.</ref>

==Career==
Paranjpye started her career in [[All India Radio]] ([[All India Radio|AIR]]) in [[Pune]], [[Maharashtra]], [[India]] as an announcer and soon got involved with AIR's Children's Program.

Over the years, Paranjpye has written and directed plays in [[Marathi language|Marathi]], [[Hindi]], and [[English language|English]] for adults and children. She has written and directed six feature films, two children's films, one of them being [[Nirupama Aani Parirani]], and five documentaries. She has written many books for children, and six of them have won national or state level awards.

Paranjpye worked for many years as a director or a producer with [[Doordarshan]] Television in [[Delhi]]. Her first made-for-TV movie – ''The Little Tea Shop'' (1972), won the Asian Broadcasting Union Award at [[Teheran]],<ref name=WB>[http://info.worldbank.org/etools/library/latestversion.asp?241504 Sai Paranjpye, Indian Filmmaker]{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} library, [[World Bank]].</ref> [[Iran]]. Later that year, she was selected to produce the inaugural program of [[Bombay]] (Mumbai) [[Doordarshan]].

In the 1970s, Paranjpye twice served as the Chairperson of [[Children's Film Society of India]] (CFSI), which is a government of India organization with the objective of promoting and ensuring value-based entertainment for children.<ref name=CMS>[http://www.cmsvatavaran.org/vatavaran2003/the_festival/nr/7.htm Director’s Profile] cmsvatavaran.</ref> She made four children's films for CFSI, including the award-winning ''Jādoo Kā Shankh'' (1974) and ''Sikandar'' (1976).<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110519215153/http://movies.nytimes.com/person/266545/Sai-Paranjpye/biography Biography] movies [[New York Times]].</ref>

Paranjpye's first feature film ''[[Sparsh (film)|Sparsh]]'' (The Touch), was released in 1980. It won five film awards, including the [[National Film Award (India)|National Film Award]]. ''Sparsh'' was followed by the comedies ''Chashme Buddoor'' (1981) and ''Kathā'' (1982). ''Kathā'' was a musical satire based on the folk tale of the [[The Tortoise and the Hare|hare and the tortoise]].<ref name=WF>[http://www.1worldfilms.com/India/kathathetale.htm Katha Review] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230220203912/http://1worldfilms.com/India/kathathetale.htm |date=20 February 2023 }} World Festival of Foreign Films.</ref>
She next made the TV serials ''Ados Pados'' (1984) and ''Chhote Bade'' (1985). Paranjpye worked as director, writer and narrator for the Marathi drama ''Maza khel mandu de''. It was played on 27 September 1986 at Gadkari Rangayatan, Thane.<ref>{{cite book |last=Paranjpye |first=Sai |title=Maza Khel mandu de}}</ref>

Paranjpye's subsequent movies include ''Angoothā Chhāp'' (1988) about the National Literacy Mission; ''[[Disha]]'' (1990) about the plight of immigrant workers; ''[[Papeeha]]'' (Forest Love Bird) (1993); [[Saaz (film)|Saaz]] (1997) (possibly inspired by the lives of Indian playback singing sisters, [[Lata Mangeshkar]] and [[Asha Bhosle]]);<ref>[http://im.rediff.com/entertai/may/15saaz.htm Sai Paranjpye's latest film, Saaz] [[Rediff.com]], 14 May 1997.</ref> and ''Chakā Chak'' (2005), which was aimed at creating public awareness about environmental issues.<ref name=Pune>[http://cities.expressindia.com/fullstory.php?newsid=132817 NIGHT OUT with Sai Paranjpye] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060321024445/http://cities.expressindia.com/fullstory.php?newsid=132817 |date=21 March 2006 }} [[Indian Express]], Pune Newsline, Tuesday, 7 June 2005.</ref>

She also made the serials ''Hum Panchi Ek Chawl Ke'', ''Partyana'' and ''Behnaa''. [[Sridhar Rangayan]] assisted her in the film ''Papeeha'' and in the serials ''Hum Panchi Ek Chawl Ke'' and ''Partyana''.{{citation needed|date=March 2021}}

Paranjpye has also written and staged plays like ''Maza Khel Mandu De'', ''Jaswandi'' and ''Sakhe Shejari''.<ref name="Scroll-Ramnath-Grin-2020" />

Paranjpye directed several documentary movies, including ''Helping Hand'' (London), ''Talking Books'', ''Capt. Laxmi'', ''Warna Orchestra'', and ''[[Pankaj Mullick]]''. Her 1993 documentary ''Choodiyan'', on the anti-liquor agitation in a small Maharashtra village for the Films Division, received the [[National Film Award for Best Film on Social Issues]].<ref name=WB/>

In 2001, Paranjpye made the movie for children, ''Bhago Bhoot''. At the first Indian International Women's Film Festival, held in [[Goa]] in 2005, a review of her movies was held, and it featured her best movies.<ref>[http://lists.whatwg.org/pipermail/goanet-goanet.org/2005-December/036992.html New Feature Film "Xapai" to be directed by Sai Paranjpye] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171012201843/http://lists.whatwg.org/pipermail/goanet-goanet.org/2005-December/036992.html |date=12 October 2017 }} Goanet, 18 December 2005.</ref> She headed the jury in the feature film category of the 55th [[National Film Awards]] for 2007.<ref>[http://www.ptinews.com/news/269524_National-awards--free-from-lobbying---Paranjpye National awards "free from lobbying": Paranjpye] [[Press Trust of India]], 2009.</ref>

In July 2009, Paranjpye's documentary film ''[[Suee]]'' was released, emerging from the South Asia Region Development Marketplace (SAR DM), an initiative spearheaded by the [[World Bank]].<ref name=WB/> ''Suee'' explores a number of areas in the lives of [[injecting drug users]] including treatment, care, peer and community support, rehabilitation and the workplace, and was produced in partnership with the [[Mumbai]]-based [[NGO]] Sankalp Rehabilitation Trust. The 29 minute film was aired on Doordarshan on [[World AIDS Day]], 1 December 2009.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130416011204/http://www.unaids.org/en/KnowledgeCentre/Resources/FeatureStories/archive/2009/20090810_ICAAP_WB_IDU_film_GVA.asp|title=Injecting drug users take central role in anti-stigma film}} Accessed 22 January 2010</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.3dsyndication.com/showarticle.aspx?nid=DNMUM139008 |title=NCB drive against drug abuse gets rolling – DNA – English News & Features – Mumbai |publisher=3dsyndication.com |date=2009-06-29 |access-date=2011-10-16 |archive-date=4 October 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111004102149/http://www.3dsyndication.com/showarticle.aspx?nid=DNMUM139008 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2016, she released her autobiography, ''Saya: Majha Kalapravas'', written in Marathi. It was a bestseller that had reached its fifth edition in 2020. She then released ''A Patchwork Quilt – A Collage of My Creative Life'', the English version of her autobiography, in 2020, with some chapters rewritten.<ref name="Scroll-Ramnath-Grin-2020">{{Cite web|date=28 November 2020|last=Ramnath|first=Nandini|title=Sai Paranjpye interview: 'I guess I was born with a grin'|url=https://scroll.in/reel/979306/sai-paranjpye-interview-i-guess-i-was-born-with-a-grin|access-date=2021-03-20|website=Scroll.in}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Sai was married to theater artist Arun Joglekar; they had a son, Gautam, and a daughter, Winnie. Sai and Arun separated after two years.<ref>[http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshow/15374687.cms Sai speak!] ''The Times of India'', 8 July 2002.</ref> They remained friends until Arun's death in 1992. After their separation, Arun acted in Sai's ''[[Sparsh (film)|Sparsh]]'' (1980) and ''[[Katha (1983 film)|Katha]]'' (1983).<ref>{{IMDb name|id=0423659|name=Arun Joglekar}}</ref> Their son, [[Gautam Joglekar]] is a director of Marathi films (Pak Pak Pakaak, Jai Jai Maharashtra Maaza) and a professional cameraman, and their daughter Winnie Paranjpe Joglekar is an educationist and homemaker. Winnie acted in many of Sai's movies, dramas and TV serials in the 1980s.<ref>{{IMDb name|id=2243051|name=Vinni Paranjpye Joglekar}}</ref> Winnie and her husband, Abhay, now deceased, have two children; Abeer and Anshunee. Gautam starred as the male lead in [[Nana Patekar]]'s directorial venture ''[[Prahaar: The Final Attack|Prahaar]]'' with [[Madhuri Dixit]] playing the female lead.

{{Short description|None}}
{{Use Indian English|date=November 2025}}

'''Shashi Sumeet Productions Pvt. Ltd.''' is an Indian company founded by Shashi Mittal and Sumeet Hukamchand Mittal which produces [[Indian soap opera]]s, [[entertainment]] and reality programming on Indian television.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.indiantelevision.com/television/production-house/fiction/shashi-sumeet-productions-launch-marketing-and-creative-agency-150129|title=Shashi Sumeet Productions launch marketing and creative agency|date=29 January 2015}}</ref> Some of its notable works include: ''[[Diya Aur Baati Hum]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.indiantelevision.com/television/tv-channels/gecs/shashi-sumeet-productions-diya-aur-baati-hum-completes-3-glorious-years-140902|title=Shashi Sumeet Productions' Diya Aur Baati Hum completes 3 glorious years|date=2 September 2014}}</ref> ''[[Punar Vivah]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/2015-04-07/Party-all-night-for-the-team-of-Diya-Aur-Baati-Hum-142461|title=Party all night for the team of Diya Aur Baati Hum!|website=The Hans India}}</ref> ''[[Yeh Un Dinon Ki Baat Hai]]'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.televisionpost.com/shashi-sumeet-relive-their-love-story-with-sets-yeh-un-dino-ki-baat-hai/|title=Shashi-Sumeet relive their love story with SET's 'Yeh Un Dino Ki Baat Hai'|website=Television Post|access-date=19 October 2019|archive-date=8 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190708095914/https://www.televisionpost.com/shashi-sumeet-relive-their-love-story-with-sets-yeh-un-dino-ki-baat-hai/|url-status=dead}}</ref>  ''[[Barrister Babu]], [[Meet: Badlegi Duniya Ki Reet]], [[Dhruv Tara – Samay Sadi Se Pare]]''.

'''''The Hunting Party''''' is an American [[Procedural drama|procedural]] crime drama television series created by JJ Bailey for [[NBC]]. The series premiered on January 19, 2025, and revolves around a small investigative team assembled to track down and capture the most dangerous killers known to have just escaped from a top-secret prison whose existence is not known to the public.

In May 2025, the series was renewed for a second season, which premiered on January 8, 2026. In June 2026, the series was canceled after two seasons.

== Premise ==
After a prison hidden underneath the Wyoming countryside suffers an unexpected explosion, the nation's worst serial killers are once again at large. Former [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] [[Offender profiling|profiler]] Rebecca, "Bex", Henderson is brought back into the fold alongside an elite team of soldiers, spies, and special agents to help track down and recapture these deadly criminals before they kill again. Thrust into a world of intrigue and conspiracy, Bex must grapple with not only her own complex past but also the enduring mystery of what was happening at this prison and who caused the explosion in the first place.

==Cast and characters==
===Main===
* [[Melissa Roxburgh]] as Rebecca "Bex" Henderson, an FBI Special Agent and criminal profiler
* [[Nick Wechsler (actor)|Nick Wechsler]] as Oliver Odell (season 1), Bex's former partner and lover
* [[Patrick Sabongui]] as Jacob Hassani, a [[Central Intelligence Agency|CIA]] officer
* [[Josh McKenzie]] as Shane Florence, a prison officer at an underground silo known as ''The Pit'' in Cheyenne, Wyoming
* [[Sara Garcia (Canadian actress)|Sara Garcia]] as Maj. Jennifer Morales, an [[Military Intelligence Corps (United States Army)|Army Intelligence]] officer

===Recurring===
<!--Reliably sourced and/or confirmed to make 4+ appearances in the series. Do not include co-stars as they are just actors who have super minor roles and are below guest starring.-->
* [[Zabryna Guevara]] as Elizabeth Mallory, the United States Attorney General
* [[Kari Matchett]] as Colonel Eve Lazarus, a high-ranking military officer and a former inmate of The Pit who is secretly Shane's mother
* [[Matt Frewer]] as Dr. Henry Dulles, a scientist and doctor who used to work in The Pit studying the inmates
* [[Siobhan Williams]] as Sarah Dulles, Dr. Dulles' daughter
* Luke Forbes as Jonathan Peck (season 2), an associate of Colonel Lazarus who is part of the Inmate Recovery Task Force

===Special guest stars===
<!-- Credited as special guest stars only -->
* [[Eric McCormack]] as Ron Simms (season 2), a serial killer who preys on women who are searching for love
* [[Niecy Nash-Betts]] as Erica Burke (season 2), a detective who brought a serial killer to justice in the past
* [[Kelsey Grammer]] as Noah Cyrus (season 2), the leader of a Chicago-based doomsday cult known as the Thirteenth Hour
* [[John Corbett]] as Xander Wax (season 2), a biochemist who kills people by using lethal animal venoms

==Production==
===Development===
In August 2022, it was announced J.J. Bailey had entered into an overall deal with [[Universal Television]] with the first project to be developed being [[procedural drama]], ''The Hunting Party'', created by Bailey and Jake Coburn.<ref>{{cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|title=Writer JJ Bailey Inks Overall Deal With Universal TV, Sets ''The Hunting Party'' Crime Procedural At NBC|url=https://deadline.com/2022/08/jj-bailey-the-hunting-party-crime-procedural-nbc-overall-deal-universal-television-1235100314/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=August 25, 2022|access-date=May 12, 2024}}</ref> In February 2023, it was announced [[NBC]] had set up a writers room for the series with a formal straight-to-series order taking place one year after.<ref>{{cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|title=NBC Sets Writers Rooms For ''The Hunting Party'' & ''Grosse Pointe Garden Society''|url=https://deadline.com/2023/02/nbc-writers-rooms-the-hunting-party-grosse-pointe-garden-society-1235261878/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=February 16, 2023|access-date=May 12, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|title=NBC Orders ''The Hunting Party'' Crime Procedural Series|url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/josh-mckenzie-nbc-drama-series-the-hunting-party-cast-1235918344/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=February 28, 2024|access-date=May 12, 2024}}</ref>

On May 12, 2025, NBC renewed the series for a second season.<ref name="S2 renewal">{{cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=May 12, 2025|title=''The Hunting Party'' & ''Brilliant Minds'' Renewed For Season 2; NBC Plans To "Lean Into" Them In 2025-26|url=https://deadline.com/2025/05/the-hunting-party-brilliant-minds-renewed-season-2-nbc-1236392332/|website=Deadline Hollywood|access-date=May 12, 2025}}</ref> On June 2, 2026, NBC canceled the series after two seasons, but is slated to be shopped to other networks.<ref>{{cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=June 2, 2026|title=''The Hunting Party'' Canceled By NBC After 2 Seasons, Will Be Shopped|url=https://deadline.com/2026/06/the-hunting-party-canceled-nbc-shopped-1236939365/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=June 2, 2026}}</ref>

===Casting===
In May 2024, it was announced [[Melissa Roxburgh]] was cast as the show's lead.<ref>{{cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|title=Melissa Roxburgh To Star In NBC Series ''The Hunting Party''|url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/melissa-roxburgh-the-hunting-party-nbc-1235909619/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=May 9, 2024|access-date=May 12, 2024}}</ref> Later that same month, it was announced [[Patrick Sabongui]], Josh McKenzie and Sara Garcia had joined the cast as series regulars.<ref>{{cite web|last=Petski|first=Denise|title=Patrick Sabongui & Sara Garcia Join NBC Drama Series ''The Hunting Party''|url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/patrick-sabongui-sara-garcia-nbc-the-hunting-party-1235911885/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=May 10, 2024|access-date=May 12, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Petski|first=Denise|title=Josh McKenzie Joins NBC Drama Series ''The Hunting Party''|url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/josh-mckenzie-nbc-drama-series-the-hunting-party-cast-1235918344/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=May 15, 2024|access-date=May 15, 2024}}</ref> In June 2024, [[Nick Wechsler (actor)|Nick Wechsler]] joined the cast as a series regular while [[Kyra Leroux]] was cast in a recurring role.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2024/06/nick-wechsler-the-hunting-party-kyra-leroux-cast-nbc-1235962186/|title=Nick Wechsler Joins NBC Drama 'The Hunting Party' As Series Regular; Kyra Leroux Also Cast|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|last=Petski|first=Denise|date=June 7, 2024|access-date=January 12, 2025}}</ref>

===Filming===
Filming in Vancouver for the first season of the series began on June 20, 2024, and concluded on November 19, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dgc.ca/en/british-columbia/productions|title=DGC BC Production List|website=[[Directors Guild of Canada]]|date=October 25, 2024|access-date=October 28, 2024|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/20241028004103/https://www.dgc.ca/en/british-columbia/productions|archive-date=October 28, 2024}}</ref> Production moved to New York City for the second season, the premiere of which was moved to midseason after initially being scheduled for the fall.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gittins |first=Susan |date=2025-07-24 |title=THE HUNTING PARTY With Melissa Roxburgh Moves Production From Vancouver to NYC |url=http://hollywoodnorthbuzz.com/2025/07/the-hunting-party-with-melissa-roxburgh-starts-shooting-season-2-this-september-in-vancouver.html |access-date=2025-07-24 |website=Hollywood North Buzz |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=2025-07-28 |title=NBC Fall Premiere Dates: ''Law & Order: Organized Crime'' Back On Thursday, ''Hunting Party'' Held, ''St. Denis Medical'' & ''Happy's Place'' Double Pumped |url=https://deadline.com/2025/07/nbc-fall-premiere-dates-2025-1236472488/ |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Broadcast==
The series premiered on January 19, 2025, on [[NBC]].<ref name="Series premiere">{{Cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/nbc-midseason-2025-premiere-dates-suits-la-1236066326/|title=''Suits: L.A.'' Gets Premiere Date in NBC's Midseason Lineup|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|first=Rick|last=Porter|date=November 19, 2024|access-date=November 19, 2024}}</ref><ref name="The Hunting Party Premiere Date Change">{{Cite press release|title=NBC's New Drama Series "The Hunting Party" to Now Premiere Sunday, Jan. 19 at 7 p.m. ET/PT|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2025/01/13/nbcs-new-drama-series-the-hunting-party-to-now-premiere-sunday-jan-19-at-7-pm-et-pt-84112/20250113nbc01/|publisher=[[NBC]]|via=[[The Futon Critic]]|date=January 13, 2025}}</ref> The second season premiered on January 8, 2026.<ref name="S2 premiere">{{Cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2025/11/nbc-midseason-premiere-dates-onechicago-the-hunting-party-1236615558/|title=NBC Midseason Premiere Dates Include OneChicago, ''The Voice'' & ''Hunting Party''s Return, New Tracy Morgan Comedy|website=Deadline Hollywood|first=Denise|last=Petski|date=November 12, 2025|access-date=November 12, 2025}}</ref>

==Reception==
===Critical response===
On the review aggregator website [[Rotten Tomatoes]], the series holds an 18% approval rating based on 11 critic reviews. The website's critics consensus reads, "Thrilling in theory but glaringly dull in execution, ''The Hunting Party'' plays it too fast and loose with its serial killer mayhem ideas, making it just another procedural in the sea of many."<ref>{{Cite Rotten Tomatoes|id=the_hunting_party|title=The Hunting Party|type=tv|season=1|access-date=June 3, 2026|publisher_hide=y}}{{cbignore}}</ref> [[Metacritic]], which uses a weighted average, assigned a score of 34 out of 100 based on 7 critics, indicating "generally unfavorable" reviews.<ref>{{Cite Metacritic|id=the-hunting-party-2025|title=The Hunting Party|type=tv|season=1|access-date=February 3, 2025|publisher_hide=y}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

'''''Udaari''''' (title from {{langx|pnb|{{Nastaliq|اُڈاری}}}}; lit: ''Flight'') is an Urdu and Punjabi language social Pakistani television series that was created and co-produced by [[Kashf Foundation]] and [[Momina Duraid]] for [[Hum TV]]. It focused on the social and economic marginalisation of citizens in Pakistani rural society alongside highlighting deep-rooted issues such as child sexual abuse, gender discrimination and violence against women. It was originally aired from 10 April 2016 to 4 September 2016. The show is written by [[Farhat Ishtiaq]] and directed by [[Mohammed Ehteshamuddin]].''Udaari'' follows the interconnected lives of two neighbouring families, a local shopkeeper, and a university music band.As their stories cross paths, the series focuses on exploring class discrimination, taboos, stigmas, women empowerment, sexual abuse, and the power and stigmatisation of music.<ref name="hum"/><ref name="Dawn"/>

Udaari has an ensemble cast with [[Bushra Ansari]] as Sheedan, [[Samiya Mumtaz]] as Sajida, [[Urwa Hocane]] as Ameera, [[Farhan Saeed]] as Arsh, [[Ahsan Khan (actor)|Ahsan Khan]] as Imtiaz, and Hina Altaf Khan/Areesha Ahsan as Zebo.<ref name=hum>{{cite web|title=Udaari Drama|url=http://www.hum.tv/udaari-drama/|access-date=29 June 2016|publisher=Hum TV|archive-date=7 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160607091931/http://www.hum.tv/udaari-drama/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=Dawn>{{cite web|title=Urwa Hocane's latest TV Drama Udaari explores class divions through Music|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1175139|date=11 April 2016|access-date=28 June 2016|publisher=Dawn|work=Sadaf Haider|archive-date=19 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160619001124/http://images.dawn.com/news/1175139|url-status=live}}</ref> The show is set in the village of Mirpur and urban areas of [[Punjab]].

''Udaari'' received positive reviews from critics and audiences throughout its broadcast, critics considered the sensitive issues within the story's arc well-drafted and well-composed, and also lauded the entire cast's performance, it also scored the highest ratings in 2016 and was ranked as the highest rated TV series of the [[2016 in Pakistani television|2016 season]]. At the [[16th Lux Style Awards]], the series won the most for the ceremony including, Best TV Actor for Khan, Best TV Director and [[Lux Style Award for Best TV Play|Best TV Play]] for Duraid.

==Plot==

''Udaari'' follows the interconnected lives of two neighbouring families, a local shopkeeper, and a university music band. Set in the village Mirpur Khas, Rashida and Sajida are close neighbours and friends. Rashida lives with her husband Majid, their children, Meera and Ejaz, and her brother Iqbal and belongs to the hereditary musician community, whose members face social discrimination because of their profession. Sajida, a widow, struggles to raise her young daughter, Zebo, while working as a domestic servant. Meanwhile, Imtiaz returns to the village after working in Dubai and opens a mobile phone shop. In Lahore, university students Arsh, Maleeha, Haris and Farwa form a music band and participate in a televised music competition.

Meera falls in love with Sajida's nephew, Ilyas, but their relationship is strained by his family's prejudice against her background as a musician. After rescuing Sajida from local thugs, Imtiaz, being a cousin of her late husband, proposes marriage to her. Believing him to be trustworthy and seeking a stable future for her daughter, Sajida accepts, and the couple initially lead a happy married life. Following Majid's death in an accident, however, Imtiaz attempts to sexually assault Meera, who manages to escape. Sajida refuses to believe Meera's accusation and instead supports her husband, creating a rift between the two families. Influenced by his family's views, Ilyas also ends his relationship with Meera, while the villagers ostracise Rashida's family, forcing them to consider leaving the village. when Farwa leaves the band under family pressure, Maleeha and her mother, Muneera, discover Meera's singing talent at a village wedding and invite her to join the group. Meera and her family relocate to Lahore, where she joins the band, develops a relationship with Arsh, and rises to national fame after the group wins the televised competition. Back in the village, Imtiaz begins sexually abusing Zebo and threatens to kill her and Sajida if she reveals the abuse. After discovering the truth, Sajida confronts him, but Imtiaz rapes Zebo in her presence after locking Sajida in a room. Sajida escapes, stabs Imtiaz, believing she has killed him, and flees with Zebo to Lahore, where Meera and Rashida shelter them to their home, and help them begin a new life under new identities.

Six years later, Meera has become an established singer, while Sajida has built a successful business. Having survived the attack, Imtiaz tracks them down and uses his political influence to file false criminal charges against Sajida while continuing to threaten Zebo. Arsh, now a lawyer, investigates the case with Muneera's assistance and uncovers evidence exposing Imtiaz's crimes. Encouraged by Arsh and Muneera, Zebo publicly testifies against Imtiaz. Meera also recounts his earlier attempt to assault her, strengthening the prosecution's case. Ilyas later apologises and asks Meera to resume their engagement, but she refuses. Following a public campaign and protest led by Muneera, Imtiaz's political influence turns against him and he is convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment, while Sajida is acquitted of all charges. The series concludes with the reconciliation of the two families, Meera accepting Arsh's marriage proposal and the family dedicating a song to Zebo and other survivors of abuse.

==Production==

===Development===
Udaari was developed by [[Hum TV]]'s senior producer [[Momina Duraid]] of [[MD Productions]], the channel hired the award-winning director [[Mohammed Ehteshamuddin]] to direct the series.<ref name="hum"/><ref name="Dawn"/> Story of serial is written by award-winning writer [[Farhat Ishtiaq]].<ref name="Dawn"/><ref name=ahsan>{{cite web|url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1149469|publisher=HIP|work=Rozina Butto|date=9 April 2016|access-date=27 June 2016|title=Udaari is as much for males as it is for females|archive-date=18 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818173932/http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1149469|url-status=live}}</ref> It was Ishtiaq's first screenplay without a novel release, she has previously worked thrice with Momina, when she wrote mega-hit drama serials in Pakistan television history [[Humsafar]],<ref name=humsafar>{{cite news|title= Popular Pakistani television drama Humsafar reaches Toronto fans via web|url= https://www.thestar.com/living/article/1132592--popular-pakistani-television-drama-humsafar-reaches-toronto-fans-in-via-web//|access-date= 29 February 2012|work= The Star|date= 16 February 2012|archive-date= 19 February 2012|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120219230621/http://www.thestar.com/living/article/1132592--popular-pakistani-television-drama-humsafar-reaches-toronto-fans-in-via-web|url-status= live}}</ref> ''[[Mata-e-Jaan Hai Tu]]'',<ref name=mtjht>{{cite news|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/335449/mata-e-jaan-hai-tu-composition-he-wrote/|title=Mata-e-Jaan Hai Tu drama serial's composition|newspaper=[[The Express Tribune]]|date=12 February 2012|access-date=25 February 2012|archive-date=14 February 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120214091312/http://tribune.com.pk/story/335449/mata-e-jaan-hai-tu-composition-he-wrote/|url-status=live}}</ref> and ''[[Diyar-e-Dil]]''.<ref name="Dawn News">{{cite web|title=''Diyar-e-Dil'' opens with a bang and is a visual treat|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1170348/review-diyar-e-dil-opens-with-a-bang-and-is-a-visual-treat|work=Sadaf Haider|publisher=[[Dawn News]]|date=19 March 2015|access-date=7 April 2015|archive-date=4 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150404051013/http://www.dawn.com/news/1170348/review-diyar-e-dil-opens-with-a-bang-and-is-a-visual-treat|url-status=live}}</ref>

Song composition is done by [[Sahir Ali Bagga]] and Sohail Haider while background music is given by Mohsin AllahDitta who chose singers like [[Bushra Ansari]], [[Hadiqa Kiani]] and [[Farhan Saeed]] for singing. It was Insari and Kiani's second collaboration after [[Pakistan Idol]]. Kiani and Saeed collaborated on the title song and also provided the vocals for the characters of Meeran and Arsh (portrayed by Saeed).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1175655|title=Udaari is proof: A TV drama doesn't need helpless women to be a hit|first=Sadaf|last=Haider|date=22 June 2016|access-date=23 July 2016|archive-date=1 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160801000811/http://images.dawn.com/news/1175655|url-status=live}}</ref> There were discussions laid on its time slot, previously it was announced that the show will air on Saturdays replacing Durad's [[Gul-e-Rana (TV series)|Gul-e-Rana]]. However, due to promotional reasons and Slot importance the show was given time slot of Sundays, 8:00 pm, whereas the long running series, Abroo was given a time slot of Saturdays.<ref name=replacement>{{cite web|title=Udaari replaces Gul-e-Rana|date=5 April 2016|access-date=30 June 2016|publisher=HIP|work=Rozina Butto|url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1149430|archive-date=18 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818205523/http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1149430|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Udaari'' was initially planned to be released in 2017 after completion of filming but Duraid decided to release it in 2016 to For higher ratings to her channel. It was released in April and was planned to end along with Hum TV's ''[[Mann Mayal]]'' thereby both the shows were slotted to maintain Sunday and Monday slots to bring higher Television Rating Points (TRP) to them for the future.

===Casting===

Producer, writer and Director mutually chose the cast which includes [[Bushra Ansari]], [[Samiya Mumtaz]], [[Ahsan Khan (actor)|Ahsan Khan]], [[Urwa Hocane]], [[Farhan Saeed]] and Hina Altaf Khan and Areesha Ahsan to play the leading roles of Sheedhan, Sajida, Imtiaz, Meera, Arsh and Zebo.<ref name="Dawn"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Meet the cast of Udaari|url=http://enewspaper.com.pk/meet-and-greet-the-cast-of-udaari/|date=7 April 2016|access-date=30 June 2016|publisher=Enews paper|archive-date=17 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817142544/http://enewspaper.com.pk/meet-and-greet-the-cast-of-udaari/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="images.dawn.com">{{cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1175655|title=Udaari is proof:A TV drama doesn't need helpless women to be hit|publisher=Dawn|date=22 June 2016|work=Sadaf Haider|access-date=30 June 2016|archive-date=30 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160630034730/http://images.dawn.com/news/1175655|url-status=live}}</ref>

Veteran Actress [[Bushra Ansari]] was cast to portray the role of Rashida Bibi after her appraisal for her role in [[Kis Ki Ayeegi Baraat]] series,<ref>{{cite web|title=Television sequels - the next big trend?|work=Maleeha Hamid Siddiqui|publisher=Dawn|date=2 February 2013|access-date=30 June 2016|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/783234/television-sequels-the-next-big-trend|archive-date=26 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181226115740/https://www.dawn.com/news/783234/television-sequels-the-next-big-trend|url-status=live}}</ref> and [[Bilqees Kaur]]. The actress received critical acclaim within the pilot episode, according to her, this role was a challenge.

Urwa Hocane and Farhan Saeed marked their second appearance together as a couple being previously acted in [[Ary Digital]]'s Mere Ajnaabi.<ref>{{cite web|title='Mere Ajnabi has yet to show Urwas-Farhan's sizzling Chemistry|work=Kiran Farooqi|date=3 August 2015|access-date=30 June 2016|publisher=HIP|url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1147631|archive-date=30 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160130164528/http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1147631|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=8 July 2015|access-date=30 June 2016|publisher=Dawn|work=Sheeba Khan|url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1147499|title=Mere Ajnaabi|archive-date=21 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160621042047/http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1147499|url-status=live}}</ref>

''Udaari'' was [[Samiya Mumtaz]]'s second collaboration with [[Momina Duraid]] and [[Mohammed Ehteshamuddin]], she previously acted in drama-serial [[Sadqay Tumhare]]<ref name="images.dawn.com"/><ref>{{cite web|publisher=Dawn|work=Sadaf Haider|date=16 April 2015|access-date=30 June 2016|title=Can a victim of abuse ever shed her past?|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1175867|archive-date=7 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160707055317/http://www.dawn.com/news/1175867|url-status=live}}</ref> after which she was finalised to portray the role of Sajida.<ref name=proof>{{cite web|title=Udaari is proof: A TV drama doesn't need helpless women to be a hit|publisher=Dawn Images|date=22 June 2016|access-date=1 October 2016|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1175655|archive-date=5 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161005091548/http://images.dawn.com/news/1175655|url-status=live}}</ref> Alongside Mumtaz, actress Hina Altaf Khan was cast to portray series's the pivotal character of ''Zebo''. Zebo's role was initially portrayed by Areesha Ahsan as child artist.<ref name=thenews>{{cite web|title=Redefining TV's regressive narrative|publisher=International The News|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/148473-Redefining-TVs-regressive-narrative|access-date=30 September 2016|archive-date=2 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161002171944/https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/148473-Redefining-TVs-regressive-narrative|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/1119412/mawra-urwas-brother-ins-e-yazdan-set-make-acting-debut/|title=Mawra Urwa brother Ins-e-Yazdan set make acting debut/|date=6 June 2016|access-date=22 July 2016|newspaper=Express Tribune|archive-date=20 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160720010744/http://tribune.com.pk/story/1119412/mawra-urwas-brother-ins-e-yazdan-set-make-acting-debut/|url-status=live}}</ref>

''Udaari'' was [[Ahsan Khan (actor)|Ahsan Khan]]'s first portrayal of a negative role. Khan was cast to portray the role of 'Imtiaz'' a pedophile,<ref name="Dawn"/><ref name="ahsan"/><ref name=tribunee>{{cite web|publisher=Express Tribune|work=Aleena Abid|date=28 April 2016|access-date=30 June 2016|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/1093528/hero-turns-villain-heres-why-ahsan-khan-chose-to-play-a-child-molester/|title=Hero turns villain: Here's why Ahsan Khan chose to play a child molester|archive-date=2 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160702111228/http://tribune.com.pk/story/1093528/hero-turns-villain-heres-why-ahsan-khan-chose-to-play-a-child-molester/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=antagonist>{{cite web|title=Ahsan Khan to play the antagonist in Farhat Ishtiaq's 'Udaar'|publisher=hip|work=Ahmed Sarym|url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1149276|access-date=30 June 2016|archive-date=21 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160521010843/http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1149276|url-status=live}}</ref> this role was initially offered to actor [[Mikaal Zulfiqar]] who rejected it due to its grey personality. Speaking about difficulty in portraying this role, Khan states that ''Even while reading the script, I could not digest these scenes. It is definitely the most difficult character to portray on-screen'', further sommecfting on his role Khan states ''Such abuse leaves the child traumatised forever. My maid's child was suffering from it and that's what made me realise that I need to spread awareness.<ref name="tribunee"/>

Production also chose [[Behroze Sabzwari]], [[Laila Zuberi]], [[Maryam Fatima]], [[Rehan Sheikh]], Haris Waheed and Aqeel Abbas for the supporting roles of Khalid, Muneera, Farwa, Majid, Illyas and Balay respectively.<ref name="hum"/> Sabzwari received critical acclaim for his role of Tajamul in Duraid's Diyar-e-Dil, he was selected to portray Khalid alongside Zuberi who joined the series after her previous project ''[[Mann Mayal]]'' with Duraid.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Khan |first1=Sheeba |title=Gohar and Hamza; Friends who act together, stay together|work=HIP |url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1147687/gohar-and-hamza-friends-who-act-together-stay-together|date=14 August 2015|access-date=20 September 2015|archive-date=28 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150928220225/http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1147687/gohar-and-hamza-friends-who-act-together-stay-together|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Music and sound===

All the music and songs of Udaari were composed by musician [[Sahir Ali Bagga]] and Sohail Haider with Mubarak and Zahid being the sound engineer. The background score is given by Bilal Allahdittah,  the lyrics for the OST were penned down by Imran Raza. The OST ''Sajna Ve Sajna'' was sung by [[Farhan Saeed]] and [[Hadiqa Kiani]].<ref name=misc>{{cite web|title=HUM TV's Drama 'Udaari' Ft. Urwa Hocane: OST, Timings & Schedule|url=http://www.brandsynario.com/hum-tvs-drama-udaari-ft-urwa-hocane-ost-timings-schedule/|work=Hareem Zafar|date=4 April 2016|publisher=Brandynario|access-date=8 July 2016|archive-date=14 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160714003946/http://www.brandsynario.com/hum-tvs-drama-udaari-ft-urwa-hocane-ost-timings-schedule|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=pakium>{{cite web|publisher=Pakium|access-date=8 July 2016|date=16 May 2016|url=http://www.pakium.pk/2016/05/16/ost-udaari-by-farhan-saeed-hadiqa-kiani|title=Udaari OST|archive-date=18 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160718050903/http://www.pakium.pk/2016/05/16/ost-udaari-by-farhan-saeed-hadiqa-kiani|url-status=live}}</ref>  It marks the return of [[Hadiqa Kiani]] to Hum TV, since she performed for the channel's hit drama series [[Zindagi Gulzar Hai]]'s title song. Veteran actress and vocalist [[Bushra Ansari]] performed only Punjabi music for various episodes. [[Rahat Fateh Ali Khan]]'s ''Samjhawanki'' was taken and performed by [[Hadiqa Kiani]] for the series.

Udaari's full OST was released in May 2016. Saajna Ve Saajna received critical acclaim for [[Sahir Ali Bagga]] and Sohail Haider for comping and [[Hadiqa Kiani]] and [[Farhan Saeed]] for vocals. The Series dominated the Top No.1 rank according to Pakistan's Official Music App Taazi.<ref name="Naqvi">{{cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1175455|title=Pop goes the silver screen! How musicians in Pakistan found their niche in cinema - again|first=Ahmer|last=Naqvi|date=30 May 2016|access-date=23 July 2016|archive-date=11 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160811150413/http://images.dawn.com/news/1175455|url-status=live}}</ref>  "Mein Tenu Samjhawanki" received critical acclaim and success.<ref name=ostt>{{cite web|url=http://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/pakistan/video-watch-hadiqa-kianis-mesmerizing-new-track-for-udaari/|title=VIDEO: Watch Hadiqa Kiani's mesmerizing new track for Udaari|work=Daily Pakistan Global |access-date=23 July 2016|archive-date=26 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160526064944/http://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/pakistan/video-watch-hadiqa-kianis-mesmerizing-new-track-for-udaari/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Filming and locations===
[[Principal photography]] and filming began in February 2016 and finishes in June 2016,<ref name=trending>{{cite web|title=Plot & Synopsis of Hum's latest play Udaari|url=http://www.trendinginsocial.com/plot-synopsis-hums-latest-play-udaari/|date=13 April 2016|access-date=30 June 2016|publisher=trending in social|archive-date=17 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817023450/http://www.trendinginsocial.com/plot-synopsis-hums-latest-play-udaari/|url-status=live}}</ref> with approximately 25 episodes.<ref name="trending"/> Shooting was extensively done in [[Multan]]'s village [[Mirpur Khas]] and in Karachi.<ref name=location>{{cite web|last1=Bhutto |first1=Rozina |title=Team Udaari spreads on faces of locals in Mirpurkhas|date=15 April 2016|work=Rozina Bhutto|access-date=30 June 2016|publisher=hip|url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1149513|archive-date=18 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818181859/http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1149513|url-status=live}}</ref> Udaari's first promo was released in March 2016.<ref name=teasers>{{cite web|title=Udaari teaser doesn't hint towards its sensitive topic|url=https://www.hipinpakistan.com/archive/tv/2016-03-04|publisher=hip|work=Rozina Bhutto|date=4 April 2016|access-date=30 June 2016|archive-date=18 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160818191740/https://www.hipinpakistan.com/archive/tv/2016-03-04|url-status=live}}</ref> Chief editing and cinematography was done by Azhar Ali who edited the series.

===Post production and pre-release===

====Press conference====
On 7 April 2016 a press conference was held for Udaari. The programme, hosted by Shanaz Ramzi, CEO Starlinks PR began the proceedings with the series's introduction. Producer Momina Duraid said that some of the actors came out of their comfort zones for the roles that they portrayed. Furthermore, Roshaneh Zafar from Kashf Foundation reflected on common rape cases in Kasur city which led them to produce a screenplay for awarenesses against child-sexual abuse. Director Ehteshamuddin, revealed how challengingvit had been to get the writer, Farhat Ishtiaq to write the script, as not only was the subject a difficult one to portray on screen but it also needed a script that was very close to reality. Bushra Ansari shared her role which is that of a woman who is extremely confident but unrefined, and embodies the real culture of Pakistan's rural areas. She regaled the media present with her quick vivid descriptions and stories painted about the time on set in Mirpur Khas.<ref>{{cite web|title=Meet and Greet the cast of Udaari|date=8 April 2016|publisher=TrendinginSocial|access-date=30 June 2016|url=http://www.trendinginsocial.com/meet-greet-cast-udaari/|archive-date=12 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160712112105/http://www.trendinginsocial.com/meet-greet-cast-udaari/|url-status=live}}</ref>

The [[title song]] of Udaari was composed by musician [[Sahir Ali Bagga]] and Sohail Haider, the lyrics were penned down by Imran Raza. The OST was sung by [[Farhan Saeed]] and [[Hadiqa Kiani]].<ref name="misc"/><ref name="pakium"/>  It marks the return of [[Hadiqa Kiani]] to Hum TV, since she performed for the channel's hit drama series [[Zindagi Gulzar Hai]]'s title song.

The Soundtrack is produced along with the series production by Momina Duraid and Kashf Productions. The original music was recorded by the production house itself while few songs used in the show were covers of previous classics, including the song '''Mein Tenu Samjhawanki''' which was sung by [[Hadiqa Kiani]]. Actress [[Bushra Ansari]] revamped classic Punjabi Pakistani songs.

Udaari's full OST was released in May 2016. Saajna Ve Saajna received critical acclaim for [[Sahir Ali Bagga]] and Sohail Haider for comping and [[Hadiqa Kiani]] and [[Farhan Saeed]] for vocals. The Series dominated the Top No.1 rank according to Pakistan's Official Music App Taazi.<ref name="Naqvi"/>  "Mein Tenu Samjhawanki" received critical acclaim and success.<ref name="ostt"/>

==Broadcast and release==
===Broadcast===
Udaari was originally decided to release in September after completion of filming in July and post production delays, but instead Production decided to release it in April. With its release, it was initially decided to premiere on 9 April 2016, and air every Saturday night with higher reception, replacing Gul-e-[[Gul-e-Rana (TV series)|Rana]] which had maintained the slot with a high viewership for the channel.<ref name="replacement"/> But to maintain their Sunday slot, the channel instead released ''Udaari'' on 10 April 2016, airing every Sunday night, replacing [[Abro (TV serial)|Abro]], which was then shifted to Saturdays.  The channel aired a weekly episode for approximately 30–45 minutes (without commercials). It was ordered and compromised 25 episodes. It was aired on [[Hum Europe]] in UK,<ref name="timings">{{cite web|title=''Udaari'' international timings in UK, USA and UAE|url=http://www.hum.tv/hum-europe/|publisher=Hum TV|access-date=27 December 2015|archive-date=15 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160115175940/http://www.hum.tv/hum-europe/|url-status=live}}</ref> on [[Hum TV|Hum TV USA]] in USA<ref name="timings"/> and [[Hum TV|Hum TV Mena]] on UAE,<ref name="timings"/> with same timings and premiered date. All International broadcasting aired the series in accordance with their standard times.

===Homa media and digital release===
Udaari was released on [[Hum TV]]'s YouTube channel alongside its airing but in 2017, it was taken off. It was also released on a DVD set on late November 2016. In January 2017, [[iflix]] app streamed ''Udaari'' on a subscription basis but was pulled off by the channel in 2018. In December 2019, ‘’Udaari’’ was digitally released again by Hum TV on their youtube channel with all its music removed. Furthermore, the show is also available on [[MX Player]].

===Ratings and viewership===
[[Hum TV]] announced the television rating point figures for ''Udaari'' through its official [[Facebook]] page. The series premiered with 4.9 television rating points (TRPs), a figure matched by its third episode; the fourth and sixth episodes recorded 5.5 and 4.0 TRPs, respectively.<ref name="HumTV-ratings"/> Ratings subsequently increased to 7.1 TRPs for the eighth episode and averaged approximately 6 TRPs through the thirteenth episode, before rising to 7.3 for the fourteenth and 7.8 for the fifteenth.<ref name="HumTV-ratings"/> Hum TV described ''Udaari'' as its most-watched drama during [[Ramadan]], reporting that it outperformed several game shows despite the customary decline in television audiences during the period.<ref name="HumTV-ratings"/> The sixteenth episode recorded 6.2 TRPs, followed by 7.3 for the seventeenth and 7.8 for the eighteenth. The twentieth and twenty-first episodes received 6.0 and 6.6 TRPs, respectively.<ref name="HumTV-ratings"/> The finale averaged 6.8 TRPs during the 8:00 p.m. hour and 7.9 after 9:00 p.m., with portions of the broadcast reportedly exceeding 10 TRPs.<ref name="HumTV-ratings"/>
Episode-level audience reports recorded 11.5 million viewers for the eleventh episode and 11.9 million for the twelfth.<ref name="eleven"/><ref name="twelve"/> The eighteenth episode was subsequently reported to have attracted 16.5 million viewers.<ref name="eighteen"/> MediaLogic's monthly television-market reports also consistently ranked ''Udaari'' among Pakistan's leading programmes. The second episode attracted a reported audience of 21 million and ranked second both overall and in its timeslot.<ref name="medialogic-march">{{cite web |title=MediaLogic Monthly Review (March 2016) |url=http://medialogic.com.pk/tam/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Medialogic_Monthly_Review_March_2016.pdf |date=1 April 2016 |access-date=10 January 2017 |publisher=MediaLogic |archive-date=2 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202202240/http://medialogic.com.pk/tam/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Medialogic_Monthly_Review_March_2016.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref> The fifth episode also attracted 21 million viewers, ranking second overall and first in its timeslot.<ref name="medialogic-april">{{cite web |title=MediaLogic Monthly Review (April 2016) |url=http://medialogic.com.pk/tam/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Medialogic_Monthly_Review_April_2016.pdf |date=1 April 2016 |access-date=10 January 2017 |publisher=MediaLogic |archive-date=2 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202203725/http://medialogic.com.pk/tam/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Medialogic_Monthly_Review_April_2016.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref> The eighth and twelfth episodes each reached a reported 27 million viewers, ranking second overall and first in their timeslot.<ref name="medialogic-may">{{cite web |title=MediaLogic Monthly Review (May 2016) |url=http://medialogic.com.pk/tam/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Medialogic_Monthly_Review_May_2016.pdf |date=1 June 2016 |access-date=10 January 2017 |publisher=MediaLogic |archive-date=2 February 2017
