name="medialogic-june">{{cite web |title=MediaLogic Monthly Review (June 2016) |url=http://medialogic.com.pk/tam/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Medialogic_Monthly_Review_June_2016.pdf |access-date=10 January 2017 |publisher=MediaLogic |archive-date=2 February 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202202118/http://medialogic.com.pk/tam/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Medialogic_Monthly_Review_June_2016.pdf |url-status=live}}</ref> By its eighteenth episode, the series ranked first both overall and in its timeslot, with a reported audience of 27 million; the twenty-second episode retained both rankings with 26 million viewers.<ref name="medialogic-august">{{cite web |title=MediaLogic Monthly Review (August 2016) |url=http://medialogic.com.pk/tam/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Medialogic_Monthly_Review_August_2016.pdf reported to have attracted 30 million viewers and ranked first overall and in its timeslot.<ref name="medialogic-september">{{cite web |title=MediaLogic Monthly Review (September 2016) |url=http://medialogic.com.pk/tam/wp-content/uploads/2016/12/Medialogic_Monthly_Review_September_2016.pdf |access-date=10 January 2017 |publisher=MediaLogic |archive-date=2 February 2017 On the rankings of Top ten Pakistani dramas in 2016,''Udaari'' had dominated the No. #2 spot where as another [[Hum TV]] series, ''[[Mann Mayal]]'' dominated the No. #1 position. Both the shows bought a higher reception for the channel. The series competed with [[Jang Media Group|Geo TV]]'s most expensive Pakistani series, ''[[Mor Mahal]]'' which was then shifted to 22:00 slot between the course of show.

===Critical appreciation===
Actors [[Bushra Ansari]] and [[Ahsan Khan]] earned the most critical acclaim in 2016 for their portrayals.<ref name="thenews"/> Commenting on his character's acclaim, Khan stated ''It's a huge honour for me to receive this appreciation from one of the greatest villains of all time.''<ref name=bollywood>{{cite web|title=Ahsan Khan's performance from Udaari earns him praise from Bollywood|publisher=Express Tribune|work=Entertainment Desk|date=17 August 2016|access-date=20 September 2016|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/1164437/ahsan-khans-performance-udaari-earns-praise-bollywood/|archive-date=11 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160911073132/http://tribune.com.pk/story/1164437/ahsan-khans-performance-udaari-earns-praise-bollywood/|url-status=live}}</ref> Imtiaz's character was also internationally recognised, earning critical acclaim from Indian artists [[Reena Roy]] and [[Alka Yagnik]]. Speaking about series reviews from India, Khan states ''Udaari isn't being aired in India currently but these two stars have been watching my show on YouTube. I really appreciate their love and support.''<ref name="bollywood"/>

Writing for ''[[Dawn News]]'', Sadaf Haider moderately reviewed the series praising its parody if culture saying, ''Udaari reads like a brightly colored map of Pakistani society today. Divisions of class and wealth are amply illustrated but so are everyday human interactions.''<ref name=images>{{cite web|publisher=[[Dawn News]]|work=Sadaf Haider|access-date=28 August 2016|title=Urwa Hocane's latest TV drama Udaari explores class divisions through music|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1175139|date=11 April 2016|archive-date=20 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820210737/http://images.dawn.com/news/1175139|url-status=live}}</ref> Furthermore, Haider praises the casting stating, ''Udaari has a strong star cast and it looks as if we will see some great performances''.<ref name="images"/> She concluded her review saying that ''Udaari seems like a safe bet for some informative and enjoyable hour every Sunday''.<ref name="images"/> In April issue of ''[[The Express Tribune]]'', ''Udaari'' was ranked third behind ''[[Mann Mayal]]'' and ''Dillagi'''.<ref name="haider1">{{cite news|title=Here's the ultimate list of Pakistani dramas you must watch in 2016|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/1079727/heres-the-ultimate-list-of-pakistani-dramas-you-must-watch-in-2016/|first=Sadaf|last=Haider|newspaper=[[The Express Tribune]]|date=11 April 2016|access-date=1 May 2016|archive-date=2 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160502055759/http://tribune.com.pk/story/1079727/heres-the-ultimate-list-of-pakistani-dramas-you-must-watch-in-2016/|url-status=live}}</ref>

However, ''Sheeba Khan'' of ''Dawn'' praised the series script and characters saying, ''..Udaari, gave an astounding opening this week with its larger than life first episode. After watching the serial, one is blown away by the phenomenal acting and superb characterization in this drama''.<ref name=hip>{{cite web|last1=Sarfaraz |first1=Iqra |title=Authenticity and reality; 'Udaari' has it all|publisher=Dawn|work=Sheeba Khan|date=27 April 2016|access-date=28 August 2016|url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1149494|archive-date=28 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828233047/http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1149494|url-status=live}}</ref> Moreover, Khan praised Udaari's premier and culture saying ''Udaari has a very impressive opening with flamboyant characters and their dull sides of life. Every actor is immersed into the feel of his and her role, and gives a magnificent performance. All of them have acquired Punjabi accents with so much ease and grace that it will make you think as if they are not just characters, but are real people from an actual rural setting''.<ref name="hip"/> She concluded her by issue praising ''[[Farhat Ishtiaq]]'s'' writing saying ''The best part about Udaari is its characterization of each actor, for which the writer Farhat Ishtiaq should be applauded.''<ref name="Dawn"/>

''Sadaf Haider'' of ''[[Dawn News]]'' praised Udaari's direction saying, "Udaari's success lies firmly with director Ehtashamuddin's masterful ability to translate Farhat Ishtiaq's wonderful script flawlessly to the screen. He has elicited some great performances from his team and made sure this wide-ranging storyline did not lose its way".<ref name=elevn>{{cite web|title=Breaking new ground: there's more to Udaari than just child sexual abuse|publisher=HIP|work=Sadaf Haider|access-date=28 August 2016|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1175371/breaking-new-ground-theres-more-to-udaari-than-just-child-sexual-abuse|date=20 May 2016|archive-date=28 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828104812/http://images.dawn.com/news/1175371/breaking-new-ground-theres-more-to-udaari-than-just-child-sexual-abuse|url-status=live}}</ref> Furthermore, she stated that even after Seven episodes, "Uddari is successfully topping rating charts".<ref name="elevn"/> Talking about same publication, Sheeba Khan praised the Urban and rural life combination for Dawn's review, Khan states, "The director has managed to extract the best out of all of his actors and has shown a great amount of sensitivity to what should be projected on screen. Sexual abuse is a huge issue in Pakistan, yet for some odd reason has become a taboo and cannot be spoken about".<ref name="dawn">{{cite web|access-date=28 August 2016|publisher=[[Dawn News]]|work=Sheeba Khan|date=20 May 2016|title=Breaking new ground: there's more to Udaari than just child sexual abuse|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1175371/breaking-new-ground-theres-more-to-udaari-than-just-child-sexual-abuse|archive-date=28 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828104812/http://images.dawn.com/news/1175371/breaking-new-ground-theres-more-to-udaari-than-just-child-sexual-abuse|url-status=live}}</ref> Lastly she praised the theme of child abuse and societal issues by saying, "Pairing a debate on sexual abuse with a commentary on parenting is a smart move, and just shows how, of all the plays running right now, Udaari is not only intelligent and real, it highlights issues in society that need attention so they can be prevented. It shows that victims need not keep quiet and that their families should be their first line of defence".<ref name=dawn/> Further more Sadaf Haider praised the roles of [[Ahsan Khan (actor)|Ahsan Khan]] and [[Samiya Mumtaz]] praising Sajida's positivity for her Daughter Zebo, according to her reviews, was Mumtaz's most powerful role, where she portrayed the role of a village women with an extreme powerful getup sparking her role.<ref name="proof"/>

[[Dawn News]]'s article ''Sadaf Haider''  praised the Twenty first episode of ''Udaari'' with series giving its message, ''Haider'' praised the character of Zebo and Arsh stating, "Most significant of all, instead of lecturing Zebo to do the right thing, Arsh becomes a true hero by empowering her and showing her a way to take control of her life. He explains that any shame or guilt is not her burden to carry; all of it should be firmly placed on the perpetrator's shoulders, never the victim's."<ref>{{cite web|title='Main victim nahi, survivor hoon': Udaari delivers its most important message yet|date=1 September 2016|access-date=15 September 2016|publisher=Dawn|work=Sadaf Haider|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1176161|archive-date=15 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160915192445/http://images.dawn.com/news/1176161|url-status=live}}</ref>

While talking to local media about, ''[[Urwa Hocane]]'' portraying the role of Meera discussed the importance of the drama and social taboos like child abuse and rape. Hocane said, "It's about time for women to talk about this. I think Udaari has brought a change. The people who wanted to ban it couldn't because of the people who wanted the drama to bring about a change. Girls don't speak about such things. I am probably destined to change that mindset."<ref name=web>{{cite web|title=After Udaari, Urwa tells women to talk about issues that aren't highlighted in society|date=22 September 2016|access-date=2 October 2016|publisher=Pakistan Today|work=web desk|url=http://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2016/09/22/entertainment/after-udaari-urwa-tells-women-to-talk-about-issues-that-arent-highlighted-in-society/|archive-date=3 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161003064952/http://www.pakistantoday.com.pk/2016/09/22/entertainment/after-udaari-urwa-tells-women-to-talk-about-issues-that-arent-highlighted-in-society/|url-status=live}}</ref> Furthermore, talking about her role of Meera being a local musician, Hocane stated,  "I want to change the mindset of people. Bushra jee told me that the word miraasi comes from miraas. You should be proud of it rather than feel horrible about it."<ref name="web"/>

In addition to critical reviews Imtiaz's character received wide media attention and has been a subject of popularity since the beginning, commenting in his role [[Ahsan Khan (actor)|Ahsan Khan]] stated that "Even while reading the script, I could not digest these scenes. It is definitely the most difficult character to portray on-screen".<ref name=imtiaz>{{cite web|date=28 April 2016|access-date=15 September 2016|title=Hero turns villain: Here's why Ahsan Khan chose to play a child molester|publisher=[[Express Tribune]]|work=Alveena Abid|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/1093528/hero-turns-villain-heres-why-ahsan-khan-chose-to-play-a-child-molester/|archive-date=5 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160905105821/http://tribune.com.pk/story/1093528/hero-turns-villain-heres-why-ahsan-khan-chose-to-play-a-child-molester/|url-status=live}}</ref> Moreover, Khan decided to donate 20% of his fee from the serial to the victims of the heinous crime, he also began working with an NGO to make his contributions more substantial and concrete.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ahsan Khan wants to do more than Udaari, makes huge pledge to child abuse victims|date=4 August 2016|access-date=15 September 2016|author=Hamza Rao|work=Daily Pakistan Global|url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/ahsan-khan-wants-to-do-more-than-udaari-makes-huge-pledge-to-child-abuse-victims/|archive-date=23 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160923075937/https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/lifestyle/ahsan-khan-wants-to-do-more-than-udaari-makes-huge-pledge-to-child-abuse-victims/|url-status=live}}</ref> ''Khan'' commented on the series theme "child abuse" stating, "Such abuse leaves the child traumatised forever. My maid's child was suffering from it and that's what made me realise that I need to spread awareness."<ref name="tribunee"/> commenting on critical acclaim Khan stated "It's a huge honour for me to receive this appreciation from one of the greatest villains of all times."<ref name="bollywood"/> Khan's negative role of child molester earned him critical acclaim.<ref name="thenews"/>

Moreover, ''Fatima Awan'' of ''Review It'' praised the role of rape-victim ''Zebo'', according to her ''Udaari'' played a major role in educating their audience against communal crimes. Apart from sexual abuse, ''Awan'' also commented on other societal issues such as politician's negative support and bribing police which plays a major role in societies. The role of Zebo was furthermore praised when ''Awan'' stated that every girl should stand for justice and live her life not as a victim but as a survivor. Further more ''Awan'' commented on the final episode of Udaari where she praised the roles of Zebo, Sajida, Imtiaz, Arsh, Muneera, Meera and Sheedan. With Arsh (Portrayed by ''[[Farhan Saeed]]'') ''Awan'' praised the message he gave against child sexual abuse and in favour of Women's rights, she praised the roles of Sajida and Zebo where the two finally sealed justice and Munnera educating her society. According to her review, Udaari has proved to be the major commercial success of 2016.

===Controversies===

On 10 May 2016, '[[Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority]]' ([[PEMRA]]) issued a notice against ''Udaari'' calming that it had inappropriate content for Television audiences.<ref>{{cite web|title=Child abuse drama Udaari gets PEMRA notice for 'immoral content' and that's the problem|access-date=28 August 2016|publisher=[[Dawn News]]|work=Sadaf Haider|date=13 May 2016|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1175342|archive-date=28 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828234400/http://images.dawn.com/news/1175342|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite abuse is disturbing, but it exists in Pakistan, PEMRA!|publisher=[[The Express Tribune]]|work=Fatima Azhar|date=16 May 2016|access-date=28 August on 25 May 2016 Momina Duraid responded to PEMRA regarding the reality of society and responded the issue, as a result the issue was taken back.<ref>{{cite news|title=You are willing to ban Udaari, but Duraid stated that, ''We feel that Pemra might have been misled by a group of people who would never want our society to raise and flourish. We will explain our view point and present it with evidence. We are attaching articles and feedback supporting Udaari with the our reply''. Following this ''Udaari'' received support from several audiences and various TV Artists including actress [[Yumna Zaidi]] .<ref>{{cite news|title=Producer Momina Duraid responds to PREMRA|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/1103312/udaari-producer-momina-duraid-responds-to-pemras-show-cause-notice/|newspaper=[[The Express Tribune]]|date=16 May 2016|access-date=28 August 2016|archive-date=28 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828225107/http://tribune.com.pk/story/1103312/udaari-producer-momina-duraid-responds-to-pemras-show-cause-notice/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Legacy and impact ===
Hocane termed her role in the series as "her most impactful role".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1487044 |title=The Icon Interview: The ‘Hocane’ Phenomenon |date=9 June 2019 |author=Maliha Rehman |work=Dawn.com }}</ref>

''Udaari'' received global recognition due to its tackling the taboo themes with authenticity and sensitivity, which got it huge viewership and global acclaim.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/369738-udaari-receives-global-recognition-bbc-reports|title=Udaari receives global recognition, BBC reports|work=The News|date=17 September 2018|access-date=25 March 2022|archive-date=25 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220325100504/https://www.thenews.com.pk/amp/369738-udaari-receives-global-recognition-bbc-reports|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/sonyarehman/2016/05/18/the-tv-serial-that-got-pakistan-talking-about-child-abuse/|title=The TV Serial That Got Pakistan Talking About Child Abuse|work=Forbes|date=18 May 2016|access-date=25 March 2022|archive-date=25 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220325100629/https://www.forbes.com/sites/sonyarehman/2016/05/18/the-tv-serial-that-got-pakistan-talking-about-child-abuse/|url-status=live}}</ref> '''''Yahan Ke Hum Sikandar''''' is an Indian [[Hindi language]] teen drama television series which aired on [[DD National]] from 2011 to 2013. The show stars assembled cast of [[Tom Alter]], Saksham Dayma, Anu Nain, Dhruv Raj Sharma, Tanvi Chaturvedi, Ritu Chauhan and Puneet Kumar. The show was created, directed and produced by Dilip Sood for [[Doordarshan]]. The story and dialogues were written by Taqi Imam and Harish Vyas. Following success of the first season, the show returned with the second season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.in.com/tv/shows/dd-national-174/yahan-ke-hum-sikandar-18275.html|title=Yahan Ke Hum Sikandar|website=in.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170721143212/http://www.in.com/tv/shows/dd-national-174/yahan-ke-hum-sikandar-18275.html|archive-date=2017-07-21|url-status=dead|access-date=2017-07-21}}</ref>

==Plot==
;Season 1
Five students studying in the Government school in [[Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh]], India; have their aspirations and dreams. Samuel ([[Tom Alter]]), a British who did not leave India after independence, teaches History to students in school and helps students as their guide. Ali (Saksham Dayma) helps his father in his metal welding shop due to financial condition of his family. He studies in school and wants to excel in [[boxing]]. Aisha (Anu Nain), a girl from middle-class family, wants to make her career in [[Badminton]]. Radhey (Dhruv Raj Sharma) is her happy-go-lucky friend. He likes Suhani (Tanvi Chaturvedi), an upper-class girl studying in Sunshine Public School, an English medium school; and follows her frequently. Sameer (Punit Kumar) is simple and smiling friend and schoolmate of Ali, Aisha and Radhey. Ranjana ([[Ritu Chauhan]]), a free spirited girl is also friends with and secretly admires Ali. Karan, a classmate of Suhani, is their antagonist who turns their friend in end. The series shows these small town children's life and conflict with society and culture to achieve their dreams.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://dwarkaparichay.blogspot.in/2011/10/blog-post_12.html|title=यहाँ के हम सिकंदर - नया धारावाहिक|last=Sharma|first=Prembabu|date=12 October 2011|website=Dwarka Parichay|language=Hindi|trans-title=Yahan Ke Hum Sikandar - New Serial|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170721072237/http://dwarkaparichay.blogspot.in/2011/10/blog-post_12.html|archive-date=2017-07-21|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/yahan-ke-hum-sikandar/cast/779496/|title=Yahan Ke Hum Sikandar|website=TVGuide.com|language=en|access-date=2017-07-21|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170823164240/http://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/yahan-ke-hum-sikandar/cast/779496/|archive-date=2017-08-23}}</ref>

;Season 2
They complete their schooling and go to college. Their struggles and joys continue. Ashima and Ranjna join them.

The show was broadcast on [[DD National]], two episodes per week. The first season ended with 110 episodes. The second season ended on 25 July 2013 with 65 episodes.{{citation needed|date=November 2023}}

'''''Yaqeen Ka Safar''''' ({{langx|ur|{{nq|یقین کا سفر}}|lit=The Journey of Trust}}) is a [[Pakistanis|Pakistani]] television [[Pakistani drama|drama series]] produced by [[Momina Duraid]] through [[MD Productions]] for [[Hum TV]]. It was written by [[Farhat Ishtiaq]], based on Ishtiaq's novel ''Woh Yakeen Ka Naya Safar'' and was directed by [[Shahzad Kashmiri]]. It aired from 19 April 2017 to 1 November 2017 for a total of 29 episodes.<ref name=dawnn>{{Cite news|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1179488|title=47% of our readers believe Yaqeen Ka Safar deserves to be on Netflix|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|date=2018-02-20|work=Images|access-date=2018-05-02|language=en-US}}</ref>

''Yaqeen Ka Safar'' tells the story of Asfand and Zubiya, who grow after facing hardships and struggles. It was written and produced by the creators of ''[[Humsafar]]'', ''[[Mata-e-Jaan Hai Tu]]'', ''[[Diyar-e-Dil]]'', ''[[Udaari]]'' and ''[[Bin Roye]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.muzent.com/yakeen-ka-safar-hum-tv-dramas-details-cast/|title=Yaqeen Ka Safar - Hum TV Dramas Details & Cast|last=Abbasi|first=Zaib|date=2017-04-05|work=Music & Entertainment - MuzEnt|access-date=2017-04-05|language=en-US}}</ref> Its ensemble cast consists of [[Ahad Raza Mir]] as Dr Asfandyar, [[Sajal Ali]] as Dr Zubiya, [[Shaz Khan]] as Daniyal, [[Hira Mani]] as Gaiti and [[Suhaee Abro]] as Noorie in leading roles. It aired simultaneously in Pakistan, the UK, the US, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, and the UAE on the same date and time. The first half of the show was set in Karachi and later in [[Neelum District|Neelum Valley]].

''Yaqeen Ka Safar'' was one of the highest-ranked dramas in Pakistan in 2017.

==Premise==
''Yaqeen Ka Safar'' starts with three stories.

Zubia Khalil is a young girl mourning her mother's sudden death at the hands of her physically violent father. Zubia needed to visit a friend's house to borrow important lecture notes and she insisted that her mother accompany her, despite her father forbidding her mother to leave the house alone. When Khalil, father of zubia discovered Zubia's mother disobeyed him, he slapped her so hard she fell and ended up hitting the corner of the bed, dying on the spot. Zubia's aunt, Mahjabeen Khala consoles the devastated; Zubia tells her the truth. But Khalil threatens her and the whole family to stay silent regarding the cause of the mother's death.

The second story involves a family in [[Islamabad]] celebrating their son Daniyal's wedding to Gaiti Ara. Daniyal is a young lawyer who has recently graduated from London and is extremely fearless, confident, brave and honest. Asfandyar is Daniyal's younger brother, who will soon leave for Karachi to complete his medical studies after his brother's wedding. Daniyal is a lively person and quite ambitious as well. The family maintains a significant reputation in the community as Usman, Daniyal and Asfandyar's father, is a successful lawyer, too. Asfandyar is engaged to Faryal.

The third storyline involves Noori, a young girl living in a rural village of Sindh (Rab Nawaz.) who is gang-raped by a minister's son, Jahangir Shah, along with two of his friends. The police inquire about the incident and ask her quite inappropriate questions. Noori's younger brother stands up for her, but her parents remain silent because of their poverty. The police threaten Noori's father. Their family is insulted in the village, so Noori leaves her home. She is then found by and taken to Karachi by Rumana, an NGO lady in Karachi. Rumana informs Daniyal about the Noori gang rape incident.

==Production==
===Development===

Hum TV's senior producer Momina Duraid of MD Productions, developed ''Yakeen Ka Safar.'' The channel hired the director [[Shahzad Kashmiri]] who previously directed ''[[Bin Roye (TV series)|Roye]]'' for the same channel. Along with Kashmiri, they finalised Mirza Zeeshan Baig as the art director.<ref>{{Cite web |last=NewsBytes |title=Yakeen Ka Safar will star Sajal Aly and Ahad Raza Mir |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine |access-date=2026-02-10 |website=www.thenews.com.pk |language=en}}</ref> It was Baig's return to Hum Television after he directed ''[[Diyar-e-Dil]]'', ''[[Mann Mayal]]'', [[Sanam (TV series)|''Sanam'']], ''[[Dil Banjaara]]'' and ''[[Alif Allah Aur Insaan]]'' for the same channel. Tameen Nazami and Safdar Hussain Rind were the cinematographers. The serial is based on award-winning writer [[Farhat Ishtiaq]]'s novel ''Woh Yakeen Ka Ek Naya Safar''. Ishtiaq also wrote the screenplay, while Muhammad Wasi-ul-Din composed the script, who has previously worked with her with the channel's series ''Diyar-e-Dil'' and ''Bin Roye''. Ishtiaq has previously worked with Duraid, where she wrote mega-hit drama serials in Pakistan television history, ''[[Humsafar]]'',<ref name=humsafar>{{cite news |title= Popular Pakistani television drama Humsafar reaches Toronto fans via web| url =https://www.thestar.com/living/article/1132592--popular-pakistani-television-drama-humsafar-reaches-toronto-fans-in-via-web// |access-date= 29 February 2012 | work=The Star |date=16 February 2012}}</ref> ''[[Mata-e-Jaan Hai Tu]]'',<ref name=mtjht>{{Cite news|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/335449/mata-e-jaan-hai-tu-composition-he-wrote/|title=Mata-e-Jaan Hai Tu drama serial's composition|publisher=[[The Express Tribune]]|date=12 February 2012|access-date=25 February 2012}}</ref> ''Diyar-e-Dil''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Diyar-i-dil-An upcoming drama serial by Farhat Ishtiaq|url=http://gossip.pk/2014/08/13/dayar-e-dil-upcoming-drama-based-farhat-ishtiaq-novel/|access-date=13 January 2015|archive-date=14 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150614050133/http://gossip.pk/2014/08/13/dayar-e-dil-upcoming-drama-based-farhat-ishtiaq-novel/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Diyar-e-Dil – The City of Heart|url=http://blogs.humnetwork.com/dayaar-e-dill-city-of-heart/|publisher=[[Hum TV]]|date=16 March 2015|access-date=5 April 2015}}</ref><ref name="DDdev">{{cite web|title=Farhat Ishtiaq and Haseeb Hassan talk Diyar-e-Dil - The director and writer of the drama say they are working with a 'dream team'.|url=http://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1146877/|publisher=HIP|date=23 March 2015|access-date=25 September 2015|archive-date=19 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230419205628/https://www.hipinpakistan.com/news/1146877|url-status=dead}}</ref> ''Bin Roye''<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://feed.pk/4846/humayun-saeed-mahira-khan-starrer-bin-roye-to-on-air-as-drama-in-coming-months/|title=Humayun Saeed-Mahira Khan starrer Bin Roye to on-air as Drama in coming months {{!}} FEED|last=Hamza|first=Rana|website=feed.pk|access-date=20 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blogs.tribune.com.pk/story/28580/five-reasons-why-you-should-or-should-not-watch-bin-roye/|title=Five reasons why you should (or should not) watch Bin Roye|access-date=23 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://m.gulfnews.com/life-style/celebrity/desi-news/bin-roye-rides-pakistani-new-wave-1.1551281|title='Bin Roye' rides Pakistani new wave|access-date=23 July 2016}}</ref> and ''[[Udaari]]''.<ref name=proof>{{cite web|title=Udaari is proof: A TV drama doesn't need helpless women to be a hit|publisher= Dawn Images|date=22 June 2016|access-date=1 October 2016|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1175655}}</ref> Waqar Ali and Suhail Haider composed the song, while MAD Music gave the background score. [[Hadiqa Kiani]] and Richa Sharma performed the OST. ''Yaqeen Ka Safar'' is the second collaboration of writer and director after 2015's hit film ''[[Bin Roye]]''. The show aired a weekly episode for 35–40 minutes (minus commercials) every Wednesday.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}}

There were several discussions regarding its time slot. It was announced that the show would premiere on 12 April 2017, airing an episode on Friday's replacing ''[[Dil Banjaara]]''. However, since [[Dil-e-Jaanam (2017 TV series)|''Dil-e-Jaanam'']] bought lower ratings to channel's Wednesday slot, ''Yakeen Ka Safar'' was shifted to Wednesdays and was delayed till 15 April 2017 due to promotional reasons.{{citation needed|date=November 2022}}

===Casting===

[[Sajal Ali]], [[Ahad Raza Mir]], [[Shaz Khan]] and [[Hira Salman]] were selected to portray the leading roles of Zubiya, Asfandyar, Daniyal and Gaeti.<ref name="return">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/amp/175742-Sajal-Aly-returns-to-the-small-screen|title=Sajal Aly returns to the small screen|date=31 December 2016|work=The News International|access-date=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181021024543/https://www.thenews.com.pk/amp/175742-Sajal-Aly-returns-to-the-small-screen|archive-date=21 October 2018}}</ref><ref name="star">{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/amp/199105-Yakeen-Ka-Safar-will-star-Sajal-Aly-and-Ahad-Raza-Mir|title=Yakeen Ka Safar will star Sajal Aly and Ahad Raza Mir|date=17 April 2017|work=www.thenews.com.pk|author=News Bytes|access-date=}}</ref> Aly made her television comeback two years after her 2015 TV series [[Gul-e-Rana (TV series)|''Gul-e-Rana'']]. After completing her [[Bollywood]] debut, [[Mom (film)|''Mom'']], Sajal portrayed Dr. Zubiya and signed ''[[O Rangreza]]'' for the same channel.<ref name="return" /> Mir, who made his television debut in [[Sammi (2017 TV series)|''Sammi'']], was finalised after his success in portraying the role of Salar in ''Sammi''.<ref name="return" /><ref name="star" /> The actor received critical acclaim and appraisal for his role as Dr Asfandyar. Film actor Shaz Khan was finalised to portray the role of Daniyal during his filming session in the channel's upcoming film [[Parwaaz Hay Junoon]]. While Salman returned to the network after her 2015 TV serial ''[[Preet Na Kariyo Koi]]'', portraying the role of Gaeti, Salman joined filming after completing her [[ARY Digital|ARY]] project ''[[Sun Yaara]]'', alongside Salman her husband [[Mani (actor)|Mani]] was also cast where he portrayed the role of Dr. Haroon.<ref name="star" /> The production house also chose actors [[Farhan Ali Agha]], [[Mohammed Ehteshamuddin]], and [[Maryam Nafees]] to play the roles of Usman, Noori, Khalil and Khajista.

==Release==
''Yakeen Ka Safar'' premiered on 19 April 2017<ref>{{cite web|title=Hum TV to shift 'Maan' for 'Mann Mayal'|url=http://www.media247.co.uk/bizasia/hum-tv-to-shift-maan-for-mun-mayal-2016|work=Raj Bahadur|publisher=Bizasia|date=24 January 2016|access-date=25 January 2016|archive-date=30 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160130015957/http://www.media247.co.uk/bizasia/hum-tv-to-shift-maan-for-mun-mayal-2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> and aired weekly, with a new episode being broadcast every Wednesday at 8:00 pm.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hum TV Programming schedule|url=http://www.hum.tv/schedule.php|publisher=[[Hum TV]]|access-date=25 January 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151007033151/http://www.hum.tv/schedule.php|archive-date=7 October 2015|df=dmy-all}}</ref> The show aired on [[Hum Europe]] in the UK,<ref name="timings">{{cite web|title=''Yaqeen Ka Safar'' international timings in UK, USA and UAE|url=http://www.hum.tv/hum-europe/|publisher=Hum TV|access-date=27 December 2015}}</ref> [[Hum TV|Hum TV USA]] in the US<ref name="timings" /> and [[Hum TV|Hum TV Mena]] in the UAE,<ref name="timings" /> with the same times and premiere date. It was broadcast by Hum Network's new channel ''Hum World HD'' for the US and Canada. It was rebroadcast on [[Hum TV]] in Pakistan, premiering on 8 October 2018 at the 10 pm slot. In 2019, it also aired on the national channel [[PTV Home]] started in August 2019, airing two episodes  (Friday and Saturday) every week. A dubbed version is currently airing on Hum Pashto 1 in Pashto under the title ''دباور سفر''.

===Home media and digital release===
''Yakeen Ka Safar was'' also released on [[Hum TV]]'s [[YouTube]] channel alongside its airing, but later the channel deleted all its episodes. It was also released on the [[iflix]] as a part of the channel's contract. When the contract was terminated in 2019, all its episodes were removed and thus could not be streamed digitally anymore. Later ''Yakeen Ka Safar'' was also released on [[Over-the-top media service|OTT]], the platform [[MX Player]]. In July 2019, the channel re-uploaded all episodes on [[YouTube]]. A few episodes are also available on [[Prime video|Amazon Prime Video]].

Mad Music gave the [[background score]] for the series. The [[title song]] of ''Yakeen Ka Safar'' was composed by [[Waqar Ali]], while [[Naseer Turabi]] penned the lyrics. [[Hadiqa Kiani]] performed the [[Original soundtrack|OST]]. The singer returned to Hum TV after singing the OST for the channel's hit drama series ''[[Udaari]]'' in 2016. The OST "Mitti kay Parindey" was composed by [[Syed Suhail Haider]], and its lyrics were written by [[Kashif Anwar]]. [[Richa Sharma (singer)|Richa Sharma]] performed the OST.

== Reception ==
The serial received critical praise, especially for the storyline, cinematography and performances of the star cast.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.dunyanews.tv/18237/|title=Yaqeen Ka Safar was a beautiful journey|date=2017-11-06|website=Dunya News}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.somethinghaute.com/yakeen-ka-safar-concludes-and-heres-our-verdict/?|title=Yakeen Ka Safar concludes and here's our verdict|date=2017-11-02|website=Something Haute|author=Mahwish Zaidi}}</ref> While praising the refreshing storyline without much romantic angle and multiple themes of the series, ''[[The Express Tribune]]'' wrote, "''Yaqeen Ka Safar'' is honest and original, and has changed the paradigm of Pakistani dramas."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/article/59539/yaqeen-ka-safar-is-honest-and-original-and-has-changed-the-paradigm-of-pakistani-dramas?|title=Yaqeen Ka Safar is honest and original, and has changed the paradigm of Pakistani dramas|date=2017-11-04|newspaper=The Express Tribune|access-date=2021-06-13|author=Sadaf Pervez}}</ref> While reviewing positively, Buraq Shabbir of ''[[The News International]]'' said it was more realistic than other serials aired at that time stating, "It views people as professionals while tapping into their personal lives as well, making it more relatable".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/tns/detail/564078-can-pakistani-dramas-move-beyond-domestic-issues|title=Can Pakistani dramas move beyond domestic issues?|date=24 September 2017|author=Buraq Shabbir|work=The News International|access-date=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221005202422/https://www.thenews.com.pk/tns/detail/564078-can-pakistani-dramas-move-beyond-domestic-issues|archive-date=5 October 2022|quote=Aside from this, Yakeen Ka Safar that features Ahad Raza Mir and Sajal Aly as doctors, has a medical angle to it and is more realistic than any other TV serial on air these days. It views people as professionals while tapping into their personal lives as well, making it more relatable.}}</ref> ''[[DAWN Images]]'' praised Mir's complex and nuanced portrayal of Dr. Asfandyar.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1179037|title=How Yakeen ka Safar's Asfandiyar is the leading man Pakistani dramas desperately needed|date=26 December 2017|work=DAWN Images|access-date=|author=Maria Kari}}</ref>

'''Yasir Hussain''' ({{langx|ur|{{nq|یاسر حسین}}}}) is a Pakistani screenwriter, actor, director, playwright and host from [[Karachi]] best known for his comic roles.<ref>{{cite web|title= Local humour in 'Karachi se Lahore' will make it worth watching |url= https://www.dawn.com/news/1178355 |website=DAWN|date= 27 April 2015 |access-date=1 August 2015}}</ref> He hosted ''[[The After Moon Show]]'' on [[Hum TV]]. He is also known for playing the antagonist in the 2018 social drama ''[[Baandi]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/330573-|title=Yasir Hussain to play antagonist in Baandi|last=Shirazi|first=Maria|website=www.thenews.com.pk|language=en|access-date=2019-02-12}}</ref>

== Early life and family ==
Hussain was born in [[Karachi]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rehman |first=Maliha |date=18 February 2024 |title=THE ICON INTERVIEW: THE IMPERFECT WORLD OF YASIR HUSSAIN |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1814904/the-icon-interview-the-imperfect-world-of-yasir-hussain |website=[[Dawn News]] |quote=“I am a Kashmiri born in Karachi and Punjabi is not my language. I have learnt it through watching Punjabi movies!” he tells me.}}</ref> into a [[Muslim Rajputs|Rajput]] family originally from [[Azad Kashmir]] that moved to [[Rawalpindi]] when he was five.<ref name="yhns">{{cite web |last=Saiyid |first=Dushka |date=8 November 2013 |title=Is Yasir Hussain the New Naseeruddin Shah? |url=https://www.youlinmagazine.com/youth/is-yasir-hussain-the-new-naseeruddin-shah/MTQ= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240101133230/https://www.youlinmagazine.com/youth/is-yasir-hussain-the-new-naseeruddin-shah/MTQ= |archive-date=1 January 2024 |access-date= |website=youlinmagazine.com |quote=His Kashmiri Rajput family is not well disposed to his or his sister’s careers in acting and singing respectively.}}</ref> 

He's the youngest in a family of twelve siblings, including a sister who's a [[Dubai]]-based singer, Schumaila Hussain, and a brother who's a [[scriptwriter]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alam |first=Junaid |date=6 October 2017 |title=Here is what you need to know about the versatile Yasir Hussain |url=https://arydigital.tv/need-know-versatile-yasir-hussain |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240721112937/https://arydigital.tv/need-know-versatile-yasir-hussain |archive-date=21 July 2024 |website=[[ARY Digital]]}}</ref> In recent years, Schumaila has gained attention for singing the OSTs of dramas ''[[Muqabil]]'' (2016) and ''[[Khamoshi (TV series)|Khamoshi]]'' (2017-2018) while she has also done works for [[Lollywood]] and [[Hindi cinema|Bollywood]].<ref>Sadiq Saleem (31 March 2018), [https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/299018- "Introducing Schumaila Hussain"], ''[[The News International]]''. Retrieved 20 October 2018.</ref>

== Career ==

=== Theatre ===
Hussain remains associated with Kopycats Production as they produced some of the great plays for theatre which were written by [[Anwar Maqsood]] like ''Half Plate'', ''Pawney 14 August'', ''Sawa 14 August'' and ''Saichin'' and the most popular ''[[Aangan Terha]]'' in which Yasir Hussain played the role of Akbar which was originally played by [[Salim Nasir]].<ref name="yhns" /><ref>{{cite web|title= I want to make writers become stars in Pakistan |url= http://tns.thenews.com.pk/want-make-writers-become-stars-pakistan/#.VbzeKXgcBAg |website=TNS – The News on Sunday|access-date=1 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=27 January 2019 |title=Yasir Hussain back to theatre with Aangan Terha's sequel "Naach Na Jaanay" |url=https://style.pk/yasir-hussain-back-to-theatre-with-aangan-terhas-sequel-naach-na-jaanay/}}</ref>

=== Cinema ===
Hussain made his [[Lollywood]] debut as Moti in the film ''[[Karachi Se Lahore]]'' (2015) written by himself and directed by Wajahat Rauf.<ref>{{cite web|title=' Karachi Se Lahore': a long but uneventful journey| url= http://tribune.com.pk/story/929333/k|website=The Express Tribune| date= 30 July 2015 |access-date=1 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title= Pakistani Actress Ayesha Omar's Karachi Se Lahore All Set to Make a Splash in Hollywood |url= http://www.masala.com/make-way-for-ayesha-omar-her-debut-film-karachi-se-lahore-200959.html |website=Masala!|access-date=1 August 2015}}</ref> He reprised his role as Moti in ''[[Lahore Se Aagey]]'' (2016) was a spin-off to ''Karachi Se Lahore'' and was released on 11 November 2016.

=== Television ===
Hussain has acted in television serials including sitcom ''[[Coke Kahani]]'' (2012) and drama serial ''[[Dareecha]]'' (2011-2012).<ref>{{cite web|title= Syed Yasir Hussain the all-rounder is here to stay |url= http://www.magtheweekly.com/13-19june2015/interview3.asp |website= MG The Weekly |access-date=1 August 2015}}</ref> He appeared in multiple telefilms and a drama serial ''Shaadi Mubarak Ho'' (2017), opposite [[Kubra Khan]], directed by Wajahat Rauf and written by Yasir Hussain himself.<ref>{{cite web |title=Shadi Mubarak Ho Drama on ARY Digital: Cast, Promo, OST & Timings |date=29 June 2017 |url=https://www.brandsynario.com/shadi-mubarak-ho-drama-ary-digital-cast-promo-ost-timings/ |publisher=Ghazala Sulaiman |access-date=29 June 2017}}</ref> 

He has been noted for his role as an antagonist in drama serial ''[[Baandi]]'' (2018-2019).<ref>Sabeeh, Maheen. (2018-11-06) [https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/330573- Yasir Hussain to play antagonist in Baandi]. Thenews.com.pk. Retrieved on 2019-08-12.</ref>

He made his directorial debut with the drama serial ''[[Koyal (TV series)|Koyal]]'' (2021-2022).<ref>{{cite web |date=2021-07-29 |title=Yasir Hussain spills the beans on his directorial debut |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1188100 |access-date=2021-11-04 |website=IMAGES}}</ref>

=== Host ===
Beginning in 2018, Hussain hosted two seasons of ''[[The After Moon Show]]''.<ref>[https://www.facebook.com/TheAftermoonShow/ The Aftermoon Show with Yasir – Home]. Facebook. Retrieved on 2019-08-12.</ref>
== Personal life ==
Yasir Hussain publicly proposed to TV actress [[Iqra Aziz]] at the [[Lux Style Awards]].<ref>[https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/495170 Yasir Hussain proposes to Iqra Aziz at Lux Style Awards 2019, the actress says]. thenews.com.pk (2019-07-08). Retrieved on 2019-08-12.</ref><ref>[https://www.geo.tv/latest/242495 Yasir Hussain proposes to Iqra Aziz at Lux Style Awards 2019 | Entertainment]. Geo.tv (2019-07-08). Retrieved on 2019-08-12.</ref><ref>[https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/495568 Who won at the mega Lux Style Awards 2019? | Entertainment]. thenews.com.pk (2019-07-08). Retrieved on 2019-08-12. == Controversies ==

=== Jokes about Pathans ===
Yasir Hussain has received criticism from [[Pashtuns|Pathan]] community for mocking their language [[Pashto]] and trying to elicit racist responses from audiences toward [[Pathan jokes]].<ref>[https://images.dawn.com/news/1177517 Yasir Hussain's terrible Hum Awards joke is proof desi comedians need a reality check – Comment – Images]. Images.dawn.com. Retrieved on 2019-08-12.</ref>

=== Comments about Turkish actors ===
Yasir Hussain was also criticized for his unwelcoming attitude towards Turkish actors and actresses when they came to act in Pakistani ads. He got trolled on every post for his fights but some celebrities agreed he was being bullied and the trolling was getting too much.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-07-16|title=Armeena Khan says Yasir Hussain is being bullied, Twitter disagrees|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/2255125/a|access-date=2020-08-02|website=The Express Tribune|language=en}}</ref>

'''Zaheen Tahira''' (1931 – 9 July 2019) was a [[Pakistani]] [[film]] and [[television]] [[actress]], [[Film producer|producer]] and [[Film director|director]]. She also worked for [[Radio Pakistan]] and on stage.<ref name=Dawn/><ref name="memory">{{Cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1495290|title=IN MEMORIAM: FAREWELL TO ZAHEEN APA|date=21 July 2019|work=dawn|access-date=}}</ref>

==Early life ==
She was born in 1931 in [[Lucknow]], [[British India]].<ref name="auto"/><ref name="auto1"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fp.brecorder.com/2019/06/20190628492299/|title=Veteran actress Zaheen Tahira passes away|date=9 July 2019|website=Business Recorder}}</ref> According to some sources, she was born in 1935.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2001506/4-zaheen-tahira-passes-away-karachi/|title=Veteran TV actor Zaheen Tahira passes away in Karachi|date=9 July 2019|website=The Express Tribune}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1183221|title=Veteran actor Zaheen Tahira passes away at 79|date=9 July 2019|website=Dawn}}</ref>

==Career==
She was considered one of the most senior and veteran actresses in Pakistan television history.<ref name="memory"/> She dominated the TV screens in the late 1960s, 1970s and 1980s by portraying strong characters mainly on dramas produced by [[Pakistan Television Corporation]] (PTV) [[Karachi]] centre. She appeared in over 700 drama serials in lead and supporting roles. She also produced and directed a few television series. She played the lead role in Pakistan's record-breaking serial [[Khuda Ki Basti (serial)|Khuda Ki Basti]] based on the [[Khuda Ki Basti (novel)|novel of the same name]] by [[Shaukat Siddiqui]].

In 2013, the [[President of Pakistan]] awarded her the [[Tamgha-e-Imtiaz]] (Medal of Distinction) in recognition of her work in the Pakistani entertainment industry.<ref name=TheNation/>

==Illness and death ==
Tahira was admitted to [[Aga Khan University Hospital, Karachi|Aga Khan University Hospital]] in [[Karachi]] after suffering a major cardiac arrest on 23 June 2019. On 27 June 2019 she was shifted to the [[Coronary care unit|CCU]] from [[Intensive care unit|ICU]]. Her son Kamran Khan said that "Mum is hospitalized. she is getting better now, By evening they will remove the [[Medical ventilator|ventilator]]."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://jang.com.pk/news/653650-zaheen-tahiras-son-said-she-is-alive|title=''ذہین طاہرہ زندہ ہیں''، بیٹے نے موت کی افواہوں کی تردید کر دی|language=ur-PK|website=jang.com.pk}}</ref> Her grandson Danial Shahzad Khan said that "Zaheen Tahira is very much alive and is currently admitted in the coronary care unit."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/241605-zaheen-tahiras-grandson-rubbishes-rumours-of-actors-death|title=Zaheen Tahira's grandson rubbishes rumours of actor's death|website=geo.tv}}</ref>

Zaheen Tahira died in [[Karachi]] on 9 July 2019 around 9:30 am.<ref>[https://www.samaa.tv/news/2019/07/pakistani-actor-zaheen-tahira-passes-away/ Pakistani actor Zaheen Tahira passes away], ''Samaa Tv'', 9 July 2019</ref>

'''Zee Zindagi''' (also known as '''Zindagi TV''') is an Indian general entertainment channel, owned by the [[Zee Entertainment Enterprises]] (ZEEL).<ref name="tvc">{{cite web|url=http://www.zeenews.india.com/entertainment/idiotbox/coming-up-new-hindi-channel-zindagi-june-23_155247.html|title=New Hindi channel Zindagi|publisher=[[Zee News]]|date=19 May 2014|access-date=28 May 2014|archive-date=26 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626112704/http://zeenews.india.com/entertainment/idiotbox/coming-up-new-hindi-channel-zindagi-june-23_155247.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> It also promoted itself as a television channel broadcasting short-run programming and as India's new Hindi entertainment channel, rather than on-going, indefinite serials.<ref name="cb">{{cite news|title=Bye-bye unending television dramas, welcome Zindagi|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/tv/news/Bye-bye-unending-television-dramas-welcome-Zindagi/articleshow/37520651.cms|access-date=14 July 2014|work=The Times of India|date=1 July 2014}}</ref>

It has syndicated content from various countries including [[Brazil]], [[Pakistan]], [[South Korea]], [[Turkey]] and [[Ukraine]].<ref name=znd>{{cite web|title=5 reasons that make Zee's new channel 'Zindagi' a must-watch|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/entertainment/report-5-reasons-that-make-zee-s-new-channel-zindagi-a-must-watch-1996891|website=DNA India|access-date=14 July 2014|date=20 June 2014}}</ref><ref name=z>{{cite web|title=Pakistani TV shows to be back on Indian small screen|publisher=India Today|access-date=14 July 2014|date=4 June 2014|url=https://www.indiatoday.in/television/top-stories/story/pakistani-tv-shows-dhoop-kinare-tanhaiyaan-ankahi-indian-small-screen-195628-2014-06-04}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url = http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/zee-eyes-positive-returns-from-new-channel-zindagi-114061701123_1.html|title =Zindagi to launch new shows from the Muslim World|journal =Business Standard India|date = 17 June 2014|access-date = 9 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/money/report-zee-eyes-bigger-gec-market-share-with-new-channel-zindagi-1989576|title=Zee eyes bigger GEC market share with new channel 'Zindagi'|publisher=DNA India|date=19 May 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/entertainment/report-zindagi-channel-announces-total-dreamer-its-first-show-from-brazil-2360200|title=Zindagi channel announces 'Total Dreamer' - its FIRST show from Brazil|publisher=DNA India|date=20 March 2017}}</ref> It launched on 23 June 2014, ZEEL invested {{Indian rupee}}100 crores to launch the network.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/zee-entertainment-earmarks-100-cr-for-new-channel/article6034139.ece|title=Zee Entertainment earmarks 100 crores for new channel|work=The Hindu|date=21 May 2014}}</ref> Zindagi's shows ''[[Dhoop Ki Deewar]]'' and ''[[Qatil Haseenaon Ke Naam]]'' won big at [[Promax Awards|Promax]] 2022 Awards.

==History==
Its syndicated Pakistani [[soap opera]], ''[[Aunn Zara]]'', premiered on 23 June 2014, the day the channel was launched and ended its run on Zindagi on 12 July 2014,<ref name="dg">{{cite web|title='Aunn Zara', Zindagi's refreshing love story draws for a season closure today|url=http://www.dnaindia.com/entertainment/report-aunn-zara-zindagi-s-refreshing-love-story-draws-for-a-season-closure-today-2001638|publisher=dnaindia|access-date=14 July 2014|date=2014-07-12}}</ref> thus, making Zindagi the first Hindi general entertainment channel in India, to end a show in 20 days.<ref name="gh">{{cite news|title=Zindagi: New TV channel keeps its promise of new shows every month|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/tv/news/Zindagi-New-TV-channel-keeps-its-promise-of-new-shows-every-month/articleshow/38269631.cms|access-date=14 July 2014|publisher=Times of India|date=13 July 2014}}</ref> In early-May 2015, Zindagi for the first time in its history launched two lifestyle shows of [[United States|American]] origin, dubbed in Hindi. They were ''Simply Beautiful'', a health and beauty tips show hosted by Roni Proter, and ''[[Nirmala's Spice World]]'', a cookery show hosted by Chef Nirmala Narine.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.afaqs.com/news/story/44068_Zindagi-opens-afternoon-band-with-new-shows | title=Zindagi opens afternoon band with new shows | publisher=afaqs! | date=1 May 2015 | access-date=10 August 2015}}</ref> The channel also launched its first original Indian production, ''Shukriya'', a reality show, in early-August 2015. ''Shukriya'' provides a platform for common people to come on television, share their personal stories, and say 'thank you' to their dear and loved ones.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/tv/news/hindi/Indian-production-on-Zindagi-channel-soon/articleshow/47734398.cms | title=Indian production on Zindagi channel soon | work=The Times of India | date=19 July 2015 | access-date=10 August 2015 | author=IANS}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.indiawest.com/entertainment/television/zindagi-launches-non-fiction-show-shukriya-on-gratitude/article_5e5efef4-3baf-11e5-8cbf-6b36e0453cf8.html | title=Zindagi Launches Non-fiction Show 'Shukriya' on Gratitude | publisher=India West | date=5 August 2015 | access-date=10 August 2015 | archive-date=9 August 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150809001353/http://www.indiawest.com/entertainment/television/zindagi-launches-non-fiction-show-shukriya-on-gratitude/article_5e5efef4-3baf-11e5-8cbf-6b36e0453cf8.html | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.indiantelevision.com/television/tv-channels/gecs/zindagi-forays-into-original-non-fiction-programming-with-shukriya-150805 | title=Zindagi forays into original non-fiction programming with 'Shukriya' | publisher=indiantelevision.com | date=5 August 2015 | access-date=10 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.hindustantimes.com/television/tv-show-shukriya-explores-uncommon-relations-of-common-people/article1-1377565.aspx | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150814012346/http://www.hindustantimes.com/television/tv-show-shukriya-explores-uncommon-relations-of-common-people/article1-1377565.aspx | url-status=dead | archive-date=14 August 2015 | title=TV show Shukriya explores uncommon relations of common people | publisher=Hindustan Times | date=7 August 2015 | access-date=10 August 2015}}</ref> Zindagi also formed a partnership with [[BIG FM 92.7]] for seven weeks, starting on 27 July 2015 (nearly two weeks before ''Shukriya'''s launch), to promote ''Shukriya'' through the radio using various methods, programmes, and special segments. This promotion on BIG FM spanned across its 24 radio stations based in various cities of India.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.radioandmusic.com/biz/radio/private-fm-stations/zindagi-partners-big-fm-give-its-listeners-unique-shukriya-experience-150730 | title=Zindagi Partners with BIG FM to Give its Listeners a Unique 'Shukriya' Experience | date=30 July 2015 | access-date=10 August 2015}}</ref>

Following the [[2016 Uri terror attack]], Zindagi removed all Pakistani shows from their line up.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.india.com/showbiz/zee-channel-zindagi-removes-pakistan-shows-announces-new-line-up-starting-october-3-1521365/|title=Zee channel Zindagi removes Pakistan shows, announces new line-up starting October 3!|publisher=India Today|date=29 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/entertainment/television/new-line-up-on-zindagi-has-no-pakistani-serials-3053535/|title=New Line Up On Zindagi has no Pakistani serials|publisher=Indian Express|date=29 September 2016}}</ref>

Zindagi became a digital only channel starting from 1 July 2017, with the content becoming accessible only on [[OZEE]] app.<ref name=channel>{{cite web|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/zee-moves-premium-hindi-channel-zindagi-to-vod-platform-ozee/article9718405.ece |title=Zee to shutdown Zindagi from 1st July and to move the content to VoD platform OZEE|date=2 June 2017|publisher=The Hindu Business Line}}</ref>

With the launch of [[ZEE5]], Zindagi has been rebranded as [[List of programmes broadcast by Zindagi TV|Zindagi Digital]] and streams digital exclusive international shows from Turkey, South Korea, Spain, Colombia, Ukraine, Pakistan, Brazil etc. in 12 major languages starting 15 February 2018. 
All content is accessible on [[ZEE5]] app with premium membership<ref name=televisionpost>{{cite web|url=http://www.televisionpost.com/zeel-launches-vod-platform-zee5-premium-offering-priced-at-rs-99-per-month/|title=ZEEL launches VoD platform ZEE5; premium offering priced at Rs 99 per month – TelevisionPost|website=www.televisionpost.com|access-date=17 February 2018|archive-date=17 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180217024033/http://www.televisionpost.com/zeel-launches-vod-platform-zee5-premium-offering-priced-at-rs-99-per-month/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 16 July 2020 it was announced that, Zindagi channel is relaunching on [[ZEE5]]. A channel new tagline is "Zindagi Mil Ke Jiyenge".<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-07-17|title=Zindagi TV Shows Return on Zee5; Here Are The Pakistani Series You Can Watch on the Streaming Platform {{!}} 📺 LatestLY|url=https://www.latestly.com/entertainment/tv/zindagi-tv-shows-return-on-zee5-here-are-the-pakistani-shows-you-can-watch-on-the-streaming-platform-1896193.html|access-date=2020-07-19|website=LatestLY|language=en}}</ref> The Zindagi brand was launched on 21 May 2020 worldwide excluding India and on 27 May 2020 in India on ZEE5 app.<ref>{{Cite web|title=ZEE Entertainment brings back content brand Zindagi on ZEE5 - Exchange4media|url=https://www.exchange4media.com/digital-news/zee-entertainment-brings-back-content-brand-zindagi-on-zee5-106176.html|access-date=2020-07-19|website=Indian Advertising Media & Marketing News – exchange4media|language=en}}</ref>

On 4 September 2020, [[Shailja Kejriwal]], Chief creative officer- special projects Zee Entertainment Enterprises announced there were no plans for Zindagi channel to return on a television platform. All content is for [[ZEE5]] app only.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Zindagi, the channel that brought Pakistani shows to us, has gone digital|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/entertainment/zindagi-the-channel-that-brought-pakistani-shows-to-us-has-gone-digital/cid/1790958|access-date=2020-10-06|website=www.telegraphindia.com}}</ref>

Zindagi launched ''[[Dhoop Ki Deewar]]'' on 25 June 2021 starring Sajal Aly and Ahad Raza Mir. The show highlights the grief and loss war brings to people no matter which side of the border they are from.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Want to tell stories beyond the headlines – Shailja Kejriwal|url=https://thelucknowtribune.com/want-to-tell-stories-beyond-the-headlines-shailja-kejriwal/|access-date=2022-08-10|website=Lucknow Tribune|archive-date=15 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220915052608/https://thelucknowtribune.com/want-to-tell-stories-beyond-the-headlines-shailja-kejriwal/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 15 March 2021, Shailja Kejriwal, Chief Creative Officer (Special Projects) Zee Entertainment made another announcement related to Zindagi channel by saying "The new avatar of Zindagi not just has acquired content from the subcontinent, but also original shows produced in Pakistan and Bangladesh. Zindagi would produce 6-7 original shows every year and a large part would consist of content from neighbouring countries such as Pakistan and Bangladesh."<ref>{{Cite web|title=With a blend of Indian, Pakistani, Bangladeshi shows, ZEE5 to position itself as South Asian content platform|url=https://www.businesstoday.in/current/corporate/with-a-blend-of-indian-pakistani-bangladeshi-shows-zee5-to-position-itself-as-south-asian-content-platform/story/433919.html|access-date=2021-03-30|website=www.businesstoday.in}}</ref>

On 16 March 2022, Shailja Kejriwal, Chief Creative Officer (Special Projects) Zee Entertainment Enterprises hinted that in 2022 Zindagi channel will get back on television for its loyal audience.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2022-03-16 |title=Hope 2022 will see Zindagi also going back to its loyal TV audience: Zee's Shailja Kejriwal |url=https://indiantelevision.com/television/tv-channels/viewership/hopeful-of-going-back-to-zindagi-s-loyal-audiences-on-tv-in-2022-zee-s-shailja-kejriwal-220316 |access-date=2022-04-03 |website=Indian Television Dot Com |language=en}}</ref>

From 23 May 2022, Zindagi channel launched as a DTH active services on Tata Play, Dish TV, D2H and Airtel Digital TV. On Tata Play it was launched as a Tata Play Zindagi, as Zindagi Special on Airtel Digital TV and on Dish TV as well as d2h as Zindagi Active.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-23 |title=Zindagi channel to launch on Indian TV as DTH offering with Pakistani show Zindagi Gulzar Hai, among other series |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/tv/zindagi-channel-to-launch-on-indian-tv-as-dth-offering-with-pakistani-show-zindagi-gulzar-hai-among-other-series-101653287670901.html |access-date=2022-05-23 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>

Since 1 May 2025, Pakistani YouTube channels are inaccessible in India such as HUM TV, ARY Digital, Har Pal Geo, etc. and its content is unavailable citing an order from the government related to national security. Followed by this ZEE '''Zindagi''' has been removed its all Zindagi Original shows from [[ZEE5]] and YouTube along with its DTH counterpart started airing Indian shows from his library amid India-Pakistan tension.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chakraborty |first=Debdutta |date=2025-04-30 |title=Hania Amir to Ali Zafar, Pakistani celebrities go off Indian Instagram after 'legal request' |url=https://theprint.in/go-to-pakistan/pakistani-celebrities-instagram-banned-in-india/2610466/ |access-date=2025-06-23 |website=ThePrint |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-01 |title=India bans popular Pakistani drama channels on YouTube following Pahalgam terror attack |url=https://www.etnownews.com/entertainment/india-bans-popular-pakistani-drama-channels-on-youtube-following-pahalgam-terror-attack-article-151546032 |access-date=2025-06-23 |website=ET Now |language=en}}</ref>

'''ARY Digital Network''' ({{langx|ur|{{Nastaliq|ARY ڈیجیٹل شبکه}}}}) is a subsidiary of the ARY Group. The ARY group of companies is a [[Dubai]]-based holding company founded by a Pakistani businessman, Haji Abdul Razzak Yaqoob and Salman Iqbal (ARY). The network has a video on demand streaming service called [[ARY PLUS]], formerly known as [[ARY ZAP]].

== History ==
ARY Digital, formerly known as the Pakistani Channel, was launched in the United Kingdom in December 2000 to cater to the growing demands of South Asian entertainment in the region.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://profit.pakistantoday.com.pk/2020/08/08/the-shady-rise-and-rise-of-ary-group/|title=The ARY story: How a keen mid-tier trading family became one of the most powerful conglomerates of Pakistan|first2=Ariba |last2=Shahid |first1=Abdullah|last1=Niazi|date=8 August 2020|website=Profit by Pakistan Today}}</ref> It uses Samacom, a monopolising uplink provider based in the UAE, as the uplink teleport station.<ref name="CITEREFSamacom1">{{cite web|url=http://www.samacom.com/teleport.htm|title=Teleport|publisher=Samacom|access-date=2008-05-11| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080506164425/http://www.samacom.com/teleport.htm| archive-date= 6 May 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref>

===Affiliate programming===
Recently ARY Digital has affiliated with several other television networks to promote their content in Pakistan. Amongst these are [[Fashion TV]] for which a regional channel [[Fashion TV#Pakistan|FTV Pakistan]] has been airing since December 2005 on the ARY Digital network. Plans are under way for [[Al Jazeera Urdu]] in affiliation with Al Jazeera targeting 110 million Urdu-speaking households worldwide<ref name="CITEREFAMEInfo1">{{cite web|url=http://www.ameinfo.com/76550.html |title=Aljazeera and ARY Digital Network to launch Aljazeera Urdu |publisher=AME Info Middle East |access-date=2008-05-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080511025232/http://www.ameinfo.com/76550.html |archive-date=11 May 2008 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and [[HBO Asia#HBO South Asia|HBO Pakistan]]<ref name="CITEREFMOFAPak1">{{cite web|url=http://www.mofa.gov.pk/pages/Basic_Facts.htm|title=Basic Facts|publisher=Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan|access-date=2008-05-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080516072110/http://www.mofa.gov.pk/Pages/Basic_Facts.htm|archive-date=16 May 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> in association with [[HBO]]'s south-Asian division. With the network's help, [[Nickelodeon (TV Channel)|Nickelodeon]] is also planning to kick-start its operations in Nick Pakistan where it would be beamed into 2.5 million households with kids.<ref name="CITEREFAnimMag1">{{cite web
|url=http://www.animationmagazine.net/article.php?article_id=6170|title=Nick, MTV Travel to Pakistan|publisher=Animation Magazine
}}</ref>

==ARY films==
{{Main|ARY Films}}
ARY Films is film distribution company running in Pakistan. It's a part of ARY Digital Network. Thirty five films including 11 [[Urdu]], 6 [[Punjabi language|Punjabi]] and 17 [[Pashto language|Pashto]] films were released by ARY Films in 2013. Among them ''[[Waar]]'', ''[[Main Hoon Shahid Afridi]]'', ''[[Josh: Independence Through Unity|Josh]]'', ''[[Chambaili]]'', ''[[Zinda Bhaag]]'', ''[[Siyaah]]'' and ''[[Seedlings (film)|Lamha]]'' top the charts in industry.<ref>{{cite web|title=ARY Films Rules the Roost in Pakistani Cinema|url=http://arynews.tv/en/2013-ary-films-rules-the-roost-in-pakistani-cinema/|publisher=ARY News|date=31 December 2013|access-date=28 May 2014}}</ref>

==ARY Media Advisory Board==
At the turn of events leading to the emergency in December 2007, Salman Iqbal, CEO of the network announced along with the ARY Digital network committee the establishment of a media advisory board, the purpose of which would be to assess the media coverage (be it news or other programmes) on the network. Saying that ARY Digital has been reporting without bias for a while but the recent events ushering the emergency rule and temporary closure of one of the biggest news network Geo TV, ARY Digital required a better unbiased coverage. He concluded that an array of government leaders could weigh the coverage presented by the network on the basis of its rationality and coverage so that the media portrayed by the network was in verse with the way Pakistan is supposed to be imaged. The board would have seats for 20 members, each focusing on different aspects of media would provide their views on how media should be portrayed.<ref name="CITEREFYoutubeMAB1">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xAV5KlZbhbw |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211222/xAV5KlZbhbw |archive-date=2021-12-22 |url-status=live|title=ARY Digital Network announces Media Advisory Board|publisher=[[YouTube]]|access-date=2008-05-12}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

==Criticism==
For a brief period in 2003, ARY Digital received criticism upon its airing of a prisoner's derogatory comments against the Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC-3) and a video showing balded young girls behind bars begging for mercy. The contempt of court proceedings against the officials of the network were withdrawn after the judge accepted unconditional apologies.<ref name="CITEREFARYDawn1">{{cite web|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/114927/karachi-contempt-proceedings-withdrawn-against-ary|title=KARACHI: Contempt proceedings withdrawn against ARY|publisher=[[Dawn (newspaper)|DAWN Newspaper]]|access-date=2008-05-12}}</ref>

An attempted takeover of BOL Network and [[BOL News]] took place in August 2015, carried out by ARY Digital Network [[CEO]] [[Salman Iqbal]], who said that the decision was taken in view to provide career protection to media industry and its workers.<ref>{{cite news|title=ARY CEO and Founder Salman Iqbal takes over BOL Network management — says BOL will be launched in three weeks|url=http://arynews.tv/en/ary-ceo-salman-iqbal-takes-over-bol-network-management-says-bol-will-be-launched-in-three-weeks|access-date=19 August 2015|agency=ARYNEWS.tv|publisher=ARY SERVICES LTD UK.|date=19 August 2015|archive-date=21 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150821083055/http://arynews.tv/en/ary-ceo-salman-iqbal-takes-over-bol-network-management-says-bol-will-be-launched-in-three-weeks|url-status=dead}}</ref> ARY Group founder Salman Iqbal said that his media group would launch the transmission of the channel within three weeks.<ref>{{cite news|title=ARY announces Bol TV takeover|url=http://tribune.com.pk/story/940302/ary-announces-bol-tv-takeover/|access-date=19 August 2015|agency=The Express Tribune News Network|publisher=Web Desk|date=18 August 2015}}</ref> However this deal fell through and in September 2015 it was announced that ARY was not taking over BOL.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bol TV Deal Over|url=http://arynews.tv/en/bol-network-deal-no-more//ary-bol-tv-deal-over/|agency=ARY News|publisher=Web Desk}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

'''''ARY News HD''''' ({{langx|ur|{{Nastaliq|ARY نیوز}}}}) is a Pakistani news channel launched on December 2003 with the name "ARY One World", the channel was later renamed to "ARY One World" until May 2009 when it was rebranded as "ARY News". A bilingual [[news channel]] in English and [[Urdu]], it is a part of the [[ARY Digital Network]], which is a subsidiary of ARY Group. ARY is an acronym of [[Abdul Razzak Yaqoob]] and [[Salman Iqbal]], who was the owner of ARY Group. ARY head office located in [[Karachi]], [[Pakistan]].

'''Agha Sikandar''' was a Pakistani television and film actor.<ref name=DawnNews/> He appeared in classic dramas ''[[Waris (serial)|Waris]]'' and ''[[Dehleez (1981 TV series)|Dehleez]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/tns/detail/834364-stay-indoors-relive-the-classics|title=Stay indoors, relive the classics|website=The News International|date=20 August 2021}}</ref><ref name=DawnNews/> He also appeared in Urdu and Punjabi films ''[[Mian Biwi Razi]]'', ''Faslay'' and ''[[Jatt Te Dogar]]''.<ref name=DawnNews/>

==Early life==
Agha was born in 1954 in [[Lahore]], Pakistan and completed his studies at the [[University of Lahore]].<ref name=DawnNews>{{cite web|title=Crazy Diamonds – III|url=https://www.dawn.com/news/767605/crazy-diamonds-iii|website=Dawn News|date=29 November 2012 |access-date=8 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150821042012/http://www.dawn.com/news/767605/crazy-diamonds-iii|archive-date=21 August 2015|url-status=live}}</ref>

Agha's father Agha Saleem Raza (d. 1965) was an actor in Urdu and Punjabi cinema, mainly known for his roles as villain during the 30s and 40s.

==Career==
Agha was interested in acting and made his debut as an actor in late 1970s on PTV dramas and he did a number of roles in dramas in the late 1970s.<ref>{{cite web|title=List of PTV Old Actors|url=https://www.ptvold.com/p/list-of-actors.html|website=Pakistan Television Corporation|access-date=24 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190414193119/https://www.ptvold.com/p/list-of-actors.html|archive-date=14 April 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=DawnNews/><ref>{{cite web|title=Agha Sikandar|url=http://vidpk.com/p/807/Agha-Sikandar|access-date=22 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121203235929/http://vidpk.com/p/807/Agha-Sikandar|archive-date=3 December 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> He appeared in the [[Amjad Islam Amjad]] drama ''[[Waris (serial)|Waris]]'' as Farrukh, the emotional son of a widow, in a role that was a massive hit. Agha then appeared in philosophical telefilm written by [[Ashfaq Ahmed]] called ''Cinderella Aur Sakina'' with [[Saba Hameed]].<ref name=DawnNews/><ref>{{cite book|title=South and Southeast Asia Video Archive Holdings, Issue 5|publisher=Madison, WI : General Library System, University of Wisconsin--Madison|page=82}}</ref> Then in 1981 he appeared in drama ''[[Dehleez (1981 TV series)|Dehleez]]'' as Abid Khan a villain role which was also written by Amjad Islam Amjad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dailypakistan.com.pk/02-Jun-2016/391143|title=ادکارہ طاہرہ نقوی کی34 ویں برسی آج منائی جائے گی|website=Daily Pakistan|date=14 June 2021}}</ref> Agha also appeared in films and he was offered many films from filmmakers.<ref name=DawnNews/><ref>{{cite book|title=Newsletter - Afghanistan Council, Volumes 8-10|publisher=New York, Asia Society|page=8}}</ref>

In 1981 Agha appeared in film ''Faslay'' with famous actress [[Shabnam]] and actor [[Muhammad Ali (actor)|Muhammad Ali]] which was a Silver Jubilee.<ref name=OxfordUniversityPress>{{cite book |last=Gazdar |first=Mushtaq |author-link=Mushtaq Gazdar |year=1997 |title=Pakistan Cinema, 1947-1997 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=0-19-577817-0}}</ref> The following year, he appeared in film ''[[Mian Biwi Razi]]'' with actresses [[Kaveeta]], [[Tahira Naqvi]] and actor [[Nadeem Baig (actor)|Nadeem Baig]] which was box-office hit in which he did a comic role with alongside [[Sangeeta (Pakistani actress)|Sangeeta]].<ref name=DawnNews/> Agha was offered more offers from directors, they saw him to be a natural romantic hero.<ref name=DawnNews/> In 1983, he appeared in film ''[[Jatt Te Dogar]]'' with [[Sultan Rahi]], [[Mustafa Qureshi]], [[Adeeb]] and [[Bahar Begum]].<ref name=DawnNews/> Agha was known as an emotionally fragile and romantic person and he usually did the roles of characters which were emotional and fragile in dramas quite close to his life.<ref name=DawnNews/>

When Pakistan Urdu Cinema fell into decline and was replaced by Punjabi films, he felt emotional due to some problems, and his output in both dramas and films began to decline in 1985.<ref name=DawnNews/>

Agha became addicted to heroin which made him even more unpredictable and emotionally fragile.<ref name=DawnNews/> He was sent to rehabilitation to recover but he was in and out on numerous occasions.<ref name=DawnNews/> Agha tried to rekindle the fame he had between the 1970s and 1990s, he couldn't find any acting offers, which drove him into depression.<ref name=DawnNews/>

He completely disappeared from television in early 1993 as his heroin addiction worsened. Agha was emotionally battered, haunted and taunted by his addiction and failing to come to terms with the loss of friends and the fame he once had.<ref name=DawnNews/>

In 1993, Agha was found dead which was announced and according to his contemporaries he had utilised only a small portion of the talent.<ref name=DawnNews/>

==Personal life==
Agha married Rubina, the daughter of actor [[Inayat Hussain Bhatti]] and Shahida Bano.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/14-Dec-2018/agha-ali-talks-about-his-dad-in-a-candid-conversation-with-samina-peerzada|title=Agha Ali talks about his dad in a candid conversation with Samina Peerzada|website=Daily Pakistan|date=23 January 2021}}</ref>

Agha's sons [[Aagha Ali]] and Ali Sikandar are both actors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://propakistani.pk/lens/pakistani-actors-who-are-following-in-their-fathers-footsteps-pictures|title=Pakistani Actors Who Are Following In Their Fathers Footsteps|website=Pro Pakistan|date=11 April 2021}}</ref>

Agha's son Agha Ali was married to actress [[Hina Altaf]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://propakistani.pk/lens/hina-altaf-and-aagha-ali-abbas-make-an-elegant-appearance-together|title=Hina Altaf and Aagha Ali Abbas Make an Elegant Appearance Together|website=Pro Pakistan|date=8 July 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |author=<!-- Staff writer(s); no by-line --> |date=2024-12-18 |title=Actor Agha Ali opens up about divorce from Hina Altaf {{!}} The Express Tribune |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2516870/actor-agha-ali-opens-up-about-divorce-from-hina-altaf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260114133959/https://tribune.com.pk/story/2516870/actor-agha-ali-opens-up-about-divorce-from-hina-altaf |archive-date=2026-01-14 |access-date=2026-07-20 |work=The Express Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Illness and death==
Agha died of a heroin overdose on 25 May 1993 in [[Lahore]]. He was 38 years old. Although some of his co-stars initially suspected that he died from a heart attack, it was later revealed he had overdosed. He was laid to rest at [[Mominpura Graveyard|Mominpura Cemetery]] in Lahore.<ref name=DawnNews/>

'''''Benaam''''' ({{langx|ur|{{nq|بےنام}}|lit=Nameless}}) is a Pakistani television family [[soap opera|soap series]] that originally aired on [[ARY Digital]] from 2 November 2021 to 2 January 2022. It is produced by [[Humayun Saeed]] and Shahzad Nasib under [[Six Sigma Plus]]. It stars [[Komal Meer]], [[Noor Hassan Rizvi]], [[Anoushay Abbasi]], [[Shazeal Shoukat]], [[Babar Ali]], [[Nadia Hussain]], [[Imran Aslam (actor)|Imran Aslam]] and [[Saad Qureshi (actor)|Saad Qureshi]] in lead roles. The story revolves around the ill treatment and hardships faced by twin sisters Aiza and Aimal, who lives with their step-father despite having a real father, who left them before they were born.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=15 January 2022|url=https://dnd.com.pk/best-dramas-on-ary-digital/257809|title=Best Dramas on ARY Digital from 2021 to 2022|work=dispatch news desk|date=16 November 2021 }}</ref>

'''''Bhool''''' ({{langx|ur|{{nq|بھول}}|lit=Mistake}}) previously titled '''''Daag'''''<ref name=news2/><ref name=news/> is a 2019 Pakistani television series created by Abdullah Seja under their production house Idream Entertainment. It stars [[Saheefa Jabbar Khattak]], [[Affan Waheed]] and [[Saboor Ali]].<ref name=news2>{{Cite web|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1182171|title=Saheefa Jabbar is playing an older woman in her next TV serial Daag|last=Haq|first=Irfan Ul|date=2019-03-26|website=Dawn News|language=en|access-date=2019-05-01}}</ref><ref name=news>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/magazine/instep-today/449397-saheefa-jabbar-to-play-saboor-alys-mother-in-her-next-daag|title=Saheefa Jabbar to play Saboor Aly's mother in her next, Daag|last=Shirazi|first=Maria|website=The News International|language=en|access-date=2019-05-01}}</ref> Two episodes of the show are aired every Wednesday on [[ARY Digital]]. It ended on 16 October 2019, having completed 32 episodes.

==Plot==
The drama revolves around the harsh reality of a society that neither forgives nor forgets mistakes made by women. The story of the drama 'Bhool' is all about the protagonist Aiman's mistake and its harsh consequences for her. Aiman falls in love with Awais while studying in college. But her parents engage her with someone else. The situation gets dramatic when on the day of her wedding, Aiman reveals her love but her mother refuses to accept it. In desperation, she flees from home and secretly marries Awais who then keeps the poor girl in a hotel since he is afraid to introduce her to his family. When doing so, Awais's mother refuses to accept the newlywed bride and demands Awais to divorce her. This situation puts Awais in restlessness who too is not happy about the recent developments. Awais obeys his mother and kicks Aiman out from the house, divorcing her.

In her absence, not able to endure the shame inflicted by his daughter, Aiman's father passes away. Aiman then returns home to find her father's death. Since her father had wished to forgive Aiman, both her mother and brother Rashid pardon Aiman, giving her a chance to restart her life. On the other hand, Awais also marries another woman, Raniya.

After some time, Aiman gives birth to a daughter named Aisha. Rashid's efforts go in vain when Awais refuses to accept her daughter. However, knowing the truth about Aiman and Awais's nature, Raniya too gets a divorce from him. After the death of her mother, Aiman's misery aggravates as her bhabhi; Shabana maltreats her though Rashid's attitude towards her is fair. As a result, she leaves home and starts living separately with her daughter.

Time lapses and Aisha is young now. In the absence of a father, she has to endure a bitter societal attitude. However, she does not pay heed to it acting upon her mother's advice. Meanwhile, Awais becomes a victim of the growing repentance and comes to meet his daughter in the university. After that, Aiman reveals the truth to distraught Aisha about her father. Rashid's children; Murad and Nimra are young, too. Aisha becomes the love interest of her university mate; Imran but she hesitates to respond to him knowing the bitter truth about her mother. Aiman, too, fears the same ill-fate for her dear daughter. Aisha's cousin, Nimra is jealous to know the love affair between the two and starts plotting against Aisha in order to marry Imran herself.

In the meantime, Aiman gets the realization that she has got cancer and is rushed to the hospital. Rashid too dies sometime after knowing his sister's illness. Aiman entrusts Awais with the responsibility of taking care of Aisha. Aisha and Imran get married in the hospital. Nimra makes a successful suicidal attempt in desperation knowing Aisha's Nikah. In the end, Aiman too dies due to the fatal disease.
