'''''Taleem-e-Balighan''''' ({{langx|ur|تعلیمِ بالغاں|lit=Education for Adults}}) is a Pakistani social satire television serial<ref name="tribune">[http://tribune.com.pk/story/555732/older-residents-take-a-trip-down-memory-lane-with-taleem-e-balighan-screening/ Older residents take a trip down memory lane with Taleem-e-Balighan screening] ''The Express Tribune'', 29 May 2013. Retrieved 15 January 2020.</ref> that first aired on the [[Pakistan Television Corporation|Pakistan Television Corporation (PTV)]] in 1966. Written by Khawaja Moinuddin, it has been cited by critics as among the classics of [[Pakistani television]].<ref name="Dawn">{{Cite web |last=Ahmad |first=Bisma |date=13 March 2015 |title=Old but not forgotten: Top 10 Pakistani dramas to re-watch now |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1169324 |access-date=30 October 2024 |website=Dawn}}</ref>

==Plot and background==
The series is set in a ''madrassa'' (school) in which illiterate adults receive education in a satirical and humorous setting.<ref name="tribune"/> It draws on [[Muhammad Ali Jinnah]]'s guiding principles of "unity, faith and discipline", a phrase that served as a rallying slogan during the [[Pakistan Movement]] in the 1940s and which is frequently invoked in Pakistani public discourse. The slogan is referenced within the serial in comedic contexts.

The work was originally written for [[Radio Pakistan]] in the 1950s, prior to the introduction of television broadcasting in Pakistan in November 1964. It was subsequently adapted for PTV and first broadcast in 1966.<ref name="tribune"/>

==Cast==
* [[Mahmood Ali]] as Maulvi Sahib, the class teacher
* [[Qazi Wajid]]
* [[Subhani ba Yunus]]
* Qasim Jalali
* Razia Sultana
* Bakhtiar
* [[Agha Nasir]]

==Reception==
The serial brought public attention to questions of adult literacy and education in Pakistan, which have continued to be the subject of discussion.<ref>[http://pakteahouse.net/2012/07/22/taleem-e-balighan-murder-of-history-in-pakistan/ Review and discussion of 'Taleem-e-Balighan' PTV drama on pakteahouse.net]. Retrieved 15 January 2020.</ref>

'''''Tamasha''''' ({{langx|ur|تماشا}}, <abbr>transl.</abbr> "spectacle" or "drama"), also known as '''''Tamasha Ghar''''', is a to [[Television in Pakistan|Pakistani]] Urdu-language television reality show which airs during season run on [[ARY Digital]] and ARY Plus app in Pakistan. It adheres to the popular format of ''[[Big Brother (franchise)|Big Brother]]'', which was first developed by [[Endemol]] and [[Banijay]] in the [[Netherlands]]. The Pakistani version has celebrities as the housemates.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Amena |first=Rasti |date=2024-08-29 |title=Tamasha: Pakistani version of the Bigg Boss and its contestants list |url=https://www.siasat.com/tamasha-pakistani-version-of-bigg-boss-and-its-contestants-list-3086859/ |access-date=2024-09-28 |website=The Siasat Daily |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Narang |first=Gaurvi |date=2022-08-24 |title=Pakistan creates on Salman Khan's Bigg Boss masala with Tamasha Ghar. Of course, viewers love it |url=https://theprint.in/go-to-pakistan/pakistan-creates-salman-khans-bigg-boss-masala-with-tamasha-ghar-of-course-viewers-love-it/1097807/ |access-date=2024-09-28 |website=ThePrint |language=en-US}}</ref>

==''Tamasha'' season 1==
The participants in the order of appearance and entered in house are:
*[[Maira Khan]] – Television actress. She is known for portraying various roles in serials.
*Nigah Jee – Choreographer ( EVICTED: DAY 15)
*Mareeha Safdar – Model and actress.
*Syed Saim Ali – Television and film actor and presenter.
*Faiza Khan – Actress ( EVICTED: DAY 7)
*[[Nouman Javaid]] – Singer. He is known for his songs in the [[Hindi]] film ''[[Jashan]]''.
*Aamna Malick – Television actress.
*Umer Aalam – Television actor and model.
*[[Humaira Asghar|Humaira Ali]] – Model and actress.
*[[Saeeda Imtiaz]] – Actress. Known for her role in the Pakistani film [[Wajood (2018 film)|''Wajood'']].
* Sehr Beg – Fitness trainer.
*Aadi Adeal Amjad – Host and television presenter.
*[[Rauf Lala]] – Comedian.

=== Weekly summary ===
{| class="wikitable" style="width:100%; font-size:85%; line-height:20px;"
|-
! rowspan="10" style="background:#8E22AC; color:#fff;" | Week 1
! '''Entrances'''
| On Day 1, Maira, Nigah, Mareeha, Saim, Faiza, Nouman, Aamna, Umer, Humaira, Saeeda, Sehr, Aadi and Rauf entered the house as contestants.
|-
!Wazir
|On day 2, by random selection Maira was chosen as Wazir of the house by Badshah Salamat.
|-
! rowspan="6" |Immunity Task
|'''Token Walay Aur Rakhwalay'''
On day 2, the 12 unsafe housemates were provided with 12 tokens each for the spending 24 hours. The basic necessities will be availed using the tokens; one time meal will be utilized using 2 tokens; Tea, fruits and egg can be consumed using one token; using washroom, make-up room and gym will also be available after using one token; 1 hour's sleep can be taken after using one token. The game will be supervised by Maira, with the support of other housemates. Wazir has the power to confiscate tokens in case she catches the housemates red handed, violating rules of the game. The housemate with the most tokens at the end of 24 hours will be immune from eviction.
|-
!Result – Mareeha won the immunity and saves herself from "Khatray Ka Ghar" as she had more tokens. Aaman and Rauf were nominated for eviction as they had least cards at the end of the task.
|-
|'''Aaqa Aur Ghulam'''
On day 4, the contestants in '''Khatray Ka Ghar''' i.e.; Faiza, Umer, Nigah, Rauf and Aamna, were given an opportunity to get safe from getting evicted. They were servants of the already immune housemates for the task and listen to the orders of their owners. At the end of the task, the owners will decide the best servant who will be immuned from the '''Khatray Ka Ghar'''.
|-
!Result – Baadshah cancelled the task due to poor performance of the housemates
|-
|'''Yaaron Yehi Dosti Hai'''<br>
On day 6, the unsafe contestants have to choose a contestant who would play as their representative in the task. Aadi was chosen as the moderator of the task therefore no one can choose him as a representative.
* Faiza chose Saeeda;
* Nigah chose Noman;
* Umer chose Sehr;
* Amna chose Saim and
* Rauf chose Maira.

In the garden area, two phone booths were placed for male and female representatives. The chosen representatives have to stand in the booth till the end of the task. The person whose representative is the last-standing will be immune from the eviction.
|-
!Result – No one came out of the phone booth. Hence, no one was immune.
|-
!Punishment
|
* On day 4, Umer was nominated for the eviction directly as Saim called him out for using foul language in the task "Aaqa Aur Ghulam".
* On day 5, Maira was dismissed as Wazir due to mismanagement and housemates were given the right to decide whether she will be able to continue her tenure as Wazir. Everyone except Aadi and Umer voted in her favor. Baadshah conducted a poll among the housemates to decide who should be the next Wazir between, Aadi and Umer. The majority choses Aadi as an interim Wazir. 
|-
!Exit
|On day 7, Nigah was saved by the housemates' vote. Faiza Khan was evicted after facing public votes.
|-
! rowspan="11" style="background:#8E22AC; color:#fff;" |Week 2
!Wazir
|On day 8, the safe housemates (i.e, Aadi, Maira, Saeeda, Noman, Nigah, Rauf) were eligible for Wazarat. The housemates had to vote who they want to make Wazir for the week. By housemates, voting, Noman becomes the Wazir.
|-
! rowspan="2" |Talk to the family Task
|On day 9, in the gaming area all the males and females have to stand on a stepping podium with balancing a ball on the pole. The last standing male/female will get a chance to talk to their family.
|-
!Result – Nigah from males and Mareeha from females won the task
|-
! rowspan="4" | Immunity Task
|'''Tamasha Bank'''
On day 10, the garden was designed with two printing stations, and one bank was designed in the gaming area. Noman had to choose a housemate who will play the role of Banker, he chose Aadi. In each round both the teams have to prepare currency notes and deposit them in the bank. Each team have to deposit notes to the banker. Bankers have the right to reject the currency offered by the depositors. The approved notes will be handed over to Wazir for keeping in respective team's safe. After the end of the rounds, the team with the most approved currency notes in their safe will be declared winner of the task. The winning team will end up being nominated for eviction. The teams were as follows:

* Team A – Khatray Ki Ghanti team – Humaira, Mareeha, Saim, Aamna and Sehr
* Team B – Safe zone team – Maira, Saeeda, Rauf, Umer and Nigah
|-
!Result – Team A had 184 approved notes where Team B had 158 approved notes. Therefore, Team A won and got immuned from nominations and Team B was nominated.
|-
|On day 12, the housemates were divided into pairs as; Saeeda and Sehr; Mareeha and Rauf; Humaira and Aadi; Umer and Maira; Nigah and Noman; Saim and Amna. In the gaming area, each individual from the pair has to build a tower using blocks, whereas his partner has to throw balls to destroy other pairs towers. The team with highest tower will win the task. The winning pair will be rewarded with the one housemate with immunity and another with the opportunity to talk to the family. 
|-
!Result – Mareeha and Rauf won the task. Rauf got immune from "Khatray Ka Ghar" and Mareeha gave her power to talk to the family to Rauf as well.
|-
! rowspan="2" |Luxury Dinner Task
|'''Hasna Mana Hai'''
On day 13, the housemates were divided into two teams as;

'''Team A:''' Umer, Rauf, Saeeda, Maira, Saim and Aamna;

'''Team B:''' Aadi, Mareeha, Noman, Nigah, Sehr and Humaira.

Team A had to make members of Team B laugh. If all the members of Team B laugh during the task, team A will win the task or vice versa.
|-
!Result – Team B won.
|-
!Ration Task
| '''Tawazan Barkarar Rakhiye'''<br>
On day 14, the housemates have to balance the see-saw for the specified time whereas Lala or Aadi will sit on the on one side of the ride whereas two housemates at once can use their force to balance the see-saw and not let the Lala or Aadi touch the ground.
|-
!Exit
|On day 15, Nigah was evicted after facing public votes.
|-
! rowspan="5" |Week                                                           3             
!Wazir
|On day 15, Badshah chose Umer as the Wazir of the house.
|-
! rowspan="4" |Immunity Tasks
|
|-
|
|-
|'''Saanp Seerhi''' (Snake and Ladder)
On day 18, like a board game, unsafe housemates have to roll a dice and navigate the board. Landing on the ladder advances a player to a square further up the board while landing on a snake means they have to go back to the previous square, where snake's tail is connected. The player to reach the final square wins the game.
|-
|'''Result – Saaeda won and becomes safe from "Khatray ka Ghar                                                               |
|}

*{{note|01|1}}: Mareeha was saved, where as Rauf and Amna were nominated as a result of "Token Walay Aur Rakhwalay".
*{{note|02|2}}: Umer was nominated by "Adnan Siddiqui" for violating house rules.
*{{note|03|3}}: On day 9, Umer was saved by guests; Ahmed Shah, Abubakr Shah and Umer Shah.
*{{note|04|4}}: Umer, Rauf, Maira, Saeeda and Nigah lost the task "Tamasha Bank" against nominated contestants; Mareeha, Humaira, Aamna, Saim and Sehr were saved and as a result they were nominated.
*{{note|05|5}}: On day 12, Rauf won the immunity by winning the task.
*{{note|07|7}}: Everyone was nominated for eviction by "Adnan Siddiqui" except Noman by virtue of being Wazir of last week.
*{{note|08|8}}: Saim and Maira were saved as they won "Train Task".
*{{note|09|9}}: Saeeda got saved by winning the "Saanp Seerhi" task.
*{{note|10|10}}: Rauf got saved by winning the task.
*{{note|11|11}}: Due to violations in the puzzle task, all housemates were nominated by Adnan Siddiqui including Wazir Humaira.
*{{note|12|12}}: Mareeha saved herself by winning the task and became the Wazir.
*{{note|13|13}}: Saeeda saved herself by winning the task "Grabstick".
*{{note|14|14}}: Saim, Umer and Aadi got saved by winning tasks but Umer nominated himself and saved Rauf.
*{{note|15|15}}: Umer, Humaira and Noman evicted on Day 28. However, Humaira entered the house later the same day, where as Umer came back on Day 29.
*{{note|16|16}}: Aadi, Mareeha and Maira won ticket to finale week task and entered the final week.
*{{note|17|17}}: Humaira and Maira ejected from the house after physically assaulted.
*^18 : On Day 35, elimination occurred. Saeeda and Saim get evicted while Umer and Rauf Lala become the last two finalists.
*^19 : On Day 40 – out of the 6 finalists, Humaira and Maira get evicted due to violating the rules of physical violence. Saeeda re-enters as a guest to stay until the finale.
*^20: Finale occurs on Day 43. The winner is decided by the votes of audience. Umer Aalam becomes the winner of Tamasha Season 1 while Mareeha Safdar becomes the Runner-up. Aadi Adeel Amjad becomes the second runner up while Rauf Lala becomes the third runner up.

== ''Tamasha'' season 4 ==
Season 4 premiered on 9 August 2025.

The contestants are;

*Saif Ali Khan – Singer, Songwriter, Musician (Winner)
*Yaseen Ali – Actor (Runner-up)
*Sarah Neelum – Model and actress (2nd runner-up)
*Malaika Farooq – Influencer and business owner (4th place)
*Muslim Abbas – Actor and podcaster (5th place)
*Maham Mirza – Model and reality tv star. Competed in ''Super Diva. Eliminated Day 62''
*Kanwal Farooq – Influencer and fashion designer. ''Eliminated Day 61''
*Zainabb Raja – Actress. ''Eliminated Day 57''
*Omi Butt – Actor, chef and entertainer. ''Eliminated Day 57''
*Maddy – Fitness trainer. ''Eliminated Day 50''
*Daniya Kanwal – Musician, dancer and actress. Participated in [[BOL Champions season 1|''Champions Season 1'']]. ''Eliminated Day 50''
*Rida Tariq – Fashion Designer ''Eliminated Day 43''
*Ahmer Hussain – Actor. ''Walked Day 21. Re-entered Day 25. Eliminated Day 43''
*Sarah Omair – Television actress. ''Eliminated Day 36''
*Kashif Khan – Actor and Comedian. Winner of ''[[Comedy Circus]]'' season 1. ''Eliminated Day  29''
*Ovais Riaz- Social media content creator. ''Eliminated Day 23''
*Ghaniya Siddiqi – Model, Host and makeup artist. ''Eliminated Day 15''
*[[Quaid Ahmed]] – Singer. ''Eliminated Day 8''

=== Notes ===
: {{color box|#cfc|border=silver}} indicates the Wazir.
: {{color box|#C2DFFF|border=silver}} indicates the Nominees for house Wazir.
: {{Color box|#959FFD|border=silver}} indicates that the Housemate was directly nominated for eviction prior to the regular nominations process.
: {{Color box|#008080|border=silver}} indicates ticket to finale.
: {{Color box|#73FB76|border=silver}} indicates the winner.

'''''Teri Raza''''' ({{langx|ur|{{nq|تیری رضا}}|lit=Your Pleasure}}) is a Pakistani [[Pakistani drama|television series]] that first aired on [[ARY Digital]] on 8 July 2017 and ended on 2 February 2018. It was produced by [[Fahad Mustafa]] and Dr. Ali Kazmi under their banner [[Big Bang Entertainment]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.somethinghaute.com/4-mind-boggling-things-happened-teri-raza/|title=4 mind-boggling things that happened in 'Teri Raza'|date=2017-12-06|work=Something Haute|access-date=2018-11-13|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.somethinghaute.com/teri-raza-suhana-really-deserve-rameez-not-imtiaz/|title=Teri Raza: Why Suhana really does deserve Rameez, not Imtiaz|date=2017-10-01|work=Something Haute|access-date=2018-11-13|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Plot==
''Teri Raza'' centers on Suhana, a young college student in love with her chauvinist classmate Rameez. Her parents arrange a marriage for her with her older, well-settled relative, Imtiaz, after an [[Istikhara]] is performed by her grandmother. Suhana initially resists but eventually agrees to the marriage when Rameez's careless attitude leads her to believe he is not serious about their relationship. After marrying Imtiaz, Suhana cannot adjust to her new life and remains in love with Rameez. Imtiaz, realizing her feelings, divorces her, and she returns to Rameez. Due to his grandmother mother's pressure, Imtiaz marries her colleague Seema, leading Suhana to move on. Thus, she marries Rameez despite the opposition of her family who cut the ties with her after her decision. Her marriage suufers due to chauvinism of Rameez and his ture nature. At this turbulent stage, Suhana then learns that Imtiaz still loves her.

* [[Shamim Hilaly]] as Sitara: Imtiaz's mother and Suhana's aunt

== Reception ==
===Critical reception===
The series was received mixed reviews, with critics panning characterisation of the female lead. The character received the highest votes in the "most annoying TV character" category by critics and readers of the ''[[DAWN Images]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1179488|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250907212349/https://images.dawn.com/news/1179488 |title=47% of our readers believe Yakeen Ka Safar deserves to be on Netflix |date=20 February 2018 |archive-date=7 September 2025 |work=DAWN Images |url-status=live}}</ref>

The series was panned in the year-ender articles of several publications, with Sadaf Haider of ''[[DAWN Images]]'' criticised characterisation of Suhana's character,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://images.dawn.com/news/1179094|title=The good, the bad and the inexplicable of Pakistani TV in 2017|last=Haider|first=Sadaf |date=22 December 2017|work=Images ([[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]]) |access-date=13 November 2018|archive-date=16 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250416071255/https://images.dawn.com/news/1179094|url-status=live|language=en}}</ref> Buraq Shabbir of ''[[The News International]]'' noted the inconsistent treatment of the characters,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/tns/detail/564681-looking-back-tv-2017|title=Looking back at TV in 2017 {{!}} TNS - The News on Sunday|website=tns.thenews.com.pk|author=Buraq Shabbir|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251124080912/https://www.thenews.com.pk/tns/detail/564681-looking-back-tv-2017|archive-date=2025-11-24|url-status=live |language=en |access-date=13 November 2018}}</ref> and Mahwash Badar of ''[[The Express Tribune]]'' opined that the "story seems very clichéd but the dialogues are beautiful and the story keeps shifting in and out of intrigue to keep the audience hooked".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://tribune.com.pk/article/56539/the-hits-and-misses-from-the-pakistani-drama-industry-in-2017|title=The hits and misses from the Pakistani drama industry in 2017 |access-date=13 November 2018 |website=tribune com.pk |author=Mahwash Badar |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226192140/https://tribune.com.pk/article/56539/the-hits-and-misses-from-the-pakistani-drama-industry-in-2017 |archive-date=26 December 2024 |url-status=live |language=en}}</ref>

'''''Waada''''' ({{langx|ur|{{nq|وعدہ}}|lit=Promise}}) is a [[Pakistani drama]] television series directed by Syed Atif Hussain, written by  Samina Ejaz. It originally aired on [[ARY Digital]] in 2016.

==Cast==

*[[Shaista Lodhi]] as Sumaira
*[[Faysal Qureshi (actor)|Faisal Qureshi]] as Shahab
*[[Saboor Ali]] as Jaana
*[[Ismat Iqbal]] as Nuzhat
*[[Srha Asghar]] as Uzma
*[[Anum Tanveer]] as Lubna
*[[Fahad Sheikh]]
*[[Hassan Ahmed (actor)|Hassan Ahmed]]
*[[Ghazala Butt]]
*[[Amir Qureshi]] 

==Plot==
Sumaira is a loving wife, mother, and daughter-in-law. She cares for everyone in the family and tries to do as much as she can for everyone at home. She makes an effort to fulfill her promise and excel in every relationship. Loyalty is all that she has to offer besides so much love.

Shahab is financially very secure as he is a rich businessman, but along with that, he also cares for his entire family; basically, he's a good husband. He promises his wife that he will never leave her, no matter what, and stand by her side in all the ups and downs.

Jaana is the maid's daughter who was fired from her previous job due to falling for the owner's son, who hated her. Jaana hunts for her next victim, who turns out to be Shahab, and disrupts his life. She schemes against Sumaira till Shahab too falls for her and she ends up marrying him.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arydigital.tv/waada-exclusive-ary-digital-drama/|title=Waada – Exclusive ARY Digital Drama -|date=8 November 2016|publisher=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arydigital.tv/videos/category/waada/page/2/|title=Waada Archives - Page 2 of 2 - Watch Latest Episodes of ARY Digital|publisher=}}</ref>

WIKIPEDIA REVISION DOCUMENT: Wahaj Ali
======================================================================

{{short description|Pakistani actor (born 1988)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2025}}
{{Use Pakistani English|date=June 2025}}
{{Infobox person
| name               = Wahaj Ali
| image              = 
| caption            = Ali in 2024
| birth_date         = {{birth date and age |df=yes|1988|12|1}}
| birth_place        = [[Lahore]], [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]], Pakistan
| education          = [[National College of Arts]]
| occupation         = {{hlist|Actor}}

| spouse             = {{marriage|Ayaza Wahaj|2016|}}

'''Wahaj Ali''' (born 1 December 1988) is a Pakistani actor known for his work predominantly in [[Pakistani dramas|Urdu]] television. He is a recipient of several accolades including two [[Lux Style Awards]], alongside two [[Hum Awards]] nominations.

He made his acting debut with [[Hum TV]]'s soap drama [[Ishq Ibadat (2015 TV series)|''Ishq Ibadat'']] (2015) and subsequently appeared in ''[[Gila (TV series)|Gila]]'' (2016). He then started in ''[[Mah-e-Tamaam]]'' (2018) and the [[Inter-Services Public Relations|ISPR]]-based ''[[Ehd-e-Wafa]]'' (2019). Ali gained praise for his portrayal as an obsessive lover in the drama ''[[Fitoor (TV series)|Fitoor]]'' and as a Bengali fighter based on [[Shafi Imam Rumi]] in the historical drama ''[[Jo Bichar Gaye]]'' both (2021). The romance drama ''[[Tere Bin (2022 TV series)|Tere Bin]]'' (2022) marked a turning point in his career and he gained further success with ''[[Mujhe Pyaar Hua Tha]]'' (2023). The former earned him the [[Lux Style Award for Best TV Actor]]. This success was followed by two poorly-received dramas.

== Early life and family ==
Ali was born on 1 December 1988<ref>{{cite web |last=News Desk |first= |date=1 December 2025 |title=Wahaj Ali receives heartfelt wishes as he celebrates 37th birthday |url=https://dailytimes.com.pk/1410706/wahaj-ali-receives-heartfelt-wishes-as-he-celebrates-37th-birthday/ |access-date=6 December 2025 |website=Daily Times}}</ref> into a [[Punjabi Muslims|Punjabi]] family in [[Lahore, Punjab]].<ref>{{Cite web |accessdate=10 December 2021 |date=1 December 2020 |title=Wahaj Ali, the versatile actor, celebrates his 32nd birthday |url=https://www.bolnews.com/2020/12/01/pakistani-celebrity/wahaj-ali-the-versatile-actor-celebrates-32nd-birthday-today/index.html/amp |website=Bol News}}</ref><ref name="HBDWahaj">{{Cite web |date=1 December 2022 |accessdate=11 December 2022 |title=Birthday wishes pour in for actor Wahaj Ali |url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/02-Dec-2022/birthday-wishes-pour-in-for-wahaj-ali?version=amp |website=Daily Pakistan}}</ref> His father was a government employee and his mother was a teacher. He is the only child of his parents.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 October 2018 |title=Wahaj Ali |url=https://socialdiary.pk/wahaj-ali/ |website=Social Diary}}</ref> Ali earned his [[Master's degree|Master's]] in Multimedia Arts from the [[National College of Arts]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Profile on LinkedIn |url=https://pk.linkedin.com/in/wahaj-ali-47164321 |website=[[LinkedIn]]}}</ref>

== Career ==

=== Early work in theater and TV production ===
Ali began his career as a theater actor in 2007 before joining a TV channel in the news and programming department.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shabbir |first=Buraq |date=31 May 2020 |title=From theatre to television to films |url=https://www.thenews.com.pk/tns/detail/664899-from-theatre-to-television-to-films |access-date=22 August 2022 |website=[[The News International]]}}</ref> From 2009 to 2011, he worked as an assistant producer at [[Samaa TV]]. After 2011, Ali was producer at [[Jang Media Group|Geo TV]].<ref name=":0" />

=== TV debut and success (2015–present) ===
Marking his television debut as a leading actor in 2015 with the drama [[Ishq Ibadat (2015 TV series)|''Ishq Ibadat'']], he went on to play lead in several notable television serials, including ''[[Hari Hari Churiyaan|Hari Hari Churiyan]]'' (2017), ''[[Dil Nawaz]]'' (2017), ''[[Mah-e-Tamaam]]'' (2017), ''[[Dil-e-Bereham]]'' (2019), ''[[Bharam]]'' (2019) [[Fitoor (TV series)|''Fitoor'']] (2021) and ''[[Ishq Jalebi]]'' (2021). 

In 2021, Ali delivered a critically lauded performance as [[Shafi Imam Rumi]], a Bangladeshi freedom fighter, in the historical drama ''[[Jo Bichar Gaye]]'', showcasing his range and dramatic intensity.<ref>{{cite news |date=19 January 2022 |title=Maya Ali, Wahaj dominate with their sizzling chemistry in 'Jo Bichar Gaye' |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/2339457/maya-ali-wahaj-dominate-with-their-sizzling-chemistry-in-jo-bichar-gaye |access-date=16 June 2025 |work=The Express Tribune}}</ref> His portrayal was described as "powerful and emotional" by reviewers, particularly in the show's climactic scenes.{{cn|date=May 2026}}

He reached widespread popularity across South Asia with his portrayal of Murtasim Khan in the 2022–23 romance drama ''[[Tere Bin (2022 TV series)|Tere Bin]]'', which became a cultural phenomenon.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sayem |first=Kawser Md. |date=4 June 2025 |title=Pakistani Drama Tere Bin Emerges as an All-Time Audience Favourite |url=https://unb.com.bd/category/Entertainment/pakistani-drama-tere-bin-emerges-as-an-all-time-audience-favourite/161280 |access-date=16 June 2025 |website=UNB News}}</ref> According to a ''[[Gulf News]]'' op-ed written in June 2025, years after the end of the drama, Ali’s "magnetic presence" and "emotional chemistry" with co-star [[Yumna Zaidi]] were key to the show's success.<ref>{{cite news |last=Radhakrishnan |first=Manjusha |date=17 June 2025 |title=Tere Bin: Why this hit Pakistani love drama still has us hooked and when you can expect season 2 |url=https://gulfnews.com/entertainment/tere-bin-why-this-hit-pakistani-love-drama-still-has-us-hooked-and-when-you-can-expect-season-2-1.500166124 |access-date=16 June 2025 |work=Gulf News}}</ref>

== Media image ==
Ali has established himself as one of the leading Urdu television actors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://galaxylollywood.com/2023/06/12/how-wahaj-alis-approach-to-fame-sets-him-apart/|title=The art of staying grounded: How Wahaj Ali has handled fame and success - Exclusive|accessdate=16 June 2023|website=Galaxy Lollywood|date=12 June 2023 }}</ref> ''[[Dawn (newspaper)|Dawn]]'' noted, "The fact that all his different avatars have been so well-received is testament to his talent."<ref name="WahajI">{{Cite web |title=The Icon Interview - Wahaj Ali: 'Im in no hurry' |url=https://www.dawn.com/news/1662026 |work=Dawn |author=Maliha Rehman |date=5 December 2021 |access-date=23 December 2021}}</ref> ''Something Haute'' noted, "Wahaj Ali's choices and the credibility they have amassed, have played a pivotal role in positioning him right at the top of the artistic food chain."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.somethinghaute.com/the-rising-of-wahaj-ali/|title=The Rising of Wahaj Ali|date=29 March 2023|accessdate=16 April 2023|website=Something Haute|author=Aamna Haider Isani}}</ref> He has been placed in Hello Pakistan's HOT100 list, in the "Trailblazers" category.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/14-Dec-2022/headliners-trailblazers-trendsetters-celebs-who-made-it-to-hellopakistan-s-hot100-list-of-2022%3fversion=amp|title=Headliners, trailblazers, trendsetters - Celebs who made it to Hello Pakistan's #HOT100 list|accessdate=16 December 2022|website=Daily Pakistan|archive-date=15 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221215012342/https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/14-Dec-2022/headliners-trailblazers-trendsetters-celebs-who-made-it-to-hellopakistan-s-hot100-list-of-2022?version=amp|url-status=dead}}</ref> Ali received the "Sexiest Heartthrob" title at [[Hello! (magazine)|Hello Magazine Awards]] in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/17-May-2023/tere-bin-couple-yumna-zaidi-wahaj-ali-set-couple-goals-with-walima-photoshoot%3fversion=amp|title='Tere Bin' star couple Yumna Zaidi and Wahaj Ali set couple goals with their Walima photoshoot|accessdate=29 May 2023|website=Daily Pakistan}}</ref> He serves as an ambassador for a number of brands such as [[Head & Shoulders]] and [[7 Up]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.samaaenglish.tv/news/40037796|title=Wahaj Ali's cross-border fandom, wins hearts in India with 'Tere Bin'|website=Samaa TV|language=en|date=4 June 2023|accessdate=22 June 2023}}</ref>

WIKIPEDIA REVISION DOCUMENT: Acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance
======================================================================

{{Short description|2026 business acquisition}}
{{Use American English|date=February 2026}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=March 2026}}
{{Infobox acquisition
| logo = Paramount Skydance Logo.svg
| logo2 = Warner Bros. Discovery.svg
| logo2_caption = Logos before the acquisition
| initiator = Paramount Skydance (renamed [[Skydance]])
| target = [[Warner Bros. Discovery]]
| type = [[Mergers and acquisitions|Full acquisition]]
| cost = $110.9 billion
| initiated = {{start date and age|2026|02|27}}
| completed = {{end date and age|2026|10|06}}
| status = Completed
| resulting_entity = 
| logo3 = Skydance Corporation Dark Logo 2026.svg
| logo3_caption = Logo after the acquisition
}}

On October 6, 2026, Paramount Skydance acquired [[Warner Bros. Discovery]] (WBD) for $31 per [[Share (finance)|share]], valuing the company at $110.9 billion, with the combined company renamed '''[[Skydance]]'''. The acquisition was funded by the [[Larry Ellison|Ellison family]] and [[RedBird Capital Partners]], with additional funding being provided by the [[sovereign wealth fund]]s of [[Saudi Arabia]], [[Qatar]], and the [[United Arab Emirates]] (which hold non-voting shares in the company). WBD had originally planned to [[Corporate spin-off|spin off]] its less profitable [[List of assets owned by Warner Bros. Discovery#Global Linear Networks|linear television assets]] as a new company, leaving the flagship [[Warner Bros. Entertainment|Warner Bros. studio]] and streaming businesses. After Paramount Skydance began making unsolicited offers to acquire WBD as a whole, its [[board of directors]] placed the company up for [[auction]]; in December 2025, WBD initially accepted an $82.7 billion offer by [[Netflix, Inc.]] to acquire the WB studios and streaming business, with the remaining assets continuing as a spin-off known as [[Discovery Global]].  

Paramount continued to make unsolicited offers for WBD into 2026, arguing that its offer provided better [[shareholder value]] than that of Netflix, would give Paramount and WBD the [[Economies of scale|scale]] needed to compete with [[Big Tech|tech companies]] while preserving a commitment to the [[Movie theater|cinema]] industry, and would face less [[antitrust]] scrutiny due to Netflix's projected [[subscription video on demand]] (SVOD) market share post-acquisition. Paramount CEO [[David Ellison]] stated that the combined company would release at least 30 films per year, and maintain the creative independence of divisions such as [[HBO]]. On April 23, 2026, WBD shareholders approved a revised offer by Paramount at $31 per share, including an agreement to pay Netflix's [[breakup fee]], and pay an ongoing penalty to WBD shareholders if the sale was not completed by a specific deadline.  

Politicians and members of the [[film industry]] expressed concern over the resulting scale of the company, its potential impact on jobs, [[movie theater]]s, and [[cable television]]. Concerns were also raised over the Ellison family's relationship with the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]], its potential influence on the editorial operations of CNN, and the backing of the acquisition by [[Middle East|Middle-Eastern]] wealth funds. The acquisition was approved by the [[U.S. Department of Justice]] on June 12, 2026, with no major concessions. The [[European Commission]] imposed conditions requiring Paramount to exit its [[United International Pictures]] distribution venture with [[Universal Pictures]], while the [[United Kingdom]] is requiring that its individual news and children's businesses maintain editorial independence, and will prohibit the combination of its linear and on-demand services for five years.

The completion of the acquisition was delayed by a federal [[antitrust]] lawsuit from California and eleven other states, which sought antitrust remedies due to the combined company's total market share of box office and cable television revenue. The [[Writers Guild of America]] (WGA) also filed a similar suit. Paramount negotiated a five-year [[consent decree]] to resolve the California lawsuit, mandating specific investments towards film production and acquisition, restrictions on its engagement with film exhibitors and television providers, and the establishment of an independent board to oversee the editorial integrity and independence of [[CBS News]] and [[CNN]] post-acquisition, among other conditions. Amid concerns that the antitrust remedies were not strong enough to address the original concerns, the settlement was approved by the court on September 30, 2026, and the acquisition was completed on October 6, 2026. 

The combined company—renamed Skydance Corporation—is led by Ellison and former [[Mattel]] executive [[Ynon Kreiz]] as co-CEOs; its holdings include two of the five [[major film studios]] ([[Warner Bros. Pictures]], [[Paramount Pictures]] and related assets such as [[DC Entertainment]]), streaming services (such as [[HBO Max]], [[Paramount+]], [[Philo (company)|Philo]], and [[Pluto TV]]), television studios ([[CBS Studios]], [[Paramount Television Studios]], and [[Warner Bros. Television Studios]]), various television networks and cable channels (including the [[CBS]] broadcast network; legacy [[Turner Broadcasting System|Turner]] brands such as [[TBS (American TV channel)|TBS]], [[TNT (American TV channel)|TNT]], CNN, and [[Adult Swim]]; legacy [[Discovery Inc.]]/[[Scripps Networks Interactive|Scripps]] channels such as its [[Discovery Channel|namesake]], [[HGTV]], and [[Food Network]]; legacy Paramount cable networks such as [[BET]], [[Comedy Central]], [[MTV]], and [[Paramount Network]]; children's brands [[Cartoon Network]] and [[Nickelodeon]]; pay television brands HBO and [[Showtime (TV network)|Showtime]]; and various international television channels), as well as sports divisions ([[CBS Sports]] and [[TNT Sports (United States)|TNT Sports]]).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cobb |first=Kayla |date=2026-10-08 |title=Skydance's New TV Empire Explained: Who's in Charge and What May Be Ahead {{!}} Analysis |url=https://www.thewrap.com/media-platforms/tv/skydance-tv-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-merger-analysis/ |access-date=2026-10-09 |website=TheWrap |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Background ==
[[Warner Bros. Discovery|WBD]] was established on April 8, 2022, and created through [[AT&T]]'s [[divestment]] of [[WarnerMedia]] and WarnerMedia's subsequent merger with [[Discovery, Inc.]], via a [[Reverse Morris Trust]] transaction.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hayes |first=Dade |date=April 8, 2022 |title=Warner Bros Discovery Merger Closes, Altering Media Landscape |url=https://deadline.com/2022/04/warner-bros-discovery-merger-closes-altering-media-landscape-1234997171/ |access-date=February 17, 2026 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Sherman |first=Alex |date=February 1, 2022 |title=AT&T to spin off WarnerMedia in $43 billion Discovery media merger, cuts dividend |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220201120118/https://www.cnbc.com/2022/02/01/att-to-spin-off-warnermedia-in-43-billion-discovery-media-merger.html |archive-date=February 1, 2022 |access-date=December 20, 2025 |work=[[CNBC]]}}</ref> Through the agreement, Discovery executives would assume majority control over the merged company, while AT&T would no longer hold any ownership interest.{{Citation needed|date=March 2026}} AT&T attempted to reinvent itself as a major player in the [[Show business|entertainment industry]] through [[Acquisition of Time Warner by AT&T|acquiring]] Time Warner and [[DirecTV]],<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Gryta |first1=Thomas |last2=Hagey |first2=Keach |last3=Cimilluca |first3=Dana |last4=Sharma |first4=Amol |date=October 22, 2016 |title=AT&T Reaches Deal to Buy Time Warner for $85.4 Billion |url=http://www.wsj.com/articles/at-t-reaches-deal-to-buy-time-warner-for-more-than-80-billion-1477157084 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161023013659/http://www.wsj.com/articles/at-t-reaches-deal-to-buy-time-warner-for-more-than-80-billion-1477157084 |archive-date=October 23, 2016 |access-date=December 16, 2025 |work=The Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref> but later reversed course after losses and unsuccessful synergies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Porter |first=Rick |date=2025-06-09 |title=It's Not You, It's WB: A Brief History of Warners' 21st Century Mergers and Breakups |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/warner-bros-discovery-breakup-failed-mergers-1236260379/ |access-date=2026-06-23 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |url-status=live}}</ref> Issues facing WBD were its initial debt load of over $43 billion and heavy market devaluation of its stock, with it losing over 60% of its value by early 2025.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Sherman |first=Alex |date=December 6, 2022 |title=David Zaslav's top priority at Warner Bros. Discovery win back Hollywood? |url=https://www.ft.com/content/db177b75-0d53-4dde-a9e4-c0f36b9bf913 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20240516011156/https://www.ft.com/content/db177b75-0d53-4dde-a9e4-c0f36b9bf913 |archive-date=May 16, 2024 |access-date=February 17, 2026 |website=[[Financial Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=White |first1=Dade |last2=Hayes |first2=Peter |date=January 5, 2023 |title=Tax Write-Offs For Content Are Over At Warner Bros Discovery As CFO Once Again Scolds Entertainment Biz For 'Spending Frenzy' |url=https://deadline.com/2023/01/warner-bros-discovery-content-writeoffs-cfo-scolds-entertainment-for-spending-frenzy-1235212199/ |access-date=February 17, 2026 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-date=January 6, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230106001348/https://deadline.com/2023/01/warner-bros-discovery-content-writeoffs-cfo-scolds-entertainment-for-spending-frenzy-1235212199/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Despite these efforts, the linear [[Cable television|cable networks]] of WBD continued to lag behind in profits compared to the more profitable streaming and studios businesses.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Warner Bros. Discover. Downgraded To 'BB+' O |url=https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/type/HTML/id/3372936 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250915184042/https://www.spglobal.com/ratings/en/regulatory/article/-/view/type/HTML/id/3372936 |archive-date=September 15, 2025 |access-date=February 17, 2026 |website=S&P Global Ratings |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref>

On December 12, 2024, WBD restructured its operations into two divisions: Streaming & Studios and Global Linear Networks. WBD president and CEO [[David Zaslav]] said the new structure would provide "flexibility with potential future strategic opportunities."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Flint |first=Joe |date=December 12, 2024 |title=Warner Discovery to Restructure, Setting Up Potential 'Strategic Opportunities' |url=https://www.wsj.com/business/media/warner-discovery-to-restructure-setting-up-potential-strategic-opportunities-37fabf0f |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241216055943/https://www.wsj.com/business/media/warner-discovery-to-restructure-setting-up-potential-strategic-opportunities-37fabf0f#selection-5313.0-5316.0 |archive-date=December 16, 2024 |access-date=February 17, 2026 |website=The Wall Street Journal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 12, 2024 |title=Warner Bros. The successor companies would have been named "Warner Bros.", comprising the Streaming & Studios division, and "Discovery Global", comprising the Global Linear Networks division.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Weprin |first=Alex |date=July 28, 2025 |title=Warner Bros. == Initial bidding war ==
{{Multiple image
| direction         = vertical
| image1            = Netflix 2015 logo.svg

In September 2025, Paramount Skydance CEO [[David Ellison]] convened a board meeting to discuss a possible acquisition of WBD, a move reported as intended to strengthen Paramount's competitive position against Amazon, Disney, and Netflix. Several days later, Ellison met with Zaslav at his home to propose a cash-and-stock bid of $19 per share. The offer was formalized in a subsequent letter that set the cash component at 60%. Later in September, Paramount Skydance raised its offer to $22 per share with a 67% cash component, a $2 billion reverse-termination fee payable if the deal failed to clear regulatory review, and a provision for Zaslav to remain as co-CEO and co-chairman of the combined company. On October 13, 2025, Paramount Skydance submitted a third offer, raising the bid to $23.50 per share with an 80% cash component. WBD continued to reject Paramount's proposals.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Flint |first1=Joe |last2=Schwartz |first2=Brian |last3=Andrews |first3=Natalie |date=December 9, 2025 |title=Behind Paramount's Relentless Campaign to Woo Warner Discovery and President Trump |url=https://www.wsj.com/business/media/paramount-netflix-warner-bros-battle-ellisons-a86fe15c |access-date=December 9, 2025 |website=The Wall Street Journal |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251210075307/https://www.wsj.com/business/media/paramount-netflix-warner-bros-battle-ellisons-a86fe15c |archive-date=December 10, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> An analyst suggested that the bid was meant to preempt potential interest in the studio's business post-split, and take advantage of a "period of industry-wide instability".<ref name="SwallowWhole" />

After Paramount's three failed attempts, talks of a potential sale of WBD began circulating in October,<ref>{{Cite web |last1=James |first1=Meg |last2=Masunaga |first2=Samantha |date=October 12, 2025 |title=Warner Bros. Discovery sale talks heat up after initial Paramount bid rejected |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2025-10-12/warner-bros-discovery-sale-talks-heat-up-board-rebuffs-paramount-initial-bid |url-status=live |website=Los Angeles Times |access-date=October 12, 2025 |archive-date=April 24, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260424185939/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2025-10-12/warner-bros-discovery-sale-talks-heat-up-board-rebuffs-paramount-initial-bid }}</ref> and the company announced it was reviewing strategic alternatives to its previously announced plan to split into two companies after receiving unsolicited interest from multiple parties.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=James |first1=Meg |date=October 21, 2025 |title=Warner Bros. Discovery officially hangs a 'for sale' sign around company |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2025-10-21/warner-bros-discovery-paramount-bids-sale-larry-ellison |url-status=live |website=Los Angeles Times |access-date=October 21, 2025 |archive-date=April 12, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260412022942/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2025-10-21/warner-bros-discovery-paramount-bids-sale-larry-ellison }}</ref> On October 30, 2025, [[Netflix, Inc.]] was reported to be actively exploring a bid for the Streaming & Studios unit; the company stressed that it remained "predominantly focused on growing organically", and was not interested in WBD's legacy linear television businesses.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Kopecki|first1=Dawn|last2=Chmielewski|first2=Dawn|last3=Crowley|first3=Amy-Jo|date=October 30, 2025|title=Exclusive: Netflix taps bank to explore bid for Warner Bros Discovery|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/netflix-taps-bank-explore-bid-warner-bros-discovery-2025-10-30/|access-date=December 5, 2025|website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

In the first round of non-binding proposals submitted on November 20, 2025, Comcast and Netflix made cash-and-stock and mostly-cash bids for the Streaming & Studios unit, respectively, while Paramount Skydance made an all-cash offer for the entirety of WBD at $25.50 per share, backed by debt financing from [[Apollo Global Management]] and Middle-Eastern [[Sovereign wealth fund|sovereign wealth funds]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Hayes|first1=Dade|last2=Johnson|first2=Ted|title=And So It Begins: Paramount, Netflix And Comcast Formally Submit Bids For Warner Bros. Discovery|url=https://deadline.com/2025/11/paramount-netflix-comcast-submit-wbd-bids-1236625396/|website=Deadline|date=November 20, 2025|access-date=November 22, 2025}}</ref> [[Starz Entertainment|Starz]] submitted a $25 billion bid for the Global Linear Networks division and 20% of the Streaming & Studios division.<ref>{{Cite web |last=James |first=Meg |date=November 20, 2025 |title=Warner Bros. auction poised to recast Hollywood with Paramount, Comcast and Netflix vying for the prize |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2025-11-20/warner-bros-selling-company-paramount-comcast-netflix-what-to-know |access-date=November 20, 2025 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |archive-date=November 20, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251120113320/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2025-11-20/warner-bros-selling-company-paramount-comcast-netflix-what-to-know |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bolies |first=Corbin |date=December 17, 2025 |title=Starz Placed $25 Billion Bid for All of Warner Bros. Discovery's Cable Networks |url=https://www.thewrap.com/starz-warner-bros-discovery-bid/ |access-date=December 17, 2025 |website=TheWrap |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226010225/https://www.thewrap.com/starz-warner-bros-discovery-bid/ |archive-date=December 26, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> 

After the initial round of bids, WBD solicited a second round of bids. On December 1, 2025, Netflix, Paramount and Comcast all once again submitted binding second-round bids, with Paramount submitting an all-cash $26.50 per share offer for the entire company.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=December 1, 2025 |title=Paramount Skydance's Latest Bid for Warner Bros. Discovery Backed by Three Middle Eastern Wealth Funds |url=https://variety.com/2025/biz/news/paramount-skydance-bid-warner-bros-discovery-arab-wealth-funds-1236597217/ |url-status= |website=Variety |access-date=December 1, 2025}}</ref> After the auction process concluded in December, [[Standard General]] was approached by Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders about a potential acquisition of WBD's Global Linear Networks division.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Whittock |first=Jesse |date=December 18, 2025 |title= Standard General Holds Talks Over Warner Bros. Discovery Cable TV Assets – FT|url=https://deadline.com/2025/12/hedge-fund-warner-bros-discovery-cable-tv-assets-ft-1236652310/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]] |access-date=December 18, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226010250/https://deadline.com/2025/12/hedge-fund-warner-bros-discovery-cable-tv-assets-ft-1236652310/ |archive-date=December 26, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

As the process moved to a final decision, Paramount sent a letter to Zaslav alleging that the sale had become "tilted" in favor of Netflix. The letter claimed that the WBD board had embarked on "a myopic process with a predetermined outcome", pointing to alleged conflicts of interest regarding the friendship of Zaslav and Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos and questioning whether the auction remained fair.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=December 4, 2025 |title=Paramount Skydance Alleges Warner Bros. Discovery Sales Process 'Has Been Tainted by Management Conflicts' That Favor Netflix Bid |url=https://variety.com/2025/biz/news/paramount-skydance-warner-bros-discovery-sale-tainted-management-conflicts-netflix-bid-1236599906/ |access-date=December 4, 2025 |website=Variety |archive-date=December 4, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251204162303/https://variety.com/2025/biz/news/paramount-skydance-warner-bros-discovery-sale-tainted-management-conflicts-netflix-bid-1236599906/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Boorstin |first1=Julia |last2=Rizzo |first2=Lillian |last3=Sherman |first3=Alex |last4=Faber |first4=David |author1-link=Julia Boorstin |author4-link=David Faber (journalist) |title=Paramount questions Warner Bros. Discovery on 'fairness and adequacy' of sale process: Read the full letter |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2025/12/04/paramount-questions-warner-bros-discovery-sale-process-letter.html |work=[[CNBC]] |date=December 4, 2025 |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260826191259/https://www.cnbc.com/2025/12/04/paramount-questions-warner-bros-discovery-sale-process-letter.html |archive-date=August 26, 2026 |access-date=July 28, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On December 5, 2025, multiple news outlets reported that Netflix had emerged as the leading bidder and had entered exclusive negotiations with WBD to acquire its studio and streaming business, despite objections from Paramount Skydance. Netflix announced the acquisition shortly after, which valued WBD at $82.7 billion enterprise value ($72.0 billion equity value and $59 billion of debt from [[Wells Fargo]], [[HSBC]], and [[BNP Paribas]]), and priced post-split Warner Bros. shares at US$27.75.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Grantham-Philips |first1=Wyatte |last2=Ott |first2=Matt |date=December 5, 2025 |title=Netflix to acquire Warner Bros. studio and streaming business for $72 billion |url=https://apnews.com/article/netflix-warner-acquisition-studio-hbo-streaming-f4884402cadfd07a99af0c8e4353bd83 |access-date=December 5, 2025 |website=Associated Press |archive-date=December 5, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205132404/https://apnews.com/article/netflix-warner-acquisition-studio-hbo-streaming-f4884402cadfd07a99af0c8e4353bd83|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Barnes |first1=Brook |last2=Hirsch |first2=Lauren |last3=Sperling |first3=Nicole |date=December 5, 2025 |title=Netflix to Buy Warner Bros. in $83 Billion Deal to Create a Streaming Giant |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/05/business/warner-brothers-discovery-netflix.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=December 5, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |archive-date=December 6, 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/05/business/warner-brothers-discovery-netflix.html |url-status=live}}</ref> The acquisition would mark a departure from Netflix's stated "builders, not buyers" strategy and a shift toward growth through acquisition. Analysts had not widely anticipated Netflix's participation in the auction process prior to the December reports.<ref>{{Cite web |first1=Harshita Mary |last1=Varghese |first2=Aditya |last2=Soni |first3=Dawn |last3=Chmielewski |date=December 5, 2025 |title=Netflix to buy Warner Bros Discovery's studios, streaming unit for $72 billion |url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/netflix-agrees-buy-warner-bros-discoverys-studios-streaming-division-2025-12-05/ |website=[[Reuters]] |language=en |access-date=December 14, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251206051627/https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/netflix-agrees-buy-warner-bros-discoverys-studios-streaming-division-2025-12-05/ |archive-date=December 6, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> Analysts also estimated that a merged Netflix–Warner Bros. entity would have controlled 30.3% of the U.S. streaming market.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Cobb|first=Kayla|date=December 5, 2025|title=Warner Bros. Discovery-Netflix Merger Would Account for 33% of US SVOD Market|url=https://www.thewrap.com/wbd-netflix-merger-streaming-market/|access-date=December 6, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205173422/https://www.thewrap.com/wbd-netflix-merger-streaming-market/|website=TheWrap|archive-date=December 5, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref>

Paramount argued that its bid would face fewer regulatory and antitrust obstacles than the Netflix deal, as a combination of Netflix and HBO Max would have represented about 43% of global subscription video-on-demand subscribers. The company also accused Netflix of "obfuscat[ing] its dominant position in streaming" by counting social networks such as [[Facebook]], [[TikTok]], and [[YouTube]] as part of its competition, reflecting "neither reality nor the historical practice of competition enforcers."<ref name="ParamountAttacksNetflix" /> It also warned that the Netflix deal would likely lead to fewer theatrical film releases,<ref name="ParamountAttacksNetflix">{{Cite web |last=Hayden|first=Erik|date=December 5, 2025|title=How Paramount Attacked Netflix's Bid for Warner Bros.|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/paramount-letter-netflix-comcast-warner-bros-1236442793/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251209005553/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/paramount-letter-netflix-comcast-warner-bros-1236442793/|archive-date=December 9, 2025|access-date=December 6, 2025|website=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> referring to public statements by Netflix executives who questioned the long-term role of movie theaters. It was noted that most of Netflix's theatrical releases had either been [[Limited theatrical release|limited releases]] intended primarily to secure awards eligibility, or alternative programming (such as a sing-along version of ''[[KPop Demon Hunters]]'', and event screenings of the ''[[Stranger Things]]'' [[Chapter Eight: The Rightside Up|series finale]])<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hibberd|first=James|date=October 23, 2025|title=Netflix's 'Stranger Things' Series Finale Officially Coming to Theaters, Despite Previous Statements|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/netflix-stranger-things-finale-theaters-tickets-1236408174/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251023142452/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/netflix-stranger-things-finale-theaters-tickets-1236408174/|archive-date=October 23, 2025|access-date=October 23, 2025|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref> that are not subject to theatrical windows.<ref name="ParamountPromisesToRelease" /> Sarandos later stated that Warner Bros. would operate "largely like it is today" and maintain a 45-day theatrical window for its releases if it were acquired by Netflix, as the studio generated "billions of dollars of theatrical revenue that we don't want to put at risk".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Spangler|first=Todd|date=January 16, 2026|title=Netflix to Keep Warner Bros. After the board of WBD endorsed Netflix's lower but previously signed agreement instead of a higher all-cash offer from Paramount Skydance, the company filed suit in the [[Delaware Court of Chancery]]. The complaint asked the court to require WBD to provide additional details about its decision-making process, including how it assessed the Netflix transaction, valued its remaining "Global Networks" business, and evaluated the risks and pricing of Paramount's competing tender offer. At the same time, Paramount indicated that it was prepared to pursue a proxy fight. The company announced plans to nominate its own slate of directors to WBD's board in an effort to encourage shareholders to support Paramount's bid rather than the agreement with Netflix.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rizzo |first=Lillian |date=January 12, 2026 |title=Paramount Skydance sues Warner Bros. During the litigation, Paramount Skydance asked WBD for more disclosure about valuations, debt assumptions, adviser analyses, and the board's reasoning for favoring the Netflix deal over Paramount's offer, as part of litigation tied to its takeover attempt.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldmsith |first=Jill |date=January 12, 2026 |title=Merger Math: Paramount Suit Wants WBD To Show Its Work |url=https://deadline.com/2026/01/paramount-lawsuit-warner-bros-discovery-merger-calculations-1236680919/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260114214710/https://deadline.com/2026/01/paramount-lawsuit-warner-bros-discovery-merger-calculations-1236680919/ |archive-date=January 14, 2026 |access-date=January 12, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref> The Delaware Court of Chancery declined to grant Paramount Skydance's request for expedited proceedings, but instead accepted to grant Netflix's request for expedited proceedings. The court's decision allowed WBD to continue pursuing the Netflix deal while Paramount Skydance's litigation proceeded on a standard timetable.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hatherly |first=Duane |date=January 15, 2026 |title=If you can't sue them, replace them: Paramount's new WBD play |url=https://www.mediaweek.com.au/paramount-launches-wbd-proxy-war-court-loss-jan-2026/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260122225207/https://www.mediaweek.com.au/paramount-launches-wbd-proxy-war-court-loss-jan-2026/ |archive-date=January 22, 2026 |access-date=January 15, 2026 |website=[[Mediaweek (Australia)|Mediaweek]]}}</ref> On January 13, 2026, Netflix amended its bid from a cash-and-stock deal to all-cash, while maintaining its $27.75 per share price.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler|first=Todd|date=January 13, 2026|title=Netflix Prepping All-Cash Bid for Warner Bros. Studios and HBO Max Amid Paramount Skydance Pressure: Report|url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/netflix-all-cash-offer-warner-bros-studios-streaming-1236630571/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260114113114/https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/netflix-all-cash-offer-warner-bros-studios-streaming-1236630571/|archive-date=January 14, 2026|access-date=January 13, 2026|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref>

On January 22, 2026, the [[U.S. Department of Justice]] (DOJ) launched an [[antitrust]] review of Netflix's proposed deal. WBD disclosed in a regulatory filing that both companies had received a formal "second request" for information from the [[United States Department of Justice Antitrust Division|DOJ's Antitrust Division]] on January 16, which paused the statutory waiting period and prevented the transaction from closing pending further review. The second request signaled heightened scrutiny of whether the transaction could lessen competition in streaming, film production, or television distribution markets.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brooks|first=Tyler|date=January 22, 2026|title=DOJ Opens Antitrust Review Into Netflix's Proposed $83 Billion Warner Bros. Acquisition|url=https://usaherald.com/doj-opens-antitrust-review-into-netflixs-proposed-83-billion-warner-bros-acquisition/|access-date=January 22, 2026|website=[[USA Herald]]<!-- Is this a reliable source? I've never heard of the publication, there is no Wikipedia article about it, and they offer "contract journalism", in which they are paid to write a story. they retain control over what they report in such stories, but is that an accepted practice for a reliable source? -->|archive-date=January 22, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260122230450/https://usaherald.com/doj-opens-antitrust-review-into-netflixs-proposed-83-billion-warner-bros-acquisition/|url-status=live}}</ref>
