=== Revised offers ===
On December 22, 2025, Paramount Skydance amended its offer to address investor concerns, including financing assurances backed by David Ellison's father [[Larry Ellison]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-22 |title=Larry Ellison pledges $40-billion personal guarantee for Paramount's Warner Bros. bid |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2025-12-22/larry-ellison-to-personally-back-paramount-bid-for-warner |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919010621/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2025-12-22/larry-ellison-to-personally-back-paramount-bid-for-warner |archive-date=September 19, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> WBD said it would review the revised proposal and advised shareholders to take no action while it evaluated the offer.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldsmith|first=Jill|date=December 22, 2025|title=WBD Advises Shareholders Not To Take Any Action As It Reviews Paramount's Amended Takeover Offer|url=https://deadline.com/2025/12/warner-bros-discovery-review-paramount-new-takeover-offer-1236655458/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226011459/https://deadline.com/2025/12/warner-bros-discovery-review-paramount-new-takeover-offer-1236655458/|archive-date=December 26, 2025|access-date=December 22, 2025|website=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]]}}</ref> 

Some shareholders said the revised bid still needed improvements.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Kerber|first1=Ross|last2=Kopecki|first2=Dawn|date=December 23, 2025|title=Paramount's new offer for Warner Bros is not sufficient, major investor says|url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/paramounts-new-offer-warner-bros-is-not-sufficient-major-investor-says-2025-12-23/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/paramounts-new-offer-warner-bros-is-not-sufficient-major-investor-says-2025-12-23/|archive-date=December 23, 2025|access-date=December 24, 2025|website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> [[Harris Associates]], which owned about 4% of WBD through its Oakmark funds, described the revised offer as improved but insufficient. Portfolio manager Alex Fitch said the competing bids from Paramount and Netflix appeared roughly comparable and that changing transactions would involve costs. He added that Paramount would need to offer stronger incentives to secure shareholder support.<ref>{{cite news|last=Kopecki|first=Dawn|date=December 23, 2025|title=Paramount's new offer for Warner Bros is not sufficient, major investor says|website=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/paramount-nominate-directors-election-warner-bros-discovery-files-lawsuit-2026-01-12/|access-date=January 15, 2026|archive-date=January 12, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260112181214/https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/paramount-nominate-directors-election-warner-bros-discovery-files-lawsuit-2026-01-12/|url-status=live}}</ref> Mario Gabelli, founder and chairman of [[GAMCO Investors]], said he was "highly likely" to tender his clients' shares to Paramount Skydance.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Manfredi |first=Lucas |date=December 10, 2025 |title=Mario Gabelli 'Highly Likely' to Tender Warner Bros. Discovery Shares to Paramount |url=https://www.thewrap.com/mario-gabelli-warner-bros-discovery-shares-paramount-tender/ |access-date=December 10, 2025 |website=TheWrap |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226011629/https://www.thewrap.com/mario-gabelli-warner-bros-discovery-shares-paramount-tender/ |archive-date=December 26, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> GAMCO holds approximately 5% of WBD's non-index institutional shares.<ref>{{cite news|last=Kerber|first=Rose|date=January 8, 2026|title=Some of Warner Bros biggest Investors are split on Paramount offer|website=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/some-warner-bros-biggest-investors-are-split-paramount-offer-2026-01-08/|access-date=January 15, 2026}}</ref>

On January 7, 2026, ''TheWrap'' reported that Pentwater Capital Management—WBD's seventh-largest shareholder—sent a letter to the board urging it to more fully engage with Paramount Skydance's amended proposal. Pentwater chief executive Matt Halbower told CNBC that he viewed Paramount's offer as economically superior to Netflix's, citing valuation and regulatory factors. He also questioned the board's stated concerns about financing risk and argued that Paramount's investors had the capacity to complete the transaction.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Manfredi|first=Luca|date=January 7, 2026|title=Warner Bros. Discovery Shareholder Pentwater Capital Management Says Paramount's Revised Bid Is 'Economically Superior' to Netflix|url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/pentwater-capital-management-paramount-warner-bros-bid-economically-superior/|access-date=January 8, 2026|website=The Wrap|archive-date=January 13, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260113004043/https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/pentwater-capital-management-paramount-warner-bros-bid-economically-superior/|url-status=live}}</ref> 

On January 16, 2026, British [[Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport|digital, culture, and media secretary]] [[Lisa Nandy]] met with David Ellison to discuss issues affecting the UK's film and television sector.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 16, 2026|title=UK minister met Paramount CEO Ellison in London on Thursday, source says|url=https://wiky.com/2026/01/16/uk-minister-met-paramount-ceo-ellison-in-london-on-thursday-source-says/|access-date=January 16, 2026|website=[[WIKY-FM]]|archive-date=January 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260117074021/https://wiky.com/2026/01/16/uk-minister-met-paramount-ceo-ellison-in-london-on-thursday-source-says/|url-status=live}}</ref> On February 5, 2026, Ellison published an open letter to the UK creative community outlining commitments tied to Paramount's bid for WBD, including increased content investment, continued theatrical releases, and preserving [[HBO]] as a distinct brand. Ellison described a Paramount–WBD combination as pro-competition, and criticized the rival Netflix deal as potentially creating excessive market power, a claim Netflix disputed. He also highlighted Paramount's UK operations and pledged support for competition and the creative workforce.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kanter|first=Jake|date=February 5, 2026|title=Paramount CEO David Ellison Takes Dig At 'Monopolistic' Netflix In Open Letter To UK Creatives About Warner Deal |url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/paramount-david-ellison-netflix-warner-open-letter-1236709783/ |access-date=February 5, 2026|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref>

On February 10, 2026, Paramount Skydance added incentives to its bid, stating that it would cover Netflix's $5.8 billion [[breakup fee]], and backstop a debt exchange that would relieve WBD of its obligations to its bondholders. As a display of confidence in the "speed and certainty of regulatory approval" for the deal, Paramount also offered a "ticking fee"—under which it would pay approximately $650 million per-quarter to WBD shareholders if the acquisition was not closed within 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Goldsmith|first=Jill|date=2026-02-10|title=Paramount Sweetens Offer For Warner Bros. Discovery|url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/paramount-sweetens-offer-warner-bros-discovery-1236714137/|access-date=2026-06-10|website=Deadline|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260908162611/https://deadline.com/2026/02/paramount-sweetens-offer-warner-bros-discovery-1236714137/|archive-date=September 8, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Soni|first=Aditya|date=February 10, 2026|title=Paramount sweetens Warner Bros bid with ticking fee, Netflix break-up fee cover|url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/paramount-revises-offer-warner-bros-with-25-cent-ticking-fee-2026-02-10/|access-date=February 10, 2026|website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> 

On February 11, 2026, [[Ancora Holdings]]—an [[activist shareholder]] with a stake valued at nearly $200 million—announced it would vote against the Netflix transaction, support Paramount Skydance's bid, and threatened to initiate a [[proxy fight]] if the board declined to engage with Paramount. Ancora argued that Paramount's amended proposal could qualify as a "superior proposal" under WBD's "rushed" and "flawed" agreement with Netflix, citing what it described as regulatory risks associated with the Netflix deal.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Forristal|first=Lauren|date=2026-02-11|title=Activist investor Ancora publicly opposes the WBD-Netflix deal|url=https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/11/activist-investor-ancora-publicly-opposes-the-wbd-netflix-deal/|access-date=2026-07-01|website=TechCrunch|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260909071044/https://techcrunch.com/2026/02/11/activist-investor-ancora-publicly-opposes-the-wbd-netflix-deal/|archive-date=September 9, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |date=February 11, 2026 |title=Activist Investor Slams WBD For Rushing Into 'Flawed' Netflix Deal, Tells Board To Engage With Paramount As Temperature Rises |url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/activist-investor-warner-bros-discovery-netflix-paramount-1236714881/ |access-date=February 11, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref>

=== Reopening negotiations with Paramount ===
On February 17, 2026, WBD said it would reopen negotiations with Paramount Skydance after Netflix granted Paramount a seven-day waiver to submit a "best and final" offer. WBD said Paramount had verbally agreed to raise its bid to at least $31 per share if talks resumed, which WBD accepted. The same day, David Ellison wrote to Senator [[Cory Booker]] arguing that Netflix's proposed acquisition would harm competition, and that Paramount Skydance's ownership would expand streaming and theatrical distribution. Ellison did not address most of Booker's questions regarding his communications with the Trump administration or potential changes to [[CNN]]. Also on February 17, Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos criticized Paramount's bid on CNBC, accusing the company of creating confusion for shareholders. Ancora said it would pursue a proxy fight to replace directors if WBD failed to adequately consider Paramount Skydance's offer.<ref>{{cite web|last=Goldsmith|first=Jill|date=February 17, 2026|title=Warner Board Says Paramount Agreed To Raise Offer To $31 A Share Or More If Two Sides Engaged|url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/warner-bros-discovery-says-paramount-agreed-to-higher-offer-1236726616/|access-date=February 17, 2026|website=Deadline Hollywood|archive-date=February 17, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260217125331/https://deadline.com/2026/02/warner-bros-discovery-says-paramount-agreed-to-higher-offer-1236726616/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Hayes|first=Dade|date=February 17, 2026|title=Ted Sarandos Accuses Paramount Of "Flooding The Zone With Confusion" In WBD Merger Saga|url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/netflix-ted-sarandos-paramount-warner-bros-merger-1236727718/|work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en-US|archive-date=February 18, 2026|access-date=February 18, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260218005022/https://deadline.com/2026/02/netflix-ted-sarandos-paramount-warner-bros-merger-1236727718/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Manfredi|first=Lucas|date=February 17, 2026|title=Warner Bros. Activist Investor Praises Board, Netflix for Reopening 'Necessary Discussions' With Paramount Skydance|url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/warner-bros-activist-investor-ancora-holdings-paramount-talks-reopened-reaction/|archive-url=https://archive.today/20260217213921/https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/business/warner-bros-activist-investor-ancora-holdings-paramount-talks-reopened-reaction/|archive-date=February 17, 2026|access-date=February 18, 2026|website=TheWrap|language=en-US}}</ref>

Growing investor opposition strengthened Paramount's position. Pentwater Capital, a hedge fund and significant WBD shareholder, stated publicly that Paramount's offer was economically more favorable when accounting for regulatory risk and deal certainty. The firm also held discussions with Paramount about potentially supporting a challenge to WBD's board.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Babu |first1=Juby |last2=Kopecki |first2=Dawn |last3=Herbst-Bayliss |first3=Svea |url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/paramount-eyes-pentwater-capitals-halbower-warner-bros-board-seat-2026-02-12/ |title=Paramount eyes Pentwater Capital's Halbower for Warner Bros' board seat |work=Reuters |date=February 12, 2026 |access-date=February 12, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Vinn |first1=Milana |last2=Kopecki |first2=Dawn |url=https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-02-17/warner-bros-rejects-paramounts-revised-offer-but-gives-studio-a-week-to-negotiate-better-deal |title=Warner Bros Rejects Revised Paramount Bid, but Remains Open to a Final Offer |agency=Reuters |work=[[U.S. News & World Report]] |date=February 17, 2026 |access-date=February 17, 2026}}</ref> On February 20, 2026, Paramount said it had satisfied a [[Hart–Scott–Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act|Hart–Scott–Rodino]] (HSR) waiting period related to its unsolicited bid for WBD and argued that there was no U.S. statutory barrier to completing the transaction. Netflix disputed Paramount's characterization, stating that the expiration of an HSR waiting period does not indicate regulatory approval and that further review could still occur. The exchange reflected competing public messaging by Paramount and Netflix as regulators continued examining the proposed deals.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Goldsmith|first=Jill|date=February 20, 2026|title=Paramount Clears A U.S. Antitrust Hurdle In Bid For Warner Bros. Discovery; Netflix Notes Rival Is 'A Long Way' From Getting Regulatory Signoffs — Update|url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/paramount-clears-us-antitrust-hurdle-warner-bros-discovery-1236730560/|work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en-US|archive-date=February 20, 2026|access-date=February 20, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260220152229/https://deadline.com/2026/02/paramount-clears-us-antitrust-hurdle-warner-bros-discovery-1236730560/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On February 22, 2026, the DOJ issued a civil investigative demand of Netflix and WBD to investigate their offer, arguing that it threatened to create a "monopoly".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patten |first=Dominic |date=February 22, 2026 |title=Netflix Officially Under DOJ Antitrust Scrutiny "To Create A Monopoly" With Warner Bros Merger; Feds Want Details From Producers & Filmmakers On Streamer's Leverage |url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/doj-netflix-wb-deal-antitrust-probe-1236731978/ |access-date=February 22, 2026 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-date=February 22, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260222183928/https://deadline.com/2026/02/doj-netflix-wb-deal-antitrust-probe-1236731978/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On February 23, 2026, Paramount's insiders told ''Variety'' that Paramount's revised offer for WBD would likely come in at $32 per share.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Spangler|first=Todd|date=February 23, 2026|title=Paramount Is Expected to Raise Price of Warner Bros. Discovery Bid. Will Netflix Walk Away?|url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-warner-bros-discovery-higher-bid-will-netflix-walk-away-1236670140/|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=February 23, 2026|language=en-US|archive-date=February 23, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260223140919/https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-warner-bros-discovery-higher-bid-will-netflix-walk-away-1236670140/|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Netflix exit, shareholder approval ===
On February 24, 2026, WBD stated it had a received a revised offer from Paramount and was reviewing it in consultation with its financial and legal advisors.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |date=February 24, 2026 |title=Warner Bros. Discovery Reviewing Paramount's Revised Takeover Offer |url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/warner-bros-discovery-reviewing-paramount-revised-proposal-1236734321/ |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=February 25, 2026 |language=en-US |archive-date=February 25, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260225024742/https://deadline.com/2026/02/warner-bros-discovery-reviewing-paramount-revised-proposal-1236734321/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Two days later, WBD confirmed that it considered Paramount's increased bid to be superior to Netflix's current offer, triggering a four-business-day period during which Netflix could improve its offer. Paramount's latest bid was reported to be valued at $31 per share.<ref>{{cite web |last=Grantham-Philips |first=Wyatte |title=Warner Bros. Discovery deems Paramount's takeover bid superior to Netflix deal |url=https://www.local10.com/news/2026/02/26/warner-bros-discovery-deems-paramounts-takeover-bid-superior-to-netflix-deal/ |website=WPLG Local 10 |date=February 26, 2026 |access-date=February 26, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260312140757/https://www.local10.com/news/national/2026/02/26/netflix-walks-away-from-warner-bros-deal-clearing-the-path-for-paramount/|archive-date=March 12, 2026|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Maas |first1=Jennifer |last2=Littlejohn |first2=Cynthia |url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/netflix-declines-raise-bid-warner-bros-discovery-1236674149/ |title=Paramount Skydance Poised to Acquire Warner Bros. Discovery After Netflix Bows Out of Bidding War |work=Variety |date=February 26, 2026 |access-date=February 27, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260226232001/https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/netflix-declines-raise-bid-warner-bros-discovery-1236674149/ |archive-date=February 26, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Netflix subsequently declined to increase its bid, and Sarandos and Greg Peters released a statement stating that the deal was "no longer financially attractive".<ref>{{cite web |title=Netflix Declines to Raise Offer for Warner Bros. |url=https://about.netflix.com/en/news/netflix-declines-to-raise-offer-for-warner-bros |website=Netflix |date=February 26, 2026 |access-date=February 26, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260226230236/https://about.netflix.com/en/news/netflix-declines-to-raise-offer-for-warner-bros |archive-date=February 26, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/netflix-declines-to-raise-offer-for-warner-bros-1236738005/ |title=That's All, Folks: Netflix Walks Away From Warner Bros., Refusing To Raise Offer |work=Deadline Hollywood |date=February 26, 2026 |access-date=February 27, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260227004857/https://deadline.com/2026/02/netflix-declines-to-raise-offer-for-warner-bros-1236738005/ |archive-date=February 27, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Weprin |first=Alex |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/netflix-backs-out-warners-deal-paramount-win-1236516763/ |title=Netflix Backs Out of Warner Bros. Bidding, Paramount Set to Win |work=The Hollywood Reporter |date=February 26, 2026 |access-date=February 27, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260227000733/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/netflix-backs-out-warners-deal-paramount-win-1236516763/ |archive-date=February 27, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The next day, Paramount Skydance formally announced its intent to acquire WBD for $31 per share, valuing the company at around $110 billion. The deal was expected to be completed by the third quarter of 2026 at the earliest, pending regulatory and shareholder approval.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |date=February 27, 2026 |title=Massive Merger Confirmed: Paramount And WBD Reveal Details Of $110 Billion Deal |url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/massive-merger-confirmed-paramount-and-wbd-reveal-details-1236738785/ |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=February 27, 2026 |language=en-US |archive-date=February 27, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260227220450/https://deadline.com/2026/02/massive-merger-confirmed-paramount-and-wbd-reveal-details-1236738785/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The ''Wall Street Journal'' reported that $24 billion of the $110.9 billion equity acquisition would be funded by the sovereign wealth funds of [[Saudi Arabia]], [[Qatar]] and the [[United Arab Emirates]]. A Paramount filing with the [[Federal Communications Commission]] (FCC) stated that it would be 49.5% foreign-owned following the acquisition, and that these foreign stakeholders would not have voting power.<ref name="FCCFundingOK">{{Cite news |last=Hayes |first=Dade |date=April 27, 2026 |title=Paramount, In Request For FCC Funding OK, Notes It Will Be 49.5% Foreign-Owned After WBD Merger |url=https://deadline.com/2026/04/paramount-fcc-request-wbd-merger-middle-east-1236873732/ |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=April 27, 2026 |language=en-US}}</ref> Paramount is also raising $44.5 billion in secured debt to finance the purchase and repay "certain existing debt".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |date=2026-09-24 |title=Paramount Moves Ahead With $7.5 Billion Debt Raise, Part Of Package To Finance WBD Acquisition |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-starts-raising-debt-to-finance-wbd-deal-1237112515/ |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260924184647/https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-starts-raising-debt-to-finance-wbd-deal-1237112515/ |archive-date=September 24, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |date=2026-09-28 |title=Paramount Woos Investors With $44 Billion Debt Sale To Finance WBD Deal |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-woos-bond-investors-judge-weighs-warner-deal-1237115650/ |access-date=2026-09-30 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260930070200/https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-woos-bond-investors-judge-weighs-warner-deal-1237115650/ |archive-date=September 30, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

During a conference call on March 2, Ellison stated that the merger was "not about consolidation", but to "expand our reach and enhance our ability to create the world's most compelling stories and experiences." Ellison confirmed that there were plans to merge Paramount+ with HBO Max, and that HBO would continue to operate with creative independence, citing its status as a "crown jewel" that had produced "some of the most powerful stories told over generations."<ref name="SweepingVision">{{cite web |last=Weprin |first=Alex |date=March 2, 2026 |title=David Ellison Unveils Sweeping Vision for Warner Bros: 'This Is About Reinventing the Business' |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/david-ellison-talks-warner-bros-deal-comments-1236519395/ |website=The Hollywood Reporter |publisher= |access-date=March 17, 2026 |archive-date=March 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260307184709/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/david-ellison-talks-warner-bros-deal-comments-1236519395/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="OneStreamer">{{cite web |last=Maglio |first=Tony |date=March 2, 2026 |title=HBO Max and Paramount+ Will Become One Streamer |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/hbo-max-paramount-plus-one-streaming-service-1236519451/ |website=The Hollywood Reporter |publisher= |access-date=March 18, 2026}}</ref> He also stated that the company would continue to license and produce content to and with third-parties.<ref name="SweepingVision" /><ref name="OneStreamer" />

A shareholder vote on the deal was scheduled for April 23, 2026; the advisory firm [[Institutional Shareholder Services]] recommended that shareholders reject a $886 million [[golden parachute]] offer by Zaslav, calling it "extraordinary".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |date=April 9, 2026 |title=Leading Shareholder Advisor ISS Backs WBD-Paramount Merger But Slams David Zaslav's "Windfall" Payout |url=https://deadline.com/2026/04/david-zaslav-golden-parachute-warner-bros-paramount-merger-1236785413/ |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=April 9, 2026 |language=en-US |archive-date=April 9, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260409124746/https://deadline.com/2026/04/david-zaslav-golden-parachute-warner-bros-paramount-merger-1236785413/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On April 9, Paramount completed the [[syndicated loan|syndication]] of a [[bridge loan|bridge]] facility and entered into permanent financing transactions with a group of 18 lenders to support the deal.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Goldsmith |first=Jill |date=April 9, 2026 |title=Paramount Seals, Refines Debt Financing As It Moves Towards WBD Deal |url=https://deadline.com/2026/04/paramount-debt-financing-warner-bros-discovery-merger-1236785653/ |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |access-date=April 9, 2026 |language=en-US |archive-date=April 10, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260410031113/https://deadline.com/2026/04/paramount-debt-financing-warner-bros-discovery-merger-1236785653/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On April 15, 2026, Senator [[Cory Booker]] held a spotlight hearing on the potential impacts of the proposed acquisition. The hearing included testimony by filmmaker [[David Borenstein]], actor [[Mark Ruffalo]], attorney [[Katie Phang]], Mara Verheyden-Hilliard of the [[Partnership for Civil Justice Fund]], and WGA East director of legal services Michael Isaac; Ellison was invited to testify at the hearing, but was unable to attend due to a death in his family.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Johnson |first=Ted |date=April 14, 2026 |title=Cory Booker To Hold "Spotlight" Hearing On Paramount-Warner Bros. On April 23, 2026, WBD's shareholders voted to approve the sale of the company to Paramount Skydance, but voted against compensation packages for Zaslav and other WBD executives.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=April 23, 2026 |title=Warner Bros. On May 12, 2026, Paramount's chief legal officer [[Makan Delrahim]] told [[California Attorney General]] [[Rob Bonta]] that the acquisition would "help drive meaningful improvements for movie theaters and their audiences" by "broadening theatrical distribution to tap into the magic of the moviegoing experience and create momentum behind films before they reach streaming services", reiterating Ellison's pledge for the company to release 30 films per-year with a theatrical window of at least 45 days. He contrasted the acquisition to the previous [[acquisition of 21st Century Fox by Disney]], stating that Paramount would not consolidate studios or reduce its theatrical output like Disney, and that its offer was "informed" by a post-[[COVID-19 pandemic|COVID-19]] market "with three streaming giants dominating audience attention on the one hand, and theaters slowly reemerging as a critical marketing engine and cultural phenomenon that can support Paramount–WBD's efforts to compete in the entertainment ecosystem on the other."<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 12, 2026 |title=Paramount Defends Warner Bros. Discovery Merger In Letter To California AG, Says Combined Companies Will Have Incentive To Boost Theatrical |url=https://deadline.com/2026/05/paramount-warner-bros-california-attorney-general-letter-1236899772/ |access-date=May 12, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en}}</ref>

On May 14, 2026, in a letter co-signed by House Democrats [[Sam Liccardo]] and [[Deborah Ross (politician)|Deborah Ross]], members of [[European Parliament]] [[Nathalie Loiseau]], [[Brando Benifei]], and [[Andreas Schwab]] warned that the deal would undergo a "rigorous and comprehensive review" by EU officials, as it threatened to "substantially lessen competition across interconnected markets, including film and television production, content licensing, theatrical distribution, and streaming services".<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 14, 2026 |title=U.S., EU lawmakers pledge European scrutiny of Paramount's WBD deal |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/14/paramount-wbd-congress-eu-david-ellison.html |access-date=May 14, 2026 |website=[[CNBC]] |language=en |archive-date=May 14, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260514115501/https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/14/paramount-wbd-congress-eu-david-ellison.html |url-status=live}}</ref> In Europe, it was also noted that the merger could create issues with Paramount's [[SkyShowtime]] joint venture, as HBO Max operates in nearly all of its markets, while Comcast and Paramount are subject to non-compete clauses in the markets where SkyShowtime operates.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 15, 2026 |title=Paramount's Warner Bros. During a lunch reception after WBD's [[upfronts]] presentation on May 14 (which ''Deadline'' writer Dade Hayes said was jokingly referred to as "[[the Last Supper]]" by a greeter), chief revenue officer Bruce Campbell acknowledged an incoming "year of change" for the company, and told his colleagues and the press that "this team is up for the challenge".<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 14, 2026 |title=WBD Staffers Raise Upfront Glass As Yet Another Corporate Merger Looms |url=https://deadline.com/2026/05/wbd-paramount-merger-upfronts-1236901683/ |access-date=May 14, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en}}</ref> On May 19, it was reported that the acquisition could be completed as early as mid-July.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 19, 2026 |title=Paramount Hopes to Finalize Warner Bros. On May 25, 2026, the sale was approved by the [[Antimonopoly Committee of Ukraine]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 25, 2026 |title=Ukrainian Antimonopoly Committee approves historic Paramount–Warner Bros merger |url=https://newsukraine.rbc.ua/news/ukrainian-antimonopoly-committee-approves-1779713377.html |access-date=May 25, 2026 |website=[[RBC-Ukraine]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260525191724/https://newsukraine.rbc.ua/news/ukrainian-antimonopoly-committee-approves-1779713377.html |archive-date=May 25, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, Ellison met with members of the DOJ to discuss the deal, once again reiterating the company's plans for theatrical releases.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Exclusive: Paramount appears to sway DOJ staff on Warner Bros. takeover |url=https://www.semafor.com/article/05/26/2026/paramount-appears-to-sway-doj-staff-on-warner-bros-takeover |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260817121145/https://www.semafor.com/article/05/26/2026/paramount-appears-to-sway-doj-staff-on-warner-bros-takeover |archive-date=August 17, 2026 |access-date=2026-09-07 |work=Semafor |language=en |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Lawsuit and delay ===
On July 13, 2026, the state of California alongside 11 other states filed an antitrust lawsuit in the [[U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California]], seeking to halt the acquisition. The motion argued that the combined company would control over a quarter of U.S. box office and cable television revenue respectively,  giving it undue leverage over film exhibitors and television providers that could increase costs to consumers. The suit also argued that since Paramount's previously announced commitments were not legally-binding, the company could still "harm competition by reducing investment and innovation, degrading quality, and raising the price of those 30 films they produce".<ref name="StatesBlock" /><ref name="WGACinemaUnited" />

A Paramount spokesperson stated that the company would "vigorously defend" itself in court, arguing that the lawsuit was based on a "fundamentally flawed application of the antitrust laws", and that not approving the acquisition would result in "harm [to] entertainment workers who have already suffered over recent years as technology has disrupted their livelihood and cost California tens of thousands of entertainment jobs."<ref name="StatesBlock">{{Cite web|last=Johnson|first=Ted|date=2026-07-13|title=California, Other States Sue To Block Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger|url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/state-antitrust-lawsuit-paramount-warner-bros-1236980723/|access-date=2026-07-13|website=Deadline|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260913005332/https://deadline.com/2026/07/state-antitrust-lawsuit-paramount-warner-bros-1236980723/|archive-date=September 13, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="WGACinemaUnited">{{Cite web|date=July 13, 2026|title=WGA, Cinema United Praise States For Suing To Block "Dangerous" Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger|url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/hollywood-industry-react-paramount-wbd-merger-lawsuit-1236981045/|access-date=2026-07-13|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260713184954/https://deadline.com/2026/07/hollywood-industry-react-paramount-wbd-merger-lawsuit-1236981045/|archive-date=July 13, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> On July 14, 2026, the WGA filed its own antitrust lawsuit, arguing that the reduction of competition would give Paramount "both the incentive and the ability to lower costs by suppressing writers' wages and reducing output."<ref>{{Cite web|last=Campione|first=Katie|date=2026-07-14|title=WGA Sues To Block Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger|url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/wga-sues-over-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-merger-1236982226/|access-date=2026-07-14|website=Deadline|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714213205/https://deadline.com/2026/07/wga-sues-over-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-merger-1236982226/|archive-date=July 14, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

A court hearing for the states<nowiki>''</nowiki> lawsuit was set to begin on July 17, 2026; the case was assigned to Judge [[Araceli Martínez-Olguín]], after Paramount requested the recusal of Judge [[P. Casey Pitts]] due to his prior work as legal counsel for the WGA.<ref>{{Cite web|date=July 15, 2026|title=Paramount Seeks Recusal Of Judge Assigned To State AGs' Antitrust Challenge To Warner Bros. Discovery Merger|url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/paramount-judge-recusal-warner-bros-antitrust-case-1236983206/|access-date=2026-07-15|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260715194007/https://deadline.com/2026/07/paramount-judge-recusal-warner-bros-antitrust-case-1236983206/|archive-date=July 15, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=July 15, 2026|title=Paramount Gets New Judge In State AGs Antitrust Suit|url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/paramount-new-judge-state-ags-antitrust-suit-warner-bros-merger-1236983569/|access-date=2026-07-16|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en}}</ref>

On July 20, 2026, Judge Martínez-Olguín issued a two-week temporary restraining order prohibiting Paramount from consummating the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition. She ruled that the proposed transaction was likely to violate US antitrust laws, citing the plaintiffs' evidence that the combined company "will possess substantial market share in the wide-release theatrical distribution market."<ref>{{Cite web|last=Johnson|first=Ted|date=2026-07-20|title=Judge Grants Order To Pause Paramount-WBD Merger|url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/paramount-warner-bros-lawsuit-restraining-order-1236998321/|access-date=2026-07-20|website=Deadline|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260726103714/https://deadline.com/2026/07/paramount-warner-bros-lawsuit-restraining-order-1236998321/|archive-date=July 26, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=July 20, 2026|title=Judge says Paramount and Warner must halt merger for at least 2 weeks, granting states' request|url=https://abc7.com/post/judge-says-paramount-warner-halt-merger-least-weeks-granting-states-request/19544810/|access-date=2026-07-20|website=[[KABC-TV]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720183007/https://abc7.com/post/judge-says-paramount-warner-halt-merger-least-weeks-granting-states-request/19544810/|archive-date=July 20, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

On July 22, 2026, the sale was approved by the [[European Commission]]; it found that the acquisition would not significantly reduce competition in film production, content licensing, television broadcasting, or streaming. However, the Commission took issue with Paramount's ownership of [[United International Pictures]] (UIP)—an international  [[Film distributor|distribution]] joint venture with [[Universal Pictures]] that operates in 19 [[European Economic Area]] (EEA) territories—arguing that distributing Warner Bros. films through UIP would lead to [[market concentration]] in those markets. As a condition of the acquisition, Paramount agreed to divest its stake in UIP to Universal within 13 months of the sale's closure, and to—for 10 years following the acquisition—not enter into any distribution agreements with Universal within the EEA, nor enter into distribution agreements for Warner Bros. films in the 19 aforementioned territories with companies who also distribute Universal or Disney films.<ref>{{Cite web|date=July 22, 2026|title=Paramount's Takeover Of Warner Bros. Discovery Gets EU Greenlight|url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/paramount-warner-bros-eu-approval-1236999973/|access-date=2026-07-22|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260722201956/https://deadline.com/2026/07/paramount-warner-bros-eu-approval-1236999973/|archive-date=July 22, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Rizzo|first=Lillian|date=2026-07-22|title=EU antitrust regulators clear Paramount-WBD merger as it faces challenge by U.S. states|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/22/european-commission-paramount-wbd-approval.html|access-date=2026-07-22|website=CNBC|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260722210927/https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/22/european-commission-paramount-wbd-approval.html|archive-date=July 22, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Chee |first=Foo Yun |date=2026-07-22 |title=Paramount secures EU nod for $110 billion Warner Bros deal, US hurdles ahead |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/eu-regulators-clear-with-conditions-paramounts-110-billion-bid-warner-bros-2026-07-22/ |access-date=2026-09-17 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-07-23 |title=EU clears the Paramount-Warner merger, subject to distribution remedies |url=https://cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/493622/ |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=Cineuropa |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260917151641/https://cineuropa.org/en/newsdetail/493622/ |archive-date=September 17, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On July 23, 2026, Judge Martínez-Olguín extended the temporary restraining order through August 17, 2026 in order to provide more time for legal proceedings.<ref>{{Cite web|date=July 23, 2026|title=Judge Extends Temporary Restraining Order Pausing Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger|url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/paramount-warner-bros-merger-judge-extends-order-1237001966/|access-date=2026-07-23|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260725085905/https://deadline.com/2026/07/paramount-warner-bros-merger-judge-extends-order-1237001966/|archive-date=July 25, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, Paramount Skydance entered a joint stipulation promising to not complete the WBD acquisition until a ruling in the states' case or June 1, 2027, whichever comes first.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Salinas|first=Sara|date=2026-07-24|title=Paramount agrees to delay WBD acquisition to as late as June 2027 amid legal challenge|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/24/paramount-wbd-merger-delay.html|access-date=2026-07-24|website=CNBC|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260907063712/https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/24/paramount-wbd-merger-delay.html|archive-date=September 7, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Maddaus|first=Gene|date=2026-07-24|title=Paramount Agrees to Postpone Warner Bros. Merger Until After Antitrust Trial|url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-warner-bros-merger-postpone-antitrust-trial-1236820601/|access-date=2026-07-24|website=Variety|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260907103356/https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-warner-bros-merger-postpone-antitrust-trial-1236820601/|archive-date=September 7, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> As per its agreement, Paramount will become subject to a "ticking fee" beginning in October 2026, requiring that Paramount pay WBD approximately $7 million per-day as a penalty until it completes the acquisition.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 3, 2026 |title=Careful what you bid for: The Ellisons' Paramount/WBD deal is slipping toward a costly legal and financial cliff |url=https://fortune.com/2026/08/03/paramount-warner-ellisons-careful-what-you-bid-for/ |access-date=2026-08-03 |website=[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260803172041/https://fortune.com/2026/08/03/paramount-warner-ellisons-careful-what-you-bid-for/ |archive-date=August 3, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=July 23, 2026|title=The Paramount-Warner Bros. Clock Is Ticking: What's Next for the Megamerger Amid Antitrust Battle With States?|url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/paramount-warner-bros-whats-next-state-antitrust-lawsuit-1236819518/|access-date=2026-07-23|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260908004103/https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/paramount-warner-bros-whats-next-state-antitrust-lawsuit-1236819518/|archive-date=September 8, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=2026-09-08 |title=Paramount Repeats Demand That States and WGA Post $1.88 Billion Bond Over Warner Bros. Merger Delay, After AGs Argue Company Is Trying to 'Offload Its Responsibility' for Ticking Fees |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-rdemands-states-wga-post-bond-warner-bros-merger-delay-1236855184/ |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260909082227/https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-rdemands-states-wga-post-bond-warner-bros-merger-delay-1236855184/ |archive-date=September 9, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On August 1, 2026, it was reported that the office of California governor [[Gavin Newsom]] had pushed for attorney general [[Rob Bonta]] to seek an out-of-court resolution of the lawsuit, expressing concern that blocking the acquisition would harm the state's job market.<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Toonkel|first1=Jessica|last2=Collins|first2=Eliza|date=2026-07-31|title=Exclusive {{!}} Newsom Expresses Concerns About State Antitrust Suit Against Paramount|url=https://www.wsj.com/business/media/newsom-expresses-concerns-about-state-antitrust-suit-against-paramount-1bc20411|access-date=2026-07-31|work=Wall Street Journal|language=en-US|issn=0099-9660}}</ref> On August 4, 2026, Judge Martínez-Olguín scheduled a trial for the WBD–Paramount antitrust case for March 2027.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Johnson|first=Ted|date=2026-08-04|title=Judge Sets Paramount-WBD Antitrust Trial For March|url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/paramount-warner-bros-trial-1237016438/|access-date=2026-08-04|website=Deadline|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260804211313/https://deadline.com/2026/08/paramount-warner-bros-trial-1237016438/|archive-date=August 4, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> In a ''New York Times'' editorial the same day, David Ellison wrote that he felt the lawsuit was actually over whether he could be trusted as owner of CNN, reiterating that Paramount's news divisions "will continue to answer to the facts and to all the people they serve — not to any party or cause", and that "I believe that anyone who oversees a news organization [..] shouldn't put a finger on the scale, especially on matters involving his own company."<ref>{{Cite web|date=August 4, 2026|title=David Ellison Says Opposition to Paramount-Warner Bros. Is Over His Control of CNN, Claims He Will Not 'Bend Newsrooms to My Views'|url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/david-ellison-cnn-paramount-warner-bros-trusted-steward-1236827405/|access-date=2026-08-04|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260804140617/https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/david-ellison-cnn-paramount-warner-bros-trusted-steward-1236827405/|archive-date=August 4, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> In an earnings call, Zaslav stated that despite the uncertain fate of the acquisition, WBD's culture and work ethic had been "inspiring", and that "our focus has been 'how do we drive a stronger company to meet our business plan and deliver a stronger and higher-growth company to PSKY and David, so that Paramount coming together with Warner Bros. is even stronger?'"<ref>{{Cite web|date=August 6, 2026|title=Zaslav Admits Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Saga Has Been 'Challenging' for Employees but Claims Work Ethic Is 'Inspiring'|url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/zaslav-paramount-warner-bros-merger-challenging-employees-inspiring-1236829027/|access-date=2026-08-06|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260806134330/https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/zaslav-paramount-warner-bros-merger-challenging-employees-inspiring-1236829027/|archive-date=August 6, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

On August 6, 2026, the acquisition was approved by British authorities, with Paramount agreeing to legally-binding concessions with Nandy prohibiting it from combining linear and on-demand services for five years, and requiring it to maintain editorial independence among its news and children's divisions, and maintain its commitments to UK-produced programming for [[5 (British TV channel)|5]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Savage|first=Michael|date=2026-08-06|title=Paramount concessions lead UK to approve takeover of Warner Bros|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/aug/06/paramount-warner-bros-uk-approve-takeover-lisa-nandy|access-date=2026-08-06|work=The Guardian|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Block the Merger—an industry group opposed to the acquisition—argued that these concessions "[lend] powerful credibility" to the states' lawsuit.<ref>{{Cite web|date=August 7, 2026|title=Paramount's Warner Concessions In UK Give "Powerful Credibility" To U.S. Lawsuit, Says Anti-Merger Group|url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/paramount-warner-concessions-credibility-to-us-lawsuit-1237028488/|access-date=2026-08-07|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260907210758/https://deadline.com/2026/08/paramount-warner-concessions-credibility-to-us-lawsuit-1237028488/|archive-date=September 7, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

==== Threats by Paramount to leave California, demand for a bond ====
On August 11, 2026, it was reported that Ellison was discussing the possibility of relocating Paramount out of California as early as October if AG Bonta refused to negotiate a settlement. Bonta released a statement arguing that this threat was "another attempt to blackmail the state into letting an illegal deal through", while the WGA stated that it "further prove[d] the danger of [Paramount's] outsized power over the industry and what that will mean for writers and the creative community."<ref>{{Cite web|date=August 12, 2026|title=WGA Says David Ellison's Threat That Paramount Will Leave California Over AG's Antitrust Lawsuit "Proves The Danger Of Its Outsized Power"|url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/wga-ellison-threat-leave-california-paramount-merger-suit-1237031575/|access-date=2026-08-12|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260812125857/https://deadline.com/2026/08/wga-ellison-threat-leave-california-paramount-merger-suit-1237031575/|archive-date=August 12, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=August 11, 2026|title=David Ellison Told Top Execs Paramount Will Exit California If AG Refuses To Negotiate Settlement In WBD Merger Suit|url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/david-ellison-exit-california-wbd-merger-suit-1237031004/|access-date=2026-08-11|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260830231810/https://deadline.com/2026/08/david-ellison-exit-california-wbd-merger-suit-1237031004/|archive-date=August 30, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> When questioned on the topic at a ''[[Politico]]'' conference the next day, Delrahim commented that "there's a point at which where you have a duty, a [[fiduciary duty]] to your shareholders, and those are the factors you consider", and that if he were governor of California, "I wouldn't want to lose Hollywood from the state. I wouldn't want to lose a major company like Paramount to another state."<ref>{{Cite web|last=Katz|first=A. J.|date=2026-08-13|title=Paramount Unwilling to Sell CNN as Industry Pushes for Settlement Concessions|url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/paramount-cnn-not-for-sale-warner-bros-discovery-deal/|access-date=2026-08-13|website=TheWrap|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260907113942/https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/paramount-cnn-not-for-sale-warner-bros-discovery-deal/|archive-date=September 7, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 12, 2026|title=Paramount says CNN sale 'on the table' to resolve California suit over Warner Bros deal|url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/paramount-says-cnn-sale-on-table-resolve-california-suit-over-warner-bros-deal-2026-08-12/|access-date=2026-08-12|website=[[Reuters]]|language=en}}</ref> The company had contemplated a relocation to either Georgia, Tennessee, or Texas.<ref name="ExitThreat">{{Cite web |last=Dolak |first=Kevin |date=2026-09-12 |title=Leaked Report Details Fallout if Paramount Follows Through on California Exit Threat |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/paramount-warner-brothers-california-exit-threat-economy-1236699278/ |access-date=2026-09-13 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260913060213/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/paramount-warner-brothers-california-exit-threat-economy-1236699278/ |archive-date=September 13, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On August 14, 2026, the sale was approved by authorities in Mexico. Paramount pushed for a settlement of the US federal lawsuit, arguing that the state attorneys general had roadblocked a transaction that has been approved by the US and 67 other countries, and would rather "inflict harm without benefit to their own constituents" than "support a stronger Hollywood and deliver tangible commitments to invest in for the benefit of labor, talent and other industry participants."<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 14, 2026 |title=Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Gets Mexico's Approval, Leaving States' Lawsuit as the Only Barrier Left |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-warner-bros-mexicos-settle-ellison-1236834861/ |access-date=2026-08-14 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |language=en |last=Maddaus |first=Gene |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260815004533/https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-warner-bros-mexicos-settle-ellison-1236834861/ |archive-date=August 15, 2026 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On August 17, 2026, Paramount Skydance demanded that the states and the WGA place a $1.88 billion [[Bond (finance)|bond]] to cover the ticking fee among other regulatory and legal costs, citing obligations under the [[Clayton Act]] and section 65(c) of the [[Federal Rules of Civil Procedure]]; this bond was calculated based on the ticking fee and the scheduled date of the trial. Bonta once again accused Paramount Skydance of blackmail, arguing that that Paramount and Warner Bros. willfully negotiated the ticking fee in the sale agreement despite knowing that the transaction would face regulatory scrutiny.<ref>{{Cite web|date=August 17, 2026|title=Put Up Or Shut Up! Paramount Demands A Very, Very Big Bond From AGs & WGA Over Costs Of "Roadblock" Antitrust Suit On WBD Merger|url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/paramount-merger-antitrust-suit-bond-1237043023/|access-date=2026-08-17|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260817183808/https://deadline.com/2026/08/paramount-merger-antitrust-suit-bond-1237043023/|archive-date=August 17, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> It was also argued that the bond did not have to be placed unless it was proven that the preliminary injunction was "improvidently granted".<ref name="StatesShouldPay">{{Cite web |last=Lindsay |first=Benjamin |date=2026-09-15 |title=Trump's DOJ Says States Should Pay Paramount's $1.88 Billion Bond |url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/doj-backs-paramount-demand-states-pay-merger-bond/ |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=TheWrap |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260917214721/https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/doj-backs-paramount-demand-states-pay-merger-bond/ |archive-date=September 17, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On August 24, 2026, Bonta told ''[[TheWrap]]'' that he would be open to resume negotiating with Paramount Skydance if they stopped "disclosing confidential information from our discussions, but misrepresenting it to the press". Bonta said that the states did not want purely "behavioral" concessions, and suggested the possibility of "structural" remedies such as divesting a "significant" number of its basic cable networks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Manfredi |first=Lucas |date=2026-08-24 |title=Rob Bonta Says Warner Bros. Merger Settlement Talks Could Happen This Week if Paramount Shuts Down Leaks {{!}} Exclusive |url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/business/california-attorney-general-rob-bonta-paramount-warner-bros-merger-lawsuit-interview/ |access-date=2026-09-08 |website=TheWrap |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260908220835/https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/business/california-attorney-general-rob-bonta-paramount-warner-bros-merger-lawsuit-interview/ |archive-date=September 8, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> ''Bloomberg'' reported that banks and investors had been preparing for the possibility that Paramount may be required to divest assets in order to resolve the lawsuit, with [[New Line Cinema]] and individual cable networks generating particular interest; an analyst estimated that the legacy Turner networks could fetch at least $8 billion.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-26 |title=Paramount Might Get $8 Billion for Turner Networks, Analyst Says |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-26/paramount-might-get-8-billion-for-turner-networks-analyst-says |access-date=2026-09-08 |website=Bloomberg}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Manfredi |first=Lucas |date=2026-08-25 |title=Investment Bankers Eye New Line Cinema, WBD Cable Networks as Paramount Legal Battle Drags On {{!}} Report |url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/business/paramount-state-ag-lawsuit-investment-bankers-new-line-cinema-warner-bros-cable-network-interest/ |access-date=2026-09-08 |website=TheWrap |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260827174208/https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/business/paramount-state-ag-lawsuit-investment-bankers-new-line-cinema-warner-bros-cable-network-interest/ |archive-date=August 27, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On August 26, 2026, the attorneys general of [[Iowa]] and [[Montana]] filed a [[motion for leave]] to file a bill of complaint in the [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court]], seeking to halt the trial. It argued that the California-led lawsuit constituted "politicized antitrust enforcement by a small handful of states seeking to enjoin a $110 billion merger that the United States, most American states, and competition regulators worldwide have cleared." Iowa AG [[Brenna Bird]] wrote in a ''[[Daily Wire]]'' op-ed that "If California believes a transaction that 68 regulators approved is nevertheless illegal, it is free to make that argument. But it should make it in the one court with the authority to bind all of us, and it should make it now, before the bill for the delay comes due."<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 27, 2026 |title=ACQUISITIONS & MERGERS NEWS: Iowa and Montana sue states opposing Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, (Aug 27, 2026) |url=https://www.vitallaw.com/news/acquisitions-mergers-news-iowa-and-montana-sue-states-opposing-paramount-warner-bros-merger/ald0109f397598d534295b05c839817b7ea4d?refURL=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.google.com%2F#. |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=[[VitalLaw]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 26, 2026 |title=Paramount-WBD Antitrust Suit Heads To Supreme Court In Red State Vs. Blue State Showdown Over $111B Merger |url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/paramount-merger-supreme-court-threat-iowa-1237050615/ |access-date=2026-08-26 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260826170105/https://deadline.com/2026/08/paramount-merger-supreme-court-threat-iowa-1237050615/ |archive-date=August 26, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

A hearing on the bond request was set for September 24, 2026; on August 31, 2026, the plaintiffs filed an opposition, stating that Paramount Skydance was seeking to "extract $1.88 billion from the public and a non-profit labor union to underwrite the costs of two private contracts it entered willfully, with advice of counsel, and for its own benefit",  and that granting the request "would incentivize merging parties to negotiate extraordinary fees to inoculate themselves from state and private antitrust enforcement." The plaintiffs recommended that the request be denied, or be a "nominal" $10,000.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patten |first=Dominic |date=2026-09-01 |title=Paramount Trying To Pull Fast One With Bond Request In Trial, AGs Say |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-antitrust-suit-bond-latest-1237064223/ |access-date=2026-09-01 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-18 |title=Paramount-Warner bond hearing puts US antitrust federalism clash before court |url=https://www.mlex.com/mlex/articles/2527354/paramount-warner-bond-hearing-puts-us-antitrust-federalism-clash-before-court |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=Mlex |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919193153/https://www.mlex.com/mlex/articles/2527354/paramount-warner-bond-hearing-puts-us-antitrust-federalism-clash-before-court |archive-date=September 19, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On September 11, 2026, Judge Thomas S. Hixson requested that the plaintiffs and Paramount participate in a two-day [[settlement conference]] at the end of October, later set for October 14–15.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-15 |title=Judge Sets Date For Settlement Talks In Paramount-WBD Antitrust Case |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-attorneys-general-settlement-talks-in-october-1237104639/ |access-date=2026-09-15 |website=Deadline Hollywood |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260916004046/https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-attorneys-general-settlement-talks-in-october-1237104639/ lawsuit ignored the "reality" that studios face significant competition from streaming services, and that the acquisition has the support of the United States' three largest cinema chains ([[AMC Theatres|AMC]], [[Cinemark]], and [[Regal Cinemas|Regal]]).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-12 |title=Paramount Argues States' Antitrust Lawsuit Against Warner Bros. On September 15, 2026, the DOJ filed a statement of interest backing Paramount's demand for a bond, stating that "the plain meaning of the statute and the contemporaneous use of 'proper bond' in dictionaries and federal court decisions makes it clear the amount of the bond must be fit, suitable, adapted, and correct to compensate the defendant for 'damages for an injunction improvidently granted'", and reiterating that the acquisition had already been approved by federal authorities.<ref name="StatesShouldPay" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Patten |first=Dominic |date=2026-09-15 |title=Trump's DOJ Backs Ellison & Paramount In Antitrust Battle With States |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/trump-paramount-antitrust-suit-1237104501/ |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260916211705/https://deadline.com/2026/09/trump-paramount-antitrust-suit-1237104501/ |archive-date=September 16, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> The next day, multiple officials, including Bonta and [[Los Angeles mayor]] [[Karen Bass]], reported that Paramount officials had renewed their threat to leave California.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patten |first=Dominic |date=2026-09-16 |title=Paramount To Leave California Amid Antitrust Battle & Stalled Warner Bros Merger |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-leaving-california-merger-lawsuit-1237105417/ |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260917012527/https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-leaving-california-merger-lawsuit-1237105417/ |archive-date=September 17, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==== Settlement and consent decree ====
On September 18, 2026, ''The Wall Street Journal'' reported via anonymous sources that Paramount was in "advanced" talks with California officials on a possible settlement.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Toonkel |first=Jessica |date=2026-09-18 |title=Paramount in Advanced Settlement Talks With California's Attorney General |url=https://www.wsj.com/business/media/paramount-in-advanced-settlement-talks-with-californias-attorney-general-aab8fd3d |access-date=2026-09-19 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919231744/https://www.wsj.com/business/media/paramount-in-advanced-settlement-talks-with-californias-attorney-general-aab8fd3d |archive-date=September 19, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="SharesClimb">{{Cite web |last=Sisco |first=Josh |date=2026-09-18 |title=Paramount Shares Climb on Report of Warner Deal Settlement Talks |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-18/paramount-shares-climb-on-report-of-warner-deal-settlement-talks |access-date=2026-09-19 |website=Bloomberg News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Godoy |first1=Jody |last2=Godoy |first2=Jody |date=2026-09-18 |title=Paramount could settle with states over Warner Bros. as soon as this weekend, sources say |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/paramount-states-discuss-cnn-monitoring-film-release-commitment-sources-say-2026-09-18/ |access-date=2026-09-19 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref> CNN media correspondent [[Brian Stelter]] reported on September 20 that at least four attorneys general—including [[Letitia James]] of New York and [[William Tong]] of Connecticut—were hesitant and seeking additional concessions, including requiring CNN to remain separate and editorially independent from CBS News.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Stelter |first=Brian |date=2026-09-20 |title=Paramount nears merger settlement, but some key state AGs are not on board yet |url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/20/media/paramount-wbd-settlement-california-connecticut-bonta |access-date=2026-09-21 |work=CNN |language=en}}</ref> ''TheWrap'' reported that a "hold separate" arrangement was being discussed, which would allow Paramount to complete the acquisition while the antitrust lawsuit is pending (thus reducing the impact of the "ticking fee"), but prohibit any outright integration of the companies until it is resolved.<ref name="HoldSeparate">{{Cite web |last=Waxman |first=Sharon |date=2026-09-20 |title=Latest in Paramount-Bonta Negotiations: 'Hold Separate' Maneuver May Be Key as Deal Nears |url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/business/latest-in-paramount-warner-bros-negotiations-hold-separate-deal/ |access-date=2026-09-20 |website=TheWrap |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260920184958/https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/business/latest-in-paramount-warner-bros-negotiations-hold-separate-deal/ |archive-date=September 20, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Other concessions were also reportedly discussed, including the divestment of certain cable networks, a mandate that Paramount Pictures and Warner Bros. Pictures operate independently from each other, and the formation of an independent oversight board to monitor Ellison's film output commitment and the editorial independence of CNN.<ref name="HoldSeparate" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Weprin |first=Alex |date=2026-09-21 |title=Deal or No Deal? The Contours of a Paramount Settlement for WBD Begin to Take Shape |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/paramount-warner-settlement-terms-leak-talks-continue-1236706694/ |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260921055901/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/paramount-warner-settlement-terms-leak-talks-continue-1236706694/ |archive-date=September 21, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="SharesClimb" />

On September 21, 2026, it was announced that Paramount Skydance had reached an out-of-court settlement with the state of California and WGA that would allow the acquisition to go through, with Ellison stating that the acquisition would be completed within "approximately two weeks".<ref>{{Cite news |last=Toonkel |first=Jessica |date=2026-09-21 |title=Paramount Settles States' Antitrust Suit, Clearing Way for Warner Megadeal |url=https://www.wsj.com/business/media/paramount-settles-states-antitrust-suit-clearing-way-for-warner-megadeal-95588926 |access-date=2026-09-21 |work=Wall Street Journal |language=en-US |issn=0099-9660}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Goldsmith |first1=Jill |last2=Patten |first2=Dominic |date=2026-09-21 |title=Done! Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit, Set To Seal Deal For Warner Bros. Discovery |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-settles-antitrust-suit-to-seal-warner-bros-deal-1237109223/ |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260921170414/https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-settles-antitrust-suit-to-seal-warner-bros-deal-1237109223/ |archive-date=September 21, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=2026-09-21 |title=David Ellison Says Paramount Hopes to Close Warner Bros. Deal in 'Approximately Two Weeks' in Staff Memo |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/david-ellison-paramount-warner-deal-staff-memo-1236871327/ |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260921213105/https://variety.com/2026/film/news/david-ellison-paramount-warner-deal-staff-memo-1236871327/ |archive-date=September 21, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Paramount agreed to a five-year consent decree, imposing various concessions, including:<ref name="BontaLaysOut">{{Cite web |last=Hayes |first=Dade |date=2026-09-21 |title=Paramount Deal Terms Laid Out By CA AG Rob Bonta |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-wbd-deal-california-rob-bonta-1237109313/ |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260921195053/https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-wbd-deal-california-rob-bonta-1237109313/ |archive-date=September 21, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="KeyTerms">{{Cite news |date=2026-09-21 |title=Key terms of Paramount's Warner Bros Discovery settlement with US states |url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/key-terms-paramounts-warner-bros-discovery-settlement-with-us-states-2026-09-21/ |access-date=2026-09-21 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref><ref name="WhatIsInSettlement">{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=2026-09-21 |title=What's in the Paramount Settlement With States: Commitment to Not Sell Studio Lots, Additional $300M Yearly Investment in U.S. Film Production, CNN Oversight and More |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-states-settlement-terms-warner-bros-1236871264/ |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

* Releasing 30 films per-year for two years following the completion of the acquisition, and then at least 32 films for the next three years afterwards.
** At least 20% of this quota must be films with a budget of at least $50 million, at least 20 must be wide releases, at least 50% must be films acquired from or co-produced with a third-party, and at least four of them must be [[independent film]]s. 
** If the company does not meet the quota, it must pay a penalty of $30 million for each missed film, which will be split between the [[Motion Picture & Television Fund]], the [[National Association of Attorneys General]], and health care and retirement trust funds for Hollywood labor unions. If it does not fulfill the quota after a six-month grace period, the company will be required to divest its stake in [[Miramax]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=2026-09-21 |title=Paramount WBD Must Divest Miramax If They Miss 30 Films A Year |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-warner-bros-merger-miramax-penalty-1237109424/ |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260921221529/https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-warner-bros-merger-miramax-penalty-1237109424/ |archive-date=September 21, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>
** All films must adhere to industry-accepted release windows of 45 days in theatres, and 90 days before they are released to subscription video on-demand.
* Investing $1.5 billion over the five years (at least $300 million per-year) into productions within the United States.
** If a federal tax credit for film and television production of at least 20% is passed, the company must increase US film production to 20% in the first two years, and then 30% in the last three years. If California or New York pass an uncapped state tax credit, US production must increase to 40%.
* Investing at least $5 million per-year in a fund for acquiring independent films.
* Investing at least $9.5 million per-year in career development and education programs for employees that are laid off as a direct result of the merger.
* Maintaining Paramount and Warner Bros.' separate studio lots.
* Conditions on fees and distribution terms with exhibitors, including fees remaining unchanged for at least three years.
* Establishing a "news editorial independence board" to oversee CBS News and CNN's "adherence to ethical journalism as defined by journalism industry best practices and to editorial independence", based on "guiding editorial and journalism principles" derived from their existing policies for "accuracy, independence, fairness and journalistic integrity". The board will consist primarily of veteran journalists appointed by the company's board.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Ted |date=2026-09-21 |title=Paramount-WBD Settlement Requires CNN And CBS News Independence Board |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/cnn-cbs-news-editorial-independence-board-1237109434/ |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260921213103/https://deadline.com/2026/09/cnn-cbs-news-editorial-independence-board-1237109434/ |archive-date=September 21, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>
* Conducting carriage negotiations for the Paramount and WBD cable networks separately and independently, with restrictions on changes to existing agreements, and the use of confidential information from one half of the company being used as part of negotiations for cable networks from the other half.
** If the company violates these conditions, it will be ordered to divest the [[BET]] channels, [[Comedy Central]], [[Destination America]], [[Science Channel]], [[Smithsonian Channel]], and/or [[VH1]].
* Maintaining "service and quality levels" at [[Pluto TV]] that are "at or above" existing levels under Paramount.
* The WGA also reached a settlement that will prohibit layoffs of CBS News writers for the same five-year period, and require the company to pay its attorney's fees, and $17.5 million to the union's health fund.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Andreeva |first1=Nellie |last2=Campione |first2=Katie |date=2026-09-21 |title=WGA Settles Lawsuit Against Paramount-WBD Merger |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/wga-settlement-lawsuit-paramount-wbd-merger-concessions-1237109441/ |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260921213230/https://deadline.com/2026/09/wga-settlement-lawsuit-paramount-wbd-merger-concessions-1237109441/ |archive-date=September 21, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> 

A court hearing to finalize the terms was scheduled for September 24, 2026.<ref name="NewsomDidNotPressureBonta">{{Cite web |last=Knapp |first=J. D. |date=2026-09-23 |title=Gavin Newsom Insists He Didn't Pressure Rob Bonta Into Paramount Settlement |url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/public-policy-legal/gavin-newsom-didnt-pressure-rob-bonta-paramount-wbd-settlement/ |access-date=2026-09-23 |website=TheWrap |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260923193948/https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/public-policy-legal/gavin-newsom-didnt-pressure-rob-bonta-paramount-wbd-settlement/ |archive-date=September 23, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Bonta stated that the settlement was "not a vote of support for this merger", but that it "locks in a massive upside" in comparison to the Disney–Fox merger, and that "I'd rather resolve the case in the boardroom rather than the courtroom, and that's what happened here."<ref name="BontaLaysOut" /> Notably, the settlement does not immediately impose any of the "structural" remedies that were proposed by Bonta, but only imposes them as penalties for violations of provisions of the consent decree.<ref name="BontaLaysOut" /><ref name="KeyTerms" /><ref name="WhatIsInSettlement" /> Governor Newsom stated that he "didn't pressure" anybody to make the deal, and that "we — me, many folks, including the mayor, soon-to-be [[2026 California gubernatorial election|governor]]-elect [[Xavier Becerra|[Xavier] Becerra]] and others — preferred, in the words of Rob Bonta himself, that he focus on getting this done at the boardroom, not the courtroom."<ref name="NewsomDidNotPressureBonta" />

On September 24, 2026, the court approved an emergency motion by Block the Merger to allow the filing of amicus briefs in opposition to the settlement, which the group stated was "weak, unenforceable, and leaves workers, journalists, and consumers in the dust." Paramount opposed the motion, stating that allowing the filings would extend the hearing, and therefore force the company to "incur tens (if not hundreds) of millions of dollars of payments", while adding nothing to the record that "offer[s] the Court information or perspective that the existing record does not already supply."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Ted |date=2026-09-24 |title=Block The Merger Coalition Asks Judge To Delay Paramount-WB Settlement |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/block-the-merger-paramount-warner-bros-settlement-1237112453/ |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260924183917/https://deadline.com/2026/09/block-the-merger-paramount-warner-bros-settlement-1237112453/ |archive-date=September 24, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Manfredi |first=Lucas |date=2026-09-24 |title=Judge Grants Block the Merger Coalition's Motion to Oppose 'Weak and Unenforceable' Paramount-WB Settlement |url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/block-the-merger-coalition-emergency-motion-paramount-warner-bros-settlement-opposition/ |access-date=2026-09-24 |website=TheWrap |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260924190339/https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/block-the-merger-coalition-emergency-motion-paramount-warner-bros-settlement-opposition/ |archive-date=September 24, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Cory Booker sent a letter requesting an independent public interest review, as the settlement "has reached the Court without a competitive impact statement, without a public comment period, and without any formal opportunity for theaters, distributors, workers, or consumers to be heard."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=2026-09-24 |title=Judge Questions Legal Points of Paramount's Settlement With States at Hearing, Says a Ruling Will Come in 'Due Course' |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/judge-paramount-state-ags-settlement-hearing-1236874529/ |access-date=2026-09-25 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260925133816/https://variety.com/2026/film/news/judge-paramount-state-ags-settlement-hearing-1236874529/ |archive-date=September 25, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Briefs were submitted by Block the Merger and the [[League of United Latin American Citizens]] (LULAC); Block the Merger felt that the 30-film commitment was less than what Paramount and Warner Bros. were scheduled to release in 2027 on their own, and that the settlement's conditions on their cable operations would still allow the combined company to "use its power in other offerings—a combined HBO and Showtime (premium cable channels), a combined HBO Max and Paramount+ (streaming services), and [[CBS]] (broadcast)—to extract higher prices in basic cable negotiations, as this form of leveraging is carved out." The LULAC argued that the settlement contained "defects" that "concern the competitive harms the States pleaded, including diminished quality, variety, and viewpoints."<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 25, 2026 |title=Paramount-WBD merger conditions give the public virtually nothing judge is told |url=https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/09/paramount-wbd-merger-conditions-give-the-public-virtually-nothing-judge-is-told/ |access-date=September 25, 2026 |website=Ars Technica |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260925192851/https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/09/paramount-wbd-merger-conditions-give-the-public-virtually-nothing-judge-is-told/ |archive-date=September 25, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Patten |first=Dominic |date=2026-09-25 |title=Paramount Merger Foes Ask Judge To Reject Antitrust Settlement |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramont-merger-foes-latest-1237113622/ |access-date=2026-09-29 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260927163123/https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramont-merger-foes-latest-1237113622/ |archive-date=September 27, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> On September 30, 2026, Martínez-Olguín approved the settlement, ruling that it was a "reasonable factual and legal resolution of the dispute". Filings by Paramount stated that they aimed to complete the acquisition by October 6, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=2026-09-30 |title=Paramount-Warner Bros.
