Merger Set to Close Next Week After Judge OKs Settlement With State AGs |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-warner-bros-merger-judge-approves-settlement-ags-1236893467/ |access-date=2026-09-30 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260930193856/https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-warner-bros-merger-judge-approves-settlement-ags-1236893467/ |archive-date=September 30, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> The same day, it was announced that outgoing [[Mattel]] CEO [[Ynon Kreiz]] would become a co-CEO, responsible for integration and day-to-day operations.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=2026-09-30 |title=David Ellison Taps Mattel's Ynon Kreiz to Be Co-CEO of Merged Paramount-Warner Bros. |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-david-ellison-ynon-kreiz-co-ceo-mattel-1236893607/ |access-date=2026-10-02 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> The acquisition was completed on October 6, 2026, as planned.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hayes |first=David |date=2026-10-06 |title=Skydancing At Last: $110B Merger Of Paramount And Warner Bros. Discovery Officially Closes |url=https://deadline.com/2026/10/skydance-merger-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-1237147750/ |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=Deadline Hollywood |language=en-US}}</ref>

On October 2, 2026, Ellison announced that the combined company would be known as Skydance Corporation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=2026-10-02 |title=New Name of Paramount-Warner Bros. Unveiled: Skydance |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/name-of-paramount-warner-bros-unveiled-skydance-1236893761/ |access-date=2026-10-02 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Government and industry responses ==
=== Industry ===
[[Cinema United]], a trade association representing U.S. cinema operators, warned that industry consolidation could reduce the number of films released theatrically and increase studios' leverage in negotiations with exhibitors.<ref name="CinemaUnited" /><ref name="DirectorsGuild">{{Cite web |last=Fuster |first=Jeremy |date=December 5, 2025 |title=Directors Guild to Meet With Netflix Over Its Plans for Warner Bros. Acquisition |url=https://www.thewrap.com/directors-guild-netflix-warner-bros-deal/ |access-date=December 5, 2025 |website=TheWrap |archive-date=December 5, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205102303/https://www.thewrap.com/directors-guild-netflix-warner-bros-deal/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Barnes |first1=Brooks |last2=Hubler |first2=Shawn |date=December 6, 2025 |title=Angst Turns to Anger in Hollywood as Netflix Hooks Warner Bros. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/06/business/media/hollywood-reaction-netflix-warner-bros.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=December 6, 2025 |website=[[The New York Times]] |archive-url=https://archive.today/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/06/business/media/hollywood-reaction-netflix-warner-bros.html |archive-date=December 6, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Filmmaker [[James Cameron]] publicly backed an acquisition of WBD by Paramount, arguing that a Netflix takeover "would be a disaster" due to the company's perceived lack of commitment to theatrical releases, and that Paramount was "the best choice".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Loving |first=Casey |date=November 25, 2025 |title=James Cameron Endorses Paramount in WBD Bidding War: 'Netflix Would Be a Disaster' |url=https://www.thewrap.com/james-cameron-slams-netflix-endorses-paramount-warner-bros-bid/ |access-date=December 9, 2025 |website=TheWrap |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251125211604/https://www.thewrap.com/james-cameron-slams-netflix-endorses-paramount-warner-bros-bid/ |archive-date=November 25, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cho |first=Winston |date=February 20, 2026 |title=James Cameron Sounds Alarm Over Netflix–Warner Bros. Deal, Backs Paramount |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/james-cameron-netflix-warner-bros-deal-backs-paramount-1236510249/ |access-date=February 20, 2026 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |archive-date=February 20, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260220023230/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/james-cameron-netflix-warner-bros-deal-backs-paramount-1236510249/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Senator [[Adam Schiff]] and Representative [[Laura Friedman]] asked for details on U.S. production, union jobs, AI safeguards, and competition, seeking responses by February 15, 2026, to assess the impact of both deals on Hollywood workers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kilkenny |first=Katie |date=February 6, 2026 |title=Legislators Call for Employment Commitments From Netflix and Paramount as They Seek to Merge With Warner Bros. |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/warner-bros-merger-legislators-ask-employment-commitments-1236497231/ |access-date=February 6, 2026 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref>

[[Roy Price]] wrote that an acquisition of Warner Bros. by Netflix could lead to fewer shows being made and "a narrower range of storytelling" with "decision making around one organization's or one individual's point of view".<ref>{{cite news |last=Price |first=Roy |author1-link=Roy Price |title=Netflix's Swallowing of Warner Bros. Will Be the End of Hollywood |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/06/opinion/netflix-warner-bros-hollywood.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=December 6, 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20251207184929/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/12/06/opinion/netflix-warner-bros-hollywood.html |archive-date=December 7, 2025}}</ref> He supported an acquisition of WBD by Paramount, arguing that both companies were "spending enough to lose money but not enough to win" at streaming, but that combining scale would allow better investments in premium content, increase output, and allow the companies to pay top talent competitively, as multiple scale players would be "healthier for Hollywood than three giants and a couple of stragglers".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Price |first=Roy |date=2025-09-13 |title=A Paramount–WBD Merger Would Be Good |url=https://pricepoint.substack.com/p/a-paramountwbd-merger-would-be-good |access-date=2026-09-13 |website=Price Point |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260913213625/https://pricepoint.substack.com/p/a-paramountwbd-merger-would-be-good |archive-date=September 13, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On February 13, 2026, [[AGC Studios]] chairman [[Stuart Ford (entertainment executive)|Stuart Ford]] criticized Netflix's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. during a keynote at the European Film Market in Berlin, warning it could harm the film industry's financial model. He said a studio-streamer merger might reduce backend participation and residuals for producers and talent, though he noted that stronger theatrical commitments could lessen some concerns. Ford argued that streaming-driven consolidation could threaten traditional revenue-sharing practices that support industry workers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brzeski |first=Patrick |date=February 13, 2026 |title=Indie Veteran Stuart Ford on Netflix–Warner Deal: We Have to 'Fight Tooth and Nail' or Film Professionals Will Become 'Uber Drivers' for the Tech Giants |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/stuart-ford-netflix-warner-deal-uber-drivers-tech-giants-1236504424/ |access-date=February 13, 2026 |website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref>

On February 18, 2026, [[Cinemark Theatres]] CEO Sean Gamble said exhibitors were cautious about Netflix's pledges to maintain traditional theatrical release windows, citing the company's history and calling for firmer assurances. He described the situation as "active and fluid" as Netflix and Paramount Skydance competed for WBD. Gamble said Cinemark, individually and through Cinema United, had remained in contact with the companies and regulators to advocate for sustained exclusive theatrical windows. He added that exhibitors had long believed Netflix would eventually recognize the value of theatrical releases, noting that [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] and [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] had embraced the model.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hayes |first=Dade |date=February 18, 2026 |title=In Warner Merger Battle, Netflix Needs To Take "More Action" To Prove It Loves Movie Theaters, Cinemark CEO Says |url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/warner-bros-merger-netflix-movie-theaters-cinemark-1236728154/ |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en-US |archive-date=February 19, 2026 |access-date=February 19, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260219033037/https://deadline.com/2026/02/warner-bros-merger-netflix-movie-theaters-cinemark-1236728154/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ibarra |first=Dominoe |date=2026-07-27 |title=Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming, Benedict Wong Urging U.K. to Block "Dangerous" Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger {{!}} THR News Video |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/video/benedict-cumberbatch-alan-cumming-benedict-wong-uk-block-dangerous-paramount-warner-bros-merger-video/ |access-date=2026-07-30 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260730224734/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/video/benedict-cumberbatch-alan-cumming-benedict-wong-uk-block-dangerous-paramount-warner-bros-merger-video/ |archive-date=July 30, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Prior to the shareholder vote in April 2026, an open letter signed by over 5,000 actors and creative personnel was circulated by the WGA, [[Committee for the First Amendment]], [[Democracy Defenders Fund]], and the Future Film Coalition. The letter argued that the proposed Paramount Skydance acquisition would "prioritize the interests of a small group of powerful stakeholders over the broader public good", and would "grievously" compromise the integrity, independence, and diversity of the industry.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Ted |date=2026-04-13 |title=Major Hollywood Figures Sign On To Letter Opposing Paramount-WB Merger |url=https://deadline.com/2026/04/paramount-warner-bros-merger-hollywood-letter-1236858953/ |access-date=2026-09-07 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260907063553/https://deadline.com/2026/04/paramount-warner-bros-merger-hollywood-letter-1236858953/ |archive-date=September 7, 2026 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Mark Ruffalo]] stated that many industry members were afraid to sign the letter, since there was "a deep, ugly and pervasive fear of speaking out."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garner |first=Glenn |date=May 7, 2026 |title=Mark Ruffalo Notes Many "Were Afraid" To Sign Letter Opposing Paramount-Warner Bros Merger: "Not Unjustified" |url=https://deadline.com/2026/05/mark-ruffalo-many-afraid-sign-letter-paramount-warner-bros-1236886998/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en |archive-date=May 7, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260507215907/https://deadline.com/2026/05/mark-ruffalo-many-afraid-sign-letter-paramount-warner-bros-1236886998/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Paramount responded to the letter, reiterating Ellison's previously announced commitments to 30 theatrical releases per-year and "independent creative leadership" of its brands, and arguing that the purchase would allow the company to "greenlight more projects, back bold ideas, support talent across multiple stages of their careers, and bring stories to audiences at a truly global scale—while strengthening competition by ensuring multiple scaled players are investing in creative talent.".<ref>{{Cite web|last=Johnson|first=Ted|date=2026-04-13|title=Paramount Responds To Letter From Hollywood Figures Opposing WB Meger|url=https://deadline.com/2026/04/paramount-warner-bros-merger-creatives-letter-1236859235/|access-date=2026-09-07|website=Deadline|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260907074120/https://deadline.com/2026/04/paramount-warner-bros-merger-creatives-letter-1236859235/|archive-date=September 7, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

On April 14, 2026, it was reported that Paramount had pulled advertising from the entertainment news site ''[[The Ankler]]'' after chief columnist [[Richard Rushfield]] was seen carrying a bag of "Block the Merger" buttons at [[CinemaCon]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Waxman |first1=Sharon |last2=Bolies |first2=Corbin |date=2026-04-14 |title=Paramount Pulls Ads From The Ankler After Rushfield Boosts 'Block the Merger' Movement at CinemaCon |url=https://www.thewrap.com/media-platforms/journalism/paramount-pulls-ads-the-ankler-richard-rushfield-block-the-merger/ |access-date=2026-04-29 |website=TheWrap |language=en-US}}</ref>

[[Bob Wieckowski]] wrote, in May 2026, "this deal won't seemingly impact either" consumer pricing or competition and that "without the merger, the likely outcome will be a weaker domestic market. That will mean fewer productions, investments and jobs here in California."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wieckowski |first=Bob |date=May 7, 2026 |title=The imperfect Paramount-Warner Bros. deal could save California's entertainment industry |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/opinion/openforum/article/paramount-warner-bros-movie-california-22242594.php |access-date=May 7, 2026 |website=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |language=en |archive-date=May 8, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260508101106/https://www.sfchronicle.com/opinion/openforum/article/paramount-warner-bros-movie-california-22242594.php |url-status=live }}</ref>

From June 6–16, 2026, the [[American Economic Liberties Project]], the Committee for the First Amendment, Democracy Defenders Action, the Future Film Coalition, and WGA hosted a three-city tour of joint demonstrations known as "Main Street vs. The Merger" at the Lumiere Cinema in Los Angeles, the WGA East headquarters in New York City, and the [[Plaza Theatre (Atlanta)|Plaza Theater]] in Atlanta, Georgia.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 2, 2026 |title="Main Street vs. The Merger": Entertainment Workers, Small Businesses, and Lawmakers Convene in Three Cities to Oppose the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Deal |url=https://www.economicliberties.us/press-release/main-street-vs-the-merger-entertainment-workers-small-businesses-and-lawmakers-convene-in-three-cities-to-oppose-the-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-deal/ |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=[[American Economic Liberties Project]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260606205051/https://www.economicliberties.us/press-release/main-street-vs-the-merger-entertainment-workers-small-businesses-and-lawmakers-convene-in-three-cities-to-oppose-the-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-deal/ |archive-date=June 6, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On July 27, 2026, [[Benedict Cumberbatch]], [[Alan Cumming]] and [[Benedict Wong]] published a joint op-ed in ''[[The Guardian]]'' urging the British government to intervene in the WBD acquisition, arguing that it "would harm our workers, our culture and the public."<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Cumberbatch |first1=Benedict |last2=Cumming |first2=Alan |last3=Wong |first3=Benedict |date=2026-07-27 |title=A TV and cinema calamity could be disastrous for what you watch and what you know. Act now to stop that |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/ng-interactive/2026/jul/27/tv-cinema-paramount-warner-bros-merger-benedict-cumberbatch-alan-cumming-benedict-wong |access-date=2026-07-30 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

On July 29, 2026, [[AMC Theatres]] CEO [[Adam Aron]] published a ''Variety'' op-ed in favor of the Paramount acquisition, arguing that increased scale was necessary for traditional studios to compete with tech companies, highlighting Ellison's commitment to theatrical releases, and arguing that his stewardship of Paramount proved that he was a "consummate movie executive".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aron |first=Adam |date=2026-07-29 |title=AMC Theatres Chief Adam Aron Pushes for Paramount Warner Bros. Merger, Says 'Thanks, but No Thanks' to State AG's Blocking Deal |url=https://variety.com/2026/biz/news/amc-theatres-adam-aron-paramount-warner-bros-merger-1236823859/ |access-date=2026-09-10 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260809225931/https://variety.com/2026/biz/news/amc-theatres-adam-aron-paramount-warner-bros-merger-1236823859/ |archive-date=August 9, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Regal Cinemas]] CEO Eduardo Aznar and Cinemark then made their own statements in support of the merger and calling for a settlement, stating that they believed that Ellison would stand by his commitments, and that the uncertainty of a prolonged antitrust suit would be detrimental to the industry.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rubin |first=Rebecca |date=2026-08-18 |title=Cinemark Joins AMC Theatres and Regal in Supporting Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/cinemark-paramount-warner-bros-merger-amc-theatres-regal-1236836310/ |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260823130549/https://variety.com/2026/film/news/cinemark-paramount-warner-bros-merger-amc-theatres-regal-1236836310/ |archive-date=August 23, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |date=2026-08-06 |title=Regal Cinemas CEO Champions Paramount-WBD Merger |url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/regal-cinemas-ceo-paramount-warner-bros-merger-1237027050/ |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260806095322/https://deadline.com/2026/08/regal-cinemas-ceo-paramount-warner-bros-merger-1237027050/ |archive-date=August 6, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Cinema United then made a similar statement calling for California and Paramount to "meet in the immediate future and discuss all possible avenues" to settle the lawsuit.<ref>{{Cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |last2=Goldsmith |first2=Jill |date=2026-08-18 |title=Cinema United Urges Paramount & California AG To Resolve Lawsuit |url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/paramount-california-lawsuit-cinema-united-1237044393/ |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260921185626/https://deadline.com/2026/08/paramount-california-lawsuit-cinema-united-1237044393/ |archive-date=September 21, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In August 2026, [[WME Group]] executive chairman [[Ari Emanuel]] published a ''Wall Street Journal'' op-ed in support of the Paramount acquisition, stating that the California lawsuit was "trash" because it ignored the "fastest-growing competitors on the market" (such as [[A24]], [[Amazon MGM Studios]], and [[Lionsgate Studios|Lionsgate]], streaming video providers such as Netflix and [[YouTube]], as well as non-film media such as video games), and argued that "when government officials manipulate markets to reach political outcomes, antitrust stops protecting competition and starts threatening it."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hayes |first=Dade |date=2026-07-28 |title=Ari Emanuel Backs Paramount-WBD Deal In WSJ Op-Ed, Blasts States' Antitrust Lawsuit As "Trash" |url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/ari-emanuel-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-merger-wsj-1237006229/ |access-date=2026-09-07 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260907084323/https://deadline.com/2026/07/ari-emanuel-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-merger-wsj-1237006229/ |archive-date=September 7, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=July 31, 2026|title=Gavin Newsom Reportedly Concerned About State Antitrust Suit Against Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/gavin-newsom-concerned-state-suit-paramount-warner-bros-1236661514/|access-date=2026-08-03|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260803055359/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/gavin-newsom-concerned-state-suit-paramount-warner-bros-1236661514/|archive-date=August 3, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

On September 1, 2026, [[Tom Cruise]] voiced his support for the merger on ''[[The Pat McAfee Show]]''; he argued that Ellison's oft-promised slate was "awesome" and that Hollywood needed to come together as a "community" to support it, as it would provide more opportunities for "every writer, every director, every producer, every artist. And the only way you do it is we have to create an abundance. Its production begets production."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patten |first=Dominic |date=2026-09-01 |title=Tom Cruise gives his thoughts about the pending merger of Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery. |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/tom-cruise-paramount-merger-warner-bros-1237064750/ |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260912043320/https://deadline.com/2026/09/tom-cruise-paramount-merger-warner-bros-1237064750/ |archive-date=September 12, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dunn |first=Jack |date=2026-09-01 |title=Tom Cruise Is Confident Paramount-Warner Bros. Will Release 30 Films a Year After Merger: 'They're Going to Deliver' |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/tom-cruise-david-ellison-paramount-warner-bros-merger-1236846704/ |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260906012645/https://variety.com/2026/film/news/tom-cruise-david-ellison-paramount-warner-bros-merger-1236846704/ |archive-date=September 6, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Word of a potential deal was criticized by Senator [[Elizabeth Warren]], Block the Merger, and Mark Ruffalo. Warren stated that "as [President [[Donald Trump]]] [[Donald Trump's conflict with the news media#Removal of specific media personnel and outlets|tries to ban CNN from the White House]], it would be a massive mistake to cave on the Paramount merger", while Block the Merger stated that it was "an insult to everyone who has stood up against this harmful transaction and to the hundreds of thousands of workers, journalists, and consumers who will be hurt if it goes forward", and that "an agreement based on unenforceable concessions is a win only for David Ellison".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Murphy |first=J. Kim |date=2026-09-19 |title=Mark Ruffalo Urges California AG Rob Bonta to Reject Paramount Settlement: 'The People Don't Want It!' |url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/mark-ruffalo-slams-paramount-settlement-talks/ |access-date=2026-09-19 |website=TheWrap |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919235113/https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/mark-ruffalo-slams-paramount-settlement-talks/ |archive-date=September 19, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Patten |first=Dominic |date=2026-09-19 |title=Paramount Settlement Talks With AGs Face Political & Industry Opposition |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-settlement-opposition-1237108466/ |access-date=2026-09-19 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919210823/https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-settlement-opposition-1237108466/ |archive-date=September 19, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-19 |title=Block The Merger & Elizabeth Warren Call Out AGs For Betrayal In Deal Talks With Paramount: "A Win Only For David Ellison" |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-settlement-opposition-1237108466/ |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=Deadline Hollywood |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919210823/https://deadline.com/2026/09/paramount-settlement-opposition-1237108466/ |archive-date=September 19, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Consumer lawsuits ===
In April 2026, Paramount Skydance was sued by a group of streaming customers seeking to halt the acquisition, arguing that acquiring Warner Bros. Discovery would reduce viewpoint diversity and lead to an increase in prices for its services.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Johnson|first=Ted|date=2026-08-06|title=Judge Dismisses Consumer Lawsuit Challenging Paramount-WBD Merger|url=https://deadline.com/2026/08/judge-dismisses-paramount-warner-bros-consumer-lawsuit-1237027434/|access-date=2026-09-07|website=Deadline|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260806101130/https://deadline.com/2026/08/judge-dismisses-paramount-warner-bros-consumer-lawsuit-1237027434/|archive-date=August 6, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Patten|first1=Dominic|last2=Pedersen|first2=Erik|date=2026-05-01|title=Paramount Hit With Antitrust Lawsuit By Consumers Seeking To Stop WBD Merger|url=https://deadline.com/2026/04/paramount-sued-antitrust-block-warner-bros-deal-1236877774/|access-date=2026-09-07|website=Deadline|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260501012348/https://deadline.com/2026/04/paramount-sued-antitrust-block-warner-bros-deal-1236877774/|archive-date=May 1, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> On June 4, Paramount Skydance filed a motion to dismiss the suit, arguing that the complaint did not present enough evidence that the acquisition was anti-competitive.<ref>{{Cite web|date=June 4, 2026|title=Paramount Asks Judge To Dismiss Consumers' Antitrust Lawsuit Seeking To Block Warner Bros. Discovery Merger|url=https://deadline.com/2026/06/paramount-warner-bros-lawsuit-motion-to-dismiss-1236941138/|access-date=2026-06-04|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260910041937/https://deadline.com/2026/06/paramount-warner-bros-lawsuit-motion-to-dismiss-1236941138/|archive-date=September 10, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> In July 2026, Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín declined the consumers' request for a preliminary injunction, finding that they had "not offered any evidence and this have not made a clear showing of a likelihood of success, nor to they make a clear showing of irreparable harm."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Johnson |first1=Ted |title=Judge Denies Preliminary Injunction In Consumer Lawsuit Seeking To Block Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger |url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/paramount-warner-bros-merger-judge-denies-injunction-1236984614/ |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=July 16, 2026 |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260716234000/https://deadline.com/2026/07/paramount-warner-bros-merger-judge-denies-injunction-1236984614/ |archive-date=July 16, 2026 |access-date=July 17, 2026 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Maddaus |first=Gene |date=2026-07-17 |title=Paramount+ Subscribers Fail to Block Warner Bros. Merger as States Will Try Again Friday |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-subscribers-fail-injunction-merger-1236813567/ |access-date=2026-09-10 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260717030226/https://variety.com/2026/film/news/paramount-subscribers-fail-injunction-merger-1236813567/ |archive-date=July 17, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

=== Government ===
==== Congressional and political reactions ====
U.S. conservatives notably opposed Netflix's bids to acquire WBD in favor of Paramount Skydance's bids, due to [[David Ellison|David]] and [[Larry Ellison]]'s support of U.S. president [[Donald Trump]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Patten|first=Dominic|date=2026-02-02|title=Project Netflix: MAGA's Plan To Sandbag Warner Bros Deal; Streamer Called "Biggest Political & Ideology Messaging Machine In Human History"|url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/netflix-warner-bros-maga-1236702805/|access-date=2026-06-10|website=Deadline|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260908102124/https://deadline.com/2026/02/netflix-warner-bros-maga-1236702805/|archive-date=September 8, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref> Conservatives accused Netflix of using its dominance to promote [[left-wing]] and [[Progressivism|progressive]] ideology in the United States and internationally.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patten |first=Dominic |date=2026-01-12 |title=Trump Indicates He's Really Not Into Netflix Buying WB, Wants To Stop The Streamer's So-Called "Cultural Takeover" |url=https://deadline.com/2026/01/trump-against-netflix-warner-bros-deal-1236679318/ |access-date=2026-09-10 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260910231239/https://deadline.com/2026/01/trump-against-netflix-warner-bros-deal-1236679318/ |archive-date=September 10, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hayden|first=Erik|date=January 16, 2026|title=Ted Sarandos: 'I Don't Know Why' Trump Shared Article Saying to 'Stop' Netflix Deal for Warner Bros.|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/ted-sarandos-trump-netflix-deal-warner-bros-1236476148/|access-date=January 17, 2026|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|archive-date=January 16, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260116160832/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/ted-sarandos-trump-netflix-deal-warner-bros-1236476148/|url-status=live}}</ref> On January 11, 2026, Trump shared an [[OANN]] op-ed on [[Truth Social]] that accused Netflix of seeking to "dominate the national imagination through raw market power and ideological activism", and having "repeatedly used its global platform to elevate progressive narratives while suppressing dissenting viewpoints." During hearings on the Netflix deal, Republican lawmakers similarly criticized Netflix for promoting ideological "propaganda", "[[Diversity, equity, and inclusion|DEI]]", and "[[wokeness]]".<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Patten |first1=Dominic |last2=Johnson |first2=Ted |date=2026-02-03 |title=Netflix Attacked For Having "Wokest Content In The History Of The World" By MAGA Senators At WB Deal Hearing |url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/netflix-wb-senate-hearing-woke-content-1236707763/ |access-date=2026-09-08 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260908012039/https://deadline.com/2026/02/netflix-wb-senate-hearing-woke-content-1236707763/ |archive-date=September 8, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==== Foreign funding concerns ====
The financing for the Paramount Skydance bid includes $24 billion in funding from [[sovereign wealth fund]]s associated with [[Public Investment Fund|Saudi Arabia]], [[Qatar Investment Authority|Qatar]], and the United Arab Emirates.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=2026-04-06 |title=Paramount Skydance Secures $24 Billion From Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Abu Dhabi Funds for Warner Bros. Deal |url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/paramount-skydance-funding-saudi-arabia-qatar-abu-dhabi-funds-warner-bros-deal-1236709251/ |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=Variety |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260927193501/https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/paramount-skydance-funding-saudi-arabia-qatar-abu-dhabi-funds-warner-bros-deal-1236709251/ |archive-date=September 27, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=James |first=Meg |date=2026-09-17 |title=FCC approves foreign owners for a merged Paramount-Warner Bros. |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2026-09-17/fcc-approves-foreign-owners-for-merged-paramount-warner-bros |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260918181353/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/business/story/2026-09-17/fcc-approves-foreign-owners-for-merged-paramount-warner-bros |archive-date=September 18, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> A filing stated that these investors, along with Affinity Partners, agreed to forgo governance rights and representation on the board of directors;<ref name="EllisonsRedBird">{{Cite web |date=2026-09-17 |title=Paramount says Ellisons, RedBird will have 100% of voting shares after Warner merger |url=https://www.mlex.com/mlex/articles/2527019/paramount-says-ellisons-redbird-will-have-100-of-voting-shares-after-warner-merger |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=MLex |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260919061212/https://www.mlex.com/mlex/articles/2527019/paramount-says-ellisons-redbird-will-have-100-of-voting-shares-after-warner-merger |archive-date=September 19, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> the Ellison family and [[RedBird Capital Partners]] would remain the sole [[Class A stock|class A]] shareholders and hold all voting rights.<ref name="FCCFundingOK" /><ref name="EllisonsRedBird" /> The company said that this structure would place the transaction outside the scope of review by the [[Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States]] (CFIUS). The same filing reported that [[Tencent]] had also withdrawn its financing from the proposal, which Paramount Skydance said was intended to avoid potential CFIUS review.<ref name="FCCFundingOK" /><ref>{{cite news|last=Kurtenbach|first=Elaine|date=December 10, 2025|title=Paramount says China's Tencent withdrew from its Warner Bros bid to avert national security issues|website=Associated Press|url=https://apnews.com/article/china-paramount-warner-netflix-tencent-eb3b4b18e67438d7633e5c4a1ec227c1|access-date=January 6, 2026|archive-date=December 10, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251210075219/https://apnews.com/article/china-paramount-warner-netflix-tencent-eb3b4b18e67438d7633e5c4a1ec227c1|url-status=live}}</ref> The funding would still be subject to a review by the FCC due to Paramount Skydance's ownership of broadcast licenses, as the ''[[Communications Act of 1934|Communications Act]]'' prohibits broadcasters from being more than 25% foreign-owned without a waiver, and the acquisition would increase Paramount's foreign ownership to 49.5%.<ref name="FCCFundingOK" />

When asked about [[Jared Kushner]], whose firm Affinity Partners was among the external financiers of Paramount's bid, Trump said "I've never spoken to him about it. He's really trying to work on Gaza. His primary thing is Gaza."<ref>{{Cite AV media |title=President Trump Participates in a Roundtable |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rlwh8i70q-c |date=December 8, 2025 |language=en |publisher=[[The White House]] |quote='''The Press:''' Paramount is supported by Jared Kushner, Mr. President. Would that impact your decision? '''The President:''' If Paramount is? I don't know. I've never spoken to him about it. He's really trying to work on Gaza. His primary thing is Gaza. |via=[[YouTube]] |time=56:40 |access-date=July 14, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260728195605/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rlwh8i70q-c |archive-date=July 28, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Superville|first=Darlene|date=December 8, 2025|title=Netflix deal to buy Warner Bros. 'could be a problem' because of size of market share, Trump says|website=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://apnews.com/article/trump-netflix-warner-bros-merger-problem-f3e317b61899d34ce507ba38af4a2934|access-date=December 9, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251208072228/https://apnews.com/article/trump-netflix-warner-bros-merger-problem-f3e317b61899d34ce507ba38af4a2934|archive-date=December 8, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> Senior Trump administration officials had previously told [[CNBC]] that the administration viewed the Netflix acquisition with "heavy criticism".<ref>{{cite news|last=Mangan|first=Dan|date=December 5, 2025|title=Trump admin views Netflix and Warner Bros. deal with 'heavy skepticism': Senior official|website=CNBC|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2025/12/05/trump-netflix-wbd-deal.html|access-date=December 9, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251206203626/https://www.cnbc.com/2025/12/05/trump-netflix-wbd-deal.html|archive-date=December 6, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> Affinity Partners withdrew its financing on December 16, 2025.<ref>{{cite news|last=Schoenbaum|first=Hannah|date=December 16, 2025|title=Jared Kushner pulls out of Paramount's hostile bid for Warner Bros. Discovery|website=Associated Press|url=https://apnews.com/article/jared-kushner-paramount-warner-bros-netflix-56886b231c132f6eb7d8990f0ede3e32|access-date=December 17, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226013611/https://apnews.com/article/jared-kushner-paramount-warner-bros-netflix-56886b231c132f6eb7d8990f0ede3e32 |archive-date=December 26, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On January 14, 2026, U.S. Representative [[Sam Liccardo]], a Democrat from California, called on Paramount Skydance to submit any potential acquisition of WBD to a foreign ownership review, even if such a filing was not legally required. In a letter to David Ellison, Liccardo said that a voluntary review would demonstrate good faith, strengthen public trust, and provide assurances regarding national security, data privacy, and potential foreign influence risks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson|first=Ted|date=January 14, 2026|title=Democratic Lawmaker Calls On Paramount To Voluntarily Submit A Warner Bros. Discovery Transaction To Federal Foreign Ownership Review|url=https://deadline.com/2026/01/paramount-warner-bros-discovery-foreign-ownership-1236682920/|access-date=January 14, 2026|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|archive-date=January 15, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260115170852/https://deadline.com/2026/01/paramount-warner-bros-discovery-foreign-ownership-1236682920/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On March 23, 2026, a group of Democratic senators led by [[Cory Booker]] sent a letter to the FCC demanding a "full and independent review" of the acquisition. The senators wrote that "the constellation of foreign investment from China and from [[Arab states of the Persian Gulf|Gulf states]], with complex and sometimes competing relationships with the United States, demands rigorous, not perfunctory, review."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cho |first=Winston |date=2026-03-23 |title=Foreign Investments in Paramount-Warner Bros. Deal Flagged by Democratic Senators in FCC Letter |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/paramount-warner-bros-foreign-investments-fcc-letter-1236544632/ |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260918110434/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/paramount-warner-bros-foreign-investments-fcc-letter-1236544632/ |archive-date=September 18, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On April 27, 2026, Paramount filed with the FCC for a foreign ownership waiver, stating that the investments were needed to help the company "compete more effectively in the provision of television broadcast services and in the broader video programming marketplace", and assuring that these investors would not hold any voting power.<ref name="FCCFundingOK" /><ref name="ClearsFCC">{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Ted |date=2026-09-17 |title=Paramount-WBD Merger Clears FCC Foreign Ownership Review |url=https://deadline.com/2026/09/fcc-foreign-ownership-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-1237106980/ |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260917214155/https://deadline.com/2026/09/fcc-foreign-ownership-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-1237106980/ |archive-date=September 17, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> On May 20, the [[Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation]] sent a letter to FCC chairman [[Brendan Carr]] demanding a "rigorous" review of the deal, warning that the large equity stake held by sovereign wealth funds associated with countries hostile to [[freedom of the press]] could result in "unprecedented influence".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Ted |date=2026-05-21 |title=Senate Democrats Warn FCC Over Foreign Influence In Paramount-WBD Deal |url=https://deadline.com/2026/05/paramount-warner-bros-foreign-investors-senate-democrats-1236917793/ |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260917025108/https://deadline.com/2026/05/paramount-warner-bros-foreign-investors-senate-democrats-1236917793/ |archive-date=September 17, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On September 17, 2026, the FCC issued a [[declaratory ruling]] granting the foreign ownership waiver, stating that it would serve the public interest. The waiver is subject to conditions requiring Paramount to obtain new waivers if it seeks to change the voting interests of the foreign investors cleared by the waiver, or its foreign voting interests exceed 25% in aggregate.<ref name="ClearsFCC" /> [[Anna M. Gomez]]—the sole Democratic commissioner at the FCC—criticized the decision, warning that the sale would "let some of the most repressive governments in the world indirectly control nearly all of a combined Paramount–Warner Bros.", and that "an investment this large in one of America's biggest media companies doesn't just buy equity, it secures influence over what gets said and what gets made."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-09-18 |title=US FCC's Gomez says 'repressive governments' will indirectly control Paramount, Warner |url=https://www.mlex.com/mlex/articles/2527184/us-fcc-s-gomez-says-repressive-governments-will-indirectly-control-paramount-warner |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=Mlex |language=en-US}}</ref>

==== Trump administration and political influence concerns ====
[[File:President Trump and the First Lady Arrive at the Kennedy Center Honors.webm|thumb|right|200px|start=18:10|Trump discussing the Netflix–WBD agreement on the Kennedy Center Honors red carpet (from 18:10).]]''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' reported that after the Netflix deal was publicly announced, Larry Ellison called Trump to argue that the deal would hurt competition. Before Paramount Skydance's hostile takeover bid was announced, it was also reported that David Ellison went to Washington DC and promised Trump administration officials that he would make big changes to [[CNN]]. Larry Ellison reportedly discussed with White House officials replacing specific CNN hosts that Trump reportedly dislikes.<ref>{{cite news |last=Lowell |first=Hugo |date=November 20, 2025 |title=Larry Ellison discussed axing CNN hosts with White House in takeover bid talks |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/nov/20/warner-bros-discovery-takeover-paramount-skydance-larry-ellison |access-date=January 6, 2026}}</ref> Trump has stated that he thinks that it is "imperative" that CNN be included in an acquisition "because the people that are running CNN right now are either corrupt or incompetent".<ref>{{cite news|last=Wendler|first=Jacob|date=December 10, 2025|title=Trump says he hopes to see CNN sold in Warner Bros. merger|website=Politico|publisher=Axel Springer SE|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/12/10/trump-cnn-warner-paramount-skydance-media-00685810|access-date=December 13, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226013625/https://www.politico.com/news/2025/12/10/trump-cnn-warner-paramount-skydance-media-00685810 |archive-date=December 26, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Trump says CNN should be sold as part of Warner Bros Discovery deal|date=December 10, 2025|website=Reuters|publisher=Thomson Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/trump-says-cnn-should-be-sold-part-warner-bros-discovery-deal-2025-12-10/|access-date=December 13, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226013651/https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/trump-says-cnn-should-be-sold-part-warner-bros-discovery-deal-2025-12-10/ |archive-date=December 26, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> CNN is among the various news organizations against which Trump has pursued retaliatory litigation and his administrations have [[Donald Trump's conflict with the news media|removed the press credentials]] of their reporters,<ref>{{cite news|last=Folkenflik|first=David|date=December 12, 2025|title=CNN has endured turmoil for years. Now Trump wants role in its fate|website=NPR|url=https://www.npr.org/2025/12/12/nx-s1-5640900/cnn-trump-warner-bros-netflix-paramount|access-date=December 13, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226013809/https://www.npr.org/2025/12/12/nx-s1-5640900/cnn-trump-warner-bros-netflix-paramount |archive-date=December 26, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> and while the Paramount Skydance proposal included the purchase of CNN, the Netflix proposal did not.<ref>{{cite news|last=Bauder|first=David|date=December 9, 2025|title=Takeover bid of parent company means limbo for CNN and some fellow cable networks|website=Associated Press|url=https://apnews.com/article/cnn-warner-bros-paramount-netflix-ellison-14124eaeaadd13d31323ea3fb5312793|access-date=December 13, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226013819/https://apnews.com/article/cnn-warner-bros-paramount-netflix-ellison-14124eaeaadd13d31323ea3fb5312793 |archive-date=December 26, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Taking questions before the [[Kennedy Center Honors]] on December 7, 2025 (an event historically filmed for broadcast by Paramount's [[CBS]]), Trump told a reporter that Netflix's market share after acquiring WBD "could be a problem", and that he would "be involved in that decision." He also praised Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos, stating that "I have a lot of respect for him. He's a great person, he's done one of the greatest jobs in the history of movies." [[NBC News]] noted that it was rare for US presidents to directly intervene in antitrust cases.<ref name="TrumpShouldNotBeInvolved" /><ref name="TrumpWillStayOut">{{Cite web |date=2026-02-04 |title=Trump says he'll stay out of the Netflix-Paramount fight over Warner Bros. |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/business/media/trump-netflix-paramount-fight-warner-bros-rcna257476 |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=NBC News |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260917170917/https://www.nbcnews.com/business/media/trump-netflix-paramount-fight-warner-bros-rcna257476 |archive-date=September 17, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-08 |title=Trump says $72bn Netflix-Warner Bros deal 'could be a problem' |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cn815egjqjpo |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en-GB |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260917232530/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cn815egjqjpo |archive-date=September 17, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Benen |first=Steve |date=2025-12-08 |title=Trump plans to play a role in proposed Netflix, Warner Brothers deal: 'I'll be involved' |url=https://www.ms.now/rachel-maddow-show/maddowblog/trump-plans-to-play-a-role-in-proposed-netflix-warner-brothers-deal-ill-be-involved |access-date=2026-09-17 |website=[[MS NOW]] |publisher=[[Versant]] |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260918042115/https://www.ms.now/rachel-maddow-show/maddowblog/trump-plans-to-play-a-role-in-proposed-netflix-warner-brothers-deal-ill-be-involved |archive-date=September 18, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In an interview with CNBC on December 8, 2025, David Ellison suggested that CNN would be merged with [[CBS News]], which had been included in the [[Merger of Skydance Media and Paramount Global|Paramount–Skydance merger]] that was completed on August 7, 2025. Before the Paramount–Skydance merger, [[Paramount Global]] paid a $16 million settlement in a [[60 Minutes#Deceptive editing lawsuit|lawsuit Trump filed against the company over alleged deceptive editing on ''60 Minutes'']] that observers suggested was necessary for the merger to be approved by the Federal Communications Commission (which was required because of Paramount's ownership of 28 [[broadcast license]]s of CBS-affiliated television stations).<ref>{{cite interview|last=Ellison|first=David|date=December 8, 2025|title=CNBC Transcript: Paramount Skydance Chairman & CEO David Ellison Speaks with CNBC's David Faber on "Squawk on the Street" Today|interviewer=David Faber|website=CNBC|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2025/12/08/cnbc-transcript-paramount-skydance-chairman-ceo-david-ellison-speaks-with-cnbcs-david-faber-on-squawk-on-the-street-today.html|access-date=December 14, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226013828/https://www.cnbc.com/2025/12/08/cnbc-transcript-paramount-skydance-chairman-ceo-david-ellison-speaks-with-cnbcs-david-faber-on-squawk-on-the-street-today.html |archive-date=December 26, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last1=Hirsch|first1=Lauren|last2=Mullin|first2=Benjamin|date=April 7, 2025|title=Trump and Paramount Agree on Mediator in '60 Minutes' Lawsuit|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/07/business/media/trump-paramount-mediator-60-minutes.html|access-date=April 14, 2025|work=[[The New York Times]]|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250407205301/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/07/business/media/trump-paramount-mediator-60-minutes.html|archive-date=April 7, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref> After the acquisition, David Ellison made a series of changes to CBS News that [[Source (journalism)|anonymous sources]] within the division suggested were in response to Trump's criticisms of the organization, including hiring [[Kenneth R. Weinstein]] (the former CEO of the conservative [[think tank]] [[Hudson Institute]]) as [[Organizational ombudsman|ombudsman]], conservative columnist [[Bari Weiss]] as [[editor-in-chief]] (in a deal that also included the acquisition of her digital publication ''[[The Free Press (CBS News)|The Free Press]]''), and ending its corporate [[DEI]] initiatives. FCC chair Brendan Carr said that the agency would probably have no role in approving a proposed acquisition of WBD by Netflix, as neither companies hold broadcast licenses.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Goldsmith|first1=Jill|last2=Patten|first2=Dominic|last3=Johnson|first3=Ted|date=September 11, 2025|title=Paramount Exploring Bid For Warner Bros. Discovery|website=Deadline Hollywood|url=https://deadline.com/2025/09/paramount-exploring-bid-warner-bros-discovery-1236529093/|access-date=January 6, 2026|archive-date=September 11, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250911181210/https://deadline.com/2025/09/paramount-exploring-bid-warner-bros-discovery-1236529093/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Ted |date=December 5, 2025 |title=The Regulatory Road: Netflix Banking On Overcoming The Trump Factor In Warner Bros. Deal — Analysis |url=https://deadline.com/2025/12/netflix-warner-bros-trump-regulatory-approval-1236634472/ |access-date=December 7, 2025 |website=Deadline |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205163617/https://deadline.com/2025/12/netflix-warner-bros-trump-regulatory-approval-1236634472/ |archive-date=December 5, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>{{efn|Prior to its acquisition by AT&T, Time Warner sold Atlanta's [[WPCH-TV]] (the former WTBS, and its only U.S. broadcast station) to [[Meredith Corporation]] to streamline government approval of the deal. Turner had already [[Local marketing agreement|outsourced]] operations of WPCH under an agreement with Meredith's then-CBS affiliate [[WANF|WGCL]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite news|title=Meredith purchases Peachtree TV from Time Warner/Turner Broadcasting System|url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/radiotvtalk/meredith-purchases-peachtree-from-time-warner-turner-broadcasting-system/JGNY1b0fNQfkKagSRNf9wM/|first=Rodney|last=Ho|newspaper=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|publisher=Cox Enterprises|date=February 23, 2017|access-date=September 22, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180922211751/https://www.ajc.com/blog/radiotvtalk/meredith-purchases-peachtree-from-time-warner-turner-broadcasting-system/JGNY1b0fNQfkKagSRNf9wM/|archive-date=September 22, 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ajc-meredithcontrol">{{cite news |last=Swartz |first=Kristi E. |date=January 18, 2011 |title=Parent of CBS Atlanta to take over operations of Peachtree TV |url=http://www.ajc.com/business/parent-of-cbs-atlanta-807725.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110121024024/https://www.ajc.com/business/parent-of-cbs-atlanta-807725.html |archive-date=January 21, 2011 |access-date=January 18, 2011 |newspaper=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |publisher=Cox Enterprises}}</ref>}}

When asked in the CNBC interview whether he thought Trump was more supportive of the Paramount Skydance proposal, David Ellison said, "What I would say is I'm incredibly grateful for the relationship that I have with the President, and I also believe he believes in competition."<ref>{{cite interview|last=Ellison|first=David|date=December 8, 2025|title=Paramount Skydance CEO says their offer to Warner Bros. Discovery is superior for shareholders|interviewer=David Faber|website=CNBC|url=https://www.cnbc.com/video/2025/12/08/paramount-skydance-ceo-says-their-offer-to-warner-bros-discovery-is-asuperior-for-shareholders-a.html|access-date=December 14, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251226013950/https://www.cnbc.com/video/2025/12/08/paramount-skydance-ceo-says-their-offer-to-warner-bros-discovery-is-asuperior-for-shareholders-a.html |archive-date=December 26, 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref> Trump also previously arranged for Larry Ellison to acquire a sizable ownership share of [[TikTok]] as part of the enforcement of the [[Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act#Enforcement|ban-or-divestment law]] for foreign adversary controlled social media applications enacted in the United States in 2024. As the Justice Department's [[Antitrust Division]] and the [[Federal Trade Commission]] (FTC) have overlapping jurisdiction in reviewing [[mergers and acquisitions]] for compliance with U.S. antitrust laws,<ref>{{cite news|last=Spangler|first=Todd|date=December 5, 2025|title=Would Donald Trump Try to Block Netflix's Takeover of Warner Bros.?|work=Variety|url=https://variety.com/2025/biz/news/would-trump-block-netflix-warner-bros-deal-regulatory-approvals-1236601031/|access-date=January 12, 2026|archive-date=January 8, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260108064201/https://variety.com/2025/biz/news/would-trump-block-netflix-warner-bros-deal-regulatory-approvals-1236601031/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Zahn|first=Max|date=December 11, 2025|title=Bids for Warner Bros. Discovery face uncertain Trump approval process, some experts say|work=ABC News|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Business/bids-warner-bros-discovery-face-uncertain-trump-approval/story?id=128204415|access-date=January 12, 2026|archive-date=December 11, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251211131947/https://abcnews.go.com/Business/bids-warner-bros-discovery-face-uncertain-trump-approval/story?id=128204415|url-status=live}}</ref> Paramount Skydance submitted required forms with both the FTC and the DOJ on December 8.<ref>{{cite news|last=Manfredi|first=Lucas|date=January 8, 2026|title=Department of Justice Reviewing Paramount's Warner Bros. Discovery Bid|work=TheWrap|url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/department-of-justice-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-bid-review/|access-date=January 12, 2026|archive-date=January 8, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260108162317/https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/department-of-justice-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-bid-review/|url-status=live}}</ref> On December 12, 2025, Trump purchased corporate [[Security (finance)|debt security]] [[Bond (finance)|bonds]] from both WBD and Netflix, valued at up to $500,000 each.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weprin|first=Alex|date=January 16, 2026|title=Trump Bought Netflix and Warner Bros. Discovery Bonds In Days After Megadeal Was Announced|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/trump-bought-netflix-warner-bros-discovery-bonds-after-deal-1236476189/|access-date=January 17, 2026|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|archive-date=January 16, 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260116231005/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/trump-bought-netflix-warner-bros-discovery-bonds-after-deal-1236476189/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In a February 4, 2026, interview with NBC News' [[Tom Llamas]], Trump walked back his previous remarks and stated that he would not involve himself in reviewing the WBD deal, leaving the process to the DOJ. He explained that "there is a theory that one of the companies is too big, and it shouldn't be allowed to do it. And the other company is saying something else. They are beating the hell out of each other, and there will be a winner."<ref name="TrumpWillStayOut" /><ref name="TrumpShouldNotBeInvolved">{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Ted |date=February 4, 2026 |title=Donald Trump Now Says He 'Shouldn't Be Involved' In DOJ Review Of A Netflix Or Paramount Acquisition Of Warner Bros. |url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/trump-netflix-warner-bros-paramount-merger-1236709602/ |access-date=February 4, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |archive-date=February 5, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260205005055/https://deadline.com/2026/02/trump-netflix-warner-bros-paramount-merger-1236709602/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On March 13, 2026, Defense Secretary [[Pete Hegseth]] publicly stated that he looked forward to CNN being bought by the Ellisons while criticizing the network due to its coverage of the [[2026 Iran war]], saying: "The sooner David Ellison takes over that network, the better".<ref>{{Cite news|last=Grynbaum|first=Michael M.|date=March 13, 2026|title=Pete Hegseth Says 'the Sooner David Ellison' Buys CNN, 'the Better'|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/13/business/media/pete-hegseth-david-ellison-cnn.html|url-access=subscription|access-date=April 23, 2026}}</ref>

On May 8, 2026, the [[Freedom of the Press Foundation]] and [[Reporters Without Borders]] issued a request to Paramount chief legal officer [[Makan Delrahim]] for access to books and records under Delaware law, in order to investigate allegations that the company was currying favors with the Trump administration to expedite approval of the WBD acquisition.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bolies |first=Corbin |date=May 8, 2026 |title=Press Freedom Groups Demand Access to Ellisons' Paramount Records Amid Reports of White House Favors |url=https://www.thewrap.com/media-platforms/journalism/press-freedom-groups-call-for-paramount-records-ellisons-trump/ |access-date=May 8, 2026 |website=[[TheWrap]] |language=en |archive-date=May 9, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509123609/https://www.thewrap.com/media-platforms/journalism/press-freedom-groups-call-for-paramount-records-ellisons-trump/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On May 12, 2026, House Democrats [[Jamie Raskin]] and [[Frank Pallone]] sent a letter to Ellison requesting records of donations to Trump or his causes, and to similarly disclose whether he had made any offers to the president to change CNN's coverage post-acquisition in exchange for expedited approval.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-12 |title=US House lawmakers press Paramount CEO on Warner Brothers acquisition |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/house-lawmakers-press-paramount-ceo-warner-brothers-acquisition-2026-05-12/ |access-date=2026-09-07 |website=Reuters |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260512164446/https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/house-lawmakers-press-paramount-ceo-warner-brothers-acquisition-2026-05-12/ |archive-date=May 12, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

US attorney general and Trump's former personal lawyer [[Todd Blanche]] stated that he was "part of [the] decision" by the DOJ to approve the Paramount acquisition.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Ted |date=2026-07-15 |title=Todd Blanche Grilled On DOJ's Greenlight Of Paramount-WBD Merger |url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/todd-blanche-paramount-warner-bros-merger-1236983076/ |access-date=2026-09-10 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260715181936/https://deadline.com/2026/07/todd-blanche-paramount-warner-bros-merger-1236983076/ |archive-date=July 15, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref>

On July 15, 2026, David and Larry Ellison were sued by a Paramount shareholder, accusing them of offering "illegal private benefits" to Trump in order to expedite government approval for the sale, including the dismissal of CNN anchors that Trump had been critical of.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 15, 2026 |title=David and Larry Ellison Sued by Paramount Investor Alleging 'Illegal' Side Deal With Donald Trump to Secure U.S. Approval for Warner Bros. Takeover |url=https://variety.com/2026/film/news/david-larry-ellison-sued-paramount-side-deal-trump-warner-bros-1236812034/ |access-date=2026-07-15 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260715213233/https://variety.com/2026/film/news/david-larry-ellison-sued-paramount-side-deal-trump-warner-bros-1236812034/ |archive-date=July 15, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> Paramount argued that the suit "recycles allegations that have already been reported and already addressed", and that "no commitments from either David or Larry Ellison have been made to any government body, State AG, or federal agency regarding the future of CNN or any other news property, other than the goal to deliver truth-based journalism".<ref>{{Cite web|date=July 15, 2026|title=Paramount Calls Shareholder Suit Vs Ellisons, Board Recycled Allegations, Says No Commitments Made On News Coverage While Pursuing WBD|url=https://deadline.com/2026/07/paramount-shareholder-lawsuit-fiduciary-duty-trump-wbd-1236983298/|access-date=2026-07-16|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260716122202/https://deadline.com/2026/07/paramount-shareholder-lawsuit-fiduciary-duty-trump-wbd-1236983298/|archive-date=July 16, 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

On October 6, 2026, after the deal completed, Trump praised the newly formed company, stating “It’s gonna be a great company.”<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spangler |first=Todd |date=2026-10-06 |title=Donald Trump Praises Newly Merged Paramount-Warner Bros.: 'They're Terrific People, and It's Gonna Be a Great Company' |url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/trump-praises-paramount-warner-bros-skydance-merger-terrific-people-1236903643/ |access-date=2026-10-06 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

==== Congressional hearings and investigations ====
In February 2026, Netflix co-chief executive officer Ted Sarandos and WBD chief strategy officer Bruce Campbell testified before the [[United States Senate]] regarding the company's proposal.<ref>{{Cite AV media |title=Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos testifies on Proposed Acquisition of Warner Bros. before U.S. Senate |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=447CgcAePm4 |date=February 3, 2026 |language=en |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |via=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> While the Senate does not directly approve such transactions, the hearing provided lawmakers with an opportunity to seek information on the deal's potential impact on consumers, workers, and competitors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Godoy |first=Jody |date=February 3, 2026 |title=Netflix co-CEO faces grilling by US Senate panel over Warner Bros deal |url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/netflix-co-ceo-faces-grilling-by-us-senate-panel-over-warner-bros-deal-2026-02-03/ |access-date=February 3, 2026 |website=[[Reuters]]}}</ref> In response to questioning regarding the transaction's potential effects on theatrical distribution and the film production ecosystem, Sarandos stated that the company would commit to a 45-day theatrical exhibition window for films produced by WBD following the proposed acquisition. Lawmakers from both parties raised concerns regarding the deal's potential impact on competition, labor markets, and content distribution. Senators questioned Sarandos on issues including residual payments, employment conditions in the entertainment industry, and Netflix's market position relative to other platforms. Sarandos stated that residuals were governed by collective bargaining agreements negotiated through the [[Alliance of Motion Picture and Television Producers]] and cited industry data indicating growth in residual payments in recent years. Senators also examined the competitive relationship between subscription-based streaming services and advertising-supported platforms such as [[YouTube]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Ted |date=February 3, 2026 |title=At Senate Hearing, Netflix's Ted Sarandos Commits To 45-Day Theatrical Window, Grilled By Republican Over Transgender Content — Update |url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/netflix-warner-bros-senate-antitrust-1236707208/ |access-date=February 3, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref>

Sarandos argued that viewing patterns increasingly overlapped across platforms and cited the expansion of professionally produced content and long-form programming on YouTube, as well as its growing share of television-based viewing. Members of the [[US Department of Justice|Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Antitrust]] described the proposed acquisition as significant in scale and raised concerns regarding consolidation in the streaming industry. Subcommittee chair [[Mike Lee]] stated that the transaction warranted scrutiny due to its potential effects on competition for creative talent, content distribution, and consumer choice, including risks associated with vertical integration. Senator [[Cory Booker]] expressed concerns about the cultural and market implications of further consolidation in the entertainment industry and said that representatives of competing bidder Netflix had agreed to testify publicly at the hearing. Also testifying was Bruce Campbell, chief revenue and strategy officer of WBD. Netflix executives have stated that they have engaged in discussions with the [[U.S. Department of Justice Antitrust Division]], [[European Commission|European Union competition]] authorities, and state attorneys general regarding the transaction. The proposed acquisition remains subject to regulatory review, and Netflix has characterized the deal as pro-competitive, while regulators and lawmakers continue to assess its potential effects on market concentration and consumer outcomes.

Following testimony in February 2026 before the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Antitrust, Competition Policy, and Consumer Rights, lawmakers continued to evaluate Netflix's proposed acquisition of the studio and streaming assets of WBD. During the hearing, Sarandos addressed questions related to market competition, consumer impact, and the company's role in the global entertainment industry. The hearing formed part of a broader legislative and regulatory review process examining whether the transaction would comply with antitrust standards and serve the public interest. Lawmakers did not reach conclusions during the session, and the proposed acquisition remains subject to further regulatory scrutiny.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mihalick |first=Peter |date=February 4, 2026 |title=Netflix Wins Day in Congressional Hearing |url=https://www.realclearpolicy.com/articles/2026/02/04/netflix_wins_day_in_congressional_hearing_1162803.html |access-date=February 4, 2026 |website=[[RealClearPolicy]] |archive-date=March 12, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260312165910/https://www.realclearpolicy.com/articles/2026/02/04/netflix_wins_day_in_congressional_hearing_1162803.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On February 6, 2026, Senator [[Adam Schiff]] and Representative [[Laura Friedman]] sent a letter to Sarandos and Greg Peters, and to David Ellison, requesting detailed commitments regarding the preservation and expansion of film and television jobs in Los Angeles in connection with their respective proposed mergers involving Warner Bros. The lawmakers noted prior public statements by Sarandos and Ellison asserting that their bids for the studio would benefit consumers and strengthen competition. Sarandos had stated that Netflix's proposed merger with Warner Bros. would help create and protect jobs in the entertainment industry. Schiff and Friedman wrote that such statements should be supported by concrete, measurable commitments to California and U.S. workers, emphasizing the importance of maintaining California's role as a center of film and television production. Ellison said that Paramount and WBD would continue to operate separately and preserve jobs after the Paramount–WBD merger deal closed.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Knapp |first=JD |date=March 19, 2026 |title=David Ellison Hopes to 'Build a Stronger Hollywood' and Save Jobs by Keeping Paramount and WBD Operating Separately |url=https://www.thewrap.com/media-platforms/film-studios/david-ellison-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-merger-jobs/ |work=[[TheWrap]] |access-date=March 19, 2026 |language=en-US |archive-date=March 19, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260319193614/https://www.thewrap.com/media-platforms/film-studios/david-ellison-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-merger-jobs/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Ellison |first1=David |title=Dear Senator Schiff and Representative Friedman |url=https://www.schiff.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/David-Ellison-Letter-to-Rep.-Friedman-and-Sen.-Schiff-2-28-2658.pdf |website=schiff.[[senate.gov]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260320151543/https://www.schiff.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/David-Ellison-Letter-to-Rep.-Friedman-and-Sen.-Schiff-2-28-2658.pdf |archive-date=March 20, 2026 |language=en |date=February 28, 2026}}</ref>

On February 12, 2026, [[Gail Slater]] left her post as [[assistant attorney general]] for the [[United States Department of Justice Antitrust Division|antitrust division]]; CBS News reported she was removed by senior Trump administration officials. Confirmed with bipartisan support in 2025 and seen by some Democrats as a guard against political interference, her departure came as [[Live Nation Entertainment]] faced an antitrust trial and settlement talks with Justice Department officials outside the division, while deputy Mark Hamer also exited that week.

On February 25, 2026, Sarandos scheduled a visit to the White House by February 26 to talk about Netflix's bid.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 25, 2026 |title=Sarandos Schleps To White House To Counterpunch Paramount's Potential Upper Hand In WBD Bid |url=https://deadline.com/2026/02/sarandos-white-house-netflix-paramount-warner-bros-1236736230/ |access-date=February 25, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref> ''Axios'' later reported that after Sarandos arrived in Washington, he did not meet with Trump or any White House officials because the meeting was canceled, and that he instead met only with Justice Department officials.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fischer |first=Sara |date=2026-03-03 |title=Scoop: The White House meeting that never was |url=https://www.axios.com/2026/03/03/netflix-sarandos-trump-white-house-wbd-deal |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=Axios |language=en |archive-date=March 5, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260305163759/https://www.axios.com/2026/03/03/netflix-sarandos-trump-white-house-wbd-deal |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== U.S. states and cities ====
In February 2026, Republican [[state attorneys general]] from ([[Alabama]], [[Alaska]], [[Iowa]], [[Kansas]], [[Montana]], [[Nebraska]], [[North Dakota]], [[South Carolina]], [[Tennessee]], [[Utah]] and [[West Virginia]]) sent a letter to the [[United States Department of Justice]] to express concern that a Netflix merger with Warner Brothers would "likely result in undue market concentration that stifles competition and therefore creates higher prices, lower reliability, and less innovation for one of America's major industries—all to the detriment of American consumers."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bird |first1=Brenna |last2=Brown |first2=Derek |last3=Cox |first3=Stephen |last4=Hilgers |first4=Mike |last5=Knudsen |first5=Austin |last6=Kobach |first6=Kris |last7=Marshall |first7=Steve |last8=McCuskey |first8=JB |last9=Skrmetti |first9=Jonathan |last10=Wilson |first10=Alan |last11=Wrigley |first11=Drew |author1-link=Brenna Bird |author2-link=Derek Brown (politician) |author3-link=Stephen J. In an interview with [[MS NOW]]'s [[Jacob Soboroff]], California Attorney General [[Rob Bonta]] said reports that he was looking to require Paramount to divest [[CNN]] as a condition for the deal to go through were "opining".<ref>{{cite web | title=Will California AG Force Paramount to Sell CNN? Bonta Says 'I Have No Idea' Where That 'Comes From' | website=[[Variety (magazine)]] | date=June 30, 2026 | url=https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/california-attorney-general-force-paramount-sell-cnn-rob-bonta-1236799191/ | access-date=July 2, 2026 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260702211626/https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/california-attorney-general-force-paramount-sell-cnn-rob-bonta-1236799191/ | archive-date=July 2, 2026 | url-status=live }}</ref>

On July 13, 2026, 12 Democratic attorneys general from twelve states ([[Arizona]], [[California]], [[Colorado]], [[Connecticut]], [[Massachusetts]], [[Minnesota]], [[Nevada]], [[New Jersey]], [[New Mexico]], [[New York (state)|New York]], [[Oregon]], and [[Washington state]]), sued to block the acquisition. Bonta's press release said, "The proposed merger, the largest in Hollywood history, would combine two of Hollywood's [[Major film studios|five major film distributors]] and two of the five major basic cable channel owners."<ref>{{cite press release |title=Attorney General Bonta Files Lawsuit to Block $110 Billion Warner Bros./Paramount Merger |url=https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-bonta-files-lawsuit-block-110-billion-warner-brosparamount |website=[[oag.ca.gov]] |language=en |date=July 12, 2026 |quote=In filing today's lawsuit, Attorney General Bonta leads the attorneys general of Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, and Washington. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260714100446/https://oag.ca.gov/news/press-releases/attorney-general-bonta-files-lawsuit-block-110-billion-warner-brosparamount |archive-date=July 14, 2026 |access-date=July 14, 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The State of California v. On July 31, 2026, California Governor [[Gavin Newsom]] expressed concerns about the state lawsuit and said that if the merger were blocked, state employment would suffer. Newsom has also encouraged Bonta to find a resolution out of court. On August 11, 2026, California Democratic gubernatorial nominee [[Xavier Becerra]] urged both sides to settle the lawsuit,<ref>{{cite web | title=Xavier Becerra Urges Both Sides to Settle Paramount-WB Antitrust Suit Ahead of Trial: 'Let's Be Adults' | website=TheWrap | date=August 11, 2026 | url=https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/xavier-becerra-hopes-paramount-warner-antitrust-suit-settles-before-court/ | access-date=August 21, 2026 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260826094143/https://www.thewrap.com/industry-news/deals-ma/xavier-becerra-hopes-paramount-warner-antitrust-suit-settles-before-court/ | archive-date=August 26, 2026 | url-status=live }}</ref> followed by Los Angeles Mayor [[Karen Bass]] on August 20.<ref>{{cite web | title=L.A. Mayor Karen Bass Throws Her Support Behind Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Settlement | website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] | date=August 20, 2026 | url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/karen-bass-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-settlement-1236677994/ | access-date=August 21, 2026 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260821175844/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/karen-bass-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-settlement-1236677994/ | archive-date=August 21, 2026 | url-status=live }}</ref>
