The '''Nickelodeon Group''', also known as '''Nickelodeon Networks Inc.''' and '''Paramount Kids and Family Group''', is the children's and family entertainment division of the [[Skydance TV|TV]] division of [[Skydance]] that oversees the operations of [[cable television]] [[television channel|channel]] [[Nickelodeon]] and its derivative channels and services. It was created in 2002.

==History==
===2002–2009===
Nickelodeon Group was founded in 2002, after MTV Networks (now [[Paramount Media Networks]]) merged the business operations of Nickelodeon, [[Nick at Nite]] and [[Nicktoons (American TV channel)|Nicktoons]] into one division.

On January 4, 2006, [[Herb Scannell]] resigned from Nickelodeon. [[Cyma Zarghami]] was appointed in his place as president of the newly formed Kids & Family Group, which included Nickelodeon, Nick at Nite, [[Noggin (brand)|Noggin]], [[The N]], [[Nicktoons (American TV channel)|Nicktoons Network]], [[TV Land]], [[CMT (American TV channel)|CMT]] and [[CMT Pure Country]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Dempsey|first=John|date=January 4, 2006|title=Scannell changes channel|url=https://variety.com/2006/scene/markets-festivals/scannell-changes-channel-1117935495/|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=February 24, 2022}}</ref>

In 2007, Nickelodeon entered into a four-year development deal with [[Sony Music]] to produce music-themed TV shows for the network, to help fund and launch tie-in albums, and to produce original soundtrack songs that could be released as singles.<ref>{{cite web|date=June 14, 2007|title=Nickelodeon, Sony pact for tunes|url=https://variety.com/2007/music/markets-festivals/nickelodeon-sony-pact-for-tunes-1117966962/|website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=February 24, 2022}}</ref> ''[[The Naked Brothers Band (TV series)|The Naked Brothers Band]]'', a rock-[[mockumentary]] series of a pre-teenage rock band led by two real-life brothers who write and perform the songs, ran from 2007 to 2009; it was successful for children in the 6–11 age group. By February 2007, the band's song "Crazy Car" had appeared on the ''[[Billboard Hot 100]]'', and the soundtrack albums from the first two seasons, each of which signed to Sony Music's own [[Columbia Records]], appeared on the ''[[Billboard 200]]''. The only greenlit series produced under the Sony Music partnership, ''[[Victorious]]'', ran from 2010 to 2013. A similar hit music-themed sitcom ''[[Big Time Rush (TV series)|Big Time Rush]]'' ran from 2009 to 2013, and featured a similar partnership with [[Columbia Records]]; however, Columbia was only involved with the show's music, and Sony Music became involved with the series' production midway through its first season. It became Nickelodeon's second-most successful live-action show of all time after ''[[iCarly]]''; the ''Big Time Rush'' episode "Big Time School of Rocque" was viewed by 6.8&nbsp;million viewers for its premiere on January 18, 2010, setting a new record as the highest-rated live action series premiere in the channel's history.

===2009–present===
On February 1, 2009, Nickelodeon discontinued the [[TEENick]] block, as the name would soon be used for its own channel.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nexttv.com/article/189298-_Nick_Of_Time_For_Rebrand.php|title='Nick' Of Time For Rebrand|publisher=[[Multichannel News]]|date=March 1, 2009|access-date=June 2, 2010}}</ref>

On July 29, 2009, Nickelodeon unveiled a new logo that would be implemented toward the end of the year, designed by New York City–based creative director/designer Eric Zim. It was part of a year dedicated to strengthening the brand's identity. The logo was intended to create a unified look that can better be conveyed across all of MTV Networks' children's channels.<ref name="variety">{{cite magazine|url=https://variety.com/2009/biz/markets-festivals/nickelodeon-unveils-new-logo-1118006659/|title=Nickelodeon unveils new logo|last=Schneider|first=Michael|magazine=Variety|date=July 29, 2009|access-date=February 24, 2022}}</ref> The new logo debuted on September 28, 2009, across Nickelodeon, Nick at Nite, and Nicktoons, along with [[TeenNick]] (which replaced The N and named after the TEENick block) and [[Nick Jr. Channel]] (which replaced Noggin and named after the concurrently-running Nick Jr. block).<ref name="variety"/>

The [[wordmark]] logo bug was given a blimp background in the days prior to the [[2010 Kids' Choice Awards|2010]] and [[2011 Kids' Choice Awards]] to match the award given out at the ceremony; beginning the week of September 7, 2010, the logo bug was surrounded by a splat design (in the manner of the logo used from 2005 to 2009) during new episodes of Nickelodeon original series. The new logo was adopted in the [[Nickelodeon (UK & Ireland)|United Kingdom]] on February 15, 2010, in [[Nickelodeon (Spain)|Spain]] on February 19, 2010, in Southeast Asia on March 15, 2010, in [[Nickelodeon Latin America|Latin America]] on April 5, 2010, in India on June 25, 2010<ref>{{Cite news|title=Nick India undergoes makeover, to don new logo from June 25|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/media/entertainment/media/nick-india-undergoes-makeover-to-don-new-logo-from-june-25/articleshow/6087665.cms|access-date=2021-05-15}}</ref> and on the [[ABS-CBN Corporation|ABS-CBN]] block "Nickelodeon on ABS-CBN" in the [[Philippines]] on July 26, 2010. On November 2, 2009, a Canadian version of Nickelodeon was launched, in partnership between Viacom and [[Corus Entertainment]] (owners of [[YTV (Canadian TV channel)|YTV]], which had aired and continued to air Nickelodeon's series); as a result, versions of Nickelodeon now exist in most of North America.

In October 2009 and September 2010, respectively, Viacom acquired the ''[[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (Franchise)|Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles]]'' and ''[[Winx Club]]'' franchises into the Nickelodeon family. Nickelodeon Animation Studio produced a new [[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2012 TV series)|CGI-animated ''Turtles'' series]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2012/jul/19/tuning-in-to-tv-teenage-mutant-ninja-turtles-have-/|title=Tuning in to TV: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles have new series, toys|work=[[The Washington Times]]|date=July 29, 2012|access-date=July 23, 2013}}</ref> and new seasons of ''Winx Club'' with CGI sequences.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/network-press-releases/global-hit-animated-series-winx-club-comes-to-nickelodeon-starting-june-27/|title=Global Hit Animated Series 'Winx Club' Comes To Nickelodeon, Starting June 27|work=[[Screener (website)|Screener]]|date=June 9, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170701104555/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/network-press-releases/global-hit-animated-series-winx-club-comes-to-nickelodeon-starting-june-27/|archive-date=July 1, 2017}}</ref> Both productions comprised Nickelodeon's strategy to reboot two established brands for new viewers: ''TMNT'' was intended to reach an audience of boys aged 6 to 11, and ''Winx'' was aimed at the same age group of girls. In February 2011, Viacom acquired a third of [[Rainbow S.r.l.|Rainbow SpA]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2011/tv/news/winx-creator-in-the-pink-1118032886/|title=Winx creator in the pink|last=Vivarelli|first=Nick|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=February 26, 2011}}</ref> the Italian studio that introduced ''Winx Club''. The purchase was valued at 62 million euros (US$83&nbsp;million)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.videoagedaily.com/digitalissues/PDF/Video+Age+International+September-October+2014/files/assets/common/downloads/page0024.pdf|title=Straffi's Rainbow: Europe's Largest Animation House Has Growing Pains|work=[[Video Age Daily]]}}</ref> and led to new shows being co-developed by Rainbow and Nickelodeon, including ''[[Maggie & Bianca: Fashion Friends#Production|My American Friend]]'' and ''[[Club 57 (TV series)|Club 57]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.produ.com/noticias/iginio-straffi-de-rainbow-tuvimos-una-influencia-muy-importante-en-la-historia-de-club-57|title=Iginio Straffi de Rainbow: Tuvimos una influencia muy importante en la historia de Club 57 para garantizar su atractivo en Europa|last=Ramos-Weiner|first=Maribel|work=Produ|date=November 20, 2018|access-date=April 5, 2021|language=es|archive-date=June 21, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210621173436/https://www.produ.com/noticias/iginio-straffi-de-rainbow-tuvimos-una-influencia-muy-importante-en-la-historia-de-club-57|url-status=dead}}</ref> Also in 2011, Nickelodeon debuted ''[[House of Anubis]]'', a series based on the Nickelodeon [[Nickelodeon (Netherlands)|Netherlands]] series ''[[Het Huis Anubis]]'', which became the first original scripted series to be broadcast in a daily strip (similar to the soap opera format). Produced in the United Kingdom, it was also the first original series by the flagship U.S. channel to be produced entirely outside of North America.

2011 saw Nickelodeon's longtime ratings dominance among all children's cable channels begin to topple: it was the highest-rated cable channel during the first half of that year,<ref>{{cite web|last=Gorman|first=Bill|title=Nickelodeon Scores Its Most-Watched Second Quarter Ever|url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2010/06/29/nickelodeon-scores-its-most-watched-second-quarter-ever/55673/|date=June 29, 2010|publisher=TVbytheNumbers|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101118134446/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2010/06/29/nickelodeon-scores-its-most-watched-second-quarter-ever/55673|archive-date=November 18, 2010|access-date=October 3, 2011}}</ref> only for its viewership to experience a sharp double-digit decline by the end of 2011, described as "inexplicable" by Viacom management.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/viacom-nielsen-investigating-inexplicable-nickelodeon-260149|title=Viacom, Nielsen Investigating 'Inexplicable' Nickelodeon Ratings Drop|last=Szalai|first=Georg|magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=November 10, 2011}}</ref> The channel would not experience a calendar week ratings increase until November 2012 (with viewership slowly rebounding after that point);<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/nickelodeon-first-weekly-ratings-gain-more-than-a-year-393716|title=Analyst: Nickelodeon Posts First Weekly Ratings Gain in More Than a Year|last=Szalai|first=Georg|magazine=The Hollywood Reporter|date=November 22, 2012}}</ref> however its 17-year streak as the highest-rated cable network in total day viewership was broken by Disney Channel during that year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/ratings/2012/12/19/disney-channel-earns-historic-number-1-total-day-win-in-kids-2-11-in-2012-magical-year-two-for-disney-junior-block-693305/20121219disney01/|title=Disney Channel Earns Historic #1 Total Day Win in Kids 2–11 in 2012; Magical Year Two for Disney Junior Block|work=The Futon Critic|date=December 19, 2012}}</ref> Around late 2012, Nickelodeon made a sweeping change to their network by cancelling or ending their teen shows (''[[How to Rock]]'', ''[[iCarly]]'', ''[[Victorious]]'', ''[[Bucket & Skinner's Epic Adventures]]'', ''[[Supah Ninjas]]'', ''[[Life With Boys]]'' and ''[[Big Time Rush (TV series)|Big Time Rush]]'') in favor of newer shows targeted to a younger block.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2012/08/nickelodons-victorious-cancelled-after-three-seasons-317085/|title=Nickelodeon's 'Victorious' Cancelled After Three Seasons|first1=Dominic|last1= Patten|first2=Nellie|last2=Andreeva|date=August 10, 2012|work=Deadline}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2012/08/nickelodeons-how-to-rock-cancelled-after-one-season-325169/|title=Nickelodeon's 'How To Rock' Cancelled After One Season|first1=Nellie|last1=Andreeva|date=August 27, 2012}}</ref> On July 17, 2014, the network televised the inaugural [[2014 Kids' Choice Sports|Kids' Choice Sports]], a spin-off of the Kids' Choice Awards that honors athletes and teams from the previous year in sports.

From 2016 to 2018, the network produced TV movies based on its older properties, including those of ''[[Legends of the Hidden Temple (film)|Legends of the Hidden Temple]]'', ''[[Hey Arnold!: The Jungle Movie|Hey Arnold!]]'', ''[[Rocko's Modern Life: Static Cling|Rocko's Modern Life]]'', and ''[[Invader Zim: Enter the Florpus|Invader Zim]]''. The former two aired on the Nickelodeon channel, while the latter two premiered in August 2019 on [[Netflix]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://ew.com/tv/2017/04/04/nickelodeon-invader-zim-tv-movie/|title=Nickelodeon reviving Invader Zim for TV movie|last=Snetiker|first=Marc|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|date=April 4, 2017|access-date=July 22, 2017}}</ref>

In June 2018, Cyma Zarghami resigned as president of Nickelodeon, after 33 years of working at the network.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://deadline.com/2018/06/cyma-zarghami-departs-nickelodeon-1202403072/|title=Cyma Zarghami Stepping Down As President Of Nickelodeon Group|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=June 4, 2018|access-date=August 8, 2019|language=en}}</ref> In October 2018, ''[[All That]]'' co-creator [[Brian Robbins]] succeeded her as president of Nickelodeon.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/viacom-names-brian-robbins-president-nickelodeon-1148352|title=Viacom Names Brian Robbins President of Nickelodeon|last=Sandberg|first=Bryn|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=October 1, 2018|access-date=August 8, 2019|language=en}}</ref>

On January 22, 2019, Viacom acquired the streaming service [[Pluto TV]] for $340 million, which has since launched various Nickelodeon-branded channels.<ref>{{cite web|last=Roettgers|first=Janko|date=January 22, 2019|title=Viacom Has Bought Pluto TV for $340 Million|url=https://variety.com/2019/digital/news/viacom-pluto-tv-acquisition-1203114773/|website=[[variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=November 2, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Porter|first=Jon|date=January 23, 2019|title=Viacom acquires Pluto TV streaming service for $340 million|url=https://www.theverge.com/2019/1/23/18194071/viacom-pluto-tv-acquisition-340-million|website=[[The Verge]]|access-date=November 2, 2024}}</ref> On August 6, 2019, Viacom acquired the rights to the ''[[Garfield]]'' franchise, with plans for a new animated series.<ref>{{cite web|last=White|first=Peter|date=August 6, 2019|title='Garfield': Viacom Acquiring Classic Property; Nickelodeon Preps Animated Series|url=https://deadline.com/2019/08/viacom-to-acquire-garfield-1202662457/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=November 1, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Steinberg|first=Brian|date=August 6, 2019|title=Viacom Acquires Comic-Strip Cat Garfield|url=https://variety.com/2019/tv/news/garfield-nickelodedon-licensing-rights-viacom-1203293468/|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|publisher=[[Penske Media Corporation]]|access-date=November 16, 2019}}</ref> Later that year, Viacom signed a multi-year content production agreement with [[Netflix]] to produce several original films and series based on Nickelodeon properties.<ref>{{cite web|title=Netflix and Nickelodeon form multi-year output deal to produce original animated films and series for kids & families around the world|url=https://about.netflix.com/en/news/netflix-and-nickelodeon-form-multi-year-output-deal-to-produce-original-animated-films-and-series-for-kids-families-around-the-world|date=November 13, 2019|publisher=[[Netflix]]|access-date=November 16, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Barnes|first=Brookes|title='SpongeBob' Spinoff Highlights Netflix-Nickelodeon Deal|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/13/business/media/netflix-nickelodeon-spongebob-squarepants.html|access-date=November 16, 2019|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=November 13, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Slater|first=Georgina|title=Netflix and Nickelodeon Team Up as Disney+ Lands 10 Million Subscribers One Day After Launch|url=https://people.com/movies/netflix-nickelodeon-team-disney-lands-10-million-subscribers/|access-date=November 16, 2019|work=[[People (magazine)|People]]|date=November 15, 2019}}</ref>

After Viacom [[2019 merger of CBS and Viacom|re-merged with CBS Corporation]] to form [[ViacomCBS]] at the end of 2019, it was announced that Nickelodeon content would be available for streaming on the CBS All Access streaming service<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thewrap.com/cbs-viacom-merger-close-date-dec-4/|title=CBS and Viacom Reveal December Merger Date – Mark Your Calendars|last=Maglio|first=Tony|work=TheWrap|date=November 25, 2019|access-date=April 5, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/nickelodeon-content-coming-cbs-all-access-1257873|title=Nickelodeon Content Coming to CBS All Access|date=November 25, 2019|work=The Hollywood Reporter|access-date=December 3, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://comicbook.com/tv-shows/2019/11/25/cbs-all-access-nickelodeon-shows-danger-mouse-cloudy-with-a-chan/|title=CBS All Access to Add Nickelodeon Children's Programming|date=November 25, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}}</ref> (later relaunched as [[Paramount+]] on March 4, 2021), with ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' spinoff ''[[Kamp Koral: SpongeBob's Under Years|Kamp Koral]]'' and ''[[The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run]]'' debuting on the service that same day.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thewrap.com/spongebob-movie-sponge-on-the-run-release-paramount-plus-march-launch/|title=''SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run'' to Debut on Paramount+ at March Launch|last=Welk|first=Brian|work=[[TheWrap]]|date=January 28, 2021|access-date=January 28, 2021}}</ref> Throughout 2021, Paramount+ would announce and debut new programming based on Nickelodeon IP, including a [[The Fairly OddParents: Fairly Odder|live-action sequel series]] to ''[[The Fairly OddParents]]'' that premiered in March 2022, a [[Rugrats (2021 TV series)|CGI-animated reboot]] of ''[[Rugrats]]'', and an ''[[iCarly]]'' [[ICarly (2021)|sequel series]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Paramount+ Content Announcements|url=https://www.viacomcbs.com/files/2021/02/Paramount-Content-Addendum-2.24.21.pdf|date=February 24, 2021|website=ViacomCBS|language=en-US|url-status=live|archive-date=February 25, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225231031/https://www.viacomcbs.com/files/2021/02/Paramount-Content-Addendum-2.24.21.pdf|access-date=February 26, 2021}}</ref>

By January 2021, Nickelodeon Group announced it had consolidated its live-action film & television production operations including current series & studio content and had combined it with those of ViacomCBS's fellow production & digital media and entertainment subsidiary [[Awesomeness (company)|Awesomeness]] into forming one live-action production studio under the Nickelodeon Productions and Awesomeness names with Nickelodeon's head of live-action production Shauna Phelan and Zack Olin would serve as co-presidents of the combined production unit Nickelodeon/Awesomess Live-Action Studio whilst continued co-heading Nickelodeon's live-action scripted production operations as they would now heading Awesomeness's live-action production operations whilst Nickelodeon and Awesomnesss Films executive VP Syrinthia Studer would oversee the combined live-action production under the Nickelodeon Productions and Awesomeness names as executive vice president of live-action films.<ref>{{cite web|title=ViacomCBS Kids & Family Combines Live-Action Production Under Nick's Shauna Phelan & Zack Olin; Awesomeness' Shelley Zimmerman Exits|url=https://deadline.com/2021/01/viacomcbs-kids-and-family-live-action-production-shauna-phelan-zack-olin-awesomeness-shelley-zimmerman-exits-1234672618/|website=Deadline Hollywood|first=Nellie|last=Andreeva|date=January 13, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Shauna Phelan, Zack Olin to Lead Nickelodeon, Awesomeness Live-Action as ViacomCBS Consolidates Production, Shelley Zimmerman Exits Awesomeness|url=https://variety.com/2021/tv/news/shauna-phelan-zack-olin-to-lead-nickelodeon-as-viacomcbs-consolidates-live-action-production-shelley-zimmerman-exits-awesomeness-1234884562/|website=Variety|first=Elaine|last=Low|date=January 13, 2021}}</ref>

[[CBS Sports]] began partnering with Nickelodeon on its [[NFL on CBS|coverage]] of the [[NFL|National Football League]], with Nickelodeon simulcasting a special version of an early [[2020–21 NFL playoffs|2021]] Wild Card playoff game under the [[NFL on Nickelodeon]] banner.<ref>{{cite news|url= https://www.sportsbusinessjournal.com/SB-Blogs/Breaking-News/2020/03/NFL-WC-Games.aspx|title=New NFL would extend its partnership with Nickelodeon by allowing them to air another Wild Card game in January 2022, and a weekly highlights show hosted by CBS' [[Nate Burleson]] and ''[[Tyler Perry's Young Dylan]]'' star Dylan Gilmer.<ref>{{cite web|last=Taranto|first=Steven|date=September 10, 2021|title=Nickelodeon renews partnership with NFL for 2021 season, will broadcast 2022 Wild Card round again|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/nickelodeon-renews-partnership-with-nfl-for-2021-season-will-broadcast-2022-wild-card-round-again/|access-date=September 11, 2021|website=CBS Sports}}</ref> Nickelodeon aired its first regular-season game in 2022, with the [[Denver Broncos]] taking on the defending Super Bowl champion [[Los Angeles Rams]] as part of the NFL's Christmas Day slate.<ref>{{cite web|last=Willner|first=Barry|date=May 10, 2022|title=Slime Time: Nickelodeon to broadcast Christmas Day NFL game|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Entertainment/wireStory/slime-time-nickelodeon-broadcast-christmas-day-nfl-game-84619850|access-date=May 10, 2022|website=ABC News}}</ref>

In October 2025, two months after Paramount Global merged with Skydance Media to form Paramount Skydance, [[MTV Entertainment Studios|Showtime/MTV Entertainment Studios]] and [[Skydance Television]] were folded into the revived [[Paramount Television Studios]] shortly after, which also folded [[Nickelodeon Productions]] and the former AwesomenessTV production units into it. Paramount Television Studios would then take over as the main production arm for Awesomeness and Nickelodeon;  for the latter beginning with the upcoming ''[[Victorious]]'' spin-off series ''[[Hollywood Arts]]'' which was moved to Netflix, having been originally ordered at Nickelodeon, as the first Nickelodeon-branded series produced by the revived studio.<ref>{{cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=October 24, 2025|title='Victorious' Trina Vega Spinoff 'Hollywood Arts' Starring Daniella Monet Moves To Netflix With Series Order & Cast Set; Nick & P+ Get Second Window|url=https://deadline.com/2025/10/victorious-trina-vega-spinoff-hollywood-arts-daniella-monet-netflix-1236596090/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|access-date=October 24, 2025}}</ref>

'''Nicktoons''' (formerly '''Nicktoons TV''' and '''Nicktoons Network''') is an American [[pay television]] [[television channel|channel]] owned by the [[Nickelodeon Group]], a subdivision of the [[Skydance TV]] division of [[Skydance Corporation]]. Launched on May 1, 2002, the channel is geared towards [[children]] aged 7 to 11,<ref>{{cite web|title=Viacom|url=http://www.viacom.com/brands/pages/nicktoons.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130728042044/http://www.viacom.com/brands/pages/nicktoons.aspx|archive-date=July 28, 2013|website=Viacom}}</ref> and serves as an extension of the [[Nicktoons|eponymous brand]] used by [[Nickelodeon]] for its original animated programming.

{{As of|2023|12}}, Nicktoons is available to approximately 43 million pay television households in the United States, down from its peak of 69 million in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wrestlenomics.com/u-s-cable-network-households-universe-1990-2023-nielsen-data/|title=U.S. cable network households (universe), 1990 – 2023|website=wrestlenomics.com|date=May 14, 2024|access-date=July 28, 2019}}</ref>

== History ==
{{More citations needed section|date=September 2023}}
[[File:Nicktoons-Network-original-balloon-text-logo.png|200x200px|thumb|Nicktoons Network wordmark used from September 23, 2005 to September 28, 2009|left]]
Nicktoons launched on May 1, 2002, as '''Nicktoons TV'''. It was part of the [[digital cable]]–exclusive [[Paramount Media Networks|MTV Networks]] Digital Suite, in order to entice cable operators to pick up the network and give them a marketing advantage over satellite services.{{citation needed|date=August 2011}} However, by early 2004, Nickelodeon management changed course and offered it to [[Digital Satellite Service|digital satellite services]] [[DirecTV]] and [[Dish Network]]. The network was originally marketed as commercial-free, with comedic promos involving Nickelodeon Animation Studios, two-minute cartoon shorts from foreign markets, and former program promotions that had previously been used on Nickelodeon taking up commercial time. By September 23, 2005, as the network's distribution increased, it began to carry regular advertising.{{citation needed|date=August 2011}}

On September 28, 2009, the network's logo changed as part of Nickelodeon's universal rebranding effort.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20090802094659/https://www.variety.com/article/VR1118006659.html?categoryid=14&cs=1 Nickelodeon Unveils New Logo], ''Variety.com'', July 29, 2009</ref> A high-definition feed was launched on August 13, 2013, and is available on several providers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dbstalk.com/topic/205985-directv-hd-channel-anticipation-official-q3-13-thread/page-16|title=DIRECTV HD Channel Anticipation (Official Q3-13 Thread)|work=DBSTalk|access-date=27 October 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Official AVS National HD Channel Lineups – Cable/DBS/Fiber/IPTV – Updated 8/3/13|url=http://www.avsforum.com/t/1462894/official-avs-national-hd-channel-lineups-cable-dbs-fiber-iptv-updated-8-3-13|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130810235651/http://www.avsforum.com/t/1462894/official-avs-national-hd-channel-lineups-cable-dbs-fiber-iptv-updated-8-3-13|archive-date=August 10, 2013|access-date=27 October 2014}}</ref> Like Viacom's other HD channels, any programming produced in 4:3 SD is [[pillarbox]]ed on this feed. As the network blended in more Nickelodeon programming into its schedule, the Nicktoons website was [[Sunset (computing)|sunset]] to a [[parked domain|parking page]] directing viewers to [[Nick.com]] before it was eventually redirected quietly to the latter website.

[[File:Nicktoons logo (2023, Splatless).svg |thumb|right|Splatless version of the 2023 logo, with “<small>TOO</small><big>n</big><small>S</small>” in green-cyan, concurrently used alongside the main version since January 1, 2024]]
On January 1, 2024, Nicktoons (along with [[TeenNick]]) debuted its variant of the refreshed Splat logo and new on-air interstitials, similar to Nickelodeon's. This refresh also changes the color for "<small>TOO</small><big>n</big><small>S</small>" from blue to green-cyan.

=== NickSpongeBob ===
[[File:NickSpongeBob 2024 Logo.png|200x200px|thumb|NickSpongeBob logo used since May 23–September 8, 2025, and May 25–September 8, 2026|left]]
As part of Paramount's efforts to honor the 25th anniversary of ''[[SpongeBob SquarePants]]'', Nicktoons began to primarily run only ''SpongeBob'' and associated media daily beginning on May 13, 2024, promoted as "Non-Stop SpongeBob. All Day. Every Day." Repeat airings of new episodes of Nickelodeon's other animated series returned to Nicktoons later in the year. On May 23, 2025, Nicktoons temporarily rebranded itself as '''NickSpongeBob,''' following a trend set by the [[Nicktoons (UK & Ireland)|British and Irish version of the channel]] starting in 2022, during airings of ''SpongeBob'' shows, focusing exclusively on broadcasting content from the franchise throughout the summer. The channel returned to Nicktoons on September 8, 2025. It again rebranded to NickSpongeBob on May 25, 2026, and again returned to Nicktoons on September 8. However, the channel continued to remain fully dedicated to reruns of ''SpongeBob SquarePants''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvinsider.com/network/nicktoons/schedule/ |title=Nicktoons - TV Schedule & Listings Guide - TV Insider |access-date=October 10, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260901203919/https://www.tvinsider.com/network/nicktoons/schedule/ |archive-date=September 1, 2026 |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Programming ==
{{main|List of programs broadcast by Nicktoons}}

{{More citations needed section|date=October 2024}}
Since its inception, Nicktoons mainly aired programs carried over from the main Nickelodeon channel, with some occasional airing of Nickelodeon's live-action programming depending on Viacom's programming direction at the time.

Beginning in the mid-2000s, older shows such as ''[[Rocko's Modern Life]]'' and ''[[CatDog]]'' were removed from the schedule as more acquired programming and Nicktoons Network originals were premiering. Many of these programs were phased out in the early-2010s. ''[[Fantastic Four: World's Greatest Heroes]]'', ''[[Iron Man: Armored Adventures]]'', and ''[[Wolverine and the X-Men (TV series)|Wolverine and the X-Men]]'' were effectively cancelled when [[The Walt Disney Company]] acquired [[Marvel Studios]] in 2009.

Historically, episodes of under-performing Nickelodeon programs, including original shows and acquisitions, have been [[Burning off|burned off]] on the Nicktoons channel. Some first run shows include ''[[The Angry Beavers]]'', ''[[As Told by Ginger]]'', ''[[Back at the Barnyard]]'', ''[[Breadwinners (TV series)|Breadwinners]]'', ''[[Bunsen Is a Beast]]'', ''[[CatDog]]'', ''[[El Tigre: The Adventures of Manny Rivera]]'', ''[[Fanboy & Chum Chum]]'', ''[[The Fairly OddParents]]'', ''[[Harvey Beaks]]'', ''[[Invader Zim]]'', ''[[It's Pony]]'', ''[[Kung Fu Panda: Legends of Awesomeness]]'', ''[[Digimon Fusion]]'', ''[[Making Fiends (TV series)|Making Fiends]]'', ''[[The Mighty B!]]'', ''[[My Life as a Teenage Robot]]'', ''[[The Penguins of Madagascar]]'', ''[[Pig Goat Banana Cricket]]'', ''[[Planet Sheen]]'', ''[[Random! Cartoons]]'', ''[[Robot and Monster]]'', ''[[T.U.F.F. Puppy]]'', ''[[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2012 TV series)|Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2012)]]'', and ''[[Welcome to the Wayne]]''. Some acquired shows that were moved over and finished their runs on the network include ''[[Alvinnn!!! and the Chipmunks]]'', ''[[Ollie's Pack]]'', and ''[[Rabbids Invasion]]'' (though the later seasons moved to [[Netflix]] for its fourth and final season, Along with its Hour-Long Series Finale Follow-up "Mission to Mars").

=== NickSports ===
On September 3, 2014, a two-hour Wednesday prime time programming block named '''NickSports''' was launched, tying into the [[2014 Kids' Choice Sports|Kids' Choice Sports]] inaugurated earlier that year.<ref name="ksn">{{cite news|last1=Dickson|first1=Jeremy|title=Nicktoons adds weekly sports block|url=http://kidscreen.com/2014/09/03/nicktoons-adds-weekly-sports-block/|access-date=December 16, 2016|work=Kidscreen|publisher=Brunico Communications Ltd.|date=September 3, 2014}}</ref> The block presented mainly licensed programming focusing on sports, including the [[Rob Dyrdek]]-starring ''[[Wild Grinders]]'' and ''[[NFL Rush Zone: Guardians of the Core]]'', along with sports-related feature films such as ''[[Bend It Like Beckham]]'', ''[[Cool Runnings]]'', and ''[[Space Jam]]''.<ref name="ksn"/> Sometime in 2015, the block was moved to a Friday prime time slot. The block ended in September 2018.

== Branding ==
From 2005 until 2009, Nicktoons Network branded itself as the "Animation Capital of the World" (or "ACOW") in advertisements for the channel.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.trademarkia.com/animation-capital-of-the-world-78725074.html|title=Animation Capital of the World – Viacom|work=trademarkia.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Nicktoons Network Homepage, 2009|url=http://nicktoonsnetwork.nick.com/home.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090228193106/http://nicktoonsnetwork.nick.com/home.html|archive-date=28 February 2009|work=nick.com}}</ref> Various mascots were seen in promotional bumpers, including the Three Headed Monster.<ref>{{Cite web | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190406134728/http://www.interspectacular.com/casestudy/ThreeHeadedMonster_Small.pdf | url=http://www.interspectacular.com/casestudy/ThreeHeadedMonster_Small.pdf | archive-date=2019-04-06 | title=Case Study: Three Headed Monster | website=www.interspectacular.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Three Headed Monster, "Hook" | url=https://vimeo.com/787736404 }}</ref> Around this time, the Nicktoons Network website introduced an animated robot character with a large singular eye, animated using "photo-puppetry."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maissito.com/Nickelodeon-ACOW|title=Nickelodeon's ACOW - www.maissito.com|work=maissito.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2007/ACOW on Nicktoons – Carlos Ordonez|url=http://carlos-ordonez.com/2007-ACOW-Nicktoons|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150213182359/http://carlos-ordonez.com/2007-ACOW-Nicktoons|archive-date=13 February 2015|work=carlos-ordonez.com}}</ref>

'''Nicktoons''' is a children’s [[Arab]] [[pay television]] channel broadcasting to the Middle East & North Africa. Nicktoons was launched on 15 February 2017 and uses the [[Nicktoons (British and Irish TV channel)|British/Irish version's]] on-air broadcast graphic package produced by Beautiful Creative.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.beautifulcreative.com/nicktoons|website=Beautifulcreative.com|title=Channel Rebrand - Nicktoons|access-date=2019-06-19}}</ref> The channel is available on [[Orbit Showtime Network|OSNtv]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.timeoutdubai.com/kids/440691-the-best-family-tv-to-watch-on-osn-this-month|title=The best family TV to watch on OSN this month|work=[[Time Out Dubai]]|date=11 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.arabnews.com/node/1363961/corporate-news | title=OSN Play to offer 24 new live channels for free | date=29 August 2018 }}</ref>

'''OWN: Oprah Winfrey Network''' ('''OWN''', also known as the '''OWN Network''') is an American multinational [[Cable television in the United States|basic cable]] [[television]] network which launched on January 1, 2011, effectively replacing the [[Discovery Health Channel]], which one month later merged with [[FitTV]] to become Discovery Fit & Health (now known as [[Discovery Life]]). OWN is owned by [[Skydance Corporation]]'s [[List of assets owned by Warner Bros. Discovery|networks]] division, with a minority stake by [[Harpo Productions]].

Founded by television personality [[Oprah Winfrey]], the channel primarily focuses on lifestyle programming targeting a female audience, with an initial focus on programming with themes related to life improvement, relationships, and spirituality, and a particular focus on targeting [[African Americans]].

Initially a 50/50 joint venture, Discovery acquired a larger stake in the network in 2017 and again in December 2020, when Discovery increased its ownership in OWN from 73% to 95%. Harpo remains a "significant" minority stakeholder, and Winfrey remains contracted with the channel. OWN competes with other networks aimed at African Americans such as the now-sister [[BET Media Group]]'s [[BET|namesake channel]] and the [[E. W. Scripps Company]]'s [[Bounce TV]]. As of February 2015, OWN is available to approximately 81.9 million pay television households (70.3% of households with television) in the United States.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2015/02/22/list-of-how-many-homes-each-cable-network-is-in-as-of-february-2015/366230/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150223220414/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2015/02/22/list-of-how-many-homes-each-cable-network-is-in-as-of-february-2015/366230/|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 23, 2015|title=List of how many homes each cable network is in as of February 2015|last=Seidman|first=Robert|work=TV by the Numbers|publisher=Zap2it|date=February 22, 2015|access-date=March 14, 2015}}</ref>

== History ==
=== Development ===
After becoming Discovery Communications' new CEO in 2007, [[David Zaslav]] found [[Discovery Health Channel|Discovery Health]] to be underperforming along with its other [[digital cable]] networks launched in the last decade, and having significantly lower carriage fees in comparison to the company's namesake, [[Discovery Channel]]. As a result, he began to explore the possibility of relaunching the channel as a joint venture with another partner. Zaslav's wife was an avid reader of Oprah Winfrey's [[Oprah Daily|''O'' magazine]] (a joint venture with [[Hearst Corporation]]); believing that her [[Value (ethics)|values]] could serve as the basis for a cable network, he contacted Winfrey's agents to hold a meeting in April 2007.<ref name="nyt-own"/> On January 15, 2008, Discovery Communications officially announced that it had entered into a joint venture with Winfrey's studio [[Harpo Productions]], under which it would relaunch Discovery Health as "OWN: The Oprah Winfrey Network", in the second half of 2009.<ref name="nyt-own"/><ref name="wp-ownannounce"/>

Winfrey would serve as the chairwoman of the channel, which was expected to deal in factual programming oriented towards her personal philosophy of "living your best life"; this would include topics such as health, love, parenting, and spirituality. Discovery provided $100 million in funding, and Harpo provided access to its library and Winfrey's website, Oprah.com.<ref name="nyt-own"/> As it was still under contract with [[CBS Television Distribution]] through May 2011, her existing syndicated talk show ''[[The Oprah Winfrey Show]]'' could not initially air on OWN, but there was a possibility that a spiritual continuation or successor to the program could air on OWN in the future.<ref name="nyt-own"/>

Winfrey and her long-time partner [[Stedman Graham]] had discussed the idea of forming her own channel as early as 1992. After Winfrey demonstrated discontent over [[tabloid talk show|"confrontational" talk shows]] on television, Graham suggested that she should form an "Oprah Winfrey Network" if she were dissatisfied with the current state of television.<ref name="nyt-own"/> OWN was not Winfrey's first cable television venture, having been co-founder of the women's cable network [[Oxygen (TV network)|Oxygen]]. However, her involvement was limited to being an investor and eventually offering it an after-show component, ''[[Oprah After the Show]]'', after deciding not to offer her reruns to the network; Winfrey distanced herself from Oxygen when discussing OWN, stressing the importance of actually having influence over programming when participating in such ventures.<ref name="nyt-own"/><ref name="wp-ownannounce">{{cite news|title=Discovery, Winfrey to Team Up On Network|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/01/15/AR2008011501562.html|newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=April 29, 2017}}</ref>

==== Delays and launch ====
In November 2008, Zaslav stated that Winfrey had planned to not renew her contract with CBS for ''The Oprah Winfrey Show'' beyond the 2010–2011 season, and that the show could move to OWN in some form following the end of the syndicated run. Harpo Productions denied the report, stating that Winfrey did not declare her decision at the time to continue the show on syndication after 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tvguide.com/News/Oprah-Ending-2011-58308.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090514235548/http://www.tvguide.com/News/Oprah-Ending-2011-58308.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 14, 2009 |title=Will Oprah Winfrey End Show in 2011? |work= [[TV Guide]] |date=November 8, 2008 |access-date=November 12, 2008}}</ref> The development of OWN was affected by internal conflicts, as well as Winfrey's continued commitment to her talk show. Its launch was delayed from its originally-announced target of 2009 to an unspecified date. Zaslav pressured Oprah into moving her talk show to the channel, believing that it could expand its business.<ref name="nyt-own"/>

In November 2009, Lisa Erspamer, a Harpo executive who had been a co-executive producer of ''The Oprah Winfrey Show'' starting in 2006, was named chief creative officer of OWN.<ref name="nyt-own">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/12/19/business/19oprah.html|title=Oprah's Network Is Her Highest Hurdle|work=The New York Times|last=Stelter|first=Brian|date=December 18, 2010 |access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en}}</ref> Due to her history of working with Winfrey, the appointment of Erspamer was seen as having stabilized OWN's development; network CEO Christina Norman described Erspamer's appointment as being an "injection of Oprah's [[DNA]]" into the then-upcoming channel.<ref name="nyt-own"/><ref name=":0" /> Later on November 20, Winfrey officially announced that ''The Oprah Winfrey Show'' would conclude in 2011, after its 25th season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://mediadecoder.blogs.nytimes.com/2009/11/20/a-tearful-winfrey-explains-her-departure/|title=A Tearful Winfrey Explains Her Departure|last=Stelter|first=Brian|work=Media Decoder|date=November 20, 2009 |publisher=The New York Times|access-date=October 14, 2018|language=en}}</ref> With the end of her talk show, Winfrey's commitments with Discovery were revised; a commitment for Winfrey to host a talk show on OWN and appear in at least 35 hours of programming per year, was replaced with a commitment to appear in at least 70 hours of programming per year, including ''Oprah's Next Chapter'' (later ''[[Oprah Prime]]''), a primetime interview series hosted by Winfrey.<ref name="nyt-own"/>

The official launch of OWN was set for January 1, 2011, so that it would occur while Oprah's talk show was still on the air. Plans were then called for at least 600 hours of original programming in 2011, as well as acquired and library programming (including reruns of ''The Oprah Winfrey Show'' later in the year, and ''[[Dr. Phil (talk show)|Dr. Phil]]''); although Winfrey did make appearances in some of the programming aired on-launch (such as ''[[Oprah's Master Class]]''), her involvement was expected to increase following the end of ''The Oprah Winfrey Show''.<ref name="nyt-own" /> After the launch of OWN, Discovery Health's programming was merged into another Discovery-owned channel, FitTV, which rebranded as Discovery Fit & Health a month later on February 1, 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.multichannel.com/news/content/discovery-health-lives-combining-fittv/362449|title=Discovery Health Lives On, Combining With FitTV |website=Multichannel|date=January 17, 2011 |language=en|access-date=March 10, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tvnewscheck.com/article/2011/01/17/48429/discovery-to-launch-new-health-fitness--ch|title=Discovery To Launch New Health, Fitness Channel|work=TVNewsCheck|date=January 17, 2011|access-date=April 26, 2015}}</ref> It was subsequently rebranded again as [[Discovery Life]] in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2014/07/discovery-rebrand-fit-health-life-800818/|title=Discovery Will Rebrand Fit & Health Channel As Discovery Life|last=Lieberman|first=David|date=July 8, 2014|language=en-US|access-date=August 27, 2016}}</ref>

=== Early struggles, targeting African Americans ===
During its first year of operation, OWN struggled to build an audience and viewership,<ref name="deadline-cohenown"/> with most of its programs being low-rated besides ''[[Our America with Lisa Ling]]'' (the first OWN program to be renewed for a second season), and ''[[Season 25: Oprah Behind the Scenes]].'' Its average viewership was 135,000 during its second month on air, which was lower than that of Discovery Health.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/02/28/business/media/28own.html?_r=3&ref=business|title=Oprah's New Channel Struggles to Pull In Viewers|last=Stelter|first=Brian|work=The New York Times|date=February 28, 2011 |access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://deadline.com/2011/03/own-moves-behind-the-scenes-to-sunday-goes-to-3-nights-of-original-programming-112344/|title=OWN Moves 'Behind The Scenes' To Sunday, Goes To 3 Nights Of Original Programming|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=March 9, 2011|work=Deadline|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> Norman defended the network's ratings, stating that first-run broadcasts of its original series were drawing larger audiences than those of Discovery Health, and that Discovery's goal was to improve OWN's monthly audience to between 50 and 60 million viewers by the end of the year.<ref name=":1" /> In March 2011, the channel modified its schedule to only have three original nights of primetime programming per-week, moving ''Oprah Behind the Scenes'' to Sunday nights alongside ''Oprah's Master Class''.<ref name=":2" />

On May 6, 2011, OWN's CEO Christina Norman was removed, and replaced by Discovery executive Peter Liguori as an interim CEO.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110508072216/http://www.tvguide.com/News/Oprah-OWN-CEO-1032818.aspx "Oprah Replaces OWN CEO, Says Network Is 'Not Where I Want It to Be'"]. ''[[TV Guide]]''. May 9, 2011.</ref> In July, Winfrey assumed the role of CEO, and  named [[Sheri Salata]] as a co-president.<ref name=":0" /> By September 2011, Discovery had invested $254 million in programming for OWN.<ref name="thr-sweetiepies">{{Cite news|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/own-shifting-attention-to-african-american-viewers-271469|title=OWN Shifting Attention to Its African-American Viewers|work=The Hollywood Reporter|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en}}</ref> The October 2011 premiere of ''[[Welcome to Sweetie Pie's]]'' brought notable gains to the channel: it was the network's highest-rated series at the time, and expanded OWN's average primetime viewership to 216,000. The show was especially popular among [[African American]] audiences, which prompted OWN's executives to factor this demographic into its programming decisions and advertising sales going forward.<ref name="thr-sweetiepies"/> On October 16, 2011, the Sunday program, ''[[Super Soul Sunday]]'', premirered, which included features and segments that "present an array of perspectives on what it means to be alive in today's world."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://deadline.com/2011/09/own-to-launch-super-soul-sunday-block-176745/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181121022207/https://deadline.com/2011/09/own-to-launch-super-soul-sunday-block-176745/|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 21, 2018|title=OWN To Launch 'Super Soul Sunday' Block|date=September 27, 2011|work=Deadline|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref>

''[[The Rosie Show]],'' a talk show hosted by another formerly-syndicated personality, [[Rosie O'Donnell]], also premiered in October, to an average of 497,000 viewers (along with an additional million via a simulcast across sister channels Discovery Fit & Health, [[Investigation Discovery]], [[Destination America|Planet Green]], and [[TLC (TV network)|TLC]]).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/rosie-odonnell-own-ratings-246768|title=Rosie O'Donnell's New OWN Talk Show Soft in Ratings Debut|work=The Hollywood Reporter|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en}}</ref> By November, its ratings had fallen to an average of 171,000 nightly viewers.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tvguide.com/News/Biz-Ellen-The-Chew-Anderson-Talk-Shows-1039722.aspxy|title=The Biz: Analyzing This Season's Talk Shows|date=November 15, 2011|work=TVGuide.com|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en}}{{dead link|date=July 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> In January 2012, an attempt was made to retool the program by hiring Shane Farley (producer of the syndicated ''[[The Rosie O'Donnell Show|Rosie O'Donnell Show]]''), and giving it a smaller, more intimate studio.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.broadcastingcable.com/news/own-revamps-rosie-show-new-set-exec-producer-39036|title=OWN Revamps 'The Rosie Show' With New Set, Exec Producer|work=Broadcasting & Cable|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/entertainment/tv/chi-rosie-odonnell-show-set-changes-20120118-story.html|title=Rosie's new talk show set a head-scratcher|last=Metz|first=Nina|work=Chicago Tribune|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> However, viewership was still low, and the series was cancelled in March 2012.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.broadcastingcable.com/news/own-cancels-rosie-odonnell-talk-show-39265|title=OWN Cancels Rosie O'Donnell Talk Show|work=Broadcasting & Cable|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en-us}}</ref>

During its first year of operations, OWN's average primetime audience was 264,000 viewers. This was only slightly higher than the average primetime audience of 216,000 the channel had as Discovery Health.<ref name=":0" /> On January 26, 2012, Lisa Erspamer resigned from OWN; she was replaced in the interim by veteran Discovery executive and former TLC vice president Rita Mullin.<ref name=":0">{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/style/at-oprah-winfrey-network-the-revolving-door-spins-again/2012/01/26/gIQAvlO0TQ_story.html|title=At Oprah Winfrey Network, the Revolving Door Spins Again|last=de Moraes|first=Lisa|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date= January 26, 2012|access-date= April 12, 2012}}</ref> A March 2012 ''[[Oprah's Next Chapter]]'' interview with [[Whitney Houston]]'s daughter [[Bobbi Kristina Brown]] and her family (following Houston's death in February) became OWN's highest-rated special, with 3.5 million viewers.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://deadline.com/2012/03/oprahs-interview-with-whitney-houstons-daughter-delivers-ratings-record-for-own-242799/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160807123910/http://deadline.com/2012/03/oprahs-interview-with-whitney-houstons-daughter-delivers-ratings-record-for-own-242799/|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 7, 2016|title=Oprah's Interview With Whitney Houston's Daughter Delivers Ratings Record For OWN|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=March 12, 2012|work=Deadline|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref>

The channel's losses were estimated to be $330 million by May 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nationalledger.com/pop-culture-news/oprah-own-losses-mounting-256268.shtml|title=Oprah OWN Losses Mounting&nbsp;— Network Off a Reported $330 Million, Off The Air Soon?|last=Cook|first=Wendy|date=May 13, 2012|work=The National Ledger|access-date=May 17, 2012}}</ref> Discovery responded by raising the channel's [[retransmission consent]] fee (OWN was provided to cable providers effectively for free for its first two years on air) to a level more in line with other basic cable channels, a move that the company expected to allow the channel to break even in late-2013.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/01/18/business/media/winfreys-low-rated-cable-channel-is-poised-to-break-through.html|title=Winfrey's Channel Is Set to Break Through|last=Stelter|first=Brian|date=January 17, 2013|work=The New York Times|access-date=December 26, 2019|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

On September 15, 2012, OWN premiered ''[[Iyanla: Fix My Life]],'' a reality series starring [[Iyanla Vanzant]]. It attracted critical acclaim and high audience; its two-night premiere event was seen by 1.1 and 1.6 million total viewers respectively. The Sunday-night airing was the third-highest-rated program of the night across ad-supported cable networks, and was the highest-rated program of the night among women 18-49 and African American women 25–54.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/09/15/arts/television/iyanla-fix-my-life-on-own.html|title='Iyanla: Fix My Life,' on OWN|last=Caramanica|first=Jon|newspaper=The New York Times |date=September 14, 2012 |access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://deadline.com/2012/09/owns-iyania-fix-my-life-debuts-strong-return-of-welcome-to-sweetie-pie-hits-series-high-338396/|title=OWN's 'Iyanla: Fix My Life' Debuts Strong, 'Welcome To Sweetie Pie's' Return Hits Series High|last=Patten|first=Dominic|date=September 18, 2012|work=Deadline|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="wired-foundvoice" />

=== Tyler Perry development deal, expansion into scripted programming===
By October 2012, OWN had seen increases in audience share, especially among women in the [[key demographic]].<ref name=":3" /> That month, OWN also announced a planned expansion into scripted programming by means of an exclusive, multi-year development deal with [[Tyler Perry]], a long-time friend of Winfrey.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|url=https://deadline.com/2012/10/own-enters-scripted-programming-via-multi-year-deal-with-tyler-perry-for-2-series-345945/|title=Oprah' OWN And Tyler Perry In Deal For Scripted Series: Exclusive & Multi-Year|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=October 1, 2012|work=Deadline|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> Perry's first two productions for OWN, the primetime [[soap opera]] ''[[The Haves and the Have Nots (TV series)|The Haves and the Have Nots]]'', and the sitcom ''[[Love Thy Neighbor (American TV series)|Love Thy Neighbor]],'' premiered on May 28 and 29, 2013 respectively.<ref name="thr-perryshows">{{cite news|author=Philiana Ng|date=April 4, 2013|title=OWN Sets Premieres for Tyler Perry's Scripted Series, Greenlights Two Shows|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/own-sets-premieres-tyler-perrys-432953|access-date=April 8, 2013}}</ref> The two-hour series premiere of ''The Haves and the Have Nots'' overtook ''[[Life with La Toya]]'' (1.18 million) as OWN's highest-rated series premiere at the time, with the first episode attracting 1.77 million viewers, and growing to 1.8 million for the second.<ref name="thppi">{{cite news|last=O'Connell|first=Michael|date=May 29, 2013|title=TV Ratings: Tyler Perry Premiere Gives OWN a Record Launch|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/tv-ratings-tyler-perry-premiere-559937|access-date=May 30, 2013}}</ref><ref name="ddpl">{{cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=May 29, 2013|title=Solid Debut For Tyler Perry's 'The Haves And Have Nots' On OWN|url=https://deadline.com/2013/05/solid-debut-for-tyler-perrys-the-haves-and-have-nots-on-own-509916/|access-date=May 30, 2013|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref> The series continued to set viewership records for the channel, with its first-season finale drawing 2.6 million viewers, and the fifth episode of season 2 setting a network-record 3.6 million viewers.<ref>{{cite web|last=Patten|first=Dominic|title=OWN's 'The Haves & The Have Nots' Finale Ratings High, TNT's 'Cold Justice' Premiere Strong|url=https://deadline.com/2013/09/owns-the-haves-the-have-nots-finale-hits-highs-tnts-cold-justice-debuts-strong-578298/|access-date=September 5, 2013|website=Deadline Hollywood|date=September 4, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Kissell|first=Rick|date=March 12, 2014|title='Haves and Have Nots' Sets OWN Ratings Record With Its Finale|language=en-US|work=Variety|url=https://variety.com/2014/tv/ratings/haves-and-have-nots-sets-own-ratings-record-with-its-finale-1201130322/|access-date=November 20, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Patten|first=Dominic|date=January 8, 2014|title=OWN's 'The Haves & The Have Nots' Returns With Series & Network High|language=en-US|work=Deadline|url=https://deadline.com/2014/01/owns-the-haves-the-have-nots-returns-with-series-network-high-660627/|access-date=November 20, 2018}}</ref>

By July 2013, Discovery considered the network to be "cash flow positive".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.adweek.com/tv-video/discovery-ceo-zaslav-declares-own-cash-flow-positive-151503/|title=Discovery CEO Zaslav Declares OWN Cash-Flow Positive|website=Adweek|date=July 30, 2013 |language=en-US|access-date=November 20, 2018}}</ref> In an interview with ''[[People (magazine)|People]]'', Winfrey revealed that in 2012, she had a [[nervous breakdown]] over the channel's performance. [[Jason Russell]] commented on the condition during an interview they were filming, which made Winfrey realize she was experiencing similar symptoms. She explained that "after 25 years of being number one, I had become accustomed to success. I didn't expect failure. I was tested and I had to dig deep", and that the scenario "forced me not to just talk the talk. Failure is a great teacher. I knew this intellectually. But it's another thing if you're living it".<ref name="deadline-cohenown">{{Cite news|url=https://deadline.com/2013/08/oprah-winfrey-talks-own-network-failure-nervous-breakdown-565330/|title=Oprah Winfrey Talks OWN Network, Failure, And Symptoms Of Her Nervous Breakdown|last1=Finke|first1=Nikki|first2=Lisa|last2= de Moraes|date=August 16, 2013|work=Deadline|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref>

In May 2016, Sheri Salata resigned as co-president to launch a new "brand innovation" agency (although Winfrey and OWN were expected to be among her first clients). This left Erik Logan as sole president of the network.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/sheri-salata-exits-as-own-890585|title=Sheri Salata Exits as OWN Co-President|work=The Hollywood Reporter|access-date=November 25, 2018|language=en}}</ref> The June 2016 premiere of ''[[Greenleaf (TV series)|Greenleaf]]'' was OWN's highest-rated series premiere, with 3.04 million viewers.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://deadline.com/2016/06/oprah-winfrey-greenleaf-debut-ratings-best-ever-for-own-tyler-perry-the-haves-and-the-have-nots-1201777540/|title=Oprah-Starring 'Greenleaf' Delivers OWN's Best Debut Ratings Ever|last=Patten|first=Dominic|date=June 22, 2016|work=Deadline|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> ''[[Queen Sugar]]'' also premiered later in September to acclaim, with both series ranking among the top five ad-supported drama series on cable among women 25–54.<ref name="wired-foundvoice">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.wired.com/story/how-oprahs-network-finally-found-its-voice/|title=How Oprah's Network Finally Found Its Voice|magazine=WIRED|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref>

In July 2017, Tyler Perry signed a new film and television/short form development deal with [[Viacom (2005–2019)|Viacom]] for future productions (particularly on [[BET]]) through 2024;<ref name="wired-foundvoice" /> the film deal began immediately, while the television/short form deal would begin after the end of his partnership with OWN in May 2019. OWN stated that Perry's series would continue to air on the network through at least 2020, and that it would "continue to aggressively expand its roster of premium original scripted series."<ref name="wired-foundvoice" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://deadline.com/2017/07/tyler-perry-viacom-film-tv-deal-with-viacom-1202128622/|title=Tyler Perry Inks Mega Film & Television Deal With Viacom|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=July 14, 2017|work=Deadline|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> In August 2017, OWN premiered ''[[Black Love (2017 TV series)|Black Love]]'', a docuseries from filmmakers [[Codie Elaine Oliver|Codie Elaine]] and [[Tommy Oliver (producer)|Tommy Oliver]] on relationships within African-American communities. It was OWN's highest-rated unscripted series premiere with 1.2 million viewers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Petski |first=Denise |date=2017-08-31 |title='Black Love': OWN Orders More Episodes Amid Record Premiere Ratings |url=https://deadline.com/2017/08/black-love-own-orders-more-episodes-record-premiere-ratings-1202159154/ |access-date=2025-10-22 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref>

In December 2017, Discovery announced that it would acquire an additional 24.5% stake in OWN that it did not already own, for $70 million, with Harpo remaining as a significant minority shareholder, and Winfrey remaining CEO. Winfrey also extended her exclusivity agreement with the network and Discovery through 2025.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://deadline.com/2017/12/discovery-communications-ups-stake-in-own-70-million-harpo-deal-oprah-winfrey-extends-contract-through-2025-1202219668/|title=Discovery Communications Ups Stake In OWN Via $70 Million Harpo Deal, Oprah Winfrey Extends Contract Through 2025|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=December 4, 2017|work=Deadline Hollywood|access-date=January 9, 2018}}</ref> In April 2018, OWN ordered two new series from [[Will Packer]], the drama ''[[Ambitions (TV series)|Ambitions]]'' and the dating show ''Ready to Love''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://variety.com/2018/tv/news/own-orders-will-packer-1202755604/|title=OWN Orders Two Series From Will Packer|last=Holloway|first=Daniel|date=April 17, 2018|work=Variety|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en-US}}</ref> In July 2018, Winfrey signed a non-exclusive, multi-platform content deal with [[Apple Inc.]]; this did not affect her role at OWN.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/oprah-winfrey-inks-content-deal-apple-1120552|title=Oprah Winfrey Inks Content Deal With Apple|work=The Hollywood Reporter|access-date=November 20, 2018|language=en}}</ref>

''Wired'' considered OWN to have had a "major stake" in the push towards more diverse portrayals of African Americans in television, while [[Iyanla Vanzant]] argued that OWN had been "celebrating the unseen" among African Americans with shows that "give the minds of the viewers a different interpretation than the one that's often put out in the world."<ref name="wired-foundvoice" />

In October 2018, network president Erik Logan announced that he would resign at the end of the year to pursue a job as head of content for the [[World Surf League]]. He was succeeded by Tina Perry, who had worked business and legal affairs for [[MTV]], [[VH1]], and OWN.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/own-shakeup-tina-perry-take-gm-reins-erik-logan-heads-world-surf-league-1150238|title=OWN Exec Moves: Tina Perry Named GM, Erik Logan Departing for World Surf League|work=The Hollywood Reporter|access-date=November 25, 2018|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.broadcastingcable.com/news/tina-perry-named-gm-of-own|title=Tina Perry Named GM of OWN: Oprah Winfrey Network|work=Broadcasting & Cable|access-date=November 25, 2018|language=en-us}}</ref>

On June 9 and 10, 2020, OWN broadcast ''[[OWN Spotlight: Where Do We Go From Here?]],'' a two-night special hosted by Winfrey that discussed [[Institutional racism|systemic racism]] and [[Police brutality in the United States|police brutality]] in U.S. society following [[George Floyd protests|protests]] over the [[murder of George Floyd|police murder of George Floyd]]. The special featured appearances by politicians such as [[Stacey Abrams]] and Mayor of Atlanta [[Keisha Lance Bottoms]], and other journalists and personalities. The special was simulcast by all Discovery networks, and was seen by an average of 7.3 million viewers across both nights.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Patten|first=Dominic|date=June 12, 2020|title=Oprah Sees 11M Tune In For Two-Night 'Where Do We Go From Here?' Special On George Floyd Death & Race In America|url=https://deadline.com/2020/06/oprah-george-floyd-special-ratings-ava-duvernay-stacey-abrams-own-discovery-facebook-1202957893/|access-date=June 16, 2020|website=Deadline|language=en}}</ref> Amid the concurrent [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the channel also aired two remotely-produced series for its "Sisterhood Saturday Night" block, ''Fear Not with Iyanla Vanzant'' and the celebrity talk show ''Girlfriends Check In.''<ref>{{Cite web |last=White |first=Peter |date=2020-04-29 |title=Oprah's OWN Preps Remote Non-Scripted Series 'Fear Not With Iyanla Vanzant' & 'Girlfriends Check In' |url=https://deadline.com/2020/04/own-oprah-iyanla-vanzant-girlfriends-check-in-1202921182/ |access-date=2025-10-22 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref>

In December 2020, Discovery increased its ownership in OWN from 73% to 95% for $35 million in an all-stock deal, giving Harpo approximately 1.34 million shares in Discovery.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Goldsmith|first=Jill|date=December 22, 2020|title=Discovery Boosts Stake In OWN, Oprah Winfrey Takes Stock In Longtime Partner|url=https://deadline.com/2020/12/discovery-boosts-stake-own-and-oprah-winfrey-takes-equity-stake-in-longtime-partner-1234660727/|access-date=December 22, 2020|website=Deadline|language=en-US}}</ref>

In April 2022, Discovery Inc. merged with [[WarnerMedia]] to form [[Warner Bros. Discovery]]; the acquisition places OWN under common ownership with [[Warner Bros. Television]], which has produced a number of OWN's recent scripted series.<ref name="Andreeva">{{Cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=2022-04-07 |title=WarnerMedia-Discovery Deal To Forge Deeper Ties Between OWN, Warner Bros. TV & HBO Max |url=https://deadline.com/2022/04/warnermedia-discovery-merger-own-warner-bros-tv-hbo-max-1234996738/ |access-date=2022-04-09 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Programming==
{{Main|List of programs broadcast by Oprah Winfrey Network}}
As of 2025, the network's programming consists primarily of lifestyle programming, including syndicated reruns of [[Talk show|talk]] and [[court show]]s (particularly ''[[Dr. Phil (talk show)|Dr. Phil]]'', ''[[Hot Bench]]'', and ''[[Judge Mathis]]''), and reruns of library lifestyle programming from other Warner Bros. Discovery channels.

=== Scripted programming ===
In October 2012, OWN expanded into scripted programming by announcing an exclusive development deal with [[Tyler Perry]], beginning with ''[[The Haves and the Have Nots (TV series)|The Haves and the Have Nots]]'' and ''[[Love Thy Neighbor (American TV series)|Love Thy Neighbor]]''.<ref name="thr-perryshows" /> In February 2013, OWN ordered a third season of Perry's canceled [[TBS (American TV channel)|TBS]] sitcom ''[[For Better or Worse (2011 TV series)|For Better or Worse]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=February 20, 2013|title=OWN Picks Up Tyler Perry's Sitcom 'For Better Or Worse', Orders Third Season|language=en-US|work=Deadline|url=https://deadline.com/2013/02/own-picks-up-tyler-perrys-sitcom-for-better-or-worse-orders-third-season-435343/|access-date=November 20, 2018}}</ref>  In January 2014, OWN ordered another drama from Perry, ''[[If Loving You Is Wrong]]'', which was adapted from Perry's feature film ''[[The Single Moms Club]]''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Nededog|first=Jethro|date=June 5, 2014|title=Tyler Perry's 'Single Mom's Club' Adaptation for OWN Gets New Name|url=https://www.thewrap.com/tyler-perrys-own-series-single-moms-club-if-loving-you-is-wrong/|access-date=December 15, 2016|work=[[The Wrap]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=OWN Orders Series Based on Tyler Perry's 'Single Moms Club'|language=en|work=The Hollywood Reporter|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/own-orders-series-based-tyler-669613|access-date=November 20, 2018}}</ref> In February 2015, OWN ordered new seasons of ''For Better Or Worse'', ''The Haves and the Have Nots'', ''If Loving You Is Wrong'', and ''Love Thy Neighbor''.<ref>{{Cite news|author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.-->|date=February 27, 2015|title=OWN Wants More Tyler Perry — And Gets It|language=en-US|work=Deadline|url=https://deadline.com/2015/02/own-tyler-perry-oprah-winfrey-more-episodes-the-haves-and-the-have-nots-1201382917/|access-date=November 20, 2018}}</ref> In November 2017, OWN announced premiere dates for ''[[The Paynes]]'' (a spin-off of Perry's TBS sitcom ''[[Tyler Perry's House of Payne]]''), as well as the fifth and fourth seasons of ''The Haves and the Have Nots'' and ''If Loving You Is Wrong''.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Pedersen|first=Erik|date=November 21, 2017|title=Three Tyler Perry Series Get OWN Premiere Dates, Including Spinoff 'The Paynes'|language=en-US|work=Deadline|url=https://deadline.com/2017/11/tyler-perry-premiere-dates-own-haves-and-have-nots-if-loeing-you-is-wrong-the-paynes-spinoff-1202213219/|access-date=November 20, 2018}}</ref>

On February 2, 2015, OWN announced that it had ordered [[Ava DuVernay]]'s drama ''[[Queen Sugar]]'' (based on the Natalie Baszile [[Queen Sugar (novel)|novel of the same name]]) directly to series, marking OWN's first scripted series not produced by Tyler Perry.<ref name="usatoday-qs">{{cite web|last=Levin|first=Gary|date=February 2, 2015|title=Oprah, DuVernay creating new drama for OWN|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/tv/2015/02/02/oprah-winfrey-ava-duvernay-selma-queen-sugar/22752925/|access-date=February 2, 2015|work=[[USA Today]]}}</ref><ref name="v-queensugar">{{cite web|last=Wagmeister|first=Elizabeth|date=February 2, 2015|title=Oprah Winfrey & Ava DuVernay Creating Original Drama Series For OWN|url=https://variety.com/2015/tv/news/oprah-winfrey-ava-duvernay-own-drama-series-1201421463/|access-date=February 2, 2015|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> This was followed in July by ''[[Greenleaf (TV series)|Greenleaf]],'' a drama from [[Craig Wright (playwright)|Craig Wright]] with Winfrey as an executive producer, that follows the eponymous family's predominantly-African American [[megachurch]] in [[Memphis, Tennessee]].<ref name="deadline-greenleafpickup">{{cite web|author=Denise Petski|title=OWN Sets Megachurch Drama Series From Craig Wright & Lionsgate|url=https://deadline.com/2015/07/own-scripted-megachurch-drama-series-greenleaf-craig-wright-lionsgate-1201487797/|access-date=August 26, 2015|work=Deadline|date=July 30, 2015 }}</ref><ref name="vrt-greenleafpickup">{{cite web|author=Reece Ristau|title=OWN Picks Up Megachurch Drama|url=https://variety.com/2015/tv/news/own-megachurch-drama-greenleaf-1201553493/|access-date=August 26, 2015|work=Variety|date=July 30, 2015 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=de Moraes|first=Lisa|date=August 15, 2016|title='Greenleaf' Adds EP Kathleen McGhee-Anderson For Season 2|url=https://deadline.com/2016/08/greenleaf-oprah-winfrey-kathleen-mcghee-anderson-executive-producer-1201803669/|access-date=January 5, 2019|website=Deadline|language=en}}</ref>

In July 2017, ''Queen Sugar'' was renewed for a third season, and Harpo Films signed DuVernay to a first-look television and digital media deal.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Otterson|first=Joe|date=July 26, 2017|title='Queen Sugar' Renewed for Season 3, Ava DuVernay Inks First-Look TV Deal With Harpo Films|language=en-US|work=Variety|url=https://variety.com/2017/tv/news/queen-sugar-renewed-season-3-ava-duvernay-oprah-winfrey-1202506864/|access-date=November 20, 2018}}</ref> In August 2017, OWN also ordered [[Tarell Alvin McCraney]]'s ''[[David Makes Man]]'', a coming-of-age drama set in [[South Florida]].<ref>{{Cite news|last1=Petski|first1=Denise|last2=Andreeva|first2=Nellie|date=August 16, 2017|title=OWN Orders Coming-Of-Age Drama Series From 'Moonlight's Tarell Alvin McCraney|language=en-US|work=Deadline|url=https://deadline.com/2017/08/own-orders-coming-of-age-drama-series-moonlight-co-writer-producer-1202150362/|access-date=November 20, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=June 26, 2018|title=Tarell Alvin McCraney's OWN Series Sets Cast Led By Phylicia Rashad & Akili McDowell, Gets Title & Showrunner|url=https://deadline.com/2018/06/tarell-alvin-mccraney-own-series-david-makes-man-cast-phylicia-rashad-akili-mcdowell-showrunner-dee-harris-lawrence-1202417511/|access-date=January 5, 2019|website=Deadline|language=en}}</ref> McCraney stated that he was given offers by other outlets such as [[Netflix]], but that Winfrey (who had made a surprise visit when he visited the network to pitch the series) "from the start was wanting to open the story up and understand what it was about".<ref name="wired-foundvoice" />

OWN cancelled ''The Paynes'' in August 2019.<ref>{{cite news|last=Ho|first=Rodney|date=August 6, 2019|title=OWN ends 'The Paynes,' but will Tyler Perry's comedy move to BET or not?|work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/radiotvtalk/own-ends-the-paynes-but-will-tyler-perry-comedy-move-bet-not/d72MnRpAZRjuBzogtpuPYM/|access-date=August 7, 2019}}</ref>

On August 20, 2021, it was reported that OWN was in negotiations to revive the canceled CBS legal drama ''[[All Rise (TV series)|All Rise]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=2021-08-20|title='All Rise' Eyes Comeback With Season 3 Pickup By OWN After CBS Cancellation|url=https://deadline.com/2021/08/all-rise-eyes-season-3-pickup-own-cbs-cancellation-resurrected-comeback-1234818449/|access-date=2021-08-21|website=Deadline|language=en-US}}</ref> On September 29, 2021, the series was renewed for a third season scheduled to premiere in 2022; OWN acquired linear rights, while [[HBO Max]] and [[Hulu]] jointly acquired streaming rights.<ref name="Andreeva"/>

On January 10, 2026, OWN debuted ''Maxxed Out'', a reality series that follows host Leah Collins as she advises individuals and families experiencing debt and financial strain.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tinoco |first=Armando |date=2025-12-09 |title='Maxxed Out': OWN Sets Premiere Date & Trailer For New Series About Financial Troubles |url=https://deadline.com/gallery/maxxed-out-premiere-date-trailer-photos-own/ |access-date=2026-05-01 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref> ''Maxxed Out'' received a 2026 Critics Choice nomination for "Best Business Show."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Gold Derby |date=2026-04-30 |title='The Traitors,' 'Dancing With the Stars' lead nominations for Critics Choice Real TV Awards |url=https://www.goldderby.com/tv/2026/2026-critics-choice-real-tv-awards-nominations-full-list/ |access-date=2026-05-01 |website=Gold Derby |language=en-US}}</ref>

==International==
In Canada, the former Canadian version of Discovery Health, owned by [[Shaw Media]], did not become a Canadian version of OWN, instead shifting to a reality-based format known as Twist TV (now the Canadian version of [[FYI (Canadian TV channel)|FYI]]).<ref name="twisttv">[http://www.channelcanada.com/Article5084.html "Discovery Health Rebrands As Twist TV"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100923094101/http://www.channelcanada.com/Article5084.html |date=September 23, 2010 }}.</ref> Instead, [[Corus Entertainment]] agreed to launch a Canadian version of OWN, its existing channel Viva was relaunched as [[Oprah Winfrey Network (Canada)|OWN]] on March 1, 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.newswire.ca/en/releases/archive/September2010/29/c6210.html|title=OWN: The Oprah Winfrey Network Comes to Canada |author=[[Corus Entertainment]] (news release)|publisher=[[CNW Group]]|date=September 29, 2010|access-date=September 29, 2010}}</ref> On September 1, 2024, due to Corus' rights removal to most WBD lifestyle and factual brands, OWN was closed down. On January 1, 2025, Rogers Sports and Media acquired all the rights, including OWN, moving its content to Citytv+. During January and February 2011, selected OWN programming aired on both Viva and the co-owned [[W Network]].<ref>[http://www.newswire.ca/en/releases/archive/November2010/09/c2354.html "Corus Entertainment Announces March 1, 2011 as the Canadian Launch Date for OWN:  Oprah Winfrey Network"]. CNW.  November 9, 2010.</ref> Both Shaw Media and Corus share common ownership interests from the J.R. Shaw family, but were considered separate companies.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.allbusiness.com/marketing-advertising/marketing-advertising/6753145-1.html |title=Shaw Communications' Broadcast Properties Take on New Corporate Identity |author=[[Corus Entertainment]] |date=June 19, 1999 |access-date=October 27, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090213153653/http://www.allbusiness.com/marketing-advertising/marketing-advertising/6753145-1.html |archive-date=February 13, 2009 }}</ref> In 2011, Winfrey revealed to ''[[The New York Times]]'' that she was in final negotiations to launch the channel in [[Brazil]] and [[Argentina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://colunas.epoca.globo.com/brunoastuto/2011/12/06/deu-no-the-new-york-times-oprah-winfrey-quer-trazer-seu-canal-para-o-brasil/|title=''Oprah Winfrey quer trazer seu canal para o Brasil''| language = pt | author=[[Época (Brazilian magazine)|Época]]|date= May 12, 2011|access-date= December 6, 2011|trans-title=Oprah Winfrey wants to bring her channel to Brazil}}</ref>

In April 2013, [[TLC (British and Irish TV channel)|TLC UK]] began to air an OWN [[Block programming|block]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Oprah Winfrey & Discovery Networks Int'l Partner To Launch OWN Programming Block In The UK|url=http://blogs.indiewire.com/shadowandact/oprah-winfrey-discovery-networks-intl-partner-to-launch-own-programming-block-in-the-uk|work=IndieWire|access-date=May 29, 2013|author=Tambay A. Obenson|date=May 20, 2013|archive-date=March 17, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140317165630/http://blogs.indiewire.com/shadowandact/oprah-winfrey-discovery-networks-intl-partner-to-launch-own-programming-block-in-the-uk|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=O'Connell|first=Michael|title=OWN Launching Oprah Winfrey Block on TLC's New U.K. Effort (Exclusive)|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/own-launching-oprah-winfrey-block-432801|work=The Hollywood Reporter|access-date=May 29, 2013|date=April 3, 2013}}</ref> The same programming block began airing [[Discovery Home & Health]] in Australia on August 4, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=OWN: Oprah Winfrey Network and Discovery International to Launch OWN Programming Block in Australia, Exclusively on Discovery Home & Health|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2013/06/17/own-oprah-winfrey-network-and-discovery-networks-international-to-launch-own-programming-block-in-australia-exclusively-on-discovery-home-and-health-190405/20130617own01/|work=The Futon Critic|access-date=June 17, 2013|date=June 17, 2013}}</ref> It was announced on September 20, 2013, that the OWN Programming Block would begin airing in South Africa on [[DStv]] beginning October 17, 2013.<ref>{{cite press release|title=OWN: Oprah Winfrey Network and Discovery International Announce Exclusive OWN Programming Block in South Africa|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2013/09/20/own-oprah-winfrey-network-and-discovery-networks-international-announce-exclusive-own-programming-block-in-south-africa-281304/20130920own01/|work=The Futon Critic|date=September 20, 2013}}</ref> OWN Programming Block also debuted in Poland and Russia in August and September; it also debuted on October 28, 2013, in Balkans/Romania/Bulgaria.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oprah.com/own-uk/Oprah-Winfrey-is-on-TLC-in-the-UK-and-Poland |title=Oprah Winfrey is on TLC in the UK and Poland - @OWNTV |publisher=Oprah.com |access-date=March 17, 2014}}</ref>
