'''Rai Italia''' is the international [[Italian language]] television service of Rai Com, a subsidiary of [[RAI]], [[Italy]]'s public national broadcaster. Rai Italia operates a television network that broadcasts around the world via four localized feeds. Programming features a mix of news, discussion-based programs, drama and documentaries as well as sports coverage.

The broadcast of the signal, sent from the Saxa Rubra television production center in [[Rome]], is broadcast through several satellite, cable, IPTV and OTT platforms, as a paid service in the Americas, Africa and Australia while in Asia it is a FTA channel.

The channel falls under the Offerta Estero (International Offer) unit and produces original programs under the Rai Italy structure. The expansion took place in 2022, when the corporation announced the creation of a section on RaiPlay dedicated to such programming.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rai rilancia l’offerta all'estero tra utilizzo dell’inglese, una finestra su RaiPlay e programmi originali |url=https://www.engage.it/media-industry/rai-rilancia-lofferta-estero-tra-utilizzo-dellinglese-una-finestra-su-raiplay-e-programmi-originali-.aspx |work=engage.it |language=it}}</ref>

==History==
Rai Italia's history can be traced back to the setup of the American subsidiary '''Rai Corporation''' in 1959. The subsidiary distributed radio and television programs in the USA, with special attention to the Italian-American community. Production only started in 1971, starting a two-hour programming block limited to the New York metropolitan area. The block was delivered over cable. Thirteen years later, in 1984, the schedule got
an increase of about three hours, totalling five and a half hours and a schedule containing at least a variety show, a Domenica Sportiva segment and a local newscast. The following year, the weekly schedule increased to seventeen hours: two hours a day Mondays to Fridays, one hour on Saturdays and six hours on Sundays.

From Italy, exclusively from satellite, relays of the main news (either [[TG1]] or [[TG2]]), a Serie A soccer match and cultural and entertainment programs arrived. Then a local newscast produced by Rai Corporation was broadcast. In the early 90s, the RAI satellite network achieved coverage in 29 cities, reaching 68% of the Italian-American community. Shortly afterwards the satellite signal expanded to Latin America. Thanks to the office in [[Montevideo]], Rai distributed tapes of its content to broadcasters, entitites and institutions that were unable to pick up the satellite signal.

In April 1996, the channel upgraded to 24-hour broadcasts as '''Rai International'''. The channel was divided in three feeds: '''Rai International 1''' for America, '''Rai International 2''' for Australia and '''Rai International 3''' for Africa.<ref>SATELLITE AND INTERNATIONAL: 50. (1996). Communications Daily, 1.</ref> That same year, it started broadcasting to [[Dish Network]] as a subscription option.<ref>Trecker, J., & Courant, S. C. (1996, Aug 23). D'AMBROSIO HAS UCONN FOOTBALL COVERED: [7 HARTFORD NORTH FINAL EDITION]. Hartford Courant</ref> In December, it launched on [[Optus Television|Optus Vision]], as part of a raft of ethnic channels added to the provider.<ref>Gurvich, V. (1996, Nov 15). Mid-East and Mediterranean about to beam in on pay TV;: [Late Edition]. The Age</ref>

Its infrastructure was used in October 1997 to carry the FAO-backed Telefood telethon, where, in addition to the carriage of the event (also shown on [[Rai 2|Rai Due]]), it was tasked to downlink to television channels in the sixty participating countries.<ref>[https://www.vita.it/la-fame-in-mondovisione/ La fame in mondovisione]</ref> That same month, it announced the creation of Italica, an online project dedicated to Italian culture.<ref>Pozzer, R. (1997, Oct 06). Home fires: Each day we provide news and information via the Internet from a number of our readers' home countries.: [Final Edition 2]. The Spectator</ref> Still during fall 1997, it started carrying [[Miss Italia]]'s sister contest, Miss Italia nel mondo, after a controversy erupted the previous year involving Danny Mendez, raising awareness about the competition.<ref>Pinkus, K. (1998). Miss (Black) Italy. Black Renaissance, 2(1), 80.</ref>

In April 2001, Rai International signed a carriage agreement with [[Time Warner Cable]]. The channel was initially carried in the NY-NJ head-end but would expand to the US East Coast at a later date. Major hotels and 50 US universities now received its signal.<ref>RAI International signs US deal with Time Warner. (2001). Cable Europe, 6(8), 1.</ref>

The channel applied to the CRTC in 2003 in order to broadcast in Canada. At the time, the channel had a shadow audience of 10,000 viewers who watched its signal illegally using satellite decoders.<ref>24-hour Italian channel in view: Rai makes pitch. 'Not a token whim but a real need': [Final Edition]. The Gazette</ref> The regulator finally approved it on 13 May 2005, after a long period of requests from the country's Italian community, under the condition that it would be provided alongside basic cable channel [[Telelatino]].<ref>Tuck, S. (2005, May 14). Italian TV network gets digital licence. The Globe and Mail</ref>

The channel changed its name to Raitalia on March 30, 2008,<ref name=2008rebrand>[https://www.broadbandtvnews.com/2008/04/22/italys-rai-rebrands-international-channels/ Italy’s RAI rebrands international channels]</ref><ref>[https://www.italiaestera.net/modules.php?name=News&file=article&sid=8650 Nasce Raitalia]</ref> adopting a new logo based on the spherical designs of Italian artist [[Arnaldo Pomodoro]], using the spheres of the UN headquarters and the [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs|Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Italy)]] as references.<ref>[https://www.produ.com/television/noticias/rai-international-es-ahora-raitalia/ RAI International es ahora Raitalia]</ref> In 2009, it was restyled to the current '''Rai Italia''', adopting a logo matching the Rai channels.

From 18 May 2010, following a reduction plan approved unanimously by the Council of Administrators, Rai Italia ceased all of its original productions. From 7 October 2012, however, the channel resumed producing original content for the channel, with a new program, '''Cristiantà''', broadcast on Sunday mornings.

In November 2022, Rai announced an increase in its international television offerings over linear and its Rai Play platform. Additionally, some English-language content (mostly subtitles) was added to the daily schedule, including a news bulletin from Rai News 24.<ref name="OffertaEstero">{{cite web |url=https://www.rai.it/dl/doc/1669027045923_Direzione%20Offerta%20Estero%20DEF%20RID.pdf |title=Un mondo d'Italia. La nuova Rai per l'estero |website=www.international.rai.it |access-date=5 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221121112540/https://www.rai.it/dl/doc/1669027045923_Direzione%20Offerta%20Estero%20DEF%20RID.pdf |archive-date=21 November 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref> There were plans to launch a standalone English service, but these were scrapped. Simultaneously, the channel's distribution to Europe began, with over three million Italian immigrants registered in Europe according to 2022 AIRE data.<ref>[https://www.key4biz.it/rai-rilancia-lofferta-per-lestero-ma-seppellisce-il-canale-in-lingua-inglese/425641/ Rai rilancia l’offerta per l’estero, ma seppellisce il canale in lingua inglese]</ref> Agreements with OTT providers in Spain and the United Kingdom were signed in December 2023.<ref>[https://italia-informa.com/rai-italia-gran-bretagna-spagna_pg3.aspx Rai  Italia sbarca in Gran Bretagna e Spagna]</ref>

In July 2025, former TG1 vice-director Mariarita Grieco was appointed head of Offerta Estero RAI, subsequently some of Rai Italia's original programs were renewed, including its flagship ''Rai Italia''.<ref>[https://lespresso.it/c/televisione/2025/7/2/tv-rai-casa-italia-programma-italiani-estero-roberta-ammendola/55336 Novità per "Casa Italia", il programma di punta del canale Rai che sta particolarmente a cuore a Palazzo Chigi]</ref>

==Audience and programming==
Rai Italia is targeted at Italian [[expatriate]]s, [[Italian diaspora|foreign citizens of Italian descent]], and non-Italians interested in [[Italian language]] and [[Culture of Italy|culture]]; as such the network features a mix of the best programming from Rai as well as original programming created especially for this channel. In 2022, Rai Italia claimed to have an audience of 20 to 22 million viewers.<ref name="OffertaEstero"/> The total potential audience is estimated to surpass 120 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rai.it/ufficiostampa/assets/template/us-articolo.html?ssiPath=/articoli/2024/02/Rai-Italia-porta-il-volley-femminile-in-5-continenti-3e724120-62e9-46bf-a980-fef812d53daa-ssi.html |title=Rai Italia porta il volley femminile in 5 continenti |website=Rai |access-date=28 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240628100347/https://www.rai.it/ufficiostampa/assets/template/us-articolo.html?ssiPath=/articoli/2024/02/Rai-Italia-porta-il-volley-femminile-in-5-continenti-3e724120-62e9-46bf-a980-fef812d53daa-ssi.html |archive-date=28 June 2024 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Rai Italia started international television broadcasting on [[New Year's Day]] 1992 as '''Rai International''', Rai Italia has worked under an agreement with the [[Italian language|Italian]] government to develop the presence of public service in international radio and television broadcasting. Rai Italia also strives to meet the demands for information and services from [[Italian language|Italian]] communities abroad.

Rai Italia broadcasts three television channels, via satellite, which vary according to the different geographical targets. No service is available for [[Europe]] as Rai's domestic channels are widely available free-to-air in this region. Rai Italia has organized the satellite service into 4 zones with each having a different localized schedule:

*'''Rai Italia Europe/Africa''' – Broadcasts to [[Europe]] (United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany, France, Austria, Slovenia, Croatia, Serbia, Bosnia, Macedonia, Spain, Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, Sweden, Norway, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia, Finland, Bulgaria, Denmark, Greece, Malta, Portugal, Romania, Poland, Netherlands) and [[Africa]]
*'''Rai Italia Asia''' – Broadcasts to [[Asia]] (Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Mainland China, Mongolia)
*'''Rai Italia Australia''' – Broadcasts to [[Australia]]

In Europe, Rai Italia has broadcast for a short period (2008-2009) of timesharing with [[Rai Med]] ([[Arabic language]] entertainment, [[Free-to-air|FTA]]), but this broadcast has ended.<ref name=2008rebrand/>

83% of the annual output consists of productions from the three main Rai channels. The remaining 17% consists of original productions, which were boosted following the creation of the Rai Italy unit in 2022.<ref name="OffertaEstero"/>
*'''{{ill|Casa Italia|it}}''': weekday format catering the diaspora, covering Italian topics. Presented by Roberta Ammendola.<ref name="OffertaEstero"/> Created in October 2018, it was named ''L'Italia con voi'' (Italy With You) before the 2022 revision. During December 2019, it carried English subtitles.<ref>[https://moondo.info/rai-italia-litalia-con-voi-ora-con-sottotitoli-in-inglese/ Rai Italia: “L’Italia con voi” ora con sottotitoli in inglese]</ref>
*'''Cristianità''': weekly religious program airing for about two hours on Sundays. The format broadcasts the Holy Mass and the Angelus live from the Vatican. Presented by Myriam Casteli. The channel also broadcasts Papal audiences on Wednesdays (as a collaboration with Rai Vaticano).<ref name="OffertaEstero"/> The program is also one of the channel's oldest original productions still on air; the program also receives calls from the Italian diaspora, particularly in the Americas, as well as their religious events.<ref>Ardizzoni, M. (2016). Borderless Nationalism: Italy’s RAI Transnational Brand. In: Volcic, Z., Andrejevic, M. (eds) Commercial Nationalism. Palgrave Studies in Communication for Social Change. Palgrave Macmillan, London. https://doi.org/10.1057/9781137500991_8</ref>
*'''Il Confronto''': Half-hour weekly program discussing political and economic topics of relevance in Italy with two experts from both sides. Presented by Monica Setta.<ref name="OffertaEstero"/>
*'''Italian Colors''': Created by means of collaboration with TGR, the items come from Rai's regional centers and consists of TGR's tourism-centric segments, often with English subtitles.<ref name="OffertaEstero"/>
*'''Paparazzi''': English-language magazine programme showing Italian culture and trending topics. Presented by [[Filippo Solibello]] and [[Marco Ardemagni]] who were both working on [[Rai Radio 2]] at the time of its creation.<ref name="OffertaEstero"/> Initially a half-hour program, beginning in its second season in 2023, its length increased to 45 minutes.<ref>[https://ambparigi.esteri.it/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/RAI-ITALIA-aggiornato-DEF-ITA-LQ-1.pdf UN MONDO D’ITALIA. NUOVI MERCATI, I NOSTRI ORIGINALS]</ref>
*'''English-language newscast from Rai News 24''': created in line with the 2022 Rai Italia reforms, a five-minute news bulletin in English is shown, presented by an Italian-American journalist.<ref name="OffertaEstero"/>
*'''Italian Food''': strand which was created following the signing of an agreement with the Italian pay television channel Gambero Rosso Channel to provide Rai Italia with 150 hours worth of its original productions, which, in exchange, are shown with English subtitles.<ref name="OffertaEstero"/> In 2024, Gambero Rosso produced the second season of ''Pizzagirls'' to air on this channel first.<ref>[https://www.gamberorosso.it/rubriche/donne-pizzaiole/ Pizzaiole donne, arriva un programma tv: purché se ne parli, per ora ci accontentiamo (nonostante la narrazione a tinte rosa)]</ref>
*'''Che Classe!''': Sitcom set in a classroom with the aim of learning Italian, shown in the summer of 2024, with subtitles in both English and Italian.<ref>[https://www.aise.it/comunit%C3%A0/che-classe-su-rai-italia-la-sitcom-per-imparare-litaliano/205809/2 Che Classe! Su Rai Italia la sit-com per imparare l’italiano]</ref>
*'''La Giostra del Gol''': sports program with highlights of Italian football and other competitions. Originally a program on mainline Rai channels in Italy in 1977, it was revived as a Rai Italia original in 2025 presented by Stefano Orsini, and is produced in association with Rai Sport.<ref>[https://www.gazzetta.it/tv/26-08-2025/rai-italia-riporta-la-serie-a-nel-mondo-con-la-giostra-del-gol.shtml Rai Italia riporta la Serie A nel mondo con La Giostra del Gol]</ref>
Other formats also exist, including formats about the diaspora in general, "Made in Italy" topics, documentaries about the country, etc. The content is also available on the Rai Italy section of [[RaiPlay]].<ref name="OffertaEstero"/>

The '''Ted Turner Campus''', formerly known as the '''Turner Broadcasting Techwood Campus''' and also referred to as the '''Techwood Campus''', is a television production complex located in [[Atlanta]], Georgia, next to the campus of the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]]. The complex houses production and broadcasting facilities for [[TNT (American TV channel)|TNT]], [[TBS (American TV channel)|TBS]], [[CNN]], [[TruTV]], [[Turner Classic Movies]], [[Cartoon Network]] and [[Boomerang (TV channel)|Boomerang]] and was the headquarters for the [[Turner Broadcasting System]].

==History==
===Early history===
The campus first started out as a club house for the Progressive Club, a Jewish social organization established in 1913. The organization would become one of the first Jewish organizations to openly express its heritage.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.atlantatimemachine.com/misc/techwd1.htm|title=1050 Techwood Drive|website=AtlantaTimeMachine|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251030182609/http://www.atlantatimemachine.com/misc/techwd1.htm|archive-date=October 30, 2025|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://archivesspace.thebreman.org/repositories/2/resources/56|title=Jewish Progressive Club Records|website=William Breman Jewish Heritage Museum|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231202210240/https://archivesspace.thebreman.org/repositories/2/resources/56|archive-date=December 2, 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> The property sat idle after the organization left the building until it was bought by [[Ted Turner]] in 1979 for $4.2 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.atlantajewishtimes.com/cnns-back-to-the-future-atlanta-move/|title=CNN's 'Back to the Future' Atlanta Move|website=Atlanta Jewish Times|date=January 25, 2023}}</ref>

===1980s===
On June 1, 1980, the complex became the headquarters for the newly launched 24-hour [[cable news]] network [[CNN]] which would go on the air at 6:00&nbsp;p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|Eastern Time]] with an introduction by [[Turner Broadcasting]] owner [[Ted Turner]].<ref>[https://meandted.com/author.htm Reese Schonfeld Bio.] (January 29, 2001) ''MeAndTed.com''. Retrieved 2007-06-18.  {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080513025424/http://meandted.com/author.htm |date=May 13, 2008 }}</ref><ref>[https://edition.cnn.com/COMMUNITY/transcripts/2000/5/8/bierbauer/ Charles Bierbauer, CNN senior Washington correspondent, discusses his 19-year career at CNN.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120929070034/http://www.cnn.com/COMMUNITY/transcripts/2000/5/8/bierbauer/ |date=2012-09-29 }} (May 8, 2000). ''[[CNN.com]]''. Retrieved 2007-06-18.</ref>

Around this time, the complex also became the home of television tapings for [[Georgia Championship Wrestling]]'s (GCW), [[Jim Crockett Promotions]], and [[World Championship Wrestling]] (WCW) from 1980 to 1989 which included ''[[WCW Power Hour|Power Hour]]'', ''[[WCW Saturday Night|World Championship Wrestling]]'', ''[[WCW Main Event|Main Event]]'', and [[Mid-Atlantic Championship Wrestling]].

On July 14, 1984, [[Vince McMahon]], owner of the [[World Wrestling Federation]] (WWF) took over the ''[[WCW Saturday Night|World Championship Wrestling]]'' program on [[Superstation WTBS]]. Unlike ''World Championship Wrestling'', which had been taping its weekly show at the time from the complex, the WWF instead replaced the format with highlights from its syndicated shows as well as clips and matches from [[Madison Square Garden]], [[Boston Garden]], and other various arenas where the promotion promoted shows in. However, this was a direct violation of a promise that McMahon had made to provide original programming and tape programs at the Techwood studios.<ref>{{cite book|first=Scott|last=Beekman|page=[https://archive.org/details/ringsidehistoryo00beek/page/122 122]|title=Ringside: A History of Professional Wrestling in America|publisher=Greenwood|year=2006|isbn=0-275-98401-X|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/ringsidehistoryo00beek/page/122}}</ref> On March 2, 1985, the WWF began airing matches from the studio and changed the name of the program to ''WWF Georgia Championship Wrestling'' which was co-hosted by ring announcer [[Freddie Miller (broadcaster)|Freddie Miller]] and [[Gorilla Monsoon]]. The program also featured interviews with various wrestlers who would be on the inaugural [[WrestleMania I|WrestleMania]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://thehistoryofwwe.com/wwf-results-1985/ |title=History of WWF in-ring action in 1985|archive-date=2007-10-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071021180216/http://thehistoryofwwe.com/85.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> The WWF would end up selling the timeslot to Jim Crockett Promotions for $1 million a few weeks after the first taping at the complex with the final ''WWF Georgia Championship Wrestling'' episode airing on March 30, 1985.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://thehistoryofwwe.com/wwf-results-1985/ |title=1985 |website=thehistoryofwwe.com |date=January 16, 2023 |access-date=February 14, 2021 |archive-date=October 21, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071021180216/http://thehistoryofwwe.com/85.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> The first episode of JCP's World Championship Wrestling aired on April 6, 1985, with matches that were taped on March 30, 1985, under the branding of ''NWA World Championship Wrestling''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://thehistoryofwwe.com/jcp-results-1985/ |title=JCP 1985 |website=thehistoryofwwe.com |date=January 16, 2023 |access-date=February 14, 2021 |archive-date=November 23, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191123050248/http://www.thehistoryofwwe.com/jcp85.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Tapings continued to be held at the WTBS studios until March 16, 1989, when WCW relocated their tapings to [[Center Stage Theater]] on March 29, 1989.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=1&nr=16878|title=NWA World Championship Wrestling
|date=April 1, 1989|website=Cagematch}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cagematch.net/?id=1&nr=16877|title=NWA World Championship Wrestling
|date=April 1, 1989|website=Cagematch}}</ref>

In 1987, CNN relocated from the campus to the [[CNN Center]] following a two-year renovation after Ted Turner had purchased the building in 1985.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ajc.com/business/2026/04/cnn-centers-rebirth-as-the-center-comes-into-focus-take-a-look/|title=CNN Center's rebirth as 'The Center' comes into focus. Take a look.|first=Zachary|last=Hansen|date=April 1, 2026}}</ref>

The complex was also where ''[[Inside the NBA]]'' on [[TNT (American TV channel)|TNT]] would be broadcast from 1989 to 2025.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5531128/2024/07/19/inside-the-nba-tv-show-tnt-praises/ |url-access=registration |title=My front row seat on 'Inside the NBA,' the greatest studio show in sports TV history|date=July 19, 2024|first=David|last=Aldridge via. The Athletic}}</ref> The program is still broadcast from the complex under a sublicensing agreement with [[ESPN]].<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://press.wbd.com/us/media-release/warner-bros-discovery-and-national-basketball-association-reach-agreement-expand-long|title=Warner Bros. Discovery and the National Basketball Association Reach Agreement to Expand Long-Standing Partnership|website=Warner Bros. Discovery|date=November 18, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|url=https://espnpressroom.com/us/press-releases/2024/11/espn-and-tnt-sports-reach-agreement-for-iconic-inside-the-nba-to-be-exclusively-distributed-on-espn-and-abc-platforms-beginning-with-2025-26-nba-regular-season/|title=
ESPN and TNT Sports Reach Agreement for Iconic Inside the NBA to be Exclusively Distributed on ESPN and ABC Platforms Beginning with 2025-26 NBA Regular Season|website=ESPN Press Room|date=November 18, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Marchand, Andrew |author2=West, Jenna |title='Inside the NBA' to continue on ABC and ESPN as part of TNT-NBA settlement: Sources |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5926632/2024/11/16/inside-the-nba-abc-espn-tnt-lawsuit/ |website=The Athletic  |date=November 16, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Jenkins |first1=Keith |title=How to watch "Inside the NBA" on ESPN: 2025-26 schedule |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46596680/2025-2026-nba-season-schedule-how-watch-dates |website=ESPN |date=October 20, 2025}}</ref>

===2010s===
On December 2, 2019, the Techwood campus was renamed to the Ted Turner Campus and was dedicated to Ted Turner.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fox5atlanta.com/news/warnermedia-renames-techwood-campus-in-atlanta-ted-turner-campus|title=WarnerMedia renames Techwood Campus in Atlanta 'Ted Turner Campus'|date=December 6, 2019|website=WAGA-TV Fox 5 Atlanta}}</ref> Several WarnerMedia executives along with Ted Turner, CNN anchor [[Wolf Blitzer]], CNN president [[Jeff Zucker]], former [[Turner Broadcasting]] CEO [[Phil Kent]], [[Headline News]] host [[Lynne Russell]], CNN correspondent Chuck de Caro, and former ''People Now'' host [[Bill Tush]] were on hand for the dedication ceremony.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/radiotvtalk/warnermedia-names-techwood-campus-after-ted-turner-adds-mural/NnzewhCrTpJws09njRORKL/|title=WarnerMedia names Techwood campus after Ted Turner, adds mural|date=December 6, 2019|first=Rodney|last=Ho|publisher=Atlanta Journal}}</ref> In addition to the renaming, a mural featuring Ted Turner was also presented.

===2020s===
On June 29, 2020, WarnerMedia (later Warner Bros. Discovery) announced their plans to sell the CNN Center and continue to lease space in the building until expansion of the Techwood campus to accommodate CNN's operations were complete.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wsbtv.com/news/local/atlanta/warnermedia-selling-cnn-center-downtown-atlanta-memo-says/VL5UQFMBIFETXJVZRTIGRJYHOE/|title=WarnerMedia selling CNN Center in downtown Atlanta|date=29 June 2020|publisher=[[WSB-TV]]|access-date=6 July 2020}}</ref> On October 30, 2023, CNN gradually began move operations to the Ted Turner Campus including control room facilities and various shows.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ajc.com/life/radiotvtalk-blog/production-officially-ended-at-cnn-center-friday-moving-to-midtown/2XVSYIULP5FT5LJVHI3U7N3EE4/|title=Production officially ended at CNN Center in Atlanta Friday, moving to Midtown | date=29 October 2023|publisher=[[Atlanta Journal Constitution]]|access-date=29 October 2023}}</ref> Several weekend shows continued to be based at the CNN Center until February 25, 2024, when the remainder of CNN's operations were relocated to the Ted Turner Campus.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-02-26 |title=CNN's ATL-Based Programming Ends Use of CNN Center Studios |url=https://www.adweek.com/tvnewser/cnns-atl-based-programming-ends-use-of-cnn-center-studios/ |access-date=2024-03-04 |website=TVNewser |language=en-US}}</ref>

On June 27, 2024, the Ted Turner Campus hosted [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]]'s first [[Joe Biden–Donald Trump presidential debate|United States presidential debate]]. The debate featured no audience and was the first debate of the [[2024 United States presidential election]] between former [[President of the United States]], [[Donald Trump]] and sitting-at-the-time [[President of the United States]] [[Joe Biden]] and was moderated by CNN anchors [[Jake Tapper]] and [[Dana Bash]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.ajc.com/things-to-do/georgia-entertainment-scene/all-eyes-on-atlanta-cnn-preps-for-presidential-debate/KXR275T6Q5BY5A3HGYKWEOHDDQ/ |title=All eyes on Atlanta: CNN preps for presidential debate |last=Ho |first=Rodney |date=June 27, 2024 |access-date=June 27, 2024 |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] | url-access=limited |archive-date=June 26, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240626173657/https://www.ajc.com/things-to-do/georgia-entertainment-scene/all-eyes-on-atlanta-cnn-preps-for-presidential-debate/KXR275T6Q5BY5A3HGYKWEOHDDQ/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 15, 2024 |title=ABC to make September debate available for simulcast on other networks |url=https://thehill.com/blogs/pundits-blog/media/4666028-abc-september-debate-2024-trump-biden/ |access-date=June 20, 2024 |website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]] | last1=Mastrangelo |first1=Dominick |language=en |archive-date=May 20, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240520030218/https://thehill.com/blogs/pundits-blog/media/4666028-abc-september-debate-2024-trump-biden/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.theverge.com/2024/6/27/24186831/presidential-debate-watch-start-time-biden-trump |title=How to watch Biden vs. Trump in the first 2024 presidential debate |date=June 27, 2024 |last=Davis |first=Wes |work=[[The Verge]] | access-date=June 27, 2024 |archive-date=June 27, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240627135206/https://www.theverge.com/2024/6/27/24186831/presidential-debate-watch-start-time-biden-trump |url-status=live}}</ref>

'''The CW Network, LLC''',<ref>{{cite web |title=The CW Network and Sinclair Expand and Extend Affiliation Partnership |url=https://sbgi.net/the-cw-network-and-sinclair-expand-and-extend-affiliation-partnership/ |website=Sinclair, Inc |language=en |date=31 August 2023 |quote=The CW Network, LLC is one of America’s major broadcast networks and reaches 100% of US television households.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=THE CW NETWORK TO BECOME THE EXCLUSIVE BROADCAST HOME TO WWE NXT |url=https://corporate.wwe.com/news/company-news/2023/11-07-2023 |website=corporate.wwe.com |language=en |quote=The CW Network, LLC is one of America’s major broadcast networks and reaches 100% of US television households.}}</ref> commonly referred to as '''the CW<!--lowercase "the CW" is correct per [[MOS:THEINST]]-->''', is an American commercial [[terrestrial television|broadcast television]] [[television network|network]] that is controlled by [[Nexstar Media Group]], which holds an 81.1% ownership interest.<ref name=nexstarthecw>{{cite news |last=Hanlon |first=Tim |title=The CW's Strange Next Act Is Starting To Make Sense |url=https://www.tvrev.com/news/the-cws-strange-next-act-is-starting-to-make-sense |work=TVREV |date=September 24, 2026 |access-date=September 25, 2026 |quote=Its original 2022 stake was 75%, but that had already grown to 79.7% by last fall, reached 80.8% at year-end and stood at 81.1% as of June 30.}}</ref><ref name="nexstarcwstake">{{cite web |title=Commission File Number: 000-50478 |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1142417/000119312526339827/nxst-20260630.htm |access-date=25 September 2026 |quote=As of June 30, 2026, Nexstar also owns an 81.1% ownership interest in The CW Network, LLC, the fifth major broadcast network in the U.S. |publisher=United States Securities and Exchange Commission}}</ref> The network's name is derived from the first letters of the names of its two founding co-owners, [[CBS Corporation]] and [[Warner Bros. Entertainment]], which were acquired by [[Paramount Global]] and [[Warner Bros. Discovery]] respectively.<!--Please see RfC (permalink [[Talk:The CW/Archive 3#Request for comment on content dispute]]), which was closed with a determination that the "C" in "CW" stands for the "CBS Corporation" rather than "CBS", before making changes--> Nexstar acquired a 75% controlling stake in the network on October 3, 2022, with Paramount Global and Warner Bros. 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015045938/https://deadline.com/2022/10/mark-pedowitz-exits-cw-chairman-ceo-nexstar-1235130707/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref
