The CW debuted on September 18, 2006, as the successor to [[UPN]] and [[the WB]], which had both shut down that month. Its first two nights of programming—on September 18, 2006, and September 19, 2006—consisted of reruns and launch-related [[television special|specials]]. The CW marked its formal launch date on September 20, 2006, with the two-hour premiere of the [[America's Next Top Model season 7|seventh cycle]] of ''[[America's Next Top Model]]''. The network's programming lineup is intended to appeal mainly to viewers between the ages of 18 and 34, although from 2008 to 2011 the network shifted its programming to appeal to women in that demographic.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last1=Paul J. Gough |last2=James Hibberd |date=May 13, 2008 |title="90210" Upfront and Center for CW |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |publisher=[[Nielsen N.V.|Nielsen Company]] |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/90210-upfront-center-cw-111620 |access-date=April 17, 2020 |archive-date=July 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190717040222/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/90210-upfront-center-cw-111620 |url-status=live }}</ref> As of August 2017, the network's audience was evenly split between men and women.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Holloway |first=Daniel |date=August 2, 2017 |title=CW Chief Looks to Lure Women Viewers Back With 'Dynasty,' 'Riverdale' |language=en-US |work=Variety |url=https://variety.com/2017/tv/news/dynasty-riverdale-tca-1202513508/ |access-date=October 19, 2017 |archive-date=June 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190621101835/https://variety.com/2017/tv/news/dynasty-riverdale-tca-1202513508/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

The CW runs programming seven days a week: airing nightly in prime time along with a Saturday morning live-action [[Educational entertainment|educational programming]] block produced by [[Hearst Media Production Group]] called ''[[One Magnificent Morning]]''.

The CW is also available in Canada on [[pay television]] providers through stations [[owned-and-operated station|owned-and-operated]] by Nexstar and on [[network affiliate|affiliates]] owned by others that are located within proximity to the [[Canada–United States border]] (whose broadcasts of CW shows are subject to [[simultaneous substitution]] laws imposed by the [[Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission]], if a Canadian network holds the broadcast rights); it is also available through two Nexstar-controlled stations that are classified in the U.S. as [[superstation]]s—New York City–based ''[[de facto]]'' [[Flagship (broadcasting)|flagship]]{{efn|Nexstar operates this station on behalf of [[Mission Broadcasting]]}} [[WPIX]] and Los Angeles–based ''[[de jure]]'' flagship{{efn|This station is directly owned-and-operated by Nexstar}} [[KTLA]].

Additionally, the network is available in [[northern Mexico]] through affiliates located near the [[Mexico–United States border|Mexico–U.S. border]] (such as [[KUSI-TV]]—[[San Diego]]/[[Tijuana]], [[KECY-TV|KECY-DT3]] in [[El Centro, California]], [[KVIA-TV|KVIA-DT2]] in [[El Paso, Texas|El Paso]], and [[KGBT-TV]] in [[McAllen, Texas|(McAllen]]/[[Brownsville, Texas]]) on pay television providers. In both Canada and Mexico, some [[free-to-air]] CW affiliate signals originating from the U.S. are receivable over-the-air in border areas depending on the station's [[broadcast range|signal coverage]].

== History ==
=== 1993–2006: Predecessors and formation ===
{{Main|The WB|UPN}}

In April 1993, the [[Federal Communications Commission]] (FCC) ended the [[fin-syn]] rules that prohibited television networks from owning the rerun rights to programs they broadcast. Fearing that the networks would stop buying programs from independent studios, [[Warner Bros. Television]] and [[Paramount Television]] each decided to start their own networks.<ref name="lowry19991226">{{Cite news |last=Lowry |first=Brian |date=1999-12-26 |title=The Whims of War |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1999-dec-26-ca-47501-story.html |access-date=May 25, 2012 |work=Los Angeles Times}}</ref>

[[The WB]] and [[UPN]] both launched within one week of each other in January 1995, just as the [[Fox Broadcasting Company]] had started to secure a foothold with American television audiences.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=10-K |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1142417/000095017025028949/nxst-20241231.htm|access-date=2026-01-14 |website=www.sec.gov}}</ref> The two networks launched to limited fanfare and generally mediocre to poor results.{{r|lowry19991226}}<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clarendon |first=Dan |date=2020-01-04 |title=The WB Launched 25 Years Ago, and Millennials Will Never Forget |url=https://www.tvinsider.com/844403/the-wb-network-legacy-25th-anniversary/ |access-date=2024-05-04 |website=TV Insider |language=en-US}}</ref> However, over the subsequent {{frac|11|1|2}} seasons, both were able to air several series that became quite popular, such as ''[[Buffy the Vampire Slayer]]'', ''[[Angel (1999 TV series)|Angel]]'', ''[[Star Trek: Voyager]]'', ''[[The Sentinel (TV series)|The Sentinel]],'' ''[[7th Heaven (TV series)|7th Heaven]]'', ''[[Dawson's Creek]]'', ''[[Charmed]]'', ''[[Smallville]]'', ''[[Everwood]]'', ''[[Gilmore Girls]]'', ''[[Reba (TV series)|Reba]]'', ''[[The Steve Harvey Show]]'', and ''[[America's Next Top Model]]''.

Although their simultaneous starts and competition for affiliate stations initially caused the two networks to appear as rivals, by 1999, they had adopted differing strategies: The WB targeted young women, while UPN targeted young men.{{r|lowry19991226}} Towards the end of their first decade on the air, the WB and UPN were in decline, unable to reach the audience share or have the effect that Fox had gained within its first decade, much less than that of the [[Big Three television networks|Big Three]] networks ([[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], [[CBS]], and [[NBC]]). In the eleven years that UPN and the WB were in operation, the two networks lost a combined $2 billion.<ref name="wsj2008">{{Cite news |last=Rebecca Dana |date=May 16, 2008 |title=It's No Gossip, Ratings Slip Threatens CW Network |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |publisher=[[Dow Jones and Company]] |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB121089546043097065 |access-date=August 9, 2017 |archive-date=December 30, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230071618/https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB121089546043097065 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Chris-Craft Industries]], [[Viacom (1952–2005)|Viacom]], and Time Warner officials had discussed a possible merger of UPN and the WB as early as September 1995, only eight months after their respective launches; however, discussions ultimately broke down over issues on how to combine Chris-Craft and [[Tribune Broadcasting]]'s station interests in the proposal to merge the networks, since the two companies' station portfolios overlapped with one another in several major markets.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Thomas Tyrer |date=September 18, 1995 |title=Fledgling Networks UPN, WB Already Pondering Merger |work=[[AdAge]] |publisher=[[Crain Communications]] |url=http://adage.com/article/news/fledgling-networks-upn-wb-pondering-merger/85731/ |access-date=February 7, 2015 |archive-date=February 9, 2015 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150209153236/http://adage.com/article/news/fledgling-networks-upn-wb-pondering-merger/85731/ |url-status=live }}</ref> By 2003, however, Time Warner became mired in several debt problems. The company had already been responsible for shutting down Warner Bros.' [[Warner Bros. Animation#1990–2004: Warner Bros. Feature Animation|in-house animation department]] and for selling off major portions of the conglomerate, such as the 2004 sale of [[Warner Bros. Records]] and the rest of [[Warner Music Group]] to an investor group led by [[Edgar Bronfman Jr.]] and [[Thomas H. Lee Partners]].

[[File:The CW prelaunch logo.svg|225px|thumb|right|The network's original pre-launch logo]]
Executives from CBS and Warner Bros. announced on January 24, 2006 that they would respectively shut down UPN and the WB; they would combine resources to form a new broadcast network, to be called the CW.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2016/tv/news/cw-wb-network-upn-merger-announcement-10-years-ago-1201687040/|title=Birth of the CW: UPN-WB Network Merger Deal Rocked TV Biz 10 Years Ago|last=Littleton|first=Cynthia|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190809180649/https://variety.com/2016/tv/news/cw-wb-network-upn-merger-announcement-10-years-ago-1201687040/|archive-date=August 9, 2019|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=January 24, 2016|access-date=July 27, 2016}}</ref> They confirmed that the network would—at the outset—feature programming from both of its predecessors-to-be as well as new content developed specifically for the new network.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jessica Seid |date=January 24, 2006 |title='Gilmore Girls' meet 'Smackdown'; CW Network to combine WB, UPN in CBS-Warner venture beginning in September |work=[[CNNMoney.com]] |publisher=[[Time Warner]] |url=https://money.cnn.com/2006/01/24/news/companies/cbs_warner/ |access-date=August 3, 2020 |archive-date=March 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316043531/https://money.cnn.com/2006/01/24/news/companies/cbs_warner/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Carter |first=Bill |date=January 24, 2006 |title=UPN and WB to Combine, Forming New TV Network |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/01/24/business/media/24cnd-network.html?bl |access-date=February 18, 2017 |archive-date=October 17, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151017035638/http://www.nytimes.com/2006/01/24/business/media/24cnd-network.html?bl |url-status=live }}</ref> Warner Bros. and CBS expected to produce inexpensive shows for the network, which they could sell outside the U.S.<ref name="goldberg20220513">{{Cite magazine |last=Goldberg |first=Lesley |date=May 13, 2022 |title=Mad About The CW Cancellations? Blame Streaming, But Also Its Unusual Corporate Structure |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/the-cw-cancellations-blame-streaming-but-also-its-unusual-corporate-structure-1235146038/ |magazine=The Hollywood Reporter |language=en-US |access-date=May 13, 2022 |archive-date=June 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220610022440/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/the-cw-cancellations-blame-streaming-but-also-its-unusual-corporate-structure-1235146038/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Then CBS chairman [[Les Moonves]] explained that the name of the new network was formed from the first letters of CBS and Warner Bros., joking, "We couldn't call it the [[Flush toilet|WC]] for obvious reasons."<ref>{{Cite web |last1=James |first1=Meg |last2=Gold |first2=Matea |date=2006-01-25 |title=CBS, Warner to Shut Down 2 Networks and Form Hybrid |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2006-jan-25-fi-cw25-story.html |access-date=2024-05-15 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-01-25 |title=UPN, The WB join as spinoff |url=https://www.dailynews.com/general-news/20060125/upn-the-wb-join-as-spinoff/ |access-date=2024-05-15 |website=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Although some executives reportedly disliked the new name, Moonves stated in March 2006 that there was "zero chance" the name would change, citing research claiming 48% of the target demographic were already aware of the "CW" name.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ben Grossman |date=March 15, 2006 |title=CW Staying CW, Says Moonves |url=http://www.broadcastingcable.com/news/news-articles/cw-staying-cw-says-moonves/79264 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070915031033/http://www.broadcastingcable.com/article/CA6316450.html |archive-date=September 15, 2007 |publisher=[[Reed Business Information]] |periodical=[[Broadcasting & Cable]] }}</ref>

In May 2006, the CW announced that it would pick up a combined thirteen programs from its two predecessors to air as part of the network's inaugural fall schedule: seven series held over from the WB (''[[7th Heaven (TV series)|7th Heaven]]'', ''[[Beauty and the Geek (American TV series)|Beauty and the Geek]]'', ''[[Gilmore Girls]]'', ''[[One Tree Hill (TV series)|One Tree Hill]]'', ''[[Reba (TV series)|Reba]]'', ''[[Smallville]]'' and ''[[Supernatural (American TV series)|Supernatural]]'') and six held over from UPN (''[[America's Next Top Model]]'', ''[[Veronica Mars]]'', ''[[Everybody Hates Chris]]'', ''[[Girlfriends (American TV series)|Girlfriends]]'', ''[[All of Us]]'' and ''[[WWE SmackDown|WWE SmackDown!]]''). Upon the network's launch, the CW chose to use the scheduling model utilized by the WB due in part to the fact that it had a more extensive base programming schedule than UPN, allowing for a larger total of weekly programming time for the new network to fill. (The WB carried 30 hours of programming each week because it had a children's program block and a daytime lineup that UPN did not offer; UPN was primarily a prime time-only network with 10 weekly hours of network programming at the time of the network's shutdown.)<ref>{{Cite news |last=Crupi |first=Anthony |date=January 24, 2006 |title=UPN, WB to Merge Into CW Network |work=Ad Week |url=http://www.adweek.com/news/advertising/upn-wb-merge-cw-network-83687 |access-date=November 12, 2015 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304064454/http://www.adweek.com/news/advertising/upn-wb-merge-cw-network-83687 |url-status=live }}</ref> Also, according to at least one news report, prior to launch, the network's "formal" name was set to be "The CW Television Network".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Learmonth |first1=Michael |title=Secret’s out as rivals elope |url=https://variety.com/2006/scene/markets-festivals/secret-s-out-as-rivals-elope-1117936727/ |work=Variety |date=24 January 2006}}</ref> It is believed that, by the time of the network's launch in 2006, the decision had been made, in the style of merging its predecessor networks to form the CW, to also merge the brandings of its predecessor networks as well (using the "The" from The WB & "Network" from UPN alongside utilizing "CW" in reference to CBS Corporation & Warner Bros.) for the CW's legal entity, while retaining '''The CW Television Network''' as the network's formal branding (while just "CW" would eventually come to be its public-facing branding).

=== 2006–2011: Launch and early struggles ===
[[File:The CW (2006–2024).svg|225px|thumb|right|Logo used from September 18, 2006 to January 13, 2024]]
Like UPN and the WB, the CW targets its programming towards younger audiences. CBS and Time Warner hoped that combining their networks' schedules and affiliate lineups would strengthen the CW into a fifth "major" broadcast network;<ref>{{cite web |title=Nexstar Media Group, Inc. Investor Presentation January 2023 |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250603143910/https://www.nexstar.tv/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Nexstar-2023-Investor-Deck-1.31.23-Final.pdf |quote=Owns The CW, America’s 5th major broadcast network}}</ref> however, research years later would indicate that, despite the combined efforts of the two companies in the creation of the CW resulting in the establishment of a persistent fifth network, the attempt at forming a fifth "major" network would end up falling short on account of significantly lower ratings and smaller viewership than the four majors, especially since, rather than appealing to a broad, mass-market demographic, the network focused primarily on younger demographics (adults 18–34 and teens), which limited its overall household reach compared to the majors. One week before the network's official launch, on September 11, 2006, a new, full version of the network website was launched, the website began to feature more in-depth information about the CW's shows.

The CW launched with a premiere special/launch party from the [[CBS Paramount Television|CBS Paramount]]-produced ''[[Entertainment Tonight]]'' at [[Warner Bros. Studios Burbank|Warner Bros. Studios]] in [[Burbank, California]] on September 18, 2006, after a repeat of the tenth-season finale of ''7th Heaven'';<ref name="zap2it-1559260">{{Cite news |date=August 18, 2006 |title=CW Staggers Its Debut—New net will roll out schedule over two weeks |work=[[Zap2It]] |publisher=[[Tribune Media Services]] |url=http://www.zap2it.com/tv/news/zap-cwpremieredates,0,1559260.story |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060818103850/http://www.zap2it.com/tv/news/zap-cwpremieredates,0,1559260.story |archive-date=August 18, 2006 }}</ref> the same schedule was repeated on September 19, 2006, with the sixth-season finale of ''Gilmore Girls''.<ref name="[[TV Guide]]">''[[TV Guide]]'', September 11, 2006, p. 8</ref> The network continued to air season finales from the previous season through the remainder of the first week, except for ''America's Next Top Model'' and ''WWE SmackDown!'', which respectively began their new seasons on September 20, 2006, and September 22, 2006, with two-hour premieres. When ''Top Model'' made its network premiere on September 20, 2006, the CW scored a 3.4 rating/5 share (with hourly ratings of 3.1/5 and 3.6/6, the CW placed fifth overall) in the [[Nielsen ratings|Nielsen household ratings]]. It scored a 2.6 rating among adults 18–49, finishing fourth in that age demographic and beating the 2.2 rating earned by Fox on that night. The network's second week consisted of season and series premieres for all of its other series from September 25, 2006, to October 1, 2006, with the exception of ''Veronica Mars'', which debuted its third season on October 3, 2006.<ref>{{Cite press release |title=THE CW NETWORK ANNOUNCES ITS INAUGURAL 2006-2007 PREMIERE SCHEDULE |date=July 17, 2006 |publisher=The CW |url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2006/07/17/the-cw-network-announces-its-inaugural-2006-2007-premiere-schedule-21795/20060717cw01/ |access-date=September 2, 2015 |via=The Futon Critic}}</ref>

Despite having several of the most popular programs carried over from UPN and the WB as part of its schedule, the CW—even though it experienced some success with newer programs that launched in subsequent seasons which became modest hits—largely struggled to gain an audience foothold throughout its first five years on the air.<ref>{{Cite web |last=James |first=Meg |date=September 20, 2006 |title=CW Network Faces Struggle to Find a Winning Strategy |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2006-sep-20-fi-cw20-story.html |access-date=October 17, 2023 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> Because of declining viewership for the network during the 2007–08 season and effects from the [[2007–08 Writers Guild of America strike|Writers Guild of America strike]], the network announced on March 4, 2008, that it would eliminate its comedy department (dismissing executive vice president of comedy Kim Fleary and senior vice president of comedy Steve Veisel), while also combining its drama and current programming departments into a single scripted programming unit. The corporate restructuring resulted in the layoffs of approximately 25 to 30 employees.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Michael Schneider |date=March 3, 2008 |title=Strike, ratings slip lead to CW layoffs |url=https://variety.com/2008/scene/markets-festivals/strike-ratings-slip-lead-to-cw-layoffs-1117981768/ |access-date=August 28, 2015 |publisher=[[Reed Business Information]] |periodical=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |archive-date=October 5, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151005011538/http://variety.com/2008/scene/markets-festivals/strike-ratings-slip-lead-to-cw-layoffs-1117981768/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=James Hibberd |date=March 4, 2008 |title=CW downsizes, sheds comedy division |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/cw-downsizes-sheds-comedy-division-106143 |access-date=August 28, 2015 |publisher=Nielsen Company |agency=[[Associated Press]] |periodical=The Hollywood Reporter |archive-date=September 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924175538/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/cw-downsizes-sheds-comedy-division-106143 |url-status=live }}</ref> It also included the elimination of certain positions, other newly opened positions being left unfilled, and layoffs from the [[Kids' WB]] unit, as the block was set to be replaced by [[Toonzai|the CW4Kids]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ishibashi |first=Michael |date=2020-09-28 |title=Beyond Toonami: TV's Forgotten Anime Blocks |url=https://www.cbr.com/toonami-tv-forgotten-anime-blocks/ |access-date=2024-05-15 |website=CBR |language=en}}</ref>

On May 9, 2008, the CW announced that it would lease its Sunday lineup (then running from 5 p.m. to 10 p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|Eastern]] and [[Pacific Time Zone|Pacific Time]])<ref>{{Cite news |date=May 9, 2008 |title=The CW "Outsources" Its Sunday-Night Block; Two Dramas, Two Comedies Coming |work=[[TV Guide]] |publisher=[[Macrovision]] |url=https://www.tvguide.com/news/the-cw-outsources-12191/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080511221532/http://community.tvguide.com/blog-entry/TVGuide-News-Blog/Todays-News/Cw-Puts-Sunday/800039275 |archive-date=May 11, 2008 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Michael Schneider |date=May 9, 2008 |title=CW outsources Sunday to MRC |url=https://variety.com/2008/tv/features/cw-outsources-sunday-to-mrc-1117985413/ |access-date=September 2, 2015 |publisher=Reed Business Information |periodical=Variety |archive-date=January 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114142109/http://variety.com/2008/tv/features/cw-outsources-sunday-to-mrc-1117985413/ |url-status=live }}</ref> to production company [[MRC (company)|Media Rights Capital]] (MRC). As Sundays have historically been a low-rated night for the network during its first two seasons on the air (due to stiff competition from CBS, ABC, and Fox's strong Sunday lineups, and complicated further by NBC's acquisition of ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday Night Football]]'' in September 2006, shortly before the CW debuted), the move allowed the CW to concentrate on its Monday through Friday prime time schedule, while giving MRC the right to develop and schedule programs of its own choosing and reap advertising revenue generated by the lineup. The Sunday series that were scheduled—two reality series (''[[4Real]]'' and ''[[In Harm's Way (TV series)|In Harm's Way]]'') and two scripted series (romantic dramedy ''[[Valentine (TV series)|Valentine]]'' and drama ''[[Easy Money (TV series)|Easy Money]]'')—performed poorly in the ratings (averaging only 1.04 million viewers),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Michael Schneider |date=November 20, 2008 |title=CW ends time-buy deal with MRC |url=https://variety.com/2008/scene/markets-festivals/cw-ends-time-buy-deal-with-mrc-1117996223/ |publisher=Reed Business Information |periodical=Variety |access-date=December 10, 2017 |archive-date=January 28, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190128083503/https://variety.com/2008/scene/markets-festivals/cw-ends-time-buy-deal-with-mrc-1117996223/ |url-status=live }}</ref> prompting the CW to scrap its agreement with MRC and program Sunday nights on its own starting on November 30, 2008. With no first-run programming available to run on Sundays as a backup, the network added reruns of ''[[The Drew Carey Show]]'' and ''[[Jericho (2006 TV series)|Jericho]]'', and movies to replace the MRC-produced programs.<ref>{{Cite news |date=November 20, 2008 |title=CW Takes Back Its Sunday Nights, Sets 'Jericho' Reruns |work=TVWeek |publisher=Dexter Canfield Media |url=http://www.tvweek.com/in-depth/2008/11/cw-takes-back-its-sunday-night/ |access-date=September 2, 2015 |archive-date=January 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114142109/http://www.tvweek.com/in-depth/2008/11/cw-takes-back-its-sunday-night/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

One of the shows carried over to the network from UPN, ''[[WWE SmackDown]]'', ended its run on the CW after the September 26, 2008 episode due to negotiations ending between the [[WWE]] and the CW on renewing the program. Representatives for the CW later confirmed that it had chosen not to continue carrying ''SmackDown'' because the network had redefined its target audience as exclusively females 18 to 34 years old,<ref name="wsj2008" /> whereas ''SmackDown'' targeted a predominantly male audience. Following ''SmackDown''{{'}}s move to [[MyNetworkTV]] that same season, the [[Fox Entertainment Group|Fox]]-owned network (which launched the same month as the CW's debut, albeit two weeks earlier, on September 5, 2006) started beating the CW in the Friday ratings every week from that program's debut on the network, though the CW continued to beat MyNetworkTV overall.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 25, 2009 |title=Fox Still Likely to Pass CBS in Adults 25–54 to Top All Key Age Demos |url=http://tvbythenumbers.com/2009/03/25/fox-still-likely-to-pass-cbs-in-adults-25-54-to-top-all-key-age-demos/15178#more-15178 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090327075403/http://tvbythenumbers.com/2009/03/25/fox-still-likely-to-pass-cbs-in-adults-25-54-to-top-all-key-age-demos/15178#more-15178 |archive-date=March 27, 2009 |access-date=March 27, 2009 |website=[[TV by the Numbers]]}}</ref>

The CW generally struggled in the Nielsen ratings from its inception, primarily placing fifth in all statistics tabulated by [[Nielsen Holdings|Nielsen]] (total audience viewership and demographic ratings). On several occasions, the CW was even outrated by the Spanish-language network [[Univision]]. This led to speculation within the industry (including a May 16, 2008 article in ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'')<ref name="wsj2008" /> that CBS, Time Warner or both companies might abandon the venture if ratings did not improve. However, the CW's fortunes were buoyed in the 2008–09 and 2009–10 television seasons thanks to increased ratings among females in the 18–34 demographic and the buzz that some of its newer series (such as ''[[Gossip Girl]]'', ''[[90210 (TV series)|90210]]'' and ''[[The Vampire Diaries]]'') had generated with audiences. Executives with CBS Corporation and Time Warner also emphasized their commitment to the network.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Josef Adalian |date=August 21, 2008 |title=CW Parents Emphasize Support of Network |url=http://adage.com/article/media/cw-parents-emphasize-support-network/130465/ |publisher=Crain Communications |periodical=AdAge |access-date=September 2, 2015 |archive-date=October 15, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015101401/http://adage.com/article/media/cw-parents-emphasize-support-network/130465/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On May 5, 2009, the CW announced that it would give the five hours of network time on Sundays back to its affiliated stations that fall, effectively becoming a weeknight-only network in prime time, in addition to the CW Daytime and the CW4Kids blocks (the latter block, airing on Saturday mornings, would remain the only weekend programming supplied by the network).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Michael Malone |date=May 5, 2009 |title=Tribune Psyched to Take back Sundays on The CW |work=Broadcasting & Cable |publisher=Reed Business Information |url=http://www.broadcastingcable.com/news/programming/tribune-psyched-take-back-sundays-cws/34685?rssid=20105 |access-date=May 6, 2009 |archive-date=September 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924125508/http://www.broadcastingcable.com/news/programming/tribune-psyched-take-back-sundays-cws/34685?rssid=20105 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Andreeva | first=Nellie |date=May 6, 2009 |title=CW Drops Sundays In Another Blow to Broadcast Model |work=[[Reuters]] |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/entertainmentNews/idUSTRE54514E20090506 |access-date=May 6, 2009 |archive-date=May 8, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090508012535/http://www.reuters.com/article/entertainmentNews/idUSTRE54514E20090506 |url-status=live }}</ref> This change meant the Sunday late afternoon repeat block that the CW inherited from the WB (formerly branded by that network as "EasyView") was discontinued. Subsequently, in mid-May, 65% of the CW's affiliates, including those carrying the CW Plus, signed agreements to air the replacement ''[[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer|MGM]] Showcase'' movie package on Sundays.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andreeva |  first= Nellie  |  date=May 13, 2009 |title=CW Affiliates Booking MGM Movie Pack |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/cw-affiliates-booking-mgm-movie-83903 |publisher=[[Guggenheim Partners|Prometheus Global Media]] |agency=Associated Press |periodical=The Hollywood Reporter |access-date=April 17, 2020 |archive-date=July 31, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200731093141/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/cw-affiliates-booking-mgm-movie-83903 |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== 2011–2016: New leadership and content shift ===
On April 28, 2011, [[Mark Pedowitz]] was appointed by the network to succeed original president of entertainment [[Dawn Ostroff]]; Pedowitz was made the network's first president and assumed broader responsibilities in the CW's business operations than Ostroff had.<ref name="thr-pedowitz">{{Cite news |last=Lacey Rose |date=April 28, 2011 |title=Mark Pedowitz Named President of The CW |work=The Hollywood Reporter |publisher=Prometheus Global Media |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/mark-pedowitz-named-president-cw-183298 |access-date=April 17, 2020 |archive-date=July 31, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200731093234/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/mark-pedowitz-named-president-cw-183298 |url-status=live }}</ref> As president of entertainment, Ostroff oversaw entertainment operations while John Maatta, the network's chief operating officer, handled business affairs; both reported to a board consisted of CBS and Warner Bros. executives. Maatta began reporting to Pedowitz as a result of the latter's appointment as network president.<ref name="thr-pedowitz" /> Pedowitz revealed that the core target demographic of the network would not change, though the CW would attempt to lure new viewers. Pedowitz began looking to bring comedies back to the CW after Ostroff had publicly declared that the difficulty of developing comedies for its target demographic was the reason for their removal from the network following the [[2008–09 United States network television schedule|2008–09 season]] (with ''Everybody Hates Chris'', and ''[[The Game (2006 TV series)|The Game]]''—a spin-off of ''Girlfriends''—becoming the last comedies to be cancelled).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lacey Rose |date=August 4, 2011 |title=CW Chief: Network Is in Search of Close-Ended Series, Comedies and a Superhero Show |work=The Hollywood Reporter |publisher=Prometheus Global Media |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/cw-chief-network-is-search-219442 |access-date=September 4, 2011 |archive-date=August 5, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110805195100/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/cw-chief-network-is-search-219442 |url-status=live }}</ref> The network also ordered more episodes of its original series and ran them consecutively starting on September 12 through the first week of December without repeats.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Christina Radish |date=August 5, 2011 |title=The CW President Mark Pedowitz Talks RINGER, SUPERNATURAL, NIKITA, GOSSIP GIRL, Developing More DC Superheroes, and More |url=https://collider.com/cw-mark-pedowitz-ringer-supernatural-smallville/ |access-date=September 4, 2011 |website=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |archive-date=September 25, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110925081958/http://collider.com/cw-mark-pedowitz-ringer-supernatural-smallville/107697 |url-status=live }}</ref> In July 2012, Pedowitz no longer referred to the target demographic of the CW as women 18–34, but rather that it would now be an "18–34 adult network".<ref name="Molloy">{{Cite news |last=Tim Molloy |date=July 30, 2012 |title=CW's Plans Include More Men, More Muppets |url=https://www.thewrap.com/tv/column-post/cws-plans-include-more-men-more-muppets-49921 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200513094229/https://www.thewrap.com/tv/column-post/cws-plans-include-more-men-more-muppets-49921/ |archive-date=May 13, 2020 |access-date=April 17, 2020 |work=[[The Wrap]] |publisher=The Wrap News Inc.}}</ref>

Although the network was still not profitable, CBS and Warner Bros. were very successful in selling their CW shows overseas. In 2011, a $1 billion deal with [[streaming service]] [[Netflix]] became another way to sell CW shows.{{r|goldberg20220513}} The introduction of action-superhero series ''[[Arrow (TV series)|Arrow]],'' based on [[DC Comics]]' [[Green Arrow]], received favorable reviews from critics and became a hit with audiences when it premiered. As evidence of the network's refocusing toward a broader audience, ''Arrow'' not only premiered to some of the highest viewership totals in the network's history (the third-highest overall {{as of|2015|lc=y}}, behind the series premieres of ''The Vampire Diaries'' and ''The Flash''), but it also gave the network its strongest performance in the demographic of males 18–34 since ''Smallville'' ended its run in May 2011. The network also found success with its summer programming in 2013 with the revival of the U.S. version of the improv comedy series ''[[Whose Line Is It Anyway? (American TV series)|Whose Line Is It Anyway?]]'', which later became a year-round staple on the network's schedule. ''Arrow'' continued to perform strongly, leading to a spin-off with ''[[The Flash (2014 TV series)|The Flash]]'', which surpassed ''The Vampire Diaries'' as the highest-rated premiere in the network's history and became the most-watched show on the network. ''[[Jane the Virgin]]'' earned some of the highest critical praise of any series during the 2014–15 television season, and became the first CW series ever to be nominated for, and win, a [[Golden Globe Award]], with lead actress [[Gina Rodriguez]] winning the Golden Globe for [[Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Television Series Musical or Comedy|Best Actress - Television Series Musical or Comedy]]. Other CW shows like ''[[The Flash (2014 TV series)|The Flash]]'', ''[[The 100 (TV series)|The 100]]'', and ''[[Nikita (TV series)|Nikita]]'' would also go on to be nominated for [[Primetime Emmy Awards]] categories, and several shows from 2011 to 2019 being nominated for categories in the [[Teen Choice Awards]], [[Saturn Awards]], and others.

Overall, the network ended the 2014–15 season posting its highest average total viewership in a single television season since 2007–08 with 2.15 million viewers, a 12% increase in total viewership year-to-year; the CW also posted its highest seasonal demographic ratings among males ages 18–49 with a 0.8 share.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bibel |first=Sara |date=May 13, 2015 |title=The CW Delivers its Most-Watched Season in 7 Years |url=http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2015/05/13/the-cw-delivers-its-most-watched-season-in-7-years/403500/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150516004027/http://tvbythenumbers.zap2it.com/2015/05/13/the-cw-delivers-its-most-watched-season-in-7-years/403500/ |archive-date=May 16, 2015 |access-date=September 2, 2015 |website=[[TV by the Numbers]]}}</ref>

Expanding on the success of the network's [[Arrowverse]] franchise, ''[[Legends of Tomorrow|DC's Legends of Tomorrow]]'' premiered to high ratings for the network and became the most-watched show on the network's Thursday night block in two years. The 2015–16 season also saw ''[[Crazy Ex-Girlfriend]]'' become one of the most critically acclaimed shows of the season and the second show on the network to be nominated for, and win, a Golden Globe Award, with actress [[Rachel Bloom]] winning a Golden Globe Award for [[Golden Globe Award for Best Actress – Television Series Musical or Comedy|Best Actress - Television Series Musical or Comedy]].

=== 2016–2021: Streaming era deals ===
The network's Arrowverse expanded again with ''[[Supergirl (TV series)|Supergirl]]'' being moved to the network from CBS for its second season. The debut of [[Archie Comics]]-based ''[[Riverdale (American TV series)|Riverdale]]'' signaled the network's foray into mining their parent studio's library of [[Intellectual property|IP]] to create new television series based on recognizable properties. This led to another new DC Comics series, ''[[Black Lightning (TV series)|Black Lightning]]'', and a rebooted ''[[Dynasty (2017 TV series)|Dynasty]]''. While it met with poor ratings, ''Dynasty'' proved lucrative thanks to the Netflix output deal and international syndication,<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 13, 2017 |title=Q2 2017 CBS Corp Earnings Call |url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/edited-transcript-cbs-earnings-conference-033925537.html |website=Yahoo! Finance |access-date=May 13, 2018 |archive-date=May 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180513152723/https://finance.yahoo.com/news/edited-transcript-cbs-earnings-conference-033925537.html |url-status=live }}</ref> which earned CBS Studios millions of dollars per episode.{{r|goldberg20220513}}

Selling CW series like ''Dynasty'' to Netflix and overseas markets was so profitable for Warner Bros. and CBS that the network almost stopped cancelling shows, and expanded its broadcast schedule.{{r|goldberg20220513}} On February 14, 2018, the CW announced that it would add a 2-hour primetime block on Sunday nights beginning in the fourth quarter of 2018 (it later added a third hour in October 2023), returning the network to Sundays for the first time since the lease to Media Rights Capital ended in 2009, as well as expanding the CW's primetime slate from 10 hours a week to 12. Discussions with CBS and Warner Bros. about the expansion began as early as July 2017; both gave their approval to the move that December, with the network reaching clearance deals with key affiliate partners in early 2018.<ref>[https://variety.com/2018/tv/news/cw-sunday-primetime-block-1202698748/ "CW Plans Sunday Primetime Block for 2018-19 Season,"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180218230544/http://variety.com/2018/tv/news/cw-sunday-primetime-block-1202698748/ |date=February 18, 2018 }} from ''Variety'', February 14, 2018</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=February 14, 2018 |title=The CW Reclaims Sunday, Will Expand Its Schedule To 6 Nights In Fall 2018 |language=en-US |work=Deadline |url=https://deadline.com/2018/02/the-cw-reclaims-sunday-expand-schedule-to-6-nights-fall-2018-1202288000/ |access-date=February 14, 2018 |archive-date=February 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180214201629/http://deadline.com/2018/02/the-cw-reclaims-sunday-expand-schedule-to-6-nights-fall-2018-1202288000/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On June 12, 2018, [[AT&T]] received antitrust approval to acquire Warner Bros. parent Time Warner, with the acquisition closing two days later. Time Warner was renamed [[WarnerMedia]] and AT&T became a co-owner of the CW with CBS.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 15, 2018 |title=AT&T Completes Acquisition of Time Warner Inc. |url=http://about.att.com/story/att_completes_acquisition_of_time_warner_inc.html |access-date=June 15, 2018 |website=AT&T |archive-date=September 19, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180919095512/http://about.att.com/story/att_completes_acquisition_of_time_warner_inc.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Gold |first=Hadas |title=Judge approves $85 billion AT&T-Time Warner deal |work=CNNMoney |url=https://money.cnn.com/2018/06/12/media/att-time-warner-ruling/index.html |access-date=June 12, 2018 |archive-date=July 11, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180711204644/https://money.cnn.com/2018/06/12/media/att-time-warner-ruling/index.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The CW debuted reboots of ''[[Charmed (2018 TV series)|Charmed]]'', ''[[Roswell, New Mexico (TV series)|Roswell]]'', and ''Originals'' spin-off ''[[Legacies (TV series)|Legacies]]'' during the 2018–19 season. Despite modest ratings, their renewals—along with the renewal of the entire 2018–19 lineup (absent those series already previously announced as ending)—reflected their value to the network's founding co-owners CBS and Warner Bros., which received the windfall of selling them to Netflix and international buyers.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 29, 2013 |title=TCA: Les Moonves Latest Exec To Try To Explain CW To TV Critics |url=https://deadline.com/2013/07/tca-cbs-ceo-les-moonves-latest-exec-to-try-to-explain-cw-to-tv-critics-551479/ |publisher=Deadline Hollywood |access-date=May 16, 2019 |archive-date=July 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200729004142/https://deadline.com/2013/07/tca-cbs-ceo-les-moonves-latest-exec-to-try-to-explain-cw-to-tv-critics-551479/ |url-status=live }}</ref> This strategy continued with the 2019–20 season debuts of the new Arrowverse series ''[[Batwoman (TV series)|Batwoman]]'', ''Riverdale'' spin-off ''[[Katy Keene (TV series)|Katy Keene]]'', and ''[[Nancy Drew (2019 TV series)|Nancy Drew]]''.

On August 13, 2019, CBS and [[Viacom (2005–2019)|Viacom]] officially announced their [[2019 merger of CBS and Viacom|intention to re-merge]], with the combined company to be named [[Paramount Global|ViacomCBS]]. The merger was completed on December 4, 2019, making them officially with AT&T's WarnerMedia co-owners of the CW.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Gasparino |first1=Charles |last2=Moynihan |first2=Lydia |date=August 13, 2019 |title=CBS, Viacom agree to merge, forming a $28B entertainment firm |url=https://www.foxbusiness.com/media/cbs-viacom-merger-agreement |access-date=August 13, 2019 |website=Fox Business |archive-date=March 11, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210311031847/https://www.foxbusiness.com/media/cbs-viacom-merger-agreement |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Szalai |first1=George |last2=Bond |first2=Paul |last3=Vlessing |first3=Etan |date=August 13, 2019 |title=CBS, Viacom Strike Deal to Recombine |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/cbs-viacom-strike-deal-recombine-1075545 |access-date=August 15, 2019 |publisher=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |archive-date=August 14, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190814215200/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/cbs-viacom-strike-deal-recombine-1075545 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="ViacomCBSOfficialPDF">{{Cite web |date=August 12, 2019 |title=CBS and Viacom To Combine |url=https://www.cbscorporation.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/ViacomCBS-Press-Release-FINAL.pdf |website=CBS |access-date=December 1, 2019 |archive-date=August 13, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190813190148/https://www.cbscorporation.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/ViacomCBS-Press-Release-FINAL.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2019 |title=Viacom and CBS Corp. are officially back together again |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/viacom-cbs-merger-stock-companies-are-officially-back-together-again/ |website=[[CBS News]] |access-date=December 18, 2019 |archive-date=December 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191206105230/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/viacom-cbs-merger-stock-companies-are-officially-back-together-again/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

WarnerMedia and ViacomCBS did not renew CW's Netflix deal in 2019, intending to use their shows on the network for their own streaming services.{{r|goldberg20220513}}<ref name="Deadline Hollywood">{{Cite web |date=May 15, 2019 |title=The CW-Netflix Deal Not Being Renewed, With Network's New Shows To Be Shopped Individually |url=https://deadline.com/2019/05/cw-netflix-deal-not-renewed-batwoman-nancy-drew-katy-keen-streaming-rights-1202615561/ |publisher=Deadline Hollywood |access-date=May 15, 2019 |archive-date=May 15, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190515211746/https://deadline.com/2019/05/cw-netflix-deal-not-renewed-batwoman-nancy-drew-katy-keen-streaming-rights-1202615561/ |url-status=live }}</ref> International sales also mostly ended, because both companies wanted to retain rights to their own shows to compete with Netflix outside the U.S.{{r|goldberg20220513}} WarnerMedia's [[HBO Max]] streaming service subsequently acquired exclusive streaming rights to Warner Bros.-produced CW shows.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 29, 2019 |title=Scope Of HBO Max's Deal For The CW Series Revealed |url=https://deadline.com/2019/10/hbo-max-deal-the-cw-series-volume-scope-katy-keene-batwoman-1202772168/ |publisher=Deadline Hollywood |access-date=January 16, 2021 |archive-date=January 22, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122043150/https://deadline.com/2019/10/hbo-max-deal-the-cw-series-volume-scope-katy-keene-batwoman-1202772168/ |url-status=live }}</ref> This began with the 2019–20 season, with the Warner Bros.-produced ''Batwoman'' and ''Katy Keene'' debuting on HBO Max after their current seasons finished airing on the CW. The CBS Studios-produced ''Nancy Drew'' was originally announced to be heading to corporate-sibling owned CBS All Access, but appeared on HBO Max instead. The reason for this was amid the rebranding of CBS All Access to [[Paramount+]] and the changes surrounding the ViacomCBS merger, CBS and Warner Bros. made the collective decision to have all CW shows have a singular streaming home on HBO Max.<ref name="CW HBO Max Partnership">{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2021 |title=With All New CW Series Currently HBO Max-Bound, Steamer & Net Forge Ties That Go Beyond Library Content |url=https://deadline.com/2021/01/walker-republic-of-sarah-new-cw-series-hbo-max-relationship-beyond-library-content-1234672556/ |publisher=Deadline Hollywood |access-date=January 16, 2021 |archive-date=January 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115223942/https://deadline.com/2021/01/walker-republic-of-sarah-new-cw-series-hbo-max-relationship-beyond-library-content-1234672556/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Beyond being the streaming home of CW programming, HBO Max shares a co-ownership connection with the network, which allows for programming partnerships. This began with DC Comics series ''[[Stargirl (TV series)|Stargirl]]'', which the CW shared with [[DC Universe (streaming service)|DC Universe]]. DC Universe and the CW co-financed the series,<ref name="CW HBO Max Partnership" /> with episodes premiering on DC Universe and airing the next day on the CW. After DC Universe was folded into HBO Max, ''Stargirl'' was renewed with a new co-finance deal in which the CW receives first-run airings followed by its launch on HBO Max.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 3, 2021 |title='Kung Fu' & 'Stargirl' Renewed At The CW |url=https://deadline.com/2021/05/kung-fu-stargirl-renewed-at-the-cw-1234748891/ |publisher=Deadline Hollywood |access-date=August 15, 2021 |archive-date=May 3, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210503174408/https://deadline.com/2021/05/kung-fu-stargirl-renewed-at-the-cw-1234748891/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Going forward, the CW and HBO Max will continue to collaborate on potentially co-financing new projects, with the model of premiering first on HBO Max and a second run on the CW.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2021 |title=How The CW Is Plotting a Return to Business as Usual During a Pandemic |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/how-the-cw-is-plotting-a-return-to-business-as-usual-during-a-pandemic |publisher=The Hollywood Reporter |access-date=January 16, 2021 |archive-date=January 15, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115155135/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/how-the-cw-is-plotting-a-return-to-business-as-usual-during-a-pandemic |url-status=live }}</ref> "They creatively have to want the show too and believe that the show should go on their platform first for them to work," CW CEO Pedowitz said. "For us its a great model because it's a way to get excellent summer scripted programming and maximize programming across platforms."<ref name="CW HBO Max Partnership" />

On May 13, 2021, the CW announced that it would begin programming Saturday nights on a regular basis beginning in the 2021–22 television season, following approval of the expansion by the network's key affiliate groups.<ref name=block>{{Cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=May 13, 2021 |title=The CW Expands Primetime Schedule To Saturday, Returns Weekday Afternoon Block To Affiliates |url=https://deadline.com/2021/05/the-cw-primetime-schedule-saturday-weekday-afternoon-block-returned-affiliates-1234755841/ |publisher=Deadline Hollywood |access-date=May 13, 2021 |archive-date=May 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513223622/https://deadline.com/2021/05/the-cw-primetime-schedule-saturday-weekday-afternoon-block-returned-affiliates-1234755841/ |url-status=live }}</ref> As part of the deal, the CW ceased programming [[the CW Daytime]] block and returned the time to its stations. With the addition of Saturday nights, the CW has programming on every night of the week for the first time in the network's history, becoming only the sixth US English-language commercial broadcast network ever and the first since Fox to have offered prime time content on a nightly basis.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 13, 2021 |title=The CW Expands to Saturdays This Fall, Making It a Seven-Night Network for the First Time |url=https://variety.com/2021/tv/news/the-cw-saturday-night-launch-fall-2021-1234972898/ |publisher=Variety |access-date=May 13, 2021 |archive-date=May 13, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513223622/https://variety.com/2021/tv/news/the-cw-saturday-night-launch-fall-2021-1234972898/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== 2022: Acquisition by Nexstar ===
On January 5, 2022, ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' reported that WarnerMedia and ViacomCBS were exploring a possible sale of either a majority stake or all of the CW, and that [[Nexstar Media Group]], which became the CW's largest affiliate group when it acquired former WB-era network co-owner [[Tribune Broadcasting]] in 2019, was considered a leading bidder.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Flint |first=Joe |date=January 5, 2022 |title=WarnerMedia and ViacomCBS Are Exploring Possible Sale of CW Network 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220106024412/https://www.wsj.com/articles/warnermedia-and-viacomcbs-are-exploring-possible-sale-of-cw-network-11641436892 |url-status=live }}</ref> Network president and CEO [[Mark Pedowitz]] confirmed talks of a potential sale but added that it was "too early to speculate what might happen".<ref name=THR01062022>{{Cite web |last1=Goldberg |first1=Lesley |last2=Weprin |first2=Alex |date=January 6, 2022 |title=ViacomCBS and WarnerMedia Exploring Sale of The CW In late June 2022, ''The Wall Street Journal'' indicated a purchase of the CW by Nexstar was close,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Flint |first=Joe |date=June 29, 2022 |title=Nexstar Nears Deal to Acquire Majority Control of CW Network |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/nexstar-nears-deal-to-acquire-majority-control-of-cw-network-11656537393 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220629235344/https://www.wsj.com/articles/nexstar-nears-deal-to-acquire-majority-control-of-cw-network-11656537393 |archive-date=June 29, 2022 |access-date=June 29, 2022 |website=The Wall Street Journal}}</ref> and on August 15 Nexstar confirmed it had "entered into a definitive agreement" to acquire a 75% majority share in the network;<ref name="tv">{{Cite web |last=Hayes |first=Dade |date=October 3, 2022 |title=New Day Dawns For Broadcast TV As Nexstar Closes Deal For Control Of The CW |url=https://deadline.com/2022/10/nexstar-closes-deal-for-control-of-the-cw-mark-pedowitz-exits-top-job-1235133428/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014023432/https://deadline.com/2022/10/nexstar-closes-deal-for-control-of-the-cw-mark-pedowitz-exits-top-job-1235133428/ |archive-date=October 14, 2022 |access-date=October 3, 2022 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref> the remaining 25% would be shared equally by Paramount Global (the former ViacomCBS) and [[Warner Bros. Discovery]] (the company formed by [[Discovery, Inc.]]'s acquisition of WarnerMedia from AT&T). Additionally, Nexstar stated that Mark Pedowitz would remain the chairman and CEO of the CW.<ref name="NewswireToday" /> Though no monetary terms were announced, Nexstar reportedly would not pay any cash or stock up front, and would absorb approximately $100 million of network debt.<ref name="DeadlineConferenceCall">{{cite web |last=Hayes |first=Dade |date=August 15, 2022 |title=The CW Will Be A web |last=Weprin |first=Alex |date=November 20, 2022 |title=Nexstar's Next Battle: Making The CW Numbers Work |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221205034349/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/cw-nexstar-future-deal-sale-terms-1235266033/ |url-status=live }}</ref> As the sale did not entail the transfer of any [[Federal Communications Commission|FCC]] broadcast licenses, Nexstar immediately took operational control of the network.<ref name="TVNC08152022">{{cite web |last=Messmer |first=Jack |date=August 15, 2022 |title=Nexstar Management Of CW Is Immediate |url=https://tvnewscheck.com/business/article/nexstar-management-of-cw-is-immediate/ |access-date=August 15, 2022 |work=TVNewsCheck |archive-date=August 15, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220815170609/https://tvnewscheck.com/business/article/nexstar-management-of-cw-is-immediate/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Nexstar, in a conference call that took place the day its purchase was announced, indicated a desire to run the CW cost-consciously. Citing research that indicated the network spends "almost twice" the amount other broadcast networks spend on programming, a partial reason for the May 2022 cancellations,<ref name="goldberg20220513"/> Nexstar stated that it planned to seek shows with smaller production budgets or a reasonably-priced acquisition fee, including unscripted fare, syndicated content, and other content that can create profits through broadcast airings.<ref name=DeadlineConferenceCall/> Nexstar also stated that it aimed for the CW to turn a profit by 2025.<ref name=THR01062022/><ref name=BC08152022/>

In the conference call, Nexstar indicated that it wanted to convert the CW into a network with broad appeal. It cited data indicating that the young audience which the CW focused upon preferred watching its shows through streaming platforms instead of during live broadcasts, while the average audience of a broadcast CW affiliate was approximately 58 years old.<ref name=DeadlineConferenceCall/> Nexstar indicated that it would focus on the older audiences as well and not just the younger demographic.<ref name="NewswireToday">{{cite web |date=August 15, 2022 |title=Nexstar Media Group to Acquire The CW Network |url=https://www.nexstar.tv/nexstar-media-group-to-acquire-the-cw-network/ |access-date=August 15, 2022 |work=Nexstar Media Group, Inc. |archive-date=August 15, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220815110032/https://www.nexstar.tv/nexstar-media-group-to-acquire-the-cw-network/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=BC08152022>{{cite web|url=https://www.nexttv.com/news/nexstar-expects-the-cw-to-be-profitable-by-2025|title=Nexstar Expects The CW To Be Profitable by 2025|last=Lafayette|first=Jon|work=Broadcasting & Cable|date=August 15, 2022|access-date=August 15, 2022|archive-date=August 16, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816174230/https://www.nexttv.com/news/nexstar-expects-the-cw-to-be-profitable-by-2025|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thewrap.com/nexstar-acquires-cw-network-warner-bros-discovery-paramount/|title=Nexstar to Acquire 75% Controlling Stake in The CW Network|last=Lindsay|first=Benjamin|work=The reported to have been seeking older-skewing dramas, [[police procedural]]s, and sitcoms.<ref>{{cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=August 29, 2022|title=The CW Widens Programming Scope To Include Sitcoms & Procedurals, Begins Testing Outside Studio Deals With 'The Hatpin Society' From EP Rachel 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220830013047/https://deadline.com/2022/08/the-cw-programming-plans-nexstar-future-the-hatpin-society-1235101264/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Paramount Global and Warner Bros. Discovery would still produce content for the CW as primary content suppliers, though Nexstar noted that the arrangement would be primarily for the [[2022–23 United States network television schedule|2022–23 broadcast season]]. It indicated that it "will have the option to extend the partnership" with Paramount and WBD beyond that season.<ref name=DeadlineConferenceCall/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thewrap.com/nexstar-cw-network-majority-control-deal/|title=Nexstar Close to Deal to Buy Majority Stake in The CW (Report)|last=Katz|first=Brandon|work=The Wrap|date=June 29, 2022|access-date=June 30, 2022|archive-date=June 30, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220630121857/https://www.thewrap.com/nexstar-cw-network-majority-control-deal/|url-status=live}}</ref> Nexstar stated in September 2022 that it would seek to supplement the CW's content by acquiring projects from studios beyond solely Paramount and WBD.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-09-07/nexstar-is-looking-for-new-shows-as-it-acquires-the-cw-network|title=Nexstar Is Looking for New Shows as It Acquires the CW Network|last=Shields|first=Todd|work=Bloomberg|date=September 7, 2022|access-date=September 7, 2022|archive-date=September 26, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220926134549/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-09-07/nexstar-is-looking-for-new-shows-as-it-acquires-the-cw-network|url-status=live}}</ref> while any the CW content not licensed to other streaming services would continue to appear on its own streaming platform CW Seed.<ref name="goldberg20220513"/>

On October 3, Nexstar officially announced that it had closed the deal to acquire the majority ownership of the CW. Longtime chairman and CEO Mark Pedowitz resigned from his role, with Dennis Miller taking over as the president of the CW.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Steinberg|first=Brian|date=October 3, 2022|title=Mark Thirty to forty employees were laid off on November 1, including several executives.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|date=November 2, 2022|title=CW Layoffs: More Details Emerge About Hewitt was replaced with Beth Feldman as the senior vice president of the network's communications unit.<ref>{{cite web|date=November 1, 2022|title=Nexstar Replaces Longtime CW Comms Chief Paul Hewitt On November 8, Nexstar announced that the carryover programming from the former majority parent companies of the CW, Paramount and WBD, would be minimal by the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/cw-shows-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-nexstar-2023-2024-1235426407/|title=CW's Carryover Programming From Paramount, Warner Bros. === 2023–present: Focus on sports and unscripted ===

On May 18, 2023, the CW unveiled its schedule for the [[2023–24 United States network television schedule|2023–24 broadcast season]], consisting mostly of acquired shows from outside the U.S., and unscripted series.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Otterson |first1=Joe |last2=Maas |first2=Jennifer |date=May 18, 2023 |title=The CW 2023 Upfront Takeaways: Superheroes (Mostly) Fly Away While Acquisitions Rule — For Now |url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/cw-2023-upfronts-superheroes-acquisitions-1235617473/ |access-date=May 19, 2023 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> Schwartz criticized the previous co-owners of the network, stating that it would no longer exist for benefiting them, and that the shows left over from the previous regimes did not perform well on linear broadcast. He added that in order to achieve profitability, the CW was focusing on acquired shows and co-productions while expanding its audience.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goldberg |first=Lesley |date=May 18, 2023 |title=Superhero Shows "Had Their Time" as New CW Leaders Outline Plans to Make Network "Bigger and Profitable" |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/nextar-pitches-cw-reinvention-less-superheroes-older-audience-1235495292/ |access-date=June 20, 2023 |website=The Hollywood Reporter}}</ref> He also revealed that the network was in production or negotiations for a total of 72 shows.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=White |first1=Peter
|date=May 18, 2023 |title=The CW "No Longer Built For The Benefit Of Studios," Says Brad Schwartz As He Reveals 70 Scripted & Unscripted Series In Production & Development |url=https://deadline.com/2023/05/the-cw-no-longer-built-for-the-benefit-of-studios-brad-schwartz-70-projects-1235371562/ |access-date=May 19, 2023 |website=Deadline Hollywood |language=en-US}}</ref>
On February 25, 2023, [[CW Sports]] was launched by acquiring the rights to [[LIV Golf]]<ref name="wp-liv"/> and soon expanded by acquiring [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] college football and basketball games,<ref>{{cite web |title=ACC Football and Basketball Coming to The CW Network This Fall ''[[WWE NXT]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Porter |first=Rick |date=2023-11-07 |title='WWE NXT' Moving to The CW From USA in 2024 In January 2024, during the [[29th Critics' Choice Awards]], The CW launched a new brand identity by DixonBaxi—which updated the logo with a bolder appearance, changed the network's main color from green to [[red-orange]], and introduced a new "stage" device used in promos (formed by extending the C lettering from the logo), as well as a new [[sound trademark]] of a struck [[match]]. Spadaccini explained that the rebranding was intended to help make the network's brand more consistent and optimized for digital platforms, the word "The" was removed from the logo to streamline its appearance (especially in use cases such as "CW Original" or "CW Sports"). Spadaccini said that the network's name and verbal branding would remain the CW.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schneider |first=Michael |date=January 12, 2024 |title=The CW Unveils New Branding Look, Dropping the 'The' and Embracing a 'Hot Sauce' Color Palette (EXCLUSIVE) |url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/the-cw-new-branding-logo-look-critics-choice-awards-1235870260/ |access-date=January 12, 2024 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref>

The CW unveiled its Fall schedule for the [[2024–25 United States network television schedule|2024–25 broadcast season]] in May 2024, with programming consisting of co-produced scripted series, game shows, unscripted series, and an expansion of CW Sports.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=May 16, 2024 |title=The CW Fall 2024-25 Schedule |url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/the-cw-fall-2024-25-schedule-superman-amp-lois-season-4-sullivans-crossing-1235918405/ |access-date=May 23, 2024 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Three of its four remaining pre-Nexstar scripted series, ''[[Superman & Lois]]'', ''[[All American: Homecoming]]'', and ''[[Walker (TV series)|Walker]]'', would conclude that year.<ref>{{cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|title=''All American: Homecoming'' Cancelled; EP Nkechi Okoro Carroll "Devastated" That Show Will End With Season 3 On CW|url=https://deadline.com/2024/06/all-american-homecoming-cancelled-season-3-final-1235959307/|work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=June 5, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Hailu |first=Selome |title='Superman & Lois' to End With Season 4 at the CW |url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/news/superman-and-lois-end-season-4-cw-1235778555/ |date=November 2, 2023 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|title=''Walker'' Canceled By CW After 4 Seasons|url=https://deadline.com/2024/05/walker-canceled-cw-4-seasons-1235926564/|website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=May 21, 2024}}</ref> Miller and Schwartz revealed that the network planned to air its own [[television film]]s later in 2024, with Miller adding that they planned to do more deals for sports programming. The CW's losses meanwhile declined by $50 million for the first quarter of 2024, compared to the $100 million loss during the quarter when Nexstar acquired it.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Otterson |first=Joe |title=CW Bosses on Doing Original TV Movies, Landing WWE's 'NXT,' and Potential New Sports Rights Deals |url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/cw-original-movies-nxt-sports-rights-deals-1236006189/ |date= May 16, 2024 |access-date=June 19, 2024 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> In June 2024, Schwartz stated that he hoped to have more scripted series on air, but their new financial model necessitated finding production partners.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schneider |first=Michael |title=The CW's Brad Schwartz Dismisses Concerns That Canadian Series on U.S. TV Are Seen as a 'Discount Bin' |url=https://variety.com/2024/tv/news/the-cw-brad-schwartz-canada-1236033952/ |date= June 11, 2024 |access-date=June 12, 2024 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> CW Studios was launched in August 2024 after the CW pulled ''[[The Librarians: The Next Chapter]]'' from their [[2024–25 United States network television schedule|Fall schedule]] and sold the series to [[TNT (American TV network)|TNT]].<ref name=CWStudios>{{Cite web |last=White |first=Peter |title=How 'The Librarians: The Next Chapter' Landed A Two-Season Order At TNT & Turned The CW Into A Studio| url=https://deadline.com/2024/08/the-librarians-the-next-chapter-season-2-tnt-1236049235/| date=August 23, 2024 |access-date=August 23, 2024 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}}</ref> The CW retained a stake in the series through the newly formed studio, providing the network with an in-house production arm.<ref name="CWStudios"/>

Miller departed as president of the CW in October 2024, with Brad Schwartz being promoted to fill the role.<ref>{{cite web|last=Weprin|first=Alex|title=The CW Undergoes Layoffs As It Seeks to "Transform" Network to Reach "Broader" Audience|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/the-cw-layoffs-network-cuts-sports-1236060190/|work=The Hollywood Reporter|date=November 12, 2024|access-date=November 18, 2024}}</ref> In November 2024, Nexstar reported that the CW had reduced its operating losses by $119 million year-to-date, exceeding the goal of $100 million for the year. Nexstar executives attributed this to lower cost programming and credited the growing CW Sports portfolio for increasing the network's viewership.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cobb|first=Kayla|title=Nexstar Reduces CW Operating Losses by $119 Million, Surpassing Expectations|url=https://www.thewrap.com/nexstar-reduces-cw-operating-losses-119-million/|work=The Wrap|date=November 7, 2024|access-date=November 7, 2024}}</ref> The CW underwent a round of layoffs later in the same month to streamline the network's focus on sports and unscripted programming, with Liz Wise Lyall, head of the scripted programming department, and Betsy Slenzak, vice president of the unscripted programming department, exiting.<ref>{{cite web|last=Andreeva|first=Nellie|title=The CW Undergoes Layoffs With Scripted PR Hit Hard; Read Brad Schwartz's Memo To Staff|url=https://deadline.com/2024/11/the-cw-layoffs-scripted-pr-1236174249/|work=Deadline Hollywood|date=November 12, 2024|access-date=November 12, 2024}}</ref> In December 2024, Nexstar acquired additional ownership of The CW, raising its stake from 75% to 77.1%.<ref name=":1" />

Michael Perman was appointed as the Senior Vice President of CW Sports in February 2025, overseeing programming and media rights for the division.<ref name="Perman">{{cite web|last=Vlessing|first=Etan|title=The CW Network Taps Michael Perman to Lead Sports Efforts|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/business/business-news/cw-network-michael-perman-1236135746/|work=The become profitable by 2026.<ref>{{cite web|last=Hayes|first=Dade|title=The CW Will Become Profitable In 2026, Nexstar Reaffirms, With 40% Of Its Programming Now of the [[fiscal year]] 2024-25, the CW had reduced its year-over-year losses by $126 million.<ref>{{cite web|last=Cobb|first=Kayla|title=Hot Off the Success of NASCAR and WWE, CW Bosses Are
