of the fiscal year 2025–26, the CW recorded its strongest primetime performance in the past eight quarters,<ref>{{cite web|last=Maas|first=Jennifer|title=This Far Into a Revamp, Here's Why The CW Still Isn't Looking for a Rebrand|url=https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/cw-rebrand-explained-programming-all-american-1236393686/|work=Variety|date=May 12, 2025|access-date=May 31, 2025}}</ref> despite increasing its loss compared to the same quarter in the previous year.<ref>{{cite web|last=Maas|first=Jennifer|title=CW Loss Increases by 'Mid-Teen Millions' in Q1 as Nexstar Continues to Project 2026 Profitability Goal|url=https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/cw-loss-increases-2026-profitability-goal-1236390115/|work=Variety|date=May 8, 2025|access-date=May 31, 2025}}</ref> In June 2025, the CW ordered six [[Television film|television movies]] inspired by the [[Harlequin Enterprises|Harlequin]] romance novels which would be broadcast on the network during fall 2025, starting with ''Montana Mavericks'' which received a theatrical release before airing.<ref name="Olander1">{{cite web|first=Loree |last=Seitz |title=The CW Orders 6 Primetime Movies Inspired by Harlequin Romance Novels|url=https://www.thewrap.com/the-cw-harlequin-romance-novels-movies/|work=TheWrap|date=June 25, 2025|access-date=June 25, 2025}}</ref> 

Nexstar [[chief financial officer|CFO]] Lee Ann Gliha stated in December 2025 that the programming costs of the CW had been more than halved, with programming hours increasing by 40% and the sports portfolio accounting for 40% of its programming. Gliha noted that the CW's [[Owned-and-operated station|owned-and-operated stations]] were profitable for Nexstar, and that the CW itself was on track to turn a profit in 2026.<ref name="Gliha">{{cite web|last=Hayes|first=Dade|title=The CW Will Turn A Profit "At Some Point" In 2026, Parent Company Nexstar's CFO Says|url=https://deadline.com/2025/12/the-cw-network-profit-nexstar-1236642530/|work=Deadline Hollywood |date=December 8, 2025|access-date=December 10, 2025}}</ref> The CW's viewership increased by 13% in 2025, largely accredited towards the airing of sports.<ref>{{cite web|last=Schneider|first=Michael|title=Top-Rated Television Networks: Ranking 2025’s Winners and Losers|url=https://variety.com/2025/tv/news/top-rated-channels-2025-tv-network-ratings-most-watched-1236613231/|date=December 29, 2025|access-date=December 30, 2025|work=Variety}}</ref>

In April 2026, the CW announced a pair of streaming partnerships with the Disney-owned [[ESPN]] and [[Roku, Inc.|Roku]]. Under the deals, the CW's entertainment programming would stream next-day on [[The Roku Channel]] while [[CW Sports]] programming would be simulcast on the [[ESPN (streaming service)|ESPN app]] for subscribers of the "Unlimited" tier. The CW's own app would continue to offer next-day streams of its programming.<ref>{{cite web|last=Hayes|first=Dade|title=The CW Teams With ESPN & Roku In Streaming Partnerships Unveiled During Upfront Push|url=https://deadline.com/2026/04/the-cw-espn-roku-streaming-partnerships-1236875143/|date=April 29, 2026|access-date=April 29, 2026|work=Deadline Hollywood}}</ref> ''[[All American (TV series)|All American]]'', the final pre-Nexstar scripted series on the CW, concluded on September 28, 2026, with the network having shifted its strategy from attracting young adults into becoming a mainstream platform attracting a large audience of all ages.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cobb |first=Kayla |date=September 29, 2026 |title=''All American'' Boss Breaks Down Series Finale and What Would Have Happened in Season 9 |url=https://www.thewrap.com/creative-content/tv-shows/all-american-season-8-finale-nkechi-okoro-carroll-interview/ |access-date=September 29, 2026 |website=[[TheWrap]] }}</ref>

== Programming ==
=== Network programming and scheduling ===
{{Main|List of programs broadcast by The CW}}

As of October 1, 2023, the CW provides 18 hours of regularly scheduled network programming each week, over the course of seven days. The network offers 15 hours of prime time programming to its owned-and-operated and affiliated stations, airing from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. [[Eastern Time Zone|Eastern]] and [[Pacific Time Zone|Pacific Time]] on Monday through Saturday nights and 7 p.m. to 10 p.m. (Eastern and Pacific) on Sunday nights.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The CW Broadcast Schedule |url=https://www.cwtv.com/schedule/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231001183456/https://www.cwtv.com/schedule/ |archive-date=October 1, 2023 |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=The CW Network |language=en}}</ref> Outside of prime time, a three-hour [[Regulations on children's television programming in the United States|educational programming]] block called "[[One Magnificent Morning]]" (which airs as part of the CW schedule through a time-lease agreement with [[Hearst Media Production Group]]) airs on Saturday mornings from 8 a.m. to 11 a.m. in all time zones, subject to re-schedulings due to local or CW sports broadcasts.

Similar to Fox, along with network forerunners the WB and UPN, the CW uses the "common prime" scheduling practice, avoiding the 10 p.m. (Eastern and Pacific) hour broadcast by the "Big Three" networks (NBC, CBS, and ABC). The network, unlike the Big Three, does not air any national [[news]]casts, [[Late-night television in the United States|late-night programming]], and, since 2021,<ref name="block" /> [[Daytime television|daytime programming]] (outside of sports). It also did not run prime-time programming on Saturday nights and during the primetime access hour on Sundays until the 2021–22 and 2023–24 broadcast seasons respectively.<ref name="block" /> Because of these factors, the CW's affiliates handle the responsibility of programming non-network time periods, with the majority of its stations filling those slots mainly with syndicated programming. However, some of the network's affiliates broadcast their own local news or sports programs (either produced by the station itself or through outsourcing agreements with an affiliate of another network), preempting network prime time programming to a specific time period (New York City affiliate [[WPIX]], for instance, preempts CW prime time to the afternoon).

The Hearst-produced Saturday morning block, One Magnificent Morning (which is subject to scheduling variances similar to the weekday hour in some markets, such as in [[WUPA|Atlanta]] and [[XETV-TDT|San Diego]]), is designed to be [[broadcast delay|tape delayed]] and therefore recommended to air in the same time slot in all time zones. However, it is broadcast one hour earlier on affiliates of the CW Plus in the [[Central Time Zone|Central]], [[Mountain Time Zone|Mountain]] and [[Alaska Time Zone]]s. In [[Guam]], CW Plus affiliate [[KTKB-LD]] in [[Hagåtña, Guam|Hagåtña]] airs the CW lineup on a one-day tape delay from its initial broadcast because of the time difference between Guam and the [[continental United States]] as the island is on the west side of the [[International Date Line]].

''Supernatural'' (which initially aired on the WB) was the final CW series carried over from either of the network's respective predecessors that continued to be broadcast, airing its final episode in November 2020.

The CW formerly aired short segments during commercial breaks within certain episodes of its programs known as "Content Wraps"—a play on the network's name—to advertise one company's product during part or the entirety of a commercial break, a concept since classified under the term of [[native advertising]]. The entertainment magazine series ''[[CW Now]]'' was inspired in part by the success of the Content Wraps as it was intended to be a series with [[product placement]];<ref>{{Cite web |last=Steven Mallas |date=September 25, 2007 |title="CW Now": Content or Commercial? |url=http://www.fool.com/investing/general/2007/09/25/cw-now-content-or-commercial.aspx |website=[[The Motley Fool]] |access-date=September 30, 2007 |archive-date=October 12, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071012002003/http://www.fool.com/investing/general/2007/09/25/cw-now-content-or-commercial.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref> the program was canceled in 2008, after a single 23-episode season. For the 2006–07 season, the CW reached an agreement with [[American Eagle Outfitters]] to incorporate tie-ins with the company's [[Aerie (clothing retailer)|aerie]]<!--- no caps as stylized ---> clothing line as part of the Content Wrap concept within the network's Tuesday night schedule, which included subjects in the commercials commenting on plot points in each of the shows.{{citation needed|date=August 2024}} The agreement was cut down to regular advertising in February 2007, after a fan backlash by viewers of both shows and general criticism of the campaign.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 4, 2006 |title=The Aerie Girls and Terrible TV Advertising |url=http://www.makemewatchtv.com/2006/10/04/the-aerie-girls-and-terrible-tv-advertising/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100918085714/http://www.makemewatchtv.com/2006/10/04/the-aerie-girls-and-terrible-tv-advertising/ |archive-date=September 18, 2010 |access-date=December 14, 2010 |website=Make Me Watch TV }}</ref>

=== News programming ===
The CW began to introduce national news programming under Nexstar ownership, in partnerships with sister properties [[NewsNation]] and ''[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]''. It aired its first national news special on December 6, 2023, simulcasting the [[2024 Republican Party presidential debates and forums#December 6, 2023 – Tuscaloosa, Alabama|fourth Republican presidential primary debate]] with NewsNation.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Weprin |first=Alex |date=November 9, 2023 |title=NewsNation and The CW Snag GOP Primary Debate, Megyn Kelly and Elizabeth Vargas to Moderate |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/politics-news/newsnation-the-cw-republican-primary-debate-megyn-kelly-elizabeth-vargas-1235643004/ |access-date=November 9, 2023 |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]}}</ref> In February 2024, it was reported that the network was developing a [[Sunday morning talk show]] with ''The Hill''.<ref>{{cite web |date=February 16, 2024 |title=Nexstar Plans Weekend NewsNation Politics Talk Show for The CW |url=https://www.thewrap.com/the-hill-sunday-politics-talk-show-cw-nexstar/ |access-date=February 19, 2024 |work=The Wrap}}</ref> The new program was later announced as ''The Hill Sunday'' with [[Chris Stirewalt]], which premiered March 3, 2024 on NewsNation, and made its CW premiere on April 7, 2024.<ref>{{cite web |date=February 29, 2024 |title=Chris Stirewalt Aims to Break From Trend of Media 'Malpractice' With Sunday NewsNation Show |url=https://www.thewrap.com/chris-stirewalt-newsnation-sunday-show/ |access-date=February 29, 2024 |work=The Wrap}}</ref> The CW would simulcast NewsNation's ''Decision Desk 2024'' coverage of the [[2024 United States presidential election]] on November 5, 2024, and [[Chris Cuomo]]-hosted town halls with president [[Donald Trump]] on April 30, and on the [[2025 United States federal government shutdown|federal government shutdown]] on October 15 (headlined by guest [[Tom Homan]]).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-22 |title=NewsNation announces 2024 election coverage |url=https://www.newscaststudio.com/2024/10/22/newsnation-2024-election-coverage-plans/ |access-date=2024-11-03 |website=NewscastStudio |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2, 2025 |title=NewsNation Sees Nearly 750,000 Viewers for Donald Trump Town Hall Hosted by Chris Cuomo |url=https://barrettmedia.com/2025/05/02/newsnation-sees-nearly-750000-viewers-for-donald-trump-town-hall-hosted-by-chris-cuomo/ |access-date=May 3, 2025 |website=Barrett Media |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Ted |date=2025-10-14 |title=NewsNation And CNN To Host Town Halls Amid Shutdown And Trump Administration Immigration Raids |url=https://deadline.com/2025/10/town-halls-newsnation-cnn-1236584579/ |access-date=2025-10-22 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref>

Local news programming on CW affiliates—if any—is often outsourced to another major network affiliate in the market, usually a sister station via co-ownership or [[Local marketing agreement|local marketing agreements]], or as part of an outsourcing agreement with a third-party. Scheduling of local news often mirrors that of Fox affiliates, with local morning shows intended to compete with the national morning shows on the [[Big Three (American television)|Big Three networks]] (and often being an extension of a morning show on a Big Three affiliate), and prime time newscasts within the 10 p.m.–11 p.m. Eastern/Pacific (9 p.m.–10 p.m. Central/Mountain) time slot following network programming.

Only six CW stations have autonomous local news operations, most of which carried over from previous affiliations: WPIX in New York City, WGN in Chicago, and [[KTLA]] in Los Angeles started their news departments as independent stations or during early affiliations with other networks including DuMont (KTLA) and CBS (WGN); [[WISH-TV]] in [[Indianapolis]] (formerly CBS)<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Jeff Newman |last2=Anthony Schoettle |date=October 1, 2014 |title=WISH-TV Expanding Daily Newscasts by Four Hours |work=[[Indianapolis Business Journal]] |publisher=[[American City Business Journals]] |url=http://www.ibj.com/articles/49771-wish-tv-expanding-daily-newscasts-by-four-hours |access-date=December 17, 2014 |archive-date=December 8, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141208192115/http://www.ibj.com/articles/49771-wish-tv-expanding-daily-newscasts-by-four-hours |url-status=live }}</ref> has been airing local news since 1956, [[KRON-TV]] in [[San Francisco]] (formerly NBC and MyNetworkTV) has produced local news since 1957, while [[KUSI-TV]] in San Diego has aired local news since 1990.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ch. 51 quietly slips newscast on the air|page=C5|work=San Diego Union-Tribune|first=Joe|last=Stein|date=September 28, 1990}}</ref> KTLA has the largest number of weekly hours devoted to local news programming of any CW affiliate, and any broadcast television station in the U.S., with {{frac|94|3|4}} hours of scheduled news each week.

Outside of network programming, several CW affiliates have carried telecasts of [[college basketball|basketball]], [[college football|football]] and in some cases, other collegiate sporting events (such as [[college baseball|baseball]] or [[College ice hockey|hockey]]) that are produced by syndicators, while a few carry games from local teams of major professional sports leagues such as [[Major League Baseball]] (the [[New York Mets]] on [[WPIX]]) and the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] (the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on [[KTLA]]).

=== Children's programming ===
{{Main|Kids' WB|Toonzai|Vortexx|One Magnificent Morning}}

On September 23, 2006, the [[Kids' WB]] children's programming block—which originated on The WB in September 1995 and continued to be produced by Warner Bros.—was carried over to the CW as part of its inaugural programming lineup; although the network on which it originated ceased operations, the "Kids' WB" branding was retained for the block.

On October 2, 2007, through a joint decision between corporate parents Warner Bros. and CBS Corporation, the CW announced that it would shut down Kids' WB and lease the programming rights of the Saturday morning timeslots to [[4Licensing Corporation|4Kids Entertainment]] (which was producing a competing children's programming block, [[4Kids TV]], for [[Fox Broadcasting Company|Fox]] at the time of the announcement). The CW cited competition from children's cable networks and a challenging advertising marketplace as factors in the decision.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Michael Schneider |date=October 2, 2007 |title=CW turns to 4Kids on Saturdays |url=https://variety.com/2007/digital/markets-festivals/cw-turns-to-4kids-on-saturdays-1117973235/ |publisher=Reed Business Information |periodical=Variety |access-date=December 10, 2017 |archive-date=September 19, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170919234111/http://variety.com/2007/digital/markets-festivals/cw-turns-to-4kids-on-saturdays-1117973235/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Kids' WB ended its nearly thirteen year-old run on May 17, 2008 (though some CW affiliates that delayed the block to Sundays, such as [[Atlanta]] affiliate [[WUPA]], aired the block for the last time on May 18).

The following week on May 24, 4Kids Entertainment took over programming of the CW's Saturday morning timeslots, with the debut of a new block, [[Toonzai|The CW4Kids]]. Its lineup initially consisted mostly of programs carried over from Kids' WB and 4Kids TV, before eventually adding first-run 4Kids-produced shows such as ''[[Chaotic (TV series)|Chaotic]]'' as well as new seasons of ''[[Yu-Gi-Oh! Duel Monsters|Yu-Gi-Oh!]]'' and ''[[Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (2003 TV series)|Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Annemarie Moody |date=November 30, 2007 |title=Brands Old and New for 4Kids at Licensing Expo 2008 |url=http://www.awn.com/news/brands-old-and-new-4kids-licensing-expo-2008 |website=[[Animation World Network]] |publisher=AWN, Inc. |access-date=September 2, 2015 |archive-date=September 15, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150915052112/http://www.awn.com/news/brands-old-and-new-4kids-licensing-expo-2008 |url-status=live }}</ref> The block was rebranded to [[Toonzai]] on August 14, 2010 (though The CW4Kids name was retained as a sub-brand to fulfill branding obligations with the network). Toonzai ended its run on August 18, 2012, after 4Kids Entertainment auctioned off their assets in bankruptcy court.<ref name="animenewsnetwork.com">{{cite news|title=4Kids Sells Yu-Gi-Oh!, CW Network-Related Assets Jointly to Konami, Kidsco|url=https://www.animenewsnetwork.com/news/2012-06-26/4kids-sells-yu-gi-oh-cw-network-related-assets-jointly-to-konami-kidsco|access-date=October 20, 2012|newspaper=AnimeNewsNetwork|date=June 26, 2012}}</ref>

On July 3, 2012, [[Saban Brands]] announced that they had acquired the rights to program the CW's Saturday morning timeslots from 4Kids Entertainment in bankruptcy proceedings.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Andrew Wallenstein |date=July 2, 2012 |title=Saban Brands to rebuild CW toon block |work=Variety |publisher=Penske Media Corporation |url=https://variety.com/2012/tv/news/saban-brands-to-rebuild-cw-toon-block-1118056206/ |access-date=July 7, 2012 |archive-date=September 21, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921055400/http://variety.com/2012/tv/news/saban-brands-to-rebuild-cw-toon-block-1118056206/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=C. Marcucci |date=July 3, 2012 |title=The CW signs Saban Brands for kids block |url=http://rbr.com/the-cw-signs-saban-brands-for-kids-block/ |website=Radio & Television Business Report |publisher=Streamline RBR, Inc. |access-date=July 13, 2012 |archive-date=July 8, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120708223949/http://rbr.com/the-cw-signs-saban-brands-for-kids-block/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The block was relaunched as [[Vortexx]] on August 25, featuring programs produced by Saban Brands such as ''[[Power Rangers Lost Galaxy]]'' and ''[[Digimon Fusion]]''. Vortexx also aired notable third-party programming such as ''[[WWE Saturday Morning Slam]]'', which marked the return of WWE programming to the network since ''WWE Smackdown'' departed in 2008.<ref name="wwe-slam-pr">{{Cite press release |title=WWE Returns to Kids Time Slot with Original Content Anchoring Vortexx on The CW |date=August 10, 2012 |publisher=[[Saban Capital Group|Saban Brands]] |url=http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/wwe-returns-to-kids-time-slot-with-original-content-anchoring-vortexx-on-the-cw-165714726.html |access-date=August 10, 2012 |agency=[[PR Newswire]] |archive-date=August 17, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120817235751/http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/wwe-returns-to-kids-time-slot-with-original-content-anchoring-vortexx-on-the-cw-165714726.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On June 5, 2014, the CW announced an agreement with Litton Entertainment (now [[Hearst Media Production Group]]) to program a block of live-action series designed to comply with the FCC's [[E/I|educational programming]] guidelines. Vortexx (which was the last remaining non-educational children's block on the major U.S. broadcast networks) was replaced by [[One Magnificent Morning]] on October 4.<ref>{{Cite news |date=June 5, 2014 |title=The CW Sets 5-Hour Saturday Morning Block |work=Deadline Hollywood |publisher=Penske Media Corporation |url=https://deadline.com/2014/06/the-cw-saturday-morning-block-litton-entertainment-740867/ |access-date=June 6, 2014 |archive-date=June 6, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140606224600/http://www.deadline.com/2014/06/the-cw-saturday-morning-block-litton-entertainment/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Gail Sullivan |date=September 30, 2014 |title=Saturday morning cartoons are no more |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |publisher=[[Jeff Bezos|Nash Holdings LLC]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/morning-mix/wp/2014/09/30/saturday-morning-cartoons-are-no-more/ |access-date=October 11, 2014 |archive-date=October 6, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006122243/http://www.washingtonpost.com/news/morning-mix/wp/2014/09/30/saturday-morning-cartoons-are-no-more/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The block features a mix of wildlife and lifestyle-themed programs, similar to those featured on the Litton-produced blocks aired by [[Litton's Weekend Adventure|ABC]] and [[CBS Dream Team|CBS]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kevin Downey |date=June 5, 2014 |title=CW Joins With Litton For Sat. }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The CW-Network Partners with Litton Entertainment on New Block |url=http://www.litton.tv/resources/CW-Network-Partners-with-Litton-Entertainment-on-New-Block-3.pdf == Stations ==
{{Original research|date=May 2022}}
{{Main|List of The CW affiliates (table)|List of The CW affiliates (by U.S. state)|The CW Plus|Nexstar Media Group}}
<!--- Please update station count in the below paragraph whenever the accompanying list referenced is updated. --->

The CW has over 46 stations owned or operated by its majority owner Nexstar Media Group<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-12-18 |title=Nexstar Television Stations in Grand Rapids, Sioux Falls, and Panama City To Begin Carrying CW Network Programming on January 1 |url=https://www.nexstar.tv/nexstar-stations-in-grand-rapids-sioux-falls-and-panama-city-to-begin-carrying-cw-programming-jan-1/ |access-date=2024-01-04 |website=Nexstar Media Group, Inc. |language=en-US}}</ref> and current and pending affiliation agreements with 221 additional television stations encompassing 50 states, the District of Columbia and three U.S. possessions.<ref name="recw">{{Cite web |title=Network Search: CW |url=http://www.rabbitears.info/search.php?request=network_search&network=CW |access-date=November 15, 2019 |website=RabbitEars |archive-date=January 21, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200121191124/https://www.rabbitears.info/search.php?request=network_search&network=CW |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="recwplus">{{Cite web |title=Network Search: CW+ |url=http://www.rabbitears.info/search.php?request=network_search&network=CW%2B |access-date=November 15, 2019 |website=RabbitEars |archive-date=March 4, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200304124518/https://www.rabbitears.info/search.php?request=network_search&network=CW%2B |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="StationIndex">{{Cite web |title=Network Profile: The CW |url=http://www.stationindex.com/tv/by-net/cw |website=Station Index |access-date=March 12, 2015 |archive-date=April 2, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402143151/http://www.stationindex.com/tv/by-net/cw |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Nexstar">{{Cite web |title=NEXSTAR MEDIA GROUP TO ACQUIRE THE CW NETWORK |url=https://www.nexstar.tv/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Final-Nexstar-Investor-Deck-re-CW-Acquisition-8-15-22-_-Revised.pdf |access-date=March 2, 2023 |archive-date=August 15, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220815170728/https://www.nexstar.tv/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Final-Nexstar-Investor-Deck-re-CW-Acquisition-8-15-22-_-Revised.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> Counting only conventional CW affiliates and over-the-air affiliates of the CW Plus, the network has an estimated combined national reach of 100% of all households in the U.S. (or 330,866,316 Americans with at least one television set); this makes the CW the largest U.S. broadcast network by population reach percentage. As of January 2023, three U.S. states ([[Delaware]], [[New Hampshire]], and [[New Jersey]]) and three U.S. territories ([[American Samoa]], [[Puerto Rico]] and the [[United States Virgin Islands]]) do not have their own locally licensed CW affiliates, largely because those areas are either located within the broadcast ranges of stations in nearby states or served by out-of-market stations via cable or satellite. Delaware is served by Philadelphia's [[WPHL-TV]] and [[Salisbury, Maryland]] affiliate [[WMDT|WMDT-DT2]], while New Hampshire is served by four CW stations based in three neighboring states (including Boston affiliate [[WLVI]]). New Jersey is served by WPHL and New York City affiliate WPIX.

As a newer broadcast network, the CW maintains affiliations with low-power stations (broadcasting either in [[analog television|analog]] or [[digital terrestrial television|digital]]) in a few markets, such as [[Boise, Idaho]] ([[KYUU-LD]]). In some markets, including both of those mentioned, these stations also maintain digital simulcasts on a subchannel of a co-owned/co-managed full-power television station. The CW also maintains a sizeable number of subchannel-only affiliations, the majority of which are with stations in cities located outside of the 50 largest Nielsen-designated markets and receive the network's programming via the CW Plus; the largest subchannel-only CW affiliate by market size, as of February 1, 2024, is [[WZTV|WZTV-DT2]] in [[Nashville, Tennessee|Nashville]], [[Tennessee]].

Nexstar Media Group is the largest operator of CW stations by numerical total, owning or providing services to 41 CW-affiliated stations, and also is the largest in terms of overall market reach, owning or providing services to CW stations (including its largest affiliates in New York and Los Angeles), covering 32% of the U.S.<ref name="Nexstar" />

=== Digital multicasting and cable television ===
Unlike the other major networks, the CW distributes its programming in small and certain mid-sized markets throughout the U.S. (generally those ranked among the bottom 110 [[Nielsen Media Research|Nielsen]] [[media market]]s) through [[the CW Plus]], a separate national feed and programming service that is carried on a mixture of full-power and [[Low-power broadcasting|low-power station]]s in some markets, and cable-only outlets and [[digital subchannel]] affiliations on major network stations in markets that do not have enough commercial stations to support a standalone CW affiliate (several of the CW Plus's digital subchannel outlets originally operated as cable-only affiliates at the network's launch). The programming service offers its own master schedule of syndicated and [[brokered programming]] acquired by the network (including some feature films and [[infomercial]]s) during non-network programming time, although some CW Plus affiliates may also run local newscasts produced by a major network affiliate.

CW predecessor the WB previously had two cable-only affiliate outlets: [[WGN America]], the national [[superstation]] feed of WGN-TV at the time, from January 1995 to October 1999<ref>{{Cite web |last=Linda Moss |date=September 20, 1999 |title=WGN Drops WB, Adds Movies, Sitcoms |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-55897252.html |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150328150223/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-55897252.html |archive-date=March 28, 2015 |access-date=June 22, 2013 |publisher=[[Reed Business Information|Cahners Business Information]]|via=[[HighBeam Research]] |url-access=subscription |periodical=[[Multichannel News]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=MaryWade Burnside |date=October 7, 1999 |title=Last night Dawson's last ? WGN ceases to air WB programming |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-18522684.html |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150328150224/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P2-18522684.html |archive-date=March 28, 2015 |access-date=June 22, 2013 |publisher=The Daily Gazette Company |via=HighBeam Research |url-access=subscription |location=Charleston, WV |newspaper=[[The Charleston Gazette]]}}</ref> and network-operated [[the WB 100+ Station Group]] (the direct predecessor to the CW Plus), which was formed in September 1998 and had several of its cable-only outlets join the CW Plus at the CW network's launch. Not all of the network's cable-only affiliates were CW Plus outlets; [[WT05]] in [[Toledo, Ohio]] offered its own schedule of syndicated programs during non-network time that was programmed by its then-owner [[Block Communications]], which also operates that market's major cable provider [[Buckeye CableSystem]] (WT05 now exists as "CW13", having been converted into a digital subchannel of [[Gray Television]]-owned ABC affiliate [[WTVG]] in October 2014). Though the CW is the only network with a station group that includes cable-only outlets, it is actually one of only three networks that have had cable-only stations within its affiliate body (ABC formerly had a cable-only affiliate in [[Winchester, Virginia]]-based [[TV3 Winchester]] until Gray shut the channel down in December 2013).

=== Affiliate issues ===
==== Problems with Time Warner Cable ====
Some [[Time Warner Cable]] subscribers around the country were unable to watch CW programming when the network debuted, as stations in several markets were not able to reach carriage deals with the provider to distribute the local affiliates. In markets such as [[Charleston, South Carolina]]; [[El Paso, Texas]]; [[Honolulu]], Hawaii; [[Palm Springs, California]]; [[Beaumont, Texas|Beaumont]]; [[Waco, Texas|Waco]] and [[Corpus Christi, Texas]], where the CW is broadcast on a digital subchannel of one of the market's major network affiliates, there were unsuccessful attempts in getting Time Warner Cable to carry the subchannel affiliates<ref>{{Cite web |last=[[John M. Higgins]] |date=October 2, 2006 |title=Time Warner Cable Squeezes CW Stations |url=http://www.broadcastingcable.com/news/news-articles/time-warner-cable-squeezes-cw-stations/81083 |publisher=Reed Business Information |periodical=Broadcasting & Cable |access-date=September 2, 2015 |archive-date=September 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924122034/http://www.broadcastingcable.com/news/news-articles/time-warner-cable-squeezes-cw-stations/81083 |url-status=live }}</ref> (CW then-co-parent Time Warner had owned Time Warner Cable until it [[Corporate spin-off|spun off]] the provider into a separate company in 2009; TWC was later acquired by [[Charter Communications]] in 2016).

Some affiliates eventually signed carriage deals with Time Warner Cable, but not all of the CW affiliates received carriage on the provider's basic cable tiers (for example, [[Syracuse, New York]] affiliate [[WSTQ-LP]] could only be viewed on [[digital cable]] channel 266 in the [[Ithaca, New York|Ithaca]] market). The largest market without a known affiliate is the [[Johnstown, Pennsylvania|Johnstown]]–[[Altoona, Pennsylvania|Altoona]] market, whose closest CW station was CBS-owned WPCW (now [[WPKD-TV]], an independent station) in [[Pittsburgh]], which is carried on Charter's Johnstown and Altoona area systems; WPKD-TV was originally targeted to serve that area before it refocused its programming toward the Pittsburgh market in the late 1990s.

On February 2, 2007, [[Beaumont, Texas]] CBS station [[KFDM]] made its CW-affiliated subchannel available to Time Warner Cable customers in the market on channel 10. On April 20, 2007, ABC affiliate [[KVIA-TV]] in El Paso, Texas began broadcasting its CW-affiliated subchannel on Time Warner Cable channel 13.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 19, 2007 |title=The CW Wait Over |url=http://www.kvia.com/Global/story.asp?S=6394674 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927022003/http://www.kvia.com/Global/story.asp?S=6394674 |archive-date=September 27, 2007 |website=[[KVIA-TV]] |publisher=[[News-Press & Gazette Company]]}}</ref> On April 21, 2007, [[KCWQ-LP]] made its broadcast debut on channel 5 on Time Warner Cable in the Palm Springs area.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 20, 2007 |title=CW to debut on Time Warner |url=http://www.thedesertsun.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20070420/BUSINESS06/704200345 |publisher=Gannett Company |newspaper=[[The Desert Sun]] |access-date=July 1, 2022 |archive-date=July 1, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220701074856/https://www.desertsun.com/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Pappas Telecasting bankruptcy ====
One of the network's major affiliate groups, [[Pappas Telecasting|Pappas Telecasting Companies]], filed for [[Chapter 11, Title 11, United States Code|Chapter 11 bankruptcy]] for thirteen of its television stations on May 10, 2008. Within the petition, Pappas specifically cited the network's low ratings and lackluster performance as one of many complications that had forced it to make the filing.<ref>{{Cite web |title=PAPPAS TELECASTING ANNOUNCED TODAY THAT CERTAIN AFFILIATES HAVE FILED FOR CHAPTER 11 PROTECTION |url=http://www.pappastv.com/pressdetail.php?id=108&prYr=2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080921223623/http://www.pappastv.com/pressdetail.php?id=108&prYr=2008 |archive-date=September 21, 2008 |access-date=June 17, 2008 }}</ref> Several of the stations have since been sold either in business transactions with representatives involved in Pappas's bankruptcy proceedings or via station auction processes as the company winds down operations.

Although Pappas had originally stated that none of its stations would be affected at all by the closing, two stations owned by the company that were formerly affiliated with the CW have ceased operations. On May 29, 2008, [[Yakima, Washington]] affiliate [[KCWK]] (which served the south-central portion of that state) shut down and the station's offices were closed, leaving that area without locally based CW programming and forcing pay television providers to carry Los Angeles affiliate KTLA in order to provide the network's programming to their subscribers. The situation was resolved in April 2009, when [[Fisher Communications]] announced that its CBS affiliates in the area, [[KIMA-TV]] and satellite station [[KEPR-TV]], would carry the network through [[digital terrestrial television|DTT]] subchannel affiliations.

Subsequently, [[WGBP-TV|WLGA]] in [[Columbus, Georgia]] lost its CW affiliation in April 2009 to a subchannel of NBC affiliate [[WLTZ]] because of the network's concerns about Pappas' financial state;<ref>{{Cite news |last=Andrea V. Hernandez |date=April 3, 2009 |title=WLTZ's parent firm to carry CW Network in Columbus |work=[[Ledger-Enquirer]] |publisher=[[The McClatchy Company]] |url=http://www.ledger-enquirer.com/2009/04/03/672471/wltzs-parent-firm-to-carry-cw.html |access-date=December 14, 2010 |archive-date=May 13, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110513012327/http://www.ledger-enquirer.com/2009/04/03/672471/wltzs-parent-firm-to-carry-cw.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> WLGA ultimately ceased operations in June 2010 as it was unable to compete in the market as an independent station.<ref>{{cite web |date=June 23, 2011 |title=BLSTA - 20110623ADL Notification of Suspension of Operations / Request for Silent STA |url=https://licensing.fcc.gov/cgi-bin/ws.exe/prod/cdbs/forms/prod/cdbsmenu.hts?context=25&appn=101433121&formid=910&fac_num=11113 |publisher=Federal Communications Commission}}</ref>

==== Tribune's relations with the CW ====
While [[Tribune Media]] had solid affiliation deals with the CW on several of its stations, it also maintained a strong affiliation alliance with Fox. But with new management and ownership taking over Tribune in 2008, it was apparent that the company would switch one of its CW-affiliated stations to Fox (at least those in markets without a Fox owned-and-operated station or a former O&O that was acquired by Local TV, which Tribune later acquired in 2013<ref>{{Cite news |last=Robert Channick |date=July 1, 2013 |title=Acquisition to make Tribune Co. largest U.S. TV station operator |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |publisher=Tribune Publishing |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/business/breaking/chi-tribune-buying-local-tv-20130701,0,3402241.story |url-status=dead |access-date=July 1, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130704152051/http://www.chicagotribune.com/business/breaking/chi-tribune-buying-local-tv-20130701,0,3402241.story |archive-date=July 4, 2013 }}</ref>), adding to more questions surrounding the CW's future. In a March 2008 seminar by Tribune's then-chairman and CEO [[Sam Zell]], it was revealed that the company's San Diego outlet KSWB-TV would switch its affiliation from the CW to Fox that August, with KSWB assuming the Fox affiliation from [[XETV-TDT|XETV-TV]], which had been a Fox charter affiliate since that network's October 1986 inception. XETV (which is licensed to [[Tijuana]], [[Baja California]], Mexico under the ownership of [[Grupo Televisa]] but whose U.S. operations are programmed by [[Entravision|Bay City Television]]) was not informed of Zell's deal until it was made public.<ref>{{Cite web |title=XETV, KSWB Battle For Fox Affiliation In San Diego |url=http://radiomatthew.com/posts/xetv-kswb-battle-for-fox-affiliation-in-san-diego/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080609113416/http://radiomatthew.com/posts/xetv-kswb-battle-for-fox-affiliation-in-san-diego/ |archive-date=June 9, 2008 |website=RadioMatthew.com}}</ref>

After the news broke, XETV planned on suing to prevent the switch because it would violate an affiliation contract that XETV had with Fox that was not set to expire until 2010. However, on July 2, 2008, XETV announced that it would join the CW on August 1 (the same day that KSWB became a Fox affiliate) and rebrand as "San Diego 6".<ref>{{Cite web |title=XETV Becomes San Diego 6—New Home of The CW Television Network |url=http://www.fox6.com/news/local/story.aspx?content_id=7a4bac12-8df5-48e6-8f68-d8e355f50b95 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080707223418/http://www.fox6.com/news/local/story.aspx?content_id=7a4bac12-8df5-48e6-8f68-d8e355f50b95 |archive-date=July 7, 2008 |access-date=October 25, 2014 }} (July 2, 2008)</ref> Though twelve of Tribune's thirteen other CW-affiliated stations have remained with the network, all of them began to de-emphasize the network from their branding (e.g., "CW 11") in favor of one with a stronger local identity. On-air branding that excised the CW name began being implemented by the stations in July 2008, either on-air (in the case of KWGN-TV) or through their websites (as part of a redesign for all of the Tribune stations' websites).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Michael Schneider |date=September 1, 2008 |title=Tribune gives CW the cold shoulder |work=Variety |publisher=Reed Business Information |url=https://variety.com/2008/scene/markets-festivals/tribune-gives-cw-the-cold-shoulder-1117991420/ |access-date=May 22, 2012 |archive-date=January 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114142109/http://variety.com/2008/scene/markets-festivals/tribune-gives-cw-the-cold-shoulder-1117991420/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Some of these stations eventually began reincorporating the CW branding starting in 2011, such as KDAF/Dallas, KIAH/Houston and [[KRCW-TV]]/[[Portland, Oregon]].

Tribune Company president and CEO [[Peter Liguori]] said in a May 2014 discussion at the MoffettNathanson Media & Communications Summit that he was "not pleased with where the CW is [in regards to its ratings performance]", stating that the network "should not program to [young] people who don't watch [conventional] television". Liguori also stated that he would consider collaborating with the network in regards to improving its programming slate, possibly by incorporating programs from the company's Tribune Studios unit (a production division which launched shortly after Liguori was appointed president of Tribune in November 2013) onto the network, as well as having Tribune play a larger role in the CW's management.<ref>{{Cite news |last=David Lieberman |date=May 15, 2014 |title=Tribune CEO Says He's "Not Pleased" With CW's Performance |work=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |publisher=Penske Media Corporation |url=https://deadline.com/2014/05/tribune-ceo-says-hes-not-pleased-with-cws-performance-731112/ |access-date=May 23, 2014 |archive-date=May 23, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140523024148/http://www.deadline.com/2014/05/tribune-ceo-says-hes-not-pleased-with-cws-performance/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Speaking at [[Goldman Sachs]]' 23rd Annual Communacopia Conference in September 2014, Les Moonves acknowledged that Tribune had been looking for more input in how the network is programmed and noted that Liguori is a former programmer (having previously served in executive roles at Fox, [[FX (TV network)|FX]] and [[Discovery Communications]]), saying that "[Liguori] would like to participate. He has some good ideas. He's part of our team. Will there be some change in how the CW is structured going forward? I don't know." Moonves went on to reiterate that Tribune is "a very important part of [CBS'] future" (considering that Tribune had recently acquired the CBS affiliation for its Indianapolis station and then-CW affiliate [[WTTV]], following disagreements between CBS and longtime affiliate WISH-TV, which would eventually take over the CW affiliation in January 2015, over [[reverse compensation]] demands by the network).<ref>{{Cite news |last=Jon Lafayette |date=September 10, 2014 |title=Showtime Could Stream in International Markets; Moonves also hints at CW changes |work=Broadcasting & Cable |publisher=Reed Business Information |url=http://www.broadcastingcable.com/news/currency/showtime-could-stream-international-markets/133869 |access-date=October 4, 2014 |archive-date=October 6, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006065618/http://www.broadcastingcable.com/news/currency/showtime-could-stream-international-markets/133869 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In an October 2014 interview with ''[[Broadcasting & Cable]]'', Liguori appeared to reverse course on his previous statements and spoke of Tribune's support of the network. Liguori said in a statement, "We are very encouraged by the recent uptick in the CW['s] ratings and the positive critical response to the new primetime lineup. In particular, [CW CEO Mark Pedowitz] has put in place a programming strategy that will help the network appeal to a wider, more inclusive audience, which is important for our stations across the country. We were glad to support the launch of the new shows through editorial and promotional initiatives, and we look forward to more continued collaboration to build upon this momentum."<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 27, 2014 |title=Bet on The CW Paying Off For the Network's Parents |url=http://www.broadcastingcable.com/news/currency/bet-cw-paying-network-s-parents/135127 |access-date=March 12, 2015 |publisher=NewBay Media |periodical=Broadcasting & Cable |archive-date=October 31, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141031081157/http://www.broadcastingcable.com/news/currency/bet-cw-paying-network-s-parents/135127 |url-status=live }}{{subscription required|date=March 2015}}</ref>

In January 2016, the CW and Tribune began negotiations on a new affiliation deal, as the original 10-year agreement signed at the network's inception was approaching its end. Complicating matters was the desire by the CW's then-parent companies, CBS and Warner Bros., to stream the network's programming as a standalone pay [[Over-the-top content|OTT]] service. The impasse in negotiations resulted in a months-long standoff between the two groups.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tribune Impasse Is Behind CW OTT Option—TVNewsCheck.com |date=January 13, 2016 |url=http://www.tvnewscheck.com/article/91468/tribune-impasse-is-behind-cw-ott-option |access-date=December 30, 2016 |archive-date=March 22, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322130030/https://tvnewscheck.com/article/91468/tribune-impasse-is-behind-cw-ott-option/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On May 23, 2016, the CW and Tribune announced they had come to a new affiliation agreement. As part of the deal, Tribune's Chicago flagship [[WGN-TV]] would leave the network and revert to being an independent station after nearly 21 years of being affiliated with the CW and its predecessor network, the WB. A major factor in this decision was WGN-TV's large use of local sports programming at the time, which led to many pre-emptions of the CW while WGN-TV had to move as many as 30 games a year to another local station in Chicago.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=May 23, 2016 |title=The CW & Tribune Reach New 5-Year Agreement, Chicago Affiliation Switches To Fox-Owned Station WPWR |url=https://deadline.com/2016/05/the-cw-tribune-new-affiliate-agreement-2-1201761192/ |access-date=December 30, 2016 |archive-date=October 25, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161025134022/http://deadline.com/2016/05/the-cw-tribune-new-affiliate-agreement-2-1201761192/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The CW affiliation moved to [[WPWR-TV]], a [[Fox Television Stations]]-owned [[MyNetworkTV]] station.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Littleton |first=Brian Steinberg, Cynthia |date=May 23, 2016 |title=CW, Tribune Stations Set Affiliation Deal as WGN-TV Chicago Goes Indie |url=https://variety.com/2016/tv/news/cw-tribune-affiliation-wgn-1201780975/ |access-date=December 30, 2016 |archive-date=February 28, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170228183044/http://variety.com/2016/tv/news/cw-tribune-affiliation-wgn-1201780975/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 19, 2019, Tribune Media was acquired by Nexstar Media Group.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Feder |first=Robert |date=September 16, 2019 |title=FCC approves Tribune Media sale: What's next for WGN? |url=https://www.robertfeder.com/2019/09/16/fcc-approves-tribune-media-sale-whats-next-wgn/ |access-date=September 17, 2019 |website=RobertFeder.com |archive-date=September 21, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190921084452/https://www.robertfeder.com/2019/09/16/fcc-approves-tribune-media-sale-whats-next-wgn/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Channick |first=Robert |date=September 19, 2019 |title=Nexstar completes purchase of WGN owner Tribune Media |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/business/ct-biz-nexstar-tribune-sale-completed-wgn-20190919-i3ba4p4yibhfjo3vrki4ebe6ke-story.html |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=Chicago Tribune |archive-date=September 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190920135307/https://www.chicagotribune.com/business/ct-biz-nexstar-tribune-sale-completed-wgn-20190919-i3ba4p4yibhfjo3vrki4ebe6ke-story.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Littleton |first=Cynthia |date=September 19, 2019 |title=Nexstar Completes Tribune Acquisition, Sean Compton to Head Programming |url=https://variety.com/2019/biz/news/nexstar-tribune-fcc-deal-complete-compton-1203334923/ |access-date=September 19, 2019 |website=Variety |archive-date=September 20, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190920090225/https://variety.com/2019/biz/news/nexstar-tribune-fcc-deal-complete-compton-1203334923/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==== Roberts Broadcasting bankruptcy ====
[[Roberts Broadcasting]] filed for Chapter 11 [[bankruptcy protection]] on October 7, 2011; the company cited the loss of the UPN affiliations on its stations in St. Louis ([[WRBU]]), [[Columbia, South Carolina]] ([[WZRB]]) and [[Jackson, Mississippi]] ([[WRBJ-TV]]) when that network shut down in favor of the CW in 2006, as much of UPN's programming consisted of minority-targeted programs that Roberts felt were compatible with their stations' target audiences (though the stations have since recovered from this setback; additionally, its station in [[Evansville, Indiana]], [[WAZE-TV]], had instead affiliated with the WB prior to 2006, as it was owned by [[South Central Communications]] until February 2007). The company had also been hit with lawsuits from Warner Bros. Television, [[Twentieth Television]] and [[CBS Television Distribution]] over its failure to pay fees for syndicated programming; Roberts eventually settled with Twentieth but lost the Warner Bros. and CBS cases.<ref name="b&c-robertsbankruptcy">{{Cite news |last=Michael Malone |date=October 10, 2011 |title=Roberts Broadcasting Files For Bankruptcy |work=Broadcasting & Cable |publisher=NewBay Media |url=http://www.broadcastingcable.com/article/475001-Roberts_Broadcasting_Files_For_Bankruptcy.php |access-date=October 10, 2011 |archive-date=October 12, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111012171227/http://www.broadcastingcable.com/article/475001-Roberts_Broadcasting_Files_For_Bankruptcy.php |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="c&p-robertsbankruptcy">{{Cite news |last=Jacob Newkirk |date=October 10, 2011 |title=WAZE Owner Roberts Broadcasting files for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy |work=Evansville Courier & Press |publisher=E. W. Scripps Company |url=http://www.courierpress.com/news/2011/oct/10/waze-owner-roberts-broadcasting-files-chapter-11-b/ |access-date=October 10, 2011 |archive-date=October 12, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111012145042/http://www.courierpress.com/news/2011/oct/10/waze-owner-roberts-broadcasting-files-chapter-11-b/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On March 24, 2011, the [[Federal Communications Commission]] (FCC) canceled WAZE's license for Roberts' failure to construct its digital transmitter facilities.<ref name="fcc-wazegone">{{Cite web |last=Kevin Harding |date=March 24, 2011 |title=Re: WAZE-TV, Madisonville, Missouri |url=https://cdbs.recnet.com/corres/?doc=25217 |access-date=March 30, 2011 |website=CDBS Public Access |publisher=[[Federal Communications Commission]] |archive-date=October 26, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026054335/http://licensing.fcc.gov/cgi-bin/prod/cdbs/forms/prod/getimportletter_exh.cgi?import_letter_id=25217 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, the station continued to broadcast via its three-station analog [[broadcast relay station#translator stations|translator]] network.

On February 20, 2012, Roberts Broadcasting announced that it was exploring the possibility of selling one or all four of its television stations in order to raise enough cash to pay off its creditors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lisa Brown |date=February 20, 2012 |title=Roberts Broadcasting Mulls Sale of TV Stations |url=https://www.stltoday.com/business/columns/lisa-brown/roberts-broadcasting-mulls-sale-of-tv-stations/article_cb921586-5bfe-11e1-a475-001a4bcf6878.html |publisher=[[Lee Enterprises]] |newspaper=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |access-date=April 17, 2020 |archive-date=July 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200729005008/https://www.stltoday.com/business/columns/lisa-brown/roberts-broadcasting-mulls-sale-of-tv-stations/article_cb921586-5bfe-11e1-a475-001a4bcf6878.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On October 22, 2012, Roberts announced that it had sold WRBJ to the [[Trinity Broadcasting Network]];<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jeff Ayres |date=October 22, 2012 |title=Roberts brothers' TV station in new hands |url=http://www.clarionledger.com/article/20121023/BIZ/310230036/Roberts-brothers-TV-station-new-hands?nclick_check=1 |publisher=[[Gannett Company]] |newspaper=[[The Clarion-Ledger]] |url-status=dead}}{{dead link|fix-attempted=yes|date=October 2026}} </ref> the deal was approved by a bankruptcy court on January 17, 2013,<ref name="stlpd-courtapproval">{{Cite news |last=Lisa Brown |date=January 18, 2013 |title=Roberts Cos.' Mississippi TV station sale approved |work=St. Louis Post-Dispatch |publisher=Lee Enterprises |url=https://www.stltoday.com/business/local/roberts-cos-mississippi-tv-station-sale-approved/article_c5ded9b7-ad9e-5b80-a3c5-f5985ff2ba77.html |access-date=January 19, 2013 |archive-date=October 3, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181003033959/https://www.stltoday.com/business/local/roberts-cos-mississippi-tv-station-sale-approved/article_c5ded9b7-ad9e-5b80-a3c5-f5985ff2ba77.html |url-status=live }}</ref> with TBN officially taking over operational control of WRBJ five months later on May 24<ref>{{Cite press release |title=NEW TBN FULL-POWER STATION SIGN-ON |date=May 24, 2013 |url=http://www.tbn.org/announcements/new-tbn-full-power-station-sign-on |website=[[Trinity Broadcasting Network]] |access-date=February 13, 2014 |archive-date=November 9, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131109172243/http://www.tbn.org/announcements/new-tbn-full-power-station-sign-on |url-status=dead }}</ref> The CW returned to the Jackson market on the second digital subchannel of CBS affiliate [[WJTV]] in September 2013. On January 3, 2013, the repeater network of WAZE ceased operations; later that month on January 28, independent station WTVW hurriedly joined the CW, in order to maintain the network in the Evansville area.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jacob Newkirk |date=January 3, 2013 |title=WAZE-TV translators shut down |url=http://jakesdtvblog.blogspot.com/2013/01/breaking-waze-tv-translators-shut-down.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131218140530/http://jakesdtvblog.blogspot.com/2013/01/breaking-waze-tv-translators-shut-down.html |archive-date=December 18, 2013 |website=Jake's DTV Blog |publisher=[[Blogspot]] }}</ref>

On December 2, 2013, Roberts filed to sell WZRB to Radiant Light Ministries, a subsidiary of [[Tri-State Christian Television]], for $2&nbsp;million.<ref name="fcc-wzrbtct">{{Cite web |date=December |url-status=live }}</ref> On December 4, Roberts also filed to sell WRBU to TCT for $5.5&nbsp;million.<ref name="fcc-wrbutct">{{Cite web |date=December 4, 2013 |title=APPLICATION FOR CONSENT TO Ion Media later chose to wind down the ex-WAZE-TV translator network entirely and instead affiliate with Nexstar's [[WTVW|WTVW-DT4]] (itself a CW affiliate on its main channel) by 2017.

==== Carriage dispute with DirecTV ====
In July 2023, Nexstar implemented a [[Blackout (broadcasting)|blackout]] of the CW, along with its affiliates for other major broadcast networks, on [[DirecTV]], [[DirecTV Stream]], and [[U-verse TV]], causing DirecTV to complain to the FCC. In return, Nexstar stated that their streaming agreement with DirecTV had expired in November 2022 and it was illegally streaming content on DirecTV Stream from the CW.<ref>{{cite web |last=Weprin ====Paramount's withdrawal and affiliation realignment====
As part of the sale to Nexstar, Paramount Global's [[CBS News and Stations]] subsidiary was granted the right to withdraw its eight affiliates from the network—in [[Atlanta]], [[Detroit]], [[Philadelphia]], [[Pittsburgh]], [[Sacramento, California|Sacramento]], [[San Francisco]], [[Seattle]] and the [[Tampa Bay]] area—which was exercised on May 5, 2023, effective September 1, 2023.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rice |first1=Lynette |date=May 5, 2023 |title=Eight CBS Stations To Ditch CW And Go Independent This Fall |work=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]] The situation of the CW in the Detroit market after the CBS withdrawal was tenuous for several months. [[Mission Broadcasting]], a company that contracts with Nexstar for the operational services of its stations, agreed to purchase [[WADL (TV)|WADL]] from Adell Broadcasting Corporation in a deal that provided for Nexstar to supply many of its operating functions. In addition, WADL became the new CW affiliate in Detroit while the deal was pending.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://missionbroadcastinginc.com/2023/05/18/mission-broadcasting-to-acquire-wadl-tv-detroit-from-adell-broadcasting/|title=Mission Broadcasting To Acquire WADL-TV Detroit From Adell Broadcasting|website=Mission Broadcasting, Inc.|date=May 18, 2023|access-date=September 1, 2023|publisher=broadcastone}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://enterpriseefiling.fcc.gov/dataentry/views/public/assignmentDraftCopy.html?displayType=html&appKey=25076ff387de8c4a0187e7ea3d64032c&id=25076ff387de8c4a0187e7ea3d64032c&goBack=N|title=Assignments|website=Licensing and Management System|date=May 17, 2023|access-date=September 1, 2023|publisher=[[Federal Communications Commission]]}}</ref> The acquisition stalled at the FCC over objections concerning the relationship between Mission and Nexstar. As a result, Adell Broadcasting removed CW programming from the station on October 30, 2023; the network's programs reappeared on Scripps-owned [[WMYD]] on November 13, 2023. The acquisition of WADL by Mission was called off in May 2024, despite the purchase being approved by the FCC a month prior.<ref name="Detr231030">{{cite news|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/entertainment/television/2023/10/30/cw-network-yanked-from-detroit-airwaves-over-business-spat/71380700007/|title=CW Network yanked from Detroit airwaves over business spat|first=Adam|last=Graham|newspaper=[[The Detroit News]]|date=October 30, 2023|accessdate=October 30, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=November 6, 2023|title=TV20 Detroit to air CW Network primetime programming, live sports starting Nov. 13|publisher=WXYZ Detroit|access-date=November 6, 2023|url=https://www.wxyz.com/news/tv20-detroit-to-air-cw-network-primetime-programming-live-sports-starting-nov-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-24 |title=WADL Sale Terminated |url=https://www.michiganmedia.com/2024/05/24/wadl-sale-terminated/ |access-date=2024-05-26 |website=Michigan Association of Broadcasters |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lafayettepublished |first=Jon |date=2024-05-23 |title=Mission Broadcasting Terminates Agreement To Buy WADL Detroit |url=https://www.nexttv.com/news/mission-broadcasting-terminates-agreement-to-buy-wadl-detroit |access-date=2024-05-26 |website=Broadcasting Cable |language=en}}</ref>

On April 19, 2024, Nexstar announced that the CW would not renew its affiliations with the seven E.W. Scripps Company-owned stations—in [[Norfolk, Virginia|Norfolk]], [[Lafayette, Louisiana|Lafayette]], [[Detroit]], [[Miami]], [[Tucson]], [[Corpus Christi, Texas|Corpus Christi]], and [[San Luis Obispo]]—that still carried the network.<ref name="b&c-scrippscwend">{{cite news |last1=Lafayette |first1=Jon |title=Nexstar Dropping Scripps-Owned The CW Affiliates in 7 Markets |url=https://www.nexttv.com/news/nexstar-dropping-scripps-owned-cw-affiliates-in-seven-markets |access-date=April 19, 2024 |work=[[Broadcasting & Cable]] |date=April 19, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> Nexstar concurrently announced that the CW would move to its own stations in Norfolk and Lafayette effective September 1, 2024;<ref name="b&c-scrippscwend"/> the move would also end WMYD's brief affiliation with the network.<ref name="td-scrippscwend">{{cite news |last1=Keys |first1=Matthew |title=Scoop: Scripps to pull CW Network affiliation in seven cities in September |url=https://thedesk.net/news/scripps-dropping-cw-network-from-stations/ |access-date=April 19, 2024 |work=The Desk |date=April 19, 2024}}</ref> On May 1, 2024, it was announced that the CW would move back to its original Chicago station affiliate, WGN-TV (Channel 9), beginning September 1, 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/movies-and-tv/2024/05/01/the-cw-chicago-wgn-wciu|title=The CW moving from WCIU back to WGN in September|last=Jevens|first=Darel|work=Chicago Sun Times|date=May 1, 2024|accessdate=May 1, 2024}}</ref>

==== Carriage dispute with Optimum ====
On January 10, 2025, Nexstar implemented a blackout of 63 of its local stations and [[NewsNation]] on [[Optimum (TV/Internet)|Optimum]], with the CW's flagship station [[WPIX]] being a major part of the dispute. Nexstar accused Optimum's owner [[Optimum Communications|Altice USA]] of making irrational demands for special terms during contract negotiations, while Altice in return accused it of demanding excessive rates for its programming and forcing it to carry unpopular channels like NewsNation.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hayes |first=Dade |date=January 10, 2025 |title=Nexstar Local Stations Including New York's WPIX, Cable's NewsNation Go Dark On Optimum In Carriage Dispute |url=https://deadline.com/2025/01/nexstar-optimum-carriage-dispute-tv-stations-wpix-newsnation-1236254076/ |access-date=January 12, 2025 |website=Deadline Hollywood}}</ref> The two reached a carriage agreement on January 18, allowing Nexstar programming to be restored on Optimum.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Garner |first1=Glenn |last2=Hayes |first2=Dade |date=January 18, 2025 |title=Nexstar & Optimum Reach Carriage Agreement After Standoff |url=https://deadline.com/2025/01/nexstar-optimum-reach-carriage-agreement-1236260597/ |access-date=January 20, 2025 |website=Deadline Hollywood}}</ref>

=== Owned-and-operated stations ===
CW stations owned by Nexstar Media Group, Mission Broadcasting, or Vaughn Media are considered O&O stations, with nearly 80 stations in markets as high as [[New York City]], [[Los Angeles]], [[Chicago]], and [[Philadelphia]], to lower markets such as [[Terre Haute, Indiana]], [[Wichita Falls, Texas]], [[Utica, New York]], and [[Evansville, Indiana]].

== Related services ==
=== Video-on-demand services ===
The CW provides [[video on demand]] access for delayed viewing of full episodes of the network's programming through various means, including via its website at CWTV.com and its [[mobile app]]s for [[iOS]] and [[Android (operating system)|Android]] devices (with programs streamable over [[Wi-Fi]] and cellular networks), a traditional VOD service—the CW on Demand—that is available on most traditional cable and IPTV providers, and through content deals with [[Hulu]], [[iTunes]] and [[Netflix]].<ref name="The CW on Hulu">{{Cite news |last=Todd Wasserman |date=October 28, 2011 |title=Hulu to Get Current Season of Gossip Girl and Other CW Content |work=[[Mashable]] |publisher=Mashable Inc. |url=http://mashable.com/2011/10/28/hulu-gossip-girl-cw |access-date=November 2, 2011 |archive-date=October 30, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111030165419/http://mashable.com/2011/10/28/hulu-gossip-girl-cw/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="CWNetflix">{{Cite news |date=October 13, 2011 |title=Netflix, CW Sign 4-Year Deal to Stream Shows |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idUS77575804120111013 |access-date=October 13, 2011 |archive-date=January 6, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160106060102/http://www.reuters.com/article/idUS77575804120111013 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In January 2007, the CW began streaming full-length episodes of several of its programs on the CWTV.com website. The most recent episodes of the network's shows are usually made available on the CW app and the CW on Demand the day after their original broadcast. Due to restrictions imposed through its deal with the streaming service, streaming of the most recent episode of any CW program on Hulu is restricted until eight days after their initial broadcast, in order to encourage live or same-week (via both [[digital video recorder|DVR]] and cable on-demand) viewing, with day-after-air streaming on either service limited to subscribers of Hulu's subscription service. The CW previously imposed a three-day delay after an episode's original airdate before making its programs available on its website and through the Hulu subscription service (originally called Hulu Plus). However, changes implemented by the network on March 15, 2012, to reduce [[copyright infringement]] of its programming content through illegal streaming and downloading internet platforms resulted in that delay being reduced to eight hours after a program's original airing through both services.<ref name="The CW on Hulu" /><ref name="CWNetflix" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Andrew Wallenstein |date=March 13, 2012 |title=CW shortens Web streaming delay to battle piracy |url=https://variety.com/2012/digital/news/cw-shortens-web-streaming-delay-to-battle-piracy-1118051427/ |access-date=July 18, 2015 |website=Variety |publisher=Penske Media Corporation |archive-date=July 12, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150712090433/http://variety.com/2012/digital/news/cw-shortens-web-streaming-delay-to-battle-piracy-1118051427/ |url-status=live}}</ref>

In October 2011, the network entered into digital distribution deals with streaming services Netflix and Hulu. The four-year Netflix agreement allowed its customers to instantly watch more than 700 hours of previous seasons of the CW's then-current scripted series, while Hulu signed a five-year deal, giving the streaming site access to next-day content from four of the five major networks (except for CW sister network CBS).<ref name="The CW on Hulu" /><ref name="CWNetflix" /> The Netflix deal was estimated to be worth $1&nbsp;billion, providing a much needed lifeline to the money-losing CW network and solidified its future as a valuable asset for then-co-owners CBS and Warner Bros.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 13, 2011 |title=UPDATE: CW Could See $1B From 4-Year Licensing Deal With Netflix |url=https://deadline.com/2011/10/netflix-signs-4-year-licensing-deal-with-the-cw-182444/ |publisher=Deadline Hollywood |access-date=May 15, 2019 |archive-date=July 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200729004324/https://deadline.com/2011/10/netflix-signs-4-year-licensing-deal-with-the-cw-182444/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The Netflix deal was renewed in 2016, updated to allow the streaming service to provide entire seasons of CW shows a week after their airing. The Hulu deal was discontinued at this time.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 20, 2016 |title=The CW To Extend Netflix Streaming Deal After Hulu Ends In-Season Pact |url=https://deadline.com/2016/06/the-cw-extend-netflix-streaming-dealhulu-ends-in-season-pact-1201775788/ |publisher=Deadline Hollywood |access-date=May 15, 2019 |archive-date=September 15, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190915094818/https://deadline.com/2016/06/the-cw-extend-netflix-streaming-dealhulu-ends-in-season-pact-1201775788/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2019, the CW and Netflix opted not to renew the deal. The respective studios of CW shows would instead sell to streaming services individually.<ref name="Deadline Hollywood" /> Beginning in 2020, WarnerMedia streaming service [[HBO Max]] (later rebranded to [[Max (streaming service)|Max]] under Warner Bros. Discovery) would be the exclusive streaming home for Warners-produced CW shows.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 9, 2019 |title=What's Coming to HBO Max: Shows, Movies Announced for WarnerMedia Streaming Service (So Far) |url=https://variety.com/2019/tv/news/hbo-max-warnermedia-shows-announced-1203262497/ |publisher=Variety |access-date=July 9, 2019 |archive-date=July 9, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709223331/https://variety.com/2019/tv/news/hbo-max-warnermedia-shows-announced-1203262497/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On October 24, 2012, the CW entered into its first video-on-demand distribution deal with a pay television provider through an agreement with [[Comcast]] that allows customers to watch the four most-recent episodes of the network's primetime shows on the [[cable television|cable provider]]'s Xfinity On Demand service, along with next-day episode content. The CW On Demand, which is accessible to subscribers at no additional charge, debuted on [[Comcast Cable|Comcast Xfinity]] systems nationwide on October 25, 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Michael O'Connell |date=October 24, 2012 |title=The CW Inks First On-Demand Deal With Comcast |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/cw-inks-first-demand-deal-382290 |publisher=Prometheus Global Media |periodical=The Hollywood Reporter |access-date=April 17, 2020 |archive-date=July 31, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200731093313/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/cw-inks-first-demand-deal-382290 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Since 2024, the CW has operated a pair of [[free ad-supported streaming television]] channels, The CW Gold and The CW Forever, featuring archival content.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-16 |title=Scoop: Nexstar's CW Network quietly launches two FAST channels on Freevee |url=https://thedesk.net/2024/07/cw-forever-cw-gold-freevee-fast-channels/ |access-date=2026-01-10 |website=TheDesk.net |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== High-definition feed ===
The CW's master feed is transmitted in [[1080i]] [[high-definition television|high definition]] with [[5.1 surround sound]]. All transmission of the network's programming moved to the format in June 2012, with the network's prime time lineup being presented in HD since March 2012 (when ''America's Next Top Model'' became the final CW program to convert to the format), with the exception of certain specials produced prior to that point (such as ''[[Grandma Got Run Over by a Reindeer (TV special)|Grandma Got Run Over by a Reindeer]]'', a [[Christmas and holiday season|holiday]] special carried over to the network from the WB) and select movie presentations. The network's Saturday morning E/I block, [[One Magnificent Morning]], is also broadcast in HD, with the final SD program, the two-season daytime talk show ''[[The Robert Irvine Show]]'' converting to the format for its second and final season in September 2017 (and in turn ending U.S. broadcast television's standard definition age).

The network is available in HD on most of its full-power affiliates, while availability of high definition content on subchannel-only or cable-exclusive affiliates varies by market; in some of these cases, the over-the-air signal is available only in [[standard-definition television|standard definition]] (a [[16:9 aspect ratio|16:9]] widescreen feed transmitted in [[480i]] SD is presented on some over-the-air affiliates to meet minimum requirements for presentation), with the station offering an exclusive high definition feed to pay television providers. Some affiliates transmit CW programming in [[720p]] HD due to technical considerations if the network is carried on a digital terrestrial subchannel of a station affiliated with another major network or if a primary feed CW affiliate carries more than one subchannel. Since June 2012, the CW Plus feed is also transmitted in HD, and the network has asked those affiliates to carry it in high definition wherever possible. With CBS beginning to use 16:9 framing for all of their graphics on September 24, 2018, the CW was the last major network that continued to use [[4:3 aspect ratio|4:3]] framing for all graphics, before switching to the 16:9 framing for all of their graphics in August 2020.

=== CW Seed ===
'''CW Seed''' (originally called '''CWD''' or the '''CW Digital Studio''') is a production arm that provided original content created exclusively for digital platforms focused in the areas of animation, [[game shows]], comedy, and digital personalities.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Ng |first=Philiana |date=May 17, 2012 |title=CW Launches Digital Studio, Unveils Online Projects |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/cw-digital-studio-cwd-326165 |magazine=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |access-date=May 4, 2013 |archive-date=August 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190806225326/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/cw-digital-studio-cwd-326165 |url-status=live }}</ref> Previously existing as a section on the CW's main website, CW Seed was spun-off to a separate domain in 2013 as a streaming platform.<ref name="Miller2013">{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Liz Shannon |date=August 28, 2013 |title=Meet CW Seed: The CW's new platform for experimentation |url=https://gigaom.com/2013/08/28/meet-cw-seed-the-cws-new-platform-for-experimentation/ |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[GigaOm]] |archive-date=June 17, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210617170819/https://gigaom.com/2013/08/28/meet-cw-seed-the-cws-new-platform-for-experimentation/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Armstrong">{{Cite web |last=Armstrong |first=Olivia |date=November 9, 2015 |title=What The Heck Is CW Seed? Get To Know The Coolest (FREE!) Streaming Service You've Never Heard Of |url=https://decider.com/2015/11/09/what-is-cw-seed/ |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[New York Post#Website|Decider]] |archive-date=June 17, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210617213842/https://decider.com/2015/11/09/what-is-cw-seed/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Gidlow">{{Cite web |last=Gidlow |first=Steve |date=October 22, 2018 |title=The CW's Rick Haskins on How CW Seed Has Bloomed |url=https://www.mediavillage.com/article/the-cws-rick-haskins-on-how-cw-seed-bloomed/print/ |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=MediaVillage |archive-date=March 22, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210322002724/https://www.mediavillage.com/article/the-cws-rick-haskins-on-how-cw-seed-bloomed/print/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The free [[Over-the-top media service|media app]] became available on several [[Digital media player|devices]], including [[Roku]] and [[Amazon Fire TV]].<ref name="Roku">{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Ed |date=November 17, 2015 |title=CW Seed now available for FREE on the Roku platform |url=https://blog.roku.com/cw-seed-now-available-for-free-on-the-roku-platform |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Roku]] |archive-date=March 22, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210322002817/https://blog.roku.com/cw-seed-now-available-for-free-on-the-roku-platform |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Amazon">{{Cite web |last=Locklear |first=M. |date=September 6, 2017 |title=The CW's free Seed app is now streaming on Amazon Fire TV devices |url=https://www.engadget.com/2017-09-06-cw-free-seed-app-streaming-amazon-fire-tv-devices.html |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[Engadget]] |archive-date=November 28, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201128031743/https://www.engadget.com/2017-09-06-cw-free-seed-app-streaming-amazon-fire-tv-devices.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

CW Seed produced various web series, including ''[[Vixen (web series)|Vixen]],'' ''[[Freedom Fighters: The Ray]]'', and ''[[Constantine: City of Demons]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moser |first=Cassidee |date=July 5, 2015 |title=CW Seed's Vixen Animated Series Voice Cast Revealed |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2015/07/05/cw-seeds-vixen-animated-series-voice-cast-revealed |access-date=October 17, 2023 |website=IGN |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 11, 2017 |title=DC's Freedom Fighters: The Ray Animated Series Coming to CW Seed With Gay Superhero Lead |url=https://comicbook.com/dc/news/dcs-freedom-fighters-the-ray-animated-series-coming-to-cw-seed-w/ |access-date=2024-05-04 |website=[[ComicBook.com]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Prudom |first=Laura |date=March 23, 2018 |title=Constantine: City of Demons - Watch a First Look from CW Seed's Animated Series |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2018/03/23/constantine-city-of-demons-watch-cw-seed-animated-series |access-date=October 17, 2023 |website=IGN |language=en}}</ref> On January 8, 2020, CW Seed acquired U.S. streaming rights to 14 series from [[BBC Studios]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dade Hayes |date=January 8, 2020 |title=CW Seed Acquires 14 BBC Studios Shows In Non-Exclusive Streaming Pact |url=https://deadline.com/2020/01/cw-seed-bbc-studios-non-exclusive-streaming-pact-1202824788/ |access-date=March 20, 2020 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |archive-date=March 20, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200320233017/https://deadline.com/2020/01/cw-seed-bbc-studios-non-exclusive-streaming-pact-1202824788/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In September 2020, the platform added over 300 hours of programming with additional seasons for existing shows and new series, such as ''[[90210 (TV series)|90210]]'', ''[[Lost Girl]]'', ''[[Nikita (TV series)|Nikita]]'', and ''[[XIII: The Conspiracy]]''.<ref name="300Hours">{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2020 |title=CW Seed Bulks Up - More Than 300 Additional Hours of Programming to Be Rolled Out Through the Remainder of The Year |url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2020/09/01/cw-seed-bulks-up-more-than-300-additional-hours-of-programming-to-be-rolled-out-through-the-remainder-of-the-year-372205/20200901cw01/ |access-date=March 21, 2021 |website=[[The Futon Critic]] |archive-date=March 21, 2021 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20210321223224/http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2020/09/01/cw-seed-bulks-up-more-than-300-additional-hours-of-programming-to-be-rolled-out-through-the-remainder-of-the-year-372205/20200901cw01/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The CW Seed app and website were reabsorbed into the CW's in April 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keys |first=Matthew |date=April 5, 2022 |title=CW moves "CW Seed" content into single CW app |url=https://thedesk.net/2022/04/cw-seed-moving-to-cw-app/ |access-date=January 16, 2023 |website=The Desk |language=en-us |archive-date=January 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230116231945/https://thedesk.net/2022/04/cw-seed-moving-to-cw-app/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''The WB Television Network''' (known simply as '''The WB''', and nicknamed "'''The Frog'''" after former mascot [[Michigan J. Frog]])<ref>{{cite web |title=Slanguage Dictionary: F |url=https://variety.com/static-pages/slanguage-dictionary/#f |website=Variety |access-date=June 1, 2021 |date=February 20, 2013}}</ref> was an American [[terrestrial television|broadcast]] [[television network]] that launched on January 11, 1995,<ref name="lat-wblaunchdate">{{Cite news |last=[[Daniel Cerone|Daniel Howard Cerone]] |date=January 2, 1995 |title=New Year Brings 2 New Networks: WB Television and United Paramount Prepare for Their Premieres This Month. But Can They Really Survive Against the Big Four? |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1995-01-02-ca-15591-story.html |access-date=September 1, 2013}}</ref> as a [[joint venture]] amongst [[Warner Bros. Entertainment]] (the network's namesake and controlling owner), [[Tribune Broadcasting]], and network president [[Jamie Kellner]]. It aired programs targeting teenagers and young adults aged 13 to 35, while its children's programming block, [[Kids' WB]], targeted youth aged 4<!--Don't change this!---> to 12. 

On January 24, 2006, Warner Bros. and [[CBS Corporation]] announced plans to merge The WB and competitor [[UPN]] into a new network, [[The CW]], later that year.<ref name="UPN, WB merge">{{Cite news |last=Anthony Crupi |date=January 24, 2006 |title=UPN, WB to Merge Into CW Network |work=[[AdWeek]] |url=http://www.adweek.com/news/advertising/upn-wb-merge-cw-network-83687}}</ref> The WB ceased broadcasting on September 17, 2006, with some programs from both it and UPN (which shut down two days earlier) moving to The CW when it launched the following day, September 18.
