Most of the Tribune Company's WB affiliates only used the network's logo within the logos of each station or used the "WB" name after the callsign in its on-air branding (an example was Los Angeles affiliate KTLA, which branded as "KTLA, The WB", after dropping its longstanding and genericized "Channel 5" brand in 1997). Many WB affiliates used another form of standardized branding: the network's [[Lakeland, Florida]], affiliate (serving [[Tampa, Florida|Tampa]]) acquired the WWWB call letters and branded on-air as "The WB 32" (it is now known as [[WMOR-TV]]). Other stations would take on a 'by city' branding approach (for example, [[KIAH|KHWB]] in [[Houston]] was called "Houston's WB", [[WATL|WATL-TV]] in [[Atlanta]] was called "Atlanta's WB", and [[WLVI|WLVI-TV]] in [[Boston]] was called "Boston's WB" – all three used the "WB (channel number)" branding prior to incorporating the station's city of primary service during the final years of the network's run); some stations which followed this scheme used a regional name instead of a specific city (such as "Capital Region's WB" for [[WCWN|WEWB]] in [[Albany, New York]], or "Hawaii's WB" for [[KHII-TV|KFVE]] in [[Honolulu]], Hawaii), while others also incorporated the channel number (such as [[Philadelphia]] affiliate [[WPHL-TV]] as "Philadelphia's WB17", or [[Mobile, Alabama]], affiliate [[WFNA (TV)|WBPG]] as "The Gulf Coast's WB55"). Many stations affiliated with The WB 100+ Station Group also followed either one of these variations on "The City/Region's WB" scheme (though the group's cable-only affiliates also used fictional call signs).

'''UKTV Media Limited''',<ref name="CompaniesHouse">{{Cite web |date=7 August 2001 |title=UKTV MEDIA LIMITED overview – Find and update company information – GOV.UK |url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/04266373 |access-date=1 September 2023 |website=[[Companies House]] |language=en}}</ref> [[trading as]] '''UKTV''', is a British multi-channel broadcaster, which, since 2019, has been wholly owned by [[BBC Studios]] (formerly [[BBC Worldwide]]), a commercial subsidiary of the [[BBC]]. It was formed on 1 November 1992 as a joint venture between the BBC and [[Thames Television]]. It is one of the United Kingdom's largest television companies.

UKTV's channels are available via a digital satellite or cable subscription in the UK and Ireland. The [[U&Dave]], [[U&Drama]], [[U&Eden]], [[U&W]] and [[U&Yesterday]] channels are also available in the UK on [[Freeview (UK)|Freeview]] and [[Freesat]], two free-to-air [[television]] services in the UK, as well as on the catch-up service [[U (streaming service)|U]]. Unlike the BBC's main television channels, funded by the [[television licensing in the United Kingdom|television licence]], UKTV's channels and online services broadcast commercial advertising and sponsorships.

Although many programmes on the channels are repeat broadcasts of productions from the BBC archives, they also broadcast programmes produced by other companies and UKTV have commissioned original programmes, such as ''[[Dynamo: Magician Impossible]]'', [[Taskmaster (TV series)|''Taskmaster'']], ''Bangers & Cash'' and the newly rebooted series of [[Bergerac (2025 TV series)|''Bergerac'']]. [[Playout]] and other technical services are provided by [[SES (company)|SES]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Priestley |first=Jenny |date=12 September 2023 |title=UKTV invests in linear with SES distribution expansion |url=https://www.tvbeurope.com/media-delivery/uktv-invests-in-linear-with-ses-distribution-expansion |access-date=12 June 2025 |website=TVBEurope |language=en-GB}}</ref>

The UKTV channels have broadcast in [[16:9 aspect ratio|16:9]] widescreen format since 31 January 2008, although some programmes originally made in [[fullscreen (aspect ratio)|4:3]] format are screened in the compromise [[14:9 aspect ratio|14:9]] [[letterboxing (filming)|semi-letterbox]] format.

== History ==
{{Further|Timeline of UKTV}}

=== Origins (1992–1997) ===
UKTV started life as a single channel, [[UK Gold]]. <ref>{{Cite news |title=UKTV:its origins and its destiny |url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2009/jan/23/uktv-origins-and-destiny |date=23 January 2009 |access-date=29 October 2026 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB}}</ref> The original partners behind the channel were the BBC's commercial arm [[BBC Enterprises]] and the outgoing ITV contractor [[Thames Television]], although before the launch the American cable operator [[Cox Enterprises]] stepped in and took a majority share, 65{{nbsp}}percent, in exchange for underwriting the costs of launching the channel.

UK Gold launched on 1 November 1992, showing [[rerun]]s of 'classic' archive programming from the archives of the BBC and Thames Television. In a sense, UK Gold succeeded [[British Satellite Broadcasting]]'s [[Galaxy (British TV channel)|Galaxy]] channel that had originally held these rights from the BBC.

Later on, United Artists Holding Europe stepped in as part owner, and that ownership eventually became a part of Flextech, which was controlled by the US cable company [[Tele-Communications Inc.|TCI]]. A second joint-venture satellite channel, called [[UK Living]], began broadcasting on 1 September 1993 with programming targeted at female viewers.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Media: How Thames turned the tide: From failed franchisee to thriving |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/media/media-how-thames-turned-the-tide-from-failed-franchisee-to-thriving-indie-producer-there-can-be-life-after-broadcasting-death-as-richard-last-witnessed-1392970.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250306125113/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/media/media-how-thames-turned-the-tide-from-failed-franchisee-to-thriving-indie-producer-there-can-be-life-after-broadcasting-death-as-richard-last-witnessed-1392970.html |archive-date=6 March 2025 |access-date=12 June 2025 |work=The Independent |language=en-GB |url-status=live }}</ref> Also in 1993, Flextech gained its first stake in the station after acquiring TCI's TV interests in Europe.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.telecompaper.com/news/flextech-set-to-acquire-tci-programming|title=Flextech Set To Acquire TCI Programming|publisher=Telecompaper|date=21 December 1993|access-date=22 June 2013}}</ref> In 1996, it started discussions about increasing its stake to gain full control; at that point, Flextech held 27% with Cox (38%), BBC (20%) and Pearson (15%).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sat-net.com/listserver/ts-news/msg00139.html|title=TS News&nbsp;– Flextech Reveals BBC, UK Gold Talks|publisher=Sat-net.com|date=14 August 1996|access-date=22 June 2013}}</ref> By the Autumn, Flextech held 80% of UK Gold.<ref name="independent.co.uk">{{cite news|last=Horsman|first=Mathew|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/flextech-ties-up-paytv-deal-1360937.html|title=Flextech ties up pay-TV deal|work=The Independent|date=30 October 1996|access-date=22 June 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.telecompaper.com/news/flextech-set-to-agree-channels-deal-with-bbc|title=Flextech Set To Agree Channels Deal With BBC|publisher=Telecompaper|date=16 August 1996|access-date=22 June 2013}}</ref> [[Living TV Group|Flextech]]'s main reason for increasing its stake in UK Gold was in anticipation of new talks with the BBC.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1996/08/15/business/flextech-and-bbc-discuss-tv-venture.html|title=Flextech and BBC Discuss TV Venture|work=The New York Times|date=15 August 1996|access-date=26 September 2021}}</ref>{{failed verification|date=September 2021}}

=== The launch of the UKTV network (1997) ===
During 1996, [[Flextech]] and the [[BBC]] held talks about a partnership to launch a new range of channels under the name UKTV.<ref name="independent.co.uk"/> [[BSkyB]] tried to compete against Flextech for the right to develop the BBC channels, but the BBC were against inviting BSkyB to participate in the pay-TV venture. BSkyB would have sought a significant share in the planned channels, in exchange for agreeing to offer them to its 3.8{{nbsp}}million direct-to-home satellite subscribers.{{citation needed|date=September 2021}} It was believed at the time that if it were spurned, BSkyB could develop competing channels before the Flextech-BBC launch, particularly arts and documentaries, as a spoiling tactic.<ref>{{cite news|last=Horsman|first=Mathew|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/sky-aims-for-stake-in-bbc-paytv-1356217.html |title=Sky aims for stake in BBC pay-TV|work=The Independent|date=1 October 1996|access-date=22 June 2013}}</ref>

The deal between Flextech and BBC was completed and signed in March 1997.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Flextech Venture Is Set With BBC |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1997/03/18/business/flextech-venture-is-set-with-bbc.html |publisher=The New York Times, taken from the Associated Press |date=18 March 1997 |access-date=29 October 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Flextech And The BBC Finally Shake Hands |url=https://uk.themedialeader.com/flextech-and-the-bbc-finally-shake-hands/ |publisher=The Media Leader |date=17 March 1997 |access-date=29 October 2026}}</ref> Initially it was assumed that the new channels would be BBC-branded: BBC Showcase, for entertainment; BBC Horizon, for documentaries; BBC Style, for lifestyle; BBC Learning, for schools, and BBC Arena, for the arts, plus three other channels including BBC Catch-Up, for repeats of popular programmes within days of their original transmission, a dedicated BBC Sport channel, and a TV version of [[BBC Radio 1|Radio 1]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Willcock|first=John|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/flextech-to-inject-pounds-20m-into-bbc-deal-1270994.html|title=Flextech to inject £20m into BBC deal|work=The Independent|date=4 March 1997|access-date=22 June 2013}}</ref> Flextech wanted these channels to carry advertisements, but the BBC argued that BBC-branded services in the UK should not, as doing so would undermine the rationale of [[Television licensing in the United Kingdom|TV licensing]].

A compromise was reached: BBC Showcase and BBC Learning, renamed [[BBC Choice]] and [[BBC Knowledge]] respectively before launch, would go ahead as BBC channels without commercials, while the deal with Flextech was passed to BBC Worldwide with control split 50/50,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bbcworldwide.com/annualreviews/report1998/Channels/page06.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101205171904/http://www.bbcworldwide.com/annualreviews/report1998/Channels/page06.htm|archive-date=5 December 2010|title=Joint venture channels|publisher=BBC Worldwide|access-date=22 June 2013}}</ref> thus allowing the remaining channels to carry advertisements. The 'UK' prefix was chosen for these new channels to capitalise on the success of UK Gold, as the brand by then had become a household name. The 'UKTV' network launched on 1{{nbsp}}November 1997 with three new channels; arts channel '[[UK Arena]]', lifestyle channel '[[UK Style]]' and documentary channel '[[UK Horizons]]'. UK Gold retained its name but received a new look in line with the rest of the network. Although the new network didn't use the BBC name and logo, its graphics and branding was in other aspects similar to those used by the BBC channels. The new graphics for the BBC and UKTV were both designed by the same company, [[Lambie-Nairn]]. Shortly before launch, it was decided the channel [[UK Living]] also owned by Flextech was to be renamed Living, instead of becoming part of the new UKTV network due to the similarity in programming between the channel and UK Style. On the same date, UK Gold celebrated its 5th anniversary.

=== Digital expansion (1998–2007) ===

[[File:New UKTV chart.png|thumb|Chart of channels in different years.]]
With the launch of digital television in the UK brought about by [[Sky UK|Sky Digital]] and [[ONdigital]] in 1998, two new channels were launched to broadcast on the new platforms: '[[UK Gold Classics]]', a sister channel to UK Gold showing older shows previously shown on UK Gold, and '[[UK Play]]', a new comedy and music channel.

UK Gold Classics was short lived however, and relaunched as UK Gold 2 in April 1999. The new channel time-shifted the morning schedule of UK Gold from 7{{nbsp}}pm for those who could not watch it at the original time.

To boost its popularity, UK Play was renamed ''Play UK'' and given a new look and new style of logo in November 2000,<ref>{{Cite news |title=UKTV becomes Play UK |url=https://www.broadcastnow.co.uk/uktv-becomes-play-uk/1204540.article |date=3 November 2000 |access-date=29 October 2026 |work=Broadcast |language=en-GB}}</ref> which the rest of the UKTV channels would adopt the following May. In November 2001, UK Style's food programming was moved to a new channel named '[[UK Food]]'.

The rebranding of Play UK failed to make the channel more popular, and on 30 September 2002 it was shut down. October saw the launch of the new free-to-view digital terrestrial platform [[Freeview (UK)|Freeview]] replacing ITV Digital, and with it the new history channel '[[U&Yesterday|UK History]]', which was included in Freeview's licence to operate the platform. UK History took many of the history-related programming from UK Horizons. In January 2003, UKTV launched a lifestyle channel for Freeview called [[UK Bright Ideas]]. However UK Bright Ideas was not created for the same reasons as UK Food and UK History to allow other UKTV channels to have more time to schedule other programming, but instead showed a mix of programming from UK Style and UK Food (and later UKTV Gardens) for Freeview viewers, to promote the lifestyle UKTV channels available on pay platforms.

UK Gold 2 was relaunched with a completely new schedule and style as UKG{{sup|2}} on 12{{nbsp}}November 2003, taking on some output similar to what used to be on Play UK before its closure, initially broadcasting from 8{{nbsp}}pm each night before later expanding to daytime.

On 8 March 2004, the network carried out a major rebranding scheme where all of the UKTV channels changed their prefixes from ''UK'' to ''UKTV''. ''UK Horizons'' was split into two channels{{snd}}[[UKTV Documentary]] and [[UKTV People]]. <ref>{{Cite news|title=UKTV to ditch UK Horizons |url=https://www.broadcastnow.co.uk/uktv-to-ditch-uk-horizons/1087841.article |publisher=Broadcast |date=5 February 2004 |access-date=29 October 2025}}</ref>

In 2005, the last new channel under the UKTV branding was launched, '[[UKTV Style Gardens]]', later renamed in 2007 to 'UKTV Gardens'. Like UKTV Food, it allowed UKTV Style to focus more on its more home-oriented programming.

=== Network rebrand ===

[[File:UKTV.svg|150px|thumb|UKTV logo from 2009 to 2013, not seen on screen like the previous and successor logos.]]
In 2007, UKTV G2 was renamed 'Dave' and began broadcasting on [[Freeview (UK)|Freeview]], replacing UKTV Bright Ideas, seen as an experiment in branding for the network. The name is said to be originated from the fact that "everyone knows a bloke called Dave", and that the name seems appropriate for a male-orientated channel. <ref>{{Cite news|title="Dave" channel targets young men |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/7005061.stm |publisher=BBC|date=20 September 2007|access-date=29 October 2026}}</ref>

On 11 June 2008, UKTV announced that it was beginning the process of rebranding its channels from generic, UKTV-prefixed names to individual and separate brands, after the successful launch of Dave.<ref>{{cite news|title=UKTV to rebrand channels|publisher=Broadcast|date=10 July 2008|url=http://www.broadcastnow.co.uk/news/multi-platform/news/uktv-to-rebrand-channels/1710309.article|access-date=7 June 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=UKTV unveils new channel brands|publisher=UKTV|date=10 July 2008|url=http://uktv.co.uk/uktv/item/aid/603804|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080712053401/http://uktv.co.uk/uktv/item/aid/603804|archive-date=12 July 2008|access-date=13 June 2008}}</ref>

The first stage of this rebranding began on 7 October 2008, when UKTV Gold was renamed G.O.L.D. (now U&Gold) and dropped its mixed entertainment schedule for pure comedy programming. UKTV Drama became the crime drama channel [[U&Alibi|Alibi]], and a new general entertainment channel called [[U&W|Watch]] (now U&W) was launched. It was with this rebrand that non-crime dramas (such as ''[[Doctor Who]]'' and ''[[Jonathan Creek]]'') was transferred to Watch. G.O.L.D. was on one level a continuation of the Gold name used since the channel's creation, but the letters also made up the channels new slogan: 'Go On Laugh Daily'.

As the UKTV network gradually rebranded from 2008, continuity announcers would usually say on each network 'Created for the BBC, chosen by' when a programme by the BBC was coming on (e.g. 'Created for the BBC, chosen by G.O.L.D.').

2009 saw the rebranding of all of the remaining channels beginning in January with UKTV Documentary's rebrand to [[U&Eden|Eden]], the name reflecting the nature programmes premiering on the channel. This was followed in February with UKTV People becoming [[Blighty (TV channel)|Blighty]], the new channel containing programming of the lives of the British population and the quirks of British society, and therefore explaining the slang name for Britain as the channel name. In March, UKTV History was rebranded as [[U&Yesterday|Yesterday]], reflecting the channel's history-themed programming.

This was closely followed in April by the re-brand of UKTV Style to [[Home (TV channel)|Home]], the new channel retaining the previous DIY shows and home makeovers and also including the programming from UKTV Gardens; however, this programming would follow a few weeks later in May, when UKTV Gardens was closed. Its channel slot was taken by [[Really (TV channel)|Really]], a new female crime medical and real life channel, similar to [[Virgin Media]]'s then-named [[Living (UK TV channel)|Living]].

The final channel to be rebranded was UKTV Food, on 22 June 2009 as [[Good Food]], to tie in with the [[Immediate Media Company|BBC]] [[Good Food (brand)|magazine]] of the same name. In June 2009, a final major tweak to these new brands occurred when, for promotional purposes, trailers began to use the same style and all channels began to use a circle-shaped variation of their logo to show that they were part of one network, making cross-channel promotion easier than previously.

On 14 June 2011, UKTV announced it would be launching Really on Freeview channel{{nbsp}}20 on 2 August 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uktv.co.uk/network/item/aid/645227|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110618023550/http://uktv.co.uk/network/item/aid/645227|archive-date=18 June 2011|title=UKTV secures free to air slot for Really, its cutting edge lifestyle channel|publisher=UKTV|date=14 June 2011}}</ref> This resulted in the timeshift channel ''Dave ja vu'' broadcasting reduced hours of 02:00{{nbnd}}04:00 on Freeview only to keep the [[Electronic program guide|EPG]] number available for future use. Really was the third of UKTV's ten brands to launch on Freeview.

=== Scripps Networks Interactive acquisition ===
Virgin Media were in talks, with a number of interested parties, to sell its 50% stake in UKTV. Bidders included [[Scripps Networks Interactive]] (a [[corporate spin-off|spin-off]] of the [[E. W. Scripps Company]]'s [[cable television]] networks and online assets), [[Discovery Communications]], [[ITV plc|ITV]] and [[Channel 4]]. Channel 4 was the least interested party, and Discovery had made offers that had been rejected. [[BSkyB]] was also said to be interested. BBC Worldwide held first refusal rights and could exercise control over who bought the stake.

On 15 August 2011, Virgin Media agreed to sell its 50% stake in UKTV to Scripps Networks Interactive in a deal worth £339m. Scripps paid £239m in cash, and about £100m to acquire the outstanding preferred stock and debt owed by UKTV to Virgin Media.<ref name="Scripps">{{cite web|url=https://www.ft.com/content/04a841ee-c729-11e0-a9ef-00144feabdc0|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20221210/https://www.ft.com/content/04a841ee-c729-11e0-a9ef-00144feabdc0|archive-date=10 December 2022|url-access=subscription|url-status=live|title=Virgin Media sells £239m stake in UKTV|work=Financial Times|date=15 August 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://investors.virginmedia.com/Stories/Scripps-Networks-Interactive-and-Virgin-Media-agree-on-UKTV-transaction-2186.aspx|title=Scripps Networks Interactive and Virgin Media agree on UKTV transaction|publisher=Virgin Media|date=15 August 2011|access-date=15 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120118001942/http://investors.virginmedia.com/Stories/Scripps-Networks-Interactive-and-Virgin-Media-agree-on-UKTV-transaction-2186.aspx|archive-date=18 January 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> Completion of the transaction was contingent on regulatory approvals in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] and [[Jersey]], which was received on 3 October 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marketwatch.com/story/scripps-networks-interactive-and-virgin-media-complete-uktv-transaction-2011-10-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111005193843/http://www.marketwatch.com/story/scripps-networks-interactive-and-virgin-media-complete-uktv-transaction-2011-10-03|archive-date=5 October 2011|title=Scripps Networks Interactive and Virgin Media Complete UKTV Transaction|publisher=MarketWatch|date=3 October 2011}}</ref> Related to the transaction, Scripps Networks Interactive and BBC Worldwide negotiated an agreement whereby, after completion, BBC Worldwide would have the option, via a combination of cash and a package of digital rights for UKTV, to increase its shareholding from 50{{nbsp}}percent to a maximum of 60{{nbsp}}percent. Scripps Networks Interactive's existing voting rights and board representation would be unaffected by this proposed arrangement, which would be subject to BBC Executive and BBC Trust approvals.

=== BT Vision deal ===
On 22 March 2012, it was announced that [[BT TV#Launch of BT Vision|BT Vision]] would offer UKTV original content on{{nbh}}demand from later in the day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uktv.co.uk/network/item/aid/651551|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120324191947/http://uktv.co.uk/network/item/aid/651551|archive-date=24 March 2012|title=UKTV creates its first IPTV content deal&nbsp;– first linear channel deal for BT Vision|publisher=UKTV|date=22 March 2012}}</ref> As part of the deal, UKTV started streaming [[linear channel]]s to BT Vision set-top boxes in late 2012. The first three were [[U&W|Watch]], [[U&Gold|Gold]] and [[U&Alibi|Alibi]] and it intended to add further channels such as Good Food, Eden and Home.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.digitalspy.com/media/news/a372534/uktv-agrees-on-demand-channels-deal-with-bt-vision/|title=UKTV agrees on-demand, channels deal with BT Vision|work=Digital Spy|date=22 March 2012}}</ref> [[U&Dave|Dave]], [[Really (TV channel)|Really]] and [[U&Yesterday|Yesterday]] were not expected to be included as they are already on [[Freeview (UK)|Freeview]], which is available through BT's hybrid IPTV/Freeview set-top boxes.

=== Corporate rebrand (2013) ===

[[File:UKTV logo.png|thumb|150x150px|UKTV logo used from 2013 to 2024]]
UKTV announced on 18 March 2013 that it would reintroduce its company brand in celebration of its 21st year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uktv.co.uk/network/item/aid/656458|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130322121707/http://uktv.co.uk/network/item/aid/656458|archive-date=22 March 2013|title=UKTV evolves company brand on and off-air to celebrate 21st birthday|publisher=UKTV|date=18 March 2013}}</ref> The UKTV logo redesign went live across the identities of their channel network and programmes on {{nowrap|Tuesday 26 March 2013}} for its 21st birthday.

=== Dispute with Virgin Media ===
For almost three weeks in summer 2018, the UKTV channels were absent from [[Virgin Media]]. On 20 July 2018, it was announced that Virgin Media would stop broadcasting all of the UKTV channels from 22{{nbsp}}July, amid a dispute over fees<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2018/jul/22/four-million-virgin-media-customers-lose-uktv-channels-dave|title=Four million Virgin Media customers lose UKTV channels|work=The Guardian|date=22 July 2018}}</ref> and the lack of on-demand content from the BBC.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2018/jul/19/virgin-media-customers-to-lose-uktvs-10-channels-in-rights-row|title=Virgin Media customers to lose UKTV's 10 channels in rights row|work=The Guardian|date=19 July 2018}}</ref> The companies were not able to agree terms<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/entertainment-arts-44915060|title=UKTV: Dave and Gold among channels dropped by Virgin Media|publisher=BBC|date=22 July 2018}}</ref> and the channels ceased to be available at just after midnight on 22 July 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.a516digital.com/2018/07/no-deal-uktv-axed-from-virgin.html|title=No deal: UKTV axed from Virgin|work=a516digital|date=22 July 2018|access-date=22 July 2018|archive-date=16 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191216101405/https://www.a516digital.com/2018/07/no-deal-uktv-axed-from-virgin.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> The channels returned to Virgin Media on {{nowrap|11 August 2018}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://corporate.uktv.co.uk/news/article/uktv-channels-return-virgin-tv/|title=UKTV channels return to Virgin TV &#124; News &#124; UKTV Corporate Site|website=corporate.uktv.co.uk}}</ref>

=== Split of channels between BBC and Discovery ===
On 1 April 2019, Discovery (formerly Discovery Communications, which had acquired Scripps Networks Interactive in 2018) announced that BBC Studios would acquire its stakes in the seven entertainment-based UKTV channels for £173{{nbsp}}million, along with the UKTV brand, and Discovery would acquire BBC Studios' stakes in the remaining channels Good Food, Home and Really. The sale closed on 11 June 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://variety.com/2019/tv/news/bbc-discovery-uktv-deal-for-channels-including-really-home-dave-alibi-1203240452/|title=Discovery, BBC Close Deal to Split UKTV Channels|last=Clarke|first=Stewart|date=12 June 2019|website=Variety|language=en|access-date=2 December 2019}}</ref>
The sale was part of a larger agreement between the two companies for international streaming rights to the BBC's natural history programming.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2019/04/discovery-bbc-reignite-global-content-partnership-1202586088/|title=Discovery & BBC Reignite Global Content Deal With SVOD & UKTV Agreement, Six Years After Ending Previous Pact|last=White|first=Peter|date=1 April 2019|website=Deadline|language=en|access-date=1 April 2019}}</ref>

=== Corporate rebrand (2024) and the launch of "U" masterbrand ===
In November 2023, it was announced that in summer 2024, all of UKTV's free-to-air channels and UKTV Play would be rebranded with the new name of "U", with the {{nowrap|free-to-air}} channels [[U&Dave|Dave]], [[U&Drama|Drama]], [[U&Yesterday|Yesterday]] and [[U&W|W]] becoming "U&Dave", "U&Drama", "U&Yesterday", and "U&W" respectively. All four channels were rebranded on 16 July. UKTV rebranded their pay channels to "U&Gold" and "U&Alibi" on 7{{nbsp}}November, and "U&Eden" became a free-to-air channel on 7 October, and rebranded on 16 October. The "U" masterbrand made all of their channels be "U"nited under the "U" brand.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://corporate.uktv.co.uk/newsroom/uktv-announces-creation-of-u-a-new-brand-to-unite-its-free-tv-and-digital-portfolio/|title=UKTV announces creation of 'U' - a new brand to unite its free TV and digital portfolio|date=29 November 2023|website=UKTV|language=en|access-date=29 November 2023}}</ref> In early July 2024, UKTV started to roll out a similar logo to its "U" masterbrand. The logo can be found on the corporate website and on "U" (UKTV Play). The rebrand was completed on 7{{nbsp}}November 2024 with the addition of "U&GOLD" and "U&alibi", uniting the entire network under the "U" brand.<ref>{{Cite web |date= |title=UKTV Corporate Website |url=https://corporate.uktv.co.uk/ |access-date= |website= |language=}}</ref>

== Marketing ==
In 2003, UKTV announced plans of an experiment which examined the effect of different break patterns on advertising. UKTV teamed up with a number of advertisers to measure the effect of reductions in advertising spots, programme trailers and the number of breaks overall.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marketingweek.com/2003/05/01/uktv-chief-announces-plans-for-tv-ad-breaks-2/ |title=UKTV chief announces plans for TV ad breaks |publisher=Marketing Week |date=1 May 2003 |access-date=22 June 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Brown |first1=Maggie |last2=Lawson |first2=Annie |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2003/aug/28/broadcasting.advertising |title=We'll be back after this shorter break, UKTV tells viewers |work=The Guardian |date=28 August 2003 |access-date=17 September 2013}}</ref>

In February 2004, UKTV reduced the length of its advertising breaks in a bid to retain viewers and attract advertisers after results of its research show that shorter breaks produce higher advertising recall levels. From 8 March, interruptions were limited to a maximum of five minutes, with three-and-a-half minutes of commercial plus one-and-a-half minutes of promotional material, instead of a standard seven-and-a-half minutes.{{citation needed|date=December 2019}}

UKTV's move was similar to a solution suggested by PHD executive strategy director Louise Jones at 2003 Marketing Week TV United Conference, with a view to cleaning up breaks. Her proposal was for broadcasters to reduce spots by 20 per cent and to charge a corresponding price increase for them; the theory being clients would not have to boost their media spending, thus improving UKTV hopes a reduction in the length of break junctions would help it to keep viewers and provide advertisers with improved cut-through.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marketingweek.com/2004/02/05/uktv-takes-break-from-the-clutter/ |title=UKTV takes break from the clutter |publisher=Marketing Week |date=5 February 2004 |access-date=22 June 2013}}</ref>

== Channels ==
UKTV's channels are available via satellite and cable in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] and the [[United Kingdom]]. In the UK, on digital terrestrial television, [[U&Yesterday]], [[U&Dave]], [[U&Drama]], [[U&W]] and [[U&Eden]] are available on the Freeview platform. Selected parts of [[U&Gold]], [[HGTV (UK & Ireland)|Home]] and [[Good Food]] were available through the now defunct Top Up TV service. The logo on the UKTV branded channels has also now been replaced by a new design.

=== Current free-to-air channels ===
UKTV's [[free-to-air]] channels are available on all platforms.

==== U&Dave ====

[[File:U&Dave (2024).svg|thumb|U&Dave logo used since 2024]]
[[U&Dave]] is a comedy-oriented entertainment channel. The channel originally came together after UK Gold 2, an evening timeshift service of UK Gold, was reinvented to aim towards a more younger {{nowrap|16–34-year-old}} audience and was relaunched as UK G2 on 12 November 2003, becoming the more "edgy and contemporary" counterpart to UK Gold. As with its predecessor, UK{{nbsp}}G2 only broadcast at night, from {{nowrap|8 pm to 5 am.}}<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/a12139/uk-gold-2-ditched-for-uk-g2/|title='UK Gold 2' ditched.. For 'UK G2'|website=[[Digital Spy]]|date=28 October 2003}}</ref> It later rebranded as UKTV G2 in March 2004, and soon expanded its hours to the daytime as well.

On 15 October 2007, UKTV G2 rebranded as Dave, becoming the first in the network not to use UKTV or any UK branding.<ref name="ukfree.tv">{{cite web|url=http://www.ukfree.tv/fullstory.php?storyid=1107051303|title=It's Dave&nbsp;– not Bright Ideas and evening History&nbsp;– ukfree.tv&nbsp;– independent digital TV and switchover advice|work=UK Free TV|access-date=4 November 2007|archive-date=13 October 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071013165239/http://www.ukfree.tv/fullstory.php?storyid=1107051303|url-status=dead}}</ref> UKTV said the name of the channel was chosen because "everyone knows a bloke called Dave".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/7005061.stm|title=Entertainment&nbsp;– 'Dave' channel targets young men|access-date=4 November 2007|date=20 September 2007|publisher=BBC News}}</ref> The rebrand included the channel being available free-to-air on [[Freeview (UK)|Freeview]], replacing [[UKTV Bright Ideas]] which only averaged a 0.1% audience share.<ref name="freeviewlaunch">{{cite web|url=http://www.digitalspy.com/tech/a70407/uktv-considers-g2-freeview-launch/|title=UKTV considers G2 Freeview launch|website=[[Digital Spy]]|date=8 August 2007|access-date=4 November 2007}}</ref> The move to Freeview saw Dave launch in the bandwidth previously used by [[U&Yesterday|Yesterday]] (previously known as UKTV History).

In October 2017, Dave briefly rebranded to '''Rupert''' as part of a commercial partnership with Snickers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Snickers |url=https://uandcreative.co.uk/project/snickers/ |access-date=6 June 2025 |website=UKTV Creative |language=en-GB}}</ref> 

On 16 July 2024, Dave was renamed '''U&Dave'''.

U&Dave currently broadcasts on channel{{nbsp}}19 on Freeview and channel{{nbsp}}157 on Freesat.

==== U&Drama ====

[[File:U&Drama (2024).svg|thumb|U&Drama logo used since 2024]]
Launched on 8 July 2013, [[U&Drama]] focuses itself as a home for British dramas from the last 40{{nbsp}}years.<ref>{{cite press release|title=UKTV raises the curtain on Drama|date=2 May 2013|publisher=UKTV|url=http://corporate.uktv.co.uk/news/article/uktv-raises-curtain-drama/|access-date=2 May 2013}}</ref> The channel became the fourth channel to launch on Freeview, after Yesterday, Dave and Really.

On 16 July 2024, Drama was renamed '''U&Drama'''.

U&Drama currently broadcasts on channel{{nbsp}}20 on Freeview and channel{{nbsp}}158 on Freesat.

==== U&W ====

[[File: U&W (2024).svg|thumb|U&W logo used since 2024]]
[[U&W]] is a general entertainment channel,  and the flagship channel. The channel launched as Watch on {{nowrap|7 October 2008.}} From launch until 2010, the channel's mascot was Blinky the eyeball, who was seen on the idents, logo, and website. A 2012 rebrand saw smoke, hairballs, crystals and liquid flying out of the logo. The channel was later rebranded as W in February 2016.

In February 2022, ''[[Broadcast (magazine)|Broadcast]]'' magazine reported that the channel will become a free channel to air in the spring, joining stablemates Dave, Yesterday and Drama as a Freeview service.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.broadcastnow.co.uk/uktv/w-set-for-free-to-air-switch/5167769.article|title=W set for free-to-air switch}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://rxtvinfo.com/2022/uktv-planning-freeview-switch-for-w-channel|title=UKTV planning Freeview switch for 'W' channel|date=16 February 2022}}</ref> In March 2022, this was confirmed by UKTV<ref>{{cite web|url=https://corporate.uktv.co.uk/news/article/uktvs-w-launches-life-unfiltered-rebrand/|title=UKTV's W launches "Life Unfiltered" rebrand as the premium entertainment channel is taken free-to-air &#124; News &#124; UKTV Corporate Site}}</ref> with the channel due to be launched on Freeview channel{{nbsp}}25 from 28 March 2022. UKTV said that this female skewing channel would be still targeted at a 25 to 44 age range but introduced a new logo for the free-to-air era,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.broadbandtvnews.com/2022/03/21/uktv-to-make-w-channel-free-to-air/|title=UKTV to make W channel free-to-air|date=21 March 2022}}</ref> which included the letter W in a slanted rectangle.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tvzoneuk.com/post/uktv-w-freetoair-announcement|title=Uktv Take W Free-To-Air with Channel Rebrand|date=21 March 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://corporate.uktv.co.uk/news/article/uktv-takes-w-free-to-air/|title=UKTV expands W's reach by taking the premium entertainment channel free-to-air &#124; News &#124; UKTV Corporate Site}}</ref>

On 16 July 2024, W was renamed '''U&W'''.

U&W currently broadcasts on channel{{nbsp}}25 on Freeview and channel{{nbsp}}156 on Freesat.

==== U&Yesterday ====

[[File: U&Yesterday (2024).svg|thumb|U&Yesterday logo used since 2024]]
[[U&Yesterday]] focuses on history and archive programmes. It originally launched on {{nowrap|30 October 2002}} as UK History, as part of the launch of Freeview, and was broadcast on the same EPG bandwidth that formerly housed Play UK. The channel rebranded as UKTV History in March 2004. Hours on Freeview were cut when Dave launched, with transmissions finishing at 6{{nbsp}}pm, but were restored on 1 June 2010.

The channel relaunched as Yesterday in March 2009. Yesterday's main focus is (as of May 2024) on programmes with historical topics and biographies, nature and wildlife, some comedy, and some historical fact drama series, often from the BBC archives.

On 16 July 2024, Yesterday was renamed '''U&Yesterday'''.

U&Yesterday currently broadcasts on channel{{nbsp}}27 on Freeview and channel{{nbsp}}159 on Freesat.

==== U&Eden ====

[[File: U&eden (2024).svg|thumb|U&Eden logo used since 2024]]
[[U&Eden]] focuses on documentaries and factual programming. The channel launched on 8 March 2004 as UKTV Documentary, as a two-way split from UK Horizons (the other being the defunct UKTV People (Blighty). The channel originally aired natural history documentaries such as ''Planet Earth'', but mid{{nbh}}2024 saw its output also start to cover other factual and reality programming although natural history programming is still part of the channel's output.

On 16 October 2024, Eden was renamed '''U&Eden''' and became a free-to-air channel.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://corporate.uktv.co.uk/newsroom/sky-and-uktv-extend-multi-year-partnership|title=Sky & UKTV extend multi-year partnership}}</ref>

=== Current pay-TV channels ===
UKTV's pay-TV channels are available on Sky and Virgin Media, but not Freeview or Freesat.

==== U&Gold ====

[[File:U&Gold (2024).svg|thumb|U&Gold logo used since 2024]]
[[U&Gold]] focuses on comedy and was, until 2008, the flagship channel of the UKTV network. It launched on {{nowrap|1 November 1992}} as UK Gold, making it the oldest channel of the network as well.

UK Gold originally operated as a joint venture between [[Thames Television]] and [[BBC Enterprises]] to show [[rerun]]s of their archive programming. Within the launch of the UKTV network and as the years went on, the output of  UK Gold (renamed UKTV Gold in 2004) was mainly British comedy programmes and sometimes feature-length films. These are a combination of internally produced shows and repeats of shows from the BBC and ITV archives. In recent years, original programmes have aired on the channel and the American version of ''[[Dancing with the Stars (American TV series)|Dancing with the Stars]]'' has had its first UK airing on the channel.

UKTV Gold was relaunched as GOLD (Go On Laugh Daily) on the morning of {{nowrap|7 October 2008}} as it transitioned exclusively to comedy programmes, with the entertainment programming moving to Watch (U&W). The channel rebranded again to simply Gold in 2010.

The channel rebranded to '''U&Gold''' on 7 November 2024.

==== U&Alibi ====

[[File:U&Alibi (2024).svg|thumb|U&Alibi logo used since 2024]]
[[U&Alibi]] focuses on crime drama and suspense thrillers. It originally launched as a rebranding of UK Arena as UK Drama in March 2000, focusing on all kinds of drama programmes. It rebranded as UKTV Drama in March 2004, and on 2 May 2006, a new timeshift service called UKTV Drama +1 was launched, to replace UKTV People's timeshift channel. (UKTV People +1)

It was relaunched as Alibi on the morning of 7 October 2008 and is now fully focused on crime dramas which are mainly taken from the BBC and ITV archives.

The channel was named '''U&Alibi''' on 7 November 2024.

=== Catch-up service ===
{{Main|U (streaming service)}}

[[File:U (2024).svg|150px|thumb|U logo used since 2024]]

In June 2014, UKTV announced a [[streaming television|catch-up service]], UKTV Play. It launched on iOS in August,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.digitalspy.com/media/a579569/uktv-launching-first-interactive-digital-service-uktv-play/|title=UKTV launching first interactive service|date=23 June 2014|first=Susannah|last=Alexander|work=Digital Spy}}</ref> on PC, [[YouView]] and [[Virgin Media]] in November,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.broadbandchoices.co.uk/news/tv/uktv-play-arrives-on-youview-and-pc-00060|title=UKTV Play arrives on YouView and PC|date=21 November 2014|first=John|last=Barker|work=Broadband Choices|access-date=18 March 2015|archive-date=17 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141217110628/http://www.broadbandchoices.co.uk/news/tv/uktv-play-arrives-on-youview-and-pc-00060|url-status=dead}}</ref> on [[Android (operating system)|Android]] devices in February 2015<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.digitaltveurope.net/319412/uktv-play-app-launches-on-android/|title= UKTV Play app launches on Android|date= 10 February 2015|work=Broadband Choices}}</ref> and on [[Freesat]] in September 2018.<ref>[https://advanced-television.com/2018/09/14/uktv-play-launches-on-freesat/ ''UKTV Play launches on Freesat''] Advanced Television. 14 September 2018. Retrieved 30 January 2019</ref> The interactive service features content from the channels Dave, Yesterday, W, and Drama.

In addition to UKTV Play, some of the networks also have catch-up services. Catch-up services for [[U&W|Watch]], [[U&Gold|Gold]], Dave and Alibi were launched on Sky Go in October 2013,<ref>{{cite press release|title=Sky extends UKTV services across Sky On Demand, Sky Go and NOW TV|publisher=UKTV|url=http://corporate.uktv.co.uk/news/article/sky-extends-uktv-services/|access-date=18 March 2015}}</ref> alongside all UKTV channels launching on Eircom's eVision TV service and Gold launching on Now TV. The following month, all channels appeared on Virgin TV Anywhere.<ref>{{cite press release|title=UKTV makes full network of channels available on Virgin TV Anywhere|publisher=UKTV|url=http://corporate.uktv.co.uk/news/article/uktv-makes-full-network-channels-available-virgin-tv-anywhere/|access-date=18 March 2015}}</ref>

In November 2023, UKTV announced that UKTV Play would be renamed '''U''' as a part of a [[rebranding|rebrand]] of the UKTV network. UKTV Play rebranded to '''U''' on 16 July 2024.

=== FAST channels ===
On 24 August 2023, UKTV launched four [[Free ad-supported streaming television|FAST channel]]s on [[Samsung TV Plus]] and [[Pluto TV]]: UKTV Play Uncovered, UKTV Play Heroes, UKTV Play Laughs and UKTV Play Full Throttle.

Due to the "U" masterbrand in 2024, UKTV Play Uncovered, UKTV Play Heroes, UKTV Play Laughs and UKTV Play Full Throttle have been renamed  U&The Past, U&Real Heroes, U&Laughs and U&Transport, respectively.

=== Former channels ===
UKTV has also had many former channels which have been replaced by others, shut down or acquired by other companies.

==== UK Arena ====
[[UK Arena]] was one of the original three UKTV network channels, launching on {{nowrap|1 November 1997}}. The channel focused on airing [[the arts|arts]] and cultural programmes and was named after BBC's ''[[Arena (British TV series)|Arena]]'' programme.

The channel was relaunched on 31 March 2000 as UK Drama (now U&Alibi) with a focus on showing dramas rather than general arts programmes.

==== Play UK ====

[[File:Plauktv.svg|thumb|Play UK logo used from 2000 to 2002]]
[[Play UK]] focused heavily on music and comedy programming, and was the first of the UKTV networks to initially launch digitally (and also to coincide with the launch of [[OnDigital]] [later ITV Digital]). It launched as UK Play on 10 October 1998 alongside the launch of Sky Digital, with a majority of its scheduling consisting of music in the morning and afternoon while broadcasting comedy in the evening. The channel rebranded as Play UK in November 2000, becoming the first of the UKTV networks to gain the new logo.

The channel broadcast for 24{{nbsp}}hours a day on digital platforms, but also aired as a filler channel on the Sky Analogue platform (on the [[Astra 19.2°E]] satellites), broadcasting between {{nowrap|1 am and 7 am}} within [[UK Horizons]]' slot during its downtime.

The closure of ITV Digital led to the channel's viewership decreasing significantly, and its failure to compete with [[MTV (United Kingdom and Ireland)|MTV]] also corresponded to its decline. The channel closed on {{nowrap|30 September 2002}} on all platforms, and a month later on 30{{nbsp}}October, its vacated EPG bandwidth space was used to launch a brand new channel for the launch of the [[Freeview (UK)|Freeview]] platform{{snd}}UK History. The programmes that formerly aired on Play UK would move to UK Gold, and eventually UK G2.

==== UK Gold Classics/UK Gold 2 ====
UK Gold Classics was a sister channel to UK Gold that broadcast older comedy programming, as the main UK Gold channel was focusing more on newer shows. It launched on 10 October 1998 and was exclusive to Sky Digital.

Due to poor viewing figures, the channel ended its run on 28 March 1999, and on {{nowrap|2 April 1999}}, it was relaunched as UK Gold 2, becoming a secondary timeshift service for UK Gold that aired the channel's daytime programming in the evening.

The channel closed on 11 November 2003, and relaunched as the younger-oriented and edgier UK G2 the following day.

==== UK Horizons ====

[[File:UK Horizons logo.svg|thumb|UK Horizons logo used from 1997 to 2001]]
[[UK Horizons]] was one of the original three UKTV network channels, launching on {{nowrap|1 November 1997}}. The channel focused on airing [[Documentary film|documentaries]] and other factual programmes and was named after BBC's ''[[Horizon (British TV series)|Horizon]]'' programme, which itself formed a staple of its output in the early years. It also produced extended versions of top BBC brands such as ''Top Gear'' and ''Tomorrow's World''. The launch editor was Bryher Scudamore and the deputy editor was Eddie Tulasiewicz.

The channel closed on 7 March 2004, as part of UKTV's relaunch. UK Horizons was split into two new channels{{snd}}UKTV Documentary and UKTV People, which both launched the following day on 8{{nbsp}}March. UKTV Documentary took over UK Horizons' slot, as well as the UK Horizons +1 timeshift service, with UKTV People being the "new" channel.

==== UKTV Bright Ideas ====

[[File:UKTV Bright Ideas.svg|thumb|UKTV Bright Ideas logo used from 2004 to 2007]]
[[UKTV Bright Ideas]] originally launched as UK Bright Ideas on {{nowrap|15 January 2003}}, initially as a [[Freeview (UK)|Freeview]] exclusive before being expanded.

Similar to [[Ftn (TV channel)|Ftn]], the channel it timeshared with, UK Bright Ideas was essentially a highlights network aimed towards the [[Freeview (UK)|Freeview]] audience, by airing programmes featured on UKTV Style, [[UKTV Food]] and [[UKTV Gardens]]. In January{{nbsp}}2005, it began showing programmes branded by UKTV Sport, presumably to increase potential audience figures by extending the programme to Freeview viewers.

It ceased broadcasting on all platforms on 14 October 2007 at 6{{nbsp}}pm. The main aim for the closure was to coincide of the rebranding of UKTV G2 as Dave, which would allow the channel to broadcast on Freeview. It would also allow Dave's timeshift service to expand to 24{{nbsp}}hours, which it wasn't able to do as UKTV G2, due to Bright Ideas sharing the same EPG bandwidth on Sky and Virgin Media. The former EPG slot on Sky was later used for a filler network{{nbsp}}UKTV Style +2.

==== UKTV Gardens ====

[[File:UKTV Gardens.png|thumb|UKTV Gardens logo used from 2007 to 2009]]
[[UKTV Gardens]] was the second offshoot network of UKTV Style, and launched on {{nowrap|23 February 2005}} as UKTV Style Gardens. As the name implies, the channel aired programmes in relation to gardening. The channel name was shortened to UKTV Gardens in 2007.

On 19 May 2009, the channel was replaced with Really, with all the gardening programmes moving back to the newly rebranded Home.

==== Blighty ====

[[Blighty (TV channel)|Blighty]] was a factual network that originally launched on 8 March 2004 as UKTV People, as a two-way split from UK Horizons (the other being UKTV Documentary, now [[U&Eden]]). The output of Blighty was ''some'' factual programming of a lighter nature, such as ''[[Top Gear (2002 TV series)|Top Gear]]'' and docusoaps like ''[[Airport (TV series)|Airport]]'', and from February{{nbsp}}2009 following its rebranding, "British" shows like ''My Brilliant Britain''. However, the majority of the channel's programming was abridged by the BBC for commercial timing purposes, a policy that some critics consider hypocritical.

The channel was available on [[Sky UK|Sky]] and Virgin Media. However, it was not available on Freeview, despite the majority of the programmes being made by the BBC.

The channel closed on all platforms on 5 July 2013, three days ahead of the launch of Drama.

==== Good Food ====

[[File:Good Food.svg|thumb|150px|The final Good Food logo, used before the [[Warner Bros. Discovery|Discovery]] acquisition]]
[[Good Food]] focused on food and cookery programming. It originally launched on 1 November 2001 as UK Food, as the first offshoot network of UK Style. It rebranded as UKTV Food in March{{nbsp}}2004, and eventually as Good Food in June{{nbsp}}2009, being the last UKTV channel to rebrand.

Good Food broadcast a range of food and cookery programmes, similar to that of the content of BBC Worldwide's [[BBC Food]] service. Initially, most of the channel's output was aired on Home as well. The Good Food website originally devised and launched by Ian Fenn and Ally Branley provides a number of services including information on programmes shown on the channel, recipes, message boards, and a wine club. Recipes come from the various shows on Good Food and some include videos taken from the demonstrations. In September 2006, Good Food's website overtook the BBC Food site in popularity for the first time, achieving a 10% market share, against the 9.63% the BBC Food site dropped to, having held the top spot since it began.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.digitalspy.co.uk/broadcasting/a38958/weekend-spy-playing-with-food.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071206154706/http://www.digitalspy.co.uk/media/a38958/weekend-spy-playing-with-food/|archive-date=6 December 2007|title=Weekend Spy: Playing with Food|date=5 November 2006|first=Joanne|last=Oatts|work=Digital Spy}}</ref> It was named "Good Food Channel" on the UKTV website due to the fact that there is a magazine named Good Food.

Following the split of the UKTV network from [[BBC Studios]] and [[Discovery, Inc.|Discovery]] on 1 April 2019, Discovery took over control of Good Food, but they eventually closed the channel a few months later on 12{{nbsp}}September, merging all its programming into their existing sister channel [[Food Network]].

==== Home ====

[[File:Home logo (UKTV).svg|thumb|150px|The final Home logo, used before the channel changed its name to [[HGTV (UK & Ireland)|HGTV]]]]
[[Home (TV channel)|Home]] was one of the original three UKTV network channels, launching on 1 November 1997 as UK Style. The channel broadcast home improvement, food, DIY and gardening programmes that are a combination of internally produced shows and repeats of shows mainly from the BBC archive. Eventually, the food programmes were moved onto an offshoot network named UK Food (Good Food) in November{{nbsp}}2001, and the gardening programmes followed suit onto UKTV Style Gardens in February 2005. It was rebranded as UKTV Style in March 2004, and eventually the channel was rebranded as Home in April 2009.

On 1 March 2016, Home became a free-to-air network as it launched on [[Freeview (UK)|Freeview]].

Following the split of the UKTV network from [[BBC Studios]] and [[Discovery, Inc.|Discovery]] on {{nowrap|1 April 2019}}, Discovery took over control of Home, and in June, Discovery announced that the channel would be rebranded under their [[HGTV]] brand,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/discovery-sets-hgtv-uk-gok-wans-how-look-good-naked-1221192|title=Discovery U.K. to Rebrand Home as HGTV, Revive Gok Wan's 'How to Look Good Naked'|website=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=26 June 2019|language=en|access-date=30 June 2019}}</ref> with the channel rebranding as such on 21 January 2020.

Eventually, Warner Bros. Discovery closed HGTV on 13th January 2026, nearly six years after its rebrand from Home. HGTV's former programming moved to [[Really (TV channel)|Really]] and its channel slot on Freeview and [[Freesat]] was taken by [[TLC (British and Irish TV channel)|TLC]].

==== Really ====

[[File:Really logo 2013.svg|thumb|The Really logo, still used after the Discovery buyout]]
[[Really (TV channel)|Really]] focuses entirely on medical crime, real life and lifestyle shows and was another offshoot from UKTV Style. It launched on {{nowrap|19 May 2009}}, replacing UKTV Gardens.

Following the split of the UKTV network from [[BBC Studios]] and [[Discovery, Inc.|Discovery]] on {{nowrap|1 April 2019}}, Discovery took over control of Really.

CCXTV was launched on 15 April 2020 as an entertainment channel and took over Create and Craft's channel number (Freeview{{nbsp}}23), broadcasting from 7{{nbsp}}am until 10{{nbsp}}pm. Even though Create and Craft still had a shopping slot early on in the morning on Channel{{nbsp}}23, the rest of the schedule was made up of imports and re-runs of shows like ''[[The Bold and The Beautiful]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tvforum.uk/tvhome/new-channel-ccxtv-launching-15th-april-45473|title=New channel CCXTV launching 15th April: CCXTV launches on Wednesday 15th April, on Freeview. - TV Forum|website=tvforum.uk}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ontvtonight.com/uk/guide/listings/channel/8397013191/ccxtv.html|title=CCXTV - TV Listings Guide|website=Ontvtonight.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cordbusters.co.uk/new-freeview-channel-ccxtv-bold-and-the-beautiful/|title=New Freeview Channel, CCXTV, Is Bringing Back "The Bold And The Beautiful"|first=Or|last=Goren|date=13 April 2020|website=Cord Busters}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ccxtv.co.uk/schedule|title=Schedule &#124; CCXTV|access-date=27 November 2020|archive-date=5 December 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201205144345/https://www.ccxtv.co.uk/schedule|url-status=dead}}</ref> On {{nowrap|7 December 2020}}, CCXTV moved to Freeview channel{{nbsp}}73, with Dave Ja Vu moving to channel{{nbsp}}23.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/a516digital?lang=en|title=Occasionally mutters something about digital TV from the sidelines these days.|website=twitter.com|access-date=14 January 2022}}</ref>{{unreliable source?|date=April 2021}}

On 25 January 2021, it was announced that timeshift channel Drama+1 would be taking over Freeview channel{{nbsp}}73 on 1 February 2021, with CCXTV ending transmission.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rxtvinfo.com/2021/plug-pulled-on-ccxtv-freeview-channel|title=Plug pulled on CCXTV Freeview channel|website=Rxtvinfo.com|date=25 January 2021|access-date=25 January 2021|archive-date=30 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210130063346/https://rxtvinfo.com/2021/plug-pulled-on-ccxtv-freeview-channel|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==== UK Living ====
UK Living was originally affiliated with UK Gold but did not become part of the UKTV network, instead transferring to Flextech to be operated as a wholly owned company, and it changed its name to [[Sky Living|Living]] before the UKTV network launched.

==== GoldText ====
An analogue [[teletext]] service known as GoldText was available on UK Gold, but has since closed down.

=== Operating names ===
{{update section|date=December 2018}}
In the [[production logo]] screen at the end of UKTV's original commissions, for the channels [[U&W|Watch]], [[U&Gold|Gold]] and [[U&Dave|Dave]] the name UK Gold Services Ltd. is used instead of UKTV, as all three channels spawned from the original UK Gold channel. For the remaining channels, [[U&Alibi|Alibi]], [[U&Drama|Drama]], [[U&Eden|Eden]] and [[U&Yesterday|Yesterday]], the name UKTV New Ventures is used instead of UKTV.

=== Timeshift channels===
UKTV launched its first one-hour timeshift network{{snd}}[[UK Horizons|UK Horizons +1 Hour]] (U&Eden +1), in May 2001. This was followed up with the launch of [[HGTV (UK & Ireland)|UK Style +]] (HGTV +1) in February{{nbsp}}2002,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.broadcastnow.co.uk/uktv-to-air-timeshifted-uk-style-on-sky/1136163.article|title=Uktv to Air Timeshifted UK Style on Sky}}</ref> and [[U&Gold|UK Gold +1]] (U&Gold +1) in August 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tech/a8717/uk-gold-timeshift-channel-launches/|title=UK Gold timeshift channel launches|website=[[Digital Spy]]|date=1 August 2002}}</ref>

November 2003 saw the launch of UK Food +1 (Good Food +1), while 2004 saw the additions of [[U&Yesterday|UK History +1]] (U&Yesterday +1) in January,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tech/a13200/uk-history-1-launches-on-sky/|title=UK History +1 launches on Sky|date=28 January 2004|website=Digital Spy}}</ref> and [[U&Dave|UKTV G2 +1]] {{nowrap|(U&Dave Ja Vu)}} in November.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tech/a16709/epg-debut-for-two-new-1s-wine-tv/|title=EPG debut for two new +1s, Wine TV|website=[[Digital Spy]]|date=1 November 2004}}</ref>

2005 saw the addition of UKTV People +1,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tech/a18264/uktv-people-1-joins-sky-epg/|title=UKTV People +1 joins Sky EPG|website=[[Digital Spy]]|date=12 January 2005}}</ref> which was closed the following year<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tech/a31736/uktv-people-timeshift-closes/|title=UKTV People timeshift closes|website=[[Digital Spy]]|date=18 April 2006}}</ref> and replaced with UKTV Drama +1 (U&Alibi +1) in May 2006.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tech/a32356/three-additions-to-sky-epg/|title=Three additions to Sky EPG|website=[[Digital Spy]]|date=2 May 2006}}</ref>

December 2007 saw the launch of UKTV Style 2 (U&W) on Sky, a two-hour timeshift service that existed as a filler network whenever UKTV needed the space for another channel. It closed on 15 September 2008, in order to prepare for the launch of Watch.

Watch +1 (U&W +1) launched with the channel on 7 October 2008.

Drama +1 (U&Drama +1) launched on 16 September 2019.

=== HD channels ===
UKTV launched its first HD channel; [[Good Food|Good Food HD]] on 31 August 2010. The channel was originally available exclusively on [[Sky UK|Sky]] channel{{nbsp}}283.

[[U&Eden#U&Eden HD|Eden HD]] launched on 4 October 2010 on [[Sky UK|Sky]] channel{{nbsp}}559 and was the second HD simulcast from UKTV.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uktv.co.uk/network/item/aid/637940|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100828111206/http://uktv.co.uk/network/item/aid/637940|archive-date=28 August 2010|title=UKTV announces Good Food and Eden HD channel rollout|publisher=UKTV|date=9 August 2010}}</ref> Both channels are [[High-definition television|high-definition]] [[simulcast]]s of their standard definition counterparts.

UKTV announced on 29 July 2011 that they would be launching three new HD channels, [[U&Dave|Dave HD]] and [[U&W|Watch HD]] (then known as W HD and now U&W HD) launched in October{{nbsp}}2011, and [[U&Alibi|U&Alibi HD]] launched in July 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uktv.co.uk/network/item/aid/646048|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111107010131/http://uktv.co.uk/network/item/aid/646048|archive-date=7 November 2011|title=UKTV enters VoD market with landmark HD content deal with Sky|publisher=UKTV|date=29 July 2011}}</ref>

As part of Virgin Media's deal to sell its share of UKTV, all five of UKTV's HD channels were also added to Virgin's cable television service by 2012.<ref name="Scripps"/> Eden HD and Good Food HD were added on 7 October 2011, followed by Dave HD (now U&Dave HD) on 10{{nbsp}}October and Watch HD on 12{{nbsp}}October.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://my.virginmedia.com/customer-news/articles/UKTVNew/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111011064522/http://my.virginmedia.com/customer-news/articles/UKTVNew/|archive-date=11 October 2011|title=Virgin TV just got even bigger|publisher=Virgin Media|access-date=4 October 2011}}</ref>

On 2 October 2017, UKTV launched [[U&Gold|U&Gold HD]], replacing Eden HD on Sky. It was soon added to Virgin Media in August{{nbsp}}2018, replacing the SD feed.

2022 saw Yesterday HD (now U&Yesterday HD) launch on Sky in August and Virgin Media in December.

'''Warner Bros. Entertainment Inc.''' ('''WBEI'''),{{efn|Pronounced "''Warner Brothers''".<ref name="Thomson_Page_1">{{cite book |last=Thomson |first=David |author1-link=David Thomson (film critic) |title=Warner Bros: The Making of an American Movie Studio |date=2017 |publisher=Yale University Press |location=New Haven |isbn=9780300197600 |page=1 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OaYsDwAAQBAJ&pg=PA1 |access-date=August 17, 2023}}</ref> The abbreviated form is always used in writing, except when referring to the four Warner brothers themselves.<ref name="Gomery_Page_150">{{Cite book |last1=Gomery |first1=Douglas |authorlink1=Douglas Gomery|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=s0PP2Gm8xNcC&pg=PA150 |title=Movie History: A Survey |last2=Pafort-Overduin |first2=Clara |date=2011 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=9781136835254 |edition=2nd |location=New York |page=150 |via=[[Google Books]] |access-date=March 20, 2023 |archive-date=April 9, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409130025/https://books.google.com/books?id=s0PP2Gm8xNcC&pg=PA150 |url-status=live}}</ref> It is never read out loud as "Warner Bros" ([[Help:Pronunciation respelling key|<i title="English pronunciation respelling">-⁠BROHZ</i>]] or similarly); the opening voiceover of ''[[The Lego Batman Movie]]'' (2017) alludes to this common mistake.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 4, 2017 |title=The LEGO Batman Movie review: everything is awesome! |url=https://www.digitalspy.com/movies/a820489/lego-batman-movie-review-everything-is-awesome/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |publisher=[[Digital Spy]]}}</ref>}} also commonly known as  simply '''Warner Bros.''', is an American [[multinational corporation|multinational]] [[outline of entertainment|entertainment]] corporation owned by [[Skydance]]. Headquartered at the [[Warner Bros. Studios Burbank|Warner Bros. Studios complex]] in [[Burbank, California]], it was formed on December 3, 2002<ref name="Kaplan">{{Cite web |last=Kobrin |first=Janet A. |date=February 26, 2007 |title=Warner Bros. Entertainment Inc. v. The Kaplan Trust: Declaration of Janet A. Kobrin |url=https://ttabvue.uspto.gov/ttabvue/ttabvue-92043813-CAN-41.pdf#PAGE=20 |publisher=[[U.S. Patent and Trademark Office]]|access-date=January 1, 2026}}</ref> to incorporate the Warner Bros.-branded film and television assets of then-parent company AOL Time Warner (later the second iteration of Time Warner, [[WarnerMedia]], and [[Warner Bros. Discovery]]).

The main studio houses of Warner Bros. Entertainment are [[Warner Bros. Pictures]], one of the [[major film studios|"Big Five"]] major American film studios and the third oldest film studio in the United States still in operation (after [[Paramount Pictures]] and [[Universal Pictures]], both founded in 1912), as well as the original flagship Warner Bros. brand holder and its distribution arm. It also includes [[New Line Cinema]], [[Warner Bros. Pictures Animation]], and [[Warner Bros. Clockwork]].

== History ==

=== Early predecessors ===
This company is derived from [[Warner Bros. Pictures (1923–1967)|the original Warner Bros. Pictures]], which four brothers—[[Harry Warner|Harry]], [[Albert Warner|Albert]], [[Sam Warner|Sam]] and [[Jack L. Warner]]—founded in 1923. The company established itself as a leader in the American film industry, before diversifying into animation, television and video games.

It was acquired by fellow film studio [[Seven Arts Productions]] in 1966 to form [[Warner Bros.–Seven Arts]]. This was itself acquired two years later in 1969 by [[Kinney National Company]], which eventually became [[Time Warner]].

=== Time Warner Entertainment Company ===
On June 30, 1992, Time Warner transferred most of its Warner Bros. Inc. subsidiary's assets, including the film, television production and cable businesses, into [[Time Warner Entertainment|Time Warner Entertainment Company, L.P.]] (TWEC), a new [[limited partnership]] with [[Toshiba]] and [[C. Itoh & Co.]] where each invested US$500 million for a 6.25% share. The deal was intended to relieve debt pressure from the merger between Time Inc. and Warner Communications two years earlier.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Japanese partners close Time Warner deal |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1992/06/30/Japanese-partners-close-Time-Warner-deal/4865709876800/ |access-date=January 2, 2026 |agency=[[United Press International]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Willman |first=David |date=July 1, 1992 |title=Time Warner Completes Deal With Japanese |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1992-07-01-fi-1279-story.html |access-date=January 2, 2026 |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref>

In 1993, [[US West]] joined the partnership with a US$2.5 billion investment for a 25% share.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Time Warner closes U S West deal |url=https://www.upi.com/Archives/1993/09/15/Time-Warner-closes-U-S-West-deal/1472748065600/ |access-date=January 2, 2026 |agency=[[United Press International]]}}</ref> By 1996, TWEC was owned 74.49% by Time Warner and the remainder by US West.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 14, 1996 |title=TIME WARNER COMPANIES INC (Form: 10-Q) |url=https://content.edgar-online.com/ExternalLink/EDGAR/0000736157-96-000043.html?hash=2fa0b6ba95c7c903592fb821916571cfc4bffb3ea4996001507d353fa148bed7 |access-date=January 2, 2026 |website=Edgar Online}}</ref> After the 1996 acquisition of [[Turner Broadcasting System]], its film studio [[Castle Rock Entertainment]] was transferred to TWEC in 1997.<ref name=":1">{{cite magazine |last=Cox |first=Dan |date=December 7, 1997 |title=Castle Rock near split-rights deal |url=https://variety.com/1997/film/news/castle-rock-near-split-rights-deal-111741789/ |magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref>

=== Current company incarnation ===
In March 2003, AOL Time Warner regained full control of the Warner Bros. film and television production assets from TWEC and placed them in the newly formed Warner Bros. Entertainment Inc. wholly-owned subsidiary, which had been formed on December 3, 2002. TWEC retained only [[Time Warner Cable]], which was eventually spun off.<ref name="Kaplan" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Time Warner Inc.: Annual report for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2003 (Form 10-K) |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1105705/000095014404002438/g87394e10vk.htm |access-date=2026-01-02 |website=U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission}}</ref>

WBEI gained [[Turner Entertainment Co.]] in 2006<ref>{{Cite web |title=EX-21 SUBSIDIARIES OF THE REGISTRANT |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1105705/000095014407001550/g05042exv21.htm |access-date=2026-01-02 |website=www.sec.gov}}</ref> and [[New Line Cinema]] in 2008, both of which originated from Turner.<ref name="dial-d">{{cite news |date=April 16, 2008 |title=Dial 'D' for disaster: The fall of New Line Cinema |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/features/dial-d-for-disaster-the-fall-of-new-line-cinema-809545.html |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220618/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/features/dial-d-for-disaster-the-fall-of-new-line-cinema-809545.html |archive-date=June 18, 2022 |work=[[The Independent]] |location=London}}</ref>  After the 2018 [[acquisition of Time Warner by AT&T]], the Turner subsidiary was broken up, with cable television assets like [[Cartoon Network]], [[Boomerang (TV network)|Boomerang]], [[Adult Swim]] and [[Turner Classic Movies]] transferred to WBEI on March 4, 2019.<ref name="cnbc-wmreorganize">{{cite news |author=Lauren Feiner |date=March 4, 2019 |title=WarnerMedia reorganizes its leadership team after AT&T acquisition |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2019/03/04/warnermedia-reorganizes-its-leadership-team-after-att-acquisition.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190304182211/https://www.cnbc.com/2019/03/04/warnermedia-reorganizes-its-leadership-team-after-att-acquisition.html |archive-date=March 4, 2019 |access-date=March 4, 2019 |work=[[CNBC]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Michael Schneider |date=March 12, 2019 |title=What the End of the Turner Brand Could Mean for Its Channels |url=https://variety.com/2019/tv/news/turner-brand-time-warner-tnt-tbs-trutv-1203160652/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330181409/https://variety.com/2019/tv/news/turner-brand-time-warner-tnt-tbs-trutv-1203160652/ |archive-date=March 30, 2019 |access-date=April 23, 2019 |work=Variety}}</ref><ref name="WarnerCN">{{cite news |last1=Littleton |first1=Cynthia |date=March 4, 2019 |title=Warner Bros. Wants to Rev Up Kid's Content With Looney Tunes, Hanna-Barbera |url=https://variety.com/2019/biz/news/warner-bros-cartoon-network-hanna-barbera-1203154521/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190305061048/https://variety.com/2019/biz/news/warner-bros-cartoon-network-hanna-barbera-1203154521/ |archive-date=March 5, 2019 |access-date=March 4, 2019 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]}}</ref> After the 2022 [[merger of Discovery, Inc. and WarnerMedia]], [[Cartoon Network Studios]] and [[Hanna-Barbera Studios Europe]] were transferred to the Warner Bros. Television Group.<ref>{{cite web |last=Schneider |first=Michael |date=2022-10-12 |title=Warner Bros. TV Group Lays Off 82 Staffers, Consolidates Some Unscripted and Animation Departments in Belt-Tightening Restructure |url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/warner-bros-tv-group-layoffs-82-staffers-channing-dungey-1235400286/ |access-date=2022-10-12 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|language=en-US}}</ref>

On October 6, 2026, Warner Bros. Discovery and [[Paramount Skydance]] [[Acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance|merged]] to create [[Skydance]].<ref name="ReutersSkydanceName">{{cite news |last=Mehraj|first=Anzar|date=October 2, 2026|title=David Ellison says combined Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery will be named Skydance|url=https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/david-ellison-says-combined-paramount-warner-bros-discovery-will-be-named-2026-10-02/|access-date=October 3, 2026|work=Reuters}}</ref> After the acquisition, [[Warner Bros. Television Group]] reported directly to the Skydance TV division along with [[CBS Studios]] and [[Paramount Television Studios]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=2026-10-07 |title=Skydance Co-CEO On Prospect Of Company's TV Studios Merging |url=https://deadline.com/2026/10/skydance-tv-studios-merging-warner-bros-cbs-studios-ptvs-1237148403/ |access-date=2026-10-07 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref>
